who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 21 years old at the start of employment. No prior professional experience is required.
how_to_apply: Complete the in-person application and interview during the scheduled Application and Interview Weekend.
notes: The organization's Gallery Fellowship (ages 16 to 24) and 10-month Mural Studio job are separate programs. The old ArtWorks web address now redirects to 1001colors.org. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: 8 weeks, June to July; 20 to 30 hours a week, Monday to Friday about 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
pay_detail: $13 an hour

who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).
duration: 2 years
pay_detail: No cost listed on the page (public school program)

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Call the Alameda County Workforce Development Board main line at (510) 259-3842. You can also use the Contact Us link on the youth page.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead. The youth page says to find a local Future Force provider through its Future Force page. The youth page lists no individual provider phone numbers.
pay_detail: Not stated. The youth page mentions paid and unpaid work experience but gives no wage.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Most programs are ages 14 to 18 (14 by Sept 28, 2026 for the fall session). Outreach Assistantships need age 16+.
how_to_apply: Apply online (up to six programs, ranked). Save your Application ID for the Teen Dashboard. Most programs require an interview; offers must be accepted within 72 hours. A parent/guardian consent form is required after you accept.
notes: One program per session. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required for every program; teens without one should contact ASM. Applying again each session needs a new application. The apply page still shows fall 2026 wording, but fall programs began Sept 28, so the fall round is over for new applicants until the spring window opens. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.
duration: Spring: late Feb to mid May. Summer: late June to early Aug. Fall 2026: Sept 28 to Dec 12.
pay_detail: Paid stipend based on program level and frequency. Dollar amounts vary by program and are not stated on the apply page.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older for Discovery Station and Astronomy volunteering. Commit to at least 8 hours a month for one year.
how_to_apply: Click 'Apply Now' on the volunteer page, create an account in the museum's volunteer system, complete the orientation and online training, and sign a Program Volunteer Agreement.
notes: The Astronomy Education volunteer role (also 16+, at least 4 hours a month for one year) was marked 'not recruiting at the moment'. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: At least 8 hours per month for one year
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade. A local American Legion Auxiliary Unit must pick and sponsor you. Each high school can send only one delegate. If no Unit sponsors your school, you can apply as a statewide alternate. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor. Or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. The site has a list to find one. Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Many use a form, an essay or an interview. Picked students then fill out an online form. It opens in February 2027. Is there no Unit at your school? You can apply as a statewide alternate. That form opens in April 2027.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages. The 2027 session will be the 84th. Adult staff must be at least 20 or out of high school for at least three years, so staff roles are not for teens.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22 to 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15, in grades 7 to 10. You need a 2.5 GPA or higher and must pass a Red Cross Level 4 swim test. You also need your own ride.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add an unofficial school transcript, two letters of recommendation and a resume. Add a short letter, about one page, under the heading "Tell Us About You". Interviews follow.
notes: The program page does not give start and end dates or pay. Ask the aquatics team. Email arpdaquatics@alamedaca.gov or call the city at 510-747-7400. It is held at Encinal Swim Center, 230 Central Ave. Residency is not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students aged 16 and older. The program page does not list residency or other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Application link on the program page. It goes to the city job site. Watch for the posting in March.
notes: The program page does not say if the job is paid, how long it lasts, or if a work permit is needed. Ask Human Resources at 510-747-4900.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.
duration: Shifts

who_can_apply: High school students interested in local government. The program page does not list an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online intern application. The link is on the program page.
notes: Projects serve Dublin, Fremont, Livermore, Pleasanton, Sunol and the eastern unincorporated areas of Alameda County. The program page does not give hours, start dates or pay. The office is at 4501 Pleasanton Ave, Pleasanton. The intern director is Katy Felton. The page shows two different email addresses, so call the office to check.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. If you are 17 or younger, you need a work permit from your school unless you have already graduated. Some jobs, such as racing, cash handling, childcare, amphitheater usher, entertainment transport and parking seller, need you to be 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the job form online. Or print the paper form and send it in.
notes: Pay examples from the program page: Admissions Ambassador $18.00, Exhibits Attendant $17.00, Event Operations Tech $20.00. The job email is jobs@alamedacountyfair.com. The phone is 925-426-7600. The fair office is at 4501 Pleasanton Ave. The program page does not say how many hours a week you will work.
pay_detail: $17.00 to $20.00 per hour, depending on the job, as listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school, college and STEM trade school students. The program page does not list an age or residency rule.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say how to apply. Check it again in February or March 2027.
notes: The program page does not give program dates, pay or an age limit, so ask before you plan. Questions: alcoitd@acgov.org.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. The link is on the page. The library phone is 510-745-1500.
notes: The teen page is thin and does not name a teen role or branch. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO) for volunteer roles such as book reviews and LEGO coding.
duration: 1st Tuesday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 pm
pay_detail: Community service hours only

who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the 'How to become a Book Reviewer' page linked from the teen page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for the advisory role, where teens suggest ideas for library events and projects.
pay_detail: Community service hours only

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school AND either live in Oakland or attend an OUSD school or charter, both when you apply and during the cohort. Spring cohorts are for 10th to 12th graders. Summer 2027 is for current 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application that must be done in one sitting (no save). Pick your cohort, upload a resume, and answer short-answer questions (75 words minimum each for spring, 150 for summer). Draft answers first. Then an interview. Questions: healprogram@alamedahealthsystem.org.
notes: As of 2026-10-16, the 2026-27 dates, pay and rules are on the HealthPATH page, healthpath-ahs.org/healprogramapply. That page does not load with https. So this card links to the AHS news post that points to it. Type healthpath-ahs.org/healprogramapply into your browser for the live dates and the form. The page says HEAL is for high school students of color. The written rule is that you live in Oakland or go to an OUSD school. The AHS volunteer program is a different program, and it is for ages 18 and up. The page does not say if you need a work permit for the stipend. Ask the program.
duration: Spring 2027: about 5 weeks, Mon to Thu 4 to 6 pm (Cohort A Jan 11 to Feb 11, B Feb 22 to Mar 25, C Apr 5 to May 13). Summer 2027: June 14 to July 23, weekdays 9 am to 4:30 pm.
pay_detail: Fall 2026 cohorts: $400 stipend. Summer 2027: $2,000 stipend. Spring 2027 pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at Alameda High School. You can choose to enroll as early as 9th grade. The program page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Read the CTE brochure and watch the Try Out a Career videos on the program page. Then pick CTE classes when you choose your courses. The program page links to a district enrollment page.
notes: The program page does not describe the courses in each pathway or any work based learning. School office phone: 510-337-7022. Ask the CTE teachers if a class earns college credit.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. These are school classes.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school teens in grades 6 to 12. No experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the city registration page. Go to the meetings. Finish your scene prep. Work at least two event nights. Help clean up after.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Building, 2203 Central Ave. The haunted house is at South Shore Mall. Questions: call 510-747-7529 or 510-747-7575, or email arpd@alamedaca.gov. The program page does not give event dates or a fee.
pay_detail: Volunteer. You can earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education programs.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.
duration: One afternoon
pay_detail: Free to attend. The fair covers part-time jobs and internships, but the page does not say if they are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens. The program page does not give ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Open the Underground Teen Center page. Use the Alameda Youth Committee link to sign up online with the city.
notes: Ages, grades, meeting times and any fee are not stated on the program page. Call City Hall at 510-747-7400 to ask. The same page describes the Underground Teen Center, where the After Dark program is for middle and high school teens.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not list pay or a fee.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 by the first day of the event (October 3 in 2026).
how_to_apply: New volunteers apply online. If you hear nothing in 30 days, email the Navigator Manager listed on the FAQ page.
notes: You pay your own travel and housing. Most teams stand and walk for long hours outdoors.
duration: Nine morning sessions, from the first Saturday in October to the second Sunday in October.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Uniform pack, event admission and parking, access to the Navigator tent.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. You must pass a City of Albuquerque background check before you start.
how_to_apply: Send the online volunteer application. You must also attend a full-day orientation in late May (it was May 30 in 2026). The education team tells you about openings and training.
notes: The page also says 16 years or older in one place and 16 to 18 in another. Costs for the teen are gas and lunch. Shifts are mornings, afternoons or full days. A recommendation letter can be requested after finishing.
duration: At least 40 hours (10 shifts) over seven weeks, June 1 to July 25 (2026 session)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get free BioPark admission, discounts and a certificate after 40 hours.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors ages 16 to 19.
how_to_apply: Apply online in March. Use the BioPark internship page.
notes: Interns work with an animal care team or a plant team. Volunteer coordinator for other teen roles: 505-848-7142.
duration: 8 consecutive weeks, Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026: June 1 to July 24)
pay_detail: $5,000 stipend, paid in two halves at week 4 and week 8

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who can pass a City of Albuquerque background check.
how_to_apply: Send in the online volunteer form. Pass a background check. Go to the online open house. Then go to a 2 day orientation in person. Coordinator: 505-848-7142.
notes: Uniform colors are black, brown, khaki or white. Orientation days in 2026 were June 1 and 3 or June 2 and 5.
duration: 2026: June 1 to July 25. At least 40 volunteer hours over an eight-week period.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free BioPark admission, discounts, behind-the-scenes tours.

who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older who worked as a BioPark Nature Guide or Camp Counselor in a past year. Background check required.
how_to_apply: Call the Volunteer Coordinator at 505-768-3443 about openings. Then apply and pass a background check.
notes: You need earlier BioPark experience. This is a second step after Nature Guides.
duration: One semester. At least 6 hours a week between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Staff can fill out an evaluation form if your school needs one (give two days notice).

who_can_apply: The City page does not state a minimum age. The City's 2026 job fair listing says age 15 and up.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the City job site. Then fill out the other forms: a background check, a liability form and a student work form. Anyone under 18 also fills out a drug test consent form. Call a pool to set up an interview with the pool manager. Lifeguards must first pass the City water test.
notes: Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross lifeguard card, plus CPR and First Aid. They must pass the water test. They must do this before the pool manager interview.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Paid. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors interested in STEAM careers who can commit 10 to 20 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form. Ask a teacher, mentor or parent to send in a recommendation form.
notes: Explora is in Old Town Albuquerque.
duration: Two school years (junior and senior year), 10 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid internship. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form.
notes: The volunteer page lists a minimum age of 14.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Albuquerque high school students ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Apply in spring. Use the City's Jobs and Internships page. Questions? Call the Educational Initiatives Office at 505-767-5898.
notes: The school-year Job Mentor Program is a 9th to 12th grade elective that earns 0.5 elective credit each semester. The page says interns earn minimum wage.
duration: 7 weeks, up to 25 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid. Wage not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their junior or senior year, and recent graduates, who live in the Albuquerque metro area. The page lists no age.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The City's Youth Connect page lists it with an age of 17 and up, so ask the City before you apply.
notes: Partners named on the page: National Hispanic Cultural Center, Tricklock Theatre, the Public Library, the Balloon Museum and National Institute of Flamenco. The City's list says age 17 and up. The program page has a grade rule. They do not match.
duration: Summer. Length not stated.
pay_detail: Paid. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: You must be in high school now (freshman to senior). You speak for communities across the City. The page gives no minimum or maximum age. The City's Youth Connect list shows ages 14 and up.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to MYAC link on the City's Youth Connect page. The page gives no further steps.
notes: Meetings were on Zoom in Sept 2026.
duration: Meets quarterly (Sept, Dec, March, June), first Wednesday, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 who are entering 7th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the program page. Questions go to the Junior Docent Coordinator, Sioux Rivera. The page says applications are closed.
notes: Unpaid and costs $175. The 2026 session had a required training week June 1 to 5. Contact is the Junior Docent Coordinator listed on the program page. Applications were closed on the page when checked.
duration: Training week June 1 to 5. Work period June 8 to July 31 (2026 session). Typical commitment is two 4-hour shifts a week.
pay_detail: Teens pay a $175 fee. Limited financial help is available.

who_can_apply: Students 16 and older.
how_to_apply: Email the museum's Volunteer Coordinator. The email is on the program page. No separate form is described.
notes: Hours depend on your schedule and the museum's needs. Events named on the page include STEM Day and Nuclear Science Week. The program page does not say whether applications are open. Ask about pay when you write.
duration: At least 12 weeks, full time or part time
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and older can volunteer without a parent or guardian, unless it is a school or group activity. Younger teens and kids must come with an adult.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the online sign-up portal for individuals and families. Pick an open date and time. You get a confirmation email. Groups of five or more fill out a group form at least 3 weeks ahead.
notes: Teens under 16 can join with an adult. Children 8 and up can help in the warehouse with enough adults. Children must be 12 or older to work in the clean rooms. Wear closed-toe shoes and no tank tops.
duration: Shifts are 2 hours long, on weekdays and Saturdays.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: At least 16 years old. Full-time enrolled high school students with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 for research, technical or business jobs (2.5 for clerical or laborer jobs). Some jobs need U.S. citizenship.
how_to_apply: Make a username on Sandia's careers site. Filter for Student jobs. Apply to each internship on its own. A student guide PDF is linked on the page.
notes: Minimum age is 16 per the page. Listings change, so check the careers tool for current postings.
duration: Summer or year round. During the school year, high school students work up to 25 hours a week.
pay_detail: Competitive pay. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: June option: kids going into 8th, 9th or 10th grade. 8th and 9th graders get priority. July option, where you live on campus: kids going into 11th or 12th grade. Students 16 and older get priority. You need a computer at home or time on site for homework.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add a personal statement of 400 to 500 words. Ask one math or science teacher to email a recommendation. Email your latest unofficial transcript. Packets that are not complete are not accepted.
notes: The page says room and board might be covered for the July residential option. The program page lists a phone number and email for help with the application.
duration: June option: June 1 to 12. July residential option: June 22 to July 17 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Tuition, lunches and materials are covered in the June option. Students get a small stipend after finishing. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Volunteers can be as young as 16. The page lists the 16 year minimum for Guest Services at UNM Sandoval Regional Medical Center.
how_to_apply: Fill out the youth application. Then have an interview with the Guest Services team. You also get a tuberculosis screening and go to orientation. The page lists phone numbers to call, one for the Sandoval hospital and one for UNM Hospital.
notes: The page does not list a minimum age for volunteering at the main UNM Hospital, so call that office to ask. The listed steps are for Guest Services at the Sandoval hospital.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: New Mexico residents with a valid SSN or ITIN (used for payment only). You need an interest in a health career and leadership. The page says juniors and seniors, and also lists rising sophomores.
how_to_apply: Use the online form. You send a student application, a profile with short essays and one recommendation form.
notes: The page does not state an age. It says it focuses on health equity in African American communities and other communities of color. The page still showed the 2026 cycle when checked. Confirm the next dates.
duration: One week (June 15 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: A stipend after you finish. The amount is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The 2024 cohort was youth ages 14 to 22. Rules for 2027 are not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Email programs@workingclassroom.org to get on the list for the 2027 program.
notes: Ages and hours come from the first (2024) cohort. Confirm the 2027 rules.
duration: 2024 cohort: 300 hours over 8 months
pay_detail: Paid. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students. Exact ages and residency rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Call YDI at 505-352-3466 about this program, or 505-977-3216 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.), or email ccordova@ydinm.org.
notes: Only five young people are hired each summer, so it is very small. Ask YDI about the age rule.
duration: June to mid-August
pay_detail: Paid summer employment. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. Residents of Albuquerque and Bernalillo County. Other rules not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Email youthbuild@ydinm.org. Office: 3411 Candelaria Rd. NE, Suite D, Albuquerque.
notes: The page calls this the final class, so check that a cohort is still open.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 25. Each youth must register. Parents do not need to register.
how_to_apply: Register on the fair page for the youth who will attend.
notes: The 2026 page listed jobs by the youngest age. Aquatics aide and lifeguard: 15 and up. Community center recreation leader: 16 and up. Library teen volunteer: 13 to 17, a younger age range than the fair's 14 to 25 invitation. BioPark education volunteer: 14 and up. Dates are for the 2026 fair.
duration: One day
pay_detail: Event is free. Jobs listed there are paid; pay not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 can apply to volunteer. The Teen Advisory Group is for ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application online. Go to a Teen Volunteer Orientation. The dates are on the library events page. Use an email that is not from your school. You can write to volunteer@alexlibraryva.org.
notes: The page was last updated in March 2025. Confirm the age range and orientation dates by email. Volunteers cannot lead story times.
duration: No required hours listed
pay_detail: Unpaid. Service hours can be earned.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, in middle or high school, who live in the City of Alexandria. You must be allowed to work in the U.S. Your household must get SNAP, Medicaid, TANF or free or reduced lunch. Or its income must be at or below 130% of the poverty line. Students with an IEP can also qualify.
how_to_apply: Send the Smartsheet youth application one time, with all your papers. You need proof of an Alexandria address, proof you can work, proof of income or benefits, and a photo ID. Some students with benefits need only three papers.
notes: Forms that are not complete, or sent more than once, can slow or hurt your application. Questions: DCHSSummerYouth@alexandriava.gov or 703-746-5940 (4850 Mark Center Drive, Floor 6). The page does not mention work permits.
duration: 6 weeks (June 22 to July 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Paid; rate and weekly hours not stated on the program page (a city video page says 20 to 30 hours per week)

who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. The page says internships are open to all ages, including high schoolers. No minimum age is stated for teen volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then meet a staff member for an interview and training. Interns use a different form. Teen Advisory Board members use their own form.
notes: Alive says it runs free drop-in hours after school and over the summer, plus teen-led clubs. Locations named on the site are Naperville, Aurora and Hanover Park. The page says internships are open to all ages, including high schoolers.
duration: Teen volunteer hours are not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get service hours for volunteering. Internships are non-paid.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th graders, 12th graders and post-secondary students. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Apply during the window; the process includes an interview. The page encourages students to attend a performance and check back next year. Contact: collision.project@alliancetheatre.org or 404-733-4700.
notes: Free thanks to the Palefsky family. Exact dates were not printed on the application page, only the January to mid-April range. The Alliance also lists a year-long Teen Ensemble, but its current page was not read so it is not listed.
duration: 3 weeks, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily (June 29 to July 17 in 2026, with performances July 17 and 18)
pay_detail: Free to all participants. No stipend mentioned.

who_can_apply: School year: students who have started 10th grade or are at least 16. Summer: students at least 14.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Junior Application. Contact Chasity Drees. Chasity Drees is the Volunteer Coordinator. Email cdrees@altru.org. Or call 701.780.5125.
notes: The page does not mention shots or background checks. Ask the coordinator what is needed before you start.
duration: At least one shift a week, 2 to 4 hours, for at least one semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth in 8th through 12th grade, both 4-H members and non-members. Check the program page for exactly how grade level is counted.
how_to_apply: Register in 4-H Online and pick a session track. Fill out the financial help form by the same date if you need it.
notes: Tracks in 2026 were Choose Your Adventure, Animal Science Roundup, MVP Leadership, Mission Moon and Horticulture. Cancel by June 1 for a full refund. After that there are no refunds.
duration: 3 days (June 23 to 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: $260 for 4-H members and $275 for non-members in 2026. Financial help is offered.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their junior or senior year. The page says 'All students are welcome.'
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer 2027 Interest Form on the page. It tells you when applications open. Then register online. You ask for financial help on the registration form.
notes: The page only says applications open 'in January'. No exact opening day is known. Dates are marked tentative on the page.
duration: One week. Tentative 2027 sessions: July 11 to 15 and July 18 to 22.
pay_detail: The page lists $450 through June 26 or $500 for late registration (this may be last year's price). It covers housing, meals, a t-shirt and on-campus costs. You can ask for financial help on the registration form.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. No school or city rule is stated for these year-round roles.
how_to_apply: Fill out an application and book a free fingerprint check with the Volunteer Coordinator. Call 714-765-4994 or email VolunteerOffice@anaheim.net. Some roles also need a TB test from the last 2 years.
notes: Fingerprinting is free, but you pay for your own TB test. The page does not post open shifts, so ask the coordinator which roles need help now. Court ordered hours go to the Graffiti Removal Program instead (714-765-5158).
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21. If you are 15, you must have finished 8th grade. You must keep a GPA of 2.0 or higher and be able to run, lift, climb and crawl.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Fire Explorers Interest Form on the program page. You will be told when spots open. Email FireExplorer@anaheim.net with questions.
notes: Spots go first to Public Safety Pathways grads. Then to Anaheim residents. Then to Anaheim students. Explorers do not enter burning buildings. They do not replace firefighters.
duration: Meetings every other Tuesday, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 21. The page also says you must be a current 7th to 12th grade student. Keep a 2.0 GPA or higher and good attendance. You must never have been arrested and must not use drugs. You must be able to run and do push-ups and sit-ups.
how_to_apply: Email Explorers@anaheim.net to say you are interested. Go to 4 meetings in a row as a guest, in business casual clothes. Then fill out an application. You must pass a written test, an interview and a background check.
notes: Meetings are at the Anaheim Police Department. Academies are held twice a year, often at a military base, and are strict, with drills and exercise. Every Explorer must go to at least one. Questions: Youth Engagement Coordinator, 714-765-1928. The city volunteer page links to an old Explorer page that is gone, so use the police site.
duration: Weekly meetings, Wednesdays 6 to 8:30 p.m., plus at least one 4 day academy
pay_detail: Unpaid. The department pays for most of the uniform. You buy a few items, like shoes and a flashlight.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 years old and in high school.
how_to_apply: Pick a branch on the program page. Contact the coordinator listed for that branch. Each branch has its own contact and its own rules.
notes: An accepted application does not promise hours. Hours are given out as needed. The library does not give court-ordered service hours. The Mobile Library (Bookmobile and STEAM Van) takes summer applications in April and needs volunteers 2 to 6 p.m. on at least one Monday to Thursday. The Teen Podcast takes applications at the start of fall.
duration: At least 2 hours a week at Central Library and Canyon Hills
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 years old. Space is small. Anaheim residents and Anaheim students go first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need a TB clearance slip from the last two years. Book a free fingerprint appointment at City Hall. Pick a VolunTEEN orientation date. Choose your program, site and weeks. Sign the waivers.
notes: You pay for your own TB test. Fingerprinting is free. Bring a photo ID to the fingerprint appointment. Last cycle, site assignments were emailed by May 30. Questions: Volunteer Coordinator, 714-765-4994. The city also lists other volunteer jobs for ages 13 and up. Examples are trail work at Oak Canyon Nature Center and youth sports coach assistants.
duration: Weeks you choose when you apply
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a letter that confirms your community service hours.

who_can_apply: In-person volunteer roles are for ages 16 and up. At-home projects are a good option for anyone under 16. Vet clinic support is 18 and up. School service roles need an agreement signed by a parent and a teacher.
how_to_apply: Dog Care, Cat Care, Shelter Support and School Service Hours are open as of 2026-10-10. Wildlife is closed and Clinic Support is full. Sign up on the volunteer page for the role you want. You also take a short online Safety and Protocols training and pay the $35 membership fee. For school hours, use the School Service page.
notes: Animal care roles ask for at least six months. The page says Shelter Support is not eligible for court-ordered service hours. Sites include South Elgin, Bloomingdale Petco, Algonquin Petco and Geneva Petco. Others are the St. Charles office and Elburn Forest Preserve.
duration: Dog and cat care: at least 40 hours over 6 months, with weekly or every-other-week shifts. Animal care roles ask for at least six months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $35 volunteer membership fee for all opportunities.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who go to school in Michigan and play a string, wind, brass or percussion instrument (harp too). Pianists are not considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the A2SO site. Send a one take YouTube video of you playing one part of a solo piece with an accompanist.
notes: This is a contest, not a job. The page is for the 2026 contest. Expect similar timing next year, from August to late September.
duration: Final round Nov 7, 2026. Winner plays Feb 23, 2027.
pay_detail: $50 application fee (email jpepper@a2so.org if the fee is a problem). Prizes: $500 grand prize, $250 runner-up.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in Washtenaw County. Ages and grades are not stated on the page. The page does not say where the council meets.
how_to_apply: Application not open. Watch the Youth Council page in 2027. Contact: Community Investment Officer at (734) 663-0401 x116.
notes: One member also serves as a voting member of the foundation board. Pay and time commitment are not stated on the page.
duration: Time commitment not stated
pay_detail: Pay not stated

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. After review you are contacted with details on signing up for a required volunteer orientation, then you pick shifts.
notes: Older library posts mention a summer teen volunteer program. The current page only describes the year-round program. Michigan's Youth Employment Standards Act covers employers of anyone under 18, including volunteers. Ask the program if you need a work permit.
duration: Ongoing; you commit to the shifts you sign up for
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: You must live in Michigan and go to a Michigan high school. You must be close enough to travel to Ann Arbor. Rising juniors and seniors are best. Most students come from partner schools: Ypsilanti Community, Lincoln and Belleville. There is no GPA minimum.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest form. One letter of recommendation is required. The page does not describe the later steps.
notes: The page shows an Interest Form Closed button even though it says the form opens Oct 12, so check the page for the current status. Commuter program, so you live at home.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027. You must be on campus at least 35 of the 40 days.
pay_detail: $4,000 for taking part

who_can_apply: Teens 14 and older.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application or the 2026 printable PDF. Teens must also complete a work permit. The page says that from October 2, permits are done online in the Youth Employment Permit Portal (YEPP). Call Stacey at 734-475-8732 ext. 212.
notes: Chelsea is about 15 miles west of Ann Arbor. The library page says teen volunteers need a work permit even though the role is unpaid.
duration: Year-round. Hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older to volunteer alone at the warehouse or Community Kitchen. Younger kids can come with an adult. The warehouse takes ages 8 and up. The kitchen takes ages 12 and up.
how_to_apply: Create a user account with Individual Registration and sign up for shifts in advance; no walk-ins. If you need school hours signed or an observer will attend, call the volunteer coordinator first.
notes: Not teen-specific, but a steady way for teens 14 and up to earn volunteer hours. Warehouse work involves moderate lifting. Groups of four or more use a separate group form. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Single shifts; you can volunteer as often as you like
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High-school-aged youth who live in Ypsilanti and the surrounding townships. For the summer, you must have finished 9th grade and cannot miss more than 4 days. The school-year program is for teens who finished the summer program in good standing.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Youth and Schools page when applications open. Questions: Jenny Pritchett, jenny@growinghope.net.
notes: Michigan requires a work permit for workers under 18. From Oct 2, 2026 permits come through the state Youth Employment Permit Portal.
duration: Summer 2027: June 15 to Aug 6, Monday to Thursday, 9 AM to 2:30 PM. After school: Sept to May, Tue/Wed/Thu, 4 to 6 PM.
pay_detail: $14 an hour, plus free weekly produce bags in the growing season.

who_can_apply: The page says community volunteers include high school and college students, corporate partners and retirees. It does not state a minimum age. Ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: For the Hands-On Museum, email volunteer@aahom.org. For wildlife volunteering at Leslie Science & Nature Center, fill out the application linked on the page. Or email volunteer@lesliesnc.org.
notes: The page is short. It gives no age rule, hours, training or start dates, so email first. The Hands-On Museum's old address (aahom.org/volunteer) now sends you to this page. The Leslie wildlife application link goes to a file named Adult_Volunteer_Application.pdf, so ask Leslie before a teen applies for wildlife work.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 (must be 12 before registering). Those about to turn 18 within 6 months may prefer the adult orientation.
how_to_apply: Online registration only, which opens about 30 days before each session. You must attend all six classes; there are no make-ups, refunds or transfers. A waitlist is available.
notes: Demand is higher than space, so you may wait months. After training you volunteer without a parent present. Inactive for 6 months or more means retaking the training. Shelter is at 3100 Cherry Hill Rd, Ann Arbor. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: 6 training sessions, then a 2 to 4 hour per month volunteer commitment
pay_detail: $205 program fee for the 6 session training (training, T-shirt, supplies). Limited scholarships for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. Beginners are welcome.
how_to_apply: Register online on the Film Camp page. Questions: Holly Behrend, hbehrend@marquee-arts.org.
notes: This camp costs money. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates.
duration: 2026 dates: June 29 to July 3, July 6 to 10 and 13 to 15, and July 20 to 24
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $576.25 for session 1, $901.25 for session 2, $576.25 for session 3, or $1,901.25 for all sessions.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. You live in Hillsdale, Jackson, Lenawee, Livingston or Washtenaw County.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page and choose your county.
notes: This prepares you for internships. It is a course, not a job. The same agency runs SummerWorks, a paid summer program, for Washtenaw County.
duration: 4 weeks per cohort
pay_detail: The course is free. Eligible participants can earn cash incentives for finishing it. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Any teen of high school age. It is best to sign up ahead, but you can sign up when you come.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen sign up form on the website or sign up when you come. Questions: Hananiah Wiggins, hananiah@neutral-zone.org, (734) 214-9995.
notes: This is a free teen center, not a paid job. Future Corps for high schoolers meets the first Monday of each month, 4 to 6 PM, and helps with first-job support. Neutral Zone is at 310 E Washington St, Ann Arbor.
duration: Weekly programs all school year
pay_detail: Free. Donations are welcome.

who_can_apply: High-risk youth ages 13 to 18 in Washtenaw County.
how_to_apply: Not stated for this program. The page lists the Drop-In Center at (734) 485-2222 and a contact form at ozonehouse.org/contact-us/.
notes: The page also lists a monthly Career Panel for youth 13 to 20. It is the third Thursday at 5 PM at the Ypsilanti Drop-In Center, and food is served. A Peer Outreach Worker team for youth 15 to 19 was coming back in winter. WorkZone paid internships are for ages 18 to 20.
duration: One week, offered twice a year at the Drop-In Center
pay_detail: All Ozone House services are free.

who_can_apply: The course is open to ages 15 and up. The page says you are prepared to be a lifeguard when you turn 16. Fifteen year olds who finish the course can join the city's Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program.
how_to_apply: Register for the course by calling 734-794-6237 or at Mack Indoor Pool (715 Brooks St., inside Ann Arbor Open School). Pool jobs are applied for online through the city's job board when posted.
notes: The lifeguard certification page says 15 year olds can join the Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program. The recertification section says 15 year olds can be eligible for a city lifeguard job. These two statements differ. Ask the pool at 734-794-6237 what age you can be hired. Michigan says minors must get a work permit before starting a job unless exempt. The permit comes through a Michigan school. See the state youth employment page. You get no refund of the course fee if you fail the course.
duration: Weekend course: Friday evening, Saturday and Sunday
pay_detail: Course fee $200, fully refunded if you pass, apply, are hired and start work at a city pool. Pay for pool jobs is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: The page says individuals and groups of all ages can volunteer. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Individuals use the online volunteer calendar and sign-up. Groups submit the Group Volunteer Inquiry form. Email a2parksevents@a2gov.org or call 734.794.6627.
notes: Ask staff whether a teen needs a parent signature. The page does not say.
duration: One-day to long-term. Group projects run April to October.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Rising 9th graders for Counselors in Training. High school students for counselor roles.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Call Peace Neighborhood Center at (734) 662-3564. 1111 N. Maple Rd., Ann Arbor.
notes: Ask whether the job is paid before you apply. The page also lists College and Career Prep for high school students, Monday to Thursday during the school year.
duration: Summer Youth Services runs eight weeks
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for most roles. Survey Squad is 16 and up. Ushers must be 18. The page says 12 and 13 year olds may volunteer with an adult volunteer. Volunteers work under the supervision of festival staff.
how_to_apply: Pick a volunteer role and a night on the A2SF volunteer sign-up page. Questions: call 734-994-5999.
notes: Seasonal: shifts are in the summer festival only. Usher spots for 2026 were closed. Check the page in spring for 2027 sign-up.
duration: Single shifts at the festival
pay_detail: Unpaid. Completed shifts earn perks such as access to special hospitality areas, and select benefits include tickets to some performances and prize giveaways.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when programming begins (you must turn 16 by June 1 of the program year) AND you live in, or attend school in, Washtenaw County. Participants may take part for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Online application (opens January): your contact info, parent or guardian contact, approximate household income, possible summer conflicts, and one reference who is not a relative. Accepted minors need a parent or guardian signature.
notes: A paid internship is not guaranteed: the site says a subset of participants is selected, though staff aim to match everyone. After acceptance you need I-9 identification documents and a bank account in your name for pay (this is for payroll, not a fee). Professional development is Tuesday or Wednesday evenings online, then Fridays 10am to 2pm in person from June. Michigan requires a work permit for minors under 18 to work; as of Oct 2, 2026 permits are issued through the state's Youth Employment Permit Portal, not schools. Contact: mail@summerworks.info.
duration: Program runs April to August; internship is 10 weeks between June and August
pay_detail: Internships pay $15 or $17 per hour depending on whether you have finished high school or an equivalent (employer FAQ). About 20 to 25 hours a week.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Ann Arbor and Livingston volunteer page (the link goes to the hospital's volunteer system at stjoemercyann.vsysweb.com). Then an interview, paperwork, health screening and a required orientation.
notes: Requirements listed for volunteers: interview, two TB skin tests, proof of varicella and MMR immunity, Tdap, this year's flu shot, health clearance form, one non-relative reference, and orientation; background checks apply to volunteers 18 and over. Also on the same page: The Farm at Trinity Health takes volunteers age 15 and up (no background check under 18). The Apply Now link is http, not https, so it is not in the apply_url field. Volunteer office phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Year-round roles with some seasonal placements (a summer teen cohort exists)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18. The commission has 21 members: 2 from each county district and 3 at-large.
how_to_apply: Email britt@neutral-zone.org. Ask when you can apply.
notes: Pay and meeting schedule are not stated on the page. Neutral Zone is at 310 E Washington St, Ann Arbor, phone (734) 214-9995.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students in the county school districts that run each program. The page says to contact your district CTE director or high school counselor. Other-district rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor or your district CTE director. The page does not list steps.
notes: Programs differ by school. Ann Arbor, Chelsea, Dexter, Lincoln, Manchester, Milan, Saline, Whitmore Lake and Ypsilanti each list their own. Washtenaw ISD phone: (734) 994-8100.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 enrolled in at least one high school class (or homeschooled) who show college-level skills. Seniors: GPA 2.5 or higher. Grades 10 and 11: SAT 480 or PSAT 460 or higher. Grades 9 to 12: or take the Accuplacer or a writing sample at WCC.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WCC application, set up your NetID, upload proof of academic level and the parent consent and principal or counselor approval forms from the dual enrollment packet, then register for classes. Call 734-973-3682 for help.
notes: The page does not list application deadlines or information night dates. It links to an Academic Dates page. WCC dual enrollment is not a job.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the page. Your high school may pay (it sends a billing form), or you pay or use a payment plan.

who_can_apply: Michigan residents. 8th graders (9th Grade Program) need passing grades in English, math, science and social studies. 9th graders (Middle College) need 1 credit each in English, math, science, social studies and electives by the end of the school year. 10th graders (Middle College) need 2 credits each in those subjects. Washtenaw County residents get priority.
how_to_apply: Go to an Admissions Informational Meeting first (6:00 to 7:30 PM on Dec 1, 2026; Jan 19, Feb 1, Feb 10 online, Feb 18 online, 2027). Then use the online application. Placement tests follow if you are admitted.
notes: Admissions office phone: (734) 677-5360. General line: 734-973-3300. This is a school program, not a job. The admissions page does not mention tuition, fees or books, so confirm the no-cost claim by calling the admissions office.
duration: Several years of high school
pay_detail: The page says graduates finish without paying tuition, fees or books.

who_can_apply: The Youth Volunteer Corps is for teens ages 11 to 17. Ages for the other youth volunteer roles are not stated on the page. Youth sports coaches must be at least 14.
how_to_apply: Use the Begin your application button on the volunteering page. Questions: volunteer@annarborymca.org.
notes: The page's own link to a Youth Volunteer Corps page was a dead link when checked, so details of YVC projects and dates are not confirmed. The Y also lists other volunteer roles that appear aimed at adults. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Varies: one-off service projects or ongoing roles
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Corps form on the page when it opens in late April, then attend a one-hour training. A work permit is provided at orientation. Phone: 734-482-4110.
notes: The library says teens need a work permit even for this volunteer role. Michigan rules cover volunteers under 18. Permits now go through the state Youth Employment Permit Portal (since Oct 2, 2026).
duration: Summer. Hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Create Your Own Project is for grades 10 to 12. The page gives no grade rule for the Teen Advisory Group.
how_to_apply: Use the TAG application, the event volunteer sign-up form or the project proposal form linked on the page. Teen Librarian Assistant spots are full, so that form puts you on a waitlist. Phone: 734-482-4110.
notes: The library says TAG members must fill out a work permit. Pokemon card game helpers meet Thursdays 5 to 6 PM starting October 1.
duration: Teen Librarian Assistant: one hour weekly or every other week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 16. Applicants complete an online application and an on-site interview, then required trainings. Both a parent and the teen sign liability forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during an open window, attend an interview, then the online and on-site training days.
notes: Spring and Fall sessions are weekends only; Summer shifts run seven days a week. The Aquarium also lists other youth roles for ages 11 to 18 (Ocean Neighbors, Teen Science Cafe Volunteer, Student Eco-Ambassadors). The Education Volunteer role is for ages 16 and up with at least 100 hours in six months.
duration: 60 hours over a 10-week session (Spring, Summer or Fall), one shift a day each week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program (60 service hours).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who want to build skills, get work experience, or start a career. The program page does not list other rules or the counties served.
how_to_apply: Call 303-636-1260 and leave a voicemail. Or fill out the Support Assessment Form on the Connecting Colorado website. You can also use the Training Interest Form on the program page.
notes: Arapahoe/Douglas Works! has its main office in Centennial. Ask which county rules apply to you. Douglas County teens 15 to 17 can also look at the DCYEP program.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list exact ages. The library teen section is for ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Teen Volunteer Application on the page. The page lists drop in volunteer events at Koelbel and Smoky Hill libraries.
notes: Each branch Teen Advisory Board meets monthly to talk about trends and plan events.
duration: Semester and summer volunteer options
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 living in Cherokee, Clayton, Douglas, Fayette, Gwinnett, Henry or Rockdale County. In-school or out-of-school youth who face a barrier such as offender history, homelessness, foster care, parenting, disability or being a basic-skills-deficient or English learner diploma holder.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Contact the provider for your county. Clayton: 770-997-4511 (640 Hwy 138 SW, Riverdale). Gwinnett: 404-913-0769 (3805 Crestwood Pkwy NW, Suite 300, Duluth). Cherokee: 770-345-5483. Henry: 404-913-0769. Douglas: 770-997-4511. Fayette: 770-910-7733. Rockdale: 770-991-7608.
notes: This is the only Gwinnett and Clayton county youth workforce program found. The City of Atlanta, Fulton, DeKalb and Cobb are not on this page's county list; see their own entries. Providers named on the page: Cherokee Youth Works and Hearts to Nourish Hope. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either. The page does not mention wages, stipends or work experience pay.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Center, Del Campo, El Camino Fundamental or Inderkum High School who meet federal rules for financial need and/or being first in the family to go to college, and want to go beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Upward Bound application, then staff review eligibility and interview the student and family if eligible. Contact arctrioub@arc.losrios.edu or (916) 484-8033 (Mon to Fri, 9 am to 6 pm).
notes: Only for students at the four listed partner schools. Summer participation is required. The dedicated application page did not show details when read. Ask staff for current dates.
duration: Year-round, including a required summer component
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Your local Extension office helps you join.
how_to_apply: Call your local Extension office. Then make a profile to join as a youth member.
notes: Also open to younger kids; teen parts are the leader roles. State programs listed include a teen leadership group, shooting sports, STEM projects and a camp on 55 acres of pine forest. Dates were not posted on the program pages.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county office about fees.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page states no age or residency rule for the teen services.
how_to_apply: Write your resume with the template, then apply for jobs on the Teen Job Board (hosted on Indeed). Book 1-on-1 resume or mock interview sessions through the Microsoft Forms link on the page.
notes: In Virginia, 14 and 15 year olds must have a work permit (Youth Employment Certificate) to work; under 14 cannot get one. The page links the state Department of Labor and Industry portal. The separate Youth Employment Program on the same site is for ages 18 to 24, not teens.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Pay depends on the employer. Services are free.

who_can_apply: Summer Volunteer Squad is for teens going into grades 7 to 12. You must live in Arlington Heights.
how_to_apply: Use the volunteer application link on the library volunteer page. New Middle School Panel members sign up on the page.
notes: There is also a Tween Advisory Group for grades 4 to 6, which is for younger kids.
duration: Summer for the Squad. The Middle School Volunteer Panel meets monthly during the school year, over snacks. Check the library calendar for dates.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 entering grades 10 to 12. Must be an Arlington resident.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open in early March. To find the form, search for the name Arlingteens Leaders on the arlingtonva.us site. Look for the one that says teens.
notes: Dates above are from the 2026 flyer; check the page in March for 2027. Contact: 703-228-3329.
duration: Two weeks (July 20 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Lunch is provided on the first and last day.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 by May 1 and at least two years older than the oldest camper at the site. Works at county run camps only.
how_to_apply: Sign up in the county system with a household account. It is a free volunteer activity. Finish the ePACT paperwork. Pick your sessions and camp sites. If you are new, sign up for an interview. Email campvol@arlingtonva.us.
notes: Registration opened Feb 18, 2026 and closed when full. The page gives no 2027 dates yet.
duration: At least 2 consecutive weeks per assignment, no more than 8 hours a day
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to register.

who_can_apply: Arlington County youth ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: The page has no application steps. Email Linh Nghe, Prevention Director, at lnghe@arlingtonva.us to ask about joining.
notes: Ask about service hours or a stipend; the page does not say.
duration: Meets the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month in the school year, 6:30 to 8:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 and a half years old. The page lists this rule for all volunteers and links a separate Teen Volunteer Application.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Volunteer Application (Google form on the page). Questions: armc-volunteers@armc.sbcounty.gov or Volunteer Management, 400 N. Pepper Avenue, Colton, CA 92324.
notes: Minimum age is 14 and a half. The page lists no application deadline or start dates.
duration: At least 100 hours; one 2-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who start tasks on their own. You like the arts and feel at ease with kids.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Sign Up link on the volunteer page, which opens a Google Form. You can also call the Armory at (626) 792-5101.
notes: Hours and session dates are not on the page. The Armory's Fall Studio 2026 classes are on a separate page.
duration: Each Studio session (hours not listed)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 years old. Students can join one week, all six or any number of weeks.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the registration link on the Teen Academy page. Questions: Office of Engagement.
notes: Courses change every week. Students agree to the handbook rules when they sign up. The Teen Academy page does not mention scholarships; ask the Office of Engagement.
duration: Six weeks of themed courses (2026: June 1 to July 24)
pay_detail: $185 per one-week course (Week 3 is $148). Morning (9 to 11:30 a.m.) and afternoon (12:30 to 3 p.m.) courses.

who_can_apply: Adults 18 and up. Teens must be at least 16 years old when they apply.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-437-5500.
notes: You need at least 50 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.
duration: One 4 hour shift a week (minimum 4 hours of service each week)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Adults 18 and up. Teens must be at least 16 years old when they apply.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Then go to an interview. You also need a health screening and a criminal background check. You need orientation papers and training on site. Phone: 847-755-8708.
notes: You need at least 100 volunteer hours before you can ask for written proof of hours (for school or court). Uniform and ID badge are required whenever you volunteer.
duration: 4 hours a week, at least 100 hours over 6 continuous months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Young women and men in grades 7 to 12. You must work at least 30 hours a year. Meetings and events count toward hours.
how_to_apply: Call 949-645-6929 to ask how to join. The chapter volunteer page has an Adult Member Application. Ask the chapter whether teens can use it.
notes: Membership costs are not stated on the program page. The thrift shop and office are at 2220 Fairview Road, Costa Mesa. Awards go to those with 50, 75 and 100 or more hours a year. Events include a spring luncheon and a June Senior Medallion Event.
duration: Monthly meetings in the school year. At least 30 hours a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12. No minimum GPA is required, but the page says students should show a GPA of 2.7 or higher.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Call 480-727-4948 or use the contact details on the program page.
notes: Students must stay on campus for the whole program. Meals are provided. Next dates are not stated on the program page.
duration: One week on the ASU Tempe campus
pay_detail: Free for all students. There is no cost to apply.

who_can_apply: Students entering grade 11 or 12. No minimum GPA is required, but the page recommends a GPA of 2.7 or higher.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Call 480-727-4948 or use the contact details on the program page.
notes: This is a residential program on the ASU campus. The deposit is not refunded. Next dates are not stated on the program page.
duration: Four days on the ASU Tempe campus
pay_detail: Accepted students pay a $50 deposit that is not refunded. The page lists no other fees.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors and seniors. You need a 3.25 unweighted GPA and A or B grades in high school math and science. You must qualify for Arizona in-state tuition and have lived in Arizona for the last 2 years.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You will need financial information from a parent or guardian. Upload a one page personal or career statement. Upload an unofficial high school transcript. Have one recommender send a letter on school letterhead.
notes: The program page lists 2027 dates. Its Spanish section shows 2026 dates for the first and last program days, so confirm the dates with the program.
duration: About 6 weeks. The 2027 program is June 6 to July 16.
pay_detail: Free for students in 2026: tuition, room and board, and class materials. The 2027 page lists no fee.

who_can_apply: Arizona high school juniors. Picks look at leadership. They look at community service, grades, and family income. They also ask if you are first in your family to go to college.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. A recommendation is optional. A teacher can write it. So can another person who works in education. It uses an online form.
notes: The page names both a 2026 application and a summer 2027 group. Confirm the year and deadlines with the program at 480-965-5187.
duration: Online June 14 to 18, 2027, then a Tempe campus visit on June 21, 2027
pay_detail: Free to students who apply and are selected.

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade who live in Georgia.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link for the institute on the 21st Century Leaders site. Spots are limited and some students go on a waitlist. Acceptance comes by email, so check spam.
notes: Expect applications to open around January again, as they did last year. The same group runs Leadership Connect all year. It is online and self-paced. Seniors who finish 3 levels can get a paid summer internship and a scholarship.
duration: About one week, residential (overnight)
pay_detail: Applying is free. The page says some institutes, including SYLI, may cost to attend, and that financial aid is available. The price is not listed.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in the Atlanta area.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City of Atlanta jobs website when the posting is open. You may be asked to interview, then you go to orientation. Every participant is matched with a mentor.
notes: This is the airport's own summer job program, separate from the Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program. The 2026 City of Atlanta job posting linked from the page was no longer showing. Questions: atlworkforce@atl.com.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Paid. The page does not state a rate.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Clayton County, Fulton County, or Atlanta city public schools.
how_to_apply: Ask the work-based learning teacher or the counselor at your school. You can also apply on your own on the City of Atlanta jobs site.
notes: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning Coordinator first, since credit comes through your school. The airport's Registered Apprenticeship is for ages 18 and up, so it is not listed here. Questions: atlworkforce@atl.com.
pay_detail: Paid, part-time. The page does not state a rate.

who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older by June 2 of the summer.
how_to_apply: Submit the online SPEAK application and have a non-relative adult submit a recommendation form. Attend a 2-hour group interview and the mandatory training day. If you also apply to the paid internship, only the internship application is needed.
notes: Application window usually closes March 1 (2026 pattern). The page gives no 2027 dates yet.
duration: 50 hours between June 2 and July 24 (2026), including a required 6-hour training day. Shifts Tuesday to Sunday in 2-hour blocks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: 16 or older by June 2 of the summer, and a rising sophomore, junior or senior at a Metro Atlanta Title I school. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the internship application and have a non-relative adult (teacher, mentor or boss) submit the recommendation form. Group interview at the Garden, then virtual orientation with a guardian. Questions: lboren@atlantabg.org.
notes: Only for students at Metro Atlanta Title I schools. Work is outside in all weather and includes lifting 40 lbs. Applying here also covers the SPEAK volunteer program. The Garden's Gainesville site has its own separate teen program.
duration: 7 weeks (June 2 to July 16 in 2026), 18 hours a week, Tuesday through Thursday
pay_detail: $12 per hour, paid every two weeks.

who_can_apply: Students 15 to 17 in 10th or 11th grade who are doing well in school. Selection uses nominations from schools, ABL members and community partners. A parent must approve the application.
how_to_apply: The student fills out the application linked on the program page. A parent or guardian approves it. Call 404-584-8126 to ask about dates and nominations.
notes: Pay, dates, cost and site locations are not listed, so call to confirm first. Atlanta Business League is at 931 Martin Luther King Jr. Dr. NW. The summer season is from the program name on search results, not the page; confirm.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Summit Trail Apartments are for young adults ages 17 to 24. The page does not list ages for the drop-in center.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Need Housing Support form on the CHRIS 180 page, or call 404-486-9034 or 1-800-896-4106. The team says it will reach out privately. Main office: 1030 Fayetteville Road, Atlanta.
notes: Support and housing, not a job. Call to ask about ages for the drop-in center, hours and where it is. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: Cost is not listed.

who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. For dual enrollment, you must be on track to graduate and have a 2.0 GPA. Early College Essentials and Cybersecurity need a 2.6 HOPE GPA and grade 11 or 12.
how_to_apply: Take the YouScience career quiz (recommended). Talk to your school counselor. Then submit the online application. Students with an IEP or 504 plan also need a team review.
notes: Career paths include HVAC, Culinary Arts, Dental Science and Patient Care. Atlanta Technical College runs the dual enrollment paths. They include Carpentry and Cybersecurity. The page lists more. You can be denied if there is no room or you miss the minimums.
duration: Part of the school day: morning group 9:15 to 11:30 am, afternoon group 12:30 to 2:45 pm
pay_detail: School program. The page does not mention pay. Dual enrollment is through Atlanta Technical College.

who_can_apply: Volunteers 8 and up at most ongoing projects. Anyone under 18 must come with an adult chaperone who stays the whole shift. Groups need 1 adult for every 4 youth ages 8 to 11 and 1 adult for every 8 youth ages 12 to 17. Adults register for shifts themselves.
how_to_apply: An adult signs up for a shift on the volunteer calendar. Then email volunteers@acfb.org or call 404-419-1727 to add the youth to the registration. Groups of 8 or more fill out a group request form.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Wear closed-toe, closed-heel shoes. Stay for the whole shift. Come on time because late volunteers more than 30 minutes cannot serve. Special events may have other age rules.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who have completed 9th grade and want to learn about health care careers. The page lists no residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form online. Add a photo of your face, your shot records, and two forms. A parent or guardian signs one of them. Then take a career quiz online and do an interview. Not everyone gets in.
notes: The page says it is closed for now. If you get in, you need a TB blood test before you start. In 2026 they held free online help hours two days a week while the form was open. Late or missing forms may not be read.
duration: 7 weeks. In 2026 it ran May 26 to July 14, plus 20 hours of virtual learning labs and 40 hours of community engagement a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says TELP is an unpaid educational program and you get documentation of your service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students who excel in science and are interested in research. The minimum age is 16. Competitive.
how_to_apply: Online application form, then an interview. You may not miss any starred program dates and may miss at most one week of lab time.
notes: Funding for 2026 came from the Army Educational Outreach Program, so the dates and stipend can change from year to year. Bring your own meals and get yourself to downtown Atlanta daily. No housing is provided. Join the ION email list on the home page to hear about 2027.
duration: About 6 weeks, 40 hours a week. In 2026 it ran June 22 to a symposium on August 6.
pay_detail: Stipend. The 2025 rate was $4,500; the page says the 2026 rate was not guaranteed. MARTA passes or parking may be reimbursed.

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed 9th, 10th, 11th, or 12th grade before class starts. In-person courses also require you to be at least 16 by the start of class, with no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Register and pay in the GSU Marketplace Mall store linked from the Registration page. No essay or application.
notes: Online courses are open to younger high schoolers who are under 16. Sign up for the program's newsletter on the home page to hear when the 2027 schedule is posted.
duration: 4 or 5 days per course. In person 9:30 AM to 3:45 PM, online 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. 2026 courses ran June 1 to July 23.
pay_detail: Costs $275 to $350 per course in 2026. Fee help is available if you qualify for free or reduced lunch (documentation required). Email NeuroscienceSchool@gsu.edu.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Participating sites listed: Adams, Bessie Branham, C. T. Martin, Dunbar, Grove Park, Martin Luther King Jr., Peachtree Hills, Pittman, Rosel Fann, Thomasville, William Walker, Zaban, @Promise South and @Promise MLK. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register for the Atlanta Teen Leader Program. The catalog lists atlantaga.gov/iparcs as the City registration site for its programs. Confirm the steps with your nearest participating recreation center.
notes: Source is the City's 2026 summer catalog, so it does not say which summer the Dec 31, 2026 registration cutoff is for. Ages and pay for the actual summer jobs are not stated. Georgia requires a work permit for any job under 16. The City's iParcs page blocked automated reading.
duration: The 2026 Teen Leaders Summer Academy ran June 8 to July 24, Monday to Friday.
pay_detail: Teen Leader activities are free. Pay for the summer employment program is not stated in the catalog.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at an APS high school that offers the Mentorship and Internship classes. You do not have to be labeled gifted. Your school picks the students.
how_to_apply: There is no separate form on the page. Ask your guidance counselor whether your school offers the class, or call the gifted office at 404-802-7585. The coordinator matches you using a career survey from early fall.
notes: The coordinator matches students to internships after a career survey in early fall. Students and families arrange their own rides. You must finish the fall Mentorship course first.
duration: Fall mentorship class, then a 60-hour one-on-one spring internship that begins in January and concludes with the Capstone Celebration in April. Hours per week and days are not stated.
pay_detail: The page does not say whether you get pay or school credit. It calls Mentorship and Internship classes.

who_can_apply: Atlanta Public Schools students. The district page does not list grade, age or GPA rules, so ask your school counselor or the CTAE office.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. Call or email the Work-Based Learning contact, or ask your school counselor.
notes: The phone on the page is (404) 802-5878. The page also lists CTAE career paths. They include Engineering Drafting, Allied Health, Cybersecurity and Culinary Arts. Students in other districts use their own district.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated on the district page. You earn high school credit.

who_can_apply: Atlanta youth ages 14 to 24. Documents asked for: original birth certificate, proof of City of Atlanta residency, state or school photo ID, original Social Security card, and a work permit for anyone under 16.
how_to_apply: Register online on the city's SYEP sign-up page with an email address you check daily. Upload your documents in the SYEP portal when asked. You are matched to openings, invited to orientation, and sent an offer letter. Some employers interview first.
notes: A work permit is needed only for ages 14 and 15 (Georgia requires one under 16). You start it after you have a job offer, through your school district. Not guaranteed: the city says selection is competitive. Questions: syep@atlantaga.gov or (404) 546-3000. The registration list asks for an original Social Security card; this is the official city program, so upload documents only inside the SYEP portal and never send them by email or text. The city's atlantaga.gov pages blocked automated reading, so confirm the 2027 timeline with the SYEP team.
duration: June 8 to July 16 in 2026 (about 6 weeks). Some positions may extend.
pay_detail: Paid. The page says competitive wages and does not state a rate.

who_can_apply: Young business owners ages 11 to 17. You have a product or service, you have paying customers and you want to grow.
how_to_apply: Click Apply now on the YMB Fuel page. Applications are reviewed, then there is a shortlist and interviews. You must commit to attend.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Your business needs paying customers already. For newer ideas the site lists YMB Spark (early-stage help) but its page was not read. YMB also holds an annual Summit (two days, ages 11 to 17 can register); dates and cost were not on the page. The page says the program takes place live in Atlanta, Georgia, and may have virtual parts.
duration: One week summer intensive
pay_detail: Free to join. Grants are given at Pitch Day; the amounts are not listed.

who_can_apply: Aurora residents ages 14 to 18 who are in high school.
how_to_apply: Check that you meet the rules, then fill out the BEO Interest Form (Google form).
notes: The page does not name the employers or say if internships pay. For city help, call 311 or 630-256-4636. The City's Summer Youth Programs page said summer 2026 programs are closed and to look for summer 2027.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. As of 2026-10-10, the program page says nothing about pay. Ask the program team.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not give an age or grade range or a residency rule. Ask the teen librarians.
how_to_apply: Write to the Teen Librarians. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is teens@aurorapubliclibrary.org.
notes: The library's teen volunteer page said summer reading volunteers for 2027 apply in the spring. It also lists outside groups that take teen volunteers, with their own age rules.
duration: Meets on the 1st Monday of every month at 6 p.m.
