pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It does not say if service hours are given.

who_can_apply: Aurora residents ages 15 to 24. At least two young people must lead each project.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Questions: youthservdiv@aurora.il.us.
notes: 10 to 50 projects share $50,000. Funds go out by Nov 13, 2026, and projects end by Apr 15, 2027. Ages up to 24 can apply. Next round not posted.
duration: Applications Aug 24 to Oct 16, 2026
pay_detail: You do not get paid. Each project can receive a microgrant of $1,000 to $5,000 to carry it out. The money pays for the project, not a wage to you.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 17 who are in good standing at school and live in Aurora or North Aurora. A signed waiver is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and the waiver using the link at the top of the Youth Court page. Print and sign the waiver and bring it to your first session. Contacts on the page: rodriguezs@aurora.il.us or sarmientos@aurora.il.us.
notes: Training dates are not listed on the page. The page says Youth Court is for youth who committed first time offenses. Teens serve as jurors.
duration: Meets the third Tuesday of each month, 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and 14 may volunteer only with an adult who is also a volunteer. Ages 15 and 16 may volunteer on their own, but an adult must attend orientation with them. The page gives no general rule for 17 year olds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the individual volunteer application, then go to orientation. A criminal background check is part of orientation. Email animalservicesvolunteers@austintexas.gov for help.
notes: Read the volunteer handbook linked on the page first.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers give at least 6 hours a month.

who_can_apply: Austin, TX residents who attend an Austin-area high school, ages 15 to 18 when applying, available for the whole program with no more than 3 days absent.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link posted on the page) with an essay. Choose your preferred track on the application. Email SummerHSIntern@austintexas.gov with questions.
notes: Separate from the Austin ISD / Austin Chamber paid internship. Placements depend on site access and career interest.
duration: 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026)
pay_detail: $13 per hour, 20 hours per week

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 19 who live in Austin. Must be able to commit to the full internship. Acceptance depends on the City of Austin document check and New Employee Orientation.
how_to_apply: No application is open now. Join the mailing list on the page, or read the FAQ PDF. Questions go to the email link on the page.
notes: The age range on the page is 17 to 19. The page calls applicants high school students. It does not state pay, grades or a 2027 application window. Check when the mailing list announces 2027.
duration: 8 weeks (June to July in 2026)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The hourly amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 cannot go on active building sites. They do other projects, and there must be 1 adult for every 5 kids. Ages 16 and 17 may help build new homes. They may not use power tools or work above 6 feet. They must bring a parent or guardian over 21. Home Repair and Blitz Build need 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer calendar (austinhabitat.volunteerhub.com) or the general sign-up page. The youth page does not give its own steps. Call Volunteer Services at 512-472-8788 ext. 106. Or write to volservices@austinhabitat.org.
notes: The age 12 start is for the project ideas listed for 12 and up. Confirm the right sign up path for your age with Volunteer Services.
duration: Family Build Days happen 3 to 4 times a year. Other timing is not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. Ages 14 and 15 need a parent or guardian over 21 to train and volunteer with them at all times. Ages 16 and 17 can volunteer on their own with parental consent given on the online application.
how_to_apply: Pay the fee, go to a virtual welcome orientation, finish online training, then take a hands on training session and pick a shift. Start from the Get Started button on the volunteer page.
notes: The youth page does not list a fee, but the volunteer page does. This page does not cover the clinic volunteer program.
duration: At least 3 months, 2 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid. One time registration fee of $20 for students ($35 for adults), paid at orientation.

who_can_apply: Austin ISD students who will be in grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Interest Form linked on the page. Students heard by March 30. They had to go to orientations in late April and mid May. Contact Cecilia Gutierrez at cecilia.gutierrez@austinisd.org.
notes: Info sessions in 2026 were held on Google Meet in December and January. The page lists the work period as ending July 23 in one place and July 24 in another.
duration: 6 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 23, with a break June 29 to July 3)
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend for living expenses

who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 17 living in Central Texas who will be a sophomore, junior or senior in the coming fall (homeschoolers welcome). Must be able to work legally in the U.S., or be willing to waive pay on a student-only visa. About 10 teens are hired each year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Foundation's Teen Library Fellowship page when the application opens. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at kathleen.houlihan@austintexas.gov.
notes: Fellows must attend a mandatory monthly Sunday afternoon retreat at the Central Library; travel stipends are available. The Foundation page says ages 15-17 and $21 per hour; library pages say $22 per hour and one library page says ages 15-18, so confirm when applications open.
duration: 9 months (about August to May)
pay_detail: $21 per hour on the Foundation page ($22 per hour on the library pages), up to 10 hours of work per month

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 (no younger than 13 and no older than 17 by Aug 1 for fall, Dec 1 for spring, or May 1 for summer). Must pass a background check (fingerprinting for ages 15+ who lived outside Texas in the last seven years) and attend a mandatory orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application posted on the Teen Volunteer Program page during the window. There may be an interview with the volunteer coordinator; you get three business days to accept an offer. Not every applicant gets a placement.
notes: Placement depends on the library branch and supervisor, and the library gets more applicants than placements. Contact: APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov. Limit of two absences per season.
duration: Fall (Oct-Dec) and spring (Mar-May): 10 weeks, one 2-hour shift a week. Summer (June-July): 8 weeks, one 2 to 4 hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students living in Central Texas, ages 16 to 18 (or turning 16 in the year they apply), interested in creative careers and Latinx issues, and able to work legally in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit a personal application, a portfolio and teacher recommendations, then do one-on-one and panel interviews. Questions: caminos@austintexas.gov.
notes: About 10 to 12 teens per cohort. Competitive. The page says the next round is expected in Spring 2027, with no exact date posted.
duration: 10 months, mid-to-late August through early June; most Saturdays 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. plus Wednesday evenings
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 6 to 10 hours per week

who_can_apply: Lifeguard training and hiring starts at age 15 with no upper age limit. You need a physical Social Security card and Texas-issued ID for the in-person paperwork.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the online lifeguard job application. Step 2: visit the Aquatic Office in person at 2818 San Gabriel St. with your Social Security card, Texas ID and any hiring paperwork emailed to you. Questions: 512-974-9330.
notes: The 2026 posting also offered a $200 stipend for guards trained and working 40 hours before July 4, 2026. One library list says age 16+; the Parks page (dated March 20, 2026) says 15. Texas hour limits apply to 15 year olds.
duration: Seasonal; training happens before the swim season
pay_detail: Starting at $22.05 per hour (March 2026 posting)

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be 15 by June 1 and free for the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online volunteer application. If you are accepted, you get orientation and training details later. Email sdmc.volunteers@stdavids.com. Or call 512-544-4491.
notes: Records are required for 2 MMR doses, 2 chickenpox doses or history, Tdap within 10 years, a TB test within 90 days and a flu shot. Homeschooled teens may apply year round. Up to 2 service day absences may be requested ahead of time.
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July, two 4 hour shifts a week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by June 1 and available the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online application. Then you get an email asking for a teen and parent agreement, two letters of support, short essay answers and shot records. Teens who are picked get an invite to interview. Orientation is by invite. Email namc.volunteers@hcahealthcare.com or call 512-901-1223.
notes: St. David's Medical Center in central Austin has a separate teen program with different ages (15 to 18) and dates. Apply to the campus whose rules you meet.
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July. Weekly hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: The VolunTeens link goes to an online volunteer form (Volgistics). The form needs JavaScript. Check it for the current steps.
notes: Thinkery also runs a teen Counselor in Training program for summer camps. Its page was not found (404), so it is not listed here. Check the dates, cost and application window before you apply. On 2026-10-10 the VolunTeens link went to a bare application form with no program text. So the 60 training hours, 40 service hours and 208 VolunTeen figures could not be checked again.
duration: 60 hours of training plus 40 hours of service
pay_detail: Volunteer service. Cost and pay are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or school or home rules. It says applications are closed and to watch for future chances.
how_to_apply: No application is open now. Contact Urban Roots at info@urbanrootsatx.org or 512-750-8019 to ask when the next one opens.
notes: Details on this page are thin. The page does not name a Summer Farm Program. Ask about ages, pay and season before counting on it. The same page lists free elementary day camps (2nd to 5th grade) and a free middle school Food Lab, which are not for high schoolers.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Described as paid youth internships. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 (out of school youth services target ages 16 to 24). The page says low income youth. For training scholarships and case managed help, the main page lists U.S. work authorization, living in Austin or Travis County, and one more need related to work, income or school.
how_to_apply: Click Get Started on the Youth Services page. It leads to the Jumpstart Your Career registration form and a career info session. You can also use the contact page or call your local career center.
notes: The Jumpstart form asks for the last four digits of a Social Security number. It uses them to check your info on WorkInTexas.com. Summer jobs through SEAL need year round part in WIOA. No income limit is listed.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the services. Paid work experience is named only for the SEAL program (students with disabilities ages 16 to 22). Pay amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in the City of Austin or its Extraterritorial Jurisdiction (ETJ). Students who only attend school in Austin are not eligible. No citizenship rule. A 2.5 GPA or higher is preferred, but applicants are read as a whole.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the application in Spring 2027. Send questions to the program coordinator. Her email is abrianna.citta01@austintexas.gov.
notes: Members may attend national conferences each year, including one in Washington, D.C. The page does not say who pays for travel.
duration: Monthly meetings and service events. Term length is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Pay is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 22 who live in the Austin and Travis County area. You need a reliable ride. You must be able to get a driver's license within 90 days. You must have a high school diploma or GED, or be working toward one.
how_to_apply: Complete the online interest form linked on the page. Call 512-972-4785 or email AYD@austintexas.gov.
notes: The page says the work is paid work with the City, plus mentoring and career planning. It does not give pay, hours, length or application dates. Call before applying. Office: 1416 Montopolis Drive, Austin.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay, hours and length are not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 20 who live in the City of Austin or its extraterritorial jurisdiction and are eligible to work legally in the U.S. No academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Online application (about 1.5 hours), short-answer questions, and one reference who completes a recommendation form. Accepted members become City of Austin employees and must verify work eligibility.
notes: Meetings are held at locations around Austin and transportation help may be available.
duration: One year, June to May; one full council meeting a month
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 10 to 15 hours per month

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Libraries prefer a commitment of at least six months for regular volunteers.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch you want. Volunteers are recruited, interviewed and trained at the local branch.
notes: Not every branch recruits teens, so call first. Volunteer jobs can involve lifting boxes of books and standing for a while.
duration: Regular volunteers: at least 6 months preferred. Volunteens: summer program.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25. The city page lists seats by council district. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Contact the liaison, Tyron Rice, trice@baltimorecity.gov, 443-827-8421, to ask about open seats and the application.
notes: Members are appointed by the Mayor. Seats are limited, so ask before applying. Check the commission website for the current application.
duration: Term lasts until December 2028 for current members
pay_detail: Not stated on the city page.

who_can_apply: High school students from Baltimore City. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Complete the Baltimore City YouthWorks application, then the BCLC application linked on the Civic Works page.
notes: The Civic Works page looks out of date (it mentions 2025). Check the page in spring, or use its Contact Us page, before relying on dates.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: Not stated on the Civic Works page. Teens apply through the YouthWorks summer jobs application.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page's teen event filter lists ages 14 to 17. Be Involved is open to any teen at any branch. Teen Advisory Boards and Buddies use applications.
how_to_apply: For Be Involved, check the events calendar and drop in. For Teen Advisory Boards or Buddies, contact your local branch. Questions: yfe@bcpl.net.
notes: Older BCPL announcement pages were not available, so past application windows are not confirmed here.
duration: Be Involved is drop-in. Teen Advisory Board and Buddies dates are not posted on this page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service-learning hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 who work well with kids and teens and are comfortable talking with the public.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application and send it to the Volunteer Coordinator (volunteers@mdsci.org). Expect a placement interview.
notes: The page links two different youth application PDFs, so ask which one is current. Schedule and hours are not posted. Contact: 410-545-5940.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 17. Apply with a portfolio of art or design work.
how_to_apply: Online application (a fee applies), submit work samples, then deposit if accepted. Email precollege@mica.edu with questions.
notes: Prices are the 2026 amounts from MICA's 2026 payment page. The main page does not list tuition amounts. Prices for 2027 are not posted. The main page says to submit 6 pieces of work.
duration: 2 or 4 weeks (2026: about July 12 to Aug 8)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $3,850 for 2 weeks or $7,700 for 4 weeks. Commuter $2,725 for 2 weeks or $5,450 for 4 weeks. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Students about to enter 11th or 12th grade. Recent graduates must plan to study actuarial science at Morgan in the fall. The application is competitive. Students who are considered get a phone interview.
how_to_apply: Apply through the SAAMS program. Some students get a phone interview. Email msusaams@morgan.edu for application updates.
notes: The FAQ says there are no additional costs or fees beyond travel to and from campus for the last week, and it does not say who pays that travel. Phone (443) 885-3964. Check the page for the application window.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: No cost to attend. Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Local high school students who finished 9th grade, are interested in marine biology or environmental science, and can do the full program including the training week and the shifts.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in December. Selected students come to an in-person interview with Aquarium volunteer staff.
notes: Training week is required (2026: June 22 to 26). The page lists both 12 shifts over six weeks and at least 10 shifts across five weeks, so ask which applies. Closing date for 2027 not posted. Students do not work directly with animals except at the Living Seashore exhibit.
duration: About 6 weeks of volunteering after a training week (2026: June 29 to Aug 9)
pay_detail: Unpaid. $40 fee for registration and materials if accepted (need-based scholarships are available).

who_can_apply: Baltimore City high-schoolers, per the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Branches Fall 2026 application on the Parks & People page. Contact Sophie Poirier, sophie.poirier@parksandpeople.org, 410-448-5663 x108.
notes: Held at 2100 Liberty Heights Avenue, Baltimore. The page also mentions a summer job part. Ask about the summer and spring sessions. The Branches page says applicants must be able to apply for a work permit, must attend all in-person sessions, and that a family orientation is required. The foundation phone is (410) 448-5663 and the email is info@parksandpeople.org.
duration: A fall session, Monday to Thursday 4:30 to 6:30 pm (the 2025 session ran Sep 30 to Dec 18)
pay_detail: Paid. The rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens who live in Baltimore City and are in grades 9 to 12, and can attend the meetings.
how_to_apply: Application on the Pratt Library page when it opens in spring. Not open now.
notes: Meets 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 6:00 to 7:30 pm at the Central Library.
duration: 8 months (November to June)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service learning hours. Dinner is provided at meetings.

who_can_apply: Baltimore City teens in grades 6 to 12. Space in each group is limited.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Pratt Library page when a new series opens. Not open now.
notes: Each series has a new theme. The page does not announce the next series.
duration: 4 weekly sessions per group
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service learning hours.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in teaching. Applicants are selected.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Towson College of Education page when registration opens, likely in February. Contact Assistant Dean Omari Jackson, 410-704-3877.
notes: The 2026 Towson news notice says the program is free, with free daily lunch. The one-credit course is Exploring Careers in Education.
duration: 4 days, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. (2026: July 13 to 16)
pay_detail: Free. Lunch is provided each day.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Baltimore City with a strong interest in biology, chemistry, medicine or related fields.
how_to_apply: See the RAMP page for the application process when it reopens. Teens also need a YouthWorks application for pay.
notes: Held on the UMB campus in downtown Baltimore. Scholars earn Stop the Bleed and CPR/AED certifications in summer one.
duration: 2 years: 5 weeks in July and August, about 10 school-year sessions, then a second 5-week summer
pay_detail: Summer parts can be paid through YouthWorks. Up to $500 for the school-year research rotations.

who_can_apply: Middle school and high school students. The page gives no age or residency rule.
how_to_apply: Register online on the UMBC SEA page when 2027 registration opens.
notes: The page lists extendedlearning@umbc.edu as the contact. The original link now redirects to youthprograms.umbc.edu.
duration: 1 week per course
pay_detail: Standard prices range from $374 to $499 depending on the course.

who_can_apply: High school students. Priority goes to Baltimore City residents and Baltimore City Schools students. Some spots are held for Baltimore County students. Others are considered if space is left.
how_to_apply: Register through Wide Angle (registration is required for all students). Email the programs team or sign up for their newsletter for the next registration.
notes: Wide Angle follows the Baltimore City Schools calendar.
duration: Fall 2026 high school classes: Sep 28 to Dec 11 (no classes Thanksgiving week)
pay_detail: High school students who attend at least 50% of classes can get a pro-rated stipend (a W-9 form is needed).

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21. The page does not give a residency rule for this program.
how_to_apply: Contact Wide Angle through their programs page. The details are not listed on the page.
notes: Wide Angle has also been a worksite for Baltimore YouthWorks (a lead, not confirmed here). Ask them how MediaWorks is funded and how to apply.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Described as a paid summer intensive. The rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Baltimore City residents ages 14 to 21 (age counted as of mid-March of the program year). Needs identity and work authorization papers.
how_to_apply: Apply online in the YouthWorks portal and upload ID, work authorization and tax forms. Under 18 also needs a Maryland work permit signed by a parent. Applying early does not guarantee a job.
notes: Pay of $15 and the work permit rule come from the 2026 pages. The 2027 pay is not posted yet. Help desk (410) 545-1820. Credit recovery classes can also be a paid worksite.
duration: About 5 weeks (June 29 to July 30, 2027)
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2026 (up to 5 hours a day, 5 days a week, 25 hours)

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Can give at least 25 hours between mid-May and mid-September. Basic English.
how_to_apply: Apply when the page reopens. Then you do a 30 minute interview. Orientation is in early April. Training runs April to June.
notes: The day it reopens is not posted. Contact the Volunteer Coordinator through the page.
duration: Mid-May to mid-September, shifts of 2 to 5 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Every 25 hours earns ticket codes and access to dress rehearsals.

who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
duration: June 22 to July 31, 2026, 10 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: $20 per hour (high school, 2026)

who_can_apply: Urban youth in Beacon. The page does not list exact ages or other rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the program's Facebook page for the application. Questions: 845-831-4287.
notes: Ages and pay are not on the page, so ask first. Program site: Beacon Recreation Center, 23 West Center Street, Beacon.
duration: Hired three times a year: spring, summer and fall
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens. The program page does not state an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. The library's main phone number is 503-644-2197.
notes: The council meets on the first and third Thursdays, 5 to 6 PM, at Beaverton City Library Main. Members must attend meetings and events.
duration: Meets twice a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit. The number of hours is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth age 13 and older. You must agree to give at least 80 hours of service within one year of starting. You must attend an initial training held online.
how_to_apply: Fill out the RISE Youth Leader application online. Then attend the virtual training. Questions? Call Melissa Marcum-Fredrick at 503-619-3941.
notes: The same page lists a Junior Lifeguard program for ages 12 and up. It also lists community and cultural events for ages 14 and up.
duration: At least 80 hours within a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work. It can count for school community service hours.

who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g rules for getting into college. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.
duration: 6 or 8 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $15,987 (8 weeks, June 22 to Aug 14) or $14,687 (6 weeks, July 6 to Aug 14). There is also an application fee. One media scholarship was offered in 2026.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteer: fill out the application. No age is stated. Youth Worker: ages 14 to 25. No experience is needed. A work permit is required if under 18.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: complete the Teen Volunteer Application form. Paid work: go through Berkeley YouthWorks (2180 Milvia St, 510-981-4970); see the YouthWorks page for the current interest form.
notes: The library page also lists other groups that take teen volunteers. Berkeley YouthWorks serves Berkeley residents. You must show proof that you live there. The library page says YouthWorks takes applications in March and October.
duration: Youth Worker up to 15 hours a week
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Youth Worker jobs are paid (rate not posted; no benefits).

who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students. A new group starts at the beginning of each school year.
how_to_apply: Join the Teen Council mailing list on the Teen Council page, or email teencouncil@berkeleyrep.org.
notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.
pay_detail: Transportation stipend. Free admission to teen programs and shows, and free food at events.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents (proof of residency at onboarding). Priority for youth facing barriers, such as foster care or legal system involvement, English learners, young parents, and students with IEPs or 504 plans. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online YouthWorks interest form. Chosen candidates get an email for a 15 to 20 minute interview. Contact: youthworks@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-4970.
notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.
duration: Winter 2027 placements run January to March 2027
pay_detail: Wage not posted. Ready to Work workshop stipend if you attend at least 7 of 8 sessions.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16 years old.
how_to_apply: First go to a free info session in person. Then fill out the teen volunteer form. You also go to a training and show your shots: MMR, chicken pox, Tdap, and a flu shot in flu season.
notes: Junior volunteer spots open by season and fill up. Volunteers get free parking and free flu shots. Questions: shvolunteerservices@jh.edu or 301-896-3092.
duration: At least 6 months, one 4-hour shift a week.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17 for the whole program. Students must graduate high school in 2027 or 2028 (2026 page). Needs three recommenders: an English teacher, a business or social studies teacher, and a counselor.
how_to_apply: Fill out the survey to see if you qualify. Name three people to write you a recommendation. Then send the application with a resume, a one-page essay and a 3-minute pitch video. Questions: gesummer@lehigh.edu.
notes: Costs a lot. Ask about aid early since priority aid deadline was in February. Residential, no early departure.
duration: 3 weeks (2026: July 5 to 25)
pay_detail: $7,000 program fee (2026) covering tuition, room and board. Limited need-based aid for priority applicants.

who_can_apply: Current and former foster youth in Alameda County, per the homepage (it says it serves over 500 each year). The age range and intake steps are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Call 510.980.9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org (both from the site footer). Staff connect youth to coaching, training and job resources.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07. The site loaded this time (the earlier certificate error is gone). The homepage and employment page say who is served and what coaching covers, but do not state an age range, costs or an intake process, so those are left blank or not stated. This is a coaching service rather than a paid job, so the type is the closest available. The employment page lists outside job boards and training partners (Civicorps, Oakland Private Industry Council, EASTBAY Works), which are separate organizations. The jobs page is for B:E staff openings, not youth jobs. Call before relying on it.
pay_detail: No pay to the youth is stated. The cost of services to the youth is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not say which clubhouse hosts each Industry Club or whether you must be a member first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Industry Clubs interest form on the page, or email membership@bgcncil.org or call the South Elgin office at (847) 608-5017. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free and signs up through MyClubHub (bgcncil.org/join/).
notes: The organization runs Elgin and South Elgin clubhouses (administrative office at 735 Martin Dr, South Elgin) plus Aurora, Batavia and a Schaumburg Teen Center, but the Industry Clubs page does not say where each session meets. Ask before you sign up. Elgin clubhouses follow the School District U-46 calendar.
duration: 8 to 10 week sessions
pay_detail: Described as paid; the amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Keystone Club is for ages 14 to 18. Youth of the Year is for ages 10 to 18. You must be a Club member. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free, and you must meet the local residency or school district rules.
how_to_apply: Create an account in MyClubHub, pick your clubhouse and fill out the membership application. Staff will email next steps and a start date. Contact for Youth of the Year: cmaxwell@bgcelgin.org.
notes: Age limits can differ by clubhouse. The Industry Clubs (paid career programs for teens) are a separate listing. A Schaumburg Teen Center page exists but only shows a calendar.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Teen membership is free. Winners of Youth of the Year are eligible for Club scholarships.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who have been Club members for 2 or more years and meet academic requirements. The page does not list the academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your Clubhouse. The site lists a 3300 High Street address.
notes: The same Teens page lists Keystone Clubs (ages 14 to 18) and Youth of the Year (ages 16 to 18, a $20,000 scholarship opportunity, not a job). They are not separate cards because the page gives no joining steps. Staff openings are posted on LinkedIn (the careers page does not list them). Season, pay rate, hours and deadlines are not stated, so confirm with the Club before a teen applies. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
pay_detail: The page says 'Paid positions and income.' The pay rate and hours are not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. Summer Teen Internship: rising high school freshmen through seniors who are 14 or older. To intern or volunteer you must have a Social Security Number and be able to complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up and Apply Here links on the club's Volunteer page. Questions? Email Emily Mungul at emungul@bgcp.org.
notes: The page links a separate document on the application process and compliance rules. The SSN requirement is for the club's background check; a teen without an SSN cannot do this one. Summer internship hours are 8:00 am to 12:00 pm, 1:00 to 5:00 pm, or both. BGCP's paid Youth Program Leader jobs ($22 to $25 an hour) do not list an age. Mid-Peninsula Boys & Girls Club and Boys & Girls Clubs of North San Mateo County have joined BGCP, per BGCP's news page.
duration: Program Support: at least 1 hour a week on the same day for at least 6 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 3:00 to 6:00 PM, September to May. Summer internship: at least 3 weeks in June to July, Monday to Friday, mornings, afternoons or both.
pay_detail: School-year Program Support is unpaid volunteering. Pay for the Summer Teen Internship is not stated; it is listed on the club's Volunteer page.

who_can_apply: LIT: ages 15 to 17. CIT: ages 16 to 17 who already did LIT (in person or virtually). CITs must commit to two sessions, one of them a 7-day session. No city or residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the LIT/CIT online application on the Teen Leadership page. Then register for camp and pick the 'CIT/LIT programs' price option, which waives the fee once you are accepted. Training is at camp in Session 1A, or a required virtual training.
notes: Apply early. The FAQ says spots often fill by early April. The camp told teens in rounds. For example, it replied by March 2 for the Feb 16 deadline. Buses leave from San Francisco. For Session 1, there is also a stop near Travis Air Force Base. Teens who are 15 can sign up as regular campers instead. People 18 and up can apply for camp staff jobs. Contact: camperapplication@kidsclub.org.
duration: In 2026, LIT/CIT training was June 17 to 20, then camp sessions ran June 20 to Aug 5. LITs can do one or more sessions; CITs do two.
pay_detail: Free: the camp fee is waived for all sessions for accepted LITs and CITs. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who are current Club members. Membership costs $20. Teens may take part only once per calendar year.
how_to_apply: Join the Club ($20 membership) at kidsclub.org/register, then contact the High School Services Director or Clubhouse staff at your Clubhouse to sign up. You must attend one training session.
notes: Contact: Earl Declet, edeclet@kidsclub.org. The 2025-26 flyer lists LIT at these clubs: Willie Mays (Bayview), Excelsior, Don Fisher (Fillmore), Columbia Park and Mission (Mission), Tenderloin, and Springer (Sunnydale). Finishing LIT can lead to summer jobs. Teens under 18 cannot join the adult volunteer program. The site says to join a club, where there are youth volunteer roles. Club teens can also join Keystone Club. Its members raise at least $3,000 to go to a national meeting. The flyers do not say if you need a work permit.
duration: About 10 weeks: 70 hours of on-the-job experience after 10 hours of Work-Based Learning training.
pay_detail: Teens who complete the requirements receive an $800 gift card.

who_can_apply: High school students, rising 9th to 12th grade. The program page does not list a city rule.
how_to_apply: Use the Summer Starts Here button on the program page. It goes to the parent portal. Check back this spring for the class list.
notes: Hours are 10:00am to 5:30pm. The clubhouse has a tech center, recording studio, industrial kitchen and gym. The program page does not list jobs or paid internships. Phone: 510-483-5581. The same club runs a drop-in teen center for ages 13 to 18.
pay_detail: Free for teens. This is a program, not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who enjoy hands-on learning, per the program page. One camp is for middle and high school students. The other camps listed are for 3rd to 6th graders.
how_to_apply: Use the sign up link for your camp on the program page. Questions? Email workforcedevelopment@msubillings.edu. Or call 406-896-5965.
notes: The page does not say which year the dates are for. Check before you plan.
duration: One week, Monday to Friday. Middle and high school camp dates on the page: July 27-31
pay_detail: $250 per student. Drone equipment and materials are included.

who_can_apply: Youth in school, ages 14 to 21, who have low income and at least one barrier from the state list. Youth out of school, ages 16 to 24, can also qualify under other rules. The barriers include a disability, foster care and no home. Being behind in basic skills is also a barrier.
how_to_apply: The state page has no application form. It points to a provider list. For Billings, the May 2026 list names District VII HRDC, contact Kelly Marquardt, 406-247-4788, kmarquardt@hrdc7.org.
notes: Other providers on the May 2026 state list: Missoula District XI HRDC (Lynda Schuldheisz, 406-728-3710) and Opportunities, Inc. in Great Falls (Jeff Beisecker, 406-761-8462). Only some teens qualify. Ask the provider first.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid and unpaid work experience are both listed. Pay rates are not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students. The program page does not state an age or grade rule beyond that.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form linked on the program page. For questions call the center at 406-294-5099.
notes: Training is mandatory. The page does not list fall session dates. The center is at 7026 S Billings Blvd.
duration: Spring 2026 session: training March 26, then Thursdays 3:30 to 5:15 PM, April 2 to May 21
pay_detail: Volunteer role. Pay and service hours are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students with a documented disability, an IEP or a 504 plan. The summer camp is limited to 30 students. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: The page does not list student steps. Schools that want to take part should contact Richie Solomon at 406-657-2092 or richard.solomon@msubillings.edu.
notes: If you do the campus visits in the school year, you get into the summer camp if you want to go.
duration: Four-day summer camp each June
pay_detail: Free. Tuition, fees, books, lodging and meals are covered for accepted camp students.

who_can_apply: Students at Senior, Skyview, West, Hardin or Lockwood high schools who finished 8th grade, are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and want to go to college. Your parents must not have a four-year degree, and your family must meet income rules. The page does not list the income limits.
how_to_apply: Get a paper application from the Upward Bound staff. Return it to your school counselor or mail it in. Eligible students get an interview. Phone: 406-657-2116. Email: upwardbound@msubillings.edu.
notes: Students not selected go on a waiting list. Selection looks at grades, recommendations and the interview. The program page does not say if the summer program is free. The summer page says students can get a stipend of up to $90.
duration: Six weeks in summer plus school-year advising
pay_detail: Free. Summer students can get a stipend of up to $90.

who_can_apply: Most positions need you to be at least 15 years old. Lifeguards must hold a lifeguard certification.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. It links job descriptions and a lifeguard course sign-up. Call 406-969-3131 to ask when hiring opens.
notes: 2026 lifeguard training weekends were May 1-3, May 8-10, May 15-17 and May 22-24, limited to the first 10 sign-ups. The program page does not say whether training will be held next spring.
duration: Summer season. Start and end dates are not stated.
pay_detail: The page says pay is competitive but gives no hourly number. The $150 lifeguard certification fee is paid back after one month of work.

who_can_apply: Youth. The program page does not state an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Here link on the program page. It opens the YDAT volunteer site for Billings. Make an account, then sign up for projects. A parent can set up a profile for each child. Phone: 406-657-8371.
notes: The program page does not list ages, dates or hour rules. Call the parks office to ask what ages can join.
duration: Project by project
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens. Age or grade rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Apply through the library's Teen Advisory Board page. The page says to contact hoys@billingsmt.gov for more information. The main library phone is 406-657-8258.
notes: The library's volunteering page says no new volunteers are being taken now. Ask if they take late applications.
duration: School year (2026-2027), meeting the first and third Wednesday of each month at 4:30 p.m. in the CO+LAB
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 and older.
how_to_apply: The page does not list steps. Email Kaylinn at kaylinn@wisewonders.org to start.
notes: The museum job page says there are no open jobs now. It asks people to send a resume and cover letter to info@wisewonders.org for future jobs.
duration: Hours are not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Volunteer role. No pay is mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. You must apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the program page. Questions? Contact Angel Shandy, Museum Art Educator. Call 406-256-6804 ext. 238. Or email arteducator@artmuseum.org.
notes: The page does not give a year for the Spring dates; they are listed under Spring 2027. The page does not say how many service hours you get.
duration: Meets the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of each month, 3:30 to 5 PM
pay_detail: Free to join. The program page does not mention pay or a stipend.

who_can_apply: Members are youth ages 9 to 19 (a 19-year-old must still be in high school). Ages are counted on October 1.
how_to_apply: Find a club on the county club list. Contact the club leader first, because the leader must approve you. Then enroll online with the link on the county 4-H page. Extension office: 406-256-2828.
notes: Some clubs have waiting lists. The $25 fee is paid to the club.
duration: 4-H year starts October 1
pay_detail: Member fee is $25. Most shooting sport projects cost $15 more per discipline.

who_can_apply: High school students and recent graduates, ages 16 to 19 (from the 2024 report).
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe a student sign-up. Contact Big Sky Economic Development in Billings to ask how to join.
notes: Based on an August 2024 report that says 34 students finished in 2024. Ask Big Sky Economic Development if the program still runs.
duration: One summer
pay_detail: Paid positions. The wage is not stated.

who_can_apply: Each job lists its own minimum age, 14 or 15. Lifeguards need Lifeguard, First Aid and CPR certification. The page says 'FREE training if you join our team!'
how_to_apply: Fill out the BPRD Job Application PDF in Adobe Reader (not in your web browser). Lifeguards also fill out the Aquatic Application Supplement Form. Email to jobs@bisparks.org or drop off or mail to 400 E. Front Ave., Bismarck, ND 58504.
notes: The page lists the season dates without a year. Park maintenance and some other jobs are for older workers. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.
duration: Varies. Youth basketball runs Oct 26 to Jan 16. Open Gym Supervisor is Nov to March on weekend afternoons. BLAST leader is 15 to 20 hours a week after school. Arena attendant is 25 to 30 hours a week.
pay_detail: Paid. Pay rates are not listed on the program page. Employees get a benefits pass for golf, pool and fitness.

who_can_apply: Girls ages 7 to 18 for workshops. A separate College and Careers Community serves ages 18 plus.
how_to_apply: Check the community events page for current workshops: community.wearebgc.org/events.
notes: The home page did not name a Bay Area chapter, prices or workshop dates. Check the events page for what is open now. Code Along videos are free on YouTube. Home page shows no workshop price, so the card is not in the paid group.
duration: Workshop length varies
pay_detail: Workshop cost and pay are not stated on the home page. The Code Along videos on YouTube are free. The page does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: Students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade who may want a future career in healthcare. Download the camp form for the full qualifications and paperwork.
how_to_apply: Download the camp application form from the Carilion news page, then follow its instructions. Contact the camp directors at lmfreeman@carilionclinic.org or krproctor@carilionclinic.org.
notes: The camp is in Roanoke, not Blacksburg. 2027 dates are not posted; check the Carilion camps news page in early 2027.
duration: 4 days (June 16 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The page seeks volunteers and student volunteers. It lists no minimum age or youth rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Contact form on the volunteer page. You can also email info@historicsmithfield.org. Or call 540-231-3947.
notes: No age rule is posted, so ask whether teens under 16 or 18 need a parent. Shifts are Wednesday to Saturday daytime for tours and the store.
duration: Museum season April to December; July camp; some roles year-round
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. You need a parent signature and your shot record. You also need a note of support from a teacher, school counselor or an adult who is not family.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application. Send the other forms. They are a disclosure and release form, a signed parent consent form, your shot record and a note of support.
notes: The page also lists a signed disclosure and release form and parental consent form. You must keep your scheduled shifts. Hospital address: 3700 South Main Street, Blacksburg.
duration: 3 to 9 hours a week in the school year. More shifts allowed in summer and school breaks with parent permission.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A free meal in the cafeteria for a 3-hour shift.

who_can_apply: Community and project clubs are for ages 9 through 18. The home school Senior club is ages 14 to 19. Clubs have size limits and fill first come, first served, and they depend on volunteer leaders.
how_to_apply: Email one of the Extension 4-H staff on the page. They are Kendra Young kkyoung@vt.edu, Lesa Miller lvmiller@vt.edu and Margarita Palomino mrpalomi@vt.edu. Or call the Montgomery County Extension office at 540-382-5790. Staff pass your request to the club leaders.
notes: The clubs page does not give an age rule or meeting time for the Teens for a Better Tomorrow club, so ask staff. This is a youth club, not a paid job.
duration: Clubs meet 9 to 12 months a year. Home school clubs meet Oct to early May.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the clubs page. Ask the Extension office.

who_can_apply: Selected students from nine public high schools in the partner divisions: Radford City, Giles, Floyd, Pulaski and Montgomery County public schools.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor or gifted resource teacher, tell your parents, line up two teacher recommenders, get your transcript, then fill out the NRVGSAH Application Packet.
notes: School districts arrange transportation to Radford. Choose from visual arts, dance, theatre, music, design, history, politics and philosophy. The program is new.
duration: Three hours each weekday morning during the school year
pay_detail: Page says students earn nearly two years of college credit at no cost to the family.

who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors from Virginia or other states. It is not just for girls. Any student who is interested can apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a typed essay of 400 words about why you like science, math or IT. Get one letter from a counselor, teacher or adult leader. Contact David Horton, rhorton@radford.edu, or 540-831-5958.
notes: Radford is about 15 miles from Blacksburg. Families get students to and from campus. You share a room with one other student.
duration: One week, residential (dates not shown on the page)
pay_detail: $1,600 covers tuition, room and board. Competitive scholarships can cover the full cost, and earlier applicants are more likely to get one.

who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. No age range is given.
how_to_apply: Online application form linked on the camp website. Email info@same-vatech-stemcamp.org to check the 2027 dates.
notes: Site says the camp is a day camp at Virginia Tech and was postponed to Summer 2027. The old July 1 deadline and July dates on the site may be out of date, so confirm with the organizers.
duration: 3 days (July 22 to 24 listed for the postponed 2026 camp)
pay_detail: Cost not stated.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a minimum 3.5 GPA. The page lists no location rule.
how_to_apply: Register online during the winter window. The page gave no apply link when read, so use the contact on the page: Louann Morrow, lomorrow@vcom.edu.
notes: Next-cycle dates are not posted; expect a similar early-year window. Camp has a strict dress code (closed-toe shoes, no shorts or hats) and no phones in the anatomy lab.
duration: One week (two sessions in 2026: weeks of June 21 and July 5)
pay_detail: Free. Meals, lodging and activities are included. No pay.

who_can_apply: Enrolled senior 4-H members in Virginia. The page says the event is for 4-H youth ages 14 to 18. You must be signed up as a member through 4-H Online.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H first. Your county 4-H office can help. Then register through your family profile in 4-H Online. Your county 4-H agent handles unit delegations.
notes: You must already be a 4-H member. Part of the page still shows last year's details, so check the newest page. Statewide event that happens to be in Blacksburg, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card.
duration: 4 days (2026: June 16 to 19)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $310 for full time registration, $70 for the one-day competition. Each unit gets one first-time delegate scholarship for half the cost ($155).

who_can_apply: Anyone who lives in Montgomery County can join. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must come to every activity. They must also fill out a sign up form. No minimum age is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer sign up form linked on the FAQ page. Call 540-382-5775 or email hayesaw@montgomerycountyva.gov. Hours are Mon to Fri, 8:30 to 5.
notes: Teens need an adult with them, so it works best for families or a parent who volunteers too. A volunteer inactive for more than 12 months may be removed from the roll.
duration: No required hours
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Current 8th or 9th grade students at a Virginia middle, high, home-school or private school. You must be a Virginia resident and a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident, with at least a C+/B- average (2.7 GPA) and a desire to explore STEM. The program is meant for students without STEM experience.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the BLAST page. Pick one session. A recommender and a school counselor must also submit forms online before the deadline.
notes: This is a state program with sessions at five universities, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card. The page says applicants must be a current 8th or 9th grader in one place. It describes rising 9th and 10th graders in another place. That means the same thing, since you apply in the school year before. The page lists the window as December 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027.
duration: 3 days, in college dorms
pay_detail: Free for all participants. Meals are provided during the session.

who_can_apply: Rising 8th and 9th grade students. Any student who might like cybersecurity is welcome. You do not need any previous experience.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the CyberSpark page. Phone: 540-231-4312.
notes: Mostly for younger teens (rising 8th and 9th graders). Cost and whether it is a day camp or overnight are not stated, so ask the program. Camp, not a job.
duration: 5 days
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Everyone in grades 9 to 12. No prior design courses needed.
how_to_apply: Use the registration links on the page for the Blacksburg or virtual session. No refunds after the May 15 close. Questions: Chris Pritchett, cpritche@vt.edu.
notes: Page shows 2026 information. Expect registration to open around Dec 1 again, but this is a past pattern and not confirmed. Overnight campers stay in suite-style dorms with an RA.
duration: One week (2026 Blacksburg session June 21 to 27)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: Blacksburg session $1,250 (materials not included, about $100 estimated); virtual session $250. Needs-based scholarships are offered through the registration form.

who_can_apply: Campers ages 15 to 18. The page lists no school or residency rules. Limit of 16 campers.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the link on the STEM Summer Camp page. For a scholarship, email the contact on the page. That is kdivitto@vt.edu or the Fralin education director.
notes: The same page lists camps for younger ages; only the Geosciences camp for ages 15 to 18 is for teens. The page shows 2026 details, so confirm before planning for 2027.
duration: One week, 9am to 4pm (2026: June 1 to 5), day camp, no overnight
pay_detail: $120 for the week (2026). Two scholarships are available each week for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Rising 7th or 8th graders. First-time applicants get preference.
how_to_apply: Three parts: a student application with a one paragraph essay on what interests you about engineering, a parent form (consent, and financial statement if you want a scholarship), and a recommendation from a math, science or technology teacher.
notes: For younger teens. The drone week is residential only. Phone 540-231-7337.
duration: Three sessions, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm: June 14 to 20 (drone camp, residential), June 22 to 26, and June 29 to July 3 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: day camp $350 per week, residential $1,000 per week. Needs-based scholarships available through the parent form.

who_can_apply: High school students who start their senior year in 2026-27. You need a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 or the same in another scale. You need to have done or be doing pre-calculus. You also write a short note about why you are interested.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the PIP page and submit a statement of interest. Questions: PCOBrecruiting@vt.edu.
notes: Only for rising seniors, so a teen has one chance to apply. Travel to Blacksburg is on the family.
duration: 10 days, residential (page dates: Thursday July 9 to Saturday July 18)
pay_detail: Free. The page says cost of attendance is covered except travel to and from Blacksburg. No pay.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents entering grade 10, 11 or 12. You must be a first generation college student. That means neither parent graduated from a four year college in the U.S. or abroad.
how_to_apply: Send in the Pathways application linked on the page. Contact Perry Martin at pathways@vt.edu with questions.
notes: Only for Virginia residents who would be first generation college students. The pages do not say whether the summer program is free. The eligibility text on the page mentions students entering grades in the fall of 2025, so it may be out of date. Check the application link before you plan.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. Ask pathways@vt.edu.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders with at least two years of lessons on violin, viola, cello or double bass.
how_to_apply: Registration information is not posted yet (the 2026 page said it was coming soon). Questions: stringproject@vt.edu.
notes: Dates are last year's. The page said registration information was coming soon.
duration: 3 days, residential (June 12-14 in 2026)
pay_detail: $450 covers meals, dorm housing, T-shirt, music and supplies

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12 at listed schools. They include Blacksburg High, Auburn High, Christiansburg High and Eastern Montgomery High. It mostly serves students who are first in their family to go to college and have lower family income. Any student who needs college prep help may join.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the Talent Search page if you attend a listed school. A Spanish application PDF is also posted.
notes: Not a job. It is a free college access program. Out-of-school and adult learners are not covered by this card.
duration: Ongoing through school years
pay_detail: Free. No pay.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students, per the Virginia Tech engineering pre-college list. The camp pages do not give more rules.
how_to_apply: There are two parts. One is a student application. It has activities, short essays of 120 words or less each, and a transcript. The transcript does not need to be official. The other is a parent form. It has consent and a financial statement used for scholarships. The application is shared with the C-Tech2 camp. You can choose either camp or both.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The pages are partly out of date (they mention the 2025 application), so check the newest page and confirm dates with the program. The Virginia Tech C-Tech2 camp has its own card in this guide.
duration: 2 weeks, residential
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks. It covers room, board and program costs. You pay your own travel and personal items. Scholarships are available based on financial need. Cancel 30 or more days before camp for a 50% refund.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. You must be 13 by June 1.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Contact Erica Carnes at elcarnes@blankparkzoo.net or 515-974-2543. Hours count toward the Silver Cord award.
notes: You and your parents choose your shifts, and once you sign up you are expected to attend. Volunteering cannot start until the fee is paid.
duration: Primarily June, July and August. First-year teens must log at least 40 hours before December 31.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay a fee: $35 for zoo members or $40 for non-members. It covers a t-shirt, training and an online manual, and is due before orientation.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 must be with a legal guardian at all times. Ages 16 and older can volunteer on their own. Everyone must pass screening.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist through the Bloomington Volunteer Network. Use the green button on the page. That is not the application. The volunteer director will email you a link to it later.
notes: Book Buddies (K to 6th grade, all ages welcome with an adult) needs no application. Shelter hours for Book Buddies are listed on the page.
duration: 2-hour weekly shift for a minimum of 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older who can do hard physical work. That means digging, carrying mulch buckets and pulling water tanks. You must show up on time. Grant rules also ask that you treat all people fairly, no matter their gender, who they love or their race.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form linked from the job page. Questions: hello@canopybloomington.org.
notes: The page does not say which year the March and May dates belong to, but the weekday dates match 2026. Check the page again in early 2027. Work permit rules for Indiana minors were not checked.
duration: Part time, Monday to Friday 9am to 1pm (20 hours a week). Two 4-week sessions: June and July (2026 dates).
pay_detail: $15 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a class. Use the events calendar at the Eskenazi Museum.
notes: The 2026 camp was full. Younger weeks are for ages 7 to 12. Contact the museum for cost.
duration: 1 week, noon to 3 p.m. Monday to Friday (July 27 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. You must be 18 to use power tools. Student chapters exist at Bloomington High School North and South.
how_to_apply: Email ec@monroecountyhabitat.org to sign up for a build day. You can also use the contact form on the volunteer page.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and clothes you do not mind getting dirty. Groups such as schools can sign up together. ReStore roles are listed but the page does not state a separate age for them.
duration: Ongoing; many volunteers come weekly, monthly or for special events
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Lunch is provided for construction site volunteers.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not state exact grades or ages. Highly selective, about 15 to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Record a monologue of up to 90 seconds. Upload it to YouTube or Vimeo as unlisted. Then fill out the online application with the video link. The program can give you a monologue if you need one.
notes: You must live on campus. The application page is at cinemaacademy.indiana.edu/summer-sessions/afc.html. Check the exact age rules there.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: $950, which includes lodging, meals, instruction, equipment use and supplies (2026 price).

who_can_apply: Gifted high school students, such as singers, players and spoken word artists. Students are picked. Age and grade limits are not listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the camp page (an online form). Students are selected.
notes: Contact campsoul@iu.edu or the director, Ignoisco Miles. His email is imiles@iu.edu and his phone is 812-855-0816. Ask about cost and how to audition before you apply.
duration: 6 days (June 13 to 18, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18. The page has a star by this, so check the session page for exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill in the form. It is on the Cinema Academy summer sessions page.
notes: There is also a one-week Online Filmmaking Bootcamp. The Media School also holds a free one-day teen workshop on Saturday Nov 14, 2026 (Cinema, Game Dev and Journalism tracks).
duration: 1 week for most sessions; the Advanced Filmmakers Academy is 2 weeks
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Three kinds of scholarships are offered.

who_can_apply: Current Indiana high school juniors on a college-prep path. That means the Indiana GPS Diploma or GPS Diploma Plus. You need a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA. You should like teaching, counseling or student services.
how_to_apply: The online application opens in February 2027. Use the link on the page to ask for more info and get updates.
notes: The page does not state the exact day it opens or closes. Only people who live in Indiana can join.
duration: 1 week (July 11 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: Free. Food and lodging are covered.

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 18. The minimum age varies by camp, so check the page for each session. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the camp website. The scholarship form is separate.
notes: Overnight tuition includes dorm lodging. Day camp is an option for local students. Tuition includes meals, a t-shirt, a thumb drive and a water bottle. Media School also lists June and July 2027 weeks.
duration: 5 days
pay_detail: Overnight $850, day camp $500. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students. Beginners and experienced students are both welcome. Age limits are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register online and choose one workshop per session. You can sign up for one or both sessions. Full workshops may have a waitlist.
notes: Run since 1946. Check the site for cost and dorm details before you plan.
duration: 5 days per session (Session 1: July 12 to 16, 2027. Session 2: July 18 to 22, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school juniors with a GPA of at least 3.2, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math. You want a science career. Students from the other Holland programs go first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. In 2026, accepted students were told the week of April 20. Contact holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.
duration: 2 weeks (June 21 to July 3 in 2026)
pay_detail: $600 stipend after you finish the program. Accepted students also pay a $125 non-refundable registration fee.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 8, 9 or 10. You need a GPA of at least 3.0, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. Contact Kody Beaver, holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.
duration: About 1 week (July 19 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: $125 non-refundable registration fee, charged only to accepted students

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9, 10 or 11. You need a GPA of at least 3.2, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math. You want a science career.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. You contact your assigned mentor before the program. Expect to work some evenings. Contact Kody Beaver, holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.
duration: About 1 week (July 12 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: $125 non-refundable registration fee for accepted students

who_can_apply: Students of all backgrounds and experience levels. The IU O'Neill School page says middle and high school students. Exact ages are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register and pay the deposit through the camp sign up page (IU Conferences payment page). Financial aid form is separate.
notes: Labs may be cancelled if too few students sign up, and you would be offered another lab. Camp size is limited. The camp says it is cheaper than many other university camps.
duration: About 1 week (check-in July 5, check-out July 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: housing and meals $950 ($150 deposit plus $800 tuition); commuter with meals $750; commuter without meals $500. Scholarships awarded on a rolling basis after May 15.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 18. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form on the workshop page. A liability form and details are emailed before the workshop.
notes: Drop-off and pick-up are at the Franklin Hall commons atrium (601 E Kirkwood Ave). This is separate from the summer HSJI program.
duration: 1 day, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. Lunch is provided.

who_can_apply: People 14 and older (the page also welcomes adults). Parents of kids under 14 can email musicsp@iu.edu. You do not need an audition or past experience.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form and pay the deposit and tuition. Questions go to musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: There is also a summer intensive linked from the page. Group class is Tuesdays 8:30 to 9:30 p.m. Eastern.
duration: 12 weeks, entirely on Zoom
pay_detail: Track 1 (private lessons plus group class) $800. Track 2 (group class only) $550. A $50 non-refundable deposit is credited to tuition.

who_can_apply: Ballet intensive: ages 13 to 18, admitted by a filmed prescreen of a classical variation. Contemporary intensive: ages 14 to 18, must have completed grade 8, no screening.
how_to_apply: Online registration form and $100 fee; ballet applicants upload a private YouTube link to a classical variation. Do not pay tuition until accepted. Then submit the Participant Agreement Form.
notes: Intense schedule (Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM). The student pays; this is not a job.
duration: 1 to 3 weeks: June 6-12, June 13-19 (ballet) and June 20-26 (contemporary), 2027
pay_detail: Tuition $1,000 per one-week session ($2,000 for two, $3,000 for three) plus $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals $550 per session; commuter meal plan $115 per session.

who_can_apply: High school age (pre-college) and undergraduate brass players. The page gives no exact age range. You send a placement recording for ensemble placement.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Also upload a placement recording to the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Confirm 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 27 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $750 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional youth housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 on brass, woodwinds, voice, strings or rhythm instruments. No audition to get in, but you send a placement recording.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Then upload a placement recording that has not been edited. YouTube links are fine. Use the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Check the 2027 dates and prices before you plan.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: Tuition $775 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices). Need-based aid and merit awards exist.

who_can_apply: Students currently in grades 8 to 12 who play in band or orchestra. Jazz band requires an audition on the first day.
how_to_apply: Online registration form plus the $100 registration fee, tuition by the payment deadline, then a Participant Agreement Form. Contact: musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: Costs and dates are from the 2026 session page. The student pays; this is not a job. The Jacobs Academy also lists other pre-college summer programs.
duration: One week (June 14 to 20 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026: residential tuition $1,120 (housing and meals); commuter tuition $815 (lunch and dinner); $100 non-refundable registration fee credited to tuition. Need-based financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Serious pianists ages 12 to 19. You must be able to practice several hours a day. You should play music that is early advanced to advanced. The director can admit exceptional students under 12. You must audition with a recording.
how_to_apply: Pay the $100 fee in the online sign-up form. Then upload a list of the music you play and two different pieces you play from memory. Send them as recordings to the Jacobs audition portal. Pay tuition only after you are accepted.
notes: The director is Dr. Elizabeth Yao (elizyao@iu.edu). Check the 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 2 weeks (June 27 to July 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $2,400 plus a $100 deposit credited to tuition (2026 prices). Housing and meal plans cost extra. Financial aid and scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18. You send a placement recording so you can be placed in studios and groups.
how_to_apply: Finish the online sign-up and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Then upload a recording for placement in the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Confirm 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 1 week (July 5 to 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $900 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices). Need-based aid exists.

who_can_apply: Serious string players ages 12 to 18. You must audition by recording.
how_to_apply: Pay the $100 fee in the online sign-up form. Then upload two different pieces as recordings to the Jacobs audition portal. YouTube links are fine. Pay tuition only after you are accepted.
notes: Directed by Prof. Mimi Zweig (zweig@iu.edu). Confirm 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 4 weeks (June 20 to July 18 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $3,200 plus a $100 audition fee credited to tuition (2026 prices). Housing and meal plans cost extra. Need-based aid and merit scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Any high school student. Only 50 team spots are available.
how_to_apply: Apply online. It is first come, first served.
notes: The page shows the August 28 and October 3 dates without a year; the date has already passed this fall. Travel costs are not discussed on the page. Expect it to repeat in fall 2027 but confirm.
duration: One day (Saturday)
pay_detail: No cost to apply or attend

who_can_apply: High school students with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale. The page says the experience is open to all students. Selective, seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Online application: 100-word statement, 250-word response, GPA and business-related activities. No exceptions for missed deadlines.
notes: The page lists weekday dates (for example 'Wednesday April 7') that match 2027, and a fall 2026 virtual session (Oct 13 and 20, 2026) whose application closed Sept 25, 2026. Applications are not reviewed until after the deadline.
duration: One day in person, or two virtual sessions
pay_detail: No registration fees; breakfast and lunch provided. In-person students pay their own travel to Bloomington, housing and personal costs.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 who want to explore cybersecurity. Students with little or no technical background are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. Contact the summer camp team at luddycmp@iu.edu or Joshua Streiff at jostre@iu.edu.
notes: Costs money. It is a camp, not a job. The page does not say whether it is residential or a day camp. Ask the summer camp team.
duration: 1 week, June 2027 (exact dates not set)
pay_detail: Program fee $300.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Applications open in January 2027 through the Luddy high school programs page. Contact the summer camp team at luddycmp@iu.edu or Joshua Streiff at jostre@iu.edu.
notes: Costs money. It is a camp, not a job. The same page lists the Luddy Cybersecurity Immersion Camp, which has its own card.
duration: Residential camp, July 2027 (exact dates not set)
pay_detail: Program fee $950. It covers on-campus lodging, meals and activities.

who_can_apply: High school students completing grades 9 to 12. Only 20 students are accepted from around the country.
how_to_apply: Email Program Director Ansley Valentine (arvalent@iu.edu). Send a photo and a resume of your stage and backstage theatre work. Then you get audition materials.
notes: Costs a lot, so ask about aid. Run with Stages Bloomington. Confirm 2027 dates and cost with the program before applying.
duration: 3 weeks
pay_detail: Tuition is $4,575 with housing and meals. A $500 non-refundable deposit is due on acceptance and the other $4,075 is due June 5 (2026 terms).

who_can_apply: High school students finishing junior year with a GPA of at least 3.0 out of 4.0. You like leading and community work. Clubs and your application essays count too.
how_to_apply: Apply online with an application and essays. Check the box on the form if you want a travel scholarship. Questions: iurlp@iu.edu.
notes: Check the page in the fall for 2027 dates. The page does not say if housing is on campus.
duration: 5 days (June 21 to 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free if accepted. You pay your own travel to Bloomington and spending money. Travel scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors with a GPA of at least 3.0, recommended by a principal or guidance counselor, living with a parent or guardian within commuting distance of campus. IU GPA of at least 2.5 is also required once enrolled.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, then email openprgm@iu.edu for the form and instructions.
notes: Only for students who live close enough to commute to Bloomington. Costs are real college credit fees. Not a job.
duration: One or more courses per term (fall, spring or summer)
pay_detail: Students pay the regular IU undergraduate credit-hour and mandatory fees (student health fee waived). Dollar amounts are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students who care about the environment. The program is online.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the 2027 application opens in January 2027. Questions: essi@iu.edu.
notes: Entirely online, so students anywhere can join. The page shows quotes from 9th, 10th and 11th grade alumni. Participants receive a certificate of completion.
duration: Not stated for 2027
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students. Most come with a teacher or school group, but the page says exceptions can be made. Email essi@iu.edu to ask.
how_to_apply: Email the ESSI team at essi@iu.edu to ask about attending. Registration opens in fall 2026.
notes: Most students attend with a teacher or school group. The page says exceptions can be made if you email essi@iu.edu.
duration: 1 day (9:30 AM to 2:30 PM in the sample schedule)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 3 to 12 can enroll in regular 4-H. You must enroll every year.
how_to_apply: Enroll online in 4HOnline (the 'Click here to enroll' link on the county page). Call Purdue Extension Monroe County at 812-349-2575 for help.
notes: County 4-H camp is for grades 3 to 8, so older teens do not use it. The Extension office is at 3400 S Walnut St, Bloomington, IN 47401. This is a youth club, not a paid job.
duration: Program year starts Oct 1
pay_detail: $20 enrollment fee per member for grades 3 to 12 ($5 for Mini 4-H, grades K to 2).

who_can_apply: The city says it connects volunteers of all ages. Each posting sets its own rules, so check the listing for age limits.
how_to_apply: Search for chances at BloomingtonVolunteerNetwork.org. Make an account and sign up. Call the coordinator at 812-349-3433.
notes: You need an account on the volunteer network site. Parks volunteer pages on the city site list events, camps and clean-ups but do not state ages.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer opportunities
