notes: Also offers CCAP classes at your high school and a Summer Academy. Middle schoolers have a separate Bridge to College program.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived. Out-of-state and international students pay $370 per unit. You buy your own books and arrange your own transportation. Maximum 11 units.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page encourages students of all backgrounds to apply, especially Oakland public and charter school students. No skills, experience or GPA is needed. Admission is competitive: an initial review, then an information session for applicants and families. Age and residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application from February 1 to March 31, then an initial review and an information session for applicants and families. The page also has an interest survey to get application updates.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07 after reading the program's own page. The old chabotspace.org/volunteer/ link now returns 404, so the card points to the Galaxy Explorers page. This is a fee-based program ($1,500 a year tuition) unless the family qualifies for Career Access, which is based on need and census tract data. Floor shifts are 2 per month in the school year and 3 per month in summer. Whether paid Interns need a California work permit is not stated on the page, so we leave the work permit answer blank.
duration: 3 years (summer before 10th grade through 12th grade)
pay_detail: Annual tuition is $1,500 per student (one payment by June 1, or $750 by June 1 and $750 by September 1). The need-based Career Access program covers tuition and adds a stipend. 12th-grade Interns receive a stipend.

who_can_apply: Junior counselors are 16 to 17 years old. Applicants need three written references from people who are not close relatives.
how_to_apply: Complete the camp job application (opens in December) and have three references fill out the reference form. Contact Andy Davis, Camp Director, at (217) 333-3955 or ardavis1@illinois.edu.
notes: Staff live on site during camp weeks. Program staff and senior counselors must be 18 or older. Illinois work permit rules were not checked.
duration: 2026 plan: paid training May 26 to June 1, then counselor sessions June 2 to July 30 (Camp Corral July 5 to 10)
pay_detail: Salary plus room and board. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The page says PRE-CE adds research spots for students with strong interest and promise. That includes students from rural or under-served communities. It runs next to researcHStart (a separate card).
how_to_apply: Application materials come out each fall. For PRE-CE, contact Stephanie Dietrich. She is the Senior Manager for Education. Her email is sdrich@illinois.edu.
notes: PRE-CE runs at the same time as researcHStart. The Cancer Center at Illinois is a host site for it. For researcHStart you must be 16 or older. You apply online with two recommendations and then have an in-person interview. The stipend is taxable. Dates for 2027 are not posted. Past summers ran from the second full week of June to the first week of August.
duration: About 8 weeks, 40 hours a week, from the second full week of June to the first week of August
pay_detail: $4,000 taxable stipend

who_can_apply: High school volunteers must be 14 or older. Students must provide up-to-date immunization records.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button under 'Students (college/teen)' on the Carle Foundation Hospital volunteer page (opens an online application) and send immunization records.
notes: The next listed deadline is the spring term deadline of November 15; confirm the year and current rules with Carle Volunteer Services. Other Carle sites list their own teen age ranges.
duration: By term (fall, spring, summer)
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who meet at least one condition, such as low family income, a disability, being a school dropout, homeless or foster youth, or needing extra help to finish school or get a job.
how_to_apply: The page gives no workNet address or walk-in hours. General CCRPC office: 1776 E Washington St, Urbana, IL 61802, (217) 328-3313.
notes: Eligibility rules apply, so not every teen qualifies. Call to ask about summer paid placements. The workforce site may be updated separately at eciwork.net. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated for youth. A separate Work Experience page says qualified interns can have up to 240 hours of wages covered.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 and up, with basic computer knowledge. A 9 year old who turns 10 by September 1 can ask for an exception.
how_to_apply: Register one camper per camp online when registration opens, with a $20 non-refundable deposit. Call 217-265-5342 with questions.
notes: The 2026 page says registration is closed. 2027 dates are not posted.
duration: 1 week per camp (2026 camps June 8 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Price not stated on the page. The page says free or reduced price camps may be offered to qualifying families (scholarship waiver page).

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 17. Candidates are picked through an application and interview.
how_to_apply: Email or call Stacey Clementz at the Homer Lake Interpretive Center, (217) 896-2455, or use the online volunteer application on the page.
notes: Youth program volunteers (school programs, September to May) and public program volunteers are also listed on the page; age rules for those are not stated. The District also has public volunteer events that need no application.
duration: Summer day camps (June to July per the volunteer page); weekly hours not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer position.

who_can_apply: Ages 10 to 15. Pre-registration is required.
how_to_apply: Call 217-344-7297 or visit the shelter to enroll. Payment is due when you enroll.
notes: The page does not mention volunteer age minimums. Ask the shelter about teen volunteering.
duration: Meets the 2nd Tuesday of each month, 4:00 to 5:30 pm. Four sessions a year (spring, summer, fall, winter)
pay_detail: $35 for a 3 month membership (includes a T-shirt).

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list an age range or require 4-H membership.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through ZSuite (Illinois 4-H event sign-up) when it opens. Ask for the Trailblazer scholarship in the same sign-up.
notes: Stay at Bousfield Hall, 1214 S. First St., Champaign. Refunds in 2026 had to be requested in writing by May 15. Questions: illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
duration: About 4 days, Sunday to Thursday (2026: June 21 to 25). June 2027 dates are expected.
pay_detail: 2026 price was $500 base fee plus a fee for each academy ($550 base if registered late). 2027 prices are not posted. Campus parking was $60 for the week. Need-based Trailblazer scholarships were offered.

who_can_apply: High school students with little or no Arabic. The page lists no grade or age rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and pay the $25 fee. Send a high school transcript, a note from a teacher and a scholarship form. Counselors email transcripts to silmw-uiuc@illinois.edu.
notes: The page says an early admission date gives a better chance at the largest scholarship. Dates and deadlines may change by spring. Contact: linguistics@illinois.edu, (217) 244-0661.
duration: 2 weeks, June 13 to 26, 2027 (residential)
pay_detail: Tuition is not listed on the program pages. There is a $25 application fee and a $250 deposit after admission. Scholarships are awarded based on financial need and/or academic merit. The page says its 2026 program was funded by a Qatar Foundation International grant.

who_can_apply: High school students who are rising sophomores through seniors. Students come from around the country.
how_to_apply: Register on the page starting Nov 1, 2026. For the scholarship, also submit a one-page essay on why you want to be an architect by the deadline.
notes: Contact: Elizabeth Abosch, eabosch2@illinois.edu. There are no refunds if you cancel, miss days or come for part of it. Sign up early, because spots fill.
duration: One week, July 11 to 17, 2027 (residential, on campus)
pay_detail: Program fee $1,300 (includes lodging and meals). The page also mentions a $100 non-refundable fee. A partial-tuition scholarship for two students is offered (apply with a one-page essay).

who_can_apply: Each camp lists its own ages. In 2026 camps were for ages 10 and up (some 10 to 17, some 12 and up). Check the age before registering.
how_to_apply: Registration opens when 2027 details are posted on the MakerLab summer page. A $20 non-refundable deposit applies.
notes: 2026 camps ran June 1 to July 31. Lunch supervision and late pickup were $10 a day each.
duration: 1 week, 3 hours a day (morning or afternoon sessions)
pay_detail: $250 a week in 2026. Optional lunch hour supervision and late pickup were $10 a day each.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors at Champaign-Urbana high schools (per the College of LAS page). You should be curious about science and health.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Email uiuc-spheres@illinois.edu.
notes: The LAS page lists neuroscience, molecular and integrative physiology and sociology as research areas. Ask about the exact eligibility because the two pages describe it differently.
duration: 6 weeks in summer (exact dates not posted)
pay_detail: $2,400 summer stipend for successful participation

who_can_apply: Junior high and senior high music students. The 2026 senior band page said students completing grades 8 to 12. Students bring their own instruments. Some ensembles need an audition video.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the ISYM site when it opens. Questions: music@illinois.edu or 217-333-2620. Students must provide their own instruments.
notes: Prices were checked for the senior band only. The 2026 senior session was July 6 to 11. Read each ensemble page for its cost and rules.
duration: 1 week per ensemble
pay_detail: 2026 Senior Band cost: $775 resident (housing and meals) or $575 commuter. Other ensembles may differ.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 16 or older who meets the health requirements and passes a background check. The page has no separate teen program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application. Show your shot records. Finish a background check. To reach Volunteer Services, call (217) 443-5279. Or write to SHMC.VolunteerServices@osfhealthcare.org.
notes: The hospital page now uses the name OSF Sacred Heart Medical Center - Urbana. The page does not say if the application is open right now, so call first. The page does not show an application link.
duration: 3 to 4 hours a week for at least 6 months (encouraged)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: The page says 15 year olds can apply for lifeguard and swim instructor. Minimum ages for other jobs are not stated; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the District's job listings (linked from the Employment Opportunities page). Aquatics questions: Ryan Hays, ryan.hays@champaignparks.org. HR: hr@champaignparks.org.
notes: Lifeguard classes are run by the District in Champaign-Urbana. Concession workers get a paid-for Food Handler's certification. Illinois requires an employment certificate under age 16 (see the Illinois rules on this site).
duration: Seasonal jobs run April to November and do not exceed 6 months; summer camp is a 10-week program
pay_detail: Paid job. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages. Lifeguard certification is covered 100% by the Park District.

who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 years old who are enthusiastic, hardworking and willing to learn. Teen volunteers may work at most 25 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Champaign Park District Volunteer Portal, then view opportunities. Questions: volunteer@champaignparks.org.
notes: Some roles (for example Prairie Farm) run only part of the year.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid. Hours can count toward high school volunteer requirements.

who_can_apply: At least 15 years old, attending an area high school or home-schooled, with course prerequisites and assessment requirements met. For high school credit you also need your school's approval and good standing.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply page under Dual Credit. Early College Services: 217-353-2663, earlycollege@parkland.edu (office U214).
notes: Early College students do not qualify for financial aid. Credit and grades go on a permanent Parkland transcript. The Early College page also lists an Early College and Career Academy with programs such as Automotive Technology, Certified Nurse Assistant and EMS.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Tuition is not stated on this page. It says courses are affordable and in some cases reduced or tuition-free.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 18. Each camp sets its own age range, and the student must meet it by the first day of camp.
how_to_apply: Register online at parkland.edu/ceRegister, by phone at 217-351-2235, or in person at Community Education, 1315 North Mattis Ave, Champaign. Ask about scholarships on the page.
notes: Camps cost money. Check each camp page for its price and ages. Scholarships are for families with financial need and are first-come, first-served.
duration: Varies by camp
pay_detail: Fee varies by camp. The page says scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Any junior or senior in the Parkland College district. Home school and private school students can apply through the ECCA office.
how_to_apply: Ask your high school counselor for the ECCA application, apply to Parkland as an Early College student if needed, and return the ECCA form with a parent signature to your counselor. Call 217-355-1382 or email nelder@efe.k12.il.us.
notes: Students need their own ride to Parkland and to off-campus clinical or job-site visits. ECCA follows the Parkland calendar, not the high school calendar.
duration: Mostly a full school year; classes 7:30 to 9:30 am on Parkland days
pay_detail: Not a job. Many high schools pay the cost, but it varies. The FAQ says financial aid is not available for dual credit students. Textbooks are loaned.

who_can_apply: High school and homeschooled students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2026 who live in the Unit 4, Urbana or Rantoul school districts.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Summer Start link on the Parkland page. A student and parent orientation is required. Contact summerstart@parkland.edu or 217-353-2346.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted yet. MTD bus vouchers were offered to students in Champaign, Urbana and Savoy who needed a ride to campus.
duration: 2026: June 1 to June 11, Monday to Thursday, 3 hours a day
pay_detail: Up to $250, paid at the end for attendance. Each missed day lowers the total.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20. Members must keep a passing GPA and complete community service.
how_to_apply: Download the application on the city page, sign it, and mail or drop it off to Champaign Police Department, ATTN: Youth Police Explorer Post 258, 82 E. University Ave., Champaign, IL 61820. Questions: Detective Michael Talbott, 217-403-6900.
notes: Members must go to meetings, keep a passing GPA and do community service.
duration: Meetings every other Thursday
pay_detail: No pay or fee stated.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. If you are 16 or 17 you need a signed waiver from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer application, then schedule the required interview. Contact: Eva Liu, Volunteer Coordinator, volunteer@champaign.org, 217-403-2000 x3.
notes: Open roles change, so look at the current listings on the page. The Douglass Branch's Club Fred program is a summer role.
duration: Typically 2 to 3 hours a week; a 4-month minimum is preferred
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Pre-college students entering the listed grades in the fall. Students from other countries may apply for the residential camps only (Camp FAQs page).
how_to_apply: Camp application (with the scholarship application inside it). See the Camp FAQs for the process.
notes: Costs do not include travel to campus. Some camps are EAGER or IDEA camps focused on broadening participation, open to all to apply. Use the WYSE mailing list for next year's dates.
duration: One week per camp (June to August in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: residential $1,500, commuter $750, day camp $550, each plus a $25 deposit. The Trail Blazer Scholarship covers 50% or 100% for students who meet its criteria.

who_can_apply: Local high school students (the page does not give exact ages or the list of schools). Placements depend on student interest and the number of campus openings.
how_to_apply: The page is written for campus departments that host a student. It does not say how a teen applies. Contact Tori Exum at texum@uillinois.edu (the team listing shows texum@illinois.edu, so check which is current), or the IHR general line at 217-333-2137.
notes: The university runs a background check for students under 18. Illinois work permit rules for workers under 18 were not checked.
duration: 8 weeks (June 15 to Aug 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: $15.00 per hour, up to 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders who live in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa or Wisconsin. No international applicants. No course prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Online application with student information, two personal statements and a teacher, mentor or counselor recommendation form (emailed after you submit). Join the Summer Program Notifications mailing list for next year's dates.
notes: Competitive: applications are ranked together, not first come first served. Housing is for selected students who do not live locally. Students get no course credit.
duration: 6 weeks (research began June 17 and ended July 31 in 2026); 30 to 35 hours a week
pay_detail: No cost except transportation. Housing, meals and a monetary award are provided (the page calls it a fellowship payment; the amount is not stated).

who_can_apply: Champaign Unit 4 students ages 14 to 19.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Youth Employment Services page on the Champaign Unit 4 School District website (linked from the city page). That school page would not load for us, so confirm the steps with the district.
notes: Only for students who attend Champaign Unit 4 schools. Illinois work permit rules were not checked.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Paid. The city page says the 2024 summer placement was a six-week, 105-hour paid work experience. Pay rate not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 can volunteer on their own with a parent or guardian signing the consent. Under 14 may not volunteer alone.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Or email volunteer@urbanafree.org. Teens 14 to 18 need a parent or guardian to read and sign a consent form. They must do it before the first onboarding interview. The paper form asks for two references who are not family.
notes: Roles marked with a star on the form (Teen Open Lab, Computer Lab, Archives, Seed Exchange, Home Delivery Driver) need extra interviews and longer commitments. Teen Open Lab shifts are Monday to Thursday 3 to 5:30 pm. Library hours are on the form. Phone 217-367-4057.
duration: At least 3 months, at least 1 hour a week, shifts up to 3 hours. Some roles need a longer commitment.
pay_detail: Unpaid (the form says no money is paid)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who have completed 7th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application (PDF or online form on the Teen Programs page). Questions: Cathy Schneider, cmschneider@urbanaparks.org.
notes: The page does not say whether CITs are paid, so ask before applying. The page does not say whether the program runs in 2027; contact Cathy Schneider (cmschneider@urbanaparks.org) for next year's details.
duration: 15 to 20 hours a week, three days a week, June 3 to July 31 in 2026 (8:15 am to 3 pm)
pay_detail: No wage is listed on the page; it is described as training for future summer and part-time jobs. Confirm with the contact.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. A parent or guardian must complete the Volunteer Waiver first.
how_to_apply: Show up. A guardian signs the Volunteer Waiver and emails it to Connor Ross (cjross@urbanaparks.org, 217-384-4062) or brings a printed copy on the day.
notes: Meets about every two weeks at different parks (Victory, Meadowbrook, Weaver, Crystal Lake, Busey Woods). The same page lists a free Teen Hangout Zone for grades 6 to 12 on select Fridays at Phillips Recreation Center.
duration: 2 hours per event (2 to 4 pm Saturdays)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can earn service hours and references.

who_can_apply: Age 15 and older. The page says you need consistent availability and a year-round commitment, including during the school year.
how_to_apply: Use the View open positions link on the city jobs page. The page also links to a separate certification and training page.
notes: Not stated on the program page whether a work permit is needed. Pay may have changed since January 2025.
duration: Peak season May to July: 20 to 40 hours a week. August to April: 5 to 20 hours a week.
pay_detail: Lifeguard I starts at $17.79 per hour. Lifeguard II (Swim Instructor) starts at $18.67 per hour. These rates are listed as of January 2025 on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. A Teen Application is on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Application on the page or call (480) 256-7086. Steps are an interview, a health check and a background check (3 to 4 weeks). You also need shot records and a TB test. Then you go to orientation.
notes: Min age is 16 for all volunteers. The page does not give a teen age cap.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours, one 4-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 at the Hamilton and Basha branches. Ages 13 to 17 at the Sunset and Downtown branches. You can apply to only one branch.
how_to_apply: Pick one branch and read its dates. Fill out the linked application form. If there is no link, there are no openings. Watch for confirmation emails, then attend the mandatory overview or training.
notes: Submitting an application does not guarantee a spot. The program is not a good fit for teens who will miss 2 or more shifts.
duration: One set shift each week for a semester, quarter or summer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: The library's volunteer interest form offers the age choices 14-17 and 18 and older. The page does not state a separate minimum age.
how_to_apply: Read the position descriptions, then fill out the volunteer interest form on the library's Volunteer with us page and pick Youth Event Support Volunteer.
notes: The 14 to 17 range comes from the age options on the interest form, not from a written rule. Call 919-968-2777 or email library@chapelhillnc.gov to confirm the minimum age and hours. The library also has a Teen Room for ages 13 to 18; no teen advisory board was listed on the pages.
duration: Ongoing; most needed in summer and on afternoons and weekends in the school year

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall after the program. A 3.0 GPA or higher is suggested. You should like research or health science.
how_to_apply: For a waitlist spot, email the program director, Dr. Hamid Montazeri, using the contact on the program page. Watch the page for the next registration.
notes: You get a certificate of completion and can ask for a letter of reference. Sessions are online and in person. The page lists a full refund if you cancel by June 29, 2026.
duration: 3 weeks. In 2026 it ran July 13 to July 31.
pay_detail: The page lists the total cost for 2025 as $1,503. It does not list a 2026 price. Cost covers lab access, food on in-person days and materials.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 in the fall after the program. Students who just finished high school can join too. A 3.5 GPA or higher is suggested.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer 2027 priority list form on the program page. You will be told when registration opens. Questions go to program director Dr. Ann Gordon.
notes: 2026 was the first year of this program. You get a certificate of completion.
duration: Weekdays 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: The 2027 cost is not posted yet. You also buy an SPSS grad pack for about $34.95 and bring your own laptop.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12 for the 2026-27 school year. No prior experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list for 2027 on the program page. Sign up for each workshop on the same page when it opens.
notes: Workshops are at the Keck Center for Science and Engineering, 450 N. Center St., Orange. Questions: engineering@chapman.edu or 714-516-5616.
duration: Workshops. The 2026 bioprinting workshop was one day.
pay_detail: The cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Children and teens ages 5 to 18. The page does not list residency rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out a member form in the online member portal. It is linked from the Membership page. Phone 434-971-9400 or email admin@bgclubcva.org.
notes: There are six clubs: Albemarle Campus, Cherry Avenue, James River, Madison, Orange and Southwood. UpNext is named only on the home page. Ask the Southwood Club how to join and what it pays.
duration: Ongoing; open after school and all day in summer
pay_detail: Low membership dues, amount not stated. UpNext pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Children ages 12 to 17 may volunteer if a parent or guardian is with them for each shift. In the Food Recovery Area, ages 12 to 16 need a parent or guardian at each shift. Volunteers ages 17 and older may work there without an adult after an initial shift with an adult. Youth groups ages 12 to 15 need one adult chaperone for every 3 children. Youth groups ages 16 and 17 need one adult for every 6 youth. Volunteers must be 18 or older at the Winchester warehouse.
how_to_apply: Create your own account on the online volunteer calendar. It is required for safety and communication. Then register for a shift. If you do not get a confirmation email, the registration did not go through. Contact the volunteer team at volunteer@brafb.org. Group sizes are 4 to 8 people at most locations. They are up to 10 at the Verona warehouse. Everyone needs their own account.
notes: A parent or guardian must be at every shift for ages 12 to 17, so this works best for families. The page lists the front desk as (540) 268-3663. The footer lists 540-248-3663. Confirm which number is right. The page names the Charlottesville warehouse and offsite locations under the 12 to 17 rule with a parent or guardian at each shift, and names the Winchester warehouse as 18 and older.
duration: One shift at a time. Shift length is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts

who_can_apply: High school students in the Charlottesville area. Grade levels are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form on the C3 youth page.
notes: The same page says C3 takes high school and college interns each term. Work includes grants, policy, marketing and energy checks. Pay and ages are not stated. See the careers page of C3.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The page says paid interns lead the group but does not say if teen members are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. The page welcomes volunteers ages 14 and up. Groups with people under 18 need at least one adult chaperone for every 10 children.
how_to_apply: Use the Schedule Orientation or Volunteer Application link on the SPCA volunteer page to choose an orientation date and fill out the volunteer application. Orientation comes before you take on tasks. Contact: volunteer@caspca.org or 434-973-5959 ext. 314.
notes: The pages do not say if 14 to 17 year olds need a parent signature. They do not say if there are limits on which animals teens can work with. Ask at orientation. The apply link goes to the SPCA's event calendar on a third party site.
duration: Ongoing. Hours and length are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The volunteer pays a $25 volunteer fee plus a separate $9 background check. The page does not say if either is refundable.

who_can_apply: Classes are free for Charlottesville City Schools and Albemarle County Public Schools students. The pages do not list grade levels. They do not list the steps to enroll.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe an enrollment process. Ask your school counselor. Contact CATEC at 434-245-2419 or catecinfo@charlottesvilleschools.org. The 2026 to 2027 Program of Studies PDF is linked from the CATEC high school program of studies page.
notes: Confirm first. Grade levels and enrollment steps are not on the pages. For 2026 to 2027, CATEC does not offer some academic courses. They are Biology II, English 12, USA Government, and Economics and Personal Finance. EMT and Fire Science are no longer dual enrollment through CVCC. Students still earn CTE credits. Address: 1000 East Rio Road, Charlottesville.
duration: School year classes. Program lengths and schedules are not stated on the program pages.
pay_detail: Free for Charlottesville City and Albemarle County students. Students earn high school elective credits, can earn industry certifications, and some programs offer dual enrollment college credit. Transportation to and from your base school is provided.

who_can_apply: Charlottesville-area youth 14 to 21 (14 by the start of the CAYIP Academy). City of Charlottesville residents get priority. Parent or guardian must also complete paperwork for youth under 18.
how_to_apply: Submit the CAYIP application (questionnaire, inventory and agreement to participate) during the session window, then a one-on-one interview. Accepted youth attend the mandatory paid CAYIP Academy. Contact: cayipinquiries@charlottesville.gov, 434-987-0018.
notes: Applications are only accepted during a session window. Transportation is not provided. Interns may miss at most 5 days per session. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers must get an Employment Certificate before any work; the page does not mention it, so ask CAYIP staff how it is handled.
duration: School-year sessions: up to 10 hours a week for 8 weeks (Fall 2026: Sept 14 to Nov 8). Summer session: 20 hours a week for 6 weeks.
pay_detail: Performance-based stipend up to $15 per hour

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Virginia Wing site lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18. The national Civil Air Patrol page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Send the squadron a message on Facebook or email 091.pa@vawg.cap.gov and they will be in touch. The Virginia Wing headquarters number on the page is 804-454-7356.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron page gives no street address, so ask for the exact meeting location before you go. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets each Tuesday from 7 to 9 p.m. at Lakeside Middle School.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says the program is for up to twelve city students. A related summer internship for four Charlottesville High School youth is supported in part by the city youth internship program (CAYIP).
how_to_apply: This is not listed. Email grow@cultivatecharlottesville.org or call 434-365-4529. Ask how to join.
notes: Pay, ages and how to apply are not posted, so ask first. The nonprofit lists "Food Justice Interns" under its City Schoolyard Garden program. Apprentice jobs on the page are for young adults, not teens.
duration: 8 weeks, 20 hours per week
pay_detail: Not stated. The City Schoolyard Garden page, checked on 2026-10-10, calls other roles paid but gives no pay for these interns. Ask first.

who_can_apply: Habitat Store: age 12 and up (ages 12 and 13 must come with a parent, guardian or older sibling). Construction site: at least 16. Power tools: at least 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a Habitat Store orientation or a building shift. Use the VolunteerHub links on the volunteer page. For Youth Build Days, email volunteer@cvillehabitat.org.
notes: Teens under 16 cannot work on the construction site. Habitat clubs at local high schools have regular volunteer chances; ask your school.
duration: Ongoing; shifts vary
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Open to all. The high school track is for rising 9th graders through college freshmen. Tuition help is offered. The site also runs free workshops for under-resourced youth (KEEP it Reel).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a workshop in the online store (first-time users make an Amilia account). Ask for tuition assistance with the online form. Email programs@lighthousestudio.org or call 434-293-6992.
notes: Light House also lists a Careers page, an Adrenaline Film Project (Nov 5 to 8, 2026) and a Youth Film Festival. Those were not read in detail.
duration: 1 to 2 weeks, 9am to 3pm (2026 listed dates June 1 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the program page. Tuition assistance is available, reviewed case by case and first come first served.

who_can_apply: High school students. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Contact Education Director Daniel Kunkel. Use the contact link on the Live Arts education page.
notes: The page gives no dates, cost, or application. Confirm the program still runs. Live Arts also lists Teen Studio (ages 14 to 18) as a class, not a job.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The Live Arts education page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask the Education Director.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. The page prefers 14 and up but will consider mature, motivated 13 year olds. Attending an Earth Roots or other teen camp session is preferred. The teen, not a parent, fills out the application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application on the page when it reopens. Waitlist or questions: connect@livingearthva.org or 434-260-0086.
notes: A leadership program, not a job. The school also runs a Teen Apprentice Program (about $3,315 tuition) that was not carded.
duration: 1 or more weeks (2026 day CIT weeks June 22 to July 24; overnight weeks June 14 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Teens pay: day CIT $365 per week, overnight CIT $515 per week (2026). No pay or stipend is mentioned. A scholarship fund exists.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in the Charlottesville area who are Music Resource Center members. Members must be in 6th to 12th grade and go to school each day.
how_to_apply: Become an MRC member (drop in at 105 Ridge St, Mon to Fri 2:30 to 7pm, no appointment), then fill out the wait list form on the MRC Certified page. Phone 434-979-5478, musicresourcecenter@gmail.com.
notes: Sophomores and younger can ask to join the wait list, but exceptions are not likely. Work permit rules for Virginia were not checked.
duration: Studio track: 32 hours of lessons plus 10 to 20 paid hours. Live sound track: 28 hours of lessons plus 10 to 20 paid hours.
pay_detail: Paid a competitive wage above the state minimum for 10 to 20 internship hours. The training is free for members. Membership fees are a sliding scale from $1 to $250 a year based on family income.

who_can_apply: Listed for ages 15 and up. Everyone must pass the in-water pretest or be removed from the class.
how_to_apply: Register through the city's Registration & Tickets system. Within 72 hours of registering, email swimprograms@charlottesville.gov with the subject Lifeguard Pretest to book the pretest at least 8 days ahead.
notes: The page does not say the class leads to a job. The city lists seasonal and variable-hour jobs on governmentjobs.com; none were open on 2026-10-09. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before any work.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Course fee not stated on the page (an optional CPR mask is $15).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 15 (must be 13 by June 1). The page lists no grade or school rule.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through the Y account system (Daxko) and pay the fee. Weekly sign up closes two weeks before each week. Money help is on the scholarship page. Contact youth@piedmontymca.org or 434-270-7534.
notes: A paid program for teens, not a job. It is a leadership step toward working as a camp counselor later. A Greene County CIT program is also listed on the Y site but was not read.
duration: Up to 9 weeks (2026: June 8 to Aug 7), 7:30am to 5:30pm, plus free training June 1 to 5
pay_detail: Teens pay. $50 registration, then $175 per week for YMCA members or $200 per week for non-members. The June 1 to 5 training week is free. No wages or stipend are listed.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at a school that takes part. You must meet the rules to join, and your school and a parent or guardian must say yes. Homeschooled juniors and seniors can take Dual Credit classes. Freshmen and sophomores are looked at one by one.
how_to_apply: For dual enrollment, sign up with your high school counselor. For Dual Credit, apply through PVCC admissions at admissions@pvcc.edu.
notes: More than 1,200 high school students join each term. Early College has rules to qualify. It may have district scholarships.
duration: Each semester
pay_detail: Dual enrollment classes taught in your high school are no cost to the student. Dual Credit classes taken on your own outside the school day require tuition.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers ages 15 to 18 for the summer months.
how_to_apply: The page has a general volunteer link (Apply here). It does not say it is for junior volunteers. Call the volunteer office to ask.
notes: Only the age range and summer timing are posted. GPA, grade, hours, and deadlines are not stated. Confirm everything before applying.
duration: Summer months; hours not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth who live in Charlottesville City or Albemarle County. You can be in grade 7 up to high school graduation.
how_to_apply: Send one form for each student on the program Application and Wait List page. Contact partnerships@virginia.edu or 434-924-2414.
notes: Pay and internship details are not posted. Ask the office. There is a wait list.
duration: Ongoing; summer camps for younger students and internships for high schoolers
pay_detail: Paid internship placements for high schoolers. Pay rate and hours are not stated on the page. The program itself is free, with transport and meals provided.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders who are 15 to 18 years old by the program start date. Design-curious students are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form by the deadline. Include a note for the scholarship review. Free Zoom info sessions ran Dec to March. Questions: program director Kyle Sturgeon, sturgeon@virginia.edu.
notes: Summer 2026 was fully enrolled. Each session has 20 students and at most 10 can stay overnight in UVA dorms. Day students commute.
duration: 6 days, 9am to 4pm (2026 sessions June 8 to 13 and June 22 to 27)
pay_detail: Tuition by household income. Under $100k: tuition waived. $100k to $160k: $1,350 (day) or $1,600 (overnight). $160k and up: $1,650 (day) or $1,900 (overnight). Overnight adds $250 in the listed prices.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with strong academic records. The page gives no GPA cutoff. Housing is not provided and high school students cannot use UVA housing unless they are in UVA Advance.
how_to_apply: Send the Online Non-Degree Student form and choose Summer Session. Send a Medical Consent Form for Minors signed by a parent. Ask your counselor or principal for a Secondary School Report and your transcript. Contact summer@virginia.edu or 434-924-3371.
notes: Families set up their own housing. For a live in option, see the separate UVA Advance card.
duration: One course per session; session dates not read
pay_detail: 2026 tuition listed per credit hour: $484 for Virginia residents or $1,787 for non-residents, plus a one-time comprehensive fee ($493 or $553) for on-Grounds courses. The page does not say which rate high schoolers pay, so ask the office.

who_can_apply: Students at Charlottesville schools (middle schools, Charlottesville High zones and Lugo-McGinness Academy). Also students who live in the city but go to a private school, are homeschooled, or go to school out of the district. The council picks its 15 members. Ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Youth Opportunity Coordination page. Call Juanika Howard at 434-529-7978. She helps youth find ways to take part.
notes: Seats are set by school and grade, so only some seats may be open at a time. Ask the coordinator when applications open.
duration: School year, monthly meetings
pay_detail: Not stated. Treat as unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 10 to 12. You send an application and two references who are not relatives. You also do a 15-minute interview.
how_to_apply: New LITs fill out the online application and have two references send the reference form. Returning LITs use a separate form. Then a 15-minute interview.
notes: This costs money and is not a paid job. You must attend at least 85% of your session. Dates shown are from summer 2026.
duration: 1 to 4 weeks, Monday to Friday about 8:30 am to 3:45 pm, plus a one-day training
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs $500 per session for new LITs, $450 for returning LITs. You earn about 140 volunteer service hours per session.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. The page lists no ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Water Warriors page. You can also sign up there for emails about Water Warriors news and events.
notes: In summer, high school students can test water samples, check CASSI units and clean trash traps with staff. Contact: Jillian Griffin, jgriffin@chattahoochee.org, or 404-352-9828.
duration: School-year program Oct 2026 to April 2027; summer shadowing for high schoolers (dates not stated)
pay_detail: Not stated. The page describes service hours and does not mention pay or a cost.

pay_detail: The program is free. Pay for the jobs it links to is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ambitious high school juniors at schools that partner with Genesys Works. Must be on track to graduate, able to work in the U.S., and able to have a lighter class schedule senior year for internship hours.

pay_detail: No fee or pay stated on the program pages

pay_detail: Stipend of $17.05 per hour through After School Matters (2026 page)

pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.

duration: Single events on select days through the year
pay_detail: Free

pay_detail: 2026: $16.20 per hour, 14.5 hours a week for 5 weeks, about $1,174.50 before taxes (may change)

The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

pay_detail: Weekly meetings appear unpaid; the page says community engagement and extra leadership work is paid. Rates not stated.

who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents who are sophomores, juniors or seniors in 2026-27. You need a B or 3.0 average and a household income under $80,000 a year. You must be able to keep the daily schedule.
how_to_apply: Sign up at the apply portal. Upload your transcript, resume, essay and an income form signed by a parent or guardian. Name two people who will recommend you. Contact: info@chicagobusinessinstitute.org or (312) 545-7855.
notes: The site shows two email endings, org and com; use the org address on the apply page. The apply page does not state pay or job sites. The home page says the program was founded to provide paid summer internships and mentions placements (one student interned with the City of Chicago), but no pay amount is given, so ask the office. Two recommendation letters are needed, so ask early. Illinois work permit rule not checked.
duration: Six weeks
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. Ask the office.

who_can_apply: You must have been in CPS this year and last year. You will be a junior or senior. You have a strong record in the hardest courses you can take. You are ready for college work.
how_to_apply: Fill out an online application. It has short essays, a graded work sample, a teacher recommendation and transcripts. It also has an online interview in mid-August. For the $0 tuition option, you need financial aid papers.
notes: UChicago classes do not follow the CPS calendar, so you attend even when your high school is on break. Many students stop after Winter Quarter.
duration: Autumn, Winter and Spring Quarters; one course per quarter
pay_detail: $800 tuition plus $75 lifetime transcript fee (books not included) if household income is over $60,000. $0 tuition, with books and fees covered, if under $60,000.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who are at least 16 by June 14, 2027 and live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana. College freshmen and sophomores can also apply. Must commit to both summers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in recommendations. At least one must be a teacher or professor. Up to 12 applicants are accepted.
notes: You must find your own housing and ride to UChicago. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. One application covers all the UChicago cancer pathway programs that fit you.
duration: Two summers of 8 weeks (2027: June 14 to Aug 6, 35 to 40 hours a week) plus monthly 2 to 4 hour online sessions from Feb 2027 to Dec 2028
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $5,000 per year

who_can_apply: Full-time high school students who live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, and can attend every weekday, 4 hours a day. Up to 20 students per year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: Virtual program run with Kentucky, Michigan, Penn and UT Austin. No minimum age is listed. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for the stipend.
duration: 2 weeks, July 12 to 23, 2027, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to noon CT, online
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old (some roles need 18+). Applicants for the Summer Volunteer Program must be at least 18 at the time the application is submitted. Must interview, pass health screening, a drug screen and a background check, and not hold certain visas (B-1, B-2, H-1B, H-4).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Volunteer application. Do it when a recruiting window is open. The form is in Volgistics. Then you talk with Volunteer Services in an interview. For questions, write to vservices@uchicagomedicine.org. You can also call 773-702-4421.
notes: The page says student volunteers must be at least 16, and some opportunities need 18 or older. The page says summer applicants must be at least 18 when the application is submitted. Summer applications open early March 2027. Next student cycle starts January 10, 2027.
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for at least 6 months or one school year; 100 hours within a year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, are at least 16 by June 14, 2027, and can commit to all 8 weeks. Max 30 students across all sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Pick your site: UChicago, UIC, UIUC, Northwestern downtown or Rush. Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: No housing or ride is provided, so pick only sites you can reach. The application asks for your GPA and a transcript. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027, 35 to 40 hours a week
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $4,000

who_can_apply: High school students. The application shows which programs you are eligible for based on your current grade. Chicagoland students can choose to commute for Career Insight and Immersion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a profile, transcript, writing sample, supplement and one recommendation letter. It also needs a parent okay and the $75 fee. Test scores are not required. You may rank up to four program choices but can be admitted to one.
notes: Expensive, not a job. Apply by the priority deadline if you need financial aid. Aid is limited and first come, first served.
duration: Varies by program. Online courses run 3 to 5 weeks and the language institute runs 6 to 8 weeks; the page does not state a length for enrichment.
pay_detail: Costs in 2026: Enrichment $3,000; Career Insight $5,890 ($4,100 commuting); Immersion $9,300 ($6,100 commuting); Practicum $15,200; online 3 to 5 weeks $4,980. Need-based partial aid is offered (not full), and Enrichment fees can be waived for income under $125,000. $75 application fee.

who_can_apply: For the Tech and AI day in 2026: students entering grade 10, 11 or 12 with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, interested in business and in UIC for fall 2027. Rules for the other days were not posted.
how_to_apply: Email bizsummer@uic.edu or call 312-996-2700 to ask about 2027. The 2026 events used an online registration form on the UIC events site.
notes: Seats were limited and filled. Grade and GPA rules above are from only one of the four days, so confirm before applying.
duration: One series of four days, June 23 to 26, 2026 (each day run by a different department)
pay_detail: The Tech and AI day was free with breakfast and lunch. Cost for other days was not stated.

who_can_apply: The page says the program includes 25 neighborhood high school teens, run with After School Matters. The page does not list an age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply link on the Youth Farm page (an online form). Questions: Aurea France, Manager of Education and Wellness, per the page.
notes: Run in partnership with After School Matters. Confirm ages, dates and pay before relying on this. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.
duration: Spring, summer and fall growing seasons
pay_detail: Stipend: 4 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 hours a week in summer. Rate not stated.

who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job. The youngest age in the whole program is 14, but most summer jobs are for 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 and 15 who live in Chicago. At least half of participants come from priority groups (for example youth with disabilities, English learners, youth in foster care or experiencing homelessness).
how_to_apply: Apply through the online Chicago Youth Works application. Youth under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form if offered a position. Partner agencies contact applicants directly.
notes: The Chicago Youth Works FAQ says youth under 16 may be required to have a work permit; Illinois law requires one for most under-16 jobs, issued through the school district or ISBE. Ask the program whether a stipend program needs one. The FAQ says the Chicago Housing Authority, After School Matters and DFSS each also have a limited number of slots for 14 and 15 year olds.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Current juniors at a public high school in Los Angeles County. You need papers to work legally in California. You should have strong grades and a real interest in science.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need an essay, a transcript and one letter from a science or math teacher or a counselor. Your letter is only asked for after the rest is done, so finish early. Info sessions are held in November and January.
notes: Very competitive. If you accept, you must turn down all other summer programs and go to every required meeting. The page mixes dates from different years, so check it again in November. Questions: Danielle Nunez, danunez@chla.usc.edu. Ask whether you need a work permit for the stipend.
duration: Summer lab work, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday, for 7 weeks. College counseling runs from April through senior year.
pay_detail: Stipend, plus a Metro card and meals at the hospital. The page does not give the amount.

who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the CHP post page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Volunteer Application, submit a school recommendation form from a teacher, counselor or administrator, interview, finish health screenings, pass the orientation quiz and attend the mandatory orientation.
notes: The hospital's general volunteer program is age 16 and up. Perks listed include free parking, a food voucher, a free uniform and a free TB test. The next cycle should be the December 30 spring deadline, but the page gives no year, so confirm.
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: There is a separate application for ages 16 to 17. Animal care and docent roles are 18 and up. Animal care also needs 100 hours of earlier volunteering.
how_to_apply: Submit the 16-17 volunteer application. Then go to the next orientation. They tell you about it by email.
notes: The center does not take court-ordered community service right now. If you have questions, write to volunteers@thelivingcoast.org.
duration: Ongoing, based on availability. In animal care, 3 absences within 60 days may result in losing your spot.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Volunteer team applicants should be in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer team form linked on the 10x10 Teen Art Expo page when applications open. Teen artists (age and grade rules for artists are not stated) can submit art when submissions open in mid November 2026. Museum phone: 513-721-2787.
notes: The museum has other volunteer groups. They are docents, visitor service aides, REC volunteers and CAM Cruiser volunteers. The main volunteer page does not state ages for them. Ask the museum before applying to those.
duration: The team meets 4 to 6 p.m. on the first Thursday of each month plus extra dates as needed, and must be free for the opening on Saturday April 10, 2027. The exhibition runs April 6 to 11, 2027.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer team

who_can_apply: The Clubs are open to youth ages 5 to 18 across Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. All youth are welcome, with no income rules. The page does not give an age range for the teen Workforce Development program itself.
how_to_apply: Click Enroll Today on the Join the Clubs page (it goes to the Club portal), or contact your preferred Club for help with the application. After acceptance, families get any extra forms. Phone: 513-421-8909. Email: info@bgcgc.org. Main office: 1205 Dewey Ave., Cincinnati, OH 45205.
notes: Confirm first. The pages do not list teen ages, teen hours, or any teen jobs. No Junior Staff program is mentioned. Clubs are at Price Hill, Avondale, Eastgate and East Westwood in Ohio. They are at Newport and Covington in Kentucky. There is also a Western & Southern Workforce Development Center.
duration: Summer: June 1 to July 31, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. School year: August 17 to May 14, Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 7:30 p.m. (hours vary by Club).
pay_detail: Free. The summer and school year programs are listed as completely free. The page does not say that teens are paid.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in high school or home-schooled, ages 14 to 18. It is a select group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the C-YA Teen Council application form on the page.
notes: The CAC teen page also lists a free Young Adult Lab on Thursdays 4 to 6 pm (open to all teens) and a Teen Art Show for ages 13 to 19. The page says enrollment for the 26-27 school year has begun and does not post a 2027-28 date. Call 513-345-8400 to confirm the current schedule.
duration: September to May, one meeting a month
pay_detail: Free to join. Dinner is provided at meetings. Perks: free admission, discounted tickets, field trips to museums and universities in another city.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Advanced dancers who have at least two full years on pointe. No audition.
how_to_apply: Sign up online when it opens. Use the Learn more link for the Ballet Intensive on the CCM Prep teen programs page.
notes: The opening date is only given as January 2027, so no day is stored. Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu.
duration: June 5 to 13, 2027 (housing check-in June 4)
pay_detail: Tuition $750. Housing is an extra $1,000.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders with a strong interest in musical theatre. An audition (video) is required.
how_to_apply: Audition through Acceptd. Choose CCM Prep: Musical Theatre Intensive. Get ready a headshot and a resume. Prepare a 60 to 90 second monologue from a published play written after 1950 and two songs (one from a musical written before 1970, one written after 1970). Send a 30 to 60 second video of you dancing alone.
notes: Housing is optional and costs extra. Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu. Tuition assistance may exist; ask CCM Prep.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks. 2027 sessions: June 14 to 20 or July 12 to 18 (1 week); June 14 to 26 or July 12 to 24 (2 weeks)
pay_detail: Tuition: $1,000 per 1-week session or $2,000 per 2-week session. Housing is an extra fee ($1,000 for a week, $1,800 for two weeks). $35 audition fee; email ccmsummer@ucmail.uc.edu about fee waivers.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12 who play a string instrument. You need to audition. You also need one letter of support.
how_to_apply: Audition through Acceptd. Choose CCM Prep: Strings Intensive. Send a headshot and two different pieces, 8 to 10 minutes in all. Send a letter from a teacher or pro.
notes: Contact CCM Prep at 513-556-2595 or ccmprep@uc.edu.
duration: June 5 to 12, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition $900. $35 audition fee; email ccmsummer@ucmail.uc.edu about fee waivers.

who_can_apply: High school seniors who are about to graduate, from the Cincinnati area.
how_to_apply: Apply online between Nov 1 and Feb 1. Questions: hssummerinternship@cchmc.org.
notes: The page does not give the year for Nov 1 and Feb 1; the year is inferred from the line that the new program starts in summer 2027. More details are to be posted. Pay and exact dates are not posted yet.
duration: One month, starting summer 2027
pay_detail: Not stated for the new program. The program page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. The old program was a paid, part-time position.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade. Seniors still in high school in spring must use the high school application.
how_to_apply: Submit the application packet by the posted due date, then attend a parent information session, an in-person interview and an orientation. Medical screening and a background check are required.
notes: Competitive: only the highest scoring applicants are accepted. Volunteers must complete at least 80 percent of their scheduled shifts. The hospital does not arrange job shadowing or senior capstone hours through Volunteer Services.
duration: Weekly 2 to 3 hour shift; Summer 2026 session
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Cincinnati Public Schools juniors and seniors with good grades. You show you are responsible. A counselor must say yes.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor. The page says counselor approval is required.
notes: Only for students at Cincinnati Public Schools. The source is a district news story, so ask your counselor for the current rules, pay and dates.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks
pay_detail: Not stated. The district news story, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask your counselor.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older, hold current American Red Cross Lifeguard Training/First Aid and CPR for the Professional Rescuer/AED certifications, and pass a water skills test. The page does not give an age for gate or pool monitors.
how_to_apply: Register for the required lifeguard course screening on the page, then apply to the open positions. Questions: CRC Aquatics, 513-357-7665.
notes: Lifeguards also attend pre-season and on-site pool training and pass an annual water skills review. Check the page for current screening dates. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Seasonal and part-time; dates not stated
pay_detail: Paid; rate not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Live in the City of Cincinnati or a surrounding community and be 14 to 24. A limited number of positions are for ages 14 and 15. Under 18, a parent or guardian signs the hiring forms; under 16 you need a work permit.
how_to_apply: Create a free account at governmentjobs.com, then apply to the Y2WK job at agency.governmentjobs.com/cincinnati. Only online applications are accepted. Applicants are contacted by phone or email for an interview.
notes: Very competitive: WVXU reported more than 1,000 teens applied last year and about 6 percent were hired. The CRC page says ages 14 to 24 and residents of the city or surrounding communities; an older City HR FAQ says only City residents ages 14 to 18, so confirm. The CRC FAQ still lists 2019 start dates, so ignore those. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Summer; roughly June to early August, dates vary by partner
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Adults can volunteer too. Groups of 10 or more can volunteer together. Great Parks supports Eagle Scout, Gold Award and senior capstone projects.
how_to_apply: Watch the Great Parks volunteer page for the March 2027 information sessions and use the Email Volunteer Engagement link on that page to ask about the teen steps. The page does not show a teen application link. Group projects use the Request a Project Match form.
notes: Confirm first: the page gives no teen application steps or time commitment. Great Parks also lists one day volunteer projects; the page did not state a minimum age for them.
duration: Long term volunteering. Time commitment is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Hamilton County residents ages 14 to 21. You can join if your family income is low or if something makes it hard for you to get a job.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth Apply Here link on the county page. Phone 513-946-0400, email Hamil_yep@jfs.ohio.gov, daily 9 am to 4 pm.
notes: The county page says Harbor helps run the program. The Eligibility and Application tabs could not be read in the text copy. Check the income rules and the form on the page. Ohio work permit rules are not on the page.
duration: Year-round; summer jobs are a main part
pay_detail: $13 per hour

who_can_apply: Age 12 or older, able to commit to an ongoing schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for three months or longer. A background check applies at age 18 and older. Court-mandated volunteers are not accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill in an application in the library's online volunteer system and pick a listing. Questions: 513-369-6968.
notes: Each branch listing sets its own details, so check the age on the listing you choose. The page also mentions meal-service and tutoring roles. It lists a separate Friends of the Library volunteer line at 513-369-6035.
duration: 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, from public, private, parochial, charter and homeschool backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Use the youth application link on the Youth Programs page when recruitment opens. Email youthprograms@cincymuseum.org to be notified.
notes: The program started in 1989. In the first summer teens shadow the Museum of Natural History and Science, The Children's Museum and the Cincinnati History Museum.
duration: Year-round through high school; first summer needs at least six shadowing sessions
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer; perks include free museum admission and parking

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18. The page says the program helps students meet service hour requirements for high school graduation and honor societies. Leader in Training is for ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application linked on the Youth Volunteer Opportunities page when recruiting reopens. Questions: volunteer@cincynature.org or (513) 965-3348. The youth opportunities page lists the main phone as (513) 831-1711.
notes: The pages checked do not give the street address. Check the Nature Center site for the location. Group service days, including for local high schools, remove invasive plants. The youth opportunities page says ages 13 to 18 may apply. It did not repeat the closed for 2026 wording. Check the status before you plan around it.
duration: Seasonal work tied to maple season and early spring. The time commitment is not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Groundwork ORV Green Team page. Contact info@groundworkorv.org or 513-301-0310.
notes: Work sites named by the City include Mt. Echo Park, Mt. Airy Forest, Mt. Storm, Caldwell Nature Preserve and Kennedy Heights Park. Pay, hours and the application window are not on the pages, so ask Groundwork ORV. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Summer; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid summer job; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Showcases are for campers entering grades 6 to 12. The page also lists academies for grades 1 to 6 or 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register online through the camp listings on the Playhouse website.
notes: Camps are at the Playhouse in Eden Park and at Mason Community Center. Before and after care cost extra. Ask the Playhouse about financial aid.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, June 1 to July 31 in 2026
pay_detail: 2026 early bird tuition: $350 for one-week showcases, $750 for two-week Academies at the Playhouse ($720 for the 9-day week of June 15). Prices rose on March 1. 2027 prices are not posted.

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 through 18. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: The Youth Services page gives no link or dates for the Summer Cadet Program. Check that page or its Facebook page for news.
notes: The Summer Cadet Program section gives ages 16 to 18 and part-time summer work. It gives no pay, hours, dates or application link. The separate Public Safety Cadet program on the same page is for young adults. Confirm with the department.
duration: Part time over the summer; exact weeks not stated
pay_detail: Described as part-time summer work for the department. The wage is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school and college students ages 15 and older. The page does not list grade levels.
how_to_apply: Email one message to job_shadows@trihealth.com. Include these items. The Job Shadow Instructions. Your Application. The Risk and Release form. The Authorization to Treat Minors form. Your immunization records. The team does not match you to a department. Look at TriHealth's services and locations first.
notes: The TriHealth volunteer page says Good Samaritan and Bethesda North hospitals use adult and teen volunteers. It does not give a teen age or steps. Email volunteer@trihealth.com or call 513-862-2368 to ask. The job shadowing page does not mention a background check.
duration: Typically about 8 to 16 hours (varies by department or unit)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Camps are organized by age and interest level. Grade rules and fees are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list on the UC summer camps page. Then apply when 2027 sign up opens. Email CEASSummerCamps@ucmail.uc.edu.
notes: Confirm grade levels, cost and dates when the 2027 page is posted. Another UC camp, the Early IT Summer Camp, has its own card in this guide.
duration: Day camps; length not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: A fee applies; the amount is not stated on the program pages. Scholarships may be available for students who need financial help.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th graders through rising 12th graders who like technology. The camp FAQ page gives this grade range.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Here link on the Early IT Summer Camp page. Tell them in your application if cost or lack of resources could keep you from taking part. Questions: ucearlyit@ucmail.uc.edu. There is a parent or guardian orientation on Zoom.
notes: The camp page has a Registration is Now Open notice, but it gives no closing date and no year for the June 1 to 18 dates, so the status stays closed-expect-reopen until the year is confirmed. The camp FAQ page gives the grade range (rising 9th through rising 12th graders) and says the camp is free. Check the dates and status before sending a teen.
duration: June 1 to June 18, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The page does not state a year and calls it a one three-week day camp.
pay_detail: Free to attend. A light breakfast and lunch are provided each day. No pay.

who_can_apply: Eligible local high school students. Space is limited. Exact age and grade rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the page. Questions: UCH-HighSchools@UCHealth.com.
notes: Offered only at UC Medical Center, 3188 Bellevue Ave. The page says joining depends on space and on who qualifies. Age and grade rules are not stated.
duration: September to March, twice a month, 6 to 8 p.m., in person
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. For the UC Medical Center summer program you must be 16 by June 1. You need a TB test, MMR and varicella proof, and a yearly flu shot.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form for your site. Then go to an orientation and do a 20 minute phone interview. Email UCHVolunteerServices@UCHealth.com.
notes: Short term or one time volunteering is not offered. West Chester Hospital is at 7700 University Drive, West Chester, OH. Volunteers are unpaid, so no work permit is needed.
duration: UC Medical Center summer: June to mid-August. West Chester: fall (Oct to Dec), spring (Feb to May) and summer (June to July) sessions.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are 16 or older by August 1 of the program year (in 2026 that date was August 1, 2026). Previous research experience is not required.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application form. You also upload a 1 page resume style summary of your school work and activities. You upload a 1 page personal statement. You rank the session you prefer. Contact: Michele Glassmeyer, Michele.Glassmeyer@uc.edu, (513) 558-6351.
notes: Costs money. The price, session dates and age cutoff above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.
duration: One week per session, Monday to Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. In 2026 there were four sessions between June 1 and June 26.
pay_detail: $1,100 (2026 price). A limited number of scholarships and financial aid awards are available.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 19. Other rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Youth page. Call the league if the form is closed.
notes: The Youth page also tells about a yearly city wide Youth Summit led by youth for youth. Its ages, cost and dates are not stated. Check the current summer dates and stipend with the league before you plan.
duration: 160 hours total, 20 hours per week (about 8 weeks)
pay_detail: A financial stipend; the amount is not stated. Work is 20 hours per week for 160 hours total.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. The page words the age rule as 13 to 17 on May 1, 2026, which looks like a leftover date for a 2027 season, so confirm.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with essays, attend one group interview and two orientations, and set up an online profile to log hours.
notes: Orientation 1 is an online course with a guardian plus a session on April 24 or 25, 2027; Orientation 2 is all day at the Zoo on May 22 or 23, 2027. The Zoo says to contact them if the fee is a hardship. Third-year and older ZooTeens have a lower 70 hour requirement.
duration: Starts May 31, 2027; 100 hours for first and second year ZooTeens, including a 40 hour camp week
pay_detail: $60 non-refundable program fee on acceptance (volunteering is unpaid)

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 18 (the page is titled 'Become a Cadet (Ages 12-18)'). The page says your local squadron can answer eligibility questions.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to about three meetings. Then apply. You can apply online if your squadron commander says you are eligible, or by mail or fax. Contact: pao@cawgcap.org.
notes: Prices on the California Wing cost page are from 2021 and 2022. Ask your squadron for current amounts. The Northern California Bay Area squadrons are listed on the wing site. The cost page says you must go to encampment to advance to Cadet Second Lieutenant.
duration: Ongoing; weekly squadron meetings
pay_detail: Dues plus uniforms. The cost page (2021 and 2022 figures) lists $45 national dues, $25 squadron dues (can be waived for hardship), and about $205 to $300 total to join with uniforms. Encampment was $300 in 2021, with financial help available. No 2026 figures are posted, so check the National site for current dues.

who_can_apply: Youth at least 12 and not yet 19. U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Visit a squadron and attend at least three weekly meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a local squadron with the Georgia Wing locator. Contact it and visit with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application, or ask if you can apply online. Wing office: 770-428-9031, publicaffairs@gawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Georgia Wing page says cadets are not obligated to join the military. The national page lists military obligation for cadets as none. Dues vary by location and the national page says $25 to $50 per year, so ask your squadron for the exact amount. The Georgia Wing home page lists squadrons including Atlanta (GA109), Marietta, Roswell, Chamblee, Lawrenceville, Cumming and others.
duration: Ongoing. A weekly squadron meeting of about 2 hours, one Saturday event monthly, and one week-long encampment in summer (national page).
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, per the national page. A very active cadet might spend about $300 to $600 in the first year before aid, with some help for uniforms and overnight fees.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 and 17 use the Youth Volunteer Application. The page lists no opportunities for anyone under age 16.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application on the page. If you have a question, you can send an email to ClarkVolunteer@SaltLakeCounty.gov.
notes: Court ordered service is 18 and older only.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application packet by the deadline. Chosen applicants get an email and an interview. Call Volunteer Services at 931-502-1055 with questions.
notes: Clarksville is northwest of Nashville. The source is a hospital news post from March 2026. Confirm the 2027 dates with Volunteer Services. The Nashville Vanderbilt University Hospital page says volunteers must be 18 or older. It says its summer high school program is on hold.
duration: Two one-week sessions (8 a.m. to 4 p.m., all five days), or a senior track of at least 40 hours in June and July
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is stated.

who_can_apply: High school students at participating schools in 14 counties, including Sacramento and Yolo. Ask the FARMS coordinator at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag or science teacher whether your school participates. Contact Mindy Cunha at mindy@landbasedlearning.org.
