notes: Advanced FARMS tier (year-long research, job shadowing) also exists. Main office (530) 795-1520. CLBL headquarters is The Maples Farm in Woodland.
duration: school year, 6+ field days
pay_detail: No cost or stipend listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at Luther Burbank High, Grant Union High and Sacramento Academic and Vocational Academy (SAVA).
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Ask a teacher or counselor at your host school, or contact the Center for Land-Based Learning: info@landbasedlearning.org or (530) 795-1520.
notes: Only at the three host schools. Grant Union students can earn college credit through a Sacramento State partnership (ACE program). Pay rate and hours per week are not posted. Paid job for a minor, so a work permit is likely needed.
duration: year-long
pay_detail: Pay rate not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: High school juniors. About 60 students are chosen for each class by the steering committee. The page lists no county or school rule.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps or link a form. Contact the Cobb Chamber: Katie Guice, 770-859-2334, kguice@cobbchamber.org.
notes: Costs money and is not a job. Ask about financial help. No application deadline is stated, so call early. The page says six evening programs but lists seven evening dates; the duration follows the dates.
duration: Aug to April: orientation, fall retreat and 7 sessions (2026-27 class)
pay_detail: $850 tuition for selected students. The page says financial help is accepted for those who cannot pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You must be 14 and in high school to join. Need a 2.0 GPA or higher, a clean background check, physical fitness and good character. Gang or organized crime ties disqualify you.
how_to_apply: Go to three meetings in a row. Then pick up an application packet and turn in a detailed application. Last step is an oral interview with a panel of cadet officers and advisors.
notes: Meets at the Cobb County Police Training Academy, 2435 East-West Connector, Austell, GA 30106. Contact Officer Andy Higgins, (770) 528-8388. New members have a 6-month trial and get a uniform after 6 meetings in a row. Not a paid job.
duration: Weekly meetings: Thursdays 6 to 8 pm in the school year, 6 to 9 pm in summer
pay_detail: Volunteer program. No fees are listed. The Post raises money to attend national contests.

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older. People 18 and older must pass a background check first. The page does not say which roles teens can take.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Cobb County Public Library Volunteer Application. You can also contact the branch where you want to help to ask what openings it has.
notes: Library phone (770) 528-2326, contactus@cobbcat.org. Branches: East Cobb, Gritters, Kemp Memorial, Lewis A. Ray, Mountain View, North Cobb, Powder Springs, Sewell Mill, Sibley, South Cobb, Stratton, Sweetwater Valley, Switzer, Vinings, West Cobb.
duration: Ongoing. Hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Cobb County School District juniors and seniors who are 16 or older. Your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator can tell you the rules at your school.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. All applications must be completed in full before they are considered. The district page lists a coordinator for each high school.
notes: District CTAE and WBL coordinator on the page: Sapph Espinoza. The job should relate to your career goals and CTAE coursework. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: A school year; students can be in WBL both junior and senior year. A 90-minute block needs at least 7.5 work hours a week.
pay_detail: Placements may be paid or non-paid, according to the district page.

who_can_apply: Cobb County residents ages 16 to 24 who meet income qualifications (decided at eligibility) and are in one of the program's target groups.
how_to_apply: Fill out the B.O.S.S. application inquiry form online (it asks if you live in Cobb County, are 16 to 24, and are in school), or call 770-528-4300 or email bossinfo@cobbworks.org.
notes: Funded through WIOA, so participants must meet eligibility rules. The same site lists a PowerUp! plumbing pre-apprenticeship and a Cobb County Fire P.R.E.P. Academy for young adults; ages are not stated, so ask CobbWorks. The main cobbworks.org site returned an error, so this entry uses worksourcecobb.org. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: Not stated. Participants enter at any stage.
pay_detail: Participants can earn up to $8,500 across the program's activities, according to the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students. You need a principal's recommendation, a parent's consent and approval from the college. The program page does not name a grade or age limit.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor and pick a class. Apply to a Peralta college online. Fill out the high school special enrollment form, signed by a parent and your counselor. Bring your transcript and a photo ID to Admissions and Records. Meet a college counselor, then sign up for classes.
notes: Most students may take up to 11 units in fall and spring and 9 units in summer. The page lists higher limits for CCAP dual enrollment, which has its own agreement. Dual enrollment does not replace a course your high school offers. College of Alameda phone: 510-522-7221.
pay_detail: Tuition and fees are free for up to 15 units of approved classes each semester. Books and travel costs are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: high school students in grades 9 to 12. Dual enrollment: students at CSM's partner high schools; talk to your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Create an OpenCCC account and apply to CSM online. For dual enrollment, meet with your high school counselor first, then register with the Dual Enrollment team. Questions: csmoutreach@smccd.edu.
notes: Dual enrollment is only through CSM's partner high schools. Concurrent enrollment is open to any high schooler but may need your counselor's approval at some schools. Skyline and Canada colleges run similar programs (not checked here).
pay_detail: Free. Dual enrollment includes textbooks and materials; concurrent enrollment is free for up to 11 units per semester.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, per the national Civil Air Patrol page. This is a composite squadron, which means it has both cadets and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email the squadron commander to ask about visiting a meeting with a parent. CAP's usual steps are listed on the Virginia and North Carolina wing pages. They are to go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Squadron location: 6709 Corporal Frank Scott Drive, College Park, MD 20740. Commander listed on the page: Capt. Estelle Roche, estelle.roche@mdwg.cap.gov. The meeting time is from the squadron page; confirm before you go.
duration: Weekly meetings, Wednesdays 6:45 to 9:00
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $55 for Maryland in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Seven teen seats for young people no older than 18 when appointed. The page does not say where you must live, but it is a city committee.
how_to_apply: Email the Recreation staff liaison through the city page to ask how to join.
notes: No meeting in March. Summer recess is June to August. Meeting places vary by month.
duration: Meets the second Monday of the month, 6:30 pm, with a summer break June to August
pay_detail: Not stated (no pay mentioned)

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old by the orientation date. No grade rule listed. Needs proof of immunizations (MMR, varicella, hepatitis B, Tdap, current flu shot, TB screen).
how_to_apply: Fill out the student form linked on the page. Go to the required orientation. Send shot records. The Lanham contact is Valerie Nicholas, Volunteer Coordinator. Her address is vnic100@luminishealth.org.
notes: Ask the Lanham coordinator for the semester due date, since the page does not list one for Lanham.
duration: One semester, at least 3 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Enrolled in grade 10, 11 or 12 in good standing, 16 by the application deadline, U.S. citizen, 3.0 unweighted GPA, and permanent residence within 50 miles of NASA Goddard (Greenbelt, MD) or NASA Wallops (Wallops Island, VA).
how_to_apply: Apply in NASA STEM Gateway, pick one or more projects, and upload a transcript plus resume details. Projects are added until the end of February.
notes: The page lists up to 55 high school students. General questions: info@spaceclub.org.
duration: Six weeks each summer, from late June until early August.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages checked.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Send an email to Jessica Peters. Her address is jessica.peters@pgparks.com.
notes: Ask for the next session dates.
duration: Not stated

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and older. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application link. Email megan.merchant@pgparks.com to ask how to apply before the March 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Confirm first. The county page has no application link. It does not describe audition steps. Maryland Department of Labor says work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland. A permit is issued only after a job offer.
duration: May to July 2027
pay_detail: Paid apprenticeship. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Prince George's County residents ages 13 to 18. No grade is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It is free. It has a short essay and a piece of original artwork in your preferred genre, such as music, dance or visual arts. Contact: Shaiday Dancy, Teen Arts Specialist, 301-446-3252, shaiday.dancy@pgparks.com.
notes: Applicants could also be invited to be a Teen Arts Council ambassador. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Eight months, October 2026 to June 2027, with meetings every two weeks
pay_detail: $300 stipend after you finish the eight month term

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 who pass the audition.
how_to_apply: Attend the audition on February 7, 2027 at 3 p.m. Questions go to megan.merchant@pgparks.com. The audition event page was not available when checked, so ask for audition details (what to prepare) by email.
notes: Maryland Department of Labor says work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland. A permit is issued only after the minor is offered a job. Confirm first. The page lists the audition but not what to prepare.
duration: Weekly rehearsals starting April 2027 and a summer performance schedule from June 28 to August 6, 2027.
pay_detail: Paid, part time. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Email jessica.peters@pgparks.com.
notes: Ask for the next session dates.
duration: Not stated

who_can_apply: Dual enrollment is for PG County Public Schools juniors and seniors. You need an unweighted GPA of at least 2.6 and must meet placement rules. Concurrent enrollment is for Maryland residents in grades 11 and 12 who are in private school, homeschooled or not in PG County. The same rules apply. Talented and Gifted is for grades 8 to 10. You must have been named gifted in the last year and have a GPA of 3.0 or higher.
how_to_apply: New students: use Apply Now on the PGCC application portal. Returning students: finish the counselor and high school certification form. Talk to your school counselor first. Phone 301-546-7469.
notes: Also look at Early Admission and Early/Middle College on the PGCC high school programs page. Early Admission is for seniors, so ask your counselor. Early/Middle College is for first-generation students. This is not a job.
duration: One college term at a time
pay_detail: PG County Public Schools pays tuition, fees and textbooks for dually enrolled students in qualifying courses. Eligible Maryland concurrent students get a 50% tuition discount.

who_can_apply: Students 16 or older. You need to clear immunization checks and a background check. You also do online training. Bring an ID to the orientation interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Send back the onboarding form by fax or by email. Go to an orientation. You will have an interview with the volunteer coordinator. Then finish training and the background check. The email is UMCapitalRegionVolunteer@umm.edu.
notes: Hospital is at 901 Harry S. Truman Drive North, Largo, MD 20774. You will get a confirmation email within two business days after sending the application and health form.
duration: 100 hours within 12 months, 4 hours per shift
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. It is hard to get in. You need to know advanced math well. UMD's camp list says rising grades 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Camp Registration form linked on the camp site. Contact: mathcamp@umd.edu.
notes: Check the FAQ page for cost and dates before applying.
duration: Two weeks (June 22 to July 2 in 2026). Page says 'See You Next Summer in 2027'.
pay_detail: UMD's 2026 camp list showed $25; the camp site does not state a cost.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade in the fall. The page does not list a GPA or location rule.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with a one page personal statement. Email a recommendation from a STEM teacher and your official transcript to summerengr@umd.edu. Contact: Sandra Crespin Melgar, summerengr@umd.edu.
notes: Costs money. Price, dates and deadline above are from the 2026 page and may change for 2027.
duration: One week, residential. In 2026: Session One July 26 to 31 and Session Two August 2 to 7 (you attend one).
pay_detail: $1,400 per student (project materials, activities, and room and board; transportation is not included). Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students from Montgomery and Prince George's Counties. 18 to 24 students are accepted. No grade level listed (UMD's camp list says grades 9 to 12).
how_to_apply: Register through the link on the event page (it was full in 2026). Questions: Abba Gumel, agumel@umd.edu.
notes: Held at 6116 Executive Blvd, North Bethesda, MD 20852. Not on the College Park campus.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily (July 27 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the camp page (the 2026 link was go.umd.edu/whatsyourstory2026). Questions: whatsyourstorycamp@umd.edu.
notes: Ask about scholarships by email.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. daily (Aug 3 to 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: $125 registration fee, includes a light breakfast and lunch. Scholarships available (no details given).

who_can_apply: Students who go to high school in Maryland or Washington, D.C., or live there. You need a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5. You must show interest and skill in math, science or engineering.
how_to_apply: Online application with a one page personal statement (12 point, double spaced), an official high school transcript, and official PSAT or SAT scores if you have them. You must attend all sessions, orientation, and the pre and post tests. Contact: Ms. Aishah Briscoe, FutureEngineer@umd.edu.
notes: The page does not say whether the program is residential. Costs money but is low compared with most pre-college programs. Dates and the $400 price are from the 2026 page.
duration: Three weeks, in person on the UMD campus. The 2026 session ran Monday July 6 to Friday July 24.
pay_detail: The whole program costs $400 per student. Scholarships are available for students with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: Current 10th, 11th and 12th graders. You should be strong in school, like robotics and show initiative. You need a high school transcript and a resume to apply.
how_to_apply: Use the online application linked from the SPARC page (Apply Now). Include your high school transcript and resume. A parent or other authorized adult must sign you in and out each day. Contact: robotics-sparc@umd.edu.
notes: Very expensive and commuter only. Participation does not guarantee admission to UMD. The page banner says Apply Now with an application deadline of December 1, 2026. Confirm the 2027 price with the program.
duration: Three weeks, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Summer 2027: Session 1 July 6 to 23, Session 2 July 26 to August 13. You enroll in one session.
pay_detail: The Summer 2026 price was $5,000 for one 3 week session (project materials and activities; lunch and transportation are not included). The 2027 price is not posted. A limited number of need based scholarships are available, and payments are not refundable.

who_can_apply: High school students from Prince George's County. No grade levels listed (UMD's camp list says grades 10 to 12).
how_to_apply: Fill out the high school student interest form linked on the camp page. Contact: Megan Newcombe, newcombe@umd.edu.
notes: Check the page in spring for 2027.
duration: One week (June 22 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free to attend

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are thinking about majoring in engineering. The page says the programs are open to all students. Gender does not matter.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps beyond saying the 2027 application opens in January 2027. Contact Jen Kuntz of the WIE Program at jakuntz@umd.edu or 301-405-0315. Scholarship and payment details are sent after admission decisions.
notes: Costs money. The program does not guarantee admission to UMD. Other UMD engineering pre-college programs are listed at https://eng.umd.edu/pre-college-programs/summer.
duration: One week, residential. The 2026 session ran Sunday July 12 to Friday July 17.
pay_detail: $1,500 per student for Summer 2026 (covers materials, activities, and room and board; transportation is not included). Scholarships are available for admitted students with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students who are sophomores or higher by September 2026, and newly graduated seniors. The page says UFCC 2026 in this section but lists 2027 dates, so confirm the year.
how_to_apply: Be free all week. Then fill out the online application. Have two adults who are not family send letters of support. They can be a teacher, counselor or club adviser. A committee will let you know. Accepted students pay the fee to hold a spot.
notes: Students arrive Sunday 2 to 3 p.m. and leave Saturday at 1 p.m.
duration: One week, arrive Sunday and leave Saturday (July 11 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $150 activity fee after acceptance ($153.50 if paid by PayPal). Tuition is covered by a Maryland Department of Natural Resources grant.

who_can_apply: Community clubs are open to youth ages 8 to 18, based on your age on December 31 of the enrollment year. Ages 5 to 7 join Cloverbuds.
how_to_apply: Find your county Extension office and pick a project. Then join on the 4-H Online site. You make a family profile, pick a club and choose projects.
notes: Also open to younger kids; teen parts are the leader roles. Call or email your county Extension office before you start to join online.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the state page. Some projects like horse or livestock cost more. Ask your county office.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. You complete an application, an interview and a health screening before you start.
how_to_apply: Apply online, then an interview and a health screening.
notes: You can get volunteer credit for scholarship applications. The page does not say which hospital sites take teens. Ask when you apply.
duration: Full-year or summer; about 3 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Two $2,500 scholarships are given each year to outstanding junior volunteers.

who_can_apply: Students in school ag education programs. No age or grade limits are stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's agriculture teacher about an FFA chapter. Use the Chapters page to find one. The Become a State Officer page explains the state officer role.
notes: The Colorado FFA Foundation helps the group, CSU Ag Education and ag teachers. Dates and fees were not on the program pages.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher about dues.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 per the Denver city page. No income rules. You must show proof of age and U.S. citizenship.
how_to_apply: Visit any Workforce Center in Colorado to register. Bring proof of age and U.S. citizenship.
notes: The Denver page and the Jefferson County workforce page both say ages 14 to 24. The state page (cdle.colorado.gov/jobs-training/youth/gsjh) would not load. If you are 14 or 15, call your local Workforce Center to check the age rule.
duration: Summer season
pay_detail: The service is free. The jobs it lists set their own pay.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are at least 16 during camp.
how_to_apply: Apply online; the 2026 page lists a waitlist form. Questions: innohub@mines.edu.
notes: The page blocked our reader, so it was read through a page summary tool. Confirm the cost and dates on the Mines page.
duration: One week, 9 AM to 4 PM. 2026 sessions: July 13 to 17 and July 20 to 24.
pay_detail: $850, lunch included. Bring a laptop if you can; loaners are available.

who_can_apply: High school students across Colorado Springs. The page does not list ages or a deadline.
how_to_apply: Download the form on the city page. Send it as shown. Email ira.cronin@coloradosprings.gov with questions.
notes: A news story said under 18 students need a parent signature. That detail is not on the city page, so ask the contact.
duration: Meets once a month
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old. A background check is needed if you are 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the page. Call 719-319-3678 or email volunteer@spacefoundation.org with questions.
notes: You can apply while the museum is closed. The museum plans to reopen in January 2027.
duration: At least two shifts a month, Tuesday through Saturday
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages depend on the job: 10 and up for Junior Docent at Rock Ledge Ranch, 13 and up for Spray Ground Assistant, Teen Volunteer and Therapeutic Recreation Discovery Camp roles, and 15 and up for Junior Park Docent at Garden of the Gods and Junior Docent at the Pioneers Museum.
how_to_apply: Register on the page for the job you want. Junior Park Docent at Garden of the Gods signs up by email to gardenofthegods@coloradosprings.gov. Some jobs need an interview and training.
notes: Junior Docents at the Pioneers Museum earn a $300 Education Stipend at the end of the summer if they do at least 40 hours. Teens ages 12 to 15 can only volunteer from 7 am to 7 pm in the school year, and until 9 pm in summer. North Cheyenne Canon teens must finish the free online Leave No Trace 101 course.
duration: Several weeks. Hours differ by job.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19. You go to a Tribal or Colorado school (online or charter too). Or you are in a home based, high school equivalency or diploma program.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in spring 2027. Contact COYAC to get a notice when applications open.
notes: The COYAC site blocked our page reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. The retreat for the current group is August 29 to 30, 2026 in Denver; the Day at the Capitol is March 1, 2027.
duration: Two year term. Monthly virtual meetings on the second Thursday, 7:45 to 9:15 PM.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says lodging and meals are provided at the retreat and travel money is available for the Capitol day.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 13 years old or in grades 7 to 12 during the 2026-2027 school year. The page says the teen program is currently full.
how_to_apply: Email teen@bexleylibrary.org to join the teen volunteer email list. That is how you hear about openings. The summer application opens April 1.
notes: The page says the library is postponing adult volunteering for now. Call the youth department with questions.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12 who live in the Columbus area can join.
how_to_apply: Download the member form from the page. Email it to youthcouncil@cmafohio.org. You can also mail it to the Youth Advisory Council Coordinator at 1390 Dublin Road, Columbus, OH 43215.
notes: Time can count toward the community service hours you need to graduate. Ask the foundation if seats are open for 2026-2027. Email youthcouncil@cmafohio.org or call 614-240-7410.
duration: Not stated on the page.
pay_detail: No pay stated. Time can count toward community service hours needed to graduate.

who_can_apply: Ohio residents in grades 7 to 12. New students need a 3.0 unweighted GPA, or ACT or SAT scores that qualify, or Columbus State placement test scores that qualify. Middle schoolers must take the reading and writing placement tests. They must reach the needed score in at least one area.
how_to_apply: Give your school a Letter of Intent. Apply to Columbus State. There is no fee or essay. Finish online onboarding. Show that you meet one of the eligibility rules. Then sign up for classes with your counselor.
notes: The college application asks you to have your Social Security number ready. Use a personal email, not a school email. Send your unofficial high school transcripts or ACT/SAT scores to your CCP advisor.
duration: Semester courses
pay_detail: Courses and textbooks are free for public school students. Transportation and other costs are the student's.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21 in Franklin County. In general, families must meet the income rules for TANF cash help. Ages 14 to 15, 16 to 18 and 18 to 21 have their own tracks.
how_to_apply: Apply through one of the partner groups on the county page. They are Columbus Urban League, Godman Guild, Lead the Way Learning Academy, Nationwide Children's Hospital and Saint Stephen's Community House. Each lists its own phone and email.
notes: Check the partner pages in winter. The county page says nothing about work permits. Nationwide Children's and Columbus Urban League already have their own cards in this guide. Godman Guild and Lead the Way phone numbers are on the county page: 614-294-5476 and 614-915-0434.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Ages 14 to 15: $1,500 stipend plus up to $300 in incentives for finishing the 6 weeks. Ages 16 to 18: wages up to $15 per hour.

who_can_apply: The page says the program serves young adults in grades 9-12 and after high school graduation. Exact age rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth and Young Adult Workforce Program interest form on the Godman Guild page.
notes: Events listed: Entrepreneur Night Nov 18, Community Service Dec 3, Resume Building Jan 27, Public Speaking Feb 24, Money Skills Apr 7, Showcase May 6. Phone 614-294-5476. The Godman Guild site has an older Ready 2 Earn link that gives a 404. Use the teen page.
duration: Monthly sessions Nov 2026 to May 2027. Summer 2026 Ready 2 Earn ran 5 weeks and 60 hours.
pay_detail: Not stated on the Godman Guild pages. The Franklin County Ready 2 Earn page lists a stipend for ages 14 to 15 and wages for ages 16 to 18 through its partners.

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and 17 can volunteer on their own. A guardian must sign a Junior and Teen Volunteer Waiver and Release. Ages 12 to 15 can join only as junior volunteers, with an adult volunteer partner over the age of 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the New Volunteer Registration form. Then use the emailed link to book an in-person STEPS orientation in Hilliard. Next, finish species training and mentoring. Then start to book shifts.
notes: The FAQ lists a junior option for ages 12 to 15. It needs an adult volunteer partner over 21. Email volunteer@columbushumane.org with questions.
duration: 4 hours a month minimum
pay_detail: Unpaid. New volunteers pay a one-time $50 mission investment.

who_can_apply: Youth in or entering grades 6 to 12 who are at least 12 years old. High school students 18 or older must be returning to a traditional high school and may need a background check.
how_to_apply: Online VolunTeen application, first come first served by branch. If your branch is missing from the drop-down, it is full.
notes: Openings vary by branch. Current or recent youth volunteers should talk to the Summer Reading coordinator at their branch. The library also has School Help, Reading Buddies and Creation Station volunteer roles; the page lists the age rule only for the summer VolunTeen role. Ohio's work permit rules for unpaid public library volunteering are not stated on the page.
duration: June 1 to July 31 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Most assignments are for ages 16 and up. Ages 11 to 15 can help only at Inniswood Metro Gardens, as Junior Volunteers. The Inniswood training is in March.
how_to_apply: Attend a Volunteer Information session and complete the volunteer application. A background check including fingerprints is part of the process.
notes: Slate Run Living Historical Farm lets children volunteer with a parent or supervising adult. Scouts can set up group service days by email. For Inniswood contact the volunteer coordinator at 614-895-6226.
duration: Flexible schedule by assignment and park
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Sort and pack and the Kitchen are for ages 13 and up. Markets and kids' meals are 16 and up. The garden is 16 and up, or 14 and up with a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Click Find an Opportunity on the volunteer page and pick a shift on the volunteer sign-up site. Groups use the group button on the same page.
notes: Sort and pack is in Grove City (3960 Brookham Drive). Other sites have no address on the page. Call 614-277-3663 with questions.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. A parent or guardian must take part in the TB test step.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online part of the Teen Program form. Mail or hand in the paper part to Volunteer Services. Then you interview and take a TB test. You go to a volunteer orientation and a unit orientation.
notes: Sites listed: Mount Carmel Dublin, East, Grove City, St. Ann's and New Albany. Phones: East 614-234-6658, Grove City 614-663-6700, St. Ann's 380-898-4097, New Albany 614-663-6334. Completing the application does not guarantee a spot.
duration: One shift (about 4 hours) a week. Summer: weekdays 8 am to 4 pm. School year: weekday evenings 4 to 7 pm or weekends 8 am to 8 pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: "Arts-interested youth." The page gives no age or grade rule. Selected teens join a cohort.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Call the museum at 614-221-6801 or watch the page for the next call.
notes: Meetings are at CMA Short North, CMA at The Pizzuti and the Broad Street location (480 East Broad Street). Ages are not stated, so confirm with the museum before you plan on it.
duration: Select Saturdays, Sept 26, 2026 to May 30, 2027
pay_detail: $1,250 stipend, paid in two installments

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19. Free registration; drop-ins are welcome.
how_to_apply: Register for free on the museum events listings, or drop in.
notes: Teens 13 and older can also visit the museum on their own at any time, per the page.
duration: Every second Thursday, 5 to 7 pm. Teen Studio: Unwind is quarterly, 5 to 7 pm.
pay_detail: Free; includes museum admission

who_can_apply: Teens who are 15 by June 1 and currently in high school. Competitive, with limited spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Get references who are not family to fill out an electronic form. Go to a group interview. Sign a commitment form. Send your shot record, including flu. No waivers are allowed. Then finish an online orientation and training for your job.
notes: You can miss no more than 2 shifts. You need to be there 80 percent of the time. Contact Family and Volunteer Services at 614-722-3635 or Volunteering@NationwideChildrens.org. The page has no direct application link.
duration: 10 weeks, June to mid-August, one 2 to 3 hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Ohio residents in their freshman, sophomore or junior year of high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online STEM Institute application when it opens. Email si-contact@osc.edu.
notes: Two phone numbers show on OSC pages, so email is safer. The page says OSC pays much of the cost. It says there are no one-on-one scholarships. The program used to be called the Summer Institute.
duration: 2 weeks, June 6 to 17, 2027
pay_detail: $600 per student ($60 per day) for housing, meals, tuition, trips and insurance. OSC says the real cost is about four times that.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2027 can take high school courses.
how_to_apply: Make a free account in the online application system. Then apply. Sign up for updates on the page to learn when applications open.
notes: Questions: ExploreASC@osu.edu or 614-292-6390. The page says some need-based aid may be available. Ask for it on the program application. Other department camps are on the department summer page. They cover philosophy, language science, humanities and mind science.
duration: 1 week per course
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per one-week course, with lunch and snacks. The 2027 fee is not posted.

who_can_apply: All high school students interested in a career in healthcare. The page gives no grade, age or residency rule. A parent or guardian must attend the required orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application (Apply Now form on the camp page). Use the Contact Us link on the camp page for questions.
notes: Free and short, so a good first health-career step. Watch the page for 2027 dates.
duration: 3 days, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Free for students. Breakfast and lunch are provided.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10, 11 or 12. A student who just finished freshman year can also apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send a high school transcript, a personal statement and a note from a teacher.
notes: The page has a few date mix-ups (one spot says 2025), so confirm the 2027 dates and cost with ccbs@osu.edu.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page. It says financial aid, including partial and full scholarships, is available.

who_can_apply: Ohio residents who will be high school sophomores, juniors or seniors and want a health career. The page suggests a 3.0 GPA overall and 3.3 in math and science. You also need two letters of support. One must be from a math or science teacher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks about school and other activities, essays and a transcript. You also need two signed letters of support. They are sent through a separate form.
notes: You must find your own housing and rides. The page only covers 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Tuition is $325. Full and partial scholarships are given based on need and application quality.

who_can_apply: Ohio residents in 8th grade at Columbus City Schools, Cincinnati Public Schools or seven other listed city districts. You must be the first in your family to go to college. Family income must be under the limit. You must earn mostly A grades.
how_to_apply: Apply in 8th grade through the Young Scholars Program page. Questions: YSP@osu.edu.
notes: Only 8th graders can start. The page says there are no costs for the pre-college portion.Other districts on the list: Akron, Canton, Cleveland, Dayton, Lorain, Toledo and Youngstown. Check the page for the income table and the current deadline.
duration: Grades 8 through 12
pay_detail: No cost stated for the program. Ohio State financial aid is offered after graduation if requirements are met.

who_can_apply: Student volunteers must be at least 12 years old or in grades 7 to 12. You must have a Pickerington Public Library card and go to an orientation. You must keep a steady schedule of 2 to 6 hours a week for about 3 months or longer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply to Volunteer link on the volunteer page. Then go to an orientation. The Volunteer Coordinator runs it.
notes: Two locations: Pickerington Main Library and Sycamore Plaza Library. Homework Help is open Monday to Thursday, 3 to 6 pm, in the school year. The VolunTeen Scholarship form is open December 1 to January 30.
duration: On-going, 3 months or longer, 2 to 6 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A VolunTeen Scholarship is open to high school students with outstanding volunteer service.

who_can_apply: Columbus residents (or people who pay Columbus taxes) ages 14 to 23. Must pass a drug test; a background check applies at 18 and older. Required documents: birth certificate and/or Social Security card, plus a state or school photo ID.
how_to_apply: Apply during the winter window listed on the program page. If you have questions, email AJRP@columbus.gov or call 614-724-2038.
notes: Work experiences vary and are matched to career interests where possible. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. The page does not say how to submit the application beyond the schedule, so confirm the method with the program.
duration: Mostly summer; some participants may continue in fall and winter
pay_detail: $15 an hour, up to 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: City of Columbus residents (getting City trash and recycling service counts) entering grades 6 to 10 in Fall 2026 who keep a 2.8 GPA. Selected applicants interview with the program directors.
how_to_apply: Email the application, last school year's report card and a letter from a teacher, administrator or community leader to CBMcGhee@columbus.gov, or drop it at Blackburn Community Center (263 Carpenter St.). Selected applicants interview.
notes: Includes middle schoolers (grades 6 to 10). There is a mandatory guardian and youth orientation on Sept 19, 2026. You can miss no more than three meet-ups without an excuse. The page says applications began May 1, 2025. That looks like a typo for 2026.
duration: Sept orientation, then 12 monthly meet-ups Oct 2026 to May 2027; ceremony May 15, 2027
pay_detail: No pay; cost not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older with the swimming skills needed. Must finish the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course (the City waives the course fee if you are hired). Completing the course does not guarantee a job.
how_to_apply: Submit the Lifeguard Interest Form, take the pre-course swimming skills test, finish the Red Cross course, then submit the employment application.
notes: The City also offers Red Cross lifeguard training for ages 15 and older. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) says school-age minors need an age and schooling certificate (work permit). In the summer, 16 and 17 year olds can show the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead.
duration: Summer season; dates not stated
pay_detail: $20 an hour (seasonal)

who_can_apply: Pre-college students who are passionate about mathematics. First-year students range in age from 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Ross Program website when the window opens. Email ross@rossprogram.org with questions.
notes: The page lists two sites. One is Otterbein University in Columbus, OH. The other is Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology in Terre Haute, Indiana. The 2026 dates were June 14 to July 24. Ask about 2027 dates when they are posted.
duration: 6 weeks (summer 2026: June 14 to July 24)
pay_detail: $7,500, covering tuition, housing and meals. Financial aid is offered for students who need it.

who_can_apply: 9th and 10th graders. The county page says IT On Ramp+ is for TANF-eligible Franklin County 9th and 10th graders.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the TECH CORPS Work-Based Learning page. Phone 614-583-9211, email info@techcorps.org.
notes: The county page lists a 6-week length and $15 per hour for IT On Ramp+; the TECH CORPS page lists 4 weeks. Ask TECH CORPS which is right for the next session. Ages are not stated, only grades 9 and 10. The TECH CORPS page gives no pay.
duration: IT On Ramp+ is 4 weeks, full day. Computing Career Corps meets weekdays 9 am to 3 pm.
pay_detail: $15 per hour for IT On Ramp+ (6 weeks), per the Franklin County page. Pay for Computing Career Corps is not stated, but students earn Work Based Learning hours.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. The page does not state a minimum age or grade.
how_to_apply: Email Meg Brown. She is the Director of Children's Education. Her address is megbrown@thurberhouse.org.
notes: The page says counselors must be 21 or older and gives no minimum age for interns. Confirm the age limit by email.
duration: Monday to Friday, at least 1 week (camp runs 8 weeks)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Thurber House can sign off on service hours. Interns provide their own transportation and lunch.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade through rising college freshmen.
how_to_apply: Register online. For a scholarship, click "applying for a scholarship" in the online registration. Questions go to Meg Brown (megbrown@thurberhouse.org).
notes: Bring a sack lunch.
duration: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday (July 20 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: $825 (includes all fees, snacks, a journal and a t-shirt). Payment plans on request. A very limited number of scholarships are given by lottery (you pay a $25 registration fee to enter).

who_can_apply: Any student in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Young Writers' Studio page. For help paying, email Meg Brown (megbrown@thurberhouse.org).
notes: Fall 2026 dates are listed. The page does not list later sessions.
duration: 6 evening sessions, 6:30 to 8:30 p.m.
pay_detail: $17 per session, with a discount for the whole season. A limited number of scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Tremont Road Branch or Lane Road Branch link on the volunteer page. Contact the teen volunteer staff listed for each branch with questions.
notes: Branches are Lane Road, Miller Park and Tremont Road. The page lists two different branch application links, so use the one for your branch.
duration: Shifts for the whole 2026-2027 school year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service hours, and teen volunteers enter a quarterly prize raffle.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 19, per the age range listed for WRTU on the Urban League Career Connect page. Other eligibility rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The Youth Leadership Team is at 3443 Agler Rd., Columbus, phone 614-257-6300.
notes: Supported by the Franklin County Board of Commissioners and employer partners. A 2024 WRTU Fellows program began with 27 youth. The Urban League's other youth programs (for example I Am My Brother's Keeper, ages 14 to 18, and VLOG, ages 14 to 19) are listed on its Career Connect page. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: Summer; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid for summer involvement; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18. Lead Volunteers are ages 16 to 18. Requirements vary and spaces are limited.
how_to_apply: Read the teen volunteer rules page. Fill out an application, even if you have volunteered before. Go to an orientation before your first shift. Use the phone number in the notes for questions.
notes: Phone 614-882-7277, option 5. No direct application link was on the page. Lead volunteers need at least 4 to 6 hours a month and summer volunteers at least 2 hours a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 12 or entering grades 7 to 12 in the fall.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Volunteens application. The library will contact you if you are approved.
notes: The page lists no orientation or hours requirement. Email the library with questions.
duration: School year (September to June) and summer (June to August)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work

who_can_apply: Anyone in grade 6 and above. You do not need to be a YMCA member.
how_to_apply: Click Start Your Application on the Hilliard Teen Leaders Club page. You can also email Taylor Stillion. His email is taylor.stillion@ymcacolumbus.org.
notes: This card is for the Hilliard branch. Other YMCA of Central Ohio branches may have their own clubs; ask the Y.
duration: Weekly meetings, Wednesdays 6 to 7 pm
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who like marine science. You must go to an info session and fill out a form.
how_to_apply: Go to an info session. Fill out the interest form. Then fill out the Apply for the Program form linked on the page.
notes: The page does not say what travel papers are needed, so ask the Zoo. The trip is 3 days on land and 3 on the water, weather permitting. Field station is on Andros Island, Bahamas.
duration: 8 days (June 19 to 26, 2027)
pay_detail: $3,500 per person. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school teams of 4 to 7 students with one faculty advisor from the school. Only 2 teams per school are accepted.
how_to_apply: Your team captain fills out the online team application on the Teen Eco Summit page. A school faculty advisor must be on the team.
notes: You need a school faculty advisor on the team, so ask one first. Only 2 teams per school are accepted. Each team needs its own project and application.
duration: Kickoff Oct. 28 or 29, 2026 (9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.), projects through the year, celebration at the end of April
pay_detail: Free to take part

who_can_apply: Teens entering grades 8 to 12 who show leadership, animal knowledge, professionalism and emotional maturity.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the Teen Volunteers page in early 2027.
notes: The page does not state the months, hours or any fee, so confirm with the Zoo. Season is listed as summer as a best fit but is not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the CHM internships page to join the mailing list.
notes: CHM says it is not accepting Teen Program applications right now; the page gives no reopening date. Join the interest list to be told when it opens. Pay and length are not stated.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth 16 and up can make their own volunteer account and sign up for some shifts. Youth 11 to 15 can volunteer with an adult.
how_to_apply: Register as a Food Bank volunteer on its volunteer site. Pick a shift on the calendar. If you are 11 to 15, a parent or guardian signs up too and adds you with the Sign up with a Team button.
notes: The rules for youth come from the Food Bank volunteer FAQ. Youth 5 to 10 can only volunteer at the Family Food Sorts. Youth under 5 cannot volunteer at the Food Bank. Team captains must be 16 or older. The FAQ lists the volunteer help desk as volunteerhelpdesk@foodbankccs.org or 855-309-3663, extension 605. The Food Bank hosts groups too, and a group can send a Group Volunteer Request. Youth 16 and up can sign up for select shifts. The shift details show which ones.
duration: By shift
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school age teens, 14 to 18. Must attend at least 6 of the 9 sessions in a cohort.
how_to_apply: Sign up through Gaining Ground. Questions go to team leader Maddie at maddie@gainingground.org.
notes: Sessions run Wednesdays and Saturdays 8:45 am to 12 pm and Fridays 1 to 3:15 pm. Pay is not explicitly stated on the page.
duration: Two 3-week cohorts, 3 sessions a week (2026: June 24 to July 11, and July 22 to Aug 8)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 21 when you are appointed. You must live in Concord or go to school in Concord. You must be able to serve for one year, September 1 to June 30. Part-time seasonal city workers can apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission Application from the city website. Email it to the City Clerk. The adult commissioners pick the youth members.
notes: The commission has five adult members and two youth members. The youth term is one year. The Clerk email is cityclerk@cityofconcord.org. The commission meets at 6 PM as needed at 1950 Parkside Drive, Concord.
duration: One-year term, Sept 1 to June 30
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Middle or high school students who are US residents at the time of submission (citizenship not required). Students may compete in the district where they live or where they attend school. Solo or teams up to four. At least half the team must be eligible for the district the team competes in.
how_to_apply: Register on the Student Registration page, then submit the app online.
notes: Any language or platform is allowed, solo or teams up to four. Check the Participating Districts page on the site to confirm your district takes part.
duration: Build time before the deadline
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Youth who are 9 by December 31 of the program year and have not turned 19 by that date can join as regular members. Younger children can join as Primary Members.
how_to_apply: Find a club near you by place and meeting time. Contact the club leader. Then enroll online in the 4-H system linked on the page, or call the County 4-H Office for help. Pick your projects and pay the fee.
notes: Adults who want to volunteer enroll too. Their fee is $30. Adult enrollment opened July 15, 2026. Open the page in a browser to see the club list and the enrollment links.
duration: Program year runs July 1 to June 30; most meetings are August to May
pay_detail: $150 per youth. Financial help is available for youth members.

who_can_apply: Students at West Contra Costa USD, Leadership Public Schools, Griffin Technology Academies, or Middle College High School on campus. Requirements vary by school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: earlycollegecredit@contracosta.edu.
notes: Serves West Contra Costa County (Richmond, San Pablo). No deadlines are listed on the page.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free: no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: Summer Read: entering 8th grade or above, with parent consent. Computer Docent and Homework Help: age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer interest form on ccclib.org/volunteer. You may be called for an interview. Forms stay on file for six months.
notes: Contact your branch to see if it is taking volunteers now.
duration: Summer Read 1 to 2 hours a week; Computer Docents at least 2 hours a week

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 24 who have barriers to finishing school, finding a job or starting a career. The page asks if you have a disability, are low income, or have been in the justice system. Those answers can get you Priority of Service.
how_to_apply: Register on CalJOBS, the state job site linked on the page. Then contact the board at the email or phone number on its site. Ask about youth services.
notes: The board office is at 4071 Port Chicago Highway, Suite 200, Concord. The page lists wdb@ehsd.cccounty.us and (925) 655-3800. The Mt. Diablo school district runs a WIOA youth program for Central County and Bay Point. Its page points East and West County youth to the County Office of Education. See those cards.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The page lists work experience as one kind of help.

who_can_apply: Cook County residents ages 14 to 19.
how_to_apply: The Cook County page points to fpdcc.com/nature/conservation-corps-programs for how to apply. That page was not available.
notes: Confirm age rules, pay and deadline on the Forest Preserves site, because it blocked my reader. Ask about working papers if you are under 16.
duration: 4 to 6 weeks
pay_detail: Paid. The amount is not stated on the Cook County page. Transportation and service clothing are provided.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in suburban Cook County who are not working or in school. It aims at the south and west suburbs but is open to all of suburban Cook County.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Chicago Cook Workforce Partnership Opportunity Works page. The Cook County page links to it. That page was not available.
notes: The page does not say how to enroll or the pay, so call or check chicookworks.org. For teens 16 to 18 who have left school.
pay_detail: Subsidized internships. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in the grades listed for each role.
how_to_apply: Click Apply for a role on the volunteer page. Questions: kwonch@cooklib.org (youth) or lhotchkiss@cooklib.org (high school).
notes: You need a library card for the adult volunteer jobs.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer work counts toward service hours.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 and up. Accepted volunteers must attend three weekend training sessions.
how_to_apply: Online youth volunteer application during the August window, then an in-person interview (5:30 to 7:30 p.m.) at COSI.
notes: Candidates who cannot attend all three trainings are told to reapply later. COSI also lists one-day Quick Impact volunteer shifts; check each listing for its age rule.
duration: Three weekend trainings (Oct to Dec in 2026), then ongoing volunteering; hours not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: California high school students completing grades 8 to 12. Non-California residents and international students cannot apply. Selected on academic strength and interest in math and science. You pick one campus and cluster choices.
how_to_apply: Online application plus teacher recommendations and parent signature. Pay the application fee. If accepted, pay one-third by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027.
notes: Competitive. Residential, so you live on campus for four weeks. Financial aid is reviewed separately from admission and needs a parent income document; it has a hard deadline. Program session dates are listed as TBA. Pick UC Davis as your campus on the application. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses (UC Davis, UC Irvine, UC San Diego and UC Santa Cruz); this card is the Davis campus. See the UC COSMOS site for the others: https://jacobs.ucsd.edu/cosmos. The dates page lists the application fee as both $48 and $46, so confirm the amount before paying.
duration: about 4 weeks (2027 dates TBA)
pay_detail: Program cost $5,793 (2027 page), plus $48 application fee and a 2.5% card fee. Financial aid is available for admitted students with need, but not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: Students who have finished 8th grade. A parent must send a one-time consent form. Your high school principal signs the concurrent form.
how_to_apply: Apply online to OCC. Pick "Enrolling in High School and College at the same time." Then your parent sends in the consent form. You email the signed Concurrent Enrollment Form to dualenrollment@occ.cccd.edu. Only handwritten signatures count.
notes: The one-time parent consent form is also honored at Golden West College and Coastline College. After you graduate you must re-apply as a first-time college student. Help: fpr@occ.cccd.edu.
duration: By term. Up to 11 units in fall or spring, 10 in summer, 3 in winter.
pay_detail: Per-unit enrollment fees are waived. Concurrent students pay the College Service, Student Health and Student Representation fees plus books and supplies. CCAP classes at high schools may only need textbooks.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. High school students may need a work permit. Lifeguards must get Red Cross lifeguard training within 6 weeks of being hired. Jobs with children need a TB test from the last 2 years.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's job board at governmentjobs.com. Pick Community Services Leader or Instructor Lifeguard, then make an account and apply. If you are picked, the city contacts you in 4 to 6 weeks.
notes: The Apply Here link on the city's own page is broken, so go to the job board directly. The lifeguard posting itself shows $10.00 to $12.16 an hour, which is below the state minimum wage and does not match the city salary page, so ask HR. The Police Cadet job needs you to be 18. The city also runs free teen centers for grades 7 to 12. Paid work under 18 in California needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=ca.
duration: Part time, up to about 20 hours a week. Some jobs are seasonal and some are year-round.
pay_detail: The city salary page lists $20.00 to $24.31 an hour for Community Services Leaders and Instructor Lifeguards.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (two separate groups).
how_to_apply: Use the Register HERE link for your committee on the Teen Committees page (cosumnescsd.gov/460/Teen-Committees). Questions: call The Grove Teen Center at 916-405-5622 or email thegrove@Cosumnescsd.gov.
notes: Meeting times, location and deadlines are not posted on the page, so ask the District. Other volunteer roles on that page (adaptive recreation, youth coaching) are 18 and older.
duration: One school year. Teen Action Academy runs September to June; Teen Leadership Committee runs August to May. Meets every other week.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, high school juniors and seniors, 2.0 GPA, and a physician-completed medical exam form.
how_to_apply: Email explorers@cosumnescsd.gov to get application details. Fire Admin phone: 916-405-7100.
notes: Serves the Elk Grove area. Needs a physician-completed medical exam form. Meeting schedule and any costs are not posted on the page.
duration: School year

who_can_apply: Chicago residents attending a Chicago high school or equivalent (graduating seniors can apply), ages 16 to 19 on the first day (June 22 in 2026), with a Social Security number or ITIN.
how_to_apply: Log in to Chicago Youth Works, finish that application, choose After School Matters under Opportunities, then search library positions (program name CPL or your branch) in the ASM application. Branch staff interview in May.
notes: Positions were offered at every Chicago Public Library location. You can apply to many branches but be hired for one. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age here is 16. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org.
duration: 6 weeks (June 22 to Aug 1 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026: $17.05 per hour, 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Ages 14 to 19 on the start date of Jan 9, 2027. Teen Best Reads and Teen Media Lab are open to current 9th, 10th and 11th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Chicago Public Library form, not the After School Matters site. Answer the open questions with care. They decide who gets an interview. Each program has a video interview in Microsoft Teams. You can apply to as many as you like. You can only accept one.
notes: In the first month you enroll with After School Matters. That needs a Social Security Number and a parent or guardian's details. Questions: teenservices@chipublib.org. Gamer's Guild groups meet at different library branches. The sub-pages list these stipends. Teen Best Reads pays $3,500 for finishing work and showing up. Teen Media Lab pays $2,200 for Spring and $1,300 for Fall. The Best Reads page is dated 2025 and gives no year. So the 2026-27 cycle rests on the main page.
duration: Starts Jan 9, 2027. Gamer's Guild to June 10; Media Lab Jan to June 22 and Sept 7 to Dec 14; Best Reads to Dec 14.
pay_detail: Paid by stipend. Teen Best Reads pays $3,500. Teen Gamer's Guild pays $1,800. Teen Media Lab pays $2,200 for spring and $1,300 for fall. You get paid for finishing work and going to meetings.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older. Some departments accept only people 18 and older. Junior volunteers under 18 need a signed parental consent form.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, then an in-person interview and a health screening. The background check applies to adults only. Questions go to cpmcvolunteer@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing 2026-10-07. Not stated on the listing: TB test or immunization requirements, application window, and pay (unpaid volunteer role). The health screening is required but its contents are not described on this listing. Sutter's separate CPMC student volunteer page could not be read from this environment, so no details from it are used here. The listing is a lobby role, so it fits teens 16 and older who want to try hospital volunteering; it is not a high school program.
duration: Minimum 100 hours in one year, at least three to four hours per week
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the listing

who_can_apply: Chicago Public Schools students. 8th graders apply through GoCPS when they apply to high school; freshmen and 10th graders ask their school counselor.
how_to_apply: Rank CTE programs on your GoCPS high school application (8th grade), or talk to your counselor (9th and 10th grade). Email CTE@cps.edu for questions.
notes: Which pathways are offered differs by school; the CTE Matrix and Guide to CTE Programs on the page list them. CPS Work-Based Learning (internships, co-op) builds on these pathways. Contact: 773-553-2108.
duration: Multi-year pathway
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Current 10th and 11th graders at a district-run CPS school; priority goes to 10th graders. Must attend an information session and submit a recommendation from a trusted adult who is not a family member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google application form, a signed Student and Parent Expectations and Consent Contract and a Recommendation Form, then email everything to ChicagoBuilds@cps.edu.
notes: It is an Illinois Works Pre-Apprenticeship site and offers the Master Builder program with City Colleges of Chicago. Classes meet during the school day in an AM or PM cohort. Contact: 773-534-0909.
duration: Two school years, 2 hours a day at Dunbar High School campus (3000 S. King Drive)
pay_detail: Earn 2.5 high school credits per year of the program. Pay for senior-year internships is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school seniors at least 16 years old with a 2.0 GPA, excellent attendance and a counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply in 11th grade through your school; contact the citywide Cooperative Education coordinator (773-553-2108) for the process.
notes: Placement and training partners listed on the page include Genesys Works and Urban Alliance. Work permit: Illinois requires one only for under 16 and the minimum age is 16. Cutting school or work can cost credit.
duration: One school year, at least 180 hours a semester (about 10 hours a week); 3 elective credits
pay_detail: Students earn wages; the rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled at a Chicago Public Schools high school, including home-schooled students per City Colleges. A 2.5 GPA and strong attendance are typical requirements. If your GPA is lower, the page says recommendation letters are accepted. Under 16 needs a principal recommendation and approval from the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, get approval from the dual enrollment coordinator at your City Colleges campus, complete the City Colleges application and pick classes. Do not pay for or enroll in a class before talking to the Early College team.
notes: Undocumented students are eligible (CPS page). Some courses need ACT, SAT or City Colleges placement scores; many courses have no prerequisites. Jumpstart Pathways and Runway 606 are related CPS options. Seven campuses; each has a dual enrollment coordinator.
duration: Per semester; dual enrollment is one course per semester at a City Colleges campus
pay_detail: Free college credit. The page says you earn college credit for free.

who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in the city of Chicago. A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and a background check.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February. Provide 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and pass a background check. Questions: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
duration: Two years; Tuesday and Wednesday 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., September to May
pay_detail: Free: uniforms, materials, snacks and transportation help provided; scholarships possible. A paid summer internship between junior and senior year is possible (pay not stated).

who_can_apply: California residents in grades 8 to 12. Up to 20 students from out of state and other countries may also be enrolled. Each department has its own assignments.
how_to_apply: Apply online by department. A full application has the form and two teacher references, not peers. It has an unofficial transcript and department assignments. It has the $20 fee. It has the financial aid request if you want aid. Students can apply to more than one department. Each needs a full application.
notes: Students who finish can get 3 units of college extension credit from the California State University system (per the FAQ). Not a job. The pages did not name the 2027 campus, so check before planning travel.
duration: About one month: first day of classes July 5 and graduation July 31, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition and fees for California residents were $5,174 for 2026; 2027 rates 'will be posted soon'. Need based aid is available to California residents (nearly half of past students had much of tuition covered). $20 application fee, with fee waivers for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 by June 2, 2027, with no exceptions. It is a commuter program with no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Admission is competitive. Payment is due when you accept. Contact Steven Denham (email link on the page).
notes: No refunds after you enroll. Students match with CU Boulder mentors in May and at orientation on June 2, 2027. Poster session July 30, 2027.
duration: June 2 to July 30, 2027; 15 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: The page does not post the cost yet. Limited scholarships for students with financial need; say so on the application.

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students, including rising 9th graders. Classes at CU Anschutz Medical Campus are for grades 10 to 12 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through Science Discovery when the next season opens.
notes: The same page lists STEM Pathfinders (two weeks, bioscience June 1 to 12, 2026, engineering July 13 to 24, 2026) for the 2026 season. Check the price and 2027 dates on the program page.
duration: One week per class. The 2026 classes ran June to July.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ninth graders through high school juniors. You must be a first-generation college student (neither parent finished a 4 year degree). You must attend a target high school. You need at least a 2.5 GPA (freshmen without a GPA are asked to apply). You also need one more thing listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Call or email the program manager first. Norma Marquez, 303-315-7070, PCDP@ucdenver.edu.
notes: The 5 week summer program has college credit classes (ENGL 1020 or ENGL 1010) and fast track math.
duration: Multi-year. Summers: 2 weeks after 10th grade, 5 weeks after 11th grade.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at NYC public high schools. Grades 11 and 12 with an 80+ GPA can take courses on the partner campus. A 70+ GPA opens some courses. Grade 10 with a 70+ GPA can take non-credit college and career awareness courses, student development courses, and a few gateway college credit courses in some programs. College Now is for NYC Public Schools 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply to a specific CUNY campus's College Now program. Talk to your school's College Now liaison if your school has a partner campus, or contact a campus program directly. Many programs are first come, first served.
notes: Graduating seniors cannot join summer sessions. Students in Early College high schools can only join in summer. Costs beyond tuition (like textbooks) are not described on the CUNY page, so ask the campus.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
pay_detail: Free. The CUNY page describes College Now as a FREE program.

who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are in 7th to 10th grade now. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday. It meets in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term. The 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.
duration: Two-year staggered terms

who_can_apply: Middle and high schoolers ages 13 to 17 as of June 1. Each member needs an individual or family zoo membership and an up-to-date tetanus shot.
how_to_apply: To apply, call (701) 223-7543 ext. 3. Or send an email to educate@dakotazoo.org. Ask for the volunteer coordinator.
notes: Ask the zoo when the next sign-up opens.
duration: Summer. At least 12 hours in June and July and 5 hours in August. Monthly meetings on the first Tuesday, 6 to 7 pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens buy an $11 Zoo Crew t-shirt and need a zoo membership. The membership price is not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Volunteers 12 years and up. If a posting has its own age rule, it is listed in that posting. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Volunteer Agreement.
how_to_apply: Make a volunteer profile on the town website. Look at the open events and service projects. Sign up for one. For a long project, you send an interest form and town staff contact you.
notes: The Teens page says the town has volunteer chances for ages 13 and up. The volunteer page says 12 and up. Check each posting. Verification of community service hours is emailed by request after a volunteer event.
duration: One-time events or longer projects
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Any Danville resident can join. So can any student enrolled in a Danville middle school or high school. The page gives no age range.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Danville Youth Council application. It is an online form linked on the program page.
notes: Meetings are at the Town Offices, 500 La Gonda Way, Danville. The Teens page says the Town is recruiting for part-time positions in youth and teen programming. It does not give an age for those jobs.
duration: Monthly meetings, September to May
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the class. On day one you take a swim test. Swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes with only your legs, then swim 50 yards. You also bring up a 10 pound brick in a timed test. Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor are for 11 to 15 year olds. Junior Lifeguarding has a swim check on day one.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: These classes can lead to city pool jobs. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later. You may get to volunteer after the class. The page does not promise a job. To get a lifeguard card, you must come to every class and pass the tests. City lifeguard jobs start at 15. Swim teacher jobs start at 15, or 14 if you did Junior Swim Instructor. That is from the 2026 job posts. See the City of Davis Seasonal Lifeguard and Swim Instructor Jobs card.
duration: varies by course
pay_detail: Summer 2026 fees: Lifeguard Training $275, Junior Lifeguard Training $185, Junior Swim Instructor $100. Check the current Rec Guide or online registration for new prices.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.
duration: 6-week season starting the week of January 18, 2027
pay_detail: $17.39 an hour

who_can_apply: RLIT: ages 13 to 15. Returning RLIT: ages 13 to 16, only if you finished RLIT before and were invited back. Outdoor Education Volunteer: ages 14 to 16 in the Summer 2026 RecGuide (the 2026 Summer Camp Handbook says 13 to 16); you need your own bike and helmet and must ride at least 10 miles a day. RLITs must clear a local records check.
how_to_apply: RLIT: sign up on the city's WebTrac site when summer sign ups open. Returning RLITs must be approved first. Outdoor Education Volunteer: fill out the online form. The link is on the city's volunteer page. Then go to a group interview. Questions? Call 530-757-5626 or email csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: These facts come from the Summer 2026 Rec Guide and the 2026 camp handbook. The summer 2027 guide is not out yet. After RLIT, you go on a list for more volunteer hours. You may be asked back as a returning volunteer. The city's paid camp leader job starts at 15. So RLIT is a good first step. You need a bike and helmet for RLIT and Outdoor Education. Davis residents sign up first. Others sign up the next Monday. As of Oct 16, 2026, the volunteer page did not list camp volunteers.
duration: RLIT 2026: Session 1 June 15 to July 2, Session 2 July 13 to 31, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., with week three spent volunteering at a camp (about 30 hours, 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.). Outdoor Education Volunteers work at least three weeks between June 15 and August 21.
pay_detail: Unpaid, and there is a program fee. Summer 2026 fees: RLIT $247 (Session 1) or $264 (Session 2). Returning RLIT $66. Outdoor Education Volunteer $122, paid only after you are accepted.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard: 15 or older. You must pass a swim skills test before you start. When hired, you need Red Cross Lifeguard Training with First Aid, CPR and AED. You also need First Aid for Public Safety (Title 22). Swim Instructor: 15 or older, or 14 if you did the city's Junior Swim Instructor class. You must be at ease in the water. You need some time spent with kids. Babysitting, tutoring, camp or volunteering counts.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Paper forms are not taken. If you get an interview, lifeguards must turn in their cards. The best fits get an interview, alone or in a small group. Everyone who applies hears back by email.
notes: 2026 mandatory trainings: lifeguards the weekend of May 16 and 17 and the week of June 15 to 18; swim instructors May 2 and 3 and June 15 to 18. You must be free on those dates to be considered. Lifeguard shifts fall between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., any day of the week, and planned vacation is capped at 14 days and must be approved before summer. To get certified first, the city's Red Cross Lifeguard Training course needs you to be 15 by the last day of the course (summer 2026 fee $275, per the Summer 2026 RecGuide). The Off-Season Lifeguard job (fall to spring) needs weekday morning and noon availability. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
duration: 2026 pool season: May 18 to September 7 for lifeguards. Swim lessons ran May 18 to August 16, 2026.
pay_detail: 2026 rates: Lifeguard $17.83 to $18.27 per hour. Swim Instructor $16.97 to $17.39 per hour. Temporary part-time, no benefits.

who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab. See the Internship and Career Development Course.
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.

who_can_apply: Summer Playgrounds camps (Rainbow Summer, Summer Quest, Kids in the Kitchen, Arts and Crafts, Kinder Camp, PM Kids Club, Teen Camp): 15 or older before camp starts. Outdoor camps (Camp Putah, Summer Sampler, Backyard Adventures): 16 or older. You must own a bike and ride up to 10 miles a day. Both jobs need CPR and First Aid cards before camp starts.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Paper forms are not taken. Good fits get an email to set up an interview. In 2026, Summer Playgrounds picks had to be free on Friday, March 13 for a group interview day.
notes: In 2026, all staff had to come to training on June 6. More trainings ran June 1 to 13. Staff also met on Monday or Tuesday nights in summer and took online trainings. Other leader jobs open to teens: Inclusion Recreation Leader (2025 post: 15 for level I, 16 for level II, open Jan 22 to Apr 1, 2025). There is also a fall leader job for the Davis Children's Nutcracker. It needs you to be 15 with a work permit and pays $16.97 an hour. The 2026 post ran Aug 31 to Sep 28, 2026, and the work runs Nov 9 to Dec 13. Senior leader and Camp Putah leader jobs need you to be 18 or a high school grad. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
duration: June through August. 2026 camps ran ten weeks, June 15 to August 21, Monday to Friday. Summer Playgrounds shifts fall between 7:30 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. (schedules vary).
pay_detail: 2026: $16.97 per hour (Community Services Specialist I). Temporary part-time, no benefits.

who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm

who_can_apply: 15 or older by the start of the program, and a current high school student who returns to high school in the fall. The page does not set a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Online application with one professional reference (name and email).
