notes: Located in Washington, DC, so it is a commute for Maryland teens. Check back in February 2027 for the application.
duration: 6 weeks, 2 shifts a week (Tue/Wed or Wed/Thu), 10am to 3pm
pay_detail: Unpaid. At least 50 service hours.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.

who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.

who_can_apply: Students at schools with a DECA chapter. A school without one can request a new chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask the DECA advisor at your high school. If there is no chapter, use the Start a Chapter link on the page or contact info@deca.org or (703) 860-5000.
notes: State groups run the local contests. This guide already lists California, Georgia and Illinois DECA. Dues, travel and conference costs were not on the page, so ask your advisor.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Membership cost is not listed on the page. Ask your chapter advisor.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County youth ages 14 to 18 who are in school. You keep at least a C average and have good attendance and behavior.
how_to_apply: Get the DCFR Explorer application packet from the page. Send it in with 3 job references and your latest report card.
notes: Contact frexplorers@dekalbcountyga.gov. Not a paid job, so no work permit.
duration: Year-round, with a 2-week summer Cadet Training
pay_detail: $50 yearly fee, due after you are fully admitted. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who live in DeKalb County.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps; check the library's Teens Get Involved page and volunteer page for the next cycle.
notes: Meeting dates were listed as coming soon. Members can miss a meeting by telling advisors through Slack or the pre-meeting survey. A search result also described a separate Teen Library Board Trustee seat, but that was not on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings for the school year; at least one meeting must be in person
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours for attending meetings.

who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 16 and older. Adult volunteers also need a background check. The page does not list any other rule for teens.
how_to_apply: There are four steps. Fill out the Volunteer Application. Sign the Volunteer Waiver. Go to a short orientation, online or in person. Then start.
notes: Call 404-294-2838 or write to Monique Larkin at mllarkin@dekalbcountyga.gov. The page gives no direct link to the application. Other park volunteering lists no minimum age. Examples are clean-up days and nature programs.
duration: Ongoing. Weekday afternoons and Saturdays.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: DeKalb County School District students, mostly juniors and seniors. The program page links to a PDF of the rules on grades, behavior and attendance. Ask your school's WBL coordinator for the current rules.
how_to_apply: Apply to your school's WBL coordinator. Ask what the current rules are.
notes: Only for DeKalb schools students. You must leave campus at the start of your first WBL class, even on days you are not scheduled to work. The district CTAE office is at 1701 Mountain Industrial Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA 30083.
duration: A school class block (1, 2 or 3 periods in a row)
pay_detail: Paid or unpaid work experience. Pay amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: 2025 rules: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 21 who pass a drug screening and background check. Interns were picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: In 2025, online registration at dekalbcountyga.gov/dsyep. That address now leads to a registration form marked no longer active. For help the 2025 county release listed the Workforce Development Manager at (470) 572-8229.
notes: Confirm that a new cycle exists before planning around it. All dates, pay and rules here are from the 2025 county release. WorkSource DeKalb also lists youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers as a service group. It sends people to ATLworks.org to check eligibility. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: About 4 weeks (June 2 to July 3 in 2025)
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2025. A 2026 rate is not posted yet, so confirm it.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18, in good standing at school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the printable volunteer application on the program page. If accepted, pass a background check, drug screening and TB skin test, and attend orientation. Call (915) 263-5243.
notes: The page gives the March 15 to May 1 window as a yearly pattern, not as dates for 2027. Check the page in March.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 14 or ages 15 to 17, depending on the workshop. Your teen must be the right age by the first day.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian registers online and pays. You need health and emergency contact details. All sales are final.
notes: Costs money. The 2026 scholarship applications are closed. The Story in Focus workshop is full and has a waitlist, according to the program page.
duration: One week, 9:30 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: $450 for museum members and $500 for nonmembers for a full-day workshop. One full scholarship is offered per camp.

who_can_apply: Current high school students, rising freshmen through graduating seniors. You volunteer once a week in June and July. You do at least one shift at Plains Conservation Center or Chatfield Farms.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the summer window opens. Questions: volunteer office email on the program page.
notes: Also on the page: Junior Counselor Program for ages 13 to 15 (1 full week of camp, Monday to Friday 8:30 to 4:30). Also Gardens Teen Leaders, a school year group for teens who finished the summer program. The page gives no exact ages for the summer program. It only says high school.
duration: Once a week, June to July
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 or older. You must be in high school or in a college undergraduate program.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application reopens. All required documents must be in by the deadline.
notes: Denver Health is at 777 Bannock Street, Denver. Students who cannot shadow can look at the MC2 internship (rising juniors).
duration: Short shadowing experiences
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores who go to school in the Denver metro or Colorado Springs area and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. You start at the beginning of junior year. No exceptions to the rules.
how_to_apply: One form is used for all sites. A team reads your essays and your GPA. They also look at what you do, what you do for your town, how much you need money help, and 1 recommendation.
notes: Sites are Denver Health and Children's Colorado at Anschutz in Aurora. Others are in Broomfield, Highlands Ranch and Colorado Springs. Contact marisa.valeras@dhha.org. Or call 303-602-2685.
duration: Junior and senior years; 100 to 120 hour paid internship in junior year
pay_detail: Paid internship. The hourly rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Denver residents ages 14 to 21 who have a job or a job offer when they apply. The job does not have to be in Denver. Self-employed teens and unpaid interns are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the open window with a job or job offer. If chosen (first 2,000 eligible applicants in 2026), watch 10 money videos, send proof of 100 hours and a W-9. Under 18: a parent signs the W-9.
notes: The city does not give you a job. You must already have one. This is a bonus program, not a job. The 2026 page lists job fairs (March, April, May 2026) and says youthworks@denvergov.org and (720) 337-9675 for job help. Look for 2027 fairs in spring.
duration: Work 100+ hours between March 1 and August 14 (2026 cycle)
pay_detail: $250 retention bonus after the program ends.

who_can_apply: Sophomores or juniors (the page ties this to the 2025-2026 school year). Ages 14 to 17 during the internship. You must be free Monday to Friday for a full session. It is for high schoolers from underserved or underrepresented communities or schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens. Pick your top two tracks and a session, and give your household income and size. No transcript or recommendation is needed.
notes: The museum site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. Out of state students can apply if they are at the museum for the whole program. Housing is not provided. RTD buses are free for riders 19 and younger. Phone 303-370-6478.
duration: Three weeks. 2026 sessions: early June to late June, or early July to early August.
pay_detail: $1,803 per session in 2026. The page says it is to cover expenses, not wages.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 15 when you apply and by the last day of the training class.
how_to_apply: Apply on the city job site. Next is a short phone interview with the water team. Then take the free lifeguard class (you pass a swim pre-test first). Last is city hiring and onboarding.
notes: The pay and steps were read through a page reader, so confirm the pay on the city job posting. The page says the city needs early morning and daytime guards who can work year-round.
duration: Year-round and seasonal schedules
pay_detail: $19.29 per hour for new lifeguards. Red Cross certification is free if you will work for the city.

who_can_apply: For the free youth meals volunteer job, you must be at least 15 years old, finish an application and pass a background check.
how_to_apply: Email andrea.garcia@denvergov.org to start. Send the online application and any documents you need through Engage Denver. Send questions to Volunteers.Recreation@denvergov.org.
notes: The page says all volunteers must be at least 15, finish an application and pass a background check. It also lists other jobs, like park clean-ups and mountain park projects. It gives no age rule for those.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. The program page does not list an age range. About 40 to 50 teens take part.
how_to_apply: The program page does not list the steps. Applications open January to March 2027. Questions go to acalvo@platteforum.org or 303-893-0791.
notes: Orientation is each August. Interns stay for one year.
duration: One year, and you can stay up to 4 years. School year: Saturdays, 3 hours. Summer: 3 days a week, 5 hours a day.
pay_detail: Hourly stipend of $11 to $15. Interns also get therapy, tutoring, groceries, and art supplies.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from across Denver. The page lists no age or grade cutoffs. Teens under 18 need a signed parent consent form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TAB interest form. Then follow up with the branch you want to join.
notes: Meetings are in person or online at some branches. The program runs only in English right now. Questions: tab@denverlibrary.org.
duration: Meetings follow the school calendar. They may be weekly, every other week, or monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Snacks are provided.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 14 or older to apply.
how_to_apply: Look at the page to see what is open. If you have questions, email volunteers@denverlibrary.org.
notes: The main volunteer page says most roles are for adults 18 and older, but teen roles exist. Positions fill up, so email the volunteer office to ask when more open.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: 4-H and FFA youth. Ages are not stated on the page. See the 2027 4-H and FFA Eligibility Guidelines linked there. Each state team arranges its own travel.
how_to_apply: Register online. Upload the State Authorized Official form and youth consent forms. Pay by check made out to CSU Extension (no credit cards). Questions: Joy Bauder, CSU 4-H.
notes: The page says all payments are due Dec 30, 2027, which looks like a typo for 2026. Ask Colorado 4-H. Contests also include horse hippology and horse bowl.
duration: January 6 to 9, 2027
pay_detail: $175 per contest if you register by Nov 16, 2026. $250 from Nov 17 to Dec 1. Adults 18 and up: $50. Hotel is extra (Renaissance Denver listed at $129 a night).

who_can_apply: Lifeguard, swim instructor and aquatic jobs: age 15 or older. Part-time camp counselor: age 16 or older and some experience with kids. Full time day camp leader: age 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Go to the summer jobs page. To see all locations, type LIFEGUARD in the search box on that page.
notes: Lifeguards need American Red Cross or YMCA lifeguard certification and CPR-AED. The Y offers lifeguard training. It reimburses the training cost after 3 months of employment. The page does not show a year, so check the jobs search for current openings.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Kids can volunteer from age 10. Those under 17 must have a parent or guardian with them during their shift. Teens who are 17 can volunteer with a parent or guardian's signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the shelter website. Some roles, such as the Litter-ary Club, need orientation first. Email the volunteer team with questions.
notes: The shelter can verify hours for the Silver Cord award. Ages 10 to 16 cannot come alone. A parent or guardian must stay for the whole shift. Questions: volunteer@arl-iowa.org.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in high school. The application asks for your grade, 9th through 12th.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the program page. Answer the essay questions. Six of them must be filled in. Upload five pieces of your art. Questions: studioclasses@desmoinesartcenter.org.
notes: A class, not a job. Next dates not posted.
duration: Nine months, once a week, following the school calendar.
pay_detail: Tuition is not listed on the program page. Ask the Studio Arts Department. The Art Center offers help with travel costs for students who need help getting to class.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for an ongoing volunteer role. The event volunteer form is for people who will not volunteer on a regular basis. Age rules for event volunteers: not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: If a job looks good to you, fill out a volunteer form. There is one for ongoing roles and one for events. Both are on the program page.
notes: The program page says the event form is a good fit for Silver Cord volunteer programs but does not explain that program. The page lists no contact name, phone or email.
duration: Ongoing, or short event shifts. Hours per week are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students who are current juniors or younger. Graduating seniors cannot join. Priority goes to the classes of 2027 and 2028. Classes with prerequisites need those finished first.
how_to_apply: Fill out a pre-registration form for each class. You can take up to two classes. Seats depend on space and placement is not promised. For classes at Central Campus or Valley High School, do not send the form. Contact the Coordinator for that program.
notes: Campuses listed for 2026 were Ames, Ankeny, Perry, Des Moines (Urban), West Des Moines, and online. Students are expected to attend when the class begins. Call (800) 362-2127 with questions.
duration: Courses run from late May through early August. In 2026 they ran from May 26 to August 5.
pay_detail: No cost to the student. Books and supplies are provided before the first day of class.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in 2026-2027, or 2025 and 2026 high school graduates, who are interested in healthcare, math or science. Ages: not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Register online with the link on the program page and pay by the deadline. Questions go to Taylor Burgraff at taylor.burgraff@drake.edu or 515-271-1823.
notes: Meals are in the Hubbell Dining Hall. Spots are forfeited if payment is not made by the deadline. No refunds after the deadline.
duration: 3 days and 2 nights in a campus residence hall (July 9 to 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: $200 per student. Financial help may be available for students who qualify.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24, in or out of school. You must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or someone lawfully admitted to the U.S. The program serves youth who face big barriers to jobs or more school.
how_to_apply: Register on IowaWORKS.gov. Then call or visit your local IowaWORKS office to meet with a career planner who checks if you qualify. You can also fill out the Workforce Services Form on the program page.
notes: The program page does not list local office addresses or phone numbers. Iowa Workforce Development is at 1000 East Grand Avenue, Des Moines, IA 50319.
duration: Not stated on the program page. Follow-up help lasts at least 12 months after you finish, as needed.
pay_detail: Paid and unpaid work experiences are listed. Pay rates are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 14 by June 1 and no older than 18, entering grade 9 or above in the fall. A parent or guardian must sign the application. Teens who turn 18 during camp need a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application. A parent or guardian must also sign it. Go to a 1-hour group interview. If accepted, attend a 3-hour training and then sign up for your weeks.
notes: Summer camp runs 9 to 4, Monday to Friday, from June to mid-August. Questions: daycamp@lhf.org.
duration: At least 2 weeks for new junior counselors, scheduled 8:30 to 4:15, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Hours may count toward a school Silver Cord award, so check with your school.

who_can_apply: The lifeguard class is for ages 15 and up. The page does not state an age rule for the jobs themselves. Call the department to ask about camp staff and other seasonal jobs.
how_to_apply: Register for the lifeguard class with the Register Here link on the city Aquatics page. Apply for jobs through the Park Jobs link on the same page. Questions: parks@dmgov.org or (515) 237-1386.
notes: The Dec 4 to 6 class date is shown without a year on the program page. Iowa work paper rules for teens were not checked. Summer camp staff jobs may have a higher age limit, so confirm before you apply.
duration: Lifeguard jobs at the indoor pool are year-round. The class meets Friday to Sunday.
pay_detail: Paid jobs. Pay is not listed on the program pages. The lifeguard class costs $200, and the city refunds the $200 if you accept a job offer with the department.

who_can_apply: High school and middle school students. Tech theatre jobs are for ages 14 and up. For education jobs, you must go to every class. You must talk with the education director. You must do training at the start of the term. The age range for education jobs is not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: New students fill out the Pre-Intern Program form. Then send the request form for the class you want. For tech theatre, call the volunteer coordinator at 563-292-8962. For education, call the education director at 515-974-5365.
notes: The request form on the page was labeled for the 2025-26 winter and spring season, so confirm it is current. The paid internships on the same page are for college students only.
duration: By semester (fall, winter, spring). Weekly hours are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up. You must be 14 by June 1 to apply. You need to be comfortable outside in all weather.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and one more set of questions. Then do an online training and orientation. Staff will contact you after they get your form. Send questions to heidi.anderson@polkcountyiowa.gov or call 515-323-5360.
notes: You keep track of your own hours and bring the paperwork for Silver Cord. The program page also lists Nature Center volunteering on the same volunteer menu.
duration: The full length of the camp you pick. Camps are 2 to 5 days, mostly in June and July, 9 AM to 3:30 PM at Jester Park.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Hours can count toward the Silver Cord award.

who_can_apply: Crew members are ages 14 to 18 in Polk County, Iowa. You must be able to work outside in all kinds of weather and get yourself to a daily meeting site.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the next application. For questions, email youthcorps@polkcountyiowa.gov.
notes: Summer 2026 sessions ran June 8 to 26 and July 13 to 31. The program provides transportation, a daily snack, lunch on Saturdays and all summer days, safety gear, and uniform shirts. Crew members are paid for days they show up to work.
duration: Summer: 3 weeks, Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 1:30 PM. Spring and fall sessions also run.
pay_detail: Stipend paid at the end of the session. The summer 2026 page said up to $1,100 for 3 weeks. The FAQ says at least $600. Crew members are paid for days they show up.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen volunteer application and a waiver signed by a parent or guardian, in pen. Turn them in at your local Des Moines library. The volunteer leader will contact you. Summer volunteers must also go to a summer orientation session.
notes: The orientation event program page was from May 2025 and has already happened. Check with your branch for the next orientation date. The page does not name which branches take teens.
duration: No set hours on the page. Work happens during the school year and for the Summer Reading Program.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application through the DMACC link on the program page. Keep your email and phone number current.
notes: The center is at 1171 7th Street, Des Moines, IA 50314 (email info@evelynkdaviscenter.org). The program page gives no phone number for Y-ExCL. Another page lists 515-697-7700 and a link on it shows 515-967-7700, so check before you call.
duration: 10 weeks: 2 weeks of training and 8 weeks of job placement
pay_detail: $12.00 an hour, 20 hours a week, Monday through Thursday

who_can_apply: High school students, including home-schooled students. You need a Special Admissions Recommendation Form each term. You, a parent, and your principal or their designee must sign it. Students on an F-1 international visa cannot be in high school and DVC at the same time.
how_to_apply: Apply to DVC. After you are accepted, submit the Special Admissions Recommendation Form in the student portal. List the classes you want. Then check prerequisites and sign up for classes.
notes: A signed form with no classes listed is not accepted. You can only sign up for the classes listed on the form. If you use a school district program such as dual enrollment, follow that program instead. Not sure which one to use? Ask your counselor.
duration: By term
pay_detail: California high school students pay no tuition. You pay student union fees and the cost of class materials.

who_can_apply: High school students in a partner school district: Acalanes, Martinez (Alhambra High School), Mt. Diablo, or San Ramon Valley. Clayton Valley Charter High School also takes part. Each program has its own steps, so talk to your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor first. Then follow the steps for your school district on the DVC page. Questions go to the Early College Credit office at DVC.
notes: College Now is a middle-college program for Mt. Diablo 11th and 12th graders. Classes are at the DVC Pleasant Hill campus. CollegeConnect lets students earn up to 30 college units before they graduate. Diamante Scholars is a separate program for Mt. Diablo seniors. The page lists the Early College Credit email as EarlyCollegeCredit@dvc.edu.
duration: Classes by school term
pay_detail: Free. You pay no tuition, textbook or enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: The classes are made for high school students. In summer they are open to all students. You must come every day. Fields include animation, business, computer programming, health, robotics and trades.
how_to_apply: Apply to DVC for summer. Then send the Special Admissions Recommendation Form, signed by you, a parent and your counselor. Then sign up for your academy in the student portal. Use the interest form on the page for updates.
notes: Health is at the Pleasant Hill and San Ramon campuses. The Special Admissions form is for students who are not graduating this spring or earlier. Public Safety is mainly for teens and new graduates who want to be police explorers or cadets.
duration: Short courses of about 1 to 2 weeks. In 2026, Health ran July 27 to 31 and Public Safety ran July 6 to 17.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the academies page.

who_can_apply: Teen volunteers, around age 15 and up. The page says a 14-year-old may start the application one month before their 15th birthday. The page does not state a maximum age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for a role. The roles are Exhibit Host, Team Spark and Team Celebration. Email a resume and a letter from an adult who is not family. Send them to VolunteerLA@discoverycube.org. Then do an interview and a mandatory orientation.
notes: The museum is in Sylmar in the San Fernando Valley. The letter of recommendation cannot come from a family member. Questions: 818-686-2835.
duration: Minimum 60 hours; two 4-hour shifts every 30 days
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need service hours that are checked. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.
duration: At least one four-hour shift every 30 days. 60 hours of service before the Cube verifies your hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.

who_can_apply: Douglas County residents ages 15 to 17, or ages 18 to 25 with a minor in the household. The minor does not have to be related to you. You need U.S. citizenship or lawful presence. Household income must be $75,000 a year or less.
how_to_apply: Use the interest form linked on the program page to see if you are eligible. Virtual information sessions are held about three times a month. You can also call 720-874-5130 or text 720-853-1837.
notes: Only for Douglas County residents. The office is in Centennial, south of Denver. Other help includes GED support and tuition help for short job training.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Services are free. Paid internships are offered, but the pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Camp volunteers and general program volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Other roles do not list an age on the page. Everyone fills out a volunteer waiver. The page says teens to seniors can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lyman Woods application for the role you want. Also fill out the volunteer waiver. Program and camp volunteers send in an application and go to an interview and training. A criminal background check is only for program volunteers 18 or older.
notes: REAP restoration workdays need an RSVP. The park district also runs Counselor in Training (C.I.T.) camps for teens. The teen camps page lists no CIT sign-up fee; it lists only a $5 or $10 per-camp withdrawal service fee. Ages for most teen camps are not listed.
duration: Camp volunteers help during the summer. Other roles are ongoing.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 18. You send audition videos. Composers send three original works.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload audition videos and pay the $75 fee. Ask one teacher to email a recommendation. For need-based aid, email a tax form.
notes: This costs money, but scholarships exist. You must meet the Feb 15 date to be considered for them.
duration: Two weeks, June 16 to 29, 2027
pay_detail: Residential $2,850. Commuter $2,000. Commuter PLUS $2,200. There is also a $75 application fee. Almost 70 percent of students get aid.

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors in 2026-27 who are at least 15 by June 1, 2027 and from the Research Triangle area. Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN to receive the stipend. Students must provide their own transportation.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a recommendation letter (links on the CeBA page). Applicants hear back in mid-April.
notes: The 2026 deadline is stated two ways. It is March 20 on the flyer and March 27 in the FAQ. The page says there is no housing or transportation help, so only local students are considered. The $2,400 is a completion award. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 31), about 9 am to 5 pm on site
pay_detail: $2,400 awarded on completion of the program

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or 17 (16 by June 24 in 2026). Students must attend both days at one site. Space is limited to 25 slots at each site.
how_to_apply: Student completes the online application and a parent or guardian completes the Participation Agreement (both on Qualtrics links on the page). No late or incomplete submissions.
notes: Both Duke pages are titled Junior Volunteer Program but describe this event for 2026. The application window was only 3 days, so watch the page in early April. Questions: DRHVolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Durham) or DRAH_VolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Raleigh). Duke University Hospital says it no longer offers a junior volunteer program for high school students.
duration: 2 days (2026: June 23-24 at Duke Regional in Durham; June 24-25 at Duke Raleigh Hospital)

who_can_apply: Durham City or Durham County residents between 14 and 24 as of June 30, 2026, per the Duke page. The Duke article describes participants as Durham-area high school students.
how_to_apply: Submit the Durham YouthWorks application and select the healthcare category (link on the Duke Community Affairs page). Contact: Kimberly Monroe, kimberly.monroe@duke.edu.
notes: Applications go through Durham YouthWorks (City of Durham), whose own page could not be read (blocked). The article says about 50 students were planned for the latest class. North Carolina requires a Youth Employment Certificate for anyone under 18 who works; the employer starts that process.
duration: 3 weeks (2026: July 6-24, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students in current grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 to attend. (The page also lists middle school programs for grades 6-8.)
how_to_apply: Join the information request list on the Duke Pre-College page to be told when 2027 dates and courses open.
notes: Courses, session dates and fees for Summer 2027 were not posted on 2026-10-09. Check back after the October 2026 announcement.
duration: Three sessions; dates to be announced in October 2026
pay_detail: 2027 residential fee not yet posted (Duke lists it as to be determined). Enrollment deposit: $500 before April 2, 2027, or $1,500 after April 1. Airport shuttle $45 each way; extra nights $120 each.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up at Dunwoody Nature Center (15 and up at Island Ford). Be mature, reliable, flexible and energetic. You must attend a pre-camp orientation, in person the first time.
how_to_apply: Write to the Junior Counselor Coordinator. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org.
notes: Phone 770-394-3322, info@dunwoodynature.org. The first email link on the page goes to a different address, so use the one in the FAQ (juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org). Camp dates are not listed on the page. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: Asked to commit to a 5-day camp week, but you can work any days you are free. Full day 9:00 am to 4:00 pm or half day 9:00 am to 1:30 pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer position, no cost. You can ask for a letter documenting your hours.

who_can_apply: Teen and adult volunteers: age 14 or entering high school. Junior volunteers: junior high school students.
how_to_apply: Junior volunteers fill out the online application, permission form and photo release. Teen and adult volunteers check openings on the museum volunteer page. You can also call or email Jessica Greenlaw.
notes: Experience with kids is helpful but not required. Summer teen volunteering is not mentioned on the page, so ask. The minimum age for the junior program is not given, only junior high.
duration: Teen shifts start at 2 hours. Junior: one weekend day (Friday to Sunday) each week for 3 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: One-time community events: ages 8 and up with an adult. Long-term roles are generally 18 and up, with limited openings for ages 13 to 17. Family roles are ages 10 and up with an adult.
how_to_apply: For long-term roles, apply online through the volunteer portal. Then meet with program staff for an interview. After that, go to orientation and training. For one-time restoration workdays, find a date on the events calendar and register.
notes: Getting started for a long-term role takes about 2 to 3 months. The FAQ page says background checks apply to people 16 and older in one place and 18 and older in another. Ask the Volunteer Services office what applies to you. Call 630-933-7233 or write to volunteer@dupageforest.org. The page does not list which long-term roles take people under 18.
duration: One-time workdays or long-term roles with a yearly minimum of hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 13, or have a guardian's permission to fill out the form. The form lets you pick the age group you want to work with, including teens 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer form (skills, preferred age group, days and times, hours per week, emergency contact). Questions: Maker_STEAM@dconc.gov.
notes: Days offered are Monday to Saturday. Time options are morning, afternoon or evening. The page does not describe a teen-only volunteer track.
duration: You choose hours per week on the form

who_can_apply: The For Teens page says the program is for all tweens and teens in grades 6 to 12. The general volunteer page says all volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Contact the teen librarian at your preferred branch. The general volunteer page also says to fill out the volunteer application form (PDF) and bring it to your nearest library.
notes: The two Durham County Library pages disagree on age: the teen page says grades 6 to 12, the general volunteer page says 14 or older. Ask the teen librarian which applies. The library says it cannot currently host court-mandated community service hours.
duration: Ongoing, set with the branch

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 years old (bring proof of age to the pre-course swim test). The page also says candidates must be at least 15 on or before the last class session, so ask which rule applies. You must pass the pre-course swim test: a 150 yard swim-tread-swim, then a timed event with a 10 pound object retrieved from 7 to 10 feet deep.
how_to_apply: Sign up online at dprplaymore.org (Register Online). Or sign up in person at any Durham Parks and Recreation site. Then pass the swim test before the course. Apply for lifeguard jobs on the City of Durham career page.
notes: Search ActiveNet for DAS for current dates. Space is limited and filled by order of pre-course test registration. Questions: DPRAquatics@durhamnc.gov, 919-560-4444. Whether teens under 18 need NC working papers was not checked.
duration: About 6 hours of online work, then in-person sessions (Spring 2026 courses ran March 30 to April 2)
pay_detail: Training is free. City of Durham pool lifeguard jobs started at $18.90 an hour on the outdoor pools page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. No experience is required.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer page and sign up for an open shift. Or email DPRVolunteers@DurhamNC.gov about the role you want. Then fill out the online volunteer application.
notes: Phone 919-560-4355. DPR also lists tutor and mentor roles with youth at recreation centers (after school and summer camp assistants); the page does not give an age for those, so ask.
duration: Shifts as listed on the volunteer opportunities page.
pay_detail: Unpaid. DPR can give you a record of service hours for school or scholarships.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. High school graduate, equivalency holder, or currently in a program leading to a diploma. GPA of 2.00 or above.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student interest form on the Durham Tech page. Or contact the Apprenticeship Coordinator, Dr. Norman Collins, at 919-536-7200 ext. 1402.
notes: Open to students 16 and up, including current high school students. Which fields are offered is not listed on this page.
duration: Varies by field
pay_detail: Pre-apprenticeship may or may not be paid. Apprenticeship pays a wage scale that increases with experience. Tuition waiver while in the apprenticeship.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. Need a 2.8 or higher unweighted GPA, or test scores showing college readiness. The career path also accepts a written recommendation from your principal. To stay in, you must keep at least a 2.0 college GPA after two college courses.
how_to_apply: Go to an interest meeting. Talk to your school counselor and the Durham Tech liaison. Then send the CCP application and papers. These are the waiver and pathway forms, test scores and transcript.
notes: Students at Middle College High School, City of Medicine Academy and Durham School of Technology use a different path and deadline. The pages state no North Carolina residency rule. Check with the college. The eligibility page confirms the 2.8 GPA or test score rule. It also confirms the principal waiver for the career path.
duration: One semester at a time
pay_detail: Tuition-free

who_can_apply: Teens and young adults ages 14 to 21 who live in Durham or Durham County. You need an email address that you check often.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open early in the year. Spots may be chosen by lottery.
notes: In 2026, more than 500 youth finished Part 1 and 120 were placed in hybrid or in-person jobs, so not everyone gets an in-person job. Questions: youthworks@durhamnc.gov. The city has a Getting Prepared Guide on the page.
duration: Part 1 training in the spring, then Part 2 summer work experience.
pay_detail: Earn up to $880 and beyond if you finish both Part 1 (training) and Part 2 (summer work).

who_can_apply: Not stated.
how_to_apply: The home page has a Sign Up button for volunteers, but the volunteer page it links to showed a 404 error on 2026-10-09. Contact EBAYC directly (offices in Oakland and Sacramento are listed on the home page).
notes: Read the home page on 2026-10-09. It says EBAYC has many volunteer opportunities and welcomes volunteer groups and student internships, but it gives no ages, dates or pay. The volunteer page linked from it (ebayc.org/volunteer/) returned a 404 error on Oct 7 and again on Oct 9, 2026. Confirm the minimum age with EBAYC.

who_can_apply: High school students in the EBMUD service area. For 2026 the East Bay program took students referred by partner groups. The Maintenance track (Stockton) required age 16 by June 24, 2026.
how_to_apply: In 2026 you could not apply to EBMUD directly for the East Bay program. Ask a partner to refer you: ACE Mentor, Biotech Partners, Eden Area ROP, Girls Inc. of Alameda County, Youth UpRising. Email internships@ebmud.com, (510) 287-0710.
notes: Referral only in 2026. Separate Mokelumne programs (Fisheries in Lodi, Ranger in Valley Springs, Maintenance in Stockton) ran in 2026 with rolling review.
duration: 6 weeks, mid-June through August, about 16 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid stipend (amount not posted)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. The program page does not list a swim test or a home city rule.
how_to_apply: Download the Junior Cadet application packet from the program page. Turn it in by the deadline. If you are picked, register by the second deadline.
notes: This is a training class, not a paid job. Sessions are full day only. The program page does not list session dates. It also lists Junior Lifeguards for ages 8 to 12 and Junior Lifeguard Aides for ages 13 to 15, with no details. Call 1-888-327-2757. For lifeguard jobs at age 16 and older, see the district lifeguard jobs page.
duration: 2 weeks per session, about 4 sessions each summer
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Financial aid is offered through the Regional Parks Foundation Campership program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The program page does not list a grade or home city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply when applications open in 2027. If you are picked after the interview, you then register for the week. Ask about the $30 scholarship through the park district financial aid line.
notes: The program page says teens earn 35 community service hours, build job skills and may get a future camp job. It does not name the parks. Contact: Stewart Reid, Recreation Coordinator, 510-544-2558. Financial aid: 1-888-327-2757, option 2.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: $50 for the one week. A limited number of $30 scholarships are available. The page lists 35 community service hours and does not mention pay.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older when the Lifeguard Academy starts in late April. You must swim 550 yards in 10 minutes or less. The district also tests a deep dive and carrying a 150 pound person in open water.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the park district job portal. Pick the lifeguard posting. You must be free for all 10 days of the academy.
notes: Lifeguard I is the entry job at age 16. Head lifeguard jobs need age 18 and a finished 12th grade. The program page does not say if a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds, so ask HR. The district also lists younger water programs: Junior Lifeguard Aides (ages 13 to 15) and Jr Lifeguard Cadets (ages 14 to 17), with no details on that page. Call 1-888-327-2757.
duration: 10 day paid academy, then a seasonal job
pay_detail: Paid. The program page says a competitive wage but gives no hourly rate. The 10 day Lifeguard Academy is paid, so there is no tuition.

who_can_apply: Gate Attendant (high school pathway): at least 16 and completed 10th grade. Other jobs have their own rules; check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply on governmentjobs.com/careers/ebparks. HR: (510) 544-2154.
notes: The 16 minimum is from the Gate Attendant page; other roles (for example lifeguard) may differ. The park district says it hires hundreds of seasonal students each year.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Pay is not posted on the youth pages. See each job posting.

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools: U-46 (Bartlett, Elgin, Larkin, South Elgin, Streamwood), District 300 (Dundee-Crown, Hampshire, Jacobs), District 301 (Burlington Central), District 303 (St. Charles East, St. Charles North, Compass Academy), Cambridge Lakes Charter and St. Edward Central Catholic. The tracks are for juniors, seniors, or juniors and seniors, depending on the track. Talk with your counselor.
how_to_apply: Talk with your parents and your high school counselor first, then use the online Dual Credit application (Apply Now). Independent enrollment also needs approval from the ECC Dual Credit office. Contact: DualCredit@elgin.edu or 847-214-7887.
notes: Accelerate College students may need to qualify for college-level courses and testing may be required. Each district publishes a Dual Credit Guide listing what its schools support. The ECC page also lists Upward Bound, Educational Talent Search and College and Career Readiness workshops.
duration: Per semester
pay_detail: Accelerate College: no tuition for district-approved courses. Independent enrollment and Dual Enrollment: students are usually billed tuition. Career tech courses the district does not approve require tuition.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 at certain schools. The middle schools are Abbott, Ellis, Kimball, Larsen, Carpentersville, Canton and Tefft. The high schools are Elgin, Larkin, Streamwood and Dundee-Crown. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You must show money need or be a possible first-generation college student.
how_to_apply: Send in the Talent Search application with your papers. You can do this online, by email to talentsearchtransition@elgin.edu, by mail or by fax. You can also get a paper copy from your school counselor. A guardian helps if you are under 18.
notes: Contact: 847-214-7764, Building K Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin. Only the schools named above are served. The page does not state a cost or federal funding; the pay_detail wording is not confirmed by the page.
duration: Ongoing through high school
pay_detail: A federally funded TRIO program. The page does not state a cost, pay or stipend.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at Dundee-Crown, Larkin or Streamwood High School who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and are either potential first-generation college students or from a low-income household (U.S. Department of Education rules). If unsure, apply and staff will tell you if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Student and parent or guardian complete the online Upward Bound application. Counselors and teachers can fill out the Student Recommendation Form. Contact: upwardbound@elgin.edu, 847-214-7253, Building K, Room K102, 1700 Spartan Drive, Elgin.
notes: Only for students at the three listed high schools. The page does not mention a summer part or a start date, so ask staff. A web search snippet suggested Elgin High School is also served, but the ECC page itself lists only the three above.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Berkeley residents ages 15 to 24, recruited through Berkeley YouthWorks.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Berkeley YouthWorks interest form (the Ecology Center sends you there). Contact alex@ecologycenter.org or 510-697-4808.
notes: Berkeley residents only. YouthWorks asks for an interest form and a 15 to 20 minute interview. Pay rate and exact academy dates are not posted.
duration: 8 weeks (summer) or 12 weeks (spring)
pay_detail: Paid; rate not posted

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending high school in the Castro Valley, Hayward, San Leandro or San Lorenzo Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Ask your home high school counselor to contact the Eden Area ROP career counselor at (510) 293-2973. Main office (510) 293-2900.
notes: Center is at 26316 Hesperian Blvd, Hayward. Cost, pay and ages are not stated on the page. Some pathways are offered only at certain high schools. Students outside the four districts are not listed as eligible. Work-based learning is mentioned (for example in education careers) but no formal internship structure is described.
duration: Classes are held Monday to Friday; course length varies by class
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 who are at least 15 years old.
how_to_apply: Download the application and email it to k12partnerships@middlesexcollege.edu, or call 732-906-2554 to schedule a virtual appointment.
notes: Separate Dual Enrollment: in participating districts, college courses are taught at the high school. Ask your counselor.
duration: Courses of 3 to 4 credits; up to 8 credits per semester
pay_detail: $150 per course plus textbooks for in-county residents; students from other counties, states or countries pay the out-of-county rate (not listed).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Registration required.
how_to_apply: Register on the library event listing (registration required). Meetings alternate between the Main Library and the North Edison Branch; members may attend at either. Main Library: 340 Plainfield Avenue, Edison, 732-287-2298.
notes: The page did not print a year for the October 14 session, and the library's own Young Adults page had no volunteer details. Confirm the meeting location when you register.
duration: Monthly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Any high school student who has finished freshman year.
how_to_apply: The volunteer office takes names in April, according to a November 2025 article. The article gives no form or phone number for the junior program. The hospital main phone is 760-340-3911.
notes: Confirm first: the dates come from a November 2025 article, not a page. The Volunteers page does not mention the junior program, and the number 760-773-1304 appears on it with no label.
duration: One shift a week from June orientation to the end of July
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Qualified students in grades 9 to 12 who can benefit from college classes. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Do the Steps for Dual Enrollment each term you want to register. The steps are listed on a separate page. Call 310-660-3344 or email dualenrollment@elcamino.edu.
notes: Unit limits are not on this page. Dual enrollment uses Remind to post updates for students.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Enrollment fees are waived for dual enrollment students.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older and done with 8th grade. One-year minimum. No summer internships or programs shorter than one year. Selection starts with an annual application seminar.
how_to_apply: Go to the yearly sign up meeting first. Then apply. The steps are on the El Camino Health junior volunteer page.
notes: Read again on 2026-10-16. There is no summer only option. Once you are in, you can stay through the summer after you graduate. Call Mountain View at 650-940-7214 or Los Gatos at 408-866-3940. Check the page in mid January 2027 to sign up for the next junior meeting.
duration: At least 1 year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 with at least an average C grade or better in school. You can stay in the Post until your 21st birthday. A criminal record does not always block you, but every applicant gets a background check. The form has a line for a parent or guardian to sign.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Police Explorers application, a PDF on the city website. Give three reasons you want to join. A parent or guardian signs it too. Every applicant gets a background check.
notes: The paper application has a line for a Social Security number. Ask the department why before you write it down, and never send it by email. The form has no date, so ask the department if it is the current one. The same page lists a paid Cadet Program for college students. It also lists Volunteers in Police Service for adults 18 and older.
duration: At least 12 hours a month
pay_detail: Explorers donate at least 12 hours a month, counted every quarter. The department buys the uniform. You bring your own shoes or boots.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 who go to El Cerrito High School or live in El Cerrito. A parent or guardian must give written consent. You can serve until your 19th birthday or until you graduate from El Cerrito High School.
how_to_apply: Submit the youth application on the city page. A parent or guardian must give written consent. Applicants will be invited to interview with the City Council at a publicly noticed meeting. The City Clerk handles questions.
notes: Ten city groups want a youth member. They include the Park and Recreation Commission, the Planning Commission and the Committee on Aging. The full list is on the page. Youth members must follow attendance rules and do orientation training. They also take a one-hour harassment prevention training. City Clerk phone: 510-215-4305.
duration: Until age 19 or graduation
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 17 can join the Shelter Volunteer, Cats at the Zoo and Community Service programs. A parent or guardian must go to orientation and basic animal handling training. Teens 14 to 16 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. That adult must also be a registered volunteer.
how_to_apply: Send a volunteer form on the volunteer portal. Then finish orientation in person or in the MyImpact app. Email the volunteer team to book your first day.
notes: Teens 16 and 17 need a parent or guardian to take Level 1 Animal Handling Training too. Maybe you only need service hours for school or NHS. The page says you can email the volunteer team and skip onboarding.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18. Volunteers 13 to 17 need a parent or legal guardian to sign a waiver.
how_to_apply: Download the form from the program page and fill it out. Email it to EPHConnections@elpasohealth.com. The program page lists no phone number for the volunteer program.
notes: The program page lists last year's totals: 3,344 backpacks, 331,947 pounds of food and 404 car seats. The totals are not dated.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Volunteers 17 and up must have a state-issued ID.
how_to_apply: Click the link on the program page. It goes to the City of El Paso volunteer page on governmentjobs.com. Apply there.
notes: The program page does not say which library branches need teen help. Call the Main Library at (915) 212-READ to ask.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. Live in El Paso, Brewster, Culberson, Hudspeth, Jeff Davis or Presidio County. Be a U.S. citizen or allowed to work in the U.S. Males over 18 must be registered for Selective Service.
how_to_apply: Check the list of who can join on the program page. Then email nextforce@borderplexjobs.com. The bottom of the site also lists 915-887-2600.
notes: The program page says its help is most useful for veterans and military spouses. It is also useful for youth in foster care and young adults who left high school. The page lists a hiring event on Nov 10, 2026 from 10 AM to 2 PM at Bassett Place. The event is called Hiring Red, White & You.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Gas money, uniforms and child care help are free.

who_can_apply: Youth interested in the fire service. The page does not list an age range or other rules. Ask the coordinator.
how_to_apply: Go to any meeting on the schedule. Or ask the coordinator for an application. You can write to efdexplorers439@cityofelgin.org. You can also call 847-931-6175.
notes: The page lists no age range and no fees. Equipment provided: uniform, bunker gear, SCBA, mask, gloves, boots and hood. Meetings are on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday at 6:00 p.m. The page now lives at elginil.gov (the old cityofelgin.org address redirects). The page does not say members become CPR certified; it lists CPR and first aid as topics. Call before you go to confirm age rules.
duration: Meetings twice a month, 1st and 3rd Wednesday at 6:00 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Uniform and gear are provided, and members become CPR and first aid certified.

who_can_apply: Individuals, families and groups, including school and youth groups. No minimum age is listed. Volunteers 18 and younger need a parent or guardian to sign the waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer preferences form and sign the waiver (a parent signs if you are 18 or younger). Questions: david.schoenknecht@elginil.gov or 847-531-7055.
notes: Wear long pants and closed toe shoes. Because no minimum age is listed, call to ask if there is one for your role.
duration: Ongoing, flexible
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Tools are provided.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 up to under 21. You live in Elgin or a nearby town and go to a local school. You have a C average or better. You have no past arrests or felony convictions. Special cases are reviewed one at a time. Boys and girls are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the application packet. It has the application, terms and a liability waiver. Then pass a background check and an oral interview.
notes: The program is linked to Boy Scouts of America. Boys and girls are welcome. The page says it serves youth in Elgin and nearby towns.
duration: Weekly meetings on Wednesdays at 6:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. Explorers are expected to give 96 volunteer hours a year.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Watch the event calendar and social media for each month's plan, then show up.
notes: Short page. It does not say how to sign up, where events happen or if there is a cost.
duration: One event each month
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 6 and up can ask to volunteer or do community service hours. The Junior Teen Advisory Group is for grades 6 to 8.
how_to_apply: Contact Adelaide Rowe, arowe@egvpl.org, (847) 439-0447 ext. 252 about volunteering. For Jr. TAG, use the Apply Online link on the page or contact Tammy Wulf, twulf@egvpl.org, ext. 248.
notes: The page does not describe a program for older teens. It only lists volunteering and the Reading Program.
duration: Jr. TAG meets monthly, year round, with snacks
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Youth appointed by the Mayor with City Council approval (10 voting seats). The page does not list ages or grades. A city factsheet in search results reportedly said ages 13 to 18, grades 7 to 12, but that is unconfirmed. The City tries to balance seats by school and council district.
how_to_apply: When a seat opens, use the Apply to the Youth Commission link (City Clerk vacancies page). Questions: youthcommission@elkgrove.gov or (916) 627-3254.
notes: Age and grade rules were not on the pages, so confirm with the City before applying. Appointed seats, so competitive. Sign up for vacancy emails on elkgrove.gov to hear when a recruitment opens. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the City page returned HTTP 403, so it could not be read again and the card stays snippet-only.
duration: Meets 2nd Tuesday, Sept to May, 6:00 pm, Elk Grove Council Chambers

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 as of June 1 of the program year (June 1, 2026 on the current page).
how_to_apply: Create a MyImpact account and complete the application, with student and parent signatures on four forms. Get a recommendation from a teacher or school counselor by the deadline and rank up to three hospital locations. Interview, health screening and orientation follow.
notes: The window was only 10 days in 2026, so watch for the 2027 posting in early 2027. Space is limited and waitlists happen. Health screening includes a TB test and proof of chickenpox and measles immunity. No shadowing, internships or clinical hours.
duration: 8 weeks (June 1 to July 24 in 2026), one shift per week, Monday to Thursday, at least 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. No program fee stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students; the page says it serves current sophomores and juniors. Application needs transcript and recommendations.
how_to_apply: Choose a program and course, review costs, then start the online application (transcript, recommendations, $70 fee). After acceptance, complete the pre-arrival checklist and pay the $350 enrollment deposit.
notes: Expensive. The nearest deadline is the Pre-Med Institute on Feb 1, 2027 (deadline_iso shows the main May 3 date). Financial aid deadline was May 1 in 2026. Information sessions are in November and December 2026.
duration: 2 to 6 weeks (2027 noncredit sessions June 13 to 26, June 27 to July 10, July 11 to 24)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: 2-week noncredit course $5,510 residential or $3,925 commuter; 3-week institute $8,264 residential; 4 weeks $11,020. $70 application fee. 2027 prices not posted.

who_can_apply: At least 16 by the start date (June 8 in 2026) and a rising or graduating senior. In-person spots need U.S. citizenship or permanent residency; others may apply to a virtual-only option. You can live anywhere in the U.S., but there is no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply in the Summer Scholars application portal. Two teacher recommendation letters are required, and one must be from a STEM teacher. You cannot submit until both are in. You cannot edit after you submit. An unofficial transcript is fine.
notes: Competitive. Parents or guardians handle off-campus housing and care for students under 18. Dates shown are from the 2026 page. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required for minors under 16; this program starts at 16.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 9 am to 5 pm (June 8 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $2,400 stipend if you finish the program. No program fee.

who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in high school. New applicants are interviewed. A non-parent adult must fill out your reference form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the LIT application on the program page. Your reference fills out the reference form. Staff set up interviews after both are in. You must come to a training of about 1.5 hours before each camp.
notes: Camps are held in Newport Beach and Modjeska Canyon. Students, not parents, must talk to ENC staff. Returning LITs do not need to interview again. Bring school paperwork on your last day.
duration: Winter Nature Camps: December 21 to 23 and December 28 to 31, 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students. Endeavor Health says most roles are for age 16 and up, but age 14 and up at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals. Health screening and orientation are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Student application. The hospital will contact the people it picks about next steps. If you have questions, call Volunteer Services at 630-527-3034.
notes: Hours per week and the length of service are not on the pages. Ask Volunteer Services. Background checks are only for ages 18 and up. Age 14 applies at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals; most roles are for 16 and up.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students. Endeavor Health says most roles are for age 16 and up, but age 14 and up at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals. Health screening and orientation are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. If the site has problems, call 331-221-3282.
notes: The Elmhurst application page had no hours or length details, so ask the volunteer office. Background checks are only for ages 18 and up. Age 14 applies at Edward and Elmhurst hospitals; most roles are for 16 and up.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.
duration: Minimum 4 hours a week and 100 hours for the year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens offer their service without pay.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online High School Volunteer application. Plan on one 30 minute sitting. Then you do an interest interview and a volunteer orientation. You may need a background check. You must also meet the health rules.
notes: The form cannot be saved and finished later.
duration: At least 6 months, 3 to 4 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. A parent or guardian must know about the commitment. You must pass the health screening and complete online orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen application. You then need online orientation and the health requirements from Endeavor Health Employee Health. Getting an assignment is not guaranteed.
notes: Endeavor Health's main page says most roles need age 16 or older and a background check is only for ages 18 and up. Apply early and check back for summer openings.

pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens offer their service without pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20. Where you are placed depends on your situation and your household income. Spots are limited and not promised.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the About page. Use the application and handbook links on the program's site. Depends on New York State funding.
notes: This is Erie County in New York (Buffalo), not Erie, Pennsylvania. Check the site for income limits.
duration: 8 weeks, 20 hours a week (2026: June 28 to Aug 28)
pay_detail: Paid. The rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Commit to 40 hours or more a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application linked on the page. Then go to one training before you start. Contact: bmoore@eriezoo.org, 814-864-4091 ext. 1125.
notes: Volunteers get a discount on food and retail items, per the Why Volunteer section. Training is offered monthly March to June.
duration: At least 40 hours a year, flexible schedule
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid. A discount on zoo food and retail items is listed.

who_can_apply: Local teens. The page does not give an age range or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Get the Teen Advisory Board form from the page as a PDF. You can also pick one up at the Youth Services Desk on the 2nd floor. Email the finished form to teens@escondidolibrary.org (shown on the page).
notes: Phone for the Teen Services Librarian: 760-839-4283 (listed on the page with a call-to-ask-questions note). Page lists no age range or cost.
duration: 2026-2027 school year; meetings on the second Monday of each month, 4:30 to 5:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Volunteers need fingerprinting and a background check. Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board members do not need them. You must have an interview with the Volunteer Coordinator. The library does not accept court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Go to the City of Escondido volunteer website. Fill out the application there. You can call or email the City Community Engagement Liaison with questions. The number is 760-839-4523.
notes: Some roles on the page are for adults only. They are shelver, Friends shop and literacy tutor. The Review Crew and Teen Advisory Board do not need fingerprinting or a background check.
duration: A regular schedule is expected
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens on the Review Crew earn 1 community service hour for every 2 qualifying book reviews.

who_can_apply: Oregon middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. A parent or guardian fills out the interest form. Spots go by lottery and a student can attend only one camp per summer.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian sends in the High School Registration Form for the camps the student wants. A lottery picks who gets in. The parent hears back.
notes: Lane also runs free summer academies for students of color in Lane County. They are called Rites of Passage. There are 4 of them. They are African American, Asian and Pacific Islander, Bridge of the Gods and Puertas Abiertas. See the Lane Community Education pages.
duration: Monday to Thursday, about 4 days (2026 high school dates: Aug 10 to 13 and Aug 24 to 27)
pay_detail: Free. Transportation and food are on your own; parking is free and LTD buses come to campus.

who_can_apply: Applicants ages 16 to 21 who can work in a group of young adults from different backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Lane-Metro Youth Corps page. You get more info and a form to apply.
notes: The program page has no date (it has a 2021 example). Confirm the current ages, pay and dates with Looking Glass before you apply. School credit is available. It runs with the Oregon Youth Conservation Corps. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 9 weeks, 32 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who are low-income and face barriers to employment.
how_to_apply: Complete the interest form on the Job Training Program page. Questions: Hailey Johnston, 458-319-2968, hailey.johnston@lookingglass.us.
notes: Office: Riverfront Career Center, 1666 West 12th Avenue, Eugene. Bus passes or gas cards are offered. Spanish speaking case managers are there. Funded by WIOA. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Youth are usually in the program a year or two; must meet a case manager at least once a month
pay_detail: $17 per hour for the paid work experience, limited to one placement capped at 200 hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. No experience needed. Crews start and end in Eugene, OR or Boise, ID. You provide your own transportation to and from orientation.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the Youth Camping page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: This is hard: you camp and work in all weather. If you leave before graduation you get a share of the stipend and lose the bonuses. The page lists possible high school credit. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks living outdoors (2026: June 13 to July 18; July 25 to Aug 29 or 30)
pay_detail: Up to $450 a week with bonuses, after $70 a week is deducted for food. $300 tuition fee, with need-based assistance.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 in the Eugene area. Teens commute to a central meeting place each day; local housing is not provided.
how_to_apply: Use the Eugene Apply link on the program page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: Possible high school credit (ask your counselor). Same program also runs in Boise and Tacoma. Dates may change. NYC is based in Eugene. Oregon BOLI says minors age 14 to 17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon (employers need a certificate to employ minors). A sibling card for the Tacoma crew uses the youth-ucf page; this card uses the program guide so the urls differ.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 32 work hours a week (2026 Oregon: June 15 to July 17 or July 21 to Aug 21)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 dependability and $20 safety weekly bonuses. Tuition fee $200, with need-based assistance.

who_can_apply: The page says volunteers range from high school students to retirees. A minimum age is not stated; ask the Science Center. A criminal background check is part of onboarding.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now on the volunteer page. Then go to a volunteer orientation.
notes: The page gives no minimum age. It lists high school students among volunteers. Email the Science Center to ask if your age is OK for the role you want. The volunteer page now sends you to eugenesciencecenter.org/volunteer.
duration: Scheduled shifts after an orientation; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include a free membership after 40 hours of service and free planetarium shows.

who_can_apply: Oregon residents in high school who have low income (for example SNAP, WIC, TANF or Pell eligible). Live on campus program: rising juniors and seniors. Day program: any rising 9th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Check that you qualify. Pick a program. Use the Register Here link on the SAIL page when sign up opens.
notes: You can get high school credit. Sign up early because programs fill.
duration: One week (2026: residential July 12 to 17; day program July 20 to 24)
pay_detail: Free summer program. UO scholarship opportunities are listed.

who_can_apply: Evanston or Chicago-area high school students who love art. You can come to meetings on Wednesdays from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Apply. Then do a short interview, take a tour of the art center and meet current members. To ask about the current application, contact Catie Bryant at cbryant@evanstonartcenter.org.
notes: The page has no closing date, and its board photo is captioned 2023-24. Email before you plan around it.
duration: School year. About 8 to 12 meetings per semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members volunteer at least 25 hours a year and earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Mainly under-resourced high school students and community members. The city workforce page says ages 17 and older. The ASPIRE page does not list exact rules, so email to ask.
how_to_apply: Write to aspire@cityofevanston.org and ask how to join. The workforce page also has a Workforce Division Engagement Form.
