notes: The city workforce page says ASPIRE works with NorthShore HealthSystem. It serves ages 17 and older. Email aspire@cityofevanston.org to ask about high school students. Also ask your school counselor.
duration: Summer internship. Length not stated.
pay_detail: Summer internships are described as paid. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students at Evanston Township High School. The page is written for ETHS students.
how_to_apply: Talk to the Early College and Career Experiences office in Room W220. Contact Abronia Young. Call 847-424-7735 or write to younga@eths202.org. You can also call the post-secondary counselor, Michelle Vazquez, at 847-424-7163.
notes: ETHS also has a Work Permits page. It says Illinois law requires minors under 16 to get a work permit before working. Permits are by appointment only, and students aged 14 to 15 in school-approved work-based learning programs do not need one.
duration: A few weeks to a semester or a year
pay_detail: Internships may be paid or unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who live inside Evanston Township High School District 202.
how_to_apply: Register online ahead of time for the winter job fair, then meet employers there. Employers use a separate job request form.
notes: Illinois law says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate), per the Evanston Township High School work permit page. The page says the program began in 1992 and last year over 40 employers offered over 300 jobs. Pay and exact summer dates are not on the page. The registration link is the 2026 form; look for a 2027 form around winter.
duration: Up to 9 weeks
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rate is not stated on the page. Confirm with the city.

who_can_apply: California students without a high school diploma or GED. You need approval from your school counselor or principal.
how_to_apply: Submit the dual enrollment application, get your high school counselor or principal to approve, then enroll. Counseling: mycounselor@evc.edu, 408-270-6475.
notes: CCAP classes are closed cohort classes held at partner high schools, so ask your school if it has an agreement. The page does not state a grade or age rule. Textbook costs for non-CCAP students are not stated.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for dual enrollment students; material fees are waived for CCAP students only

who_can_apply: 11th graders at high schools that EXP supports. The 2025-2026 list includes Carson, Gardena, Lawndale, San Pedro, Phineas Banning and Sato Academy. It also lists some Long Beach schools: Cabrillo, Jordan, Lakewood, Long Beach Poly and Wilson. Some schools in Orange County and Barstow are listed too.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to the Port directly; placement goes through EXP. Ask your school counselor if your school is an EXP school, or email internship@expfuture.org.
notes: Only for students at partner schools. Phone: 424.368.7100. The Port of Los Angeles Summer Internship (10 weeks, paid) is college students only. The page does not mention work permits.
duration: Port of LA placement is 2 to 6 weeks; other placements not stated
pay_detail: EXP lists 171 paid internships for Summer 2026. The hourly pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: The site lists Posts for ages 14 to 20 (and Clubs for ages 10 to 14). Whether you must be a Scout was not stated. Find a unit through the Council Locator.
how_to_apply: Use the Council Locator on exploring.org or joinexploring.org to find a unit near you.
notes: Exploring.org was only readable in part; fees, Scouting membership rules and California posts were not listed. The page names Learning for Life Corporation in its copyright line. apply_url is the joinexploring.org home page, which has an Enter ZIP Code box for Exploring posts and clubs near you. On exploring.org, the Council Locator heading links to the contact page, and the scouting.org Local Council Locator finds a council, not a unit.
duration: Meets regularly
pay_detail: Unpaid. Fees are not stated on the site; ask the post.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. Past interns came from Davis Senior High, Dixon High and Natomas Pacific Pathways Prep.
how_to_apply: No application process is posted. Use the contact page on the Facciotti Lab site to email the lab with a short note about your interests.
notes: Informal opportunity with no posted process, pay, dates or contact on that page. The lab names a partner teacher at Davis Senior High and lists one current intern, so openings may be rare.
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the lab.

who_can_apply: High school students in Fairfax County.
how_to_apply: Email DITHR@fairfaxcounty.gov to ask how to apply.
notes: The county page has only a short note. Ask about pay, age and how to apply by email in March or April.
duration: Mid-June until a week before school starts
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 15 at the start of the course. Must pass the lifeguard course and its swim prerequisites (swim 100 yards, retrieve a 10-pound brick, tread water without hands for one minute) and a criminal background check. No prior certification needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Park Authority Aquatic Certification page, then interview. Questions: FCPAJOBS@Fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Employment is contingent on passing the course. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Part-time; hours vary by Rec Center
pay_detail: Weekday opening and midday shifts start at $15.00 per hour; weekday evenings and weekends range from $12.41 to $15.00 per hour. Training is free (listed as a $250 value).

who_can_apply: The library's volunteer guide is for adults, youth ages 12 and over, corporate groups, and people who need to fulfill a service requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator for your branch (the guide lists names and phone numbers) or use the Volunteer Login link in the library's volunteering guide.
notes: The guide does not spell out the sign-up steps for teens, so call your branch coordinator first. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: You must be a junior now in a Fairfax County public school. You should be doing well in class. You should care about local government. You cannot also do the Governor School Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send one letter of support. It can come from a teacher, scout leader, boss or someone like that.
notes: Meetings are Wednesdays 4 to 6 pm starting in February. You get yourself to meetings and the internship. Questions: DMBYLP@fairfaxcounty.gov or 703-324-4062. Page does not give the internship year; it is July 2027 for this class.
duration: Monthly meetings from Feb 2027 plus a 3-week internship in July (40 hours per week)
pay_detail: $1,000 for completing the 3-week internship

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. You must be legally allowed to work in the U.S. You must be getting services from a referring group or the WIOA Youth Program. You must want to find work. You must be able to work at least 20 hours a week and go to the workshops.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply alone. A sponsoring group or the WIOA Youth Program picks you. Email DFSEYE@fairfaxcounty.gov or see vcwnorthern.com/eye-programs/ to find a referring organization.
notes: Referral only. The county page also lists a WIOA Youth program for ages 17 to 24 who are out of school or close to graduating. In summer 2026, 133 youth worked with 100 local employers. Virginia work permit rules were not checked.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The pay rate is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students in the Commonwealth of Virginia.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the ACCESS Academy page when it opens again. If you have questions, write to Dr. Roberto Pamas. He is the ACCESS Academy Director. His email is rpamas@gmu.edu.
notes: Held at Fuse at Mason Square, 3401 Fairfax Dr, Arlington, VA. It filled up in 2026, so apply early next year.
duration: One week, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. daily (2026 sessions: July 13-17, July 20-24, July 27-31)
pay_detail: No cost to students. Lunch provided daily. You provide your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students. No coding, health care or technology experience is required.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Fill out the Future Programs Interest Form on the camp page to get updates. Contact: Maria Uriyo, muriyo@gmu.edu.
notes: This is a day camp at George Mason University's Fairfax campus, 4400 University Drive, Fairfax, VA 22030. Not a job.
duration: 5 days, 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. each day
pay_detail: The camps list at Mason says it is a free, five day program. The camp page itself does not list a cost.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who like leadership, making peace, community work or social sciences. Students come from all over the country.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. If you are admitted, you get steps to sign up and pay a deposit. For a scholarship, check the box. Then send a personal statement and your parents' most recent 1040 tax form.
notes: Contact: Averi Jordan, ajorda22@gmu.edu. In 2026, 63 students went to the summit.
duration: Four days, overnight (page lists July 25 to 29 for Summer 2027)
pay_detail: $1,390 without college credit, or $1,500 with 1 college credit. Scholarship review is possible.

who_can_apply: High school students (GMU's camps list says ages 13 to 17). Virginia applicants must go to certain schools. Students whose family income is under 400% of the federal poverty level get priority. The researcher track is for students with no research experience. It is also for students with few health chances at school.
how_to_apply: Send the online application form. Allow about 14 days for email replies. Some applicants are interviewed. Send questions to the program director, Jonathan Sanchez. His email is jsanche@gmu.edu.
notes: The page also mentions that acceptances begin July 1, 2026. That does not fit with the December deadline. Check the timeline with the director.
duration: Spring 2027 cohort starting Jan 20, 2027 (details to be decided); year-long track for fellows and interns
pay_detail: Free. 100% virtual.

who_can_apply: Fall 2026 classes by age: 9 to 17 for 2D art, 11 to 17 for Unity, 13 to 17 for advanced Python (needs prior programming). Younger-only classes run in Manassas. Typing and basic computer skills expected.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the MGTA page when registration opens for a class.
notes: Not a job or internship. Listed because it is a real university program for teens in tech and game design. Check the page for the next session.
duration: Fall 2026: six Saturdays 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at Fairfax; summer classes are five days, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: $595 per fall class. Scholarships page exists but gives no details.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents in a public or private high school, or home-schooled in Virginia. You need a GPA of 2.5 or higher. You cannot have attended the 2026 STEM Academy (VSA) or Leadership Academy (VLA). You cannot attend another VALHEN summer program in 2027. A recommendation is required. It should come from a teacher, counselor, coach or community leader. That person must not be related to you.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in February 2027. Essays must be your own work (no AI generated or third-party essays). Contact STEM Academy Director Kerin Hilker-Balkissoon at khilkerb@gmu.edu.
notes: The camps list at Mason describes this program for ages 14 to 16 (rising sophomores and juniors). The page itself says rising juniors, so use the page. Competitive: students are selected. It is statewide for Virginia residents but held in Fairfax. It may also be on a Virginia-wide list.
duration: 3 days, 2 nights
pay_detail: Free for selected students. Overnight students get two nights of dorm housing, meals and a daily snack. A limited number of day-only slots exist. You arrange your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Highly engaged high school students. GMU's camps list says rising 11th and 12th graders. Students can register or be nominated.
how_to_apply: Use the Register page (wjmc.gmu.edu/register). Scholarship details are at wjmc.gmu.edu/scholarships/. A Nominate link is also on the site.
notes: Check the cost and deadlines with the program before you apply.
duration: One week (July 11 to 16 or July 18 to 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Tuition not stated on the program pages. A scholarship is offered.

who_can_apply: Highly engaged high school students. GMU's camps list says rising 11th and 12th graders. Students can register or be nominated.
how_to_apply: Use the Register page on the WYSE site, or have someone submit a nomination (wsp.gmu.edu/nominate). Call 703-993-5010 for cost and deadlines.
notes: The site shows a Register button for the June 27 to July 2, 2027 session, but the page does not say whether registration is open. Confirm the status and cost with the program before applying.
duration: One week (June 27 to July 2, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. Ask the program: 703-993-5010.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page to see when it opens again. You can also call Joan Flintoft at 703-799-8605.
notes: About 250 active volunteers. Some roles, like driving, need an adult with a license, so not every role is open to teens. There is no archaeology fieldwork for volunteers right now, only lab work.
duration: At least 25 hours a year to stay active.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get discounts at the estate's shops and restaurants and special tours.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. You must finish a county volunteer orientation and a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Make a profile at volunteer.fairfaxcounty.gov and search the word NCS. Apply to openings. Go to an NCS Volunteer Orientation and pass the background check. Email ncs-volunteers@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: The page has no teen-only section or list of teen roles, so ask the volunteer office what is open for 13 to 17 year olds. The phone number printed on the page has a non-Virginia area code; use the email.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are 16 by the first day of class and meet dual enrollment readiness (for example a 3.0 GPA, or set test scores). Needs a current high school transcript and parent e-consent. Residency rule not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply to NOVA for the summer term. Then fill out the Dual Enrollment Portal form in myNOVA. You pick courses, upload papers and get a parent to say yes online. Contact DualEnrollment@nvcc.edu or 703-503-6291.
notes: Selection is by lottery. The page shows 2026 dates; check in March for 2027.
duration: Six weeks, Mon and Wed 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. (June 22 to July 29 in 2026)
pay_detail: No tuition or pay listed. Textbooks are free, lunch is provided, parking pass for drivers. You arrange your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Any teen aged 14 to 17. Rec-PAC school sites have no interview; camp sites at Rec Centers and parks need an interview.
how_to_apply: Rec-PAC school sites: fill out the application and return it to the Rec-PAC office. Rec Center and park camp sites: contact the site for an interview. All CITs attend a 3-hour training and pass a knowledge test.
notes: This FAQ page looks old. It links to 2019 Rec-PAC sites. Check the fee, dates and deadline with the Park Authority at 703-324-8700 before you apply.
duration: At least one week encouraged, up to the full summer; school sites run 8:15 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts as volunteer hours. The FAQ lists a $160 fee for the whole summer at school-based Rec-PAC sites.

who_can_apply: High school age girls in Northern Virginia (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: For girls only. Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to go to all classes. Not a job.
duration: Summer weekdays
pay_detail: Free of charge. Transportation help is offered case by case.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 20 who like the idea of a career in law enforcement. There are four units. They are the Criminal Justice Academy (Chantilly), West Potomac High School, Annandale High School and South Lakes High School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Public Safety Cadets interest form on the page. The page also links an application. It links a waiver. It links a recommendation form. Email fcpdpsc@fairfaxcounty.gov with questions.
notes: An older Fairfax County police page called these units Explorer posts. They had the same unit numbers. That page no longer loads. Ask the cadet email about the current rules, such as citizenship, grades and costs. The page links an application, a waiver and a recommendation form.
duration: Ongoing unit membership
pay_detail: Unpaid. Costs for uniforms or gear are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Fairfax County high school age students (public, private or home-schooled) entering grade 10, 11 or 12 in the 2026-2027 school year. Class size is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Police Academy application on the page when the new session is posted. If you need a ride, email Captain Deanna Weand when you apply. Questions: 703-246-3332 or CPA@fairfaxcounty.gov.
notes: Classes are at Fairfax County Public Safety Headquarters, 12099 Government Center Parkway, Fairfax. Participants are expected to attend all classes. Not a job.
duration: Summer weekdays, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. Transportation help is offered case by case.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. You also need a current American Red Cross lifeguard certificate. The page links to upcoming classes.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the lifeguard page, which goes to the district's job portal. Questions: isinkler@fargoparks.com (Aquatics team).
notes: Take the Red Cross certification class first. The page links to the class list. Fargo Park District also has other seasonal jobs and an internship program on its Employment page. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.
duration: Summer. Exact start and end dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: $17 to $19 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18. A parent or guardian must sign the Teen Volunteer Permission Form.
how_to_apply: Register for each session at programregistration.library.fargond.gov or call 701.241.1495. Bring the signed permission form to your first session. The form is on the City of Fargo website.
notes: The page lists the month and day for each session but not the year. A good fit for a first volunteer experience; no commitment beyond a single session.
duration: One session of 2 hours (1 to 3 pm) on the first Saturday of each month, October to May.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12, entered as a team. A faculty advisor registers the team. Each school may enter one team and one submission. Team size and other rules are in the rule book, which the page links to.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to be your team advisor. The advisor signs up the team online. The advisor also emails a form from your principal to nyeconed@ny.frb.org. The page covers team entries only.
notes: The Chicago Fed page says teams register through the same national process and lists the same Feb 15, 2027 deadline. Good for a club, econ class or debate team.
duration: Registration Sept 10, 2026 to Feb 15, 2027. Paper due Mar 15, 2027.
pay_detail: No pay. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: Illinois high school students who will be seniors in 2027-28 or who graduate in 2027. Must be a U.S. citizen and have proof of medical insurance. No STEM prerequisites. Age and GPA are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal, a supplemental questionnaire, a PDF list of your STEM courses uploaded in the Resume section, and one letter from a STEM teacher or STEM club advisor. You cannot upload missing items after you submit.
notes: The apply link only works during the application window. Recommenders get an email upload link. It is sent only on weekdays during business hours, so line up your letter writer early. A walkthrough video is on the page.
duration: 4 weeks, July 12 to Aug 6, 2027
pay_detail: $500 per week stipend. Housing is not provided; transportation assistance is available.

who_can_apply: High school students in public, private or parochial schools, and home-schooled students with high school standing. Students attend in person. A physics course and two years of algebra help but are not required. A unique email address is required.
how_to_apply: Watch for the news in November. Then fill out the online application. If you have questions, write to saturdaymorningphysics@fnal.gov.
notes: Lectures are at Wilson Hall in Batavia. Some lectures may be off-site. Spring 2027 dates are not posted yet.
duration: 11 Saturdays, 9 a.m. to noon. Fall 2026 ran Sept 12 to Nov 21.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students across Illinois. No science prerequisite. You must attend at least 8 sessions, with no excused absences.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the application. It opens in late fall 2026. If you have questions, write to Saturdaymorningquantum@fnal.gov.
notes: Classes are held at the Olive Harvey Learning Center, 3055 East 92nd Street, Chicago. The page gives no exact open or close date for applications.
duration: Saturdays 1 to 4 p.m., February 6 to April 24, 2027 (no sessions March 20 and 27)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Enrolled in an Illinois high school JROTC program, and an Illinois high school junior, senior or recent graduate when you apply. Must be eligible to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Online application in Fermilab's Workday portal with an unofficial transcript, a resume and three short essay answers (under 200 words each). Then give contact info for one recommendation writer; the letter is due by the close date. Questions: Internships@fnal.gov.
notes: Only for cadets in an Illinois JROTC program. You cannot upload missing items after you submit, so gather everything first. Reference emails go out only on weekdays during business hours.
duration: 6 weeks, June 28 to Aug 6, 2027
pay_detail: $18 per hour. No onsite housing or transportation reimbursement.

who_can_apply: Teens at least 13 by September 1 and no older than 17 by June 1. Volunteers who turn 18 during the year may finish it.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application, an essay written by the teen, and two reference forms. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Contact: FYI@FernbankMuseum.org or 404-929-6360.
notes: Described as very competitive; teens who are not accepted are encouraged to reapply the next year.
duration: One year, June 1 to May 31, at least 45 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time $50 fee after acceptance, which can be waived for those who qualify.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 16 (age counted on September 1 of the 4-H year). You do not have to be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It names the camp and the weeks you want. Upload a resume. List two adults as references. They do not have to be from 4-H.
notes: Apply to Camp Cloverleaf, Camp Timpoochee or both. Weekly themes and prices are on each camp's page. Teens pay the camp fee, so this is not a paying job.
duration: At least 1 camp week, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Junior counselors pay the full early bird camp fee for each week they attend. They can apply for state camp scholarships.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18. Your age is counted on September 1. You can also stay until you finish high school.
how_to_apply: Call your county Extension office. Then join online in 4-H Online. Paper forms are also available.
notes: State events include iLEAD and 4-H University Legislature Day at the Capitol. Florida has three 4-H camps: Cherry Lake, Cloverleaf and Timpoochee. You do not have to be a member to go to their summer camps.
duration: 4-H year runs Sept 1 to Aug 31
pay_detail: $20 per year for community club members ages 8 to 18. Some counties charge a different amount.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. At least four hours a week. Some sites are full; check the list on the page.
how_to_apply: Step 1: online volunteer orientation. Step 2: online application. Step 3: contact them to set up an interview. Call 407-543-4047.
notes: Pick a location that is accepting applications. The internships on the same page are for college students getting credit, not high school.
duration: At least 4 hours a week, flexible
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. Competitive. Two full 8 hour days a week for the summer term (June 1 to July 31 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Send in a form with a video. Also send in a recommendation form. A Level 2 background check is required.
notes: Parents are asked to let the teen be the main contact. Fingerprint fees are reimbursed for those who finish. Max 3 excused absences.
duration: Summer term, 2 days a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Broward County students ages 16 to 18. You must be able to work in the US and have a valid ID. Your family must meet the income rule (economically disadvantaged). Picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window is open. Income and a random lottery decide who gets in. Chosen youth get a packet by mail and go to training.
notes: Funded mainly by the Children's Services Council of Broward County. Remote work is not offered. Next year dates are not posted, so check the page in winter.
duration: About 8 weeks, June to early August
pay_detail: $14 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 (13 by the first June class). Must apply, interview, attend multi day training and pass a final exam.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form when it opens in February. Attach 3 papers. Then interview.
notes: Teens are expected to handle their own email and schedule. Volunteer Office: 407-323-4450 ext. 127.
duration: Training in June; volunteering on weekends and school breaks
pay_detail: Unpaid; $30 fee for training materials and uniform

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and up. Must attend at least 5 of 6 sessions and volunteer 6 hours a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online VolunTeen form with a letter of commitment. Contact Simone Crawley, 727-623-4731.
notes: Hours may count toward service requirements; ask the museum.
duration: 6 weeks (June 7 to July 23 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free; unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students on a team from a school, homeschool group, 4-H group or nature center group. A full team has 5 competing members. The team registration fee covers up to 2 advisors. Each county sends one team.
how_to_apply: Join your regional contest first. Regional leaders sign up the winning teams. Then advisors finish signing up and pay.
notes: The key dates page is titled 2026 but lists an April 2027 contest, so confirm the year with organizers. Teams of 4 or fewer can take part but not compete for places.
duration: 1 day state contest
pay_detail: $300 per team, flat rate.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 16. You like botany, plant biology, ecology or gardening. It is run through the Miami-Dade County Public Schools Summer Youth Internship Program. Only Miami-Dade public school students get school credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add 1 letter of recommendation from a science teacher.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Look for a similar spring deadline. Recent undergraduate and graduate internships on the same page are not for high schoolers.
duration: 5 weeks (July 1 to Aug 2 in 2026)
pay_detail: Stipend at the end of the program (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in an agriculture course at their school. Joining a chapter in a nearby school district is a state and local decision.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher to enroll you in an agriculture course. Use the Chapter Locator on the site.
notes: For overnight events, an advisor or an adult your school approves must come with students. You also need a permission form and a medical form. Event fees pay for lodging and meals at most events.
duration: School year
pay_detail: National dues $7 per year plus state dues $10 per year. Local chapters may add dues.

who_can_apply: Miami-Dade County Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12 who are at least 16 years old. Upward Bound Math and Science (UBMS) students apply first; other students can be accepted if they agree to join UBMS. Applicants must be willing to get a scuba certification.
how_to_apply: Use the Join the Program link on the Your Shores page to start the application. The page lists no deadline.
notes: The page shows Saturdays from September 23 to May 25 with no year, so confirm dates with the museum. A medical checklist form and swim requirements apply. The page says participants earn a stipend but gives no amount.
duration: Saturdays, September to May
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Camp Registration Portal linked from the camp page, or call the camp at 561-624-6929.
notes: Paid camp staff jobs at this center need you to be at least 19, so this camp is the teen route. Address: 12100 Seminole Pratt Whitney Road, West Palm Beach, FL.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: The camp lists programs from $400 to $515 per week. The Leadership Camp price is not listed separately on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and 17 who apply and are accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the leadership camp application on the camp page. Then follow the steps to contact the camp. You only sign up online if you are accepted.
notes: The camp address is 7325 NE 170th Ave, Silver Springs, FL. Phone 352-625-2804. The page does not name the year of the listed weeks, so confirm 2027 dates.
duration: 1 week or more
pay_detail: $200 per week. 40 Service Learning Credits are awarded for each week.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 for the Hooked on Conservation and Paddle Adventure weeks. Age is counted on the first day of the camp week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Camp Registration Portal. No payment is due until you get a spot. Payment is due 14 days after you are told you have a spot.
notes: Capacity is 20 per teen week, so spots go fast. Address: 6650 Dickman Rd, Apollo Beach, FL. Phone 813-922-7961.
duration: 1 week day camp
pay_detail: Camp price is not stated on the program page. Limited scholarships: email Suncoast@MyFWC.com. A $25 non-refundable deposit applies.

who_can_apply: High school seniors at schools that partner with Genesys Works. The page says the Jacksonville program works with Duval County Public Schools to recruit students. The first Jacksonville class launched in 2025. The page does not state a pay rate.
how_to_apply: Start on the Genesys Works application page. Choose Jacksonville. Interview. Then confirm your spot for summer training.
notes: The page says the Jacksonville program works with Duval County Public Schools to recruit students. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The first Jacksonville class launched in 2025.
duration: 8 weeks training (summer) then a year long internship
pay_detail: Paid internship (rate not stated on the program pages)

who_can_apply: At least 16, or part of a pre approved group such as scouts or 4-H. You provide your own transportation.
how_to_apply: Pick the volunteer form that fits the park or role and send it in. To coach, contact the rec center directly.
notes: Scouts can use the Scout Project Application. Camp host applications for fall and winter 2026-27 will only be considered for spring and summer 2027.
duration: Flexible
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Duval County residents ages 16 to 21 who are in school (22 for youth with special needs). Or ages 16 to 24 who are out of school and not working or at risk of being cut off from school and work.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the MYAWP page to open the candidate portal. The page says the student application closed August 19 at 11:59 pm, and it does not list session dates.
notes: The page says demand is expected to be higher than the slots. Business interest form deadline was September 11.
duration: Sessions through the year (fall 2026 session listed)
pay_detail: Paid internship (rate and hours not stated on the page)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18. Everyone must pass the City background screening, which may include fingerprints. The page says there are more applicants than openings.
how_to_apply: Look at the openings on the volunteer page. Apply online. Staff will email you the next steps.
notes: Not everyone who applies is picked. Group volunteering: JPLVolunteers@coj.net. Teen specific openings are listed on a teen page that was not read.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens currently in high school, ages 14 to 18 when they enter the program. Apply, interview and be picked. Not all applicants are accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form in the November window. Interview. Go to the required training.
notes: The page gives the Nov 1 to Nov 25 window as the pattern each year. It does not say the exact 2026 dates are for that year.
duration: Year round: 30 hours fall, 30 spring, 80 summer
pay_detail: Unpaid; $100 annual fee for badge, shirt and materials (financial help available, nobody turned away)

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. Ages 16 and 17 need a parent or guardian signature. Photo ID is required.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch you want. Meet the Volunteer Coordinator or Branch Manager. Then send in the Volunteer Application/Agreement. A free fingerprint background check follows.
notes: The page says students can earn community service hours for graduation. The branch manager must approve your spot.
duration: Flexible, set with your branch
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders ages 15 to 18 enrolled in a Miami-Dade County Public School. Apply through your school champion. Students must complete the online pre-internship course.
how_to_apply: Finish the first steps, including the online class before the internship. Talk to your teacher champion at school. Hotline: 305-693-3005.
notes: Students may earn school credit if they pass the review and finish their work. The page says to check back for 2027 sign up details.
duration: 5 weeks (July 1 to Aug 2 in 2026), at least 30 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid by stipend (amount not stated on the program pages); students open an EdFed Credit Union account for direct deposit

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at any Jacksonville high school. You do not need to be an artist.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application when it opens. Required: two Family Day volunteer shifts. Meetings are the first and third Wednesday of each month from 5 to 6:30 pm.
notes: Past members earned upwards of 40 service hours. Members must volunteer at two Family Day events, with dates to be announced.
duration: September to April, first and third Wednesday, 5 to 6:30 pm
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer hours (past members earned 40 or more)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. You must be able to work on your own. Supervisors cannot always be there.
how_to_apply: It is not open now. To ask when 2027 forms open, call Volunteer Coordinator Amy Hester at 352-273-2055. Or send an email to volunteers@floridamuseum.ufl.edu.
notes: Return for Summer 2027 is hoped for, not promised. Confirm before planning around it.
duration: Summer; selected teens may also serve in the school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth must be at least 14 and have completed 8th grade. Adult weekday session volunteers must be 18; teens use individual postings and one time events.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the volunteer page. No application is needed for the one time events.
notes: The museum only signs volunteer hours for students who are 14 (going into high school) or older.
duration: One time events (a few hours) and posted openings
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: North Miami residents ages 15 to 18 at the time of appointment, in grades 10 to 12, with at least a 2.0 GPA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add a resume, school transcript, a minor participation form, a photo and video form, and 2 short answers (200 words each).
notes: The next cycle is not posted. Contact Library Director Paul Bazile, 305-891-5535.
duration: School year term (length not stated)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students in Orange County. Age and grade rules vary by event. Check with your branch.
how_to_apply: Register for an event at a participating branch. Questions: AskOCLS@ocls.org or 407-835-7323.
notes: Advisory boards give 1 hour of service for each monthly online meeting. For the literary magazine you must send in work to get hours.
duration: Events and monthly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours (up to 2 hours per event)

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. You need a reliable ride and must pass background and drug screens. You must be free to work the whole summer. You must pass a swim test (200 yards, tread water 2 minutes, get a 10 pound brick).
how_to_apply: Sign up for a certification class, take the swim test on day one, finish all days, then fill out the summer job application at the end of class. HR then sets up a background check and drug screening (can take up to 3 weeks).
notes: Bring a government ID and Social Security card to class, per the page. Call 407-246-4090. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Certification classes over several days (January to May); then the summer season
pay_detail: $15 to $17 an hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17, per the center. The page says applications for the 2026-2027 school year have closed.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it opens (it opens about twice a year, for Summer and School Year). Questions: volunteer@osc.org.
notes: The center says volunteering here meets most middle school and high school community service rules. Questions: volunteer@osc.org.
duration: Teams sign up for two week blocks, Monday to Friday
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Orlando residents ages 15 to 19. Go to an open house. Bring a birth certificate, a signed Social Security card, and a school or Florida ID.
how_to_apply: Go to an open house at a neighborhood center with your documents. Contact youthworkforce@orlando.gov.
notes: The 2025 city release called it paid, five week internships. The city also runs a year round version for residents 15 to 19 that was not read in detail.
duration: About 5 weeks in 2025; length for 2026 not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience (rate not stated on the program page)

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 17 who can commit to at least 100 hours. You cannot be placed where your parent or guardian works.
how_to_apply: Email a packet to vhaorlvoluntary@va.gov. Use the subject "Summer Junior Volunteer - Location Name". It is first come, first served. A parent must go to an online orientation. The student goes to an in person orientation.
notes: Applications were taken by email on 1 day only, April 15, 2026, first come first served. Sites in 2026: Lake Nona, Lake Baldwin, Viera and Daytona. Volunteers cannot be placed where a parent or guardian works.
duration: About 10 weeks (June 3 to Aug 6 in 2026); 100 hour minimum
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 when you apply. Ages 16 and 17 need a parent or guardian to co-sign the application and documents.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online TGH Volunteer form. Chosen applicants do a health check and a background check.
notes: Not all applicants are accepted. Volunteers get a free fitness center membership with 10 hours a month, per the page. Questions: volunteer@tgh.org.
duration: One 3 to 4 hour service shift a week. Start dates are May 1 and September 1.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 who live in Hillsborough County.
how_to_apply: Not open now. Watch the page for the next chance to apply. The page lists phone 813-273-3652 and text 813-352-1603.
notes: Finishers earn up to 100 service hours, per the library. Students must complete all assignments and sessions to be awarded 100 hours.
duration: Five months (July 8 to Nov 7 in 2026), hybrid
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns up to 100 Bright Futures and school service hours

who_can_apply: Students in grade 9, 10 or 11 who live inside Tampa city limits or go to a high school there (home and virtual school students who live in the city can apply too). One year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online MYC form. Then take part in a review and an interview. Contact Molly Biebel, Youth Development Coordinator, (813) 459-4002.
notes: The application form page would not open for the researcher, so the deadline is not confirmed. Age is not stated; grade 9 to 11 is the rule.
duration: One year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 20, per the department FAQ.
how_to_apply: Visit the post for your first visit; after the fourth visit ask for an application; then an oral interview with Post 275 staff. Call 813-367-8671.
notes: The FAQ says the program is run by the rules of the Boy Scouts of America. It points to the Learning for Life Exploring Program. The page says the department is taking applications now.
duration: Year round
pay_detail: Unpaid; cost not stated

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 19. A free Rec Card and program registration are required.
how_to_apply: Get a free Rec Card. Sign up. Visit a TLC site (for example Copeland Park Center, 813-975-2743).
notes: Programs build time management, team building and financial planning, per the page. Not a job.
duration: Weekly
pay_detail: Free to join

who_can_apply: Open to middle school students at Sulphur Springs K-8. Also open to high school students at Middleton High School. Also open to youth 12 to 18 at the Bob Gilbertson Central City YMCA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen sign up form and the program agreement. Email them to Meagan Smithyman at msmithyma@tampaymca.org.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page. Ask the Y.
duration: School year; summer at some sites
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Middle and high school teens. Tampa YMCA membership is required. Parents and teens must attend at least one info meeting.
how_to_apply: Join the Tampa YMCA. Contact the Club Advisor at your Y. Go to a meeting. Sign up at that Y.
notes: The page says it is at every Tampa Y family center.
duration: School year, ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid; YMCA membership required

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 when they apply (rising 9th to 12th) who are at least 13 when the institute starts. Up to 35 students.
how_to_apply: Apply through the SI@UCF application page. The page showed applications open for Summer 2026; check it for the next window.
notes: Dates for 2027 are not posted.
duration: 1 week (June 8 to 12 in 2026), at UCF Rosen Campus, 9907 Universal Blvd, Orlando

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 11 when they apply. You must be at least 13 by the start of the institute.
how_to_apply: Apply through the SI@UCF application page. Applications for Summer 2027 open in the spring.
notes: Part of UCF Summer Institute. Dates for 2027 are not posted.
duration: 3 weeks (June 1 to 19 in 2026)

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders anywhere in the US (a few spots for out of state students). For motivated students who like farming and related sciences.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CPET online application portal. Students must write a 1500 to 2000 word World Food Prize essay, due April 15, 2026 for invited students, per the page. Application fee is non-refundable.
notes: Students can compete for the World Food Prize and become Borlaug Scholars, per the page.
duration: 1 week residential (June 28 to July 3 or July 5 to 10 in 2026)
pay_detail: $800 program cost plus $25 application fee; need based scholarships

who_can_apply: Florida residents only. Rising 10th and 11th graders who are in 9th or 10th grade when they apply. Students with little or no hands-on programming experience are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CPET online portal. Send a transcript and the recommendations or prompts the page lists.
notes: Little or no coding experience is fine, per the page. Seats are limited.
duration: 2 weeks residential (July 19 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: $1,800 program cost plus $25 application fee; need based scholarships for Florida students

who_can_apply: You must live in Florida and go to a Florida high school. You must be a rising 10th to 12th grader. First picks go to first generation, low income, or little vet exposure with some animal experience.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CPET online portal. Send a transcript and the recommendations or prompts the page lists.
notes: Florida students only. Session 2 dates in the page header say 2025 which looks like a typo for 2026.
duration: 1 week residential (June 7 to 12 or June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: $1,500 program cost plus $25 application fee; need based scholarships

who_can_apply: Students who can commit at least 80 hours, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. Needs a 3.0 GPA or higher and two reference letters (not family). The page does not state an age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Interview with Volunteer Services. Bring 2 reference letters. Pass the health screen. Call 904-244-4232.
notes: UF Health Jacksonville can say no to any applicant. Age limits for students were not stated. Confirm before you apply.
duration: At least 80 hours; about one 4 hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students. Offered only at UF Health Gainesville. Both the teen and one parent must attend an info session. Ages are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Apply online in January. Then go to an info session, fill out an interest form and join a group interview.
notes: The page mixes 2026 and 2027, so check it in December. Jacksonville students: UF Health Jacksonville has its own program.
duration: About 6 weeks in summer (June 21 to Aug 5)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students who will be rising 10th graders (apply in spring of 9th grade). Open worldwide; a few spots are set aside for out of state students.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CPET online portal. Send a transcript and the recommendations or prompts the page lists.
notes: The application fee is not refundable. Housing is in the cost.
duration: 1 week residential (June 7 to 12 or July 12 to 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $1,200 program cost plus $25 application fee; need based scholarships

who_can_apply: Students in 11th grade who will be 16 or older at program start (no exceptions). Applied for in spring of 11th grade. A few spots go to students from outside Florida.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CPET online portal, with transcripts. No minimum GPA, no test scores needed.
notes: Daily meals are not included in the fee. Need-based aid is for Florida high school students. Standardized tests are not required to apply.
duration: 7 weeks (June 7 to July 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: $5,500 program cost plus $50 application fee; limited need based scholarships for Florida high school students

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders. The page says the program is open to all students. It is non-residential, so students arrange their own housing and food.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CPET online portal. Send a transcript and the recommendations or prompts the page lists.
notes: Works with UF medical students and faculty. Meals and housing are not included.
duration: 5 days (three sessions in June and July 2026)
pay_detail: $1,200 program cost plus $25 application fee; need based scholarships

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 during the application window. You must pass an interview, background check, drug screen, health checks and training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Volunteer Services form for high school students. If you have questions, call 305-243-4032 or send an email to IHSVolunteer@miami.edu.
notes: Incomplete applications were not reviewed. The same site lists a High School Student Research Trainee role that was not read.
duration: At least 5 weeks, 4 to 5 hours a day (June 16 to Aug 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders. Capacity is 20 campers.
how_to_apply: Sign up through USF Youth Experiences when 2027 sign up opens.
notes: The page lists a capacity of 20 campers. The page does not post the fee yet.
duration: One week, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM
pay_detail: The page does not post the cost yet

who_can_apply: High school students in 10th or 11th grade during the 2026-2027 school year. Apply and attend one info session (virtual or in person).
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Go to 1 info session (sign up on Eventbrite). You can join for 1 semester or both.
notes: No fee is listed. Stipend amount is not stated.
duration: Two semesters: Oct to Nov and Jan to Feb, Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 pm; ends with an event Feb 28, 2027
pay_detail: Monthly stipend (amount not stated) plus service hours

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 entering or currently in high school. The page describes a yearly commitment.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the form opens again on March 2, 2027. A reference form is required. Questions: volunteer@zoomiami.org.
notes: The page says a reference form is required. Questions: volunteer@zoomiami.org.
duration: Yearly: 15 days in summer plus 2 days a month in the school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. Space is limited. Register in WebTrac.
how_to_apply: Register through Folsom WebTrac.
notes: Source is the city's May 22, 2026 news post, which does not list a fee or the 2027 dates. Held at Oak Chan Elementary School. Check the Folsom Parks and Recreation site and WebTrac in spring 2027.
duration: 8 weekly sessions (2026: June 8 to July 31, Mon to Fri 8:30 to 4:00)
pay_detail: Fee not stated in the news post.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up for regular sessions. Volunteers under 16 must be with an adult at all times. Kids ages 5 to 11 have special Kids Day sessions.
how_to_apply: Sign up online for a session before you go. You can pick the Raleigh or Durham site, or another Food Bank site. Signing up counts as signing the volunteer form. Groups need chaperones. The Food Bank suggests 1 chaperone for every 5 youth.
notes: Raleigh coordinator: volunteerservices@foodbankcenc.org, 984.339.1010. Durham coordinator: cstone@foodbankcenc.org, 919.956.2513 (option 4). Follow the dress and safety rules given at orientation.
duration: Single sessions listed on the online calendar
pay_detail: Unpaid. You can print your service hours from the volunteer portal.

who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Apply to Foothill, then submit the Special Admit form signed by a parent or guardian and your high school principal or administrator. Meet course prerequisites; talk to your high school counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to Foothill, submit the Special Admit form (parent and principal signatures, plus an unofficial transcript if asked), register, and pay any fees. Admissions: (650) 949-7325.
notes: Foothill can give a free Clipper SmartPass for VTA buses and light rail. Undocumented students are welcome. Grades go on your permanent college record, and your parents cannot see college records. Partner-district options also exist: Middle College, College Now! (MVLA), Firebird Academy (Fremont Union).
duration: One quarter at a time
pay_detail: No cost up to 11 units in a regular quarter (6 in summer), counting Foothill and De Anza together. Textbooks and other fees are not covered.

who_can_apply: Open access and free. The page does not state an age minimum, so check the terms and the Minors privacy notice.
how_to_apply: Create a free account and pick a simulation at theforage.com.
notes: Good for a resume line, but it is not a job or an internship. The page has no age minimum and links a privacy notice for minors, so read the terms and ask a parent before signing up.
duration: Self-paced, usually a few hours
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PDF application form and email it to the Volunteer Office. Then do an interview, an orientation, two TB tests and a flu shot.
notes: Volunteer Office: (714) 378-7000, Mon to Fri 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Patient Care Pavilion, 18111 Brookhurst St. The application PDF was not checked.
duration: 150 hours per year
pay_detail: Unpaid. If accepted you pay a $25 registration fee.

who_can_apply: The employment page says positions run from teens seeking a first job to skilled professionals. Minimum age is not stated on the page, so check each posting.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the job you want from the Join Our Team page. Applications are kept on file for one year. A background check is required if you get an offer.
notes: The district says it has about 1,200 part-time and seasonal workers at times of the year. Job fair dates are from old press releases, so confirm the next one. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Seasonal and part-time
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay is listed on each posting. It is not on the main employment page.

who_can_apply: Students and school groups. The page does not list a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Use the link on the volunteer page to reserve a spot for an event. To adopt a park or trail, email Ivan Chambers at ichambers@fvpd.net.
notes: The district provides trash bags, gloves and a few litter grabbers for Adopt-A-Park groups. Ask the district if a parent form is needed for under 18.
duration: One-day projects or monthly clean-ups (Adopt-A-Park runs April to September, or May to October)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Eligible local teens. The page does not state the age range or other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Teen Corps page when it reopens. Contact the Teen Corps Coordinator through the page.
notes: Run on a community garden and the Conservatory's Farmers Market. Ages, stipend amount and dates are not on the page, so ask the coordinator. Ohio needs a working permit for paid work at ages 14 to 17, but 16 and 17 year olds do not need one for nonagricultural, nonhazardous work during summer vacation. See permit.html?state=oh for the steps.
duration: Summer program; length not stated
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old and complete an application, a background check and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then complete the background check and orientation.
notes: Some outdoor roles run March to November and the Children's Garden runs April to October.
duration: No minimum hours; weekly, monthly or seasonal
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. If you are a minor, a parent or guardian must sign a form that confirms your age and a release.
how_to_apply: Send an application. Have a character reference and an emergency contact ready. Call 615-786-0142. You can also email deborah.reschke@williamsoncounty-tn.gov.
notes: Jobs depend on what the library needs at the time. Not every applicant gets a spot.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says all Fremont high school students are welcome.
how_to_apply: Go to the volunteer portal page. Click Fill in an application. If you already volunteer through MyImpactPage.com, log in. Questions: ebuchanan@aclibrary.org.
notes: Some events in the community need extra forms. They also have a separate sign up.
duration: Tuesdays 4:00 to 6:00 p.m. (October 13, 20 and 27, 2026 listed)

who_can_apply: High school students in the Fremont, New Haven or Newark school districts. Charter, home school and independent study students should call to ask about the price.
how_to_apply: Sign up during pre-registration at your home school. Ask your school counselor, College and Career Specialist or Career Center for help with scheduling. Buses take students to and from the ROP center.
notes: Center is at 5019 Stevenson Blvd, Fremont. Phone (510) 657-1865. College credit partners named on the site: Chabot, Las Positas, Mission, Ohlone and Universal Technical Institute. Grade levels are not stated on the pages. The site's jobs page for high schoolers only links to Indeed and a company careers page.
pay_detail: Free for students in those three districts.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18 when they join. You must be in high school or have finished it. You need a C+ (2.5) grade average and must turn in report cards each term. No school discipline in the last year for things like theft, bullying or violence.
how_to_apply: When it opens, send four things: a one page essay on why you want to join, your latest report card, the Teen Volunteer Application and the Explorer application. Then you have an interview and a background check. Questions: (510) 790-6691.
notes: The background check takes about 1 to 2 months. You must go to the first three meetings. If you are not accepted, you can apply again after one year.
duration: Weekly meetings and training. New Explorers do a 4 to 6 month field training and a one week academy in San Diego their first summer.
pay_detail: This is a volunteer program. The program page does not mention pay.

who_can_apply: Each job lists its own age. Sports Instructor jobs are for ages 15 and up. Cooking, After School and Facility jobs are for ages 18 and up. You do not need work experience.
how_to_apply: Look at the current openings and apply online. No work experience? List volunteer work, clubs, group projects and sports teams. Questions: (510) 494-4347.
notes: Workers must get CPR, First Aid and AED training within 30 days of being hired. The city offers classes. Fingerprints and a TB test are also required. See each job description for the full list.
duration: Seasonal and year-round part-time jobs, with day, evening and weekend shifts.
pay_detail: These are paid part-time jobs. The program page does not list the pay; each job posting has the details.

who_can_apply: Age 14 and up. Teens aged 14 and 15 must come with an adult who also registers as a volunteer. Under 14 is not accepted.
how_to_apply: Create an account at volunteer.tcvfoodbank.org, sign the Volunteer Handbook and Consent forms, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteer@tcvfoodbank.org or call 510-598-4066.
notes: TCV does not sign court or traffic ticket hours. The page did not say whether school service hours are signed, so ask. Orientation was not mentioned on this page.

who_can_apply: Students at Fremont Unified middle and high schools. The page says limited English is not a barrier to joining career and technical education programs.
how_to_apply: The page gives no sign-up steps. Ask your school counselor or principal, or contact Leslie Heller, Director of Secondary Education, (510) 659-2513.
notes: The page is general. It lists 15 industry sectors and 58 career pathways. It does not list internship partners or work-based learning. Ask your counselor which pathways your school offers.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or residency rules. Ask the Recreation Division.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call the Recreation Division at 510-494-4300.
notes: Meets 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the first Monday of each month except July and August, at City Hall, 3300 Capitol Ave. The page lists 12 members.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeens Application linked on the zoo's support page. Group questions: volunteer@fcz.org.
notes: Fresno is in the Central Valley, outside Merced County. The page uses one application link for both VolunTeens and the junior camp counselor role.
duration: Year-round; 1-day training
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Jr. Camp Counselor Application linked on the zoo's support page.
notes: Listed on the zoo's volunteer page; pay is not stated. Fresno is in the Central Valley, outside Merced County.
duration: Summer camp weeks; hours not stated
pay_detail: Not stated; listed on the zoo's volunteer page.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Attend a Teen Advisory Board meeting or submit a book review. The page does not describe a sign-up form. Allow up to 7 business days after an activity for your credit to show. Call (714) 773-5719.
notes: Easy way to start earning service hours. The Teen Advisory Board page on the same site has more detail; it was not read.
duration: Board meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 6 p.m. (starting Sept 1, 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns volunteer service hours (1 hour per meeting or approved review).

who_can_apply: High school students age 15 and over. The hospital picks based on your application. It looks at whether you can keep the weekly commitment. It also looks at your school background and career interests. There is no job shadowing or internship.
how_to_apply: When applications open, contact St. Jude volunteer services at Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Accepted volunteers must go to an orientation and get a health screening. This takes about one month in all.
notes: Questions: Stjudevolunteers@providence.org or 714-992-3000 ext. 2878. Questions should come from the student. Health screening and orientation are required (about one month).
duration: Minimum one year and 140 hours a year. Shifts: Mon to Fri 4 to 7 p.m. or weekends 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Any high school student who lives in Fulton County, GA. You need a computer, phone or tablet and Wi-Fi.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online enrollment form. Do it during the time when sign-up is open.
notes: Enrollment for 2026-27 closed Sept 28, 2026, per the enrollment page. Call the county at 404-612-4000 to ask about late spots. The enrollment page does not mention internships. Only the county page does. Contact: customerservice@fultoncountyga.gov.
duration: One school year (2026-27 program)
pay_detail: Free to join. Members can win gift cards from $25 to $100 and other prizes. The page lists paid summer internships for juniors and seniors but gives no pay rate.

who_can_apply: Youth under 18 may apply with a parent or guardian signature. The page does not state a minimum age, so ask Volunteer Services.
how_to_apply: The page (last updated 2026/10/07) says most volunteer projects are filled. Most places have a waitlist. You can still apply. Under 18: download and print the PDF application, sign it, get a parent or guardian signature, and return it to Volunteer Services by email, mail, fax or drop-off. Then attend orientation. Email vol.services@fultoncountyga.gov or call 404-613-0125.
notes: The page says the library is on hold for community service hour requests. Students who need school hours must contact Volunteer Services early. Some branches have Teen Advisory Boards; ask the Youth Services Librarian. Library systems for DeKalb and Cobb counties are separate.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts after orientation
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 16. You go to a Fulton County school, live in Fulton County or have a family member who works for Fulton County. No serious arrest or conviction record.
how_to_apply: Send in the application with a one-page essay. The topic is on the application. Add a letter of recommendation from a school administrator.
notes: The page still shows 2025 dates, so call to confirm the current year. Contacts on the page: FCMD.JuniorDeputy@fultoncountyga.gov, 404-612-4462 or 404-612-4147.
duration: 1 week (June 23 to 27 in 2025)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost not listed.

who_can_apply: Fulton County Schools students who are at least 16, in 11th or 12th grade, and following a defined career pathway. Individual schools may add rules. Students in Atlanta Public Schools use their own district.
how_to_apply: Print and finish the WBL Interest Form. Give it to your school's WBL coordinator. Students who meet the requirements are issued an application. Grades, attendance, discipline and related coursework are reviewed. You must follow up on job leads yourself.
notes: District contact listed on the page: Leslie McHann, 470-254-0466. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: Per school term
pay_detail: School credit. The district page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.

who_can_apply: Fulton County residents in 9th to 11th grade. You must go to a school inside Fulton County lines.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a two-page essay. Also get a one-page nomination statement. It comes from a teacher, counselor, principal or community member who has known you for at least a year.
notes: Contact on the page: 404-612-7386 or the county line 404-612-4000. The length of a term is not stated.
duration: School year. Up to 20 hours a month for planning meetings and projects (over 120 hours a year).
pay_detail: Volunteer. The page does not mention a stipend.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. Bring an ID (school ID, driver's license or library card).
how_to_apply: 1) Fill out the online teen volunteer application. 2) Register for a one-time Teen Volunteer Orientation. 3) Sign up for open sessions on the teen volunteer calendar. Cancel at least 24 hours ahead.
notes: Grade 6 is under 13, so younger readers should ask about their grade. The library's Elgin Teens page also describes Studio 270, a high school teen space at 270 N. Grove Ave. (homework help, college readiness, job hunting help; phone 847-695-7577), but parts of that page look out of date, so call first. The volunteer page lists a contact email that is hidden in the page text; use the library's Contact Us page.
duration: Short sessions, about 1 hour each; you pick the ones you want
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Montana middle school and high school students (grades 6 to 12 in fall 2026 for the 2026 camp).
how_to_apply: Use the "Learn more & register for CSI camp" link on the MSU Continuing Education youth page.
notes: Held at the Gallatin College East Campus IT Cybersecurity Lab in Bozeman. Camp has no cost.
pay_detail: Free. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 17 years old. You must fill out the application yourself.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Counselor-In-Training application linked on the program page. Fees are due two weeks before your assigned week. Call the recreation counter at 714-741-5200 to ask where to turn it in.
notes: This is a program you pay to join. It is not a paid job. Camp Grove is at Edgar Park, 12781 Topaz Street.
duration: Camp Grove runs 9 weeks. In 2026 it ran June 8 to August 7.
pay_detail: You pay $60 for each week. Week 8 costs $120 and week 9 costs $85, and those two fees are not refundable. The weekly cost includes the camp trip fee.

who_can_apply: For the Atlantis Play Center and Sports jobs, you must be at least 16 years old by May 20, 2026. Day camp and resource center jobs on the same page are for ages 18 and up, by May 20, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the city page to apply on the city job site.
notes: Lifeguard and Instructor Guard jobs are on the same page. The page does not state a minimum age for them. Atlantis Play Center and Sports jobs are year round. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.
duration: Part time. Hours vary with the program.
pay_detail: Recreation Leader pay is $17.00 to $19.00 an hour. Recreation Specialist pay is $18.50 to $20.50 an hour.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 13 to 17 years old by November 19, 2026. The page calls it a program by and for Garden Grove teens. A parent or guardian must sign the forms.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and the contract. A parent or guardian signs them. You can email them to ggtac@ggcity.org. You can also drop them off at City Hall, 11222 Acacia Parkway. Or bring them to the next general meeting.
notes: Members must go to the monthly meetings and join at least 2 volunteer events. Meetings are at the Community Meeting Center, 11300 Stanford Avenue, and food is provided. Planned events include Foods of Garden Grove Live, Jack O Lantern Jamboree and Winter in the Grove. To win a scholarship you must go to at least 4 meetings and volunteer at 2 GGTAC events. Questions: 714-741-5360.
duration: September 2026 to April 2027, one meeting a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee is listed on the program page. Members can apply for scholarships.

who_can_apply: Gwinnett County Public Schools juniors and seniors who are 16 by September 1 and have coursework that matches their career choice. The school reviews grades, attendance and discipline.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. Forms: electronic agreement, WBL application, recommendation form and job site information form. Forms are uploaded in the WBL class when the semester starts. Apprenticeships need a post-high-school plan.
notes: No home-office or private-residence placements. The program cannot guarantee a job. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: One semester at a time as a school elective
pay_detail: School credit. The GCPS page does not state pay. The state says internships may be paid or unpaid and co-ops and apprenticeships are paid.

who_can_apply: Motivated rising high school seniors enrolled at a Genesys Works partner school. The Bay Area page says 100% of its students qualify for free or reduced lunch. No GPA is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview if accepted, then get summer training details. Phone 415-442-0280, email gwba@ba.genesysworks.org.
notes: You must attend a partner school, and the lists of schools and counties were not on the pages. Ask them whether your school is a partner. No 2027 dates or deadline are posted. Interns work for pay, so a California work permit applies if you are under 18.
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a school-year internship
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not posted (the page only lists total interns' wages)

who_can_apply: Geneva Public Library patrons in grades 6 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register as a Volunteen using the sign-up form on the page. Contact: geneva.library@gpld.org or (630) 232-0780, 227 S. Seventh St., Geneva.
notes: Service hours are flexible and are not listed as a set number. The page does not describe the registration steps beyond the sign-up form.
duration: Fall 2026 session: Sept 14 to Dec 4, 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students 15 and older who can work on their own after training. Year round spots are few. They mostly go to homeschool, hybrid or similar students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get an email in 24 to 48 hours with next steps. They are an interview with the Student Volunteer Committee, a background check, a drug test and shot records. Call 512-942-4777 or email sdghvolunteers@hcahealthcare.com.
notes: Georgetown is in Williamson County, north of Round Rock. Shifts can be evenings and weekends. Vaccines listed: flu, Tdap within 10 years, TB, 2 MMR and 2 chickenpox or history.
duration: 3 to 4 hours a week, up to 8 weeks in summer
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Cloverbud programs for ages 5 to 7 exist in some counties only.
how_to_apply: Contact your local county UGA Extension office, or Georgia 4-H at 706-542-4444 or ga4h@uga.edu. The site has a 'Find Your Local Club' page.
notes: The home page lists teen options. They are Ambassador Program, Leadership in Action, Step Up and Lead, Senior Conference, State Council and State Congress. The pages did not give dates or ages for each. Check with the county office.
duration: Ongoing; clubs, projects, camps and conferences run through the year
pay_detail: Not a job. The page says 4-H does not require a uniform or club fees. Camps and some activities may have their own costs, not listed on this page.

who_can_apply: High school or home school students ages 15 to 17 at the time of application. Teens need their own transportation and a parent or guardian must join the info session.
how_to_apply: Register for one mandatory virtual information session (email volunteer@georgiaaquarium.org or use the page's Contact Us interest form). A parent or guardian must attend with the teen. If chosen, attend a group interview. Bring birth certificate and photo ID.
notes: Not every applicant gets an interview. No behind-the-scenes roles for teens and no court-ordered or school service hours. The page lists the group interview as both three hours and four hours, and its weekday names for the 2026 dates do not match the calendar, so confirm exact dates with the Aquarium. Last-year dates are shown for reference only.
duration: 4 months per session: Spring (Jan to Apr) 60 hours, Summer (May to Aug) 80 hours, Fall (Sep to Dec) 60 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. $45 administrative fee (check or money order) once accepted. Perks: volunteer pass, free parking on shifts, 5 one-time daily tickets after finishing.

who_can_apply: Male high school rising seniors. The home page says to contact your local American Legion Post or your Guidance Counselor for more information.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion post or school guidance counselor. Chosen students then use the 'Request to Attend' form. They also use a permission form. Both are on the Georgia Boys State site. Questions: administration@dogboysstate.org or 229-938-9352.
notes: Boys only (Girls State is a separate program run by the Auxiliary). The program is not a paid job, so no work permit. The 2026 memo says the week includes an evening devotional, and families who object may decline the invitation. Delegates must stay all week.
duration: One week. 2026 session was June 7 to 13, 2026, about 400 delegates.
pay_detail: Not a job. The 2026 memo says delegates pay a one time $5.00 'state tax' at registration. The sponsoring Legion post handles transportation. The page does not list a program fee.

who_can_apply: Youth in Georgia foster care ages 14 to 21. The 2026 summer program was for ages 15 to 17 on June 1, 2026 (not turning 18 before July 1, 2026), with a Georgia photo ID and U.S. citizenship, permanent residence or a work card.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Georgia C.R.E.W. application on the DFCS site. Everyone, including returning youth, must apply. Call 877-423-4746 (main DFCS number).
notes: Only for youth currently in Georgia foster care. A Career Resource Connection for ages 14 and up and state ID help are also offered. The youth page still showed 2024 dates, so rely on the main page and call to confirm. Ask your caseworker.
duration: Summer program with weekly sessions
pay_detail: Summer participants get a paid incentive for attending weekly sessions. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students at a Georgia school with a DECA chapter. The state page does not list grade or age rules.
how_to_apply: The state page is written for school advisors. Chapters sign up and renew members online at deca.org. Ask a business or marketing teacher if your school has a chapter. A school can start one using the Start a Chapter page. The page says the Georgia DECA minimum is 15 members.
notes: Contact the state staff through the Contact Us page at gadeca.org.
duration: Membership is for one school year
pay_detail: Not a job. Student dues are $16 ($8 national and $8 state), per the state page.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are current sophomores or juniors. The page does not list an age limit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a permission form from a guardian. Add one letter from an adult who is not family.
notes: Camp sites are Charlie Elliott Wildlife Center in Mansfield and Camp Jekyll on Jekyll Island. Students can earn college credit for Intro to Wildlife Management (FWMT 1000) at no cost. Check YES on the application.
duration: 1 week (July 18 to 24, 2027)
pay_detail: $100, which covers all meals and lodging. The page does not mention scholarships.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school teams of 4 to 6 students. The page does not give grade rules.
how_to_apply: Go to the Resources tab of the Georgia Envirothon site. Use the sign-up section.
notes: Late registration may mean no lunch count or no team shirt. The page also lists October 9, 2026 as a training day registration date.
duration: 1 day contest
pay_detail: $250 registration fee per team. Lunch is included.

who_can_apply: Georgia students interested in business careers. The home page does not list grade, age or dues.
how_to_apply: The page says 'Joining is simple!' and links a chapter finder to see which FBLA chapters are close to you. Students join through a local chapter.
notes: Ask your school whether it has an FBLA chapter. The page does not list the state conference dates or dues.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
pay_detail: Not a job. Dues are not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education classes at a Georgia school with an ag program. The membership page says every student in those classes becomes an FFA member.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an agricultural education class at your school. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. The state page says a student is expected to be in ag classes to join FFA.
notes: If your school has no ag program you cannot join through it. The state site links a 2026-2027 state agricultural education calendar for event dates.
duration: Ongoing during the school year
pay_detail: Not a job. The membership page lists a yearly affiliation fee of $9.05 per high school student ($5.05 national, $4.00 state) and $900 per chapter for middle school. The page does not say whether families pay it.

who_can_apply: High school students in Dougherty County, GA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Apply Here form on the NFUF page.
notes: A USDA city farming grant pays for it. Office: 125 Pine Avenue, Suite 150, Albany, GA. Phone: 229-352-6591. Email: info@flintriverfresh.org.
duration: September to May: two Saturdays plus after-school hours
pay_detail: $10 per hour, about 8 to 12 hours per week during the school year.

who_can_apply: Youth 14 or older who are in foster care, or were in care for at least 6 months.
