how_to_apply: Use the Find help near you map on the site to find your Independent Living Specialist (ILS) by region or county. If you have trouble, email askilp@dhs.ga.gov. Your caseworker can also help.
notes: The page lists no phone number. For paid summer jobs for foster youth, see the Georgia C.R.E.W. card. Ask your ILS about the Education and Training Voucher (ETV) for college or training.
pay_detail: Not a job. Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Girls who finished junior year. You need high moral character and above-average school standing. An American Legion Auxiliary unit must sponsor you. Another group that a unit approves can sponsor you too. Each high school is limited to 12 girls.
how_to_apply: Contact the unit president or Girls State Chairman of a local American Legion Auxiliary unit. This is how you get sponsored. A selection committee picks the girls. Then the application is completed online. The school checks that you are eligible before school ends. Email georgiagirlsstate@gmail.com or call 678-289-8446.
notes: Girls only. The site shows 2026 dates and the 'I Want In' page says last updated 12/3/2022, so confirm with your unit before relying on the dates. Not a paid job, so no work permit.
duration: About one week. 2026 session was June 7 to 12, 2026.
pay_detail: $350.00 registration fee, usually paid by the sponsoring unit or organization. The page says sponsors are listed for each girl.

who_can_apply: Skilled and talented high school sophomores and juniors. A Georgia public school district, independent school or state charter school must nominate you. Home school students go through their local school district.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply directly. Ask your school counselor or GHP Coordinator to nominate you. Nominees then complete an online application with a parent permission form, a recommendation and a transcript. GHP project manager: (404) 444-7062.
notes: Local nomination dates differ by school district and the page says they run August to early November, so move fast. Standardized test results are no longer required. The application page is marked updated 08/2026.
duration: Mid-June to mid-July (residential)
pay_detail: Free to apply. The page says required costs are travel to the semifinalist event and the host campus, basic supplies and optional spending money. Meals and rooms are provided.

who_can_apply: Students at least 12 years old. The packet says there are no exceptions. A page is sponsored by the Lieutenant Governor or one Senator.
how_to_apply: The 2025 welcome packet says to contact your sponsoring Senator's office when you register. Staff contact: kim.campbell@senate.ga.gov or illana.burkhart@senate.ga.gov, 404-657-7004. The program web page needs a browser to load, so check it for the current form.
notes: Source is the official 2025 Senate Page welcome packet (the program web pages on legis.ga.gov only showed a loading screen to the reader). Under Georgia law cited in the packet (O.C.G.A. 20-2-692) page service counts as present at school. Dress code is business or business casual. Cell phones are not allowed while paging. The Georgia House has its own page program at legis.ga.gov/house/page-program, which could not be read.
duration: One legislative day. Report about 1.5 hours before the Senate convenes. The Senate usually convenes at 10:00 AM (check the Senate schedule the night before).
pay_detail: $20.00 honorarium paid at the end of the day, plus a certificate of service (2025 welcome packet). A 2026 amount is not posted, so confirm it.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors or seniors on track to graduate. You need a recalculated GPA of 3.0 or higher. You need test scores unless your GPA is 3.4 or higher. You need approval from your counselor and a parent. You also need proof of lawful presence.
how_to_apply: Submit the undergraduate application online. Send test scores if they are asked for. Have your counselor send your transcript through GA Futures. Perimeter College has its own application. It has five campuses.
notes: You must earn a C or better in every class to keep funding. The page gives two test score minimums. The lower ones are in the requirements list. The higher ones are in the step on test scores. Ask admissions which apply. Perimeter College lets dual students take 1000 and 2000 level classes at its campuses or online.
duration: By semester: spring, summer and fall
pay_detail: State funding (Georgia Student Finance Commission) pays tuition and mandatory fees for up to 15 credit hours a semester from the approved course list. You pay lab fees, supplies, meals and travel. Joint enrollment (not dual) is paid by the family.

who_can_apply: Students in a Georgia high school or Georgia home school. You need a 3.5 unweighted GPA and ACT, PSAT or SAT scores. You need precalculus and two finished college-level courses (AP, DE or IB). You also need proof of lawful presence in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit the Georgia Tech Dual Enrollment application in the term window. Add your high school transcript and test scores. Add AP scores if needed and proof of lawful presence. Apply for state funding at GAFutures.org.
notes: Competitive. Funding can be denied if you used your 30 hours, your high school does not take part, the course is not eligible (on-campus), or you are not a U.S. citizen, eligible non-citizen or Georgia resident. Out-of-state tuition is $1,153.46 per credit hour. Decisions come about 3 weeks after the window closes.
duration: By term: fall, spring and summer (summer is distance computer science only)
pay_detail: Most Georgia students get state funding that covers enrollment (30 credit hour limit). Self-pay in fall 2026 is $353.93 per credit hour for Georgia residents, plus fees ($531 for online-only).

who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are at least 16 years old by the program start. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the STEP page before the deadline. Questions: outreach@ae.gatech.edu.
notes: Read on the Georgia Space Grant Consortium page that hosts the STEP information; the Georgia Tech Aerospace page itself returned a 403 block. Other sessions listed for 2026 were in Augusta and Albany.
duration: 2-week day program (not residential); Atlanta session July 6 to 17 in 2026
pay_detail: Free to students (funded by industry donors). No stipend stated. Students provide their own daily transportation.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents who are rising 11th and 12th graders. You should like engineering, science, math or technology. The page does not mention a GPA rule.
how_to_apply: The page says sign-up is closed for 2026. It does not give application steps. Check the Georgia Tech College of Engineering K-20 initiatives page for the next session.
notes: The same page also describes a separate TryEngineering Summer Institute, a nine day residential program for thirty Georgia high school students at no cost, with no dates given. Georgia residents only.
duration: 2026 session was June 7 to 15, 2026, overnight on campus
pay_detail: Free to participants in 2026 (page wording). Participants stay on campus.

who_can_apply: High school students, through their own school's Work-Based Learning coordinator. The state page lists no age or grade rules. Districts set their own (Gwinnett, Fulton County and Cobb above say juniors and seniors age 16 or older).
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator or counselor. Internships can happen only after coursework related to the placement. Co-op students must be enrolled in a course directly related to the job.
notes: Youth Apprenticeship in Georgia is run through the Department of Education and local schools. The Georgia Department of Labor youth page covers work permits and child labor rules only. Georgia Work Ready was not researched. Georgia requires a work permit for students under 16 (see the Georgia Department of Labor work permit page).
duration: Varies by option. An Employability Skill Development placement can last up to one school year.
pay_detail: Co-op and Youth Apprenticeship are paid work-site experiences. Internships may be paid or unpaid.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who face barriers to education, training or employment. Both in-school and out-of-school youth are served. The page does not list the exact barriers or income rules.
how_to_apply: The state pages give no application steps. They give no list of local offices. Use the contact page at tcsg.edu or the WorkSource Georgia portal (worksourcegaportal.com). Find your local office there.
notes: The pages do not say how to enroll. A call to your local WorkSource office is the real next step. The services page says the Occupational Skills part is for ages 18 to 24. So 14 to 17 year olds would use the other services. Atlanta area teens may also see the city and county programs listed separately in this guide.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Free to join. The services page lists paid and unpaid work experiences, but the program pages give no pay rate.

who_can_apply: Sophomores and juniors currently enrolled in high school in Los Angeles County, who are at least 16 when the program starts and live within 25 miles of the Getty Center.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in early February. Questions: gettyteens@getty.edu.
notes: Supported by the Vera R. Campbell Foundation. The page calls it a paid summer internship but says only that interns receive a stipend. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Mid-June to early August; interns commit to all program days
pay_detail: Every intern gets a stipend after finishing the program. Amount not stated. Lunch and transportation to the Getty sites are provided.

who_can_apply: Girls and young women in grades 9 to 12. Programs run at the Simpson Center in Oakland (year-round) and Cal State East Bay in Hayward (summer).
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us page at girlsinc-alameda.org. Office: 510 16th St, Oakland. The site does not list application steps.
notes: The page checked on 2026-10-10 does not mention Code the Game, a fall offering, or grades 10 to 12 for coding. Internship pay, hours and ages are not posted.
pay_detail: Programs are free to families; internships are paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Aimed at girls and young women in tech. The page does not spell out the rule for other genders, so ask. Clubs meet 1 to 2 hours a week; Pathways is virtual and self-paced.
how_to_apply: Use Get Started on girlswhocode.com/programs to find a Club or begin Pathways.
notes: The page lists no cohort dates. A separate program for ages 18 to 25 also exists.
duration: 1 to 2 hours per week for Clubs
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Current high school students. Dual Enrollment: students in Glendale Unified (GUSD) and Burbank Unified (BUSD) taking courses on the class offerings list. Jump Start: everyone else, for college credit only.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Then send the Annual Digital Form signed by a parent and your counselor. Find classes, clear any prerequisites and register in MyGCC. Email dual@glendale.edu or call (818) 240-1000 ext. 4767.
notes: Jump Start credit is not guaranteed to count toward high school graduation. A weekly Zoom help hour runs Tuesdays 3:30 to 5:00 PM.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Costs and fee waivers are not stated on the page. Ask dual@glendale.edu.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 and in school. You have a disability or health condition, such as an IEP, 504 plan, ADHD or anxiety.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. STEP contacts: (818) 937-8005 or (818) 937-8057.
notes: The GYA page does not mention work permits or income rules.
duration: 120 hours
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The page lists it as a first job or summer job program. GYA serves youth from Glendale, Burbank and La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Office: 1255 S Central Ave, Glendale; (818) 937-8073, Mon to Fri 8 to 5.
notes: The page does not give the hourly rate or weekly hours, so ask the office. The GYA page does not mention work permits. Checked 2026-10-10: the page says one Apply Now form covers all programs and lists no dates, so we cannot tell if summer spots are open now. Left unconfirmed.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The hourly rate is not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21 and low income. GYA serves Glendale, Burbank, La Canada-Flintridge and the greater Los Angeles County area.
how_to_apply: One online Apply Now form covers all GYA programs. A case worker contacts you in 3 to 5 business days. Contact for TEAM: (818) 937-8006.
notes: Income limits and funding sources are not spelled out on the page checked 2026-10-10.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated whether TEAM itself pays. GYA says its other youth programs include paid work experience.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in grades 6 to 12. They live in Glenview or go to a school the library serves. Teen Advisory Board applicants must be in grades 7 to 11 and follow the same rule. Innovation Center volunteers must be in high school at a school the library serves.
how_to_apply: Fill out the youth volunteer application when it opens. The Teen Advisory Board form comes out in November. For the Innovation Center, write to innovationdesk@glenviewpl.org. For other questions, write to youthdesk@glenviewpl.org or call 847-729-7500.
notes: Returning volunteers do not need to apply again. Court ordered community service for teens must be 16 and older. It uses a separate form.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: monthly meetings and 3 to 5 programs in a one year term
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school and undergraduate students. Minimum age 15 by Jun 18, 2026 for remote or computer-lab internships and 16 for in-person wet-lab internships. No minimum GPA; transcripts are not requested.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement; interested mentors interview strong candidates and offers go out in early April. Request a fee waiver code from cosassip@gmu.edu if needed.
notes: Labs are at the Fairfax campus, the Science and Technology Campus in Manassas, or Woodbridge; students arrange their own transportation and campus housing cannot be arranged for minors. This is a paid-by-the-student internship, not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 8 weeks, full time (Jun 18 to Aug 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: $25 application fee and, if offered an internship, $1,299 tuition for 3 undergraduate credits. Both can be waived with demonstrated financial need.

who_can_apply: Exceptionally talented high school juniors and seniors. You need a non-degree application and fee. You need your official high school transcript. You need permission from your high school counselor or administrator. Non-native English speakers must meet the English proficiency rule.
how_to_apply: Complete the Non-Degree application. Send your high school transcript. Send your counselor or administrator's permission. Fairfax County Public Schools and Loudoun County Public Schools students can use the school partnership pages. These are for math and science dual enrollment.
notes: The Admissions Committee may ask for test scores or transcripts from other dual enrollment credits. The page also lists Youth Leadership Conferences and Educational Travel Programs, which were not read in detail.
duration: One semester at a time, up to 11 lower-level credits
pay_detail: An application fee and college course costs apply. The amounts are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 through 18 by June 9, 2026. You must be able to work legally in the United States and be available Tuesday to Thursday for the whole program.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the next application. In 2026, interviews were in April.
notes: You must carry your own gear and tools to the job site. You can miss no more than three days. You must be on time at Jeffco Parks & Open Space headquarters in Golden each workday. The page does not state a county residency rule.
duration: About 6 weeks (June 16 to July 30 in 2026)
pay_detail: $18 per hour (2026)

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. The program is built for young people who face barriers to work, such as low income, foster care, homelessness, disability, teen parenting or a record. The page lists no formal rules.
how_to_apply: Email youth@ging.org. The page lists 404-420-9900 as the general Goodwill number, not a program line.
notes: Address on the page: 2201 Lawrenceville Hwy, Suite 300, Decatur, GA 30033. Career centers listed: Athens, Cornelia, Decatur, Duluth, Oakwood, Smyrna and Woodstock. The page does not say which counties are served, so ask when you email. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required for minors under 16. This program starts at 16.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience. The page does not give a wage.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: The First Seasons Community Center job has a minimum age of 15. The Warming House Attendant job has a minimum age of 16.
how_to_apply: Apply online at gfparks.org/employment/apply-online/. Questions: Grand Forks Park District Human Resources, (701) 746-2750, 1060 47th Ave S.
notes: Call to check these jobs are still open, because the Oct 1 date has passed. Other postings were not read, so their ages are unknown. These include skating instructor and indoor ice arena worker. Summer lifeguard jobs at Grand Forks outdoor pools are run by Choice Health & Fitness. Their current age rule is not confirmed.
duration: First Seasons: Saturdays 10 am to 5 pm, October to mid-April, flexible or split shifts, no evenings. Warming house: about 15 to 20 hours a week, weekdays 4 to 8 pm and weekends and holidays noon to 8 pm.
pay_detail: First Seasons Community Center: $14.00 an hour to start. Warming house attendant: $12.00 an hour to start.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 16 or older for the Cleaning Squad. Most other fair jobs need 18 or more.
how_to_apply: Fill out the employment application on the fair careers page. It is online or in PDF. You can also pick one up at the State Fair Administrative Office, 501 E Fonner Park Rd, Suite 200, Grand Island, NE 68801. Or email it to the address on the flyer.
notes: Quote from the flyer: Applicants must be 16 years of age. The online application has a Social Security No. field and asks if you are authorized to work in the United States. Whether a Nebraska work permit is needed was not stated on the program pages.
duration: 2026 fair shifts: August 28 to September 7, 2026, plus training and orientation
pay_detail: Rate of pay starts at $15 per hour (2026 flyer).

who_can_apply: You must be 15 by the last day of the lifeguard course. You must pass a swim test: 300 yards, 2 minutes treading water, and a timed rescue.
how_to_apply: Look for openings and apply online at the City of Great Falls job site (governmentjobs.com/careers/greatfallsmt). The city phone number on its employment page is 406-771-1180. A Park and Recreation phone number is not stated.
notes: Classes need at least 5 people to run. The city offers certification classes through the year.
duration: Certification lasts 2 years
pay_detail: The city page says competitive wages and paid lifeguard certification. Hourly pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18. You must sign up.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the program page. Or contact Graham Kerwin, Interim Education Manager. Call 406-727-8255. Or email graham@the-square.org.
notes: The program page shows a temporary hiatus in its April 2, 2026 update, until the museum finds an instructor. Call to ask if it has restarted.
duration: Weekly. The meeting time is not set yet on the program page.
pay_detail: Free to join. Food and art supplies are provided. No stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Volunteers of any age can fill out the form. The form does not state a minimum age. If you are under 18, the form asks for a parent or guardian's contact information.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form (a PDF on the library website) and give it to the library. The library is at 301 2nd Avenue North. Phone: 406-453-0349.
notes: The form asks for the last 4 digits of your Social Security number. It is for a background check and a workers compensation report. Ask the library about this before you fill it in. Call to ask about the current age rule and openings.
duration: Most roles need an ongoing time commitment (the form lists 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, ongoing or seasonal)
pay_detail: Volunteer role. No pay is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 on June 1, 2026. Animal Care Assistants must be at least 14 and have done JZK the summer before. Advanced JZK is for returning 17 year olds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then go to a 20 minute in-person interview. After you are accepted, pay the fee. Give a negative TB test by orientation. Then go to orientation.
notes: Teens arrange their own lunch and transportation. Contact: Education@GPZoo.org or (605) 367-7003. 2026 new teen interviews were April 11 and 12, so expect the 2027 cycle to start in winter or early spring.
duration: Whole summer; the 2026 session ran through August 9. At least two half-day shifts a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay a fee after they are accepted: $85 for zoo members, $100 for non-members. It covers materials and two uniform t-shirts. Scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 by the first day of class. You must volunteer, since you cannot be forced. You must be credit deficient or at risk of dropping out. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident and a California resident. You must be clear of felony charges. You must live in one of these places: Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern, Santa Barbara or Ventura County, or in Lancaster or Palmdale.
how_to_apply: Make sure you meet the rules to apply. Fill out the Interest Form on the site. Then watch the required virtual orientation video. It is a must for the application.
notes: Meant for teens who dropped out or are at risk of dropping out. The FAQ says each ChalleNGe program runs its own admissions. Call or write the academy (contact page on its site) about county rules. Many cadets can earn a GED during the residential phase (FAQ). Some counties on the site have no separate region tag in this guide. They are Santa Cruz, Madera, Fresno, Monterey, San Benito, Kings, Tulare, Inyo, San Luis Obispo, Kern and Ventura. Lancaster and Palmdale are in Los Angeles County.
duration: The page states a 17 1/2 month residential program. The length of the follow-up phase is not stated on this page; ask the academy.
pay_detail: Free to participants (the site says offered free of charge, paid by federal and state partnerships).

who_can_apply: Best for ages 14 to 17. Returning youth ages 18 to 21 can take lead roles. The page says the group hires from nearby areas. They include Westwood, Sheridan, NE Park Hill, southern Commerce City, Montbello and NW Aurora.
how_to_apply: Use the "Current Youth Job Openings" link on the Youth Pathways page.
notes: The website moved from groundworkdenver.org to groundworkcolorado.org. The page also lists a GRIT program for ages 18 to 29, which is not for teens.
duration: Seasonal. Some teams are summer only, some run in the school year.
pay_detail: Paid staff positions. The wage is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Georgia residents in a public, private, charter or home school in Georgia, in the class of 2027, 2028 or 2029, who are 16 by April 4, 2027 (no exceptions). Proof of U.S. citizenship or U.S. person status is required for most positions. You need your own transportation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online pre-application. It has a resume (PDF), a personal statement and a letter of recommendation. It must be 100% complete before it closes. You can join the 2027 contact registry for updates. Email support.hsi.stem@gtri.gatech.edu with questions.
notes: No weekend, after hours or remote work. Housing is not provided. Do not send unsolicited emails or calls to GTRI employees about internships. The page asks this. Finishing the pre-application does not guarantee a job. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This internship requires age 16 by April 4, 2027.
duration: Five weeks, about June 14 to July 23, 2027; up to 24 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not on the page.

who_can_apply: Gwinnett County residents or students who go to school in Gwinnett County, ages 15 to 21. You must be 15 by the first workshop. You must be free for the whole paid internship program. You need a reliable ride. You cannot be a past Empower Gwinnett County Government intern. No grades or work experience are required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the posted window. A form link is on the program page. Human Resources picks applicants based on interests, career goals and department needs. No interview is required. Selected applicants get a conditional job offer. Some jobs may need a background check.
notes: The main page says the 2026 application is closed. It says the 2027 dates will be posted there. Questions: HREmployeeEngagement@GwinnettCounty.com.
duration: 2 Saturday workshops plus 4 weeks (June)
pay_detail: $15 per hour for the two workshops and the four-week internship

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who live in Gwinnett County and will be in 7th through 12th grade as of August. Everyone must pass an application process.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the page to reach the youth academy application. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page names no season or week for the sessions and gives no age range. The only date given is the May 29, 2026 application deadline, so confirm the week before planning. Season is set to summer only because the deadline is in May. Unpaid program, so no work permit. Only the general county number 770.822.8000 is listed.
duration: 1 week, Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm
pay_detail: Free. The page says the academy is free.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 to 18 years old and go to a Gwinnett County public school. Case by case, the program may approve school outside Gwinnett County. You must be in good standing in your school and community.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. The parent and the student both sign it online. Go to orientation. Turn in a recommendation from a teacher, a school leader or a community leader.
notes: The page does not say whether it pays, how long it lasts or what the exact opening date is. No essay is mentioned. County phone: 770.822.8000.
duration: Length not stated
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. The page says participants can earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. The page says the minimum age is 13 with parental permission required. Homework help covers students in grades K to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form from the Apply Online button on the volunteer page. List the branches you want. If you are a GCPS student, use a personal or parent email, not a school email.
notes: The background check on the page applies only to volunteers 18 and older. Open spots vary by branch.
duration: 40 hours over 6 to 12 months, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to be a certified lifeguard. You can start the prerequisites (an in-water skills test) at 15. Lifeguard I or II jobs need a current lifeguard training certificate by hire date.
how_to_apply: 1. Contact a year-round aquatic center and schedule the In-Water Skills Test. 2. Get certified in lifeguard, first aid and CPR/AED through the American Red Cross course. 3. Apply for the position online at GwinnettCountyJobs.com.
notes: Course costs are not listed, so ask. Email Lifeguard@GwinnettCounty.com or call 770.822.8000. The page does not mention work permits. The season is listed as part-time seasonal, with no months given.
duration: Part-time seasonal jobs at the county's year-round aquatic centers and seasonal pools. Dates are not listed.
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay is not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: The page and form do not list an age. The form asks for your school, grade and a parent or guardian signature, and asks about teen leadership training. Accepted aides must pass a background check and fingerprinting.
how_to_apply: Download the Summer Camp Aide Volunteer Application from the Day Camps page. Fill it out with a parent or guardian. Email it to CommunityServices@GwinnettCounty.com or Parks@GwinnettCounty.com, or drop it off at the camp site you want. Use a separate form for each camp site.
notes: Day camps are for children ages 5 to 13. The minimum age for aides is not stated, so call 770.822.8000 to check. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: Minimum of two weeks, picked from camp weeks between late May and July 31
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. $21 for two required camp t-shirts, paid after you are accepted.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who have finished 8th grade and have a clean record. Open to youth interested in law enforcement.
how_to_apply: Pay the sign-up fee and do an interview. Contact the Community Affairs Section to start.
notes: Sponsored by Learning for Life. Contact Cpl. Juan Reyes at 678.442.6520 or PDCommunityAffairs@GwinnettCounty.com. Community Affairs Section: 3125 Satellite Boulevard, Duluth, GA 30096. The page has no Explorer page of its own. Details come from the outreach programs page.
duration: Three Mondays a month, 6:30 to 9:00 pm, at the Police Training Center in Lawrenceville
pay_detail: One-time registration fee of $61. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students who will attend a Gwinnett high school the next school year. No ages or grades are listed. You must get yourself to the Gwinnett Justice and Administration Center in Lawrenceville and other program sites.
how_to_apply: There is an Application link on the page. The page does not describe the steps.
notes: The page does not list exact dates, ages or the application steps. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: Friday afternoons over the summer
pay_detail: Free to students

who_can_apply: The county page and flyer say the program is open to high school, undergraduate and graduate students. No ages or grade rules are listed in what was read.
how_to_apply: Find the listings and apply at VolunteerGwinnett.net. You can also call 770.822.7955. Or write to VolunteerGwinnett@GwinnettCounty.com.
notes: The VolunteerGwinnett.net listings page would not open because of a certificate error. So the open jobs, ages and hours were not read. Ask about the minimum age before you apply. The county page names Muriam Nafees as the contact for volunteer internships.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer internship. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Age 16 and up for construction sites, even with a parent or guardian. Ages 16 to 18 bring a signed minor waiver. Age 15 and under can help with fundraising, flyers or lunch for site volunteers.
how_to_apply: The page gives no online sign-up link; there is usually a volunteer kiosk on site. Call 866-450-4432 or email Volunteer@HabitatEBSV.org. Groups of 5 or more use the group pages.
notes: Hands-on building experience for age 16 and up. Specific build sites were not listed on the page; ask which are near you.
pay_detail: No volunteer fee mentioned on the page

who_can_apply: At least 16 to volunteer on a job site. The page lists no age minimum for the ReStore and no special rules for 16 and 17 year olds. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Make a VolunteerHub account (sachabitat.volunteerhub.com), register for and attend a one hour HabiTour orientation, then sign up for shifts. Email volunteers@habitatgreatersac.org or call (916) 440-1215.
notes: Ask whether under-18 volunteers need a parent signature or waiver, since the page does not say. Group volunteering contact: gcabral@habitatgreatersac.org. Office: 819 North 10th St, Sacramento.
duration: Shifts Tue to Sat (times not listed)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Free forever for teenagers.
how_to_apply: Join through hackclub.com and find or start a club.
notes: Free for teens. The page lists about 1,500 clubs and events such as game jams and a hardware hackathon in San Francisco.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Open to everyone. The page does not state an age limit. In 2026, pull requests no longer count toward rewards.
how_to_apply: Sign in on hacktoberfest.com with MyMLH, or register for a local fest.
notes: The page states no age limit; check each local fest for age rules. Pull requests no longer count toward rewards in 2026. Earn three stickers to get a sticker pack by mail, and you must sign in with MyMLH and give an address.
duration: All of October 2026
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older and currently in grades 10 to 12. Needs a physician form, reference forms and a free urine drug screen.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form and do a short interview. Then finish a longer application. It needs a counselor reference, a personal reference, a doctor form and a drug test. Then do the online and in-person orientation.
notes: Full attendance is expected without exception. Phones are not allowed on shifts. Parents cannot send the application for the teen.
duration: 7 weeks, July 6 to Aug 21 in 2026. Two 4-hour shifts a week.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Monthly projects: filter the calendar by age to see which are open to you. HandsOn Tomorrow and the Youth Volunteer Council are for Bay Area high school students; the Council requires finishing HandsOn Tomorrow first.
how_to_apply: Use the Community Calendar at handsonbayarea.org/calendar and filter by age. Email info@handsonbayarea.org or call 415-541-9616.
notes: HandsOn Tomorrow, a 2-week summer program (up to 40 hours), will not be running in summer 2026. The page does not say when it returns and does not use the word paused. The Youth Volunteer Council needs HandsOn Tomorrow first, so for now the monthly calendar projects are the way in. Age limits vary by project.
duration: Monthly projects; HandsOn Tomorrow was 2 weeks
pay_detail: No cost or pay stated on the pages

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Animal handling, public speaking or working-with-children experience helps. It is not required.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application, write a 1-page cover letter about your interests and goals, and send both by mail, email, fax or in person to 1300 Senter Road, San Jose. Selected applicants interview. Phone (408) 794-6425.
notes: Minimum 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month). Not everyone is picked, but you can reapply the next season.
duration: At least 48 hours a year (about 4 hours a month)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 at the start of camp (June 15 in 2026). Must commit three days a week for at least five weeks. Needs three PA clearances (state police record, child abuse history, FBI fingerprint) and a CPR class.
how_to_apply: Send a Letter of Interest to the Program Manager by March 15. Then get the three clearances and a CPR card. Then go to staff orientation.
notes: Only one spot per camp. Dates are for the 2026 season, so check the page in early 2027.
duration: 3 days a week for 5 to 8 weeks of summer camp
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid. Community service hours.

who_can_apply: The page says ambitious high school students, including rising juniors, may enroll. No age range or grade rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page of the Summer Session site. You send a registration application with a transcript and pay fees before the course starts.
notes: Costs money and the courses are college level. Check the site in winter for 2027 dates and prices.
duration: 2026 Session I began May 26 and Session II began June 15
pay_detail: Tuition is $4,250 per 3-credit course and $5,000 per 4-credit course (2026 prices). Financial aid on the page is only for Harvey Mudd students.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 19. On Oahu, fill out the Oahu County 4-H Interest Form to join a club or program.
how_to_apply: On Oahu, fill out the Oahu County 4-H Interest Form. On other islands, use the Contact page on the Hawaii 4-H site to find your county program. Email Christine at chanakaw@hawaii.edu with Oahu questions.
notes: About 4,000 youth take part each year across the state. Meetings can be in homes, schools or community buildings. Oahu also lists day camps, shooting sports and a garden center program.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students in Hawaii public schools (HIDOE). The program page does not state grades or ages. It covers 13 career and technical education pathways statewide.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Call the HIDOE main line at 808-784-6200 or ask your school.
notes: Act 251 (2025) gave $1.8 million for fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27. The state pays companies back for the time they spend training and supervising interns. No program contact is listed besides the main HIDOE phone line.
duration: 4 to 6 weeks in summer 2026 (6 weeks at 24 hours a week at the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum; 4 weeks at 32 hours a week at Aloun Farms)
pay_detail: $20 minimum hourly wage

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16. Summer 2026 was for high school sophomores (Class of 2028), juniors (Class of 2027), or students in a Community School for Adults. A program of study that fits the internship is preferred.
how_to_apply: Download the Student Intern Casual Employment Application and fill it out. Email it to the contact for the internship you want, or drop off a paper copy. High school internships are only for students at that school.
notes: The positions list is a separate sheet linked from the program page.
duration: Dates and hours vary by internship. Summer 2026 ran June to July.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Most positions need participants to be 17 to 38 for the whole term. A small number of positions have no upper age limit. You must be allowed to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Apply link on the Kupu Aina Corps page. Look at the host sites you can pick.
notes: Most positions take ages 17 to 38 for the whole term. Jobs are on Hawaii Island, Kauai, Maui, Molokai and Oahu. The older HYCC Summer program (17 and up) is paused. Kupu also runs the Conservation Leadership Development Program. Hawaii requires a child labor certificate (work permit) for working minors under 18. It is free. It is a Certificate of Employment for 14 and 15, and a Certificate of Age for 16 and 17.
duration: 6 or 12 month terms, part-time (20 hours a week) or full-time (40 hours a week)
pay_detail: $20 an hour, plus health insurance for 20+ hours a week, a retention bonus ($200 to $800) and paid time off.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors in good academic standing. The program page gives no age rule.
how_to_apply: Send an application, a resume, a news-style writing sample and one recommendation letter. You can apply online through the link on the page, or mail or email the materials. Phone: 808-586-9490.
notes: This is one lawmaker's office. The page does not say if you must live in her district. The email link on the page may point to the wrong address, so use the phone number to confirm.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The program page says these are non-paid positions.

who_can_apply: Hawaii students at public, private, charter or homeschool. You need a GPA of 2.5 or better and email access. Students in their last year of school get strong preference.
how_to_apply: Check the program page in spring 2027 for the new application. Questions: HighSchool_Internship@schatz.senate.gov or the Hawaii office at 808-523-2061.
notes: Interns are picked for work in the community and a mix of interests. You do not need student government experience. This program is virtual.
duration: Late September through April. You must commit to the full term.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated for the high school internship on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students at a participating Hawaii public high school. Each high school decides which classes it offers, so ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Meet with your high school counselor first. Then fill out the UH System application and the online Dual Credit Application. Get the signatures, and send both to the UH campus by its deadline.
notes: The program page says 53 public high schools offered Early College in the 2023 to 2024 school year. Classes are face to face, online or mixed. Classes at the 100 level and above earn college credit.
duration: Classes run during the school year
pay_detail: Free to students at Hawaii public schools in the program, thanks to state funding. You are not paid.

who_can_apply: Students at a Hawaii public or charter high school who meet the college campus admission rules and are under 21 on September 1 of the school year. UH Manoa does not take part in Running Start.
how_to_apply: Meet with your high school counselor first. Then fill out the UH System application and the online Dual Credit Application. Get the signatures, and send both to the UH campus by its deadline.
notes: Nine UH campuses take part. You must also pass the placement tests the campus asks for. Private school students may be able to use an Early Admit program instead. Ask the UH campus.
duration: One college class per term in fall, spring or summer
pay_detail: Varies. Student or family, the high school, or a scholarship may pay. A GEAR UP scholarship for students with low family income covers tuition, fees and books for one class, but the page says it will not be offered after the Summer 2026 term.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. The program page has no separate teen track.
how_to_apply: Email the education office or call the museum and ask to volunteer. You log your hours online after you start.
notes: The program page does not describe orientation, training or required hours. Phone: 510-581-0223, extension 161. The internships on the same page are for college and graduate students, not high school.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not list pay or service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Some jobs have their own age rules, listed on each opportunity. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the volunteer agreement.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile, then register for a one-time event or submit an interest form for a service project. Service projects need a background check and TB risk assessment before starting.
notes: This page lists many volunteer roles, not one program, so each role's own age rule applies. Verification of service hours is emailed on request. Volunteers with court orders should follow the district process (info@haywardrec.org).
duration: One-time events, or service projects that run 6 months or longer.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Library service hours cannot be used for community service required by a judge or court.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY TO VOLUNTEER online interest form linked from the library page. Questions go to hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page says the roles are subject to change, so check the online interest form for current openings. The Just for Teens page describes its events for grades 9-12, while the volunteer page says ages 13-17; the volunteer page is the one used here. An older 2023 city notice describes a monthly Teen Advisory Group meeting (1st Wednesday, Downtown Library, ages 13-17, no commitment). That notice was not re-checked for 2026, so ask hpl.teens@hayward-ca.gov whether it still meets.
duration: Flexible. Volunteers sign up for 1-hour shifts.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 20 who live in the City of Hayward or within the Hayward Unified School District boundaries. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Get the application and the Parent Agreement and Contact Information form from the City of Hayward website, or call the City Clerk at (510) 583-4400, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays. Applicants are interviewed by a panel.
notes: The official Youth Commission page returned 404. The newest notice read is from April 2025. The 2021 notice said meetings were on the first and third Mondays, so the meeting schedule may have changed. Confirm the 2026 cycle with the City Clerk before applying.
duration: Meetings at Hayward City Hall, September to June (meeting day not confirmed; the 2021 notice said first and third Mondays). The 2021 notice said two-year terms.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Download the Teen Volunteer Application (PDF on the page), fill it out and return it to the Customer Service desk at one of the four libraries. Questions: (702) 707-2665.
notes: Henderson is next to Las Vegas. Expect a wait at some branches. Ask about parent consent and hours.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. The page says interns are ages 16 to 18 in one place and 16 to 19 in another.
how_to_apply: Watch Hennepin County job listings (sign up for email notifications from the page). Libraries hiring interns: Brookdale, Brooklyn Park, Franklin, Hosmer, North Regional, Roosevelt, and Cedar Riverside Opportunity Center.
notes: Training includes hands-on learning, group reflection and an adult mentor. Hiring dates and pay are not on the page. Confirm with the library before relying on it.
duration: Year-round (summer and school year), about 6 hours a week after school and weekends
pay_detail: Described as a hired position; the pay rate is not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Only a limited number of teen volunteer spots exist at some libraries.
how_to_apply: Ask your local Hennepin County library about teen openings. If there is one, fill out the teen volunteer application (PDF). Bring it to the library. A staff member will contact you. Questions: Volunteer Services, 612-543-8633.
notes: Adult volunteers have a different process. The phone line is staffed Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who can work on their own and keep a weekly schedule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeen application (a PDF on the page). Go to the orientation meeting, which is required. Ask your local library for details.
notes: The plan differs by library branch.
duration: Weekly schedule; varies by library
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Black male students entering grades 9, 10 or 11. No coding experience needed. Must commit to the full 15 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Immersion Program page on hiddengeniusproject.org.
notes: The apply page says OUR 2027 APPLICATION IS NOW OPEN and lists no closing date. The immersion page still shows the old Feb 21, 2025 deadline. The immersion page lists Oakland and Richmond among its sites.
duration: 15 months
pay_detail: Free to join; no stipend listed

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors enrolled full time in high school for the program year. The group has 15 members.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application during the Feb 1 to Mar 1 window. Questions: HMATeenPrograms@high.org.
notes: No absences are allowed during the summer intensive. The High's Teens and College page also lists an Early College Program in Art History and Curatorial Studies with the Atlanta University Center for rising juniors and seniors, but it gave no dates or application details.
duration: One-year commitment, including a 6-week summer intensive (June 3 to July 17 in 2026), Wednesday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., plus regular meetings
pay_detail: Described as a paid position; the amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Application, interview, orientation and hands-on training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Flight Teen application online, then expect a call to schedule an interview, attend volunteer orientation, and train with an active volunteer.
notes: Year-round, ongoing applications. Weekend shifts only. Interview timing and training length are not stated.
duration: Alternating Saturdays or Sundays (1st and 3rd, or 2nd and 4th), plus an extra shift on a 5th weekend some months
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24. Many of the youth in the farm programs come from Latino and Latine backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Check the Hiring page in late January 2027 and sign up for the farm newsletter to hear about postings.
notes: The page does not give the season dates or pay. Confirm both when applications open.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Youth earn income. The hourly rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 living in the City of Los Angeles. The checklist PDF (2024 version) lists the other rules on who can join. Check the current one.
how_to_apply: Create an application on the Hire LA site, then bring or upload proof of age, right-to-work (I-9) documents, City of LA residency and the family income form.
notes: Cycle dates are not confirmed, so check with EWDD before you count on a summer 2027 spot. The home page Youth section says ages 14 to 30. That does not match the 14 to 24 overview used here, so check the current age range. The same city department runs 14 free YouthSource Centers for ages 14 to 24. They offer school help, job readiness and some paid internships. Ask at your nearest center, for example Boyle Heights 323-526-5800 or South LA 323-903-6926. Under 18 you need a California work permit. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps. Checked 2026-10-10: the home page still says "Accepting Applications for" with no year or dates, so left unconfirmed.
duration: Varies. Student to Student Success is up to 140 hours in one school semester (20 hours of training, up to 120 hours of service).
pay_detail: Paid. The home page does not state an hourly rate.

who_can_apply: Local students ages 16 to 18. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: The page lists no application or interest form for this program. Call the Volunteer Office to ask when interest will be taken again.
notes: Not offered: summer, short-term, hands-on patient care, shadowing or observation. Volunteer Office phones: Newport Beach (949) 764-8264, Irvine (949) 517-3152. The page does not state the weekly hours.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. You need 2 letters of recommendation, a negative TB test and a TB screening each year. You also go to new volunteer orientation and training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Zoo Corps application on the zoo volunteer page. A Zoo Corps description PDF is linked there.
notes: The zoo site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. Confirm the dates with the zoo volunteer office.
duration: Summer season, June to August. At least one day a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee is listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 16. High school students use a separate application and must attend an in-person orientation. Needs a health screening (MMR, varicella, flu, TB testing) and availability to start within one month of applying.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form for high school students from the Holy Cross volunteer applications page, then complete a screening interview and orientation.
notes: Another site named holy-cross.com is Holy Cross in Fort Lauderdale, Florida; use holycrosshealth.org for Maryland. Background checks are required for volunteers 18 and older. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: Not stated on the main page
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. The online form also asks you to say you are over 18, so ask the group which rule applies to a 16 or 17 year old.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form, or print the PDF form and mail it in. Then go to an orientation. Questions: admin@friendsofthelibraryofhawaii.org.
notes: This is the Friends group, not the state library system. The state library page says to contact your local branch to ask how you might participate.
duration: Not stated. Commitments can be once a day, once a week, or as often as you can come.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Warehouse minimum age is 8. Anyone 15 or younger must come with an adult age 18 or older. Some distribution sites require 13 or 14 as the minimum age. Groups of three or more can apply.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the volunteer page for warehouse shifts. Or email volunteer@hawaiifoodbank.org to save a spot for a Saturday packing.
notes: The warehouse is at 2611 Kilihau St., Honolulu. All new warehouse volunteers must go to orientation. The page lists a minimum age of 13 or 14 for some sites where food is given out.
duration: Warehouse shifts Monday to Friday except holidays and the second Thursday afternoon of each month, plus Saturday packings. Shift length not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. High school students (16 to 17) must commit to a regular weekly schedule for three months and complete onboarding health requirements.
how_to_apply: Download the High school form (Oahu and Kauai) from the Hawaii Pacific Health volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer Services. The page lists it in its volunteer section.
notes: Summer student applications close in early April and the page does not give a year. Other application windows are not stated on the page, so check back.
duration: 3 months for high school students, one weekly 4-hour shift (or two 2-hour shifts). Summer volunteers commit two months.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17. Check each role in the Opportunities Directory for its age rule. Teens who cannot give a weekly shift for three months go through the Youth and Education Department instead.
how_to_apply: Pick a role in the Opportunities Directory. Finish the Junior Volunteer Application Process. It has a $15 Junior Volunteer Application Fee. Training has a 2 to 3 hour in person class and shadow shifts. You also take online courses that can take about 5 to 6 hours.
notes: The page does not state an application window or year. It says to check back and apply at a later time. Youth who want service hours can go through the Youth and Education Department.
duration: The page asks for a weekly shift for three months. Some roles need a teen to volunteer with an adult. Check each role for its time commitment.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $15 Junior Volunteer Application Fee.

who_can_apply: Students. The page does not state ages or grades; check the application. Members serve a one-year term, volunteer at events and attend quarterly meetings.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teens4Animals Council form when it opens.
notes: Members attend quarterly meetings and field trips on topics such as responsible fishing and ethical farming. The page does not state an age or grade rule.
duration: One-year term (2026-2027), with 4-day summer training and quarterly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid. The 4-day training fee is waived for council members.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register for classes through the link on the program page.
notes: Classes and grades appear on your college transcript and can transfer to other colleges. The web address says hpu-500 but the page is titled HPU 600 and lists $600.
duration: Fall 2026 terms: 8 weeks or 16 weeks
pay_detail: $600 per class

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 who lack support. The page lists who can get paid on the job training and help with job school costs. Check the Apply Here link for the full list of rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the Kupu Community Program page.
notes: It is based at the Hookupu Center in Kewalo Basin Harbor, Honolulu. It works with Honolulu District public schools and McKinley School for Adults. They help with the diploma and with HiSET or GED tests.
duration: Year-long program
pay_detail: Not stated as a wage. The page lists eligibility for paid on-the-job training placements and/or financial help with vocational training.

who_can_apply: Hawaii residents who are 16 by the start, have finished sophomore year, and are full-time high school students. Students from any island can apply but must pay for their own housing and travel.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application. Email it with your unofficial transcript, one letter of recommendation and an essay of 500 to 700 words. Send it to ltgov.internships@hawaii.gov. Some students are then interviewed.
notes: Very small group: the page says six students are picked. The page and form differ on the start date (June 15 or June 16), and its FAQ still shows some 2025 dates, so confirm with the office.
duration: 5 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9am to noon
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not provided.

who_can_apply: The application has a box for high school students and a parent or guardian consent part. The program page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. High school students check the high school box. A parent or guardian signs the consent part. Expect a short interview and a background check.
notes: The museum matches volunteers to openings, so you may wait to hear back. Teen roles are not described on the main program page. The older application form is what shows the high school box, the parent consent part, the background check and the interview.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students now in high school or the same level. Rising seniors get first pick. Your application is checked through the OHA Hawaiian Registry Program. A parent or guardian fills it out with you.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the online application. You write short answers and an essay, and a teacher, counselor, mentor or boss fills out a recommender form. New applicants also finish the Hawaiian Registry Program application. Call (808) 594-1835 for help.
notes: The program page does not spell out an ancestry rule, but it uses the Hawaiian Registry Program to verify applicants. Ask OHA if you are not sure you qualify. You get yourself to the airport.
duration: Six days, overnight. The 2026 program ran June 21 to 26.
pay_detail: Free for chosen students. OHA pays interisland airfare, lodging, meals and program travel. You are not paid.

who_can_apply: Junior Leaders must be 13 before August 1 and no older than 17 by the camp end date (2026: July 24).
how_to_apply: Contact your local Summer Fun site (see the Summer Fun site map). Sign up as a Junior Leader.
notes: The page does not say whether junior leaders are paid or whether their hours count as volunteer service. Ask the site.
duration: 2026 program ran June 8 to July 24
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page. Paid summer aide jobs are listed separately (see the Summer Swim Aide card).

who_can_apply: Open to applicants as young as 16. You need a valid American Red Cross Lifeguard Training, First Aid and CPR/AED for the Professional Rescuer certificate. You also need work with children and teens.
how_to_apply: Apply through the online application link on the Summer Fun Jobs page.
notes: Work sites: 21 pools and 3 ocean recreation sites. Hawaii requires a child labor certificate (work permit) for working minors under 18. It is free. It is a Certificate of Employment for 14 and 15, and a Certificate of Age for 16 and 17.
duration: Seasonal full-time or part-time. The page does not give start or end dates.
pay_detail: $19.23 an hour

who_can_apply: Teens 15 to 17 need parent permission and a shot record for MMR and varicella. All volunteers commit to at least 100 hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteers form (or the High School Summer Student Program form) linked on the Queen's volunteer page. Or call Volunteer Services (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm).
notes: The page lists Teen Volunteer forms for 3 sites. They are Queen's Medical Center, Queen's West O'ahu and Queen's North Hawai'i Community Hospital. The page does not say if applications are open now.
duration: At least 100 hours; summer student program also offered
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 with a 2.8 or higher GPA, at a Hawaii high school that offers a UH Manoa course. A 2.8 GPA is a minimum and does not guarantee a spot.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school college counselor first. The program page sends you to its How to Apply page for the steps.
notes: Your high school must offer a UH Manoa course. The college work is hard, and past grades in college classes may be looked at. This program was called Manoa Academy before.
duration: One college course per term
pay_detail: The program page says there are no tuition or fee costs to students. You are not paid.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 and recent graduates. 24 spots.
how_to_apply: Use the application form on the Outreach College program page. Contact summer.programs@hawaii.edu or 808-956-9246.
notes: The cost is lower for Hawaii residents. Programs on Coconut Island run if the weather allows.
duration: One week (2026: June 1 to 5), with a boat from Heeia Kea Boat Harbor to Coconut Island each day, weather permitting
pay_detail: $750 for Hawaii residents, $1,500 for non-residents (2026).

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12. The page lists the program as a week-long summer program for students interested in health professions.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the Outreach College program page when the next application opens. Contact Noelani Ching, nching@hawaii.edu, 808-692-0948.
notes: The two pages show different prices. Confirm the cost when applications open.
duration: One week (2026: July 6 to 10)
pay_detail: $575 on the program page (Kamaaina discount of $50). The high school summary page lists $525 for Hawaii residents and $575 for non-residents.

who_can_apply: Students who will have finished their sophomore or junior year. You need a 3.5 GPA, the maturity for college work and approval from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Apply to the Summer Scholar Program. Once you are in, sign up for UH Manoa summer classes. Contact sscholar@hawaii.edu or 808-956-9246.
notes: No on-campus housing. Courses can be cancelled for low enrollment.
duration: Courses in sessions: May 26 to July 2, July 6 to Aug 14, or June 15 to July 24 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Student pays tuition, fees and materials at UH Manoa resident undergraduate rates. A $1,200 need-based scholarship is available to Hawaii students who get free or reduced-price meals or school financial aid (first come, first served).

who_can_apply: High school students. The aquarium says regular volunteers must be 18, with exceptions for teen programs.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the aquarium volunteer page when it is time. If you have a question, send an email to volunteer@waikikiaquarium.org.
notes: The page does not state the exact age range or application dates. The aquarium is open during repairs. Other aquarium volunteer roles are for 18 and older.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for 5 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The program page does not give other rules.
how_to_apply: Send your name through the interest form on the program page. If cost is a worry, use the Financial Assistance link on that page.
notes: Contact aball@ymcahonolulu.org. You can also use yaghawaii@ymcahonolulu.org. The page lists no cost or dates. Ask before you plan.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Need based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 at the time of appointment. If you are under 18, you need a parent or guardian's permission.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Honolulu Youth Commission application page. It reopens in 2027. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Seats are chosen by the Mayor or by City Council members. An earlier call for applicants in July 2026 gave a July 22 deadline. Expect a similar time next year, but this is not confirmed.
duration: One or two year term, depending on who appoints you
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 16 who can volunteer at least one full week of Zoo Camp.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application. Upload a signed Waiver of Liability and a current photo. Then set up an interview. It can be in person or on Zoom. Training is the general volunteer orientation and a zoo safety class.
notes: Regular zoo volunteer roles are 18 and older; this is the teen exception. Check the page for the current camp schedule.
duration: At least one full Zoo Camp week (Mon to Fri, 8:00 am to 2:30 pm, with extended hours to 5:30 pm). Camps run in spring, summer, fall and winter.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students in health science or biomedical science programs, or interested in health careers. Join through a school chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your health science teacher for the chapter advisor.
notes: HOSA reports over 200,000 members in 51 chartered associations. California chapter rules, dues and middle school eligibility were not on the page.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues were not stated on the page. Ask your advisor.

who_can_apply: On-site animal care volunteers must be 18 or older. Students under 18 can foster with a parent or guardian's support or make fleece blankets.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@hssv.org or see the student opportunities page for fostering and blanket instructions.
notes: No hands-on shelter work until 18. Service hours: 2 fleece blankets = 1 hour (0.5 hour each); fostering is counted by care time. Email for a service hour verification letter.
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated. HSSV provides foster supplies.

who_can_apply: Restoration days are for ages 8 to adult. Kids under 14 need an adult with them. Age rules for long-term volunteer roles are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Come to a restoration day (wear closed-toe shoes and bring water) or sign up for the monthly volunteer training. A waiver form is on the volunteer page. Contact Kenny at 714-846-1114.
notes: The Conservancy internships are unpaid. They need a related degree or college enrollment, so they are not for high schoolers.
duration: Restoration events are the last Saturday of each month, 9 a.m. to noon. Long-term volunteers start with a monthly 3 hour training.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Most roles are ages 13 to 17 (18-year-olds still in high school can also join). Teen Tech Volunteer is ages 15 to 17, Chess Club Volunteer is ages 15 to 18 in high school, and Helen Murphy toy cleaning is 13 and up. D&D Club volunteers must have attended a club meeting in the past six months.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the role you want (several library roles share one application link, so check which one). Seats for club roles are first-come, first-served, and staff email next steps. The Main Street Branch also accepts a printed teen application dropped off at the branch.
notes: Contact: Teen Services Librarian Katelyn Wong (Katelyn.Wong@surfcity-hb.org) or the library at 714-842-4481. The page also lists other Huntington Beach volunteer groups for teens, with their own age rules. They are Bolsa Chica Conservancy, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Shipley Nature Center and OC Coastkeeper cleanups. Some entries on the page look copy-pasted, so confirm details with staff.
duration: Varies by role: weekly or monthly sessions of 1 to 3 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sessions earn 1 to 3 volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: You must be 17 years old by July 1 of the year you are hired, with proof. You must pass a 1,000-yard pool swim in under 15 minutes and an 1,800-yard ocean run-swim-run.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city job site before the exam. Pass the exam and go to an interview. The best scorers join the paid training academy.
notes: A 16-year-old can apply only if they were a Huntington Beach Junior Guard last summer. Marine Safety must also back them. New hires get a uniform, fins, sunglasses and a beach parking pass. Check the city job board for the 2027 posting. Paid work under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.
duration: Seasonal, as-needed work with weekends and holidays
pay_detail: $22.50 to $27.50 an hour in the 2026 posting. Lifeguards are paid during the academy.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 20. The page also says the maximum age to apply is 19. Ask the department which age applies to you. You must be in high school or a graduate. Keep a 2.0 GPA. Pass a medical exam and a background check. You cannot have a felony conviction.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form. An advisor emails you. Go to an information meeting. Turn in the application and a Hold Harmless form. Pass a medical exam. Then take an agility test, an oral interview and a background check.
notes: The agility test has a 1-mile run, sit-ups, push-ups and a flex arm hang. The city also runs a Fire Explorer program.
duration: Monthly training on the 2nd and 4th Thursday of each month. Volunteer at least 4 hours a month.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. These are HB Union High School District students. They also include Huntington Beach residents who go to private school or are homeschooled.
how_to_apply: The page says applications are now available. It links the word Applications to its Notice of Vacancies page. No deadline is listed. For questions, contact the city staff liaison, Molly Uemura. She is at the Community and Library Services Department. The email is on the page.
notes: Application dates and the form are not on the page. Confirm with the city first.
duration: 1 year term, from the start of the school year to May. Members can reapply until graduation.
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a volunteer board

who_can_apply: High school students in Utah, Nevada, Montana, Idaho or Wyoming. You must be a rising sophomore or junior. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens.
notes: You must attend all 40 hours. A lab kit is mailed to your home. Contact: Monica Salas Jimenez, Monica.Salas@hci.utah.edu, 801-587-7885.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 12:30 PM Mountain time (2026: July 6 to 17)
pay_detail: Up to $500

who_can_apply: High school students in Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Utah or Wyoming who finished at least freshman year. Rural students are very welcome. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens. Parent consent is required.
notes: It is online only. The program manager is Jill Christian. Her email is Jill.Christian@hci.utah.edu.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 AM to noon Mountain time (2026: July 13 to 16 and 20 to 23)
pay_detail: Up to $400

who_can_apply: The program page does not list eligibility rules. It says the program aims to reach young learners, including students from rural and frontier areas of the Mountain West. Check the application for the full rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Online Application link on the page. The program manager is Liz Morales. Her email is liz.morales@hci.utah.edu and her phone is 801-581-3088.
notes: Accepted students who finish are accepted back the next summer. High school students should check that they count as advanced seniors.
duration: 10 weeks, 40 hours a week (2026: May 25 to July 30)
pay_detail: Up to $4,000 for 10 weeks (depends on education level). Housing and meals are paid for out-of-state students. Travel help for students outside Salt Lake City.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 10 who are enrolled in 4-H and in the Know Your Government project this year. You can attend as a delegate two years.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H and the Know Your Government project, then register online when it opens in December. Questions: Mike Knutz, mknutz@uidaho.edu.
notes: The event page says grades 8 to 10. Ask your county 4-H office to confirm.
duration: Weekend (2027: February 13 to 15)
pay_detail: 2026 delegate fee was $230. Bus transportation to Boise is provided; steering committee members and chaperones can get up to $75 in help.

who_can_apply: Youth who have completed 8th through 12th grade. Both 4-H and non-4-H members can come. Adult chaperones must be certified.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say how to sign up. Email fourh@uidaho.edu or call 208-885-6321 to ask.
notes: Not stated on the program page: the exact location and a closing date. Plan to sign up by mid May, because prices go up on May 16. Teens do not have to be in 4-H.
duration: 4 days
pay_detail: 4-H members pay $335 if they sign up April 10 to May 15, or $395 May 16 to May 31. Non-4-H members pay $390 or $435. Price includes lodging, meals and transportation.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 by May 31 and no older than 17 during the program. First-time applicants need a letter of recommendation (not from a family member) and an interview.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application. If this is your first time, you also upload a letter of recommendation. Then you go to the zoo for an interview. If you have questions, email zooeducation@idahofallszoo.org.
notes: The 2026 sessions started June 9, June 30 and July 21. Fees cannot be refunded.
duration: 3-week sessions, three days a week, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Registration fee of $90 per 3-week session ($72 for Tautphaus Park Zoological Society members), nonrefundable. You get a uniform shirt and zoo admission during your session.

who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 8 and up. Volunteers 15 and younger must be with an adult volunteer. Each person makes their own account.
how_to_apply: Make an account and book a shift in the VolunteerHub system. Wear closed-toe, closed-heel shoes. Download the minor waiver if you are under 18.
notes: The warehouse is not heated or cooled, so wear layers. Groups of more than 18 use the group request form.
duration: Shifts are booked in advance (length not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 16. Teachers can also attend.
how_to_apply: Mail three things to the camp director at the University of Idaho in Moscow. Send a signed application, the health and medical release form, and the fee. If cost is a problem, ask about scholarships first.
notes: The camp is at the Central Idaho 4-H Camp north of Ketchum. Parents must drive campers to and from camp. The program page lists no closing date other than the May 20 payment date. Scholarship contact is Randy Brooks at 208-885-6356.
duration: 6 days (June 15 to 20 in 2026)
pay_detail: $310 for students. It covers food, lodging and medical insurance. Rides to camp are not included. Scholarships are offered through local Idaho Soil Conservation Districts.

who_can_apply: High school juniors. Other rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the 2026-2027 ISAS application online. If you are not a junior yet, join the email list on the program page. Questions: isas@sde.idaho.gov.
notes: The program is competitive. Summer academy dates and cost are not stated on the program page. Program contact is Erin Lanigan at 208-885-1232.
duration: Online course during the school year. Summer academy is one week for chosen students.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Students may earn one science credit.

who_can_apply: The program is titled a high school internship. Age or grade rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected students then have a group interview. It is at the Idaho State Museum. Questions? Email shseducation@ishs.idaho.gov. Or call (208) 334-2120.
notes: Pay and dates shown are from the 2025 to 2026 program details on the page; the 2026 to 2027 dates may differ. The page has an interest form for teen programs.
duration: The 2025 to 2026 run was November 4, 2025 to June 16, 2026, with Tuesday meetings from 4 to 7 p.m. and at least 3 volunteer shifts
pay_detail: $500 stipend paid in two parts (December and June), as listed for the 2025 to 2026 program.

who_can_apply: Your school has to offer the class. The program pages do not say which grades can join or how students are picked.
how_to_apply: Check the schools list on ijag.org to see if your school offers iJAG. Questions: (515) 216-3140 or info@ijag.org.
notes: iJAG is not a job or internship by itself. It is a class that connects students to employers. Whether your school has it depends on your district.
duration: A semester-based elective class.
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the program pages.
