who_can_apply: Enrolled 4-H members ages 14 to 18 as of September 1 of the 4-H year, with strong visual or performing arts skills.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page. Contact Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Must attend at least 75 percent of the monthly Zoom calls.
duration: One-year term; Zoom meetings the last Tuesday of each month
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 13 or older, enrolled in or past their first year of high school, with some community service. Needs a reference from an Extension staff member, school staff member or youth worker.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Illinois 4-H Ambassador Application (the Apply for the Illinois 4-H Food Advocacy Team button, which opens form.jotform.com) and get a reference. Questions: Mark Becker, mbbecker@illinois.edu.
notes: Cost to attend in-person meetings is not stated.
duration: One Zoom meeting a month (Sunday, 7 pm) and 1 to 2 in-person meetings a year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 when applying. Must be committed to 4-H values and passionate about healthy living.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page. Contact Illinois 4-H at Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Members must attend at least one day of the Illinois State Fair. Whether you must be a 4-H member is not stated.
duration: Virtual meeting once a month for 1 to 2 hours, plus a 1 to 2 day retreat each year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 as of September 1 of the application year.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the page (an application tip sheet is linked). Contact Illinois4H@illinois.edu or 217-333-0910.
notes: Whether you must be a 4-H member is not stated on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings (recording available)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: 4-H members who are at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the page for the next training.
notes: Teens must attend one training to be on the state roster and join a spring update call to stay on it.
duration: 6-hour training, offered about three times a year; a spring update call each year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 join a 4-H Club. Your age on September 1, the start of the 4-H year, decides how you join. Teen teams: Creative Collective Art Ambassadors is ages 14 to 18, and Illinois 4-H Influencers is for high school age youth. Other teams do not list ages on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the Join 4-H page with a parent or guardian. Your local Extension office then contacts you with next steps to register. Returning members renew in Zsuite.
notes: This is club membership and volunteer leadership, not a paid job. Cost, grades and teen team application steps are not stated on the pages. Call Illinois 4-H at (217) 333-0910 or email Illinois4H@illinois.edu.
duration: 4-H year starts September 1. Teen team terms are about one year (stated for the Art Ambassadors).
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the page. Ask your local Extension office.

who_can_apply: Boys who have completed one semester of 11th grade and have at least one semester left after Boys State. Those who finished junior year get preference. A boy may attend only once as a citizen. Many are sponsored by a local American Legion post.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form; your local American Legion post will then contact you. Parents can also register eligible sons. Questions: info@illinoisboysstate.org or 309-663-0361.
notes: Boys only. Delegates must stay all week and may not drive or leave campus. The Samsung Scholarship application must be finished before arriving.
duration: Session starts June 12, 2027, at 4:00 PM (90th annual session). The registration page lists no end date.
pay_detail: $400 registration fee covering program, up to 10 scholarship contests, housing and meals. Most delegates are sponsored by a local American Legion post.

who_can_apply: Youth who meet one of these: DCFS has legal guardianship, you aged out of care at 18 or older, or you were adopted or placed with a guardian from care at 16 or older. Use it at any U.S. accredited school, in state or out of state.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Illinois Education and Training Voucher Funds on the Kaleidoscope site. File a FAFSA each year. Finish any forms your school asks for. Questions: DCFS.ETVCoordinator@illinois.gov.
notes: This is for college or training after high school, so it matters most for teens 16 to 18 who are planning ahead. It is money for school, not a job. Ask your caseworker.
pay_detail: Up to $5,000 a year for school costs. Good for five years (in a row or not) or until age 26, whichever comes first, with satisfactory academic progress.

who_can_apply: Youth in DCFS care ages 17 to 20 who work 20 hours a week or 80 hours a month. Youth in job training or an approved apprenticeship can also apply. Older former foster youth have a separate apprenticeship rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out form CFS 449-2. Then email it to the DCFS Office of Education and Transition Services, or fax it to 217-524-2101. Ask your caseworker for help.
notes: Only for youth in DCFS care (or certain former foster youth). Call 312-814-6800 or 217-785-2509 for help. DCFS Advocacy Office: 800-232-3798.
pay_detail: The page says it gives financial services but does not list the amount.

who_can_apply: Members must have an interest in marketing, management, entrepreneurship, hospitality and tourism or finance. A chapter needs a certified local educator as advisor. Grades and ages are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA chapter and advisor. If your school has none, the Illinois DECA site has a Start a Chapter page. Membership runs through the DECA membership portal linked on ildeca.org.
notes: Not a paid job. Dues and conference dates come from the DECA Inc. page for Illinois. The state site ildeca.org did not repeat them. Mailing address on the state site: 2460 Dundee Road, Box 1001, Northbrook, IL 60065.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $17 per member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local fees (not stated).

who_can_apply: Students at a school with an FBLA chapter. The page lists high school, middle level and college chapters. How to join is not explained on the program pages.
how_to_apply: Ask a business teacher about a chapter at your school. The chapters page lists active chapters by region. Use the Contact page on ilfbla.org to ask how to join or start a chapter.
notes: Dues and how to start a chapter are not on the program pages. The national FBLA site blocked automated reading, so national rules were not checked.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school girls who are current juniors. A principal, guidance counselor or home school administrator must certify leadership qualities, good character and U.S. residency. You must secure sponsorship from an American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form (name, school email, counselor name and email, school, hometown), get approval from your school official, find a sponsoring American Legion Auxiliary Unit and attend an orientation. Call 309-663-9366 or email info@alaigs.org.
notes: Girls only. The program is physically active with long walks; the registration page asks you to check with a doctor if you have limits. After the program you share your experience with your sponsoring Unit.
duration: One week, June 20 to 26, 2027
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages checked for this card. Ask the Illinois Girls State office and your local American Legion Auxiliary unit.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th graders who are Illinois residents. You need earlier research experience (a research program, course or science fair). If you do not have it, you must finish an online Research Fundamentals course first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the IMSA page when the portal opens. Questions go to Dr. Anita White at awhite@imsa.edu or 630-907-5949.
notes: Residential students live in IMSA halls and get all meals. Commuters get breakfast and lunch but must drive to the Aurora campus. Topics change each year.
duration: Two weeks. In 2026 the sessions ran June 1 to 12, June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17.
pay_detail: No pay and no program cost are stated. The Research Fundamentals course has a fee that is refunded when you finish the course and program. A need-based scholarship exists for that course.

who_can_apply: Students who are a sophomore, junior or senior at a charter or public high school in Illinois. You must be in that grade during the year you apply.
how_to_apply: Make a Submittable account with a personal email, not a school email. Then send in the online application. Finalists do a video interview. Returning members apply again. They skip the interview.
notes: The ISBE page is marked archived, so watch the page for the next call for applications. Next year's dates are not posted; the June 30 date is from the last cycle.
duration: One school year. Members meet several times a month, online and in person.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Open to volunteers who apply. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Download the Information Booth Volunteer Application PDF from the volunteer page. Call the Special Events Office at 217-782-0777. There is an optional one-hour training workshop.
notes: Ask the Special Events Office if volunteers under 18 are allowed. The page also lists paid seasonal jobs. They are in the grandstand, customer service, grounds and security. It gives no minimum age or pay, so they are not listed here.
duration: 3 to 10 days, 15 hours minimum (2026 fair Aug 13 to 23)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free fair T-shirt, admission and parking

who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and not yet 19. Members under 18 join a cadet or composite squadron, not a senior squadron.
how_to_apply: Find your local squadron with the unit locator or the Illinois Wing units page. Contact the unit to confirm a meeting. You usually go to about three meetings. Then you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. The national page says ages 12 to 18; the Illinois page says at least 12 and not yet 19. Illinois Wing HQ: 630-524-4400 or wa@ilwg.cap.gov.
duration: Weekly meetings all year
pay_detail: Dues and uniform costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask the squadron.

who_can_apply: High school students. Legislative Assistant and Press Team are open to freshmen through seniors. Lobbyist and Attorney are for sophomores to seniors. Legislator is for juniors and seniors. Anyone can be a Clerk-Bailiff.
how_to_apply: Get the registration link from your local Delegation Advisor. A student and a parent or guardian both sign the code of conduct. You pick a preferred role and give your State Senator and State Representative. Contact the state office if you have no delegation.
notes: Not a job. State office: 1315 Butterfield Rd, Suite 218, Downers Grove, IL 60515, (630) 833-9622, ilyag@ilymcayg.org.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
pay_detail: $455 program fee. Your delegation decides how it is collected (full payment, deposit, or register first). Scholarships are available through the registration application.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. No prerequisite courses.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up link on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. To ask about cost and openings, email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: Asynchronous course with weekly office hours. Only the September 2026 cohort is listed for sign-up.
duration: September 28 to December 18, 2026
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list grades for this course. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a need-based scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: IMSA does not provide a mentor or lab space in this course. Students must complete all assignments by the deadlines to earn the certificate and refund.
duration: 2026 session: March 9 to May 29, 2026
pay_detail: $200. Scholarships are based on financial need. Students who get an SRELO mentor and finish the course get the fee reimbursed.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. You must find your own research mentor and lab space if needed. IMSA cannot provide them.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the IMSA High School Online Programs page. Or apply for a scholarship instead. Do not pay if you apply for a scholarship. Email studentenrichment@imsa.edu.
notes: It is a hard program. Daily work is expected and you must meet firm deadlines. Failing three deadlines means removal without a refund. IJAS fair entries must be made as an IMSA RISE student for Region 5. Program is non-credit.
duration: September 7, 2026 to May 31, 2027
pay_detail: $1,200. Scholarships based on financial need (free or reduced lunch or SNAP) require a $150 fee, with $100 refunded if you finish.

who_can_apply: Open to all youth in grades 9 to 12. Register through your local Purdue Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Purdue Extension office if you need help signing up.
notes: The page says "contact your local Extension office for registration assistance". Confirm cost and the sign-up steps with Extension.
duration: 3 days (June 10 to 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Indiana 4-H youth in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register through 4-H Online by the deadline.
notes: The flyer was marked coming soon, so start time and details were not posted when read.
pay_detail: $25 per person, or $50 with overnight stay

who_can_apply: Youth who have completed grades 7 and 8 (so they are entering 9th grade).
how_to_apply: Sign up through 4-H Online. Contact your local Purdue Extension office if you need help signing up.
notes: Aimed at incoming 9th graders, so it fits the early end of the guide age range.
duration: 3 days (June 10 to 12 in 2026)
pay_detail: Registration fee was $250 by May 8, $275 for May 9 to 15 and $300 for May 16 to 22 (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Current 4-H members in grades 9 to 11 with strong leadership and 4-H advocacy. You must have been a member for at least 2 years before applying.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has a short questionnaire. It also has a video about why you want to be an ambassador. Use the Apply Now link on the page. Then you have an interview.
notes: You need to be in 4-H first. Find a local club through the Indiana 4-H page.
duration: Not stated on the page. Training is July 30 to August 1.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older; college-age young adults can also work. Workers are expected to live in the reserved dorm space during the job.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the page. Read the schedule for shows with no animals. Email Megan Skiba, skiba0@purdue.edu.
notes: Indiana work permit rules were not checked. Housing is required to be on site.
duration: About 4 weeks (July 31 to Aug 25, 2026)
pay_detail: Minimum wage

who_can_apply: Indiana youth in grades 3 to 12 (Mini 4-H is K to 2 in most counties).
how_to_apply: Start with the club membership page or contact your county or district 4-H office.
notes: Fees are not listed on the page.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Members must be in a business or marketing class now or have been before. The Indiana Department of Education must recognize chapters. They must have business courses. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher. Ask about joining or starting a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Indiana DECA advisor. Use indianadeca@gmail.com.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is indianadeca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Indiana.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $15 per member: $7 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Open to adults and youth. If you are younger than 18, a guardian fills out the Youth Volunteer Service Agreement. The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Create a Volunteer Profile and send the signed Youth Volunteer Service Agreement (guardian signs) to dnrvolunteer@dnr.IN.gov. Check CERVIS for current projects or contact a property near you. Phone 463-203-6562.
notes: Ask the park or property near you what age it takes. The list of tasks on the page is general and not every property offers every task.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. The page also lists unpaid internships for school credit.

who_can_apply: The state page says in-school young adults ages 14 to 21 and out-of-school young adults ages 16 to 24 may be eligible. Eligibility rules beyond age are not stated.
how_to_apply: Connect with your local WorkOne Career Center (Lafayette office serves Tippecanoe County; schedule by appointment through the WorkOne West Central site). Ask about the young adult program.
notes: This is the state workforce agency's WIOA-style youth help, not a single job. The WorkOne West Central about page (older) says a youth program for ages 16 to 24 is offered; the newer state page says 14 to 21 in school. The Bloomington (South Central) WorkOne regional page was not read, so confirm locally. Call before going. Re-read on 2026-10-09: the state page says nothing about cost or pay, so the card is not in the paid group.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask the program before you count on either.

who_can_apply: To join FFA, you must be enrolled in an agriculture course at your school. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher about enrolling in an agricultural education class. The Indiana Agricultural Education site explains how to start a program if your school has none.
notes: Not a job. Your school needs an ag class and an FFA chapter. The page links the Indiana Agricultural Education program for how to start one.
duration: School year
pay_detail: State dues are $14 per active member per year (includes national, state and district dues). Local chapters set their own local dues.

who_can_apply: Boys going into their senior year of high school. No age limit is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Registration opens January 11, 2027 on the Hoosier Boys State site. The application steps are not on the pages. Email info@hoosierboysstate.org or call 317-630-1301.
notes: The FAQ on the About page says the cost to attend is $400. The About page says a $50 non-refundable application fee is due, and the remaining $350 sponsorship fee is paid by a local American Legion Post or other community partner. Drop-off and pickup is at the MTI Center, 1215 Thunder Ave, Angola, IN. Not a job. The page links to a separate Girls State site (alahgs.org) that returned a 404, so no Hoosier Girls State card was written.
duration: One week
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. The About page lists scholarships for college. Bring no more than $30 spending money.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). Cadets can stay in until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Indiana Wing office: 4760 Andrews St, Columbus, IN 47203, 877-350-8643, info@inwg.cap.gov.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the program pages. The application lists payment options.

who_can_apply: The page says anyone seeking a work-based learning experience, and lists high schools among its partners. It does not state a minimum age. Learners can create an account on the site.
how_to_apply: Make a free learner account on the site. Search for chances by region. Then apply to each one you like.
notes: The site has a Create Your Account link for learners. The page does not state age rules for postings, so check each posting. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The site moved from indianaintern.net to workandlearnindiana.com.
pay_detail: Varies by employer. Each posting sets its own pay.

who_can_apply: Indiana high school students with an adult mentor. Grades and ages are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Not posted yet. Contact Anna Egan (williaak@purdue.edu) for questions.
notes: Check back for registration dates. A research paper is part of taking part.
duration: One event
pay_detail: Free event

who_can_apply: Hoosier students in 6th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Contact Shelby Lashbrook. Use shelby@indianaymcas.org or (317) 715-2145. Do this to join, start a delegation, volunteer or sponsor.
notes: Not a job. Office: 6610 N Shadeland Ave, Indianapolis, IN 46220, open Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
duration: School year, ending with a state conference
pay_detail: Program fees are not listed on the program page. Ask the program contact.

who_can_apply: 11th or 12th graders who have taken a career and technical education (CTE) course. The fact sheet says students come from schools that have partnered with INL. Ask your school if it is a partner.
how_to_apply: Send a resume, an unofficial transcript and the application. INL checks that you are eligible, then interviews some applicants, then runs a background check. Ask your school CTE teacher or email russell.campbell@inl.gov.
notes: This card is based on the INL fact sheet dated January 2025. Confirm current dates at stem.inl.gov. Only students from partner schools can apply.
duration: 6 weeks, mid June to early August
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the fact sheet. Transportation, food and safety gear are provided.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 by the start of the session, interested in a healthcare career, and able to attend every session date. Needs a 250-word written response, background check, TB screening, MMR, varicella and Tdap proof, an interview with a parent, an in-person orientation and photo ID.
how_to_apply: Register during the window through the 'High school students register here' link on Inova's student page. Spots are assigned by lottery, one entry per applicant, and the student handles all email.
notes: Mandatory student-and-parent info meetings are in mid-November 2026 and orientations in late December 2026 (dates differ by hospital; one of each is required). Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 4 to Jun 20, 2027; 1 shift per week, 3 to 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: The page lists a few volunteer chances for junior volunteers ages 14 to 17. Most volunteers must be 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now button on the page. Call the volunteer office: Salt Lake City 801-662-6560, Lehi 385-531-1560.
notes: The page does not say which sites take junior volunteers or which rules apply. Call first. Immunization proof is required for volunteers.
duration: Typical adult commitment is one shift a week for at least six months. The junior rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa 4-H members ages 16 to 20 on January 1 of the year they apply. They must have at least four years in a county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. The link is on the program page. The page does not list the parts of the application. Ambassadors go to monthly meetings and retreats. They find their own rides, meet with a career mentor and finish 10 hours of community or fair service.
notes: The page lists no fee or pay. Ambassadors must find their own rides. Contacts: Amy Powell, ampowell@iastate.edu, or Celine Beggs-Shoemaker, cmbeggs@iastate.edu. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: One program year, August to the next August
pay_detail: The page lists no fee or pay.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa youth in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply. Contact Iowa 4-H: 515-294-1017 or iowa4hmail@iastate.edu. Financial aid links are on the page.
notes: Cost is not stated. The page links to Iowa 4-H Foundation financial aid. Confirm dates with your county 4-H office first. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost is not stated. The page links to Iowa 4-H Foundation financial aid.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa 4-H members in grades 9 to 12. Up to 16 are picked. The page says members who hold a Reporter, Historian or Photographer role, or like media projects, fit best.
how_to_apply: Apply through State 4-H Recognition Day in 4-H Online: a one-page cover letter and a one-page resume. No interview, selection is from the written materials. You can apply more than once.
notes: The page does not say whether it pays or costs anything. Contact on the page: Clark Colby, 515-419-3301. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Events run June to August
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa 4-H members in grade 10 or 11 at the time of application. You may apply a second year.
how_to_apply: Sign up in 4-H Online. Then apply at State 4-H Recognition Day with a one-page cover letter and a one-page resume. Strong applications get an interview.
notes: The page does not say whether there is a cost. Contact: st4hcounciladvisors@iastate.edu, 515-294-1017. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: June of one year through July of the next
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Volunteer spots are open to Iowa 4-H youth who fill out the form. Paid youth staff spots are for 4-H members or alumni. Age rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Volunteers and youth staff each use an online form listed on the page. For 2027 interns, watch the page in December 2026. Email statefair4h@iastate.edu.
notes: Volunteers in the Exhibits Building or Livestock can ask for Youth Inn lodging. The Iowa State Fair also lists about 1,600 seasonal jobs on its own job site. That page does not state a minimum age or pay. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Iowa State Fair, Aug 10 to 23, 2026
pay_detail: Youth staff and intern jobs are paid. Pay rates are not stated. Volunteer spots are unpaid.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Iowa youth in grades 4 to 12 (Clover Kids is K to 3).
how_to_apply: Start on the Join 4-H page, or call 515-294-1017 or email iowa4hmail@iastate.edu. Your county Extension office can place you in a club.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Iowa residents who have finished 11th grade and have at least one semester left before graduating. Must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. Exchange students are not accepted. This program is for boys. A local American Legion Post must pick and sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Post and ask to be picked as a delegate. In January you get a selection email from your post. It has the information you need to register online. The Boys State site also has an Interest Form.
notes: The program does not provide rides. Delegates who bring cars cannot use them during the program, except in emergencies. A valid state ID card is needed to enter Camp Dodge. The program page says the Graduating Class of 2028 is the group for 2027.
duration: 6 days (June 20 to 25, 2027)
pay_detail: Unpaid, but free to attend. The local American Legion Post or other donors pay the fee.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in Iowa or Nebraska who is a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. Your paper must follow the rules in the Iowa Research Handbook. Schools can also bring up to five students to attend without presenting.
how_to_apply: Do a research project and write a paper that follows the Iowa Research Handbook. Submit the paper on the program site by the due date. Accepted papers present at the symposium.
notes: You need a research project first. The national symposium is April 20 to 24, 2027.
duration: Two-day symposium on February 22 and 23, 2027
pay_detail: Free to enter and attend. Top finalists can win scholarship prizes.

who_can_apply: Students who are in 10th, 11th or 12th grade when they apply. Students from outside the United States may apply. Students in 9th grade can no longer apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online on Submittable during the two-week window. Send a writing sample of up to ten pages. Also send a statement of purpose of 1 to 2 pages. Ask an English or writing teacher, tutor or mentor to upload one letter of recommendation. Decisions go out by email on April 9, 2027.
notes: Costs money. The program also runs 6-week online courses in winter and summer. See the program site for those. Questions: iyws@uiowa.edu or 319-335-4209.
duration: 2 weeks
pay_detail: $2,500 for one 2-week session in 2027 (room, board and teaching included). There is a $10 reading fee to apply, and it can be waived. Need-based financial aid is offered.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 and 11. The page describes it as a program for advanced high school students.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Fill in your information and pay the $95 fee. Get two letters from non-relative adults (one academic, one character). Write two essays of up to 750 words. Upload your transcript and SAT or ACT scores. Questions: summer@belinblank.org.
notes: Confirm the 2027 cost with summer@belinblank.org: the page shows the $7,500 fee for the 2026 session and does not show a 2027 fee.
duration: 5.5 weeks, June 16 to July 23, 2027
pay_detail: The 2026 session fee was $7,500 (room, board, materials, activities and 3 credit hours). The 2027 fee is not confirmed on the page; the page says to check with summer@belinblank.org. Travel and personal costs are extra. Financial aid may cover up to 95 percent. There is a $95 application fee that is not refunded.

who_can_apply: Iowa only. Students in schools with a local FFA chapter. The page does not state grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Find your school's chapter with the Chapter Locator on iowaffa.com, or ask your ag teacher. Dues are not stated on the page.
notes: About 20,800 members in 273 chapters (per the page). Only schools with an ag program have a chapter. The site has no Iowa region, so this card is tagged national and teens in other states may still see it under National. The Iowa only line at the start of What you do and Who can apply is the only guard.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students with a disability who are 14 to 21 years old. Talk to your school staff or your Vocational Rehabilitation high school contact to sign up.
how_to_apply: Talk with your school staff or your Vocational Rehabilitation high school contact. You can also apply online, with a paper form, or at your local office. Call 1-800-532-1486 with questions.
notes: The program page links to the Transition Alliance Program (TAP). It does not describe TAP. Work-based learning is one part of Pre-ETS. The program page does not say if the work is paid.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Students who are chosen as student reps from local high schools. The page lists 2026-27 reps from Beckman, Portola, Irvine, University, Northwood and Woodbridge high schools. It lists no grade or eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: The page says to look for HSYAT at your school through the Campus Clubs page. No application form is listed.
notes: The page lists no grade rules, application dates or phone number for this program. Check your school's Campus Clubs page.
duration: School year; follow the team on Instagram for events
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 and over (program assistance and toy cleaning are ages 14 to 17). Teen Summer Reading volunteers are students in grades 8 to 11. Each library has up to 20 TAG memberships.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application on the library's volunteer system at www.volgistics.com/appform/337674493. A required orientation comes before the summer program.
notes: The page lists no library contact; it points to the volunteer coordinator, and the City of Irvine main number is 949-724-6000. The page writes the Teen Volunteer Application link as volgistics.com/appform/337674493 and links it over https, so apply_url uses https.
duration: Summer Reading volunteers work a weekly two-hour shift. Other roles vary.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18, or finished 8th grade and going into 9th. You must live in Irvine or go to school there. Keep a C or better in every class. You cannot have criminal convictions or serious traffic offenses.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Interest Form on the program page. Interest cards are due January 1 for winter or June 1 for summer. Email ipdexplorers@cityofirvine.org with questions.
notes: The Orange County Explorer Academy is held twice a year. It is a hard 5-day program. You must finish it within a year of joining. The group also takes trips, such as a weekend in Sacramento for the Peace Officers' Memorial.
duration: Most Explorers stay until high school graduation
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students who will graduate in 2027 or 2028. The page also describes 11th or 12th grade in Fall 2026. You need an unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher in college prep classes. You need a strong reason to take one UCI course.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Enrollment Form. Send it to the Summer Session office. Add a copy of your latest high school transcript.
notes: This is real college credit and costs real money. The grade stays on a college record. The page names two grade groups (graduating 2027 or 2028; and 11th or 12th grade in Fall 2026), so check which one fits you. The fee page says 2026 Summer Session fees were pending the state budget and may change.
duration: One summer course (Summer Session sessions)
pay_detail: The fee page lists high school students under visiting non-UC students: $400 per unit plus a $296 campus fee and $5.50 per unit tech fee. Some courses add materials fees.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12 need parent and principal consent. Grades K to 8 also need instructor approval. You must meet each class prerequisite. There must be open seats.
how_to_apply: Find a class in the IVC schedule, write down its CRN, then complete the General Enrollment Form steps with parent and school approvals. The Director of Dual Enrollment is listed on the page.
notes: Checked 2026-10-13 against the general dual enrollment page: per-unit enrollment fees are waived for grades 9 to 12 and not for K to 8, grades 9 to 12 need parent and principal consent, and K to 8 also need instructor approval. The page says enrollment is ongoing, on a space-available basis, with no deadline. IVC/IUSD Summer College is for grades 9 to 11 at seven Irvine high schools: Creekside, Irvine, Northwood, Portola, San Joaquin, University and Woodbridge. The Early College Pathway is for some students admitted before grade 9, at Beckman and San Joaquin.
duration: By semester or summer session
pay_detail: Per-unit enrollment fees are waived for grades 9 to 12 (not for K to 8). You pay the college health fee and buy textbooks.

who_can_apply: High school students of all backgrounds can apply. Irvine residents get priority. Priority also goes to youth who are low-income or out of school. It also goes to youth in foster care and first-generation college students.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application link or contact for this summer program. It says to check back in February 2027.
notes: This program is part of a California Volunteers Youth Service Corps grant. The same page lists an adult job program for ages 18 to 30. That one is not for high school students. Training covers job search, interviewing, leadership, customer service and financial literacy.
duration: About 20 hours a week. Shifts run 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., weekdays and weekends.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page. The page calls the roles jobs ("hiring").

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian to co-sign and working papers. Everyone is interviewed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application and sign the code of conduct and harassment policies. Staff contact you if there is a fit, then interview you.
notes: The library page says teens under 18 need working papers, even to volunteer. Volunteers may not sort or shelve books.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in Northern California; grade levels not stated. The center is not open yet.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps yet. Call JA of Northern California at (925) 465-1070.
notes: Not open yet, and the page lists no registration steps or opening date. Watch for it in early 2027. The contact on the page is for sponsors and partners.
pay_detail: Free to students (page says programs are delivered at no cost)

who_can_apply: High school students whose school or group requests a program. The page does not say whether individual teens can sign up. JA Finance Park is the Los Angeles area only.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to request a program using the form on the JA high school page. The page does not say who should fill it in. Contact: info@jasocal.org or 323-957-1818.
notes: The page does not say whether teens can sign up alone. Bring the page to a teacher. JA Company Program ends with the JA Student Entrepreneurship Challenge pitch contest.
duration: Varies by program
pay_detail: No pay. The page says programs are offered at little or no cost to educators.

who_can_apply: Residents ages 15 to 24. The page implies you must live in the city but does not say it as a rule. First-time workers, low-income youth and students from underserved areas come first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the summer internship application PDF. It is linked in the city's press release.
notes: About 700 jobs in 2026. The UEZ-funded jobs pay $17 an hour for 25 hours a week. Recreation jobs are 40-hour weeks. Ask the city about rules for workers under 18.
duration: UEZ-funded jobs: July 6 to Aug 21, 2026. Recreation jobs run through the summer.
pay_detail: $17 per hour, 25 hours a week for the business-placement jobs. Pay for other jobs not stated.

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the opening. Questions: volunteer@lsc.org or 201-253-1297.
notes: No dates, pay or apply link are posted right now. Call or email before you plan. The museum is in Liberty State Park, 222 Jersey City Boulevard.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 18 (students in 6th grade or older). Boards meet at Central (1st Monday, 5 pm), Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial and Northside; Crozet is full and Gordon Avenue is not currently running.
how_to_apply: Use the Join a Teen Advisory Board page or contact your branch. The page does not say how to apply beyond that.
notes: Meeting times: Greene 1st Tuesday 4-5 pm; Louisa 3rd Thursday 3:45 pm; Nelson 2nd Thursday 4-5 pm; Northside 2nd Monday 7-8 pm. Gordon Avenue's entry on the teen volunteers page says its board is accepting applications while the TAB page says it is not currently running; call the branch.
duration: One meeting a month

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 13 years old. Teen volunteers should be able to work independently. Branches include Central, Crozet, Gordon Avenue, Greene County, Louisa County, Nelson Memorial, Northside and Scottsville.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch (Send a Message link) or email the Young Adult Services Manager through the JMRL contact form. The page does not list formal application steps.
notes: Volunteering can count toward school or club service requirements. At the time of reading, Gordon Avenue said all weekly positions were filled. JMRL's volunteer coordinator is listed as Acacia Rodgers, volunteer@jmrl.org, 434-979-7151 ext 6695.
duration: Varies by branch

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. The national site says you must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated to succeed. The program pages do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Brunswick center: 4401 Glynco Pkwy, Brunswick, GA 31525. Turner center: 2000 Schilling Ave, Albany, GA 31705. Neither center page showed a closure notice on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. That is normal for this federal program, but only enter it on the official jobcorps.gov site with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds. The Atlanta center is not listed here because its page could not be confirmed.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. The national site says it covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages do not explain parent consent for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Make a MyJobCorps account. Fill out the application. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Examples are proof of income and proof of citizenship or residency. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Address: 1480 Snelling Ave N, St. Paul, MN 55108. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. After applying, the national site says the review includes a background check (1 to 2 weeks) and a campus review (about 30 days).
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who are low income and meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules, plus background checks (per the national Job Corps site). Mostly fits teens who are out of school or want a different path. Housing is on campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at enroll.jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-JOBS (800-733-5627).
notes: Residential, so you live on campus at 3100 Meadowview Rd, Sacramento. The Sacramento page lists the trades (building construction, carpentry, cement masonry, Certified Nurse Assistant) but not the age or income rules, which come from jobcorps.gov. A federal settlement reported Aug 12, 2026 kept all 99 centers open, but that article does not name Sacramento, so confirm the center is enrolling.
pay_detail: Free tuition, housing, meals and basic medical care, plus a monthly living allowance (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The page does not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload eligibility papers. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Or call 800-733-5627.
notes: The center page footer lists 2800 Airport Hwy 21 E, San Marcos, TX 78667. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Texas has other Job Corps centers that are not covered by this card.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Phone for Curlew and Columbia Basin: 877-763-0580.
notes: Addresses: Cascades, 2060 Powerhouse Drive, Sedro-Woolley, WA 98284. Curlew, 3 Campus St, Curlew, WA 99118. Columbia Basin, 6739 24th Ave NE Bldg 2402, Moses Lake, WA 98837. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Each center page shows only a few of its trades; use See More on the center page for the full list.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 through 24 who face barriers to employment. Meeting the rules does not guarantee a spot. Funds are limited and staff pick youth who are 'most in need' and likely to succeed.
how_to_apply: Contact a youth case manager at the nearest Job Service North Dakota office. Fargo: 1350 32nd St S, 701-239-7300, infojsfg@nd.gov. Bismarck: 1601 E Century Ave, 701-328-5000, infojsbis@nd.gov. Grand Forks: 1501 28th Ave S, 701-795-3700, infojsgf@nd.gov.
notes: Not for every teen. The handbook says the program is not an entitlement. The exact list of barriers and income rules was not in the program pages, so ask the case manager. The handbook is dated 10.21 in its file name, so confirm details by phone. North Dakota work rules for minors were not checked.
duration: Work experience can happen any time of year. Length is not stated.
pay_detail: Work experience pays at least minimum wage, paid through Job Service. Pay covers up to 25 hours per week.

who_can_apply: Local high school students interested in a healthcare career. Must be at least 14.5 years old, at least a second-semester freshman, with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Must attend a Saturday orientation with a parent or guardian and complete required training. Students apply through a partner high school, which interviews and screens its own candidates.
how_to_apply: Apply through your high school. Contact the career, college or community service office at a partner school listed on the page. The school interviews and screens its own student candidates.
notes: Read on the official John Muir Health page 2026-10-07. Not stated on that page: application window or deadline, TB test or immunization requirements. It is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit is listed. Region is east-bay because Walnut Creek is in Contra Costa County, not Oakland. The Auxiliary at Walnut Creek Medical Center offers selective scholarships to high school seniors and college students who volunteered in this program. A separate Concord Medical Center high school program is not onboarding this summer; its page says to check back in March 2027. An older third-party listing said seniors are not accepted, which conflicts with the official page; confirm with the program before applying. Minimum age is listed as 14.5 on the page, stored here as 14.
duration: One 3-hour shift per week, year-round, committed through the end of senior year
pay_detail: Volunteer role; no pay stated on the page

who_can_apply: Most volunteer positions take youth 14 and older. Summer teen volunteer jobs are open to ages 13 and older as of June 1. Each job posting lists its own minimum age.
how_to_apply: Register in the library's volunteer database. This is a Samaritan volunteer profile. Then sign up for an opening with the Sign Up button. If no shift is listed, the Volunteer Coordinator follows up with you.
notes: Quote from the page: We welcome and encourage youth volunteers 14 years and older for most volunteer positions. The page says over 900 teens through adults volunteer each year. You can also become a Swift Volunteer for last-minute needs, with no obligation.
duration: One-time, short-term or weekly shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library records and verifies service hours weekly for schools.

who_can_apply: High school programs are delivered through schools and teachers, who request them. The site does not list a way for a student to sign up alone, so ask your school or call JA.
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counselor to request a JA program, or contact JA at (925) 465-1070 or info@janorcal.org.
notes: JA reached 27,947 students in 128 schools in 2025-26, mostly through schools. JA Launchpad (Silicon Valley) is listed as opening early 2027. Job shadow and internship details were not on the pages, so ask JA.
duration: Varies
pay_detail: No student fee stated. JA says programs are little to no cost to educators.

who_can_apply: Be 16 to 19 by June 1, 2027, live in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente service area, have proof of legal US work eligibility, and be free Monday to Friday about 8am to 5pm. Priority goes to juniors and seniors. Children of Kaiser employees or physicians cannot apply. The program aims at students who lack resources to explore health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply only on the KP LAUNCH online portal during the window (email submissions are not reviewed). You need a resume and a personal statement of up to 750 words. Questions: KP.LAUNCH@kp.org.
notes: Full-time hours, so no summer school or camp overlap. Competitive. A Kaiser story reportedly cited about 3,300 applicants for 318 spots, which is not confirmed here. Placement sites vary, so check that your area is offered. Kaiser may ask for COVID vaccine proof.
duration: 7 weeks, June 14 to July 30, 2027
pay_detail: $25 per hour minimum, paid every two weeks, up to 40 hours a week

who_can_apply: High school students 16 years or older (the kp.org page says ages 16 to 17). Applications open only when shifts are available. One-year commitment.
how_to_apply: When it opens again, sign up on the Kaiser volunteer site under Redwood City. You need one or two references from a teacher, coach or tutor. Then you do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. A parent must come. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Phone: 650-299-3135.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site and the kp.org Redwood City page on 2026-10-16. The two pages do not agree. kp.org says 4 hours a week for 6 months. The volunteer site says one year for high school students. Plan on one year. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing. The kp.org page also lists roles like the ER, art, pet visits and surgery. These differ by site.
duration: One year

who_can_apply: Must be 16 years or older to apply. The time commitment is one year. One or two professional references from a teacher, coach, tutor or similar are required.
how_to_apply: When it opens again, apply on the Kaiser volunteer site under San Jose. You need one or two references. Then you do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. Bring a parent. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Volunteer office: 408-972-7230.
notes: Read on Kaiser Permanente's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. The high school program is full. Check the page every few weeks, since minors are taken only when shifts are free. Kaiser does not offer job or clinical shadowing (physician, nursing, radiology, PT or OT). The kp.org page still links to volunteer-ncal.kaiserpermanente.org, which no longer works; use kpvolunteer.samaritan.com.
duration: One year

who_can_apply: Volunteers 16 years and older. The page lists separate steps for 16 and 17 year olds. You must give at least one 4-hour shift each week, Monday to Friday between 8 am and 6 pm, for a planned one year commitment.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Kaiser volunteer site. Look under High School Programs at Santa Clara Homestead. Then do a video interview. Next is a health check where you bring your shot records. A parent must come with you. Last are online trainings and an in person orientation. Volunteer office: 408-851-1717.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. The kp.org Santa Clara page links to it at kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. Shifts are on weekdays only, 8 am to 6 pm. Most students would need a free period, a late afternoon or summer days. A background check with a Social Security number is only for people over 18. The page asks for shot records. It does not say which shots, if you need a TB test, or if there are fees. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing.
duration: One 4-hour weekday shift a week for a planned one year

who_can_apply: High school students 16 years or older (the kp.org page says ages 16 to 17). Commit to one 4-hour shift a week, same day and time. The time commitment spans your high school career.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 650-742-2678. Ask when high school spots will open. Then apply on the Kaiser volunteer site under South San Francisco.
notes: Read on Kaiser Permanente's volunteer site and the kp.org page on 2026-10-16. The kp.org page says a few hours a week for a few months, but the volunteer site says the high school commitment spans your high school career; plan on the longer one. The Daly City Medical Offices page has the same high school rules. Kaiser does not offer job or clinical shadowing. The page does not list vaccine, TB test or fee rules.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, for the rest of high school

who_can_apply: High school students age 15 or older. You must give one 3 to 4 hour shift a week on the same day and time, and stay in the program for your whole high school career. The high school track is at Walnut Creek Medical Center only.
how_to_apply: Go to the Kaiser volunteer site. Open High School Programs at Walnut Creek and click Apply. You will log in or sign up as a new volunteer. Questions? Call 925-295-5487.
notes: Read on Kaiser's volunteer site on 2026-10-16. kp.org links to it at kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. This is a long commitment. The page says it lasts all through high school. The page does not list shots, a TB test or fees. It does not say if a parent must sign. Kaiser does not offer job shadowing. Adult volunteers here also cover nearby offices. The high school track is at Walnut Creek only. Kaiser's old volunteer link no longer works, so use kpvolunteer.samaritan.com. The Pleasanton and San Ramon offices said on 2026-10-16 that they are not taking high school students right now.
duration: One 3 to 4 hour shift a week, for the rest of high school

who_can_apply: Workdays are described as for all ages, individuals and families. No sign up needed unless you come with a group of 10 or more. Age rules for the longer volunteer roles are not on the pages.
how_to_apply: For workdays, just show up 5 to 10 minutes early and sign in with the leader. For longer roles, fill out the volunteer application on the site. Volunteer Office: 630-762-2741, volunteer@kaneforest.com.
notes: Bring boots or sturdy shoes, a water bottle and gloves. Info on Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects is in the Resources section of the volunteer page. Questions about workdays: Stewardship Specialist, 630-200-1290.
duration: Workdays are monthly. Cancelled when it is below zero.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Kane, DeKalb or Kendall County. The page lists no income or other rules (federal workforce funding rules may apply, so ask the provider).
how_to_apply: Pick a provider on the page and contact them directly. Providers in Kane County include Elgin Community College and Business & Career Services Inc. Waubonsee Community College covers Kane and Kendall. Not sure where to start? Call 630-762-2085.
notes: Starts at age 16, so it fits older high schoolers. The page names one contact person but lists an email that does not match that name, so phone first. Funded by a U.S. Department of Labor grant per the page. Elgin Community College's own Future Workforce Leaders program is one of the providers.
duration: Varies by provider
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one of the services; pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 as of January 1 of the event year.
how_to_apply: Registration for 2026 is closed. The page tells youth to let their Extension unit know which class session they choose. The page does not say how to register next year. Email kansas4h@ksu.edu with questions.
notes: Not stated on the program page: whether you must be a 4-H member. Ask your county Extension office.
duration: About 3 days (June 3 to 5 in 2026)

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16 by June 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in spring 2027 for the application.
notes: Spots are limited. Other high school chances are on the hospital's For High School Students page.
duration: Summer only. No year-round roles for high schoolers.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Current freshmen, sophomores and juniors who live in Missouri or Kansas. You go to a public or charter school. You do not need research experience. Shots must be up to date. First choice goes to students from poorer neighborhoods.
how_to_apply: Fill out the STAR 2.0 student form on the program page in the winter window.
notes: Held at 2401 Gillham Road, Kansas City, MO. You must attend the whole 6 weeks.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (2026: June 15 to July 23)
pay_detail: $2,600 stipend

who_can_apply: Any high school student in the Kansas City metro area, any art form. If picked for an interview you must be free in August.
how_to_apply: Use the form on the KemperTeens site when it opens again. Then interview in August.
notes: Meets at 4420 Warwick Boulevard, Kansas City, MO. You must get yourself to meetings and events. Page does not say which month applications open.
duration: Alternate Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., Sept to Nov and Jan to May (2026-27)
pay_detail: $100 per month stipend. Free to join.

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th grade can join the rising freshman program. Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade can join the other program. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: Use the application link for your program on the program page. You must go to an in-person orientation. Email VolunteerApplications@KUMC.edu or call 913-588-6560.
notes: 2026 sessions ran June 1 to July 30. There is also a program page for the Olathe location.
duration: Rising sophomore to senior: one 2-week session, Monday to Thursday. Rising freshman: half days on Friday mornings, at least 6 Fridays.
pay_detail: Volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school age students. Exact ages not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: See the volunteer page for the form when a session opens. Questions: volunteer@theworldwar.org or 816-888-8115.
notes: Adults must be 19 or older for the regular program, so this is a separate youth track. Ask about the age rule.
duration: Three sessions a year: spring, summer and fall
pay_detail: Unpaid. Museum store discounts.

who_can_apply: Students from schools across Kansas City. Age or grade not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Council application form linked on the museum's teen programs page. Questions: teens@nelson-atkins.org.
notes: Teens also get $5 tickets to special exhibitions. The same page lists Teen Open Mic Nights (free, bi-monthly) and Teen Drop-In Art Making.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer experience.

who_can_apply: Current 9th to 12th graders ages 14 to 19. You live and go to high school in Jackson, Clay, Platte or Cass counties in Missouri, or Johnson or Wyandotte counties in Kansas. You must meet employer hiring and work rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form. Finish the paperwork. Go to a prep workshop. Then interview at the spring hiring fair.
notes: The 2027 close date and hiring fair date are not posted yet.
duration: 5 weeks (2026: June 1 to July 2)
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Talk to the teen volunteer coordinator at your branch to ask if they have openings.
notes: Openings depend on the branch.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Current sophomores and juniors with at least a 3.0 GPA. You must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. You must like a health job (nursing does not count). You must also have money or school disadvantage. Family income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty line.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online STAHR form. Send a transcript with unweighted GPA. Send 1 professional recommendation through the online reference form (letters are not accepted). Questions: stahr@umkc.edu, 816-235-6169.
notes: Questions: stahr@umkc.edu or 816-235-6169.
duration: 2026: June 8 to July 17, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus August to April
pay_detail: Free. Students who meet expectations get a stipend, a scholarship, or both. Amounts not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in 8th to 12th grade at the time of application. Seniors can join for the summer season only. Mature, responsible teens who like working with the public and care about animals.
how_to_apply: Apply online for a pathway when applications open. See the zoo's VolunTEEN page.
notes: The zoo page says applications open November 2026. Exact dates are not posted.
duration: May through April. Three seasons: summer, fall, spring.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Trailblazers need 60 hours in summer and 18 hours each in fall and spring.

who_can_apply: LIT is for ages 14 to 16. CIT is for ages 16 to 17. The page says CIT is especially for rising 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Letter of Interest for LIT or CIT on the program page. You then get instructions on how to register. Call 785-257-3221 with questions.
notes: A camper scholarship (campership) form is linked on the page. Check the page in early 2027 for new dates and prices.
duration: Five nights
pay_detail: 2026 cost for five nights: LIT $800, $700 or $600 by tier. CIT $650, $550 or $450 by tier. The page says the program can be attended at no cost through a donation to the Kansas 4-H Foundation.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state ages; ask the teen librarian at your branch. Each board sets its own meeting schedule.
how_to_apply: Contact your local librarian (Teen Services Librarian). Or go to an open Teen Advisory Board meeting listed on the page. If your branch has no board, ask about starting one.
notes: KCLS serves King County outside the city of Seattle (its branches include Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way). The Seattle Public Library volunteer page showed no current volunteer openings when read on 2026-10-09. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
duration: Ongoing; meeting schedules vary by branch
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit, and can ask for a reference letter after 10 hours of volunteering within 6 months.

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade who are interested in a health care career. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens on January 4, 2027. Use the link on the Health Science Explorers page. Contact the coordinator listed on the page with questions.
notes: The same page lists a virtual Career Club for grades 9 to 12. It meets on the second Wednesday each month, 7 to 8 pm. It also lists a yearly Health Careers Fair at the Crowne Plaza in Kearney.
duration: September to May, first Wednesday of each month, 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: $100 for the program, with financial help available. Lunch is provided. Students who finish earn a $1,000 UNK scholarship.

who_can_apply: Currently enrolled high school students ages 16 to 17. Must be 16 or older when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You need a self-portrait photo, proof of COVID-19 vaccination and a questionnaire. Recommenders email letters to volunteer@med.usc.edu by April 30. If accepted, you do an interview. Then you get a health screening with a TB test, an orientation and a tour. Phone (323) 442-8436.
notes: Check the page in January for the next year's dates.
duration: 8 weeks, at least 8 hours a week and 60 hours total
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 and enrolled in high school or an equivalent program. Parent or guardian written permission is in the application. No drugs, underage drinking or gang ties, and you must pass a background check (a waiver may be allowed for past minor offenses). Cadets who join before 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Go to a weekly meeting. You learn about the program and meet the officer mentors. You can pick up an application there.
notes: Contact Officer David Buchanan, dbuchanan@kennesaw-ga.gov, 770-424-8274. Kennesaw Police, 2529 J O Stephenson Ave, Kennesaw, GA 30144. The page does not give a meeting day or time, so call first. Not a paid job.
duration: Weekly meetings. Day and time are not listed.
pay_detail: Volunteer program. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Kentucky 4-H teens in 8th grade and up (2026 listing). Sign up through your county Extension office.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Conference Registration Form. Turn it in to your county Extension office by the deadline. You must be in Kentucky 4-H through 4-H Online.
notes: Details come from the Meade County Extension listing for the state event. The Kentucky 4-H leadership page names the Teen Conference but gives no details. Scholarships are not mentioned there; ask your county office.
duration: 4 days (June 2 to 5, 2026)
pay_detail: $300 per person (2026)

who_can_apply: Kentucky youth ages 9 to 18.
how_to_apply: Join through 4-H Online. Call your local Extension office. You must be signed up to join programs.
notes: Also open to younger kids; teen parts are the leader roles. Fees are not listed on the page. The four 4-H camps are Feltner, Lake Cumberland, West Kentucky and North Central.
duration: Program year Sept 1 to Aug 31
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in at least one agriculture course. The page says members are 12 to 21.
how_to_apply: Use the Chapter Locator on kyffa.org or ask your ag teacher. Phone 502-564-3472.
notes: 25,178 members in 186 chapters (per the page). Dues are not stated.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Current Kentucky residents in 11th grade who plan to return to a Kentucky school. You must have taken the ACT, PSAT or SAT in grades 9 to 11. Public, private, parochial and homeschool students can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school or district with the online student form. Home school students should contact the GSP office. Applications are read without names. Each school or district can send a set number based on its junior class size.
notes: The deadline_iso shown is the earlier of the two deadlines. Ask your school counselor which one applies to you. Scholars agree to stay all five weeks and may leave campus for one Family Day. Leaving early means no certificate.
duration: 5 weeks (June 19 to July 23, June 20 to July 24, or June 27 to July 31, 2027)
pay_detail: Free for selected students. The state and donors cover tuition, room, board and most supplies. Families pay for travel to the program and spending money. A refundable residence deposit is required.

who_can_apply: Current high school or home school sophomores and juniors. You live in Kentucky, go to school in Kentucky, or have a parent or guardian who works in Kentucky.
how_to_apply: Create an Acceptd account and open an application for your art form. Part 1 collects your two recommenders and Part 2 has your materials and answers. Finalists do a final round audition or review.
notes: Dates may change, says the timeline page. Final auditions are held in person at Northern Kentucky University. Some are online. Email gsainfo@kentuckyperformingarts.org with questions. Or call 502-566-5192. The $35 or $50 application fee and the free or reduced lunch fee waiver are not on the GSA pages checked; confirm the fee with the GSA team before paying.
duration: 3 weeks, June 6 to 26, 2027
pay_detail: No cost to the student. Application fee is $35 for one art form or $50 for two. The fee can be waived for students who get free or reduced lunch.

who_can_apply: Any middle or high school student interested in science.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the yearly meeting of the Kentucky Academy of Science. K-12 Junior Academy students pay $0. Send in a short summary of your research. Each participant needs a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. High school oral presenters also upload a consent form that their school signs.
notes: High school oral presenters may be picked to go to the American Junior Academy of Science (AJAS 2027, Feb 17 to 21 in Chicago). The page says the academy will pay for sign up, travel and rooms for at least 6 students in 2027. The sign up page does not print the year. Confirm the October dates with the Academy.
duration: Two days, Nov 6 and 7, 2026 at Murray State University
pay_detail: Registration is free for K-12 Junior Academy students. Junior Academy student membership costs 5 dollars.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low-income and have at least one listed barrier. A barrier can be being behind in basic skills or having a disability. Out-of-school youth are ages 16 to 24 and need at least one listed barrier, such as having dropped out of school.
how_to_apply: Contact the youth career planner for your area. A map on the program page shows them. You can also contact any Kentucky Career Center office.
notes: This is a state overview. Kentucky has 10 local workforce areas. In-school youth must be low-income and meet a listed barrier. Out-of-school youth must meet a listed barrier. Ask the youth career planner for your area about your case.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Any high school student who wants to serve and lead. Clubs are set up in high schools or equivalent schools. Members are expected to do at least 50 hours of service a year.
how_to_apply: Use the Find a Key Club tool on keyclub.org, or follow the Start a Key Club steps if your school has none.
notes: Dues and local rules vary by club; dues amount not stated on the pages. Key Club International phone: 800-549-2647.
pay_detail: No pay. Members pay nominal dues (amount not listed on the program pages).

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Open to anyone. The site says its mission is a free education for anyone, anywhere. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Go to the page, pick a course, and sign up for a free account if you want to save progress.
notes: The page loads slowly because it builds in your browser. Course list seen: Financial Literacy, Personal Finance, Entrepreneurship, Careers, College admissions, Career Exploration.
duration: Self-paced
pay_detail: Free (the site says it is a nonprofit offering free education)

who_can_apply: Current students in grades 9 to 11 in the Naperville area. The page does not give a school or residency rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. For questions, contact the KidsMatter Director of Programs. Call 630-864-3960 or write to sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org.
notes: The page still showed the 2025-26 call when read. Check back in spring for the next one.
duration: One school year, with monthly meetings
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It is a leadership role.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Volunteers under 18 need a parent's approval. You must have a library card in good standing.
how_to_apply: Print the General Volunteer Application. Hand it in at the library where you want to work.
notes: The policy page says exceptions to the age 14 rule may be made for short projects such as Scout requirements. Volunteers of any age may not work at public service desks or use staff computers. In-library tasks like shelving are listed for adults only.
duration: At least 3 hours of service a month
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students with disabilities in the Knoxville area. They can be in high school or past it.
how_to_apply: Email Eva at eva@themuseknoxville.org to apply. A staff member makes a skills plan for each person.
notes: The same page lists the Muse Apprenticeship Program (MAP) with Business, Education and STEAM paths. It says the museum is no longer recruiting for 2026-27. It does not list ages, hours or pay.
duration: Groups come to the museum weekly. The length is not stated.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Age 14 and up for Family Fun Day. Age 16 and up for Summer Art Academy. Other volunteer roles at the museum are 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the KMA Volunteer Application PDF and email it to the Volunteer Coordinator at dmann@knoxart.org. Call 865-525-6101 with questions.
notes: The volunteer page does not describe its internships. Ask before you plan around one. The museum also runs Summer Art Academy afternoon workshops for teens 13 and up. In 2026 tuition was $170 for members and $200 for non-members, with a scholarship form.
duration: Dates are not listed
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 17. You must be 13 by April 1, 2027.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Upload an essay of no more than 2 pages. Give at least 2 references who are not family. Incomplete forms are not considered.
notes: Volunteer meetings are a must. They are recorded and online for now. Parents and teens should read the weekly email updates. An early review does not promise an interview or a spot.
duration: At least 50 hours per calendar year
pay_detail: Unpaid. One-time program fee of $50, plus you must keep a Zoo Knoxville membership (discounted, bought when you start volunteering).

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18; no prior experience required for the free onboarding programs. Camps run in several cities including San Francisco and Oakland, plus virtual.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form linked on the Kode With Klossy programs page.
notes: Free for all programs. Workforce development programs are for ages 18 to 26, not high schoolers. Camp dates and sites for summer 2027 are not posted yet.
duration: Code-a-Bration is 2 days; Camp is 2 weeks
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Volunteers commit to a minimum of six months and 100 service hours, about four hours of service each week.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Program application on the Kootenai Health volunteer page. Then wait to hear from them if there is an opening. Phone (208) 625-4645 or email volunteerservices@kh.org.
notes: The page says volunteer roles do not include internships or clinical shadowing. Volunteer office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 service hours
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: High school students of all levels. No ages or grades are listed.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration is open. In 2026 registration was closed and a waitlist form was on the page.
notes: Costs money, not a job. Contact doarch@kennesaw.edu. Kennesaw campus: 1000 Chastain Road, Kennesaw, GA 30144.
duration: 10 weekdays (July 6 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $1,050 for 2026. Materials for modeling and drawing are included. Scholarships are not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders for camps at the KSU Center. The Aerospace Engineering camp at the Marietta campus takes rising 6th to 12th graders.
how_to_apply: The 2026 sessions are over, though the page still shows Registration Open labels. For Summer 2027 updates, fill out the contact form on the page. No 2027 dates or registration are posted.
