notes: Places: KSU Center, 3333 Busbee Dr NW, Kennesaw. The Marietta campus hosts Aerospace. Contact discoveru@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6765. It costs money and is not a job. Confirm sign-up status with the team before you pay.
duration: One week per camp
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $499 for baking, AutoCAD, Chef's Master Class and Medical Skills; $399 for Adulting 101; $350 for Aerospace Engineering. Scholarships are not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th grade through college freshmen. The Dance Intensive is for intermediate to advanced dancers.
how_to_apply: Register on the pages for each program. They are linked from the main page. Sign-up starts November 1. Questions: arts@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6742.
notes: Not a job. The page states no cost or fee, so check each program page. The Dance, Theatre and Arts and Design intensives list no exact dates on the main page. Scholarships are not mentioned.
duration: One week for the intensives. Music camps run 3 to 6 days.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the main page. Check each program page.

who_can_apply: Rising public high school seniors (entering senior year in fall 2027) who attend a public high school in LA County and live or go to school within 10 miles of the worksite. Must be able to work legally in the U.S. and bring a school ID and proof of work eligibility. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply for a listed internship when applications open in March 2027. Questions: BAI@arts.lacounty.gov.
notes: Schedule may change. You cannot be a current or former employee of the worksite or related to its staff. The 2026 internship positions list is on the Department's site. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to August 6, 2027. Optional paid extension from September 2027 to April 2028 (22 weeks).
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly rate is not stated. Program Day participants also get a stipend for 90% participation, plus transportation help and lunch.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 20 with at least a 2.0 GPA. You can read, write and understand training materials in English. You can work on a team.
how_to_apply: Send in the Explorer Program Interest Card to hear about the next cycle. Add the program's email to your safe senders. Then apply during open enrollment. Accepted applicants get a uniform fitting and a family meeting. They also go to a two-day orientation.
notes: The page lists 12 posts. They are Vernon, Carson, Whittier, Industry, Azusa, Lancaster, Fairfax, Santa Clarita, La Canada Flintridge, El Monte, Agoura Hills and Pomona. But its sign-up form lists Posts 1 to 22. Confirm your post with the department.
duration: Ongoing after a two-day orientation; twice-monthly meetings
pay_detail: No cost or pay is stated on the page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 9 to 17 in LA County. New participants must pass a 100-yard freestyle swim test (1:30.00 for ages 14 to 17). Cadets must be 16 or 17 as of July 1 with at least two years in the program, one as an A.
how_to_apply: Register online when the season opens, usually in February or March. New participants must pass a swim test. They must bring a birth certificate or passport. Cadet and Life Saving Team applications are separate. They are posted later.
notes: The page calls the $635 an estimated operating cost and says the fee schedule is under review. Costs money and is mainly for younger kids; teens 16 to 17 can reach Cadets. Not every beach offers afternoon sessions or Session 2. Refund rules and absence limits are on the page.
duration: Two 4-week sessions in 2026: June 15 to July 10 and July 13 to August 7
pay_detail: About $635 per child for Summer 2026 (the page says the fee schedule was under review). Financial aid needs a federal tax return.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 and older can volunteer. Teen Advisory Boards are open to teens at libraries that have one.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LA County Library branch to ask about volunteer openings and whether it has a Teen Advisory Board.
notes: This covers LA County Library branches (unincorporated areas and many cities), not the City of Los Angeles library system (see the LAPL card). Tasks vary by branch and season.
duration: Varies by library
pay_detail: Unpaid; students can earn school service credit.

who_can_apply: LA County residents who are 14 to 24 when they enroll and have the legal right to work in the U.S. The county gives priority to youth with high needs, such as current or former foster youth, youth touched by the justice system, youth who are or were homeless, and LGBTQ+ youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Interest Form on the Youth@Work page. AJCC staff reach out within 48 hours to check eligibility and match you with an employer.
notes: The county released a Youth@Work Program Review and Redesign Report on August 25, 2026, so rules and pay for 2027 may change. Under 18 you need a California work permit before the first day. The pay figure is the 2025 summer rate from the county's own news release, not a 2027 promise. Long Beach youth can also use the City of Long Beach center (see the LBWIN card).
duration: About 160 hours in all: up to 140 hours of paid work plus 20 hours of job-readiness class
pay_detail: Paid work experience for about 140 hours plus a class. The page does not state an hourly wage.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 26. You live in LA County. You were hurt by COVID-19. You can go to all six weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the intake form on the academy page to join the waitlist. Questions: (844) 432-4900 or emi@opportunity.lacounty.gov.
notes: The COVID-19 impact rule is on the page, so confirm you qualify. Schedule, cost and meeting place are not listed. Confirm first.
duration: 6 weeks per cohort
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. The 2026 council has 27 members from nine areas, including the San Gabriel Valley, Central Los Angeles and the South Bay. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: The page has no application. Use the update sign-up form, email metroyouthcouncil@metro.net or call 213.922.2852.
notes: Check the page for the next recruitment. The page does not say how often the council meets.
duration: 1-year term, January to December
pay_detail: The page does not mention a stipend or pay

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. You must be going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade in 2026-2027.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain the steps. Call 301-609-4095.
notes: The page footer lists 5 Garrett Avenue, La Plata, MD 20646. Program is for the 2026-2027 school year cycle; no 2027 dates are posted.
duration: 4 to 12 hours per week in summer
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 years old and able to finish the required training. No upper age limit is stated.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist on the Zoo's volunteer page. When applications open, go to an info meeting and an interview. You are invited to these. Then finish online and in-person training. You must also pass a fingerprint background check.
notes: Applications were closed when this page was read. A negative tuberculosis test may be needed for some advanced roles. Phone: (323) 644-4200.
duration: 25 hours per year for students (50 hours per year for other volunteers)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Los Angeles County residents, 16 to 18, who will be juniors or seniors in the 2027 school year and are interested in art, museums or community events.
how_to_apply: Online application during the open window (last year July 1 to Aug 21). Questions go to teens@lacma.org.
notes: Next year's dates are not posted. Watch for a July opening. LACMA also offers NexGenLA, a free membership for LA County youth 17 and under (free museum entry plus one guest). Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 10 sessions on select Sundays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Oct 2026 to Feb 2027
pay_detail: Selected teens receive a stipend. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: The page does not state an age rule. Call the museum to ask if teens can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Click Sign Up to Volunteer on the volunteer page (a Google Form). Phone 765-742-1128.
notes: No teen rules are posted, so confirm your age is allowed before you sign up. Museum is at 102 S. 10th Street, Lafayette. Admission is free.
duration: Event by event
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours verification papers provided.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 to 17 years old on June 1 of the year they apply. Teens interested in any career field may apply. A parent or guardian must co-sign the online application. A teacher or mentor recommendation form is part of the process.
how_to_apply: Read the Zoo Teen Information Packet, apply online through the zoo's volunteer form (applicant and parent both e-sign), and submit the teacher or mentor recommendation form. Contact: zooteen@lafayette.in.gov, 765-807-1543.
notes: Opening date for 2027 is not posted; the page only says check back in January 2027. The page mentions sponsors that keep costs low for participants but does not state a fee amount. The information packet was not read, so shift length and total hours are not stated here.
duration: Summer; shift details are in the 2026 Zoo Teen Information Packet (not read)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 9. Everyone under 18 needs a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. Ages 9 to 15 need an adult chaperone (1 adult for every 5 youths). Individual 16 and 17 year olds can volunteer without a chaperone. Groups of 16 and 17 year olds need chaperones (1 adult for every 10 youths). You must be at least 14 to volunteer at the Fresh Market.
how_to_apply: Create a VolunteerHub account (a parent or guardian creates the profile for a child), pick a shift on the volunteer calendar, and bring the signed waiver to your first shift. Questions: call 765-471-0062.
notes: Some shifts have their own age rules. A parent or guardian needs to make the account for anyone under 18. Court ordered community service hours need separate approval before you start.
duration: Single shifts you pick on the calendar
pay_detail: Unpaid. Training is given at the start of your first shift.

who_can_apply: The Franciscan Health page says volunteers include men, women and teens. Minimum age for Lafayette East is not stated; the system page says each hospital sets its own age rules. Ask the volunteer manager.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form on the Lafayette page. You can also call Lisa Green at 765-502-4249. She is the Volunteer Services Manager.
notes: Call to check the minimum age before you apply. The hospice program has its own form. It was not checked for teen rules.
duration: Usually once or twice a week for 3 to 4 hours, plus orientation and at least 2 days of training
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Grade 11 and 12 students at Harrison, Jefferson, Lafayette Virtual Academy, McCutcheon, Tippecanoe Online Academy or West Lafayette high schools. Home school and private school students who live in those districts can also apply. Other students may get leftover seats if their superintendent signs an agreement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Harrison, Jefferson, McCutcheon and West Lafayette students get the enrollment form link from their counselor. Everyone else fills out the online Enrollment Form on the Next Steps page.
notes: Competitive. Seats are ranked on attendance, behavior, credits, GPA and past courses, and GLCA makes the final call. Each program has its own prerequisites on its page. The pages do not say how long the day is, how transportation works, or what it costs.
duration: School-year program for grades 11 and 12; schedule not stated
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The academics page says students can earn college credit.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors from partner regional high schools. The page does not say how a student signs up, so ask your school counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Students take part through their partner high school.
notes: Check with your high school counselor to see if your school takes part.
duration: One day
pay_detail: Free event

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 who can pass a swim test (20-yard swim, 7 to 10 foot brick dive and carry, 2 minute tread, 300-yard swim). Limited to the first 20 applicants.
how_to_apply: Fill in the form online. You can also drop it off at the Parks Office, 1915 Scott Street in Columbian Park. Or sign up in the parks online catalog under the LIFEGUARD CERTIFICATION tab.
notes: Classes meet at the Lafayette Jefferson High School pool. The page does not name the year; the weekday dates match 2026. Pay for the lifeguard job is not on this page.
duration: Four class days in March and April (2026 dates were March 12 pre-test, then April 10 to 12) plus some online Red Cross work
pay_detail: $250 course fee covers the course, materials and Red Cross certification. $200 is refunded if you pass, get hired by Lafayette Parks and finish a full season. Job pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Kids and teens ages 7 to 17. A parent must sign the registration form.
how_to_apply: Get the registration form from the Parks Office in Columbian Park, or download it. A parent signs it. Hand it to the Workreation Coordinator on your first day. Call 765-807-1500.
notes: Good first volunteer step for younger teens. Not a paid job.
duration: 1 hour a day at Tropicanoe Cove, Vinton Pool or Castaway Bay (June 1 to July 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn one Kids Can Pass for each hour worked (good for city pool admission and Columbian Park rides).

who_can_apply: High school students who are current freshmen, sophomores or juniors. Apply through Purdue Summer College for High School Students.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Purdue Summer College for High School Students application and pick it as a short-term course choice. Questions go to Anna Egan (williaak@purdue.edu).
notes: Residential. Admission is not guaranteed and you list up to three course choices on the application. Prices are 2026 and may change.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 Summer College prices for a 1-week, 1-credit program: Indiana resident $725.80 (tuition plus room and board), out-of-state $1,326.25, plus a $60 non-refundable application fee. Scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade for Senior Camp. The page says the minimum age for camp is 12. Past campers cannot repeat the same camp.
how_to_apply: Online camper application on the Boiler Vet Camp page (not open yet). Ask for a scholarship inside the same application.
notes: Call the College of Veterinary Medicine at 765-494-7607 with questions. Camp fees are all-inclusive for the hands-on in-residence camps.
duration: 7 days (Senior Camp June 20 to 26, 2027)
pay_detail: Senior Camp is $1,600 and Junior Camp is $1,300. Partial scholarships are available and requested in the application.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. No other rule is stated on the camp page.
how_to_apply: Apply through Purdue's Summer College for High School Students (the camp page says the 2026 application was there). Questions: purdueag@purdue.edu.
notes: This is a camp, not a job, and it costs money. The Purdue ag summer programs index page describes the high school camp as a two-week experience. The camp page itself says one week. Confirm the length with purdueag@purdue.edu.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the camp page. Summer College for High School Students sets the price (see the Purdue Summer College card).

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 (the Pulsar level). New students send an essay or other media about their interest. They also send two of these. One is a transcript with a 3.5 GPA in the talent area. Others are a test score of 120 or higher on an intelligence test and a 90th percentile achievement or aptitude test. A teacher or mentor letter counts. So does proof of involvement such as awards.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application through the Purdue conferences site (the Register Now link on the page). Upload your essay or media and two supporting documents. Questions: geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. Checked against the GER2I summer residential page on 2026-10-10: the 2026 dates, the $2,990 Pulsar rate, the $100 application fee and the required application materials match. The page says registration for Summer 2026 is open and also says it opens February 2, 2026, so it is inconsistent. 2027 dates are not posted. Confirm with geri@purdue.edu or 765-494-7210 before you plan. The page also lists other prices ($1,250 commuter and $1,495 residential per session). They may be for the younger levels.
duration: 2 week sessions
pay_detail: 2026 listing: $2,990 per session for Star or Pulsar, plus a $100 application fee (refunded only if not accepted). Optional $100 Saturday field trip. A 5% early bird discount applied by Feb 17. A limited number of partial scholarships exist for students with financial need, first come, first served.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th, 10th and 11th graders. The 2025 page says the camp has a focus on high school female students. Age limit not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has an Apply Now link to the Summer College application page, but it shows no year. Contact techrecruit@purdue.edu or 765-494-4935.
notes: This page looks old (2025 dates). Check Purdue Polytechnic and the Summer College site for current dates and cost before planning. Offered with Purdue Summer College for High School Students. The 2025 page lists $350 per person, including activities, lodging, meals and a camp t-shirt.
duration: 1 week, 1 college credit (page lists June 23 to 27, 2025)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page checked for this card

who_can_apply: Rising 10th and 11th graders. Age limit not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has a Register Now button linking to the Summer College registration site, but it shows no year. Contact techrecruit@purdue.edu or 765-494-4935.
notes: This page looks old (2025 dates). Check Purdue Polytechnic and the Summer College site for current dates and cost before planning. The 2025 page lists $350 per person, including activities, lodging, meals and a camp t-shirt.
duration: 1 week, 1 college credit (page lists June 23 to 27, 2025)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page checked for this card

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Grade 8-12 Students Sign up for SMAP button on the page (a form). You are then notified about upcoming sessions.
notes: The SMAP page says the program is live on Zoom. The page does not mention cost. Check the sign-up form for the current format.
duration: About 1 session a month, third Saturdays at 11:00 a.m. Eastern
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering 7th or 8th grade in fall 2027. Selected through a competitive review.
how_to_apply: Submit a student application with a Statement of Interest essay, plus a teacher recommendation (a science teacher is preferred).
notes: For younger teens. Questions: Connie Kaspar, 765-496-6095, ScienceWISP@purdue.edu.
duration: June 20 to 24, 2027, residential
pay_detail: $600 registration fee covers residence hall, meals, snacks, labs and activities. Full payment due within two weeks of acceptance.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (Class of 2027 for the 2026 camp). Purdue recommends three years of high school math and one year of chemistry or physics by summer.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A complete application needs your PSAT, SAT or ACT scores and a transcript. Applications are taken until spots are full, then a waiting list. Questions: step@purdue.edu or 765-494-7217.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. Only for students going into their senior year. The page gives 2026 information, so check it for the 2027 cycle.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: Attendance fee $2,500 for 2026. It covers activities, housing, meals and local transportation. You pay your own travel to Purdue. Need-based scholarships are available after you are accepted.

who_can_apply: High school students. Main page says ages 15 to 17. Application page: priority for GPA 3.30 or higher and at least 16 who have finished sophomore year, younger students may apply. Residential courses require being under 18 for the whole program. Course-specific rules apply.
how_to_apply: Online Summer College application: essay, high school transcript, up to three short-term course choices, $60 non-refundable fee. Admitted students first get one course; more are offered as space allows in late March to early April.
notes: Costs are summer 2026 and may change. Some courses were full for 2026 and some were canceled. The listed short courses include PREFACE and MITE, which are pre-college engineering workshops, with their own eligibility. The student pays; this is not a job.
duration: 1 or 2 weeks, residential, June and July
pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: $60 application fee. Tuition and fees $347.85 per credit hour for Indiana residents ($948.30 nonresident). Room and board $377.95 for a 1-week program, $907.08 for 2 weeks. Some courses add $60 or $200 program fees. Scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Battlefield Museum, Genealogy Center and Collections roles say volunteers must be 18 or older. The Fort Ouiatenon, History on Tour and Feast pages do not state an age rule, so ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out a volunteer application and attend an interview. Every role needs on-site training, and no experience is required. Call 765-476-8411 or email info@tippecanoehistory.org.
notes: Ask the museum whether 14 to 17 year olds can take the Fort Ouiatenon or History on Tour roles.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid. At the Feast, participants may earn one badge per 8 hour shift.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 12 or older by May 31 of the program year. No grade rule is listed. The library's volunteer page is under its Teens section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form linked on the library's Teen Volunteers page, then attend one volunteer training day. Questions: Youth Department, 765-429-0119.
notes: The page was last updated for the 2026 season, so the next cycle should open in spring 2027 but is not posted yet. Check with the Youth Department before applying. Unpaid volunteering, so no Indiana work permit question applies.
duration: Summer Reading Club season; at least one 2-hour shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 3 to 12 can join a 4-H club in Indiana. Enroll through the Tippecanoe County Extension office.
how_to_apply: Create a family account and enroll each youth in 4HOnline 2.0 (links are on the county enrollment page). Call the Extension office at 765-474-0793 with questions.
notes: The county page gives two enrollment dates (Jan 15 and Jan 1), so ask the office which one applies. The Extension office is at 1950 South 18th Street, Lafayette, IN 47905. This is a youth club, not a paid job.
duration: Program year, enrollment starts Oct 1
pay_detail: $15 per child, $45 maximum per family. The fee covers insurance, project materials and club activities.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older and good with kids. Staff should be warm and friendly, able to do many things at once and good at talking with others.
how_to_apply: Apply on Indeed through the link on the YMCA jobs page.
notes: Postings change, so check that it is still listed. Some other Y jobs on the page need 18 or older. The page does not say whether Indiana working papers are needed.
duration: Part-time: Mon to Fri 4:00 to 8:30 p.m. (2 to 3 days a week), plus weekend mornings and subbing
pay_detail: $11.00 to $12.00 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens and kids ages 10 to 15.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for L.I.T. button on the page and check the program guide for fees and schedules.
notes: Only 14 and 15 year olds are in the high school range. The page links a summer schedule guide but gives no dates on the page.
pay_detail: Fees are in a program guide linked on the page and are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older. Those 18 and over also pass a background check and need a valid Social Security number. You commit to 150 hours a year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form (PDF on the page). Email it to the volunteer office, addressed to Julia Lieberman. Then go to a Volunteer Services orientation. You also need 2 TB tests and the required seasonal flu shot. The page does not mention an interview.
notes: Volunteer Office: (949) 452-3728, 24451 Health Center Dr, Laguna Hills. The application PDF is labeled an adult form; ask the office which form teens use.
duration: 150 hours per year
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a volunteer uniform jacket ($25) and pay $5 in dues.

who_can_apply: Youth from 9th grade through age 19. 4-H and non-4-H members are welcome. Non-members sign up in 4-H Online.
how_to_apply: Sign up through 4-H Online. Contact Darren Bagley, bagleyda@msu.edu.
notes: Dates are from 2025, so confirm the next session before you plan. The 4-H site (canr.msu.edu) blocked the research tool.
duration: 3 days. The listed session was March 16 to 18, 2025.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YSC Registration Form. Send it to davidm@allenneighborhoodcenter.org. That is David McCarthy, who manages programs for all ages. You can also call (517) 999-3913.
notes: The page does not say if teens are paid. Ask before you sign up. General phone: (517) 367-2468.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 8 to 15 can volunteer only with a parent or guardian (21 or older) who stays with them. Ages 16 and up volunteer on their own. Everyone must attend an orientation.
how_to_apply: Pre-register for an orientation on the shelter website and pay the fee. Then book each shift in the volunteer portal before you come in.
notes: The shelter does not give short-term or court-ordered community service hours. It will verify school hours only after you have volunteered at least 3 months. Seats are limited and a missed orientation can be rescheduled only once.
duration: Ongoing shifts. Shelter volunteer hours: 12 to 7 p.m. Monday to Friday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday.
pay_detail: Unpaid. A one-time program fee is due at sign-up: $30 for ages 16 and up, $15 for ages 8 to 15 (covers t-shirt and badge, non-refundable).

who_can_apply: The program page does not say who can join. Ask a coordinator (see How to apply) if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Contact a coordinator. The page lists Jennifer Fenning (Clinton County RESA, 989.224.6831 ext. 2314), Zoey Morton (Eaton RESA, 517.483.1370) and Pam Kunkel-Chappell (Ingham ISD, 517.244.1329).
notes: This is a school program, not a job.
duration: 3 years (11th to 13th grade)
pay_detail: Tuition is free.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 by June 6, 2026. The page describes its teen volunteer opportunities as for teens at least 14 years old and gives no upper age limit. You need to be free for two 2-hour shifts a week. Ages 14-15 and 16-17 each have their own work permit form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeen form and a work permit form. There is one for ages 14 to 15 and one for ages 16 to 17. Then go to orientation. Email lhutting@dewittlibrary.org with questions.
notes: The library requires a work permit form even though this is volunteering. Library is at 13101 Schavey Rd, DeWitt. The page also lists an At-Home Teen Service Hour Program for school-year hours.
duration: June, July and August (2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Community members. The page does not state an age rule, so ask before you go if you are under 18.
how_to_apply: Contact the Art and Stewardship Coordinator, Heather Majano. Call (517) 319-6804 or email hmajano@cityofeastlansing.com. You can also email the Stewardship Intern, Felix Shalev, at fshalev@cityofeastlansing.com.
notes: Wear long sleeves, long pants and shoes that can get muddy. Work is canceled in freezing weather or pouring rain. Good for community service ideas, but ask about age rules first.
duration: Work days are 10 a.m. to noon
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You can work at least 25 hours a week, with some weekends and holidays.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of East Lansing jobs page. You can sign up for job alerts there.
notes: Pay and dates are from the 2025 post, so check the 2027 posting. Michigan requires a work permit for workers under 18. From Oct 2, 2026 permits are issued through the state Youth Employment Permit Portal. Aquatic center is at 6400 Abbot Road.
duration: 2025 season: May 31 to Sept 1, 2025
pay_detail: 2025 pay: lifeguards $14.50 an hour, slide operators and customer service $13 an hour. A 2026 rate is not posted on that page, so confirm it.

who_can_apply: The library page says East Lansing High School students can log limited volunteer hours through the Teen Action Group. Ages are not stated.
how_to_apply: The library is not taking general volunteers, but TAG is the exception on its page. Contact Rheanna Reeder or Zandra Blake to ask if TAG is open and how to join.
notes: The detailed TAG description is from a May 2022 library post that the site marks as possibly out of date, so confirm meeting times and who can join with the library first. Page also says the library is not accepting general volunteers at this time. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 in the United States.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the FRIB PAN page when it opens in December. Two teachers write recommendations. Questions: constan@frib.msu.edu.
notes: 2027 dates are planned, not final.
duration: About 1 week in late July (2027: July 18 to 23, planned)
pay_detail: No cost. Room and board on campus are included if you need them.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 11 at a U.S. high school (including U.S. territories). You need a reference from a teacher or coach.
how_to_apply: Apply on nsbping.org when the 2027 form is posted. Name a teacher or coach as your reference. Questions: ping@frib.msu.edu.
notes: 2027 takes grades 9 to 11, not 12. PING 2026 ran online, so check how 2027 will run.
duration: 2 weeks in summer (2026: July 12 to 25, online)
pay_detail: No cost. Housing, meals and a flight for out-of-state students are covered.

who_can_apply: All volunteers must be at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Register once through Volunteer Hub, then pick a shift from the schedule. Groups of four or more email the volunteer program manager.
notes: Not teen-specific, but open to teens 14 and up. Warehouse shifts are 9 to 11 a.m. and 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. Monday to Friday, with some late afternoon, evening and weekend shifts at Mobile Food Pantries. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Single shifts; weekday warehouse shifts are about 2 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in 5th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Contact Micaela Balzer at (517) 485-8116 ext. 144 or balzer@impression5.org.
notes: The page lists only 2026 meeting dates. Ask whether the council is taking members for the 2026-27 school year.
duration: Monthly meetings, September through May
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members get free Impression 5 membership and free or discounted workshops and camps.

who_can_apply: Students working toward a high school diploma who finished 8th grade before their first college class. Homeschool students can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online as "High School Student (Age 14+)" or with your counselor. Turn on your account and set your placement levels. Hand in the Dual Enrollment Approval Form, signed by a parent and a counselor. Then go to orientation and sign the FERPA release.
notes: The LCC application asks for a Social Security Number. The page says it is needed for financial aid after you graduate high school.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Cost not stated. The page says many school districts cover some or all of the tuition, and homeschool students may self-pay.

who_can_apply: High school instrumentalists. The page does not list grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Send the Side By Side Audition form from the page. Questions: Ashleigh Lore, ashleigh@lansingsymphony.org.
notes: Dates are from the 2025 season. Check the page in fall 2026.
duration: Rehearsals and one concert in December
pay_detail: Cost not listed

who_can_apply: The page says all ages and experience levels are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the MCC sign-up form to get on the email list. Questions: Land Stewardship Coordinator at 517-853-4614 or ecampbell@meridian.mi.us.
notes: The township also runs a Vernal Pool Patrol citizen science program and short educational programs 1 to 2 times a month. It reported 415 members in 2025. Good for service hours; ask whether a signed hours form is available.
duration: Stewardship Saturdays are every other Saturday, 9:30 a.m. to noon. Weekday Warriors are every other Thursday, 1 to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 19 (the listing shows grades 6 to 12). The listing says to check with your county MSU Extension office about scholarship funds.
how_to_apply: The listing links to a page for details and registration, which could not be checked for this card. Contact on the listing: Michelle Neff, hydemich@msu.edu, 989-539-7805.
notes: The program's own 4-H page did not load for me. The Michigan State University College of Agriculture and Natural Resources site blocks automated readers. So this card rests on Michigan State University's Spartan Youth Programs listing only. Confirm dates, price and how to register on the 4-H page. It is a statewide event held in East Lansing, so it may also be listed as a Michigan-wide card. Not a job.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 24 to 26)
pay_detail: 2025 cost was $250 and a 2026 cost is not posted on the page. It covers meals, a shared dorm room, sessions and a t-shirt. Your county MSU Extension office may have scholarship money.

who_can_apply: U.S.-based students in grades 9.5 to 12 with a 3.0 GPA or above who are still taking at least one class at their home high school. Official transcript required.
how_to_apply: Pick a course from the Designated Course List, then apply on the Applying page. Questions: DEINFO@MSU.EDU.
notes: You cannot do dual enrollment at MSU in the summer right after you finish high school. Dual enrollment students cannot get MSU scholarships or financial aid.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: In-state freshman tuition: $588.50 for 1 credit, $1,177 for 2, $1,765.50 for 3, $2,354 for 4 (through Fall 2026). Books not included. Your district may pay part under state law.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12 (ages 14 to 18). The page does not state how many spots there are.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now link on the camp page. For financial aid, email Pete Johnston at john2950@msu.edu.
notes: Held in Wells Hall on the MSU campus. Bring your own sack lunch.
duration: One week, Monday to Friday 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM. 2026 dates were July 13 to 17.
pay_detail: $495 in 2026. Covers equipment, one group lunch, and the camp film link. Financial aid or scholarship is available.

who_can_apply: Co-ed. Open to U.S. and international students entering grades 10 to 12 in Fall 2027. You need a GPA of 3.0 or better in engineering core courses (math, sciences, technology). A transcript is required.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with your transcript. Payment by credit card is the last step. It is required before MSU reviews the application. If you are not accepted, the fee is refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
notes: Residential. Mentors supervise students in the dorms, and students cannot leave campus. Contact: future-engineer@egr.msu.edu or 517-353-7282 (from the college page). Check the year of the session dates against the application page when it opens.
duration: One week, residential. Four sessions: June 13 to 17, June 20 to 24, June 27 to July 1, July 11 to 15
pay_detail: $1,199 program fee (covers activities, room and board). MSU says it offers no scholarships for its pre-college programs.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 11. It is a program for gifted and talented students.
how_to_apply: Apply through the page on the MSU gifted programs site. Phone 517-432-2129, email gifted@msu.edu.
notes: Details come from MSU Spartan Youth Programs listing. The page (gifted.msu.edu) did not load for the research tool.
duration: One week. 2026 dates: Pre-Law June 15 to 19, Pre-Med Ed July 6 to 10.
pay_detail: Fee not stated on the program page. Financial assistance is listed.

who_can_apply: Co-ed, open to U.S. and international students entering grades 11 and 12 in Fall 2027 with a GPA of 3.0 or better in engineering core courses. A transcript is required.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript. Payment by credit card is the last step and is required before review. If not accepted, the fee is refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
notes: Residential with dorm supervision. Contact: future-engineer@egr.msu.edu or 517-353-7282. Check the year of the dates against the application page when it opens.
duration: One week, residential: July 18 to 23
pay_detail: $1,299 program fee. MSU says it offers no scholarships for its pre-college programs.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12 in the fall.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the MIPA page. Phone 517-353-6761, email ask@mipamsu.org.
notes: Details come from MSU Spartan Youth Programs listing. The MIPA site (mipamsu.org) blocked the research tool, so confirm dates and cost there.
duration: 5 days, in person at MSU
pay_detail: Fee not stated on the program page. Scholarships and fundraising help are available.

who_can_apply: High school students. Most sign up with a school team and an adviser.
how_to_apply: Your school adviser signs you up on the Register page. Email executive@msumun.org with questions.
notes: Western business dress is required. The site has a scholarship page.
duration: 3 days: March 19 to 21, 2027
pay_detail: Fees are in the Pre-Conference Advisor Guide and were not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Strong students in grade 9 or 10 in the 2025-26 school year.
how_to_apply: Apply through the page on the MSU gifted programs site. Phone 517-432-2129, email gifted@msu.edu.
notes: Details come from MSU Spartan Youth Programs listing. The page itself (gifted.msu.edu) did not load for the research tool, so check it for 2027 details. Financial aid is listed on sister programs, so ask.
duration: One week. 2026 dates: June 22 to 26.
pay_detail: 2026 program fee: $1,199.

who_can_apply: Students in high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Quantum Motor City Camp form. It is linked on the MSU Engineering summer programs page. Questions: Ryan LaRose, rmlarose@msu.edu.
notes: The card links to the camp's own page (ryanlarose.com), which gives the extended April 25 deadline. The MSU summer programs page, which lists several camps, still says April 18. The MSU page lists no GPA rule. The same page lists the paid High School Engineering Institute ($1,199) and a game design camp.
duration: 3 days, residential. 2026 dates: July 29 to 31.
pay_detail: Free. Paid for by the National Science Foundation, including on-campus housing and meals.

who_can_apply: Current 11th graders from partner school districts. These are in Lansing, Detroit, Flint, Grand Rapids, Saginaw, Muskegon and nearby towns. You are interested in teaching or in body movement science. The Spartan Youth page says you must have a 3.0 minimum GPA, and a transcript is required.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Write an essay of 500 words. Send your January transcript. Give your own email and a different parent email. Name a counselor or school leader who will back you. Do an online interview. Contact Kelley Johnson at johnsok1@msu.edu.
notes: Highly selective. The Spartan Youth page lists a 3.0 GPA minimum and says it is a free residential program.
duration: One week. 2026 dates were July 5 to 10.
pay_detail: Listed as free on the Spartan Youth Programs page.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults who have trouble finding work. This includes those with disabilities or court records. Embers is for girls ages 12 to 17 who have lived through trauma. Other age limits are not listed.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Use the Contact Us page on peckham.org. You can also ask your school or job help counselor.
notes: Peckham works with local schools and state job help offices. Ask if placements are paid.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 17 who can work independently, have reliable transportation to the zoo, and can work outside in all weather.
how_to_apply: Step 1: attend an information session. Step 2: complete the application you receive afterward. Step 3: attend orientation and the required training. Keep a journal and finish monthly prompts.
notes: The zoo's volunteer page says teens 13 to 18 use this separate program; the page itself says 13 to 17, so confirm the upper age. The regular adult volunteer program is 18 and older. Returning teens (years 3 to 5, under 18) can apply for the Zoo Teen Leadership Council. Contact is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: At least 40 hours of service from June to August
pay_detail: $50 program fee (shirt, training materials, name tag), paid at orientation, not at application. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Most placements need age 16 and entering junior year of high school. Some placements need volunteers to be 17, and the Radiology placement is for ages 17 to 18.
how_to_apply: Online application on the Volunteering at Sparrow page (or ask for a paper copy at Volunteer Services). Then onboarding (2 to 3 weeks), online orientation, and placement registration links sent to onboarded volunteers.
notes: Expect a criminal background check, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap immunizations (or titers), and a flu vaccine Nov to March; teens wear a provided smock apron and closed toe shoes. Volunteers must attend at least 75 percent of shifts. Free parking for active volunteers. Volunteer Services phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.
duration: One semester (10 to 12 weeks): one 2 hour shift a week in the school year, or two shifts a week (max 4 hours) in summer
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Five-Day Intensive: rising 5th through 12th grade. Advanced Workshop: rising 8th grade through college, by audition.
how_to_apply: The sign up link and audition details are not posted yet. Contact Kelly Stuible-Clark, stuible3@whartoncenter.com, (517) 884-3166.
notes: This costs money. Ask for financial aid on the registration form.
duration: Five days for the intensive
pay_detail: 2026 prices: Five-Day Intensive $450 (East Lansing). Advanced Workshop $1,125 with room and board or $775 off campus. Financial aid is available through Arts Within Reach.

who_can_apply: Michigan high school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email your script with the form to laurie.briseno@whartoncenter.com. Use a Word file with numbered pages and no student names. The form needs a signature from a parent or guardian, a teacher who backs you, and you. Plays have no more than 4 characters.
notes: The page lists the finalist announcement as Feb 26, 2026, which looks like a typo for 2027. No entry fee is listed.
duration: Festival performance Saturday, May 15, 2027, 2 PM, Pasant Theatre (free, public)
pay_detail: Each of the six finalists receives $200.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The page does not say which districts are eligible or whether outside students can enroll.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page (watch the tutorial video first). Phone 517-244-1330.
notes: Ask your school counselor how your district sends students here.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Cost not listed

who_can_apply: Oakland residents only. The City of Oakland MSYEP page lists youth from 14 through 21 in general, and some providers serve narrower groups. This card shows 16 through 21, which the pages checked did not confirm, so ask the provider.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 533-8850 or 1 (833) 532-3674, or use the Contact Us form at lfcd.org.
notes: LFCD's own employment page does not describe this youth program, so provider details were not confirmed there. Hours and minimum-wage pay come from the City of Oakland MSYEP page. Under-18 workers need a work permit.
duration: Up to about 100 hours
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage (MSYEP rule); exact rate not posted

who_can_apply: Teen Volunteer and Teens Leading Change are for ages 14 to 19. Teen Council is for ages 11 to 19. Volunteers fill out a Teen Volunteer Intake Form and a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
how_to_apply: Contact the Young Adult Librarian or Senior Librarian at your nearest library, then complete the intake form and parent waiver. Questions: Volunteer Engagement, 213-228-7490.
notes: LAPL hosts over 2,600 teen volunteers a year across 73 branches. Openings differ by branch. Some branches also have volunteer slots listed at volunteer.lapl.org.
duration: Varies by branch; Teen Council members complete at least 20 community service hours
pay_detail: Unpaid; you earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 12 years old. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the application.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer application. After you apply, the Volunteer Coordinator contacts you. This takes a couple of weeks. They set up your orientation. Email volcoor@lclsonline.org. Or call 307.773.7225.
notes: The library also has a Teen Zone page. A background check is required for volunteers age 18 and older.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 14. You do not need lifesaving or first aid skills. The program page asks you to be comfortable in the water and have basic swim skills.
how_to_apply: Pick a session on the program page. Use the register link for that session. The page does not give sign up dates.
notes: Sessions run Monday to Thursday, 1 to 4 p.m. This is a class, not a job. The program page footer says 2026, and the course numbers end in 26. It does not state the camp year. Phone 925-373-5700.
duration: 4 days, 3 hours a day
pay_detail: $100 for Livermore residents and $120 for non-residents.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign the Youth Volunteer Waiver. Students must attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation. Some roles have extra rules: Summer Nature Camp requires the Counselor in Training (CIT) program, and Open Space Jr. Docents require age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Create a LARPD volunteer account by submitting the General Volunteer Application (use a personal email, not a school email). Attend a Summer Youth Volunteer orientation at the Robert Livermore Community Center. Then sign up for shifts through MyImpactPage. Questions: volunteer@larpd.org.
notes: The 2026 cycle is closed. Watch larpd.org/volunteer and the orientation pages for the 2027 dates; the district's pages were not all updated to the same year. The FAQ says the opportunity list may change each year. The orientation and FAQ pages list volunteer@larpd.org as the contact. Not a paid job, so no California work permit is needed.
duration: Summer weekly shifts. The 2026 FAQ says sign-ups start with a maximum of 2 weeks, with more weeks added later.
pay_detail: Volunteer position. Earn community service hours; no wage is listed.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Ages are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Open the High School Academy application on the program page. It was open until April 30, 2026. Send questions to Mario Garcia, the Program Manager. His email is neomars@nmsu.edu.
notes: The same page lists a STEM Mavericks camp for high school students. It is a two week camp about public safety and disaster relief. Dates and cost are not stated on the program page.
duration: One week (June 1 to 5 in 2026)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 16 at hire. They need lifeguard training, first aid and CPR certification before hire. The page also lists 1 year of lifeguard experience. Student recreation aides must be 16, in high school, a junior or senior, with at least a 2.0 GPA.
how_to_apply: Look for lifeguard and student recreation aide jobs on the city job openings page. You must show proof of age, GPA and school enrollment when hired.
notes: The page says first pick for lifeguard jobs goes to people 18 or older. Lifeguard jobs have drug and alcohol tests under city rules. The same page lists a free after school Teen Connection program for grades 6 to 12.
duration: Part time and temporary for student aides. Hours vary. Lifeguard hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students in partner districts: Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton and Tri-Valley, plus San Ramon Valley USD (welding) and TUSD (fire safety training). Residency and citizenship rules apply; ask Admissions & Records.
how_to_apply: Sign the CCAP Dual Enrollment form with your school counselor. You sign it once for all of high school. Questions: lpc-dualenrollment@laspositascollege.edu.
notes: Offered during and after the school day. Ages are not stated on the page.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free; tuition and fees waived and required materials provided (parking may cost extra for classes at LPC)

who_can_apply: Teens in Las Vegas. The program page does not give an age or grade range. The registration form asks for your grade, school and a parent signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the program page. Ask your nearest teen council site for meeting dates and times. Questions: call the city at (702) 229-6113, the contact named on the program page.
notes: The registration form lists councils at several high schools and community centers. Check with the city for the current site list. A parent signs the form. The form says each council has an adult advisor.
duration: Year-round. Meeting days and times depend on the site.
pay_detail: Free. The city's registration form says activities are free of charge. It does not pay teens.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 to take the lifeguard course. Lifeguard, front desk and laborer jobs need you to be at least 16. You must pass a tryout swim and an interview.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the lifeguard class on the city registration site. Then apply online for the Hourly Lifeguard job. Call Municipal Pool at 702-229-6309 or Pavilion Pool at 702-229-1488 to set your tryout swim and interview.
notes: Pay rates come from the 2026 city flyer and may change. The flyer says you must register in person to get the class fee discount. Fees are waived for current city employees.
duration: Year-round and seasonal jobs
pay_detail: Lifeguard $15 an hour. Lifeguard with water safety instructor $16. Assistant $14. Laborer $14. Pool manager $18. East side pools add 50 cents an hour.

who_can_apply: People 15 years and older. A swim skills test is part of the process.
how_to_apply: Use the link on the program page to apply online. Then do the swim test: 50 yards of freestyle, 50 yards of freestyle with a rescue tube, tread water 1 minute without hands, and pick up a 10 pound object from the bottom.
notes: The county notice has no date, so check that hiring is still open. Phone: (702) 455-1708. County pools are different from City of Las Vegas pools.
duration: Seasonal pools are open to the public May to August. Other hours and dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Pay rate is not stated on the program page. Lifeguard training is paid.

who_can_apply: Boys and girls ages 13 to 17. You cannot have a history of discipline problems in Clark County programs. You cannot have been suspended or expelled from school this school year, or last school year if you apply for a summer spot.
how_to_apply: Fill out, sign and turn in two forms. They are the Teen Leader application and a Clark County Volunteer application. Then you have an interview with the Leader of the Future supervisor at your center. Contact your local center for details.
notes: Centers include Desert Breeze, Cambridge, Helen Meyer and Hollywood. Others are Moapa Valley, Paradise, Parkdale and Bob Price. Also on the list are Silverado Ranch, Walnut and Whitney. The last two are Pearson and Winchester Dondero. You are picked from the written application, the interview and open spots.
duration: New teen leaders can volunteer up to 15 hours a week in the school year and up to 20 hours a week during vacations.
pay_detail: Volunteer position.

who_can_apply: Students age 16 or older in a Nevada high school or homeschool program, with a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Some partner schools let students in grades 9 to 12 enroll. CSN may make exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CSN Admissions Application for High School and Early College Programs. You get an NSHE ID in 3 to 5 days. Then send placement scores for English or math, go to the online orientation, and sign up for classes.
notes: Classes are at the Charleston, Henderson and North Las Vegas campuses, at several centers, or online. Discount rates do not apply in summer. CSN also lists a CTE College Credit program. It gives free college credit for some high school career classes.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: For 2026 to 2027: $92.00 per credit plus an $11.50 per credit technology fee, plus any special course fees. No application fee. Check with your high school about payment.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at a high school that works with CSN on Jumpstart. You need a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. CSN may make exceptions with your school district.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CSN Admissions Application for High School and Early College Programs. There is no application fee. CSN emails you an NSHE ID. English and math classes also need a placement test or ACT or SAT scores.
notes: Partners include Clark County School District, charter schools and private schools in the Las Vegas area. Ask your counselor which Jumpstart classes your school offers.
duration: One course at a time, during the school year
pay_detail: $110 per course for the 2026 to 2027 school year, paid to your high school. Textbooks are free from your high school.

who_can_apply: Students in the ninth grade and above can join as Junior Members.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the program page. It links to jmprogram@cyberclinicofficial.org. Questions go to the same email.
notes: UNLV Early Outreach lists this program for high school students with weekly online workshops at no cost. The program page itself does not state the schedule, so ask before you plan around it.
duration: Not stated on the program page. UNLV's youth page says weekly online workshops.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program page. UNLV's youth page lists it as no cost.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form on the page. Watch for a confirmation email. Then go to a volunteer orientation, which is a must. Contact Volunteer@DiscoveryKidsLV.org or (702) 382-3445 ext. 110.
notes: The page does not say if a parent must sign. Teen volunteers are not presenters; you can apply for presenter roles at 18.
duration: Flexible schedule around school. Hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Page mentions community service hours or work experience.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17. You must have finished volunteer training in all 8 galleries and be an active volunteer in good standing.
how_to_apply: Meet the volunteer needs first. Then use the link on the page to the museum job page. Questions: volunteer@discoverykidslv.org or (702) 382-3445 ext. 110.
notes: You have to volunteer first, so start with the Teen Volunteer Program.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Page says paid but gives no rate

who_can_apply: Teens and young adults ages 16 to 24, in school or out of school. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Call 702.602.5199 or visit EmployNVYouthHub.org. The hub is at West Charleston Library, 6301 W. Charleston Blvd.
notes: Teens 16 and up only. The next-door Teen Zone is a separate space for ages 12 to 18.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Services are free. Paid training and internships are offered; pay not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. You need to read basic English and follow instructions.
how_to_apply: The page has a Volunteer portal link (app.betterimpact.com). You can also call (702) 734-READ (7323). It does not describe the steps.
notes: The page does not say if a parent signature is needed. Ask the library.
duration: 4 to 12 hours per week for 4 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Ages 14 to 15 can volunteer with a parent or guardian. Students needing service hours can use the student sign-up.
how_to_apply: Students use the Student Volunteer Sign Up at lvnhm.org/community-service-hours-request. Others use lvnhm.org/volunteer-application. Finish safety training. Call (702) 384-3466 for the steps for parent permission.
notes: The page does not describe the permission form for 14 and 15 year olds, so call first.
duration: At least 4 hours per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Students can earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 must turn in a parental permission agreement.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form with the Apply Now link on the page. Ages 14 to 17 also send in the parent permission form.
notes: Page does not mention training or required hours.
duration: Not stated. They want long-term volunteers; group projects can be one day or an afternoon.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Can count for community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17 who like health care careers. Only 25 are accepted.
how_to_apply: Use the Medical Explorer Application link on the volunteer page. It works only in the open window. Then you have an interview in person. To get in you need a background check, a drug test, a shot check and a TB blood test.
notes: Process can take 4 to 6 weeks. The summer 2026 window was March 2 to April 3, so check the page for the next summer window. Adults 18 and over use a different application.
duration: 12 volunteer hours a month in the school year, 8 hours a week in summer. Must attend 75 percent of post activities.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Kids 10 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them the whole time. Teens 16 and 17 may come alone with a signed waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the individual application to make an account. Then pick a session on the volunteer calendar. Ages 16 and 17 bring a signed waiver to every session.
notes: Wear closed toe shoes and knee length shorts or pants. Groups should book 4 to 8 weeks ahead. Volunteer office: 702-644-3663 ext. 349.
duration: Sessions you book on the volunteer calendar
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Current high school students with a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA. Juniors and seniors get preference.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form linked on the page. If you have questions, send an email to hospitalityadmissions@unlv.edu.
notes: The page says both a 3.0 GPA rule and that any current high school student can attend. Ask the college which applies.
duration: Monday June 21 to Friday June 25, 2027
pay_detail: $850, includes meals and on-campus housing. Scholarships available: email kaila.seidler@unlv.edu.

who_can_apply: Most camps took students entering grades 9 to 12 or 10 to 12, plus 2026 high school graduates. The archaeology camp took students entering grades 8 to 10.
how_to_apply: Each camp has its own online registration form, listed in the news article. For prices, email Mary Rose Stark at maryrose.stark@unlv.edu.
notes: This is a 2026 news article. Check UNLV for the next summer list. The 2026 camp dates were Mock Trial June 1 to 5, Witnessing History June 8 to 12, Justice Law and Society June 15 to 17, Pathways to Success June 22 to 26, and Archaeology July 6 to 8.
duration: Each 2026 camp ran 3 to 5 days.
pay_detail: Cost varies by camp. The cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders and select rising 8th graders from any high school. Outreach to Title I schools and students from groups with fewer opportunities.
how_to_apply: Use the Get More Info link on the page for the online form. Questions: 702-895-3375 or coe.yccr@unlv.edu.
notes: Page still shows the 2026 cycle. Expect applications to open around December again, and confirm with UNLV.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: $110 registration and enrollment fee. Scholarships available for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students in Southern Nevada. Students outside the area can join the live online option.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then send the Parent Agreement Form by the due date, by email to sistem@unlv.edu or by mail. If you are accepted you get a registration link, a health form and a liability form.
notes: The program page does not list the session dates. A parent must sign the Parent Agreement Form. Students outside Southern Nevada can join the live virtual session.
duration: 5 sessions. You must attend all 5 to get a certificate.
pay_detail: Free. The program page says there is no fee. It does not pay students.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 and enrolled in high school. You need a grade point average of 2.5 or higher, good English, and the ability to do tasks on your own.
how_to_apply: Download the teen application from the program page. Fill it out with a parent consent form, a school records release, and a teacher or counselor evaluation. After review you get an interview. Call the volunteer office at the hospital you want.
notes: The application lists these hospitals: Centennial Hills, Valley, Henderson, Summerlin, Spring Valley and West Henderson. You also need a health screening. That includes a TB skin test each year. You must go to an orientation. Summerlin Hospital volunteer office phone: 702-233-7532.
duration: Minimum 75 hours a year. The number varies by hospital.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. You must buy a volunteer shirt.

who_can_apply: Students entering their sophomore, junior or senior year of high school who are interested in architecture or design. Priority goes to students with financial need. It also goes to students from select Kansas City and St. Louis area school districts.
how_to_apply: Register online. Fee waiver applications have two short answer questions. They ask why you want to attend and what your extracurricular activities are. Ask for a fee waiver on the application if you need one.
notes: There are optional bus rides to and from Lawrence. Fee waiver recipients from Kansas City get them.
duration: One week. 2026 dates were May 31 to June 6, 2026.
pay_detail: $1,000 (housing, meals, studio fees, materials and evening activities), with a $150 deposit at registration. Fee waivers are available for a select number of students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th and 10th graders go to the July 11 to 16, 2027 camp. Rising 11th and 12th graders go to the July 18 to 23, 2027 camp. Everyone stays overnight in the residence hall, even if they live nearby.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens in February. Send questions to the camp email. It is on the page.
notes: The page says all students must stay overnight. Check the page for cost and the theme once posted.
duration: One week each (two camps in July 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12. Adults 18 and over use a different application. The library says it does not offer community service hours at this time.
how_to_apply: Fill out the VolunTeen application when it opens. Then go to a one-hour new volunteer orientation, a 15-minute interview, and a 1.5-hour training shift with a mentor. Questions go to the Teen Librarian at the email on the page.
notes: Quote from the page: we do not offer community service opportunities at this time. So this is not for court or school-required hours. There is also a VolunTeen Youth Program Assistant (Summer) position.
duration: One-hour shift each week, evenings and weekends, for a semester (option to extend)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Grades 10 and 11. Public school students in Alameda, San Francisco and Contra Costa counties are prioritized; nearby counties are encouraged to apply. In person at Berkeley Lab at least 4 days a week for 6 weeks.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Berkeley Lab K-12 page when it opens (the 2026 application ran through apply.mykaleidoscope.com).
notes: Whether students are paid is not stated. Finishing students can join later workshops and possible lab internships in following summers.
duration: June 16 to July 24, 2026 (6 weeks, 4 days a week)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page (no stipend listed)

who_can_apply: Grades 10 to 12 in Northern California, at least 16 by the program start. Students within 30 miles of the lab are prioritized. You can do the program only once.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window and pick your top three projects. Do not contact mentors directly. Oakland Unified students also complete the ECCCO common application.
notes: The page still says 'at least 16 by June 16, 2025', so check the age date when it reopens. Some 2026 projects were hybrid or virtual. Under-18 interns need a work permit.
duration: 6 weeks (June 15 to July 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: $500 per week for 30 to 35 hours

who_can_apply: English-learning, native Spanish-speaking bilingual students.
how_to_apply: Watch the Berkeley Lab K-12 high school programs page.
notes: Grades and ages are not listed on the page. The 2026 camp is over and no 2027 camp is posted, so it is not confirmed to repeat. Page says it can lead to summer internship chances.
duration: April 8 to 11, 2026 (spring break)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 30. Youth@Work is for ages 14 to 24 and WIOA-funded services are listed for out-of-school youth ages 16 to 30. WIOA funding focuses on out-of-school youth with barriers such as low income, foster care, homelessness, juvenile justice involvement, parenting, or a disability. A Long Beach residency rule is not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Complete the Youth Interest Form on the city's Youth Services page. Partner agencies can also refer youth through the Unite Us platform.
notes: Because most WIOA funding targets youth facing barriers, a teen still in school may be steered to Youth@Work or a school-to-career program instead. Under 18 you need a California work permit for any paid placement. The city's Youth Opportunities page also lists teen volunteering at Long Beach libraries and at Parks, Recreation and Marine (ages 13 and up).
duration: Varies by program
pay_detail: Paid internships and Youth@Work (about 160 hours of paid work experience). Pay rates are not stated. Workshops and career help are free.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. The page does not state a residency rule for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the Register to Volunteer link for the teen volunteer call on the League site, or email lov@lov.org. Phone (510) 793-5683.
notes: The teen call on the homepage is for summer 2026. Confirm with the League whether it recruits again for 2027. Serves the Tri-Cities (Fremont, Newark and Union City).
duration: The 2026 summer recreation program ran July 6 to July 30, 2026, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., at Mayhews Landing Park in Newark.

who_can_apply: California high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. A select number are chosen.
how_to_apply: Apply through the LegiSchool website application. Join their mailing list for contest, town hall and internship news.
notes: The application link and 2027 dates are not on the page. The stipend amount is not stated. LegiSchool also runs Town Hall meetings in downtown Sacramento. It also runs video and essay contests for California high school students.
duration: 4 weeks, Mon/Wed/Fri afternoons (2026: starts June 22)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after the program. The amount is not posted.

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add a short essay and a high school transcript. For aid, a school or community counselor emails a letter about your need to BASE@bucknell.edu before the deadline.
notes: Questions: BASE@bucknell.edu or 570-577-3000. Check back in the fall for 2027 details.
duration: About 6 days (2026: June 21 to 26)
pay_detail: $1,750 (2026), covers housing, meals, instruction and activities. Need-based aid is available.

who_can_apply: Age 16 and 17 through the Minor Program. A parent must attend orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. The Volunteer Manager will email you a background check. Finish it. Then wait for an interview and orientation. Call Volunteer Coordinator Daniela Rakes at 859-230-5026.
notes: The page says volunteers must be 18, or 16 for the Minor Program. Ask the coordinator which jobs minors can do and whether the barns are open to them.
duration: No minimum hours. Barn shifts run 8:30 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 4:30. Park representative shifts run 9:00 to 1:00 and 1:00 to 5:00.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school youth. The council is always accepting new members.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Register for the Neighborhood Youth Council form and list your school so you get its meeting schedule. Council Ambassadors also meet outside school hours.
notes: The page lists 2 phone numbers, 859-280-8004 and 859-280-8006. Confirm which one to call. There are 4 elected roles. They are Council Ambassador, Secretary, Treasurer and Parliamentarian.
duration: Meetings at each high school during school hours
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Anyone age 14 or older. Volunteers ages 14 to 17 need permission from a parent or guardian. The parent or guardian also signs the application online.
how_to_apply: Use the online volunteer form. Have a parent or guardian sign it. Then do a screening with the Volunteer Coordinator, an orientation and any training for your role.
notes: Background checks apply to volunteers 18 and older. The page has no separate teen program.
duration: Agreed when you are accepted. Teen roles may need less time.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Lexington youth who will be in grade 10, 11 or 12. The page gives no age range and no more residency rules.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the online form. To get first pick for a summer job, finish the online Skills Sessions. Also go to the Career Fair, Verification Clinic, Parent Orientation and Youth Worker Orientation.
notes: Partners for Youth is at 162 E. Main St., Suite 210, Lexington, KY 40507. Phone 859-280-8006. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. Ask the office.
duration: 6 weeks, June 14 to July 24, 2027
pay_detail: $15 per hour, up to 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: High school students at schools in districts that take part. Talk to your guidance counselor in grade 9 or 10.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor if your district takes part. Districts that want to join can email jumpstart@uky.edu.
notes: The page does not list which districts take part. The program page says students who continue at BCTC can finish a healthcare associate degree in two years or less. A UK HealthCare scholarship has a work-back agreement, but students can choose another path with no commitment.
duration: Grades 11 and 12 coursework
pay_detail: Dual-credit courses can reduce or remove the cost of college. A UK HealthCare tuition scholarship after graduation comes with a work-back commitment. Pay while in school is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who apply to the yearly summer program. Selected teens are told by mid-April.
how_to_apply: Watch the UK HealthCare volunteer page for the next form. The steps are a packet, an interview in person and health checks. Health checks are a TB risk check and blood test, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap, and a flu shot in flu season. Call Volunteer Services at 859-323-6023.
notes: The page says adults over 18 need a background check and drug screen. Teens do not. It also says volunteering here does not lead to a job in the University of Kentucky system. The office cannot offer internships or job shadowing. The page was updated Aug 3, 2026.
duration: Summer. Adult volunteers commit to at least 2 hours a week. The teen schedule is not posted.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade. You must be able to work full time all summer. You must go to May Saturday trainings.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Lawrence Hall of Science teen internship page when it reopens; questions to lhscamps@berkeley.edu.
notes: The page URL says 2024 but the content is the 2026 posting. The page says to apply next summer; 2027 dates are not posted. Mid-January is the 2026 pattern only.
duration: June 1 to Aug 7, 2026, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; Saturday trainings in May
pay_detail: $3,500 for the full summer ($72 deducted per missed day)

who_can_apply: Page lists teens entering 9th grade or above, or at least 14 years old, who are not current volunteers. The age wording is tied to June 1, 2024 and may be outdated. No current rules posted.
how_to_apply: Check the Lawrence Hall of Science teen volunteer page; call 510-642-5132 or mail/deliver forms to the Volunteer Program, attention Veronica Urdaneta, 1 Centennial Drive, Berkeley, CA 94720. The page lists no youth volunteer email.
notes: The page says recruiting is paused and a re-imagined program is planned for 2026, with no dates. Its Apply Today teen link conflicts with the pause notice, so do not treat it as active. Call to ask whether the program has launched. The age rules come from 2024 wording, so the age fields are blank. The email veronicau@berkeley.edu was removed because neither page lists it.
duration: Summer minimum 21 hours; school year two 3-hour shifts a month

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 and up. Anyone under 18 must have a parent or a named adult with them at all times during orientation training. Youth cannot handle animals.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer account with the Become a Volunteer link on the page. Then go to orientation at a shelter with your parent or guardian.
notes: A parent or designated adult must be with you at all times through orientation. The page does not list the shelter addresses in the text read. A COVID-era section mentions remote projects for younger kids, but it may be outdated, so it is not listed here.
duration: Ongoing. Orientation first, at one of three shelter locations.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 12 in fall 2027. Past members are not guaranteed a spot back.
how_to_apply: Apply when the window opens, choosing the Animal Care track or the Education track. Questions go to the Education Team at the number on the page.
notes: The page lists a $250 per session fee. Education track volunteers work with the summer camp program.
duration: Session dates for 2027 not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Any cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Anyone who has finished 5th grade and is under 19 (teen track). You also need approval from the City of Lincoln Human Resources Department.
how_to_apply: Download and print the Minor Volunteer Application (under age 19). Fill it out. Then contact the Volunteer Coordinator at the library branch you want. Expect a 1 to 2 week wait before you hear back.
notes: Library address: 136 South 14th Street, Lincoln, NE 68508. Phone 402-441-8500. Branches may not be taking new volunteers, so call first. Tasks also listed for National Honor Society and Government and Politics students needing 10 hours.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: one meeting a month, August to May. VolunTEEN: 1 to 2 times a week during Summer Reading Challenge (May, June, July). School groups: 10 hours or more in a semester.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. You must meet WIOA income and barrier rules and enroll in the YESS Program before you are placed.
how_to_apply: Apply to the City of Lincoln job posting for the program. Staff at the American Job Center then contact you to check if you qualify. After you enroll, you are matched with a City department. Call 402-441-7975 with questions.
notes: The page does not mention work permits. Weekly workshops and possible tuition help are listed.
duration: June 4 to July 29 in 2026
pay_detail: $16 per hour plus a $200 bonus for finishing. Up to 30 hours a week. You also get a free Chromebook.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. The page text still says the 2026-27 school year, so check the grade rule for 2027 camps. This is not a commuter camp.
how_to_apply: Pre-register by the January deadline. This helps you get priority scholarships. Then register online when registration opens in February. Space is limited. It is first come, first served, with a waitlist.
notes: Camper limits are small (15 to 20 per camp for the camps listed). The page lists the years only as 2027 in the heading, so confirm the Dec 18 and Jan 22 dates are for the 2026-27 cycle. Contact: the Big Red Camps email on the page.
duration: One week: June 6 to June 11, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition for the camps listed: $625 to $850 for the week (early, regular and late rates vary by camp). Housing and food are included. Scholarships are offered.

who_can_apply: Lincoln-area high school students who are 16 by June 1 and have not graduated. U.S. citizenship is required. May 2025 graduates are eligible if they attend UNL in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application on the program page. Ask one teacher to send a reference by the deadline. Students who apply to several summer research programs can only do this one if picked.
notes: Work days are Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. The page does not mention work permits.
duration: About 8 weeks, starting June 2 in 2026
pay_detail: $15 per hour, 20 hours a week (2026)

who_can_apply: High school students interested in computing. The page does not list grades or ages. The page says the camp is designed for students with little to no computing experience. Students planning to start college in fall 2027 get priority based on total applications.
