how_to_apply: Send a short essay, your coding level, your school grades and a school transcript. You can add a scholarship request. The page points to an Apply Online page on the Raikes site.
notes: Students who expect to start college in fall 2028 are considered if they finished pre-calculus before camp. Contact is 402-472-9097.
duration: 2 weeks (July 19 to August 1 in 2026)
pay_detail: $3,000 in 2026. Nebraska high school students get $1,000 off, so $2,000. The fee covers housing, meals, teaching and activities. Full and partial scholarships are offered.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. The city code says ages 12 to 20, best if at Livermore schools. You must come to meetings and events.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Recruitment Application Form on the Youth Council page. Ask the city when it is due.
notes: The city code still calls it the Livermore Area Youth Advisory Commission.
duration: One school year. Three absences count as quitting.
pay_detail: No pay is stated.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 6 to 12 in the 2026-27 school year. You must live in Livermore. Each applicant needs a separate account and email.
how_to_apply: Click Fill in an application on the volunteer page. If you already have an account on the library volunteer portal, log in. You must go to an orientation and log your hours in your account.
notes: The program page does not give start and end dates, orientation details or the number of hours. Ask the library before you apply. The listing is for summer 2026, so look for the next summer posting.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not mention community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18 years old by June 1. No experience needed. You must be friendly and professional with guests.
how_to_apply: Fill out the ZooTeen application online (link on the page), then go to orientation. Phone: 760-346-5694.
notes: Requires attending ZooTeen orientation. Address: 47900 Portola Avenue, Palm Desert, CA 92260.
duration: Two shifts a month and monthly meetings; a 4-year program, and you can serve one year or all four
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Cost not mentioned.

who_can_apply: High school students in 9th through 12th grade in the Inland Empire who are interested in health sciences. Students 17 and a half or older may be invited to an optional shadowing week.
how_to_apply: Submit the application form, a recommendation form from a teacher or clergy member, a 200-word essay on your interest in health sciences, and the $30 fee or a waiver request.
notes: Closed until the next cycle opens. Loma Linda University is a Seventh-day Adventist institution.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to July 24), plus optional shadowing week
pay_detail: $30 non-refundable application fee (fee waiver available for financial need). The page does not list a program cost.

who_can_apply: Active middle or high school students who meet each course's prerequisites. No minimum GPA is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply free on OPENCCC. You get your Viking ID by email. Then turn in the High School Dual Enrollment Form with all signatures. Finish New Student Orientation with a score of 80% or higher on the final test. Then register once Admissions confirms your form.
notes: Students who stop attending for two main terms must reapply. Taking college classes does not affect Long Beach College Promise eligibility. To take extra units, file the Unit Max Petition.
duration: By term
pay_detail: Tuition and enrollment fees are free. Course material fees, textbooks and supplies are not covered (a Textbook Loan Program exists for hardship).

who_can_apply: Two seats are for youth under 19 at the time of appointment. Each youth is picked by their district councilmember and appointed by the Mayor.
how_to_apply: The page has no application. Ask your district councilmember's office or the city contacts listed on the page.
notes: Only two youth seats exist. Meeting location was listed as to be decided. Contacts on the page include ashleigh.griset@longbeach.gov and erika.Medrano@longbeach.gov.
duration: 2-year terms (up to 4 terms); meets every other 3rd Wednesday at 6 p.m.
pay_detail: No pay is stated

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. Must be at least 15 by July 1, 2027. Capped at 15 cadets.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the Cadet Tryouts Sign Up form on the page. Bring a resume. Pass a physical tryout: a 1000m open water swim in about 20 minutes and a run-swim-run in about 10 minutes. Then do an interview. Questions: LBJG@longbeach.gov.
notes: Very physical. Tryout date and calendar may change, so email to confirm. LBUSD students with at least one year of cadet experience can apply for a separate LBUSD Cadet Internship (details not on this page). The page header says the tryout date is not set but lists April 26.
duration: Summer; the 2026 cadet calendar is listed as not set
pay_detail: Cost or pay is not stated on the page

who_can_apply: People ages 13 and over.
how_to_apply: Use the online 'Apply to Volunteer' link. It is in the BetterImpact portal. For questions, call (562) 570-3226 or write to prmvolunteers@longbeach.gov.
notes: The page does not list hours or what each role does. Ask which sites take 13 year olds.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 years old. If under 18, you must have a valid permit to work.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Here for Recreation Jobs' link, which goes to governmentjobs.com (search for recreation). Tech help: (877) 204-4442.
notes: Pay rates are as posted on the page (the page does not date them). Under-18 applicants need a valid permit to work. Ask the department which level a first-time worker starts at. Accommodation requests: (562) 570-3188.

pay_detail: Hourly by level: $16.76 (Specialist III), $17.31 (IV), $18.09 (V), $20.87 (VII). The level depends on your qualifications.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form linked on the library's volunteer page. Questions: lbpl_volunteers@lbpl.org.
notes: Hours, locations and training are not listed on the page. Ask by email.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 as of February 27, 2027, and living in the City of Long Beach during the program year.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You answer five short questions. You also send a CV of up to 4 pages, a bio of up to 100 words and 5 poems (up to 10 pages). Paper applications go to LS-YPL@longbeach.gov or Teen Services at the Billie Jean King Main Library. Info sessions are Saturdays, Dec 12, 2026 and Jan 23, 2027, 12:30 to 2:00 PM at the Main Library. To reserve, email LS-YPL@longbeach.gov. Walk-ins are welcome.
notes: Poets must also take part in the National Youth Poet Laureate program and attend most monthly workshops. Mailed packets must be postmarked by Feb 27, 2027. Prize is a scholarship, not wages.
duration: May 2027 to April 2028
pay_detail: $1,500 scholarship for the Youth Poet Laureate; $500 scholarship for each of 4 Youth Poet Ambassadors

who_can_apply: New Mexico youth ages 14 to 25. The page says jobs are open to this age range in general.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Get 2 character reference forms from people who are not family. Then interview. Paper forms can be turned in at the YMCA or the Los Alamos or Espanola Teen Centers. Questions: lzollinger@laymca.org.
notes: The page says the 2026 grant award status was pending. The page does not state a wage.
duration: 2026: crew members June 1 to July 24
pay_detail: Paid jobs. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students who are in school during the 2026-27 year.
how_to_apply: Online Teen Docent Program application, linked from the museum site (closed for 2026-27). A 2024 article says selected applicants are called in for a brief interview.
notes: Phone 650.948.9427; the page gives no email address. Pay is not stated on the current official page, so we list it as unpaid based on a 2024 article; confirm with the museum. The lahstalon.org article is a 2024 news piece, used only for the interview and volunteer details. The museum's adult docent roles are separate and not for teens.

who_can_apply: High school students. Ages and grades are not stated.

notes: Ask about ages, the application date and whether any stipend is paid. The permit field is false only because it is described as a free program, not a job.
duration: Dates not on the program pages
pay_detail: The page calls it a free program.

who_can_apply: Youth who were in foster care at any time from age 16 to 18, or who meet a few guardianship rules. An ILP coordinator checks that you qualify.
how_to_apply: Call the Transition Aged Youth helpline at 877-694-5741 or email youthds@dcfs.lacounty.gov. Ask for an ILP coordinator.
notes: Call first to ask what you qualify for. Foster Youth Helpline: 877-846-1602. If you are in danger right now, call 911. The page does not mention the ETV college voucher; ask your coordinator about it.
pay_detail: Not a job. The page does not list a cost.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 12 through 24.
how_to_apply: Call 323-908-0011 or 1-888-YOUTH-50, or email info@myfriendsplace.org to ask about hours and how to start.
notes: This is a support center, not a job. Details on its education and job help are not on the program pages, so call. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: The site describes its resources as free.

who_can_apply: The page header says ages 13 to 19 and the FAQ says ages 15 to 19, so ask which applies. Sign-up is required and seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the sign-up form on the Teen Auto Workshop page when a date is posted. Adults who bring a teen under 18 must stay in the museum.
notes: A one-day workshop, not a job. Check the page for the next date.
duration: One session on select Saturdays, 10 am to 2 pm
pay_detail: Free to join. Museum admission is required.

who_can_apply: Youth experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The age range is not stated on the program pages.
how_to_apply: Call 310-902-2283 or email info@safeplaceforyouth.org. The site is at 2471 Lincoln Blvd, Suite 101, Los Angeles. General hours are Mon to Thu 9:15 to 7:00, Fri 9:15 to 6:15, Sat and Sun 9:30 to 3:30.
notes: Ask when you call what ages they serve, because the pages do not say. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: A paid internship through the Community Garden is mentioned. The pay rate is not stated. Cost to join is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who have finished at least 9th grade by the start and take a rigorous course load. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a 300 to 500 word essay, a teacher or counselor recommendation, a transcript and the application fee. You can rank up to three courses but you take one. Join the email update list for 2027 news.
notes: Expensive. Prices and deadlines above are the summer 2026 numbers; the 2027 numbers may change. The pages did not give an age limit.

pay_detail: Summer 2026 prices: tuition $7,401, materials $300, program fee $325, health center $104. Total $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential, plus an $85 application fee. No financial aid was mentioned. 2027 prices not posted.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th graders at a high school in the program. The page names the AUSD, LUHSD and PUSD districts. You need a signed Dual Enrollment Authorization form from a parent and your counselor. Your principal must recommend you. You do not need to be in a special program.
how_to_apply: Go to your high school counselor for the form and the steps. Get the signatures from a parent and your counselor. Your principal must recommend you.
notes: The page says it was last updated 3/15/22, so ask your counselor to confirm the steps. Grades from these classes go on your college transcript. You can also take other Los Medanos classes on your own time as a concurrent student, with principal approval. You pay all fees and costs for those concurrent classes.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Free. The page says there are no course costs and no textbook costs. Your school district pays for textbooks.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old or already started ninth grade. Needs a parent or guardian signature and a recommendation from your high school principal.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, pick the Los Rios college that offers the class, apply at that college as a dual enrollment student (parent signature and principal recommendation needed), then register.
notes: Credits go on a permanent college transcript. Whether you also get high school credit depends on your school, so ask your counselor. Your school does not need a CCAP agreement for you to take a college class. Application deadlines are by college term.
duration: Per semester
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Other fees may apply, such as the student representation fee. Books may cost extra.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Look for teen openings in the Loudoun volunteer portal. Then send the PRCS volunteer application.
notes: Questions: 703-777-0343. Also see PRCS Connect (bit.ly/PRCSteens) for current teen programs.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens who live in Loudoun County. The page lists recruiting high schools but gives no age or grade range.
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Ask through the contact form on the page or call 703-777-0343.
notes: The page does not say when applications open next year.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not listed

who_can_apply: Loudoun County high school juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Send the Youth in Government Day application online. The page has a JotForm link.
notes: Held at Douglass Community Center and the Loudoun County Government Center, both in Leesburg. The page does not mention a later date.
duration: One day, 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.
pay_detail: Cost not listed

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers must be at least 14 years old. You must be in school now or have graduated recently.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online junior volunteer form. If you qualify, you get an interview. You also get onboarding details. Then you meet the coordinator before you start.
notes: Call the Volunteer Office at 502.896.7388 for session start dates. The program page does not say what the oldest age is. You can join more than one session.
duration: Each session is about 7 to 8 weeks. You must serve at least 6 weeks.

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and older can join any shift on their own. Younger teens need a guardian. Mobile Pantry: 8 and older with a guardian. Main Distribution Center: 14 and older with a guardian, or 12 and older in a group. Community Kitchen: 15 and older with a guardian. Senior Outreach Warehouse: 12 and older with a guardian.
how_to_apply: Make an account on the Dare to Care volunteer site. Pick a shift from the calendar. Groups send a group volunteer form instead.

duration: Shift by shift. Shift lengths are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. A teen who turns 13 during the calendar year can apply. Each teen fills out their own form. The museum cannot accept a form filled out for someone else.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Interest Form yourself. Returning volunteers sign up for weeks by email. Write to education@fraziermuseum.org.
notes: Camp dates, hours and the number of weeks are not on the program page. You only fill out the form once, even if you return in later years.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 13. The form asks for a parent name, an emergency number and a parent signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application and choose a branch. Finish a Workers' Compensation form in person at the branch before you start. Call 574-1611 and ask for the volunteer coordinator at your branch.
notes: The page says volunteer hours may be tracked and shared with the Library Foundation. The branch phone number is listed on the page as 574-1611.
duration: Not stated. Availability choices on the form are after school and Saturdays.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 23. You must be enrolled in school full time.

notes: Call the volunteer office at 502-566-5141 with questions.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students.

notes: One-time online event. The event page links to a recording of the October 21, 2025 summit.

notes: Rehearsals are at 616 Myrtle St. Ask about scholarships on the camp page. The company also offers a camp called The Mechanicals for ages 15 to 18, which costs $195 for 1 week or $295 for 2 weeks.

pay_detail: $495 for the five-week program. The camp page links to scholarship information.

who_can_apply: High school students who care about fair treatment of all people and can lead. You need good attendance, grades and conduct. You must be able to meet 2 evenings a month at the Ali Center in downtown Louisville.
how_to_apply: Students must apply, but the page does not describe the steps. Use the Contact us link on the Youth Leadership page.
notes: Past spring break trips listed on the page include Chicago, St. Louis and Washington, D.C. The fall retreat is at Camp Piomingo in Brandenburg, KY. The page says the program is free.
duration: School year, two meetings a month plus three group trips
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Forest Restoration is open to ages 18 and older, or 16 and older with adult supervision. The page lists no age rule for groundskeeping, so ask.
how_to_apply: Click the Volunteer Today button on the volunteer page. Fill out the form and sign the volunteer waiver. For teen roles, send an email to info@louisvillenaturecenter.org or call 502-458-1328.
notes: The page gives no separate hours or rules for youth. The rule for ages 16 and up with adult help applies to Forest Restoration.
duration: Forest Restoration work days: Wednesdays and Fridays (10 a.m. to 1 p.m. in warm months, 1 to 3 p.m. in cold months). Groundskeeping: Monday to Friday and most Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Pick a hospital and use its summer teen application.
how_to_apply: Choose a Norton hospital. Fill out its Summer Teen form on the Norton volunteer page. Then contact that hospital's volunteer manager.
notes: Norton Audubon, Brownsboro, Hospital, West Louisville, Women's and Children's, and Norton Children's Hospital each list a teen form for ages 14 to 17. Norton Women's and Children's also has a school year teen form. Norton Scott lists no teen program. The page says only some hospitals take teen volunteers all year. Openings are limited. The page says hospital volunteers must pass a background check and health screen. It does not say if that applies to teens.
duration: Not stated. The student program takes less time than the adult program, which asks for 6 months at 2 to 4 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Young people who live in Jefferson County. The program page says ages 16 to 19. A 2025 news post from the same group said ages 16 to 21, counted on June 1.
how_to_apply: Register at summerworks.org, finish the Job Readiness training, then apply for jobs. Create or upload a resume on the site.
notes: The two pages give different top ages (19 and 21), so check the age rule when registration opens. Pay rate, hours and work permit rules are not stated on either page. Ask the program.
duration: Summer. Length is not posted.
pay_detail: You earn a paycheck. No hourly rate is posted. Private employers pay the youth they hire directly.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16 by June 1 of the program year and have taken at least one advanced science course. You need your own bank account for pay and a way to get to the Health Science Campus each day. Students related to Brown Cancer Center faculty cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Email the form to the program coordinator. Add an unofficial transcript. Add two letters of recommendation. One is from a science teacher. Finalists are interviewed online.
notes: A faculty committee picks who is interviewed. The program page does not say where you must live. Ask the coordinator at ashley.kareken@louisville.edu. The program page lists the 2026 pay and dates. They may change.
duration: 9 weeks, at least 30 hours a week (2026: June 1 to July 31)
pay_detail: $3,500 stipend for the 2026 program. The Brown Cancer Center pays other costs.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18. You need consent from a parent. You need a recommendation letter and an essay. You need shot records (2 MMR, 1 varicella) and a QuantiFERON TB blood test.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. By the deadline, send an essay (at least 1 paragraph), a letter of recommendation, consent from a parent and shot and TB records.
notes: The main volunteer page says volunteers must be 16 or older. They need a flu shot from October to April. Questions: VolunteerServices@UofLHealth.org (the program page lists no phone number).
duration: Two-week sessions. In 2026: UofL Hospital June 15 to 26 (8 a.m. to 2 p.m.), Shelbyville Hospital June 9 to 20 or July 7 to 18 (8 a.m. to 3 p.m.), Mary & Elizabeth June 16 to 27 (8 a.m. to 1 p.m.).
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Leaders-In-Training is for ages 15 to 16. Counselors-In-Training is for ages 16 to 17.
how_to_apply: Leaders-In-Training: the program page lists the sessions and price tiers. Counselors-In-Training: enrollment is by application and then an interview. A monthly payment plan and financial help are offered.
notes: This is a paid program for the teen, not a job. The program page does not name the camp town. Check the session dates before you plan, because the year is not shown.
duration: Leaders-In-Training is 2 weeks. Counselors-In-Training is 3 weeks.
pay_detail: Leaders-In-Training costs $1,515 to $1,850 and Counselors-In-Training costs $1,435 to $1,750, depending on the price tier. Kentucky sales tax of 6 percent is added. Financial help is offered.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 years old by the last day of the course.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for Lifeguard Training button to see open courses. If none are listed, call your local YMCA branch.
notes: Course sites include Norton Commons and Oldham County, plus Clark County, Floyd County and Southeast branches. The program page does not say if work papers are needed for the job. Prices can differ by location.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: The course starts at $175 for Y facility members and $225 for program members. The fee is refunded if the Y hires you as a lifeguard (hiring length rules may apply). The job pay rate is not posted.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. All volunteers need a current TB (tuberculin) skin test.
how_to_apply: The page points to the zoo's volunteer form. To ask about the teen program, send an email to the Coordinator of Volunteers at mary.taylor@louisvilleky.gov. Or call 502-459-2181.
notes: The zoo page lists no season or hours for the youth program, so the season shown is a placeholder. It also describes a separate 50-member Zoo Youth Board for students ages 13 to 18. It does not say how to join, so ask the volunteer coordinator.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Park clean-up age 10 and up (10 to 14 with an adult). Mini-camp assistant age 13 and up. School field-trip assistant is 18 and up.
how_to_apply: The 2026 summer mini-camps are at capacity for volunteers. Fill in the online volunteer form on the page and choose the position.
notes: The page does not say whether applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. A police check is not stated on the program page.
duration: Mini-camp: at least one full camp. Clean-up: up to 1 hour a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free pin, a yearly certificate and a membership discount.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 10. Open to Club members and non-members.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Formstack application linked on the page.
notes: Hours vary by age group. Location: 5215 Verona Road, Fitchburg, WI.
duration: 7 weeks, 60 hours total (June 22 to Aug 7 on the page), Tuesday to Thursday
pay_detail: $500 stipend and 0.25 school credit

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th graders (and college students) who are Boys & Girls Club members.
how_to_apply: Separate high school and college application forms are linked on the page.
notes: This is only for Club members. Schedules and places vary by placement.
duration: About 8 weeks (June 22 to Aug 14 on the page)
pay_detail: At least $15 an hour

who_can_apply: Teens and young adults ages 14 to 21 (from the Briarpatch home page). The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Complete the online referral form on the program page. Questions: yjc@briarpatch.org, or call or text (608) 444-9413.
notes: The home page says the program also gives information on work permits, but no permit rules were read. Office: 2720 Rimrock Road, Fitchburg.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay rates are not listed. Placements are described as giving income.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 living in the Madison, WI area.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Apply Today online form. Then go to Hiring Day. Questions: 608-298-6949.
notes: Earns up to 5 MMSD or Sun Prairie high school credits and two digital badges. Occasional extra weeknight or weekend work.
duration: Spring 2027: Wednesdays March 3 to May 5, 4:30 to 7:45 pm
pay_detail: $14.00 an hour for new ambassadors, $14.50 for returning ones.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12. Age rules are not listed.
how_to_apply: Click Register on the page. For a scholarship application email the contact on the page or call 608-298-6949.
notes: Prizes at the pitch event are $1,000, $500 or $250. Need-based partial scholarships are available. Call 608-298-6949 for an application.
duration: Saturdays, Feb 13 to April 17, 2027, 10 am to 2 pm
pay_detail: $160 to join. Need-based partial scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 living in the Madison area. Must have finished a CEOs of Tomorrow program, taken a school business course, or be in DECA Business Club.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Today on the internship page. Questions: 608-298-6949 or the Contact Us page.
notes: Participants earn 2 Madison College Prior Learning Credits at no cost and may earn up to 2 MMSD high school credits. The page lists weekdays with its dates, and they match 2027 (May 22, 2027 is a Saturday; June 15, 2027 is a Tuesday).
duration: Summer 2027 plan: June 23 to Aug 27 (15 to 24 hours a week)
pay_detail: Stipend of up to $1,800 for coursework and internship work. No fee listed.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. Ages 8 to 13 can volunteer with a caregiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form on the page, clear a background check, interview (in person, Zoom or phone), attend orientation, then sign up for shifts on Sign Up Genius.
notes: Volunteer Coordinator: Tim Gruber, tgruber@madisonchildrensmuseum.org. Spots may be limited at any given time, so email before you apply.
duration: One 2-hour shift each week for at least two months
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 on or before the last day of the training class. You apply and get hired before you attend the class.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City of Madison job listings. Go to the Job Descriptions and Apply Online section of the page. Look under the Parks Division.
notes: The page says the pool reopens in June 2027, which does not match its 2026 class dates, so confirm timing with Madison Parks. Work permit rule for Wisconsin minors not checked.
duration: Summer pool season; paid certification class in spring
pay_detail: Lifeguards start at $18.75 an hour. Head lifeguards start at $20.52.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 3 to 12. Each camp lists its own grades, based on grade level in fall 2027.
how_to_apply: Add the camp to the cart on the registration site and enter the student information. Look for the scholarship form on the page.
notes: The camps on this page are at the Madison campuses. The college lists camps at Fort Atkinson, Portage, Reedsburg and Watertown on a separate page.
duration: Camps run 9 am to 3 pm; length varies by camp
pay_detail: Cost is listed for each camp. Lunch and snacks are included. A limited number of scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 20 who are behind in credits for their age, have a low GPA, and want to earn a diploma and start college classes. High school counselors refer students. Must commit 1 to 3 years and keep a C average.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor, apply online with three writing prompts and your transcript, take the ACCUPLACER placement test, interview, then a committee decides within five business days. Contact 608-243-4597 or gatewaytocollege@madisoncollege.edu.
notes: The page says the program serves ages 16 to 21 in one place and 16 to 20 in the eligibility list. Check with the program.
duration: About 2 to 3 semesters on average
pay_detail: Not a job. The program covers tuition and books for up to 14 credits a semester. Students pay student fees. They also get a bus pass and $7.50 a day for lunch.

who_can_apply: Ages 8 to 17 with a parent or guardian permission. Ages 13 to 17 may volunteer solo, but openings are limited. Younger kids must come with an adult.
how_to_apply: Read the youth volunteer page, check current openings for youth positions, and sign up through the shelter volunteer process. The shelter can give a letter of completion for school service hours after six months.
notes: Shifts for ages 8 to 17 fill up quickly. The page lists other ways to help for teens who cannot do a six month shift.
duration: Most positions ask for a 6 month minimum commitment
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 15 to 21. If you are under 18, a parent must sign a separate form.
how_to_apply: Make a MyImpact volunteer account. If you are under 18, use a separate form. Fill out the waivers. They cover rides, a yearly background check and the YV4C behavior pledge. Then sign up for a shift. Contact Grace Coleman at (608) 228-2590.
notes: The event page lists only the Saturday, Oct 10, 2026 session (1 to 3 pm). Check MyImpact or call the coordinator at (608) 228-2590 for new session dates.
duration: Single sessions of about 2 hours (the one listed was Oct 10, 2026, 1 to 3 pm)
pay_detail: Volunteer, free

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 (the page says the high school programs serve grades 9-12). Other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact the program: TEENworks Manager Trevor Moores or High School Manager Vernon Hill (608-204-8039), or the center at 608-241-1574, info@goodmancenter.org.
notes: Confirm pay, hours and whether enrollment is open by phone. Address: 214 Waubesa St, Madison.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Hourly wage; the rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Individual students ages 16 or older. High school groups can contact Habitat about a project.
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us to Get Started link on the youth engagement page.
notes: The page says nothing about rules for younger teens. Contact Habitat to ask.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 at the start of the program. Residency is not stated. Teens need reliable transportation to and from the zoo.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form (Google Form linked on the page). Optional Zoom info sessions were held in February. Questions: education@henryvilaszoo.gov.
notes: The page still shows the Summer 2026 schedule, so the 2027 dates are a guess based on last year. The page's email link points to volunteer@henryvilaszoo.gov while the text says education@henryvilaszoo.gov, so check both. Phone on the page: 608-266-4732. Not a paid job.
duration: 8 weeks, two days a week (June 22 to Aug 21 in 2026)
pay_detail: $200 per teen for the summer. Scholarships are available. Applying is free and payment is due only after you are invited.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 can volunteer on their own in many roles. Ages 10 to 14 can only volunteer with a parent or guardian, and only in some roles (gate greeters, goat yard, events, wildlife champions). The youngest age for any role is 10, with a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Pick a role on the zoo's Volunteer Roles page and fill out the application at the bottom of that role's page. Join the volunteer email list through the Volunteer Inquiry Form to hear about openings and information sessions.
notes: If you need school-required hours, check with your school counselor first. The zoo does not currently support court-ordered community service hours.
duration: Seasonal; commitment varies by role
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo does not do last-minute school hour confirmations.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from the Madison area who care about the arts.
how_to_apply: Not described on the page. Call MMoCA at (608) 257-0158 to ask when the next application opens.
notes: The page may be out of date (it mentions the 2025 group), so confirm by phone before planning around it. Small group.
duration: 6 to 8 hours per month, in person at MMoCA, through the year
pay_detail: Members are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Juniors at an MMSD high school at the time of application.
how_to_apply: Send the online student application. You also need a note from a science teacher, a second note and a parent consent form. Questions: Kristen Riddle, sriprogram@madison.k12.wi.us.
notes: You must attend a March orientation with a parent or guardian and all seminars. Only for MMSD students.
duration: 9 weeks, 20 to 25 hours a week
pay_detail: The page does not say if it is paid. Students earn one UW-Madison college credit and high school science and experiential learning credit.

who_can_apply: MMSD juniors and seniors. You must pass an interview with an employer to get a placement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your Youth Apprenticeship coordinator or school counselor, join the Google Classroom, go to Workplace Success Workshops, do an intake screening, then interview with employers. Coordinator: Annie Johnston, ajohnston2@madison.k12.wi.us.
notes: The page does not name a year for February 13, so confirm the date. Related cards cover the Dane County and state youth apprenticeship programs.
duration: Program length not stated on the page. Explore runs October to December; interviews run March to July.
pay_detail: At least the state minimum wage. The page says students typically earn about $15 an hour on average.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 in the Dane County area. Juniors and seniors need a referral from their home school. MMSD applicants must be entering the fourth quarter of junior year before applying.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Legacy page (opens a Google Form). Seniors and juniors also need a referral from their home school.
notes: Free program. Staff mentor graduates for one year after completion. Phone (608) 244-4721, info@operationfreshstart.org, 2670 Milwaukee St, Madison. The program starts at 16, so the Wisconsin permit rule for 14 and 15 year olds does not apply to it.
duration: At least 1,000 program hours (total length not stated)
pay_detail: Bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated). Finishers may earn an AmeriCorps Education Award of about $2,800 for college.

who_can_apply: The form has an age category of '17 and under', and the page says teens can volunteer to complete school hours. A minimum age is not stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form (area of interest, availability, branch). Staff reply by email. A background check is required under City of Madison APM 2-44.
notes: On Oct 9, 2026 the page said Central Library had no openings and asked high school students needing hours (for example National Honor Society) to check back in fall 2026. Alicia Ashman, Hawthorne, Lakeview and Meadowridge listed no openings or a waitlist. Ask a branch before counting on hours.
duration: Varies by branch
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 17. Ages 12 to 15 must have an adult chaperone (21 or older) for the whole shift. Ages 16 and 17 can volunteer without a chaperone.
how_to_apply: Register in the Second Harvest volunteer portal and sign up for a Food Sort/Repack shift. Bring a youth waiver signed by a parent or guardian to each shift. Questions: volunteers@secondharvestsw.org or 608-216-7214.
notes: Groups with youth should add (YOUTH) to the group name when signing up.
duration: Per shift; length not stated on the page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12 from Wisconsin, across the U.S. and abroad. Admission usually looks at advanced coursework, a 3.2 unweighted GPA or similar, and essays. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application with two essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,750; commuter $2,850; international $5,100; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).

who_can_apply: The page says adults and teens interested in nature education can serve as assistant naturalists. No exact age is stated.
how_to_apply: Contact volunteer program manager Judy Kingsbury at (608) 262-5604 or judith.kingsbury@wisc.edu.
notes: Drop-in restoration work parties run most Saturday mornings from mid-February through mid-December. Check the Arboretum events calendar for times. The page does not state a minimum age for them.
duration: Camp sessions; schedule not posted
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Badger Dairy Camp registration form when it opens. Questions: badgerdairycamp@ansci.wisc.edu.
notes: Students stay in the Dejope Residence Hall, two to a room.
duration: 4 days (2026: July 8 to 11)
pay_detail: $175 non-refundable registration fee covers housing and dining. Grants and sponsors cover the rest.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay when you sign up. Send scholarship forms to info@precollege.wisc.edu.
notes: The page shows 2025 dates, so confirm the next session.
duration: 4 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays 6 to 8 pm (Oct 21 to Nov 13 in 2025)
pay_detail: $480. Full and partial scholarships available; Wisconsin students on free or reduced lunch can apply for a full scholarship.

who_can_apply: Students finishing grades 9 to 12. Admission usually looks at a 3.0 unweighted GPA or similar, coursework, interest in the course and essays. No age range is stated. The page lists tuition for domestic and international students and says students connect with peers from across the country.
how_to_apply: Online application with two short essays (about 500 words total) and an unofficial transcript. Decisions come on the 2nd and 4th Monday of each month.
notes: Full scholarship for Wisconsin residents who get free or reduced lunch; partial scholarship (up to 50%) with income paperwork; none for international students. Funds are limited and first come, first served. Contact info@precollege.wisc.edu or 608-890-3260.
duration: About 2 weeks (July 19 to 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026: domestic residential $4,450; commuter $2,600; international $4,800; plus a $100 application fee (fee waivers can be requested). Scholarships exist (see notes).

who_can_apply: Eligibility is not stated on the web page. It points to separate Program Details and FAQ files. Check them before applying.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts, two essays and a letter of recommendation. Questions: Mary Headington, education@cancer.wisc.edu.
notes: Pay and who can apply are in linked PDF files that were not checked for this card. This is a different program from HERO.
duration: 2026: June 15 to Aug 7
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin high school students going into freshman, sophomore or junior year. You must be a full time student. You need a strong interest in research or cancer jobs. Students from rural school districts get priority. Past SHE participants are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two personal statements of up to 250 words each. Someone who is not family must fill out a reference survey for you.
notes: You need a reliable computer and internet. Some money for tech is offered.
duration: 2 weeks (July 20 to 31 in 2026), weekdays 9 am to 1 pm
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend for full participation. No fee is mentioned and lab materials are provided.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Need at least a year each of algebra and geometry, a 3.0 unweighted GPA and a strong interest in math, science and engineering. Highly selective.
how_to_apply: Online application, a high school transcript and a recommendation form. Questions: esp@engr.wisc.edu.
notes: Students live in Dejope Hall with supervision from staff and undergraduate counselors. Laundry and vending cost extra.
duration: 3 weeks (July 11 to 31 in 2026), residential
pay_detail: Free: housing and meals included. No stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 and up who can commit to at least one full semester.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Wisconsin volunteer application on the UW Health volunteer page when it opens. Onboarding takes several weeks: online trainings, health assessment, placement interview, caregiver background check.
notes: Health clearance is required: seasonal flu shot, MMR, varicella, Tdap and a TB blood test. The page says waivers and exemptions are not accepted. Volunteer Services: (608) 263-6046, volunteer.services@uwhealth.org. The same page also covers Illinois locations; this card is for the Wisconsin application.
duration: At least one full semester
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students enter in 8th grade and plan to attend a participating school. The page says Madison Metropolitan School District students need at least a 2.75 GPA and must submit an application.
how_to_apply: Submit a PEOPLE Precollege application through the program site.
notes: Entry is at 8th grade, so most teens who find this are already past the usual start. Ask about joining later. A separate PEOPLE Milwaukee track starts in 9th grade.
duration: 8th grade through high school graduation
pay_detail: Cost and any internship pay are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores or juniors with a 3.0 GPA or higher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add a PDF transcript and two short answers of 150 to 300 words each on why you like pharmacy. Contact PharmD@pharmacy.wisc.edu or 608-262-6234.
notes: Check the PharmD events page for the PSP 2027 announcement.
duration: 5 days (July 12 to 16 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Domestic and international high school students with a high-intermediate (B2 or higher) level of English.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now link on the course page.
notes: After the first four weeks the course meets once a week. Two optional office hours with instructors.
duration: January 18 to April 1, 2027. Live Mondays and Thursdays 7:00 to 8:30 pm CST and Saturdays 9:00 to 10:30 am CST
pay_detail: Per student: $450 individual, $375 in a two-person team, $325 in a team of three or four.

who_can_apply: Students who are finishing grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Sign up online. For questions, write to summerartsclinic@precollege.wisc.edu or call 608-263-2242.
notes: You can stay on campus or come each day as a commuter.
duration: 1 week (July 12 to 18 in 2026)
pay_detail: Residential $1,275; daily commuter $875; plus a $75 nonrefundable fee. Need-based scholarships are limited.

who_can_apply: Students who are finishing grades 9 to 12. At sign-up, everyone picks a placement audition or a talk with staff.
how_to_apply: Register online. Questions: smc@wisc.edu or 608-263-2242.
notes: The Violin Institute has room for only 12 students. It needs a recorded audition. The date was April 1 in 2026.
duration: 1 week (June 28 to July 4 in 2026)
pay_detail: Residential $1,275; daily commuter $875; Violin Institute $1,500; plus a $75 nonrefundable registration fee. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th and 10th grade students interested in business. Preference goes to first-generation college students and students who get free or reduced lunch, but others can apply and may be waitlisted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the precollege page. If accepted, a parent signs waivers and pays the fee.
notes: Not residential: families arrange their own housing and transportation. Apply by the end of April, but programs can close when full.
duration: 4 days, June 14 to 17, 2027, 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: Nonrefundable enrollment fee; the amount is not posted. Email wsbprecollege@wsb.wisc.edu about fees and financial help.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in business. Preference goes to first-generation college and low-income students.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the precollege page.
notes: There is also a one-day workshop on April 10, 2027 called Her View, Her Voice (applications Dec 1, 2026 to Mar 26, 2027).
duration: 1 day, Nov 14, 2026, 9:30 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: Enrollment fee amount is not posted (lunch is provided). Email wsbprecollege@wsb.wisc.edu.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students interested in business. Preference goes to first-generation college students and students who get free or reduced lunch, but others can apply and may be waitlisted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the precollege page. If accepted, a parent signs waivers and pays the fee.
notes: Past field trip sites named on the page include Trek Bikes and Epic. Not residential.
duration: 4 days, 9 am to 4 pm. Session 1: June 21 to 24, 2027. Session 2: June 28 to July 1, 2027
pay_detail: Nonrefundable enrollment fee; the amount is not posted. Email wsbprecollege@wsb.wisc.edu about fees and financial help.

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 14 years old when they apply. They must live in the City of Madison limits or attend a Madison Metropolitan School.
how_to_apply: The library page does not list application steps. Call Madison Public Library at 608-266-6300 or Common Wealth Development at (608) 256-3527.
notes: The library page says the program has mandatory pre-internship training and weekly professional development during the internship. The Common Wealth Development website was under construction when checked, so confirm details with them before applying. The library page does not state the age 14 minimum, the Madison residency rule, the pay rate or the hours; confirm these with Common Wealth Development before applying.
duration: 8-week summer internship. The library page does not give dates.
pay_detail: Wages start at $15.50 an hour, about 20 hours a week (2026).

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in south central Wisconsin (job centers in Dane, Sauk and Jefferson counties). Whether in-school youth qualify is not stated.
how_to_apply: Go to a free info session. It is listed on Eventbrite from the page. Or visit a Job Center, or call 608-249-9001.
notes: Eligibility rules (such as income) are not on the page, so call before you count on a paid placement.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Free. The page says all WorkSmart Network services are free of charge and does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in participating Dane and Jefferson county school districts. Employers choose and hire apprentices.
how_to_apply: Contact your school district's School to Career Coordinator (the page lists a name and phone for each district, for example Madison Metropolitan: Annie Johnston, 608-663-5384). Register for an information night on the program page.
notes: The page lists the Jan 20, 2027 information night, but its registration link address ends in Jan202026, so confirm the date with the program. Students interested in UW Health need the Feb 17 session. Main office 608-249-9001. Ask the coordinator whether your age needs a Wisconsin work permit.
duration: 1 or 2 years
pay_detail: Paid while working; wage not stated.

who_can_apply: Rules differ by event. On the 2027 events list only one event (hackPHS in New Jersey) is marked High School. The Fellowship page gives no age or student rule. Read each event page.
how_to_apply: Browse the events list on mlh.com and read each event's age rule before registering.
notes: The pages did not state a minimum age. Many MLH events are aimed at college students, so check before you plan travel.
duration: Weekend events; Fellowship is 12 weeks
pay_detail: Event costs are not listed on the program pages; check each event. The Fellowship pays a stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who like livestock and related careers. Students from across the country can apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form on the program page. Questions go to the academy director at 785-532-1272.
notes: Only 20 students are accepted. You stay in campus housing with program staff.
duration: 4 days (June 10 to 13 in 2026)
pay_detail: $50 fee to hold your spot, due only if you are accepted. A livestock industry group pays for the other costs. You pay your own travel.

who_can_apply: Students going into their sophomore, junior or senior year of high school.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Here link on the program page. Email kstateag@k-state.edu or call 785-532-5736 with questions.
notes: Each extra brunch guest costs $15. Check the page in spring 2027 for new dates.
duration: 5 days (June 9 to 13 in 2026)
pay_detail: $75 per student in 2026. It covers 4 nights in a K-State residence hall, all meals and a Saturday brunch for up to two guests.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in health care careers. Small groups of 20 students per session.
how_to_apply: Join the 2027 Interest List on the program page. The college says details are added as they become available. Questions: College of Health and Human Sciences, phone number on the page.
notes: Quote from the page: Join our 2027 Interest List. The page does not show application dates yet.
duration: One week, June 2027 (two sessions planned). In 2026 the sessions were June 7 to 12 and June 21 to 26.
pay_detail: 2027 cost: not yet posted. The page does not state the 2026 cost.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list a grade or age rule.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Now link on the program page. For a scholarship, use the Apply for Scholarship link on the same page.
notes: The page calls it a three-day program but lists June 24 to 27. Check the dates when 2027 registration opens.
duration: June 24 to 27 in 2026
pay_detail: $800 in 2026. A limited number of scholarships are offered for students with financial need. Kansas and Kansas City area students get priority.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The page lists 12 spots.
how_to_apply: Join the 2027 Interest List linked on the youth programs page. Details are added when available.
notes: The same page also lists Farm to Fashion. It is for grades 7 to 12, June 28 to July 1, 2027, with 15 spots and cost not yet posted. It also lists a free one-day Social Impact Lab for grades 7 to 10 in spring 2028.
duration: June 7 to 10, 2027
pay_detail: Cost not yet posted

who_can_apply: The high school day is for students entering grades 9 to 12, and college students. Other days are for younger grades.
how_to_apply: Registration for 2026 is closed. The program page does not say how next year signs up. Check it again in spring 2027.
notes: Check-in starts at 8:30 am and camp starts at 9:00 am. Parents may come in for check-in and the 4:00 pm closing.
duration: 1 day for the high school group (Monday, July 27 in 2026). Other grade groups came July 28 and 29.
pay_detail: $125 per camper in 2026. Lunch and snacks are provided.

who_can_apply: Young volunteers who go to school. The application asks about your school schedule and clubs. A parent must sign if you are under 18. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Junior Docent Application PDF (link on the volunteer page), with a short bio. Call 951-902-5949 or email volunteerinfo@marchfield.org.
notes: Museum address: 22550 Van Buren Blvd, Riverside. Ask the volunteer office about the youngest age they accept.
duration: You pick 1 to 6 days a week or 1 to 7 days a month; shifts are Tue to Sun, 9 AM to 4 PM
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: In school: ages 14 to 21 and low income. You also need one more need. Examples are foster care, homelessness, a disability, or being an English learner. Out of school: ages 16 to 24 with a need listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: Check that you qualify. Gather a photo ID that shows your date of birth and your Social Security card. Create an Arizona Job Connection PLUS account. Visit the client portal first. Career centers are in Mesa, Glendale, Surprise and Tempe.
notes: Not every teen qualifies. You must meet the age and need rules. Services are free. Pay for work experience is not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Services are free. Some youth get paid work experience. The program page does not give the pay rate.

who_can_apply: At least 14, in high school, and not yet 21. A 2.0 GPA or higher if still in high school. Must be a U.S. citizen, pass a background check, physical test and written exam, and have written parent approval if under 18.
how_to_apply: Email bmarshall@mariettaga.gov to RSVP for a meeting. Attend 4 monthly meetings in a row and fill out the welcome packet. Then you get a background check, interview and a 3-month trial.
notes: The web page says ages 14 to 21; the requirements sheet says applicants must be under 21. The web page says meetings run Thursdays 6 to 8 pm, while the requirements sheet says 6 to 9 pm, so confirm the hours.Meets at 240 Lemon Street, Marietta, GA 30060. Phone 770-794-5355 or 770-794-5300 (ask for the Community Response Unit). The sheet says the fee goes to Learning for Life, Scouts BSA. Not a paid job.
duration: Meets about 3 Thursdays a month, 6 to 9 pm. Attend at least 2 a month, plus 5 volunteer hours a month.
pay_detail: Not a paid job. You pay a yearly membership fee and buy part of the uniform. Competition travel costs up to $250 per trip.

who_can_apply: High school students, college students, teachers and recent graduates can join. Students under 18 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian to go on the in-person tour. Say in your application if you are under 18.
how_to_apply: Join the mailing list with the form on the program page. You will get an email when the next session is announced.
notes: The program is free to join. In-person events are optional, because you can take part fully online. Central San works with Contra Costa Water District on the program. Central San is at 5019 Imhoff Place, Martinez.
duration: In 2026: four partial days over two weeks in February
pay_detail: Unpaid. You pay for your own travel and meals.

who_can_apply: Students who are 16 or older and are in school now or going back in the fall. If you have not graduated from high school, a work permit must be obtained.
how_to_apply: Apply in the first two weeks of March. The page does not say where to apply, so ask Central San. If you have not graduated from high school, a work permit must be obtained.
notes: Summer students are at-will, short-term workers. They do not get benefits or a promise of a regular job. When school is not in session, a minor can work up to 8 hours a day and 40 hours a week. Central San is at 5019 Imhoff Place, Martinez. The internship programs on the same page are for college students.
duration: Up to four months
pay_detail: $30 per hour

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors in Maryland public high schools. The state page does not give an age or hour rule (local school systems may add rules).
how_to_apply: Join through your high school, then apply for open positions with participating employers.
notes: More than 2,000 high school students have taken part since 2016. State office phone 410-767-2246.
duration: Part-time during high school. Length not stated.
pay_detail: Paid part-time apprentice positions. The wage is set by the employer and is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students living in the Chesapeake Bay watershed (Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Washington DC). Summer Expeditions are for rising 9th to 12th graders. No past experience needed.
how_to_apply: Use the contact form on the CBF page or call 410-268-8816. Registration for Summer Expeditions opens in early January.
notes: Earns service-learning hours at restoration events. Ask CBF about cost and scholarships for expeditions.
duration: Year-round program. Summer Expeditions last several days.
pay_detail: Not stated. Costs for Summer Expeditions are not on this page.

who_can_apply: People currently enrolled in high school or college, or graduated within one year of the start date. Needs a 2.5 GPA on an unofficial transcript. Postings have a high school minimum requirements section.
how_to_apply: Apply on the state jobs site (jobapscloud.com/MD). Send a state application, a resume, two letters of support from people who are not relatives and an unofficial transcript. If none are open, fill out the Internship Interest Form to get news. Contact: julie.kline@maryland.gov.
notes: Internships are posted by park, office or program. The places vary around the state.
duration: About 10 to 12 weeks (summer June to August, fall October to December)
pay_detail: Some are paid, some are volunteer. Check the Salary section of each posting.

who_can_apply: Anyone 11 or older (11-year-olds must be in sixth grade). The form has a teen option. The library has no court-ordered community service spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the library page and pick a preferred branch (Brunswick, C. Burr Artz, Emmitsburg, Middletown, Myersville, Point of Rocks, Thurmont, Urbana or Walkersville).
notes: Opportunities vary by branch. Hours and length are not posted.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students from the Mid-Atlantic region. The program page gives no ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Maryland Forestry Foundation. Use the camp link on the Maryland DNR page.
notes: The only page checked was a 2025 notice. Ask the Maryland Forestry Foundation for the current dates, ages and cost.
duration: 1 week (July 20 to 26 in 2025)
pay_detail: Tuition and fees are listed on the camp website (not read). The page says Maryland students may get some costs covered.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 15 or older. Swim instructors 15 or older with teaching experience (14 or older to volunteer with no experience). Front desk aides 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply online at rockvillemd.gov/careers, then come to a hiring event or interview for a skills test (200 yard swim, 2 minute tread). Call 240-314-8750.
notes: Pay and ages are from the 2026 flyer and may change. Going to the event does not guarantee a job. Course fee discounts may be available for people who want to work for the city. Under-18 workers may need a Maryland work permit; the flyer does not say.
duration: Summer season
pay_detail: 2026 flyer: lifeguard $18.25 to $19.25, swim instructor $18.75 to $20, front desk aide $17.65 to $19.00. Uncertified lifeguards start at $18.25 after they get certified.

who_can_apply: Maryland 4-H youth who are at least 14 years old by July 1 of the fair year. You need your own ride to the fair.
how_to_apply: Fill out the 4-H Youth Worker Application. It is an online form linked on the Extension page. It asks for a letter from your county 4-H Extension Educator. Youth who are picked go to training.
notes: The job description says picked youth must apply for a minor work permit. They must also fill out federal and state job forms. Contacts: Chris Anderson, 301-314-7187, and Kevin Huang, 301-405-8105.
duration: At least four 4-hour shifts during the fair (Aug 20 to Sept 14 in 2026)
pay_detail: Hourly pay at current Maryland wage standards. Fair admission and parking passes on days worked.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 or older by Teen Boot Camp.
how_to_apply: Turn in the full application when it opens. Incomplete ones are not considered. Then go to a group interview. Questions: volunteers@marylandzoo.org or 443-552-5266.
notes: 2026 timeline from the page: selections May 28, parent orientation June 10, Boot Camp sessions June 22 to 26 and June 29 to July 3. The page text is partly inconsistent about dates, so check it when it updates. The Teens menu also lists a Keeper-in-Training Camp that was not read.
duration: At least one year: 4 shifts a month, one shift at a zoo event, and a one-week Boot Camp (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. The page mentions no fees.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 (before January 1) can join and take part in projects and competitions. Ages 5 to 7 join as Cloverbuds and do not compete.
how_to_apply: Contact your local 4-H office to learn about programs and get the New Member Enrollment Packet. Fill it out and return it. The office then tells your parent or guardian where to pay online or by check. Re-enroll through 4honline.
notes: A youth group, not a job. The Get Involved page still shows a 2022-2023 fee note, but the Membership page lists the $40 fee with a $120 family cap, so confirm the current fee with your local office.
duration: Annual membership; you re-enroll each year
pay_detail: $40 per member each year, with a family cap of $120. Fee waivers can be requested through your 4-H Educator. The page says cash is not accepted.

who_can_apply: Girls who are finishing or just finished their junior year. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal inhabitant. Documents are needed at check-in. You need an interest in government, strong leadership and above average grades. A sponsor is needed.
how_to_apply: Find a sponsor (a Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or other group). Once your sponsor sends your name and email, the site emails you the online registration form. If you have no sponsor, fill out the sponsor request form on the Registration Forms page.
notes: Girls only. You can also send in an optional bill to be considered by the mock state Congress. The program says it is run by volunteers. Email Director.massgirlsstate@gmail.com with questions.
duration: One week (2026: June 13 to June 19)
pay_detail: No pay. Participants are sponsored by an American Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or community group. The student cost is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Boys who finished junior year and have at least one semester left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character, grades and service to your school are what count. A parent and a family doctor must sign a medical consent form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program interest form on the site. You will be told when applications open (late 2026). The application has your information and a short response on what Boys State would mean to you. It also has a reference from a teacher or guidance counselor. You can also ask your local Legion post or guidance counselor.
notes: Boys only (Massachusetts Girls State is a separate program). You are expected to attend the whole week. It falls during many schools' finals, so ask your school about make-up plans early. The interest form link is the one on the home page.
duration: One week: the 83rd Annual Session is June 12 to June 18, 2027
pay_detail: No pay. The goal is that tuition is paid by your local American Legion post, the Massachusetts Boys State and Girls State Foundation, a school or town, or a sponsor.

who_can_apply: Volunteers are mostly 16 or older, unless a parent or guardian comes along. The minimum age changes by job. Some jobs need training or a background check (CORI or SORI).
how_to_apply: Browse and respond to openings on the Mass Audubon Volunteer Portal. Large groups can use the group volunteer form.
notes: Busiest months are May to September. Younger teens can ask about parent-accompanied options.
duration: One day to weekly shifts; some positions are seasonal
pay_detail: Unpaid. Students can earn community service credit. 50 hours a year earns a Volunteer ID card with free sanctuary admission.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 8 to 12, generally 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YCLP contact form on the Mass Audubon site. Staff connect you with your local chapter. A local adult mentor helps you start.
notes: Upcoming summits are free: Western Mass on Monday Nov 9, 2026 in Springfield, and SouthCoast on Friday Nov 20, 2026 in Dartmouth. Ages 13 to 17.
duration: Projects take a couple of hours a month. Leadership teams meet every other week before summits and monthly otherwise.
pay_detail: The two upcoming summits are free to attend.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25 with family income at or under 200% of the federal poverty line. You also need at least one listed factor. Examples are one income in the home, being a person of color, a disability, no stable home, or leaving school. Apply through the program in your town.
how_to_apply: Find your town on the 'Find a YouthWorks Program Near You' list, then contact that local workforce board program.
notes: Each local program picks its own jobs and dates. Seats are limited. Whether a Massachusetts work permit is needed was not stated on these pages; ask the local program. The program page does not state the income limit, the eligibility factors or the age 14 minimum; those come from the FAQ PDF, which could not be read in this check, so confirm them with the local program.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks in summer; a year-round option runs September to May
pay_detail: At least the state minimum wage; hours and pay vary by site

who_can_apply: Students at a Massachusetts school with an FFA chapter. The state site lists the chapters (the list includes vocational, technical and agricultural high schools). It does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Find your school on the Massachusetts FFA Chapters page. The page does not say how to join, so ask your school how to sign up.
notes: The chapters page lists schools such as Bay Path Regional Vocational Technical H.S. in Charlton, Bristol County Agricultural High School in Dighton and Minuteman High School. Check the full list for your area. The site describes FFA as an intracurricular student group.
duration: Ongoing while you are in agricultural education
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12 with strong grades and drive. It is selective. The page says Smith does not treat people unfairly by sex or gender. Students from other countries can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with an essay, one letter from a teacher and a transcript. The fee goes up to $100 on Apr 15, 2027.
notes: Costs money. Apply early for the priority date and for aid.
duration: 2 weeks per session. Session 1: July 3 to 16, 2027. Session 2: July 18 to 31, 2027.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $4,985 per two-week session, or $9,970 for both. 2027 rates not yet posted. Limited tuition assistance is available.

who_can_apply: Secondary school students at a Massachusetts school. Every secondary school can elect two representatives to its regional council, so you run for election at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school about its Student Advisory Council election. The DESE page has an Elections link with the recommended procedure.
notes: The page gives no age or grade rule beyond secondary school, and it lists no election dates.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated. A leadership role, not a job.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12, or last spring's high school graduates. Residential students must be at least 15 at the start and no older than 19 at the end. Health programs need grades 11 to 12, 1 year of biology and age 16. Homeschoolers can apply. International students can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a transcript. Add a letter where one is needed. Add a form where a parent says yes. See the How to Apply page.
notes: Costs money; check each page for the price. Many 2027 dates say coming soon.
duration: 1 to 6 weeks; commuter or residential
pay_detail: Tuition varies by program (amount not read on the pages fetched). Limited aid: scholarships usually cover 75 to 100% of the fee, based on need.

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in high school, and seniors who just graduated. The Pre-Veterinary Medicine and Veterinary Technology programs are only for rising juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Sign up for updates on the Pre-College page now. Applications for 2027 open in January. They are reviewed on a rolling basis. Scholarship applications use the same online system.
notes: Expensive. This is a college course experience, not a job. The page also lists year-round college prep workshops (fall 2026 workshops are open).
duration: 1 to 6 weeks, depending on the program
pay_detail: $45 application fee. Listed fees: 2-week programs $4,119 residential or $2,337 commuter; 3-week $6,125 or $3,397; 6-week Research Intensives $12,813 or $7,247. Some programs add a $95 materials fee. Limited need-based partial scholarships (up to $1,000) for 1 to 3 week programs.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older when the internship starts. You must be in one of these schools, or have just graduated from one. Recent graduates must have finished no more than two calendar years ago, or be in college now. The schools are a Chapter 74 vocational technical high school (or a high school with a life sciences Chapter 74 program). Or a public or charter high school in a listed Gateway City, like Lowell, Lawrence, Worcester, Springfield, Lynn or Brockton. Or a public high school where at least 25 percent of students are low income.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Write a 250 word essay. Share something that shows your STEM interest, like a poster, slides, posts, a podcast or a video. Make a 1 minute video about yourself. Get a reference from a teacher. Questions: PROPEL@uml.edu.
notes: Eligibility depends on your school type or city. Check the Gateway City list on the apply page. Ask about a Massachusetts work permit.
duration: Summer 2026 started June 29; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid summer internship; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and older who like art, museums or teaching.
how_to_apply: Look at the Job Opportunities page of the Worcester Art Museum. Apply when jobs are posted.
notes: The page says a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts supports the NEA Teen Intern jobs. Ask the museum about a Massachusetts work permit.
duration: Flexible hours; the museum usually hires two summer interns
pay_detail: Paid internship program; pay rate not stated

who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders. International applicants need an English test (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo).
how_to_apply: Application is free. It has two short written answers and a list of involvements. Official transcripts are preferred, but self-submitted ones are accepted. Questions: pop@wpi.edu or 508-831-4900.
notes: Costs money. The exact opening day in December is not stated. Ask about financial assistance on the program policies page.
duration: Two weeks, residential. Session I: July 5 to 16, 2027. Session II: July 18 to 30, 2027.
pay_detail: $4,995 per session (includes tuition, housing, meals, field trips, workshops and activities). Financial assistance is explained on the program policies page.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Must be 16 by Sept 1.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the page when applications reopen. The page suggests joining an information session. Questions: mya@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Fundraising cannot start until you are accepted. It cannot take place on hospital or clinic grounds. Two excused absences are allowed.
duration: Cohort 8 runs 2027 to 2028. Meetings are Wednesdays 3:30 to 4:30 PM, virtual; weekly in summer, monthly in the school year.
pay_detail: You pay nothing, but you must raise $1,250 for the hospital to earn an awards package. There is no pay.

who_can_apply: High school students. Which option you can use depends on your high school. Talk to your high school counselor for course lists and deadlines.
how_to_apply: Early College Dual Credit: apply through your high school counselor. Early Admit: fill out the Early Admit forms. Then sign up for classes after you are accepted.
notes: The page says Early College has 2 options. Early College Dual Credit is usually classes at the high school. Early Admit is classes on the college campus. Compare the options on the page to pick one.
duration: By semester (fall, spring and summer)
pay_detail: Free or discounted tuition is available. Who pays varies: high school, student or family, or scholarship.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list exact ages or a city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply through the MCA Denver teens page when the window opens.
notes: Meets Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM all school year. Admission to MCA Denver is free for teens. Exact 2026 to 2027 dates are not posted, so this uses the usual pattern.
duration: Meets Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM all school year
pay_detail: Up to $300 per semester.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list exact ages or a city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply through the MCA Denver teens page when the window opens. Email teens@mcadenver.org with questions.
notes: Meets Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, one semester. Admission to MCA Denver is free for teens. Exact 2026 to 2027 dates are not posted, so this uses the usual pattern.
duration: Meets Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, one semester
pay_detail: Up to $300 for the semester.

who_can_apply: Local teens interested in the arts. The page does not list exact ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Apply through MCA Denver. How to apply is not stated on the page; see the teens page.
notes: The stipend covers materials, not wages. The studio is open to the public.
duration: 3 to 4 weeks; studio open Tuesday to Friday, noon to 5 PM
pay_detail: The museum gives a stipend for materials. A personal pay amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from San Diego. The page says the group draws teens from across San Diego County. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (one per student). Invited students get an acceptance email and onboarding documents. Questions: education@mcasd.org.
notes: Closed for 2026-2027. The program is supported in part by the California Arts Council.
duration: Sept 8, 2026 to June 2027; meets the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of each month, 5 to 7 p.m.
pay_detail: No stipend or cost mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 13 or in 8th grade at the time of application. They can be up to age 17 or 18 and a senior in high school.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Advisory Board Interest Form on the MCPL page; someone contacts you after it is received.
notes: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says there will be more chances to volunteer at MCPL in the coming year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours for attending meetings.

who_can_apply: The Maryland 4-H pages do not list an age range. Programs vary by county. Contact your local Extension office to learn which clubs and programs fit your age.
how_to_apply: Contact your local University of Maryland Extension office. Ask about clubs, camps and programs in your county. Then use the Enroll in Maryland 4-H link on the Join a Club page.
notes: Maryland 4-H Center: 8020 Greenmead Drive, College Park, MD 20740, 301-314-9070. The leadership page lists a 2026 Volunteer and Teen Forum in Ocean City in November 2026. It has workshops for adults and teens aged 13 and older.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
pay_detail: The page says costs are kept to a minimum. No amounts are given.

who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Boys State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. Phones, smartphones and smartwatches are not allowed. The site recommends against driving yourself because the week is tiring. Staff are mostly veterans. The page says that in most cases a sponsor pays the expenses, and students who are not sponsored should ask the program about costs.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 26, 2027
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.

who_can_apply: Students in a high school agricultural education program. The site says Maryland FFA has almost 3,000 student members in 50 chapters. Age and grade rules are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has an agricultural education program and FFA chapter. The Maryland FFA home page has a Join FFA button and a chapters page.
notes: The 2026 National FFA Convention and Expo is listed on the site for Oct 20 to 24, 2026 in Indianapolis. If your school has no FFA chapter, contact the Maryland FFA office through the Contact page.
duration: School year, ongoing
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the program pages. Ask your chapter advisor.

who_can_apply: Maryland residents who are seniors at a Maryland public or nonpublic high school and are at least 16 years old. You apply through the school you attend, not where you live.
how_to_apply: Contact your county page coordinator. The page has a list. Get the county's application and find its deadline. The Maryland page says the coordinator works with your high school.
notes: Each year 105 pages and 36 alternates are chosen from across the state. Program contact on the page: Tawana Offer, Tawana.Offer@mga.maryland.gov, 410-946-5120 (Student Programs).
