Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Two weeks that are not back to back during the 13-week session (second week of January to early April)
pay_detail: A meal allowance of about $50 per day worked. The Page Office arranges lodging for pages from outside Anne Arundel County who ask for it. Pages pay their own travel to Annapolis.

who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Girls State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. The Girls State page lists a Samsung American Legion Scholarship event on the last day. The page says that in most cases a sponsor pays the expenses, and students who are not sponsored should ask the program about costs.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 25, 2027
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: This center is not taking students while it is paused. To ask about other Job Corps centers, make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov or call 800-733-5627.
notes: The Labor Department paused this center in Dec 2024. Its own site has no notice, so trust jobcorps.gov. Address: 10900 Old Court Rd, Woodstock, MD.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Mt. Diablo Unified students who are interested and eligible. In 2026-2027 class capacity will be 60 juniors and 60 seniors. Talk to your high school counselor about the rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Then fill out the College Now student application on the program page. A recommendation form is also on the page. Go to the parent night if you can.
notes: The program started in fall 2016. The 2026 parent night was Wed, Feb 4, 2026. Staff phone on the page: 925-969-2512. The DVC page also lists a related program called Diamante Scholars for Mt. Diablo seniors.
duration: Junior and senior years
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the College Now page. DVC says its dual enrollment classes are free.

who_can_apply: Current Mt. Diablo Unified students who will be in 11th or 12th grade in the year they serve. You need at least a 2.0 grade point average and must be enrolled in 20 credits.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Board Member Application when the district posts it. For 2026-2027 it was sent by email to Laura Juranek at juranekl@mdusd.org, due May 29, 2026.
notes: Board meetings are usually on the second and fourth Wednesday of the month, starting at 6:00 PM. The Student Advisory Committee advises the Student Board Member. Its 2025-26 meetings were at Concord High School. The district is at 1936 Carlotta Drive, Concord.
duration: One school year, July 1 to June 30
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Central Contra Costa County or Bay Point. You must be able to work in the U.S. and show proof of low income. Priority goes to McKinney-Vento (HOPE) youth, foster youth, and justice-involved youth in Bay Point and on the Monument Corridor. Being pregnant or parenting, an English learner, or having an IEP or 504 plan can also help you qualify.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Refer a Youth form on the program page. A coordinator then works with you. Questions: Anna Ramos, 925-685-1011, extension 62028.
notes: The Workforce Development Board of Contra Costa County funds and supports this WIOA grant. For East or West Contra Costa County, the page points to the County Office of Education. The page lists 14 required program elements, including leadership development and financial literacy education.
pay_detail: The page lists paid and unpaid work experience. Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 17. Ages 10 to 13 must come with a parent or guardian. Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. A signed parent permission form is required for all youth.
how_to_apply: Click Register on the volunteer page to pick a session. Everyone must register before arriving. Groups of 5 or fewer register one by one. Larger groups fill out the group request form.
notes: The volunteer page does not name its work site. The only address on the contact page is the Decatur headquarters at 3240 Clifton Springs Road. Confirm the site when you register. MedShare does not host court-ordered or required community service.
duration: One session at a time: Wed and Fri 9 am to noon; Thu and Sat 9 am to noon and 1 to 4 pm
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Students in high school grades 9 to 12. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the next application. Accepted students get an email. Then they send shot records (varicella, MMR) and a TB test within 6 months. They also go to a required orientation by invitation only.
notes: The page covers Long Beach Medical Center only. It does not mention an Emergency Room volunteer role or its age rule.
duration: 8-week session; 2026 ran June 29 to August 21
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: High school students (grades 9 to 12) with a GPA of 3.0 or above.
how_to_apply: The pages do not explain how to apply. Use the Contact Us page at cityofmemphisyouth.org or call 901-636-6264.
notes: The same office runs B.O.S.S., a mentoring program for grades 9 to 12 with no GPA rule. Students meet a mentor 2 times a week after school at community centers. The Memphis city page gives the grade range and says participants get a stipend but gives no amount. The program page gives neither.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: A monthly stipend. The amount is not posted.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older, including students. A student under 18 needs consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online request form for applicants under 18. Ask 6 to 8 weeks ahead. Email CFCD@BMHCC.ORG with questions.
notes: The page says requests for the Baptist Memorial Hospital for Women are paused until further notice. Baptist's regular volunteer program is for ages 18 and up. The page does not list which hospitals take part, so ask when you apply.
duration: At least 2 hours and no more than two full working days (24 hours)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens. The hospital's page does not list ages or grades. Regular weekly volunteers must be 18, so VolunTEEN is the teen route.
how_to_apply: Watch the Volunteer Programs page in February. Email lbvolunteers@lebonheur.org or call 901-287-5225 with questions.
notes: Ages, fee and shot requirements are not on the hospital's own pages. Ask Volunteer Services before you plan around this. Under 18 and not in VolunTEEN: the hospital points teens to one-time group volunteer events.
duration: Four sessions with eight teens in each. Session dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by June 1 of the program year.
how_to_apply: Use the program's own form, not the general volunteer form. Send 2 references from teachers or counselors. Send a consent form from a parent. Send a photo and media release. Send a copy of a birth certificate, permit or passport. Send shot records (MMR and chickenpox) and a 200 word essay. Late entries are not accepted.
notes: Send materials by email to sandra.moore@mlh.org or mail them to Volunteer Services, 1265 Union Ave., Ste. E-161, Memphis, TN 38104. Call 901-516-7481. You must complete all four weeks.
duration: 4 weeks. In 2026 orientation was June 1 and volunteering ran June 2 to 25, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: City of Memphis youth ages 14 to 22. The page does not define what counts as a Memphis resident.
how_to_apply: The program pages do not explain how teens apply. Contact the Office of Youth Services. You must show a photo ID to pick up your paycheck.
notes: Office is at 315 S Hollywood St., Memphis, TN 38104. A separate Shelby County Commissioners summer youth program exists. The county page could not be read.
duration: 6 weeks, up to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid by paper check, up to 20 hours a week. The hourly rate is not posted on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by the first day of the session.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application. Send 2 reference letters from teachers or counselors. Send your last report card. Send a 500 word essay on why you like health services. Also send a Confidentiality Agreement and the Commitment Standards. Everything must be in or you will not be considered.
notes: Mail the papers to Teenteer Volunteer Program, Regional One Health, 877 Jefferson Ave., Memphis, TN 38103. Or scan and email them. Call Volunteer Services at 901-545-7247.
duration: One session, the week of June 2 to 4 in 2026 (June 3 was a half day)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students who will be sophomores, juniors or seniors.
how_to_apply: Applications are not open yet. If you want to know more, send an email to summeracademy@rhodes.edu.
notes: Students pick 1 class and go to 2 sessions a day. The program page lists a cost of $2900 with room and board. It says aid is available. Signing up by April 15 gives a $200 discount. The page prints a 2026 session (June 21 to July 2, 2026) next to the 2027 dates. Confirm the year with summeracademy@rhodes.edu.
duration: 2 weeks in June 2027 (residential)
pay_detail: Cost is not posted on the page. Ask summeracademy@rhodes.edu.

who_can_apply: For grades 5 to 12. Performance and production students must audition. Stax 101 students do not have to audition.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online sign up form. Performance students give a 2 song audition, a music theory test and an interview. Production students send an MP3 of their own music plus the theory test and interview. To get a discount, send proof of income after you sign up.
notes: It costs money. The academy says it serves area youth, even if they can not pay. For questions, send an email to smaprogramming@staxmusicacademy.org or call 901-942-7627.
duration: August to May (after-school), or June (summer)
pay_detail: Tuition: $1,250 per year for the after-school program (August to May) and $750 for the Summer Music Experience (June). Need-based discounts and merit scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Other rules are not posted.
how_to_apply: The pages do not explain how to apply. Use the Contact Us page at cityofmemphisyouth.org or call 901-636-6264.
notes: The city's youth services page says the program gives youth in grades 9 to 12 a chance to take part. The MYCC page says it aims to lift up young voices. Meeting times, stipend and timing are not posted.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Applicants should be in grades 7-12. The page does not state a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.

who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.
duration: One-year term, September through May. About 6 hours per month for meetings and events.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.

who_can_apply: The squadron welcomes all community members ages 12 to 18. They join its cadet program.
how_to_apply: Fill in the contact box on the squadron's Join Us page with your contact information and a short description of your interests. Email: christopher.ince@cawgcap.org. The squadron meets at 3515 Hardstand Ave, Atwater, CA 95301.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list meeting times, dues or the first visit steps. The national Civil Air Patrol cadet page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.
duration: Ongoing. Nationally the ideal time is a weekly meeting of about two hours, one Saturday event a month and a week long summer encampment. The squadron's meeting day and time are not listed.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Students at high schools that offer Merced College CCAP courses. Grade levels and partner schools are not listed. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the CCAP link. A parent fills out the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form. Pick classes with your counselor. Then give the K-12 Permit PDF to your high school CCAP counselor.
notes: The Dual Enrollment Coordinator is Jourdan L. French. Her number is 209-384-6189. For classes taken on campus, see the separate Merced College K-12 concurrent enrollment card.
pay_detail: No tuition and no books.

who_can_apply: K-12 students. Ask your high school counselor if you are eligible. English C1000 is only open to eligible 11th and 12th graders. K-8 students need a written recommendation from their principal or designee. They also need current transcripts.
how_to_apply: 1) Apply for admission for the semester you want. 2) Turn in the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form once during high school, after you get your 7 digit Merced College ID. 3) Complete the K-12 Permit form for your school level. 4) Wait for the email that lets you register in the MC Portal. 5) Pay fees online or at the Student Fees Office. Phone for the Merced campus: 209-384-6000.
notes: This is the college's own concurrent enrollment page. Merced Union High School District also has its own dual enrollment partnership with Merced College (see that separate card). Kinesiology courses with a physical activity part are capped at 10 percent of K-12 seats.
duration: By semester, including summer
pay_detail: K-12 students can enroll in Merced College classes tuition free (limitations may apply). Some physical activity courses need an extra K-12 Permit, and some fees may still apply.

who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 21 (for example, youth without a high school diploma). Teens 16 to 18 qualify only if they are out of school.
how_to_apply: Use the Click here to apply form on the EMPOWER page, or call 209-381-5926. The office is at 658 W. Main Street, Merced.
notes: Prospero (the Merced County workforce board, formerly WorkNet) lists EMPOWER as its main youth program for out-of-school youth. Prospero Youth Team: 209-724-2036. Confirm first: the page gives no start dates or wage.
duration: Not stated; follow-up services for at least 12 months after the program
pay_detail: Paid and/or unpaid work experience; wages are not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students across Merced County. The page lists the ROP at Delhi, Dos Palos, Gustine, Hilmar, Le Grand, Los Banos and Pacheco high schools. It also lists Merced Scholars Charter School. It also lists Valley Community School in Atwater and in Los Banos. Grade rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to enroll. Ask your school counselor, or contact Dora Robles, Staff Secretary, at (209) 381-6684 or drobles@mcoe.org.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list the courses, grades, cost or how to enroll. The MCOE college and career page also lists the EMPOWER program (see the separate EMPOWER card). It also lists Cal-SOAP for college and financial aid information.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost, pay and credit are not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Mercy Medical Center in Merced is a listed place to volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer interest form. The volunteer team then contacts you about an interview and orientation. You also need a background check and shots.
notes: This is the Central California system volunteer page. It lists no phone number, so use the contact page at commonspirit.org/dignity-health-central-cal-contact-us. The page does not say whether applications are open, so ask before you plan on it.

who_can_apply: Students in good academic standing at a Merced Union High School District school (Atwater, Buhach Colony, El Capitan, Golden Valley, Livingston, Merced, Sequoia, Yosemite). Complete the Merced College application, a parent consent form and a High School Permit.
how_to_apply: Apply to Merced College, submit the parent consent form and High School Permit, and talk to your school's Pathway Counselor.
notes: College privacy law applies once you enroll: parents do not get progress updates from Merced College. A college GPA below 2.0 can affect future college eligibility and financial aid.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Free: students can take college courses at no cost, up to 11 units a semester. Textbook fees are waived for CCAP classes; textbook fees apply for concurrent enrollment.

who_can_apply: Current 11th or 12th graders who go to school in Merced County and have active Medi-Cal. You answer personal questions about your interest in health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online at ucm.edu/chapply. Questions: pace@ucmerced.edu.
notes: Only for teens with Medi-Cal who attend school in Merced County. Ages are not stated, only grades 11 and 12. Check the page each fall for the next round.
duration: Spring certificate course, then 60 hours of team projects in summer 2026
pay_detail: $1,400 stipend, plus project funding, a $150 gas card and a program polo (per the flyer).

who_can_apply: Teens at least 16 years old. You must be in school in good standing or working toward a GED. A parent or guardian must agree.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer application online. Then expect a criminal background check. Expect a registered offender check and a health screening too. You also need proof of immunizations, references and an interview. Contact Anne Owens at anne.owens@mercyone.org. Or call 515-358-9265.
notes: Are you 14 or 15? Look at the teen program at UnityPoint Iowa Lutheran Hospital.
duration: At least 4 months. The weekly hours are not stated for teens.
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 12 or older. Anyone under 18 needs permission from a parent or legal guardian. An older library event page lists the teen program as ages 12 to 18, grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: See the volunteer page. Use the Volunteer Opportunities link (Volgistics). Email volunteer@mld.org. Ask about teen jobs and when orientation is.
notes: The main volunteer page does not describe a teen program. The 2020 teen event page gives the phone number (208) 472-1755. It also gives the teen steps: a flyer, a Teen Volunteer Form and orientation. Ask volunteer@mld.org to confirm the current steps.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps. Contact Mesa Aquatics at 480-644-7529 or aquatics@mesaaz.gov.
notes: Part of the City of Mesa H.Y.P.E. Teen Programs page.
duration: Summer. Exact dates not listed.
pay_detail: Volunteer role. The page says it leads to future lifeguarding.

who_can_apply: Teens can use the Teen Application. The page does not state the age range. Call to ask.
how_to_apply: Apply and interview. Then a health screen and background check. Then orientation. Use the Teen Application or Summer Student Application on the page, or call (480) 412-3258.
notes: Teen age range is not stated on the page. Banner Desert Medical Center is in Mesa.
duration: At least 6 months or 100 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application on the page or call (480) 321-4122. The process includes an interview and background research and can take up to 3 weeks.
notes: The Banner volunteer pages are not the same for each hospital. Call first, then apply.
duration: At least 100 hours within 6 months, or one shift of about 4 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, and you must be in school. Keep a C average. You need medical clearance before starting.
how_to_apply: Sign up during the August window on the program page. For questions, contact Program Coordinator Christine Mendoza. The page shows 480-644-5047 and 480-644-3883, so confirm before calling.
notes: The work is hard on the body. Cadets lift, pull or push up to 75 lbs. Community service is strongly encouraged but not required.
duration: Not stated on the program page. Most meetings are held at the Public Safety Training Facility, 3260 North 40th Street, Mesa.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. You must be 13 by the start of the program. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a camp in ActiveNet. Then get a form and an interview link. Then do the interview and the training you must take. Adaptive camps (Camp Fiesta, Wiggles & Giggles) need a form and interview before you sign up.
notes: The City of Mesa website blocked a normal page visit, so the facts come from the 2026 FAQ PDF. Check the Mesa summer registration dates. Contact: PRCFVolunteers@mesaaz.gov or 480-644-4345 (from a search listing, not the PDF).
duration: Summer camp season. Mandatory training dates differ by camp.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Program fee is $32 for Mesa residents and $38 for non-residents.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, and you must have finished 8th grade. Stay in school until you graduate. Keep a 2.0 GPA or higher. No serious police record.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest form on the Mesa cadet page. A cadet advisor then contacts you. For help, call 480-644-4869 or email PDCadets@mesaaz.gov.
notes: Members can stay in the Post until they turn 21. Cadets also do community service. Ask the post for the next recruiting date.
duration: Weekly meetings on Thursday nights
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 11 or older. Volunteering is during the school year, with extra hours in summer for the Summer Reading Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and return it to the front desk. An application does not guarantee acceptance. Missing 3 shifts without notice removes you from the schedule.
notes: The page was last updated Nov 12, 2024, so call your branch to confirm. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Female high school students who will finish their junior year in spring 2027. You must have at least one more semester before graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online delegate application. The link is on the Michigan Girls State page and the 2027 flyer. Questions go to the Girls State chairman, Beryl Robbins, at berylrobbins1980@gmail.com or (313) 318-6845.
notes: Not a job. A closing date was not on the page or flyer, so apply early. The page also lists a Samsung scholarship and a government manual to read before attending.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
pay_detail: Cost to the student is not stated on the program pages. The page asks people to donate to send a young woman to Girls State.

who_can_apply: Males who have finished junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You should like government and show leadership, character and school or community service. You must be a U.S. citizen. You cannot attend Boys State twice.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on michiganboysstate.org (the 2026 brochure says to visit the website to apply). Pay the $25 application fee and find a sponsor for the $400 program fee. Office: (517) 371-4720 ext. 123 (site) or 517-220-2754 (brochure), legion@michiganlegion.org.
notes: Not a job. Dates, fees and the deadline above are from the 2026 brochure and flyer, so confirm the 2027 details with the office. The resources page still showed a May 1, 2024 deadline, so it is out of date. Office address: 212 N. Verlinden Ave., Lansing, MI 48915.
duration: One week (2026: June 21 to 27)
pay_detail: $25 application fee paid by the student. The $400 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as a local American Legion Post or other community group (2026 brochure).

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 26 with a visual impairment. The school can refer you at your IEP meeting.
how_to_apply: Contact your local BSBP office or your school special education office. You can also fill out the form at the IEP meeting.
notes: Programs may target a certain age group, interest or skill.
duration: Programs run throughout the year
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: People 16 or older. The form has a box for ages 16 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form on the page, sign up for an open house, or contact the Volunteer Coordinator at 248-341-2756 or CIS_volunteer@cranbrook.edu. Required paperwork is needed.
notes: Special Events Volunteer is a good short option for community service hours. Nature Zone shifts are weekends and select holidays.
duration: A regular schedule is welcome but not required. Special event shifts are short.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 13 years old and enrolled in a Dearborn school. Volunteer spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Watch the orientation video. Then print the form and bring it to any Dearborn library.
notes: The library does not take court-ordered service. It cannot take all requests, so spots are few.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a marketing, management, finance, hospitality or entrepreneurship course. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Michigan DECA advisor, Dave Wait. His email is dwait@emich.edu.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is mideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Michigan.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $17 per student member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Must live in Detroit and be 14 to 24. You must show papers that prove age, residency and eligibility. Some programs also take Highland Park and Hamtramck residents.
how_to_apply: Call 313-962-WORK (9675) or visit a Detroit at Work career center (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.). Bring documents that prove age and where you live.
notes: Summer jobs are a separate track (Grow Detroit's Young Talent). Pay rates and the work permit rule for this program are not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Free to join. Offers paid and unpaid work experiences, plus stipends for training and career exploration. Amounts not stated.

who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Detroit. Ages 14 to 24. You can apply at 13 if you turn 14 by July 1.
how_to_apply: Express interest at GDYT.org. Picks are made by random lottery. If chosen, finish enrollment forms and upload documents (including a work permit for ages 14 to 17), then attend orientation.
notes: The FAQ lists a work permit for ages 14 to 17 as a required document. Up to 8,000 spots in 2026, so a lottery decides. Next year's window is likely spring 2027.
duration: About 6 weeks, up to 120 hours, usually early July through August
pay_detail: Wage jobs pay $12.50 to $15 per hour, paid every two weeks. Stipend jobs pay $1,500 to $2,000.

who_can_apply: First-time participants who go to high school or live in metro Detroit, in 10th or 11th grade, age 16 or older by program start, GPA 2.5 or higher, and allowed to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Email HAPE@hfhs.org with questions.
notes: The page says students under 18 must get a work permit. Teens must also join at least one year-round track.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 28 to Aug 7, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) plus monthly meetings September to May
pay_detail: The page says stipends or wages may be available for high school students but are not guaranteed. The program is free.

who_can_apply: Detroit-area high school students who are curious about health care. No medical experience needed. Grades and school districts are not listed.
how_to_apply: Submit the online internship application form linked on the summer internship page. For the program, email iokerek1@hfhs.org or call 313-916-2698.
notes: Very competitive: the page says 331 applied and 25 were chosen in 2025. The application link may be the 2026 form, so check the page for the next one.
duration: 7-week summer internship. Saturday sessions during the school year.
pay_detail: Program is free. Summer interns get a $1,000 stipend for 7 weeks.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors (going into 12th grade) and college freshmen, sophomores and juniors.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the program site. A 2-day orientation comes first. Students finish assignments and weekly classes.
notes: Rising seniors and college students apply to the same program. Contact: medicalmentorspipeline@gmail.com. Cost was not stated, so ask before applying.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 24 to August 6)
pay_detail: Pay and cost not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who passes a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application, then wait for an interview to find the best fit.
notes: The page does not list specific roles or hours. Ask the volunteer team (volunteers@mi-sci.org) about teen roles.
duration: Time commitment not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students from Metro Detroit with little or no investing knowledge.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application packet. Add two letters of recommendation and the signed forms. Email it to edwarddj1@udmercy.edu.
notes: Held on the McNichols Campus, 4001 West McNichols Rd. The camp page still says applications are open, but the 2026 camp dates have passed. Ask the camp director before you apply.
duration: One week. In 2026 it ran June 22 to 26, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily.
pay_detail: Free. Materials, breakfast, snacks, lunch, a T-shirt and a backpack are included.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who want to explore health careers. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: The 2026 camp is full, so you cannot apply now. The program page does not post 2027 sign-up dates. Questions can go to Nina Favor at favornf@udmercy.edu.
notes: Held at the STAR Center on the McNichols Campus. The middle school week was July 20 to 24, 2026. The high school week was July 27 to 31, 2026.
duration: One week. In 2026 the high school week was July 27 to 31, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. Breakfast, lunch and snacks are included. Campers also get a lab jacket and a blood pressure cuff.

who_can_apply: High school students in 10th, 11th or 12th grade with a GPA of 2.75 or higher. Priority goes to Wayne County residents, Detroit Public Schools Community District students, and students from disadvantaged backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and write a 300 to 400 word personal statement. An official transcript is needed if you are accepted.
notes: Program dates may change. Contact: BCAPstudentgroup@gmail.com or (313) 577-1584.
duration: 6 weeks. Monday to Thursday up to 5 hours a day, plus Friday events 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: Students who finish may get a monetary award. It depends on funding and is not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12. Choose camp I or II of a topic, not both.
how_to_apply: Register through the Summer Academy pages. Use the question link to reach the Director of Community Engagement.
notes: Cost was not stated on the pages. Ask about the scholarship page before you decide.
duration: 1 week per camp. You can mix topics across weeks.
pay_detail: Price not on the program pages. A scholarships page is listed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 by June 1. You need your own ride to the zoo.
how_to_apply: Send the application and documents on the zoo page. A parent and teen must do a phone or video interview. Go to one mandatory virtual meeting, then a full training week (9 a.m. to 4 p.m.) in late June or early July.
notes: Work is outdoors in all weather. Training hours count toward the 60. A separate Counselor in Training program is listed but the page gave no details. Questions go to the zoo education department.
duration: Summer track: 60 hours June to August. Year-round track adds shifts September to May.
pay_detail: Cost not listed

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 21 who are enrolled in a state-approved agricultural education course. The page does not list grades.
how_to_apply: Use the chapters and regions page to find a chapter near you, then ask that school about its agriculture class. Questions can go to the state office.
notes: Not a job. The homepage says there are over 10,000 members in 137 chapters. State office: association@michiganffa.org or (517) 353-9221.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teams of high school students. The page does not give an age or grade rule. It links to Start a Team and Run a Team.
how_to_apply: Join an existing school or community team or use the Start a Team link on the FIRST in Michigan site. Contact on the page: Gail Alpert, 248.425.4148.
notes: Ask your school if it has a team. FIRST in Michigan also runs FTC and FIRST LEGO League for younger students.
duration: Build and competition season
pay_detail: Registration cost not stated. Scholarships are listed through FIRST.

who_can_apply: Volunteers in the distribution center must be at least 10. Volunteers under 18 must come with a parent or guardian. Other roles outside the warehouse need volunteers who are at least 14.
how_to_apply: Register online for a shift before you come. You get an email with the place, parking and dress code. Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes.
notes: You must stay for the whole shift. Bring school service paperwork so hours can be signed. The kids program is on hold. Some roles, like Harvest Heroes drivers and site monitors, are 18 and older.
duration: Shifts are 9 am to 12 pm or 1 pm to 4 pm, Monday through Saturday
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. School service hours can be signed off.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished at least freshman year. The page recommends age 16 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply on the hospital page when it opens. Spaces are limited and picks are made after an interview. Orientation is required. The application includes a health screening checklist, and a parent must be there for any shots.
notes: Jackson is west of Ann Arbor and south of Lansing, so it may be a drive. Teens must commit to all assigned shifts.
duration: 8 weeks, at least one 4-hour shift a week (2026: June 8 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students and 2027 high school graduates who are ages 16 to 17. You must be 16 by June 16, 2027. You must be free for 9 or more weeks in June, July and August 2027.
how_to_apply: Send the information form from March 1 to March 15, 2027. Go to an information session. Pass a background check. Do a health screen. Finish a training packet. Letters of recommendation are optional.
notes: Only a limited number of teens are accepted. Others go on a wait list. Selected candidates need a TB test and TDap and MMR shots. The hospital covers the cost.
duration: 9 weeks, one 4-hour shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students and 2027 high school graduates who are ages 16 to 17. You must be 16 by June 16, 2027. You must be free for 9 or more weeks in June, July and August 2027.
how_to_apply: Send the information form from March 1 to March 15, 2027. Go to an information session. Pass a background check. Do a health screen. Finish a training packet. Letters of recommendation are optional.
notes: Only a limited number of teens are accepted. Others go on a wait list. Selected candidates need a TB test and TDap and MMR shots. The hospital covers the cost. In fall, winter and early spring, on-site spots are only for teens who already volunteer.
duration: 9 weeks, one 4-hour shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students and graduates who are ages 16 to 17. In 2026, you had to be 16 by June 17, 2026 and free for 10 or more weeks in the summer.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for next year. In 2026 you sent an information form between March 1 and March 15. Candidates went to an information session. They passed a background check and a health screen. They also finished a training packet.
notes: The page says only 30 candidates will be picked for the summer program. Letters of recommendation are optional, and the page says they can help a lot. Chosen candidates need a TB test and TDap and MMR shots. The hospital covers the cost.
duration: 10 weeks in 2026, one 4-hour shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students interested in health care, through a school chapter. The site also says you can start a chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your school health or CTE teacher about a chapter, or use the Join MI HOSA link on the site. Contact: hosa@mhc.org or (517) 347-8088.
notes: The site lists more than 10,000 Michigan members.
duration: School year. State conference in April 2027 at the Grand Traverse Resort.
pay_detail: Dues and fees not stated on the home page

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. Children must come with a registered adult.
how_to_apply: Pick a workday on the volunteering page and register online by noon the day before. For regular volunteering, send the application and waiver to volunteer@metroparks.com.
notes: Dress for dirt: long pants, closed-toe shoes, layers. Poison ivy can be present. Children must come with a registered adult. Volunteers under 14 must have an adult with them for the whole shift, and a parent or guardian must sign the waiver for volunteers under 18. The volunteering page does not mention seasonal paid jobs.
duration: About 2 hours (10 a.m. to noon)
pay_detail: Free, unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in or go to school in Jackson County.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth and Young Adult Application link on the Jump-Start Jackson page.
notes: The Summer Youth Employment page lists it as one of the Michigan Works! Southeast summer programs. Jackson is west of Ann Arbor. Ask about dates and pay.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Paid on-the-job training; rate not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who live in Livingston County. Juniors and seniors in high school, or anyone 24 or younger regardless of graduation.
how_to_apply: Use the Contact Us link on the YouthWorks page, or call the Michigan Works! Southeast office.
notes: Livingston County is northwest of Ann Arbor (Howell and Brighton area). The page does not state the work permit rule for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: 2026 program: June 15 to August 14
pay_detail: Paid; the page does not state the hourly rate

who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 26 who are in school or have been accepted at school after high school. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign a consent form. Your school fills out a form that shows the disability.
how_to_apply: Use the MRS Online Application. Forms MRS-4.0a (parent consent) and MRS-4.0b (school verification) are on the page. Phone 517-241-5324 or toll-free 800-605-6722.
notes: Work-based learning is one of five services. Ask your school transition coordinator or counselor too.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: MRS pays for services in your employment plan. Not a wage.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from around the world. The cost page lists no grade rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Now link on the Summer Youth Programs page and pay the $150 deposit at registration. Pathway programs have nothing due at application. Contact syp@mtu.edu or 906-487-2219.
notes: Extra costs can include lab fees, a $20 weekly parking pass and charter bus service. Check the Course Catalog and Scholarships pages on the SYP site for current offerings.
duration: Week-long programs
pay_detail: Exploration programs start at $1,175 live-in (tuition, fees, meals, room and board) or $700 commuter. A $150 non-refundable deposit is due at registration. Pathway program fees vary. Scholarships exist.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 in Oakland County. Other rules are not listed on the pages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Oakland NEXT application on the Youth page. Or call 248-858-5520 or email oaklandcountymiworks@oaklandcountymi.gov.
notes: The county reported 164 paid work experiences with 60 employers in 2024. The page also lists an IAmPontiac summer internship; details were not read. Ask about the work permit rule for ages 16 and 17.
duration: Not stated. Offers summer and year-round internships.
pay_detail: Internships are typically paid. Pay rate not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. A parent or guardian fills out the online application for the teen.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian completes the teen online application. Choose your site and your areas of interest. Open roles are posted on Idealist.
notes: Court-ordered community service is not offered. Groups of 10 or more use a separate group form. Adults 18 and older use a different application.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Contact it to confirm a meeting. Go to about three meetings before you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Wing HQ mailing address: 43401 N. Jefferson, Bldg. 825, Rm 317, PO Box 450048, Selfridge ANGB, MI 48045-0048. School comes first; the page says school-based squadrons may differ.
duration: Ideally a 2-hour squadron meeting each week plus about one Saturday event a month. A week-long summer encampment is encouraged.
pay_detail: Annual dues are $40 for cadets. The page estimates a fully active cadet could spend $300 to $600 in the first year, minus help for uniforms and overnight fees.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low income and have at least one listed barrier (for example basic skills deficient, English language learner, homeless or foster youth, pregnant or parenting, disability). Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with a listed barrier.
how_to_apply: Call Michigan Works! at 1-800-285-WORKS (9675). Or find your local agency by ZIP code at michiganworks.org. Then ask about WIOA Youth eligibility.
notes: Not open to every teen: eligibility depends on income and barriers, so a short call to the local agency is the real first step. The state page does not list a local application form or local youth contacts. Capital Area Michigan Works!' own site (camw.org) mentions WIOA and says 259 youth were served but does not describe its youth program in detail. Work experience for anyone under 18 in Michigan needs a work permit under the state's youth employment law.
duration: Varies by local agency
pay_detail: Not stated. The state page lists both paid and unpaid work experiences, including summer employment, as possible services.

who_can_apply: High school students (a separate middle school program exists). The pages do not list grades. You join through a school or YMCA delegation.
how_to_apply: Check the map on the YMCA page to see if your school or YMCA has a delegation. If not, use the Contact us page to start one. Then register for the conferences your delegation attends.
notes: Not a job. The deadline date is the end of regular sign-up for the February Lansing conference. Lansing sign-up opens Nov 10, 2026. Fall conference sites include Marquette, Grayling, Allendale, Saginaw, Kalamazoo and Detroit. As of Oct 13, 2026, only the District 6 fall conference in Detroit is still open. The February and April Lansing windows are not open yet.
duration: Fall district conference, then a Lansing conference of about four days
pay_detail: The base fee is not stated on the program page. A $25 late fee applies to late Lansing registration. A financial aid application is linked on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 1/2 to 18 on day one (15 1/2 means you turn 16 during the cycle). Must be a Michigan resident and a U.S. citizen or legally present, not yet have a high school diploma, not be on reporting probation, and have no felonies. Ages 15 1/2 can only do credit recovery and return to their high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Inquiry Form on the MYCA site. Then follow the steps on the Admissions Process list.
notes: It has a military style setup, but the page says you do not have to join the military. The page calls it a program for at risk youth who want to finish high school.
duration: 5.5 months residential plus 12 months after. Cycles start mid-January and mid-July.
pay_detail: Free to parents. No obligation to join the military.

who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Middlesex County and meet additional eligibility criteria. Not for teens currently enrolled in high school.
how_to_apply: Email opportunityyouthprogram@middlesexcollege.edu to start. Office: 550 Jersey Avenue, New Brunswick, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
notes: The page does not name the funding source. Teens under 18 who are not in school should check eligibility with the office. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid training and work experience are listed; the wage is not stated.

who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17, entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2026, and attending a San Diego County high school.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a mandatory in-person interview and group interview if advanced. Contact the museum's Education Specialist or see the program PDF on the page.
notes: Closed for the 2026-2027 cohort. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 15 sessions, twice a month on Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., October to May
pay_detail: $750 for full participation

who_can_apply: Minneapolis residents ages 14 to 21 who are not enrolled in college. The Foundations level is for ages 14 to 21; the Pro level is for ages 16 to 21 with previous work or volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the January window. Accepted students (notified by about Mar 10) complete a required in-person orientation in March and April, then are matched with an internship.
notes: Step Up Director phone 612-673-5041; program phone 612-673-5118. The page does not mention work permits. Not every applicant is matched with a paid internship.
duration: About 2 months (June 22 to August 21 in 2026)
pay_detail: Paid by the City of Minneapolis (Foundations level); hourly rate and weekly hours not stated on the page. Teens not matched can do a 5-week online Career Exploration Program and earn up to $599 plus elective credit.

who_can_apply: Anyone from kindergarten through one year past high school. Independent membership means you are not in a club. It needs 6th grade or older and at least two years of 4-H club experience. It also needs an adult 4-H volunteer as your mentor.
how_to_apply: Get in touch with local 4-H staff near you, or fill out the interest form. Then complete your enrollment online or with a paper form.
notes: Clubs and costs can differ by county, so contact your county 4-H staff first. This is a youth club and learning program, not a paid job.
duration: One 4-H year runs Oct. 1 through Sept. 30. You re-enroll each year.
pay_detail: Minnesota 4-H does not charge a state membership fee. Some local clubs or programs charge dues, and help may be available.

who_can_apply: Young men who have just finished their junior year of high school. The Legion says picks are based on merit and ability. A sponsor, usually a local American Legion Post, chooses from students your school recommends.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Post. Forms and delegate information are on mnboysstate.org. For questions, call 651-291-1800 or email jkelley@mnlegion.org.
notes: Boys State is for boys. The 2026 session was June 14 to 20 at Saint John's University. Girls State is a separate program run by the American Legion Auxiliary. The Boys State pages give no age number, only the junior-year rule.
duration: One week. 2027 session: check in Sunday June 13, check out Saturday June 19, 2027.
pay_detail: Fees are paid by the sponsoring American Legion Post or other community group. No dollar amount is listed. Spending money for the camp store is optional.

who_can_apply: Students at a Minnesota high school with a DECA chapter. Chapters must have business and marketing courses and an advisor employed by the school. The official pages list no grade or age rule, so ask your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, usually a business or marketing teacher. The advisor registers members online. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Jacklyn (Jackie) Schiller.
notes: DECA's page lists 86 chapters in Minnesota (high school and college counts are not split). The state site mndeca.org lists phone 218-847-5355 and posts role play and judging information. It does not explain joining, so start with your advisor.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student dues are $13 total: $5 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapters may add costs.

who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in an agriculture, food and natural resources (AFNR) course at a school with an agricultural education program. The page lists no age or grade rule. If your school has no program, the site links to how to start one.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher and sign up for an agriculture course. Joining FFA goes through that class.
notes: The home page reports 218 agricultural education programs in Minnesota. Ask your counselor whether your school has one.
duration: School year, tied to your ag class
pay_detail: National FFA dues are $7 a year. Minnesota State FFA dues are $11 starting in 2026. That is $18 for both. Local chapters and regions may charge more.

who_can_apply: Any Minnesota high school junior. Public, private and homeschooled students can apply. Each fall the program picks students from the applications. You send a 500 word essay and one letter from a teacher, counselor or advisor.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 Page Application PDF from the House Sergeant at Arms site. Email it to EducationalPrograms@house.mn.gov. You also need a 500-word essay. You need one letter of recommendation. It can come from a teacher, counselor or academic advisor.
notes: Participants stay together as a group each evening at the program-designated hotel. Questions: Sergeant at Arms office, 651-296-4860.
duration: One week (Monday to Friday) in Saint Paul. 2027 weeks run from Jan 25 to May 14, 2027.
pay_detail: Small meal stipend. The program pays for the hotel. You pay your other personal costs.

who_can_apply: The page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Sign up online or at the Employment Center (1640 Como Ave, St. Paul). Then confirm your sign-up in person. You do a 5 minute screening. Then you may be sent to interviews. Email employment@mnstatefair.org or call 651-288-4475.
notes: The FAQ dates and the page header disagree on the year, so confirm the dates. Jobs are not guaranteed. The pages do not mention work permits, so check Minnesota rules for under 18.
duration: 12 fair days (2027 fair: Aug 26 to Sept 6)
pay_detail: State Fair department jobs start at $11.50 per hour; vendors set their own pay

who_can_apply: At least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first. Cadets can stay until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the Civil Air Patrol unit locator or the Minnesota Wing Locations page. Visit a meeting with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. Ask whether you can apply online.
notes: Example squadrons: Duluth (MN-016), St. Paul (MN-042), Alexandria (MN-135). Wing office: 6275 Crossman Lane, Inver Grove Heights, MN 55076. This is a youth program, not a paid job.
duration: Ideally a 2 hour squadron meeting each week, one Saturday event a month, and one week-long encampment in summer. School-based squadrons may differ.
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.

who_can_apply: Minnesota residents ages 13 to 19 who attend a middle or high school in Minnesota. Four representatives come from each of the eight congressional districts, plus at-large seats. Applicants should be active in their community and know the three branches of Minnesota government.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview in spring. Selected applicants meet the Council director with a trusted adult in May and are sworn in. You may get a follow-up call or text.
notes: The apply page has a caption with an older appointment date from the last round, so trust the Feb 28 and Mar 31 dates above. Full Council meetings are usually one Sunday afternoon a month. Check the apply page again in January 2027.
duration: Two-year term. You travel to the Twin Cities area at least five times a year for retreats, Youth Day at the Capitol and hearings.
pay_detail: The Council pages do not mention pay or a stipend.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 who live in Minnesota.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the online form. Pick a topic and write the paper. Send it in with the permission form.
notes: Participants get Borlaug Scholar recognition.
duration: Paper due early April; event on one day in May
pay_detail: Free. Participants are eligible for a $1,000 CFANS scholarship.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.

who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)

who_can_apply: You must attend a local high school. You must be a freshman, sophomore or junior when you apply. You must turn 15 by February 1 of the following year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form for the 2027 group. The link is on the program page. Add two recommendation letters: one from a teacher and one from a coach, mentor or supervisor. Add a resume with no photo. Add a personal statement of at least 300 words. Answer the short essay questions. Some students then get an interview.
notes: Chosen students need a TB test and proof of vaccines. They also go to registration, orientation, training and shadowing shifts. The earliest start is usually March. Shifts are Monday to Friday 4 to 8 p.m., or on weekends. There are no summer-only spots. Email MHAuxiliary@providence.org or call 949-364-1400 ext. 7944.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week, year round, until you graduate
pay_detail: Unpaid. You pay a one-time $125 membership fee for an ID badge, polo shirt and jacket. You also buy black khakis and shoes.

who_can_apply: Enrolled high school students (per the summer program page). The Fall 2026 event page does not list ages.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to the museum newsletter to hear when enrollment opens. For the Fall 2026 project use the Register button on its event page. Museum phone: 406-728-0447.
notes: It is not clear if the Fall 2026 project is part of the same program as Summer TAP. Ask the museum.
duration: Summer program. Fall 2026 project: 8 weeks, Thursdays 2:30 to 5 PM, Oct 1 to Nov 19, 2026
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: The page says it accepts volunteers of all ages and abilities. It does not list a teen rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application form on the volunteer page, or stop by the center. Call 406-327-0405 to ask about age rules.
notes: Call to confirm the minimum age for the role you want. The page does not state one.
duration: Varies by role
pay_detail: Volunteer roles. No pay is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 and up to lifeguard. Ages 16 and up to be a Water Safety Instructor. You need average swimming ability. Other pool jobs have no lifeguard rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply for a posted job on the City of Missoula jobs portal. Questions: 406-552-6000 (TTY 406-552-6131).
notes: The page said summer jobs were "posted soon", so check the portal for current openings.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The city reimburses the Red Cross training course if you accept a lifeguard or Water Safety Instructor job. Hourly pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email children@missoulapubliclibrary.org. Ask for more info. Ask to join the email list. Main library phone: 406-721-2665.
notes: Snacks are free at every meeting. The page does not say how many volunteer hours you can earn.
duration: Meets Thursdays, 3:30 to 5:30 PM, in the Art Box on level two
pay_detail: Members earn volunteer hours. No pay is stated.

who_can_apply: Any Montana high school student in any grade who likes history, law and government. Students from outside Missoula can apply. They must plan their own travel and place to stay.
how_to_apply: Not offered in 2026. Fill out the interest form on the program page to get news. Contacts: Professor Claire Arcenas or Professor Jody Pavilack. They work at the University of Montana.
notes: Based on the 2025 page. The topic may change in 2027.
duration: One week, 9 AM to 4 PM (2025: July 21-25)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 19 who go to Big Sky, Browning, Heart Butte, Hellgate or Sentinel High School. You must be a likely first-generation college student or from a family that meets the income rules. The page describes the program for college-bound students with a GPA of at least 2.5. You must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page for the program on the University of Montana site. Call the TRIO Upward Bound office at 406-243-2219. Or use the email on the page: jonathan.carter@umontana.edu.
notes: Check the dates with the office. Page dates and title do not match.
duration: Six weeks
pay_detail: Free. No stipend is mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Missouri youth ages 14 to 18 (age range from the Get Involved page; the program page itself does not state age).
how_to_apply: Answer short essay questions. Have two reference forms sent in. One is from 4-H staff or faculty. One is from a teacher, coach, boss or mentor.
notes: Cost is not stated. Contact 4hyouth@missouri.edu or 573-882-9359.
duration: One calendar year starting at State Congress
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Current Missouri 4-H members in grades 9 to 12. You need a recommendation from 4-H staff. Time on State Council or a national trip is a plus, not a must.
how_to_apply: Online application with three 250 to 300 word essays and one reference form from 4-H staff (not a family member). Finalists do a Zoom interview.
notes: No registration fee. 4-H covers lodging, meals and travel during the event. Families pay to get to the check-in spot. The page says it is held in even-numbered years, so the next one would be March 2028.
duration: 3 days (March 4 to 6, 2026)
pay_detail: No registration fee. 4-H covers lodging, meals and travel during the event. Families pay to get to the check-in spot.

who_can_apply: Missouri youth, per the 4-H program page. SPIN clubs take ages 5 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use Join 4-H and Enroll now on the program page, or contact your county 4-H office. Statewide questions: 4hyouth@missouri.edu, 573-882-9359.
notes: Costs are not listed on the page.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who live in Missouri. Your household must meet the income limit (for example, gross monthly income of $2,413 or less for a household of 1, $4,109 for 3, $4,957 for 4).
how_to_apply: Call and ask for a Youth Specialist at your regional workforce board. Examples listed: Full Employment Council in Kansas City 816-471-2330 ext. 1256, St. Louis City 314-657-3557, Workforce Development Board of St. Louis County 314-615-6010.
notes: Income limits come from the page and may change. The page lists regional boards across the state for other areas.
duration: Up to 320 hours
pay_detail: Paid training. Up to 320 hours. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: The page does not say who can join or state grades or ages.
how_to_apply: Ask your ag teacher about your school's chapter. State application forms are on missouriffa.org.
notes: 26,830 members (per the page). Camp page says Missouri FFA hires college-age students for camp staff, so that job is not for most teens. Dues are not stated.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. MOCA aims for a group with different school, area and arts-access backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Not open now. See mocateens.org and the MOCA Teens page for the next call.
notes: Competitive. Check the page in summer for the next cycle.
duration: 2026-27 group starts mid-September 2026
pay_detail: Teens are paid. The page does not give an amount.

who_can_apply: Montana 4-H youth who are at least 13 years old as of October 1 of the 4-H year. Chaperones must be certified 4-H volunteers or MSU Extension staff, age 21 or older.
how_to_apply: Register online in the 4-H Zsuite system. Each county has its own deadlines and steps, so call your county Extension office early.
notes: You do not have to enter a contest. Youth State Awards are due May 1.
duration: 4 days (July 14 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $285. It covers lodging for 3 nights, 7 meals, program costs and a t-shirt. Campus parking costs extra.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 by October 1 of the current year, enrolled in 4-H for at least 2 years and this year, and be or have been a Junior Leader or club officer. A maximum age is not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: County level: fill out an application. Then interview with the County Council. State officer: send the application to the Montana 4-H Center. It must be postmarked by June 15.
notes: You must already be in 4-H. The state team page lists five state officer jobs (for example President and Publicity Chair). Contact your county extension office. The state officer page does not state the term length for officers.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid leadership role. Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Montana 4-H youth who are at least 14 years old as of October 1 of the 4-H year. Counties send ambassadors and teen leaders. Chaperones must be certified 4-H volunteers or MSU Extension staff, age 21 or older.
how_to_apply: Register online in the 4-H Zsuite system. Call your county MSU Extension office for county rules. Fill in your info and waivers before the event.
notes: Cancel before sign-up closes for a full refund. Dress is business casual on Saturday. Dress for the banquet is business professional to semi-formal.
duration: Weekend (November 6 to 8, 2026)
pay_detail: $195. It covers lodging (2 to 4 people per room), Saturday and Sunday meals and program costs. Friday dinner is on your own.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You must be a 4-H member in your home county for at least three consecutive years. You need your county agent's approval.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application and send it. Email is preferred. You can also text 406-624-9835, fax 406-994-5417 or mail it to Montana 4-H Foundation, Inc., PO Box 173580, Bozeman.
notes: The page lists two at-large youth seats. Ask your county agent early because their approval is required.
duration: Two-year term (the page says it will change to one year)
pay_detail: Unpaid board seat. Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Montana teens ages 14 to 18. You must live in Montana. Teens from other states will not be considered.
how_to_apply: Online application filled out by the teen and a parent or guardian. The parent or guardian must sign a Youth Program Release form that is emailed after you submit. Email youthprograms@mtcorps.org with questions.
notes: Yellowstone sessions leave from Bozeman and Glacier sessions leave from Kalispell. Next dates not posted yet.
duration: 9-day sessions
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer crew. $100 service award and up to 64 service hours on successful completion. The program is free to join.

who_can_apply: Montana teens ages 17 to 18. Montana residency is required. You must commit to the full summer.
how_to_apply: Online application. A parent or guardian must sign the Youth Program Release that is emailed after you submit. Interview, then a decision within 2 weeks. Email youthprograms@mtcorps.org with questions.
notes: 2026 crews were in Helena, Kalispell (Flathead Youth Corps) and Missoula. Participants must commit to the full summer. Next dates not posted yet.
duration: About 8 weeks (2026 crews: mid June to early August)
pay_detail: Living allowance of $1,200 every two weeks before taxes, plus an AmeriCorps education award ($1,565.08 for the 2026 crews).

who_can_apply: Montana high school students who are rising juniors or seniors and want a career in science or engineering. No GPA or age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. Questions: metcamp@mtech.edu.
notes: The dates and deadline come from the 2026 news release on the Montana Tech site. The program page says Montana high school students are invited to apply. Watch for a new release around February 2027.
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free. Lodging, meals and course materials are provided. You must arrange your own ride to campus.

who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. The page checked for this card does not state a minimum age for these jobs. It lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the 'apply here' link on the Recreation employment page to see the seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.

who_can_apply: Volunteers without a parent or guardian must be 14 years old. Some jobs have higher age limits. Younger children can volunteer with a parent. This is the Family Volunteer program. The adult must register separately.
how_to_apply: Open the SSL Opportunities list on the Montgomery Parks site. Pick an event approved for SSL hours. Then register. You log in or create a volunteer account. Email parksvolunteers@montgomeryparks.org with questions.
notes: If you need many SSL hours in a short time, the page says that is only sometimes possible. Contacts on the page: Montgomery Parks Customer Service (301) 495-2595, and Volunteer Services 301-495-2504 on the main volunteer page. Office: 2425 Reedie Drive, 12th Floor, Wheaton, MD 20902.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Only opportunities approved by MCPS and the Montgomery County Volunteer Center give SSL hours.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 16 to 18 years of age before graduating high school. A parent must sign a consent form.
how_to_apply: Submit the online VolunTEEN application. Also send in the VolunTEEN Program Guidelines and the Parental Consent Form. Then you do a job shadow. After that, you go to an orientation and an interview. You also do onboarding and health steps.
notes: Adults 18 and older use a different program with 30 hours in three months. The page says the wait from application to first shift is about six weeks for adults. Sturgis, Custer, Lead-Deadwood and Spearfish hospitals have their own volunteer contacts; the page does not say they take teens.
duration: One 2 to 4 hour shift a week, same day and time, for 10 to 12 weeks (at least 30 hours).
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: In 2026, Future Leaders was for age 12 or 13. Counselors in Training was for age 14. Ages were counted on June 8, 2026. You must go to a required orientation and a week of training. You must also interview, and an interview does not promise a spot.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an interview time in the Moraga Parks and Recreation online catalog. The link is on the program page. An interview does not promise you a spot. If chosen, you pick the weeks you can come.
notes: In 2026 the orientation was May 7 and training was June 8 to 12. The page says CITs gain hands-on experience that prepares them for possible future jobs with Moraga Parks and Recreation. The town website also has a Summer Jobs page.
duration: 4-week blocks with weekly AM or PM shifts; most weeks have one full day, 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM
pay_detail: $250 per session for Moraga residents. $270 per session for non-residents.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens ages 16 to 22 who are in high school or college with a 2.5 GPA or better. You need a valid California driver license and a good driving record. You must pass an oral board and a background check. You must volunteer at least 4 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Contact Lt. Steve Borbely at 925-888-7052 to ask about the Police Cadet Program and how to apply.
notes: The cadet program is on the town employment page, below the police officer and reserve officer jobs. Good character and good health are also on the list. Ask the department if it is taking cadets now.
duration: At least 4 hours per week
pay_detail: Community service role. You volunteer at least 4 hours a week.

who_can_apply: The page does not list ages, grades or a residency rule. Ask the Parks and Recreation office before you apply.
how_to_apply: Applications for the 2027-2028 term will be available in July 2027. Contact Jasmine Bateson at the email link on the program page to ask how to apply.
notes: The committee meets at 7 PM on the 2nd Thursday of every month at the Hacienda de las Flores, 2100 Donald Drive, Moraga. Its service projects change each year.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising high school students with interest in STEAM, health or biomedical research and a 3.0 GPA or higher. The research option also needs your latest report card.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. For the research option, also send your report card, an essay about lab research and two recommendation forms. One must be from a science teacher. Some applicants are interviewed.
notes: Costs money. A session can be cancelled if too few students sign up. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. Ryan Clark, 404-752-1843. Dates shown are from summer 2026.
duration: 3 weeks (June 1 to 19, 2026) or 6 weeks (June 2 to July 10, 2026), 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: 3-week option $1,000. 6-week research option $1,500. No stipend listed.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or older when they apply, in 10th to 12th grade, with at least a 3.2 GPA.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. Add your official high school transcript and one recommendation from a teacher or counselor. List your top three course choices. Test scores are optional.
notes: Costs money. The page also calls the group rising juniors and seniors in places. Confirm your grade with the Summer Academy (academicsuccess@morehouse.edu). Dates shown are from the 2026 summer. The page says the program serves students from across the metro Atlanta area and beyond, and that courses are offered online.
duration: About 6 weeks (June 1 to July 10 in 2026, finals July 6 to 10)
pay_detail: $3,500 flat fee for up to three courses, plus up to $100 per course for books and a $30 non-refundable application fee

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17. Needs two letters of reference and proof of vaccines (MMR, Tdap, TB, flu). Do not apply if you expect three or more absences in the eight weeks.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the Volunteer Services page. The page says it leads to the adult volunteer application. Call Volunteer Services at 973-971-5475 if you are not sure.
notes: Applications are selected by lottery. Check the exact open and close times on the page.
duration: June 25 to August 13, 2027. Two 4-hour shifts a week, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 1 pm or 1 pm to 5 pm.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th, 8th or 9th grade in the fall. Volunteers can return each summer through high school. After one year, you can move to Science Camp or Tree Monitor.
how_to_apply: Write to youthvolunteers@mortonarb.org and ask about the application. Ask about the deadline too.
notes: Weekday daytime shifts at most branches. Shift hours, fees and training are not listed on the page. The Arboretum's paid science fellowships are for college students, so they are not in the guide. Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects are taken by emailing volunteer@mortonarb.org.
duration: June through August, with some optional fall weekends
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Teens; the page says age limits vary by program but does not list them. Minimum time: Junior Leaders 1 week, Junior Lifeguards 2 weeks, Deer Hollow Farm interns 3 weeks.
how_to_apply: Follow the application steps on the city page (online account, email, or mail/drop-off at Mountain View Community Center, 201 S. Rengstorff Ave). Questions: TheViewTeenCenter@mountainview.gov.
notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.
duration: 1 to 3 weeks minimum, depending on role
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid
