who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who represent Mountain View teens. The committee has fifteen members plus members-at-large. Residency or school rules are not spelled out on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the city YAC page. Questions: yac@mountainview.gov or 650-903-6331.
notes: Meets twice a month, August to June, at 4:30 p.m. in person at The View Teen Center, 263 Escuela Ave. Email to ask whether 2026-27 seats are still open. Re-check on 2026-10-10 returned HTTP 403 (page could not be read), so status and verified_on were left as they were.
duration: School year, August to June
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated

who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a grade, age or GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application form linked on the summer programs page. A flyer is also posted there.
notes: The same page lists three other programs (FIRE UP, CADET, SCREP) that are for college or graduate students, not high schoolers. The symposium is in person for all summer students. The application form link is the 2026 one.
duration: 2026: presentations June 1 to 19 (Mon to Thu, 10 am to 3 pm), fieldwork July 7 to 18, symposium July 21 to 22
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask the program about cost or stipend.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors from the Metro Atlanta area with a 2.85 GPA or higher and an interest in a health career. An interview is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Apply Now form. Teacher recommendations, grades and an interview help pick who is chosen.
notes: Costs money. The same page lists a separate college track, which is not for high schoolers. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. J. Wesley Lockhart, 404-752-1197.
duration: 4 weeks (2026 program dates not stated on the page)
pay_detail: $1,000 program cost

who_can_apply: Bay Area residents who attend a local high school, are at least 15 and have finished 9th grade before it starts. Parent or guardian permission is needed under 18. GPA is not considered.
how_to_apply: Contact Academy@BayAreaMetro.Gov or 415-778-5207. The page does not detail the application steps.
notes: MTC's older 'High School Internship Program' pages date to 2018. The high school program MTC lists now is this Academy. It is mostly virtual evening sessions. It is not a job placement.
duration: 2026: virtual Thursday evening sessions in July plus a final in-person session at Bay Area Metro Center, San Francisco (July 31, 2026)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after completion; amount not stated

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who are still in high school.
how_to_apply: The online application is closed because the program is full. The program page has a junior volunteer form you can download. For job shadowing, email aststudentservices@ascension.org. For Rutherford volunteer questions, email bryan.lowe@ascension.org.
notes: Adult volunteers must be 18 or older, but this junior program is for ages 15 to 18. Applications open January 1 and close when the program is full.
duration: 3 weeks, 9:00 am to 11:00 am
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students going into 9th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe how to register. Email fire@mtsu.edu to ask about dates and sign-up.
notes: This is a day camp, so it does not include housing. The page also says a pre-law camp is being explored but is not confirmed.
duration: 4 days (day camp)
pay_detail: $300 per student. This covers activities, labs, lunch and snacks each day, and a t-shirt.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 can apply to volunteer at the Smyrna Public Library. Linebaugh Library in Murfreesboro also takes teen volunteers by semester. The page lists no age range for Linebaugh.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for the branch you want. At Smyrna, teens should fill out the form themselves, not a parent. Smyrna questions go to smyrnays@rclstn.org. Linebaugh questions go to kturner@rclstn.org or tdavis@rclstn.org.
notes: Other library branches are not taking volunteers right now, per the page. Volunteers age 18 and up use a different form.
duration: One semester. The Smyrna fall season runs Aug 17 to Nov 21. The page does not state a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. Under 18 you fill out an extra section and a parent or guardian must sign. All volunteers must clear Live Scan fingerprinting.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the Volunteer Application (PDF). The form does not say where to return it, so ask at the Murrieta library (8 Town Square).
notes: The form lists the Teen Advisory Council as one option but gives no details about it. Confirm first how to return the form.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Teens who live in the City of Murrieta and are in 9th to 12th grade at a Murrieta Valley Unified School District school. You need two references.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application with five short answers and two references. Turn it in at the Murrieta Youth Center (40644 California Oaks Rd) or email it to the city contact on the sheet. Questions: Community Services at (951) 304-PARK, ext. 6117.
notes: Confirm first: the only sheet found is for the 2024-25 term. Members must go to all mandatory city events. Meetings were on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday evenings.
duration: Nine months, October to May, with an optional extended summer term; meetings in the evening
pay_detail: Unpaid. No stipend is stated.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Apply through the museum's volunteer portal (MyImpactPage) via the Learn more link on the Volunteer page. General museum volunteer steps listed: application, background check, new volunteer orientation. Questions: volunteer@lifeandscience.org.
notes: The camp-specific application page returned an error, so the camp schedule, requirements and deadline were not confirmed. The general volunteer perk is a free membership after 100 hours in a year (not confirmed for youth).
duration: Camp weeks; schedule not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Residents of Albemarle, Charlottesville, Greene, Louisa or Nelson who are at least 17 or entering 12th grade. High school applicants need a college admittance letter or a counselor letter showing they plan to attend college.
how_to_apply: Submit an application form, an essay of at least 300 words, transcripts with GPA, a resume, a college letter, and two reference letters from non-family members, to director@jmrl.org or to the Library Director, 201 East Market St, Charlottesville.
notes: The official source read is the 2026 program flyer (PDF) on jmrl.org; the library's other pages did not list this internship. An applicant cannot receive the award more than twice. Whether a Virginia Employment Certificate is needed for 14 and 15 year olds was not stated (applicants are 17 or entering 12th grade).
duration: 200 hours of library work
pay_detail: $3,000 stipend for 200 hours, plus eligibility for a $2,000 yearly scholarship toward an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree (up to $5,000 a year total)

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 13 or older. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign a consent form. Library staff will talk with you. They may ask for personal references.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Coordinator at tolmanj@cityofnampa.us. You can find it on the volunteer page. Or call the library at 208-468-5800. Ask when applications open again.
notes: The site also lists a Teen Advisory Council under its Support section. The volunteer page does not explain how to join it.
duration: Schedule set one-on-one with the library manager
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Job seekers from high school students (ages 15 and up) to older adults. Free.
how_to_apply: Walk in. KidsMatter says no registration is necessary. You can try a mock interview, work on a resume and talk about financial literacy there. Questions: sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org or 630-864-3960.
notes: The Park District says students can use the January fair to plan summer jobs. KidsMatter's 2027 page lists mock interviews, resume help and money skills. Last year's fair also had panels on the 7 Illinois career paths. Confirm what is offered in 2027. A news post from March 2025 also described a spring job fair for summer jobs. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.
duration: One day, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
pay_detail: The fair itself is free. Employers there hire for paid jobs.

who_can_apply: Groups of 2 to 5 teens in grades 7 through 12 when the application is sent in.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the August 1 to September 30 window. The top three to five teams give a short in-person pitch, and one team is chosen to run its program.
notes: Programs cannot sell products. They cannot be about politics, medicine or religion. The idea has to be new to the library calendar.
duration: Application in fall. Event runs 30 to 90 minutes in June, July or August 2027
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library pays for the program supplies.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be in 9th grade or above. You do not need a Naperville library card. TAG is open to teens in grades 6 through 12.
how_to_apply: Volunteers fill out the online volunteer application. For TAG, write to the teen librarians and ask how to attend. The email is teenlibrarians@naperville-lib.org.
notes: The volunteer coordinator's phone on the page is 630-637-2226.
duration: TAG meets once a month for two hours at rotating library locations
pay_detail: Unpaid. TAG members earn community service hours for each meeting.

who_can_apply: Up to 8 sophomores and juniors who live in Naperville. You must live inside the city limits. Freshmen and seniors cannot apply. Students who served on a board or commission cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button on any board or commission page of the city site. Answer yes to the Mayor's Chief of Staff question. Upload a resume or a note about your interest. Say that you are free all year.
notes: The news post does not say whether it is paid. Ask Rachel Pruneda (prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018). A full job description is on the city boards page.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term
pay_detail: Not stated. The city news post and the boards page were checked on 2026-10-10. Neither says anything about pay. Ask the city.

who_can_apply: Minimum age differs for each job. Check the age listed on the posting.
how_to_apply: Find a posting on the district job board and fill out the online application for that job. Mail, email or fax is not accepted. Apply for each job separately.
notes: Only applicants chosen for an interview are contacted. The page has a table of when each job is usually posted. Ages and pay are on each posting, so check them before you apply. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Seasonal. Summer jobs include Centennial Beach and the Paddleboat Quarry.
pay_detail: Pay is listed on each job posting, not on the main employment page.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Volunteers 13 and under may volunteer alongside a parent or guardian. BINGO volunteers must be at least 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Application (17 and under) and approve a DCFS background check, at least two weeks ahead. Then email Becca (address on the Programs volunteer page) to sign up for a program. You cannot just show up, except at Nature Champion days.
notes: Volunteer hours can be confirmed by email, a signed letter or a school form.
duration: Dates listed this fall (no year printed; the weekdays match 2026): Kids' Night Out on Fridays, Nov 20 to Dec 18, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m. Santa's Workshop on Dec 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17 and 20.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The district can sign off on volunteer hours for school.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, finished 8th grade, and not older than 21. Needs a C average or better, and no serious arrests or convictions.
how_to_apply: Download the cadet application and turn it in at the front desk, 1350 Aurora Ave. A committee checks references and does a background check and an interview. Questions: NPDCadets@naperville.il.us.
notes: The police internship on the same site is for college students, so it is not listed. The department points younger people to the cadet program.
duration: Ongoing, two meetings a month
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Cadets help with security and traffic control at events.

who_can_apply: Students in high school or going into high school in fall 2026. You live in Naperville or go to high school there. You need parent permission and your own ride. You need good standing at school and no criminal contacts.
how_to_apply: Print and fill out the application and waiver at naperville.il.us/youthacademy. Send the signed forms to Sergeant Greg Rink at rinkg@naperville.il.us. Or drop them off at 1350 Aurora Ave.
notes: First come, first served and space is limited.
duration: 6 weeks, Thursday nights 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students who live inside Naperville city limits. You are a sophomore, junior or senior. Freshmen cannot apply. If you already served on a board or commission, you cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Click Apply on any board's page on the city Boards and Commissions site. Fill in the profile and the student rep questions. Upload a resume or a short statement. You can apply to up to three boards.
notes: 24 positions, two per board. Contact: Rachel Pruneda, prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018. The dates come from an August 2026 city news post.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term; most boards meet in the evening
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.
duration: Whenever you want
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.
duration: 12 weeks, June 1 to Aug 28 in 2026
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in Durham County in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Watch the Nasher Teen Council page for the next application. The page does not say when it opens. Meetings are every Thursday evening during the school year.
notes: Durham County students only. Watch the page for the next application.
duration: Thursdays 5:30 to 7:30 PM, October to April
pay_detail: Free. Snacks, dinner and parking are provided at every meeting.

who_can_apply: People over age 14 can take the Open Opportunities shifts. The 21+ events are not open to teens.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the museum's volunteer portal. Then sign up for a volunteer orientation. If you have questions, send an email to volunteer@adventuresci.org.
notes: The museum also runs Youth CR3W, a youth program with its own form. The CR3W page does not state ages, pay or schedule. Ask volunteer@adventuresci.org before you assume it fits you.
duration: No minimum hours stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free membership after 100 hours.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who are still in high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the West junior volunteer application between January and March. The hospital also asks for an interview. You must wear a uniform.
notes: Call 615-222-2127 for Midtown and West. Ascension Saint Thomas Rutherford has its own junior program. That program runs three weeks in July.
duration: 6 weeks. The program begins in June.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and older for the 2026 camps. The RISE research camps also need a 3.0 overall GPA and a 3.0 math and science GPA.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the newsletter on the camp page to hear when registration opens. Then register for the camp you want.
notes: Camps for 2027 may differ from the 2026 list. The page asks you to email Beth Bowman at beth.bowman@belmont.edu with questions.
duration: One-week camps. RISE ran about four weeks.
pay_detail: Most 2026 camps cost $425. The RISE research camps cost $1,700. One camp, VISIBL, was $0 for Metro Nashville students nominated by a science teacher. Email Beth Bowman if cost is a problem.

who_can_apply: Teens age 16 or older. Younger teens (10 to 17) can volunteer through the Family Team program with a parent or other adult family member.
how_to_apply: Download and fill out the Teen Volunteer Application. Then do the orientation training you must take. Call the Volunteer Manager at 615-353-6966 with questions.
notes: The page says the teen program is for age 16 or older and does not give an upper age. The application PDF on the page is dated June 2025, so ask the Volunteer Manager if it is the current form.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Songwriters ages 12 to 18. July applicants also send a recording of 1 original song. People who have never come before get first pick.
how_to_apply: Email camp@countrymusichalloffame.org for 2027 sign up info. If you want aid, apply for it before you sign up. For the July camp, send up to 5 minutes of audio or video of 1 original song with lyrics.
notes: Costs real money. Campers who have been to two or more camps may be waitlisted.
duration: 1 week: June 14 to 19, 2027 (beginner to intermediate) or July 12 to 17, 2027 (intermediate to advanced)
pay_detail: 2026 fees on the page: $505 for museum members and $595 for non-members. 2027 fees are not posted. Need-based aid can lower the fee to $297 or $30.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 or high school freshmen to seniors. You must pass a background check, which the museum pays for. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Today on the Teen Team page. Or sign up for an info session. Email volunteer@countrymusichalloffame.org with questions.
notes: The museum also runs a Songwriting Camp for ages 12 to 18 (June 14 to 19 and July 12 to 17, 2027). In 2026 fees were $505 for members and $595 for non-members, with need based aid.
duration: About one assignment per month
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Litter pick-up is open to all ages. Trail work, invasive plant removal and stream clean-up are for ages 18 and up, or ages 13 and up with an adult. School groups in grades K to 12 can volunteer with two or more chaperones.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile in the Friends of Warner Parks volunteer database. Fill out the information form and sign the waiver.
notes: Under 18 means you need an adult for most work. The Ambassador program is 18 and up. The page does not give an age rule for the seasonal SWEAT trail crew. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the page.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens age 15 to 18 who want to work with peers and professional artists.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe the application. Email teens@fristartmuseum.org with questions.
notes: The Frist also runs free Teen ARTlabs (art sessions with professional artists). Ages and dates for those are not listed on the Teens page; see the museum's teen events calendar.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The museum says TAAG time may count toward required service hours.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors. Genesys Works partners with specific schools. Nashville is working with Metro Nashville Public Schools for its first class.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application, then interview, then confirm you accept. Click Apply Now on the Genesys Works application page and pick the Nashville location. Email nashville@genesysworks.org with questions.
notes: This program is new in Nashville. Ask your school counselor if your school is a partner. The page does not say if a work permit is needed for teens under 18.
duration: 8 weeks of training, then a year-long internship
pay_detail: Paid internship. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: People 13 and older can have a Hands On account. Each project has its own age rule, so check the listing. Kids under 13 volunteer through the family page.
how_to_apply: Make a Hands On account and sign up for a project. A parent or guardian must sign the Hands On waiver. Bring the waiver to the project and check in with the Volunteer Leader.
notes: For school credit, bring your school's form. Ask the volunteer coordinator to check your hours.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 16.
how_to_apply: Send the finished application to Erin Adams. Staff review the forms. Then they invite students to an interview.
notes: The page still says 2026 applications are open, but that camp has passed. Ask about 2027 through the contact link. The camp is an initiative of the Benjamin Harrison Presidential Site.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. each day.
pay_detail: $350 per student, or $300 for Hermitage members. Lunch is not included. Limited financial help is offered.

who_can_apply: The program page does not state an age range. Read the STriVe online guide for details.
how_to_apply: Watch the hospital volunteering page for the application in Spring 2027. Read the STriVe online guide first.
notes: Applications may close early if the hospital gets many. The Caring Hands Crew is for anyone 16 and up who wants to help the hospital's mission.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Youth who live in Davidson County. Ages 14 to 15 apply for Experience Work. Ages 16 to 18 apply for High School Internships.
how_to_apply: Pick Experience Work or High School Internships on the POWER Youth job portal, search the job list for your age group, apply and check your email for a confirmation. Call 615-862-8860 for help.
notes: The program page says it serves ages 14 to 22 overall and lists High School Internships for ages 16 to 19. The job seekers page says 16 to 18, so this card uses 18. Confirm with Metro Action. This card covers the teen tracks only. Neither page says whether a work permit or ID is needed, so ask Metro Action. Office is at 1281 Murfreesboro Pike, Nashville.
duration: About 7 weeks (June 1 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: $12 per hour (Experience Work, ages 14 to 15). $15 per hour (High School Internship).

who_can_apply: Anyone age 13 or older. Volunteers under 18 need permission from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form for 1 person. Then watch your email for next steps.
notes: The library says it does not take every applicant. It places volunteers by what each site needs. It also asks you to keep a set weekly schedule, so check you can. The page says shorter jobs can be found through Hands On Nashville.
duration: Weekly shifts for at least 6 months and 50 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Standard food sorting is for ages 12 and older. Cold food sorting is for ages 16 and older at the Martin site. Volunteers under 18 need a parent or guardian to sign a waiver. Volunteers under 16 must come with an adult.
how_to_apply: Book a shift ahead of time on the online volunteer calendar. Bring a signed Youth Volunteer Waiver if you are under 18. Groups of 5 or more need a leader who is 18 or older.
notes: The food bank asks for 1 adult for every 7 volunteers under 18. Walk-ins may not be accepted. The sites named on the page are Martin, Nacarato and Camden, and shift days differ by site.
duration: Shift length is not stated on the program page. Stay for the full shift.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Hiring starts at age 15 for most jobs. Many jobs need you to be 16 or older. Only a limited number of jobs are open to 15-year-olds.
how_to_apply: Use the online careers portal. Send one application only, for the department you want most. A hiring manager will contact you if your application fits, so check your contact info.
notes: Do not apply to more than one department. Do not call to ask about status. The page does not say if a work permit is needed for teens under 18, so ask the employer.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Pay rate not stated on the program page. The page says you get daily pay.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Say if you want residential or day. Upload your transcript, test scores if you have them, a one-page essay and one recommendation letter. Incomplete packets are not considered.
notes: Run with Cummins as a partner. Contact Dre Davenport at ddaventp@tnstate.edu or 615-963-5389.
duration: Dates are June 7 to July 3, 2026. The length in weeks is not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: $400 per student. It is not refundable. Meals are provided.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th grade students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload your transcript, test scores if you have them, and a one-page essay. Your teacher or counselor emails one recommendation letter to Professor Kang Du.
notes: The Tennessee Department of Transportation runs and funds this program. Contact Professor Kang Du at kdu@tnstate.edu. Or call the College of Engineering at 615-963-5401.
duration: 4 weeks: 3 weeks on campus, then 1 week online.
pay_detail: Free to students. Pay or a stipend is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Open to grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $50 fee. If you are placed in a course you pay a 20% deposit one week after the admission notice. Check the box for aid if you want to apply for it.
notes: It costs money. The page offers aid for families with adjusted gross income of $105,000 or less or severe hardship. It offers a payment plan for everyone. The page mixes 2026 deadlines with 2027 session dates. Confirm both with precollege@vanderbilt.edu.
duration: One week. The tuition page lists several 2027 session dates in June and July.
pay_detail: One-week tuition on the PTY page: $2,150 (grades 7 to 8), $2,850 (grades 9 to 10), $2,950 (grades 11 to 12). Tuition covers course, materials, housing and meals. $50 application fee ($100 international).

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16. Your school must have an affiliation agreement with VUMC. Homeschool students need an agreement with their homeschool group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application in one sitting. It does not save. Upload your health insurance card, a health form, a safety quiz certificate and signed forms.
notes: Minors cannot observe in some places. These are operating rooms, emergency departments, pediatric intensive care units and the Vanderbilt Psychiatric Hospital. If your school has no agreement with VUMC, you are not eligible. Email VOE@VUMC.org with questions.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is no application fee.

who_can_apply: Teens from age 13 to high school seniors.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send 1 recommendation form from someone who is not a relative or family friend. Then go to a 60 minute group interview and all training sessions.
notes: The zoo's page and its info sheet differ on small things (how many recommendations, the fee). Send an email to volunteer@nashvillezoo.org before you apply. The dates on the info sheet are from the last cycle posted. They are interviews Mar 28 and 29 and Apr 11 and 12, and a summer start on May 26.
duration: Summer: one shift a week for at least 7 weeks plus one week of Zoo Camp. School year: at least 4 hours each semester plus one special event.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The zoo's page mentions a one-time fee that includes a uniform, but no amount is posted.

who_can_apply: High school students. David Ricardo is for first-timers with no more than one economics course. Team size and school rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the sign-up form on the challenge page (choose Teacher, Parent, Student or Friend) to get a message when registration opens. Phone: 212-827-3600.
notes: Few details are posted yet. Ask an economics teacher to be your team contact. Confirm first.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: No pay. Cash prizes. Cost to enter is not stated.

who_can_apply: Mostly low-income 16 to 24 year olds. You must be a U.S. citizen, a legal resident or allowed to work in the U.S. If you are under 18, a parent, guardian or approved adult must agree and meet an admissions rep. Some rules apply about drug use and criminal history.
how_to_apply: Make an account on the sign-up site. Fill out the application. Interview with an admissions rep. Send papers such as your ID and proof that you are a citizen or resident. A campus review can take up to 30 days.
notes: The FAQ says you may get in faster if you are homeless. It does not name foster youth, so ask an admissions rep. Only enter your ID or Social Security number on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. Check that your nearest campus is open before you plan around it.
duration: Between 8 months and 3 years, depending on the training
pay_detail: Free for students. A living allowance is paid every two weeks and goes up as training moves along. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 24 who are out of school and out of work. YouthBuild mainly serves people without a high school diploma and with little money. Local sites set their own rules.
how_to_apply: Use the program map on the YouthBuild site to find a program near you, then contact it.
notes: The site says more than 300 programs run in seven countries. The program pages do not confirm a site in Elgin, Chicago, Atlanta, New York or Los Angeles. Use the map.
pay_detail: Not stated on the national page. Ask the local program.

who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from Franklin County and surrounding areas.
how_to_apply: Register when the program reopens; contact HNHFWorkforceDev@nationwidechildrens.org.
notes: The hospital's student opportunities page also lists Project SEARCH (a 9-month internship for students with disabilities) and Upward Bound Math and Science. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.
duration: November to April; two evening sessions a month (4:30 to 8 p.m.)
pay_detail: Paid; amount not stated

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 16 to 21. Participants must be at least 16 years old at the time of registration.
how_to_apply: Register online during the registration window. Questions: HNHFWorkforceDev@NationwideChildrens.org.
notes: Popular: the page says there is overwhelming interest, and about 108 young adults took part in 2025. Schedules are Monday to Friday starting at 9 or 10 a.m. All participants are 16 or older, and Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) lets 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer give proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead of a work permit; the hospital may still ask for paperwork, so confirm.
duration: 4 or 8 weeks, about 20 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 30)
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 can join the teen programs. Age is counted as of January 1 of the program year. You join through your local county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H program. Then enroll through 4-H Online. That is the system for joining, renewing and signing up for events.
notes: The teen page was updated April 30, 2026. Clover Crew is listed as new in 2026. Programs differ from county to county. The pages do not give a fee or the dates for the teen events.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. Ask your county 4-H office.

who_can_apply: Teams of 3 to 5 students from a school, non-traditional school or youth group such as 4-H or FFA. High school teams need five members to place at state. Each team needs an adult advisor.
how_to_apply: Sign up with your county Soil and Water Conservation District. In Wake County, fill out the Wake Envirothon sign-up form. The official form is emailed to advisors later in fall 2026.
notes: The dates above come from Wake County's page. Other areas of the state have their own area dates and deadlines, so call your county district. Wake contact: Leah Purvis, 919-250-1065.
duration: Area contest plus 2 day state event
pay_detail: Wake County's district pays registration for Wake teams. Fees for other counties are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who belong to a school FFA chapter, which runs through a school agricultural education program. Homeschool students can join if they take an agriculture course and have an SAE project (for example through the NCSU Agriscience Academy chapter).
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher if your school has an FFA chapter. Take an agriculture class. The chapter advisor sends in the roster and dues. Homeschool families use the Homeschool FFA Membership Application on the page.
notes: The state office is at 4111 Beryl Road, Raleigh, NC 27606, 919-515-4206. The site says North Carolina has over 47,000 FFA members. If your school has no ag program, the page explains how a school can start one.
duration: Membership year runs Aug 1 to July 31
pay_detail: 2026-27 dues: $12 for high school students ($7 national plus $5 state) and $8 for middle school students ($7 national plus $1 state). Many chapters collect these through the school.

who_can_apply: High school students or recent high school graduates in good academic standing. Seniors may apply to take part the summer before college. College students are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Governor's Page application and send the online recommendation form to two people: a non-relative school staff or faculty member (unless homeschooled) and a non-relative adult who can speak to your fit. Applications without both recommendations are not processed.
notes: Founded in 1973. The work location is the Albemarle building, 325 N Salisbury St, Raleigh. Business clothes are required. Pages and their guardians arrange where to stay and eat in Raleigh. Office of the Governor phone: (919) 814-2000. The page does not list dates for page weeks. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: One page week of four days (Monday afternoon, then Tuesday to Thursday)
pay_detail: $200 stipend per week to help with travel and lodging costs. A limited number of host families provide meals and rides for a $100 fee paid by the page.

who_can_apply: North Carolina residents in public or non-public schools. You must meet one of the GPA or course rules in the family overview, for example a 3.25 unweighted GPA. You cannot apply on your own. Your school or district must nominate you first.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or local Governor's School coordinator. Turn in the student application at your school, not to the state office. It has one essay or audition and a personal readiness form. Turn in two recommendation forms too.
notes: Competitive. The family overview says about 1,800 students are nominated and about 800 are picked in a typical year. Students must stay the whole session and may attend only once. The overview says you may not use AI on the application.
duration: Four weeks (June 20 to July 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $600 tuition per student, collected through the school or district. Need-based scholarships are offered by the NC Governor's School Foundation. Families pay for travel.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors in good school standing. A North Carolina House member must sponsor you. You must not have been a House Page before. School principal approval is needed if you serve during the school year.
how_to_apply: Ask your own House member to sponsor you (find yours with the Find Your Legislators tool). Then fill out the online application, which goes to that member. You can ask the House Page office, Room 1329, 16 W. Jones Street, Raleigh, for a paper copy.
notes: Very competitive and you can apply with only one member. The Speaker of the House makes the final appointments. Housing in Raleigh is up to your parent or guardian. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: One week, Monday to Thursday, while the legislature is in session
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Centers: Schenck, 98 Schenck Dr, Pisgah Forest, NC 28768. Kittrell, 1096 U.S. Highway 1 South, Kittrell, NC 27544. Oconaluftee, 502 Oconaluftee Job Corps Rd, Cherokee, NC 28719. No closure notice showed on the pages on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school girls in grades 9 to 12 who are enrolled in a North Carolina public, private, charter or home school. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to girls from across the state, but all placements are in the Raleigh area.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application portal opens in early January 2027. The FAQ says to check the program website for current deadlines. Email your resume, cover letter and transcript to doa.youth.involvement@doa.nc.gov. Students who skip these documents are dropped from the process.
notes: Only 15 to 20 spots. You must get yourself to your job site every day; the program only gives rides to Wednesday and Thursday events. Contact named on the page: Jean McBride. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 4 weeks, 40-hour weeks Monday to Friday (July 2027, exact dates not posted yet)
pay_detail: $1,700 stipend, paid on the second to last day of the program. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. You are chosen by an application, a teacher's note and a group interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student form and a teacher recommendation form. Both are due by the deadline.
notes: Volunteer role, and it costs a yearly fee. Contact Lynn Cross (listed on the page) about scholarships.
duration: September to May: two planning meetings a month (Wednesdays 4 to 6pm), every cafe on first Fridays Sept to April, August retreat
pay_detail: $75 per year for snacks, T-shirt and supplies. Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 during the 2026-27 school year. Selected by application.
how_to_apply: Applications reopen in January 2027 and are due Friday, April 9, 2027 at 5pm. Students bring their own lunch. The museum supplies program materials, snacks and transport to field sites.
notes: The page also still shows last year's dates (deadline April 8, 2026). The 2027 dates above are the ones listed for the 2027 program. Location is the Nature Research Center, 121 West Jones St., Raleigh.
duration: 1 week, 9am to 4:30pm daily (June 14-18, 2027)
pay_detail: $50 for the week. Scholarships available on request.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. The page states no residency requirement. The program follows Wake County's school calendar.
how_to_apply: The page gives no step-by-step process. Staff contact is Lynn Cross (listed on the page).
notes: The page did not describe how students are picked.
duration: September to April. One monthly meeting with Living Collections staff plus two monthly group meetings with scientists (3:30-5 pm).
pay_detail: $75 per year (snacks, T-shirt, boots and protective eyewear); optional trips may cost extra for travel

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders. The museum's general volunteer rule is 18 and older; under-18s join through the teen programs.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in mid-January 2027, then attend a group interview if invited. The page does not describe the application steps; contact the listed staff member.
notes: Teens may reschedule up to 3 of the 10 shifts. Other teen programs on the museum's Teens page (Climate Resilience Institute, Cafe Coordinators, Teen Science Cafes) were listed without dates or fees.
duration: 10 weeks, June 15 to August 19. One shift a week (Tue, Wed or Thu, 10-1 or 1-4). Required orientation Saturday May 15.
pay_detail: $75 per summer (covers orientation, food, T-shirt, nametag and props)

who_can_apply: Recommended for ages 11 to 17. Free, no application stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Show up at the Daily Planet Cafe at the museum or watch live on YouTube. No sign up is listed on the page.
notes: A good first step before applying to Cafe Coordinators.
duration: 1 hour, 6pm to 7pm, first Friday of each month
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10, 11 or 12 who are in good school standing. A North Carolina senator must sponsor you. If you serve during the school year, your principal must approve it first.
how_to_apply: Contact your senator and ask for an application. It is not online and not available from the Page office. Return the finished form to your senator.
notes: Competitive. Each senator can sponsor only a set number of students. The Senate President Pro Tempore makes the appointments. Business clothes are required. Bring money for lunch each day.
duration: One week during the legislative session: report Monday afternoon, work Tuesday to Thursday
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: High school (secondary) and college (postsecondary) students in career and technical education pathways.
how_to_apply: Ask your career and technical education (CTE) teacher about your school's chapter. Your advisor signs you up on the national SkillsUSA registration site. It is linked from the NC join page.
notes: Contacts on the site: information line 919-675-1241, info@SkillsUSAnc.org, P.O. Box 88, Oxford, NC 27565. The March 1 date is described as an annual national deadline, not tied to a named year.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student membership is $14, per the NC SkillsUSA join page.

who_can_apply: Academically talented North Carolina students in their second or third year of high school who want STEM careers. Applicants must complete the Residency Determination Service process. Students are picked by Congressional District.
how_to_apply: Apply on cfnc.org with a CFNC account. Finish the Residency Determination Service step and write the essays. Your school sends your transcript and forms.
notes: 2027 campuses: Appalachian State, East Carolina, UNC Charlotte and UNC Wilmington, with dates from June 20 to July 31. Contact: summerventures@ncssm.edu or 919-416-2747.
duration: About four weeks between mid-June and end of July 2027, depending on the campus
pay_detail: No cost to accepted students. Meals and housing on campus are included. It does not pay a wage.

who_can_apply: Junior Division: ages 13 to 18 and not yet graduated from high school. There is also a Young Artist Division for ages 18 to 23. Instrumentalists.
how_to_apply: Watch the competition page for 2027 details. If you have a question, you can send it by email to education@ncsymphony.org.
notes: Niche: for serious young players. Entry fee and rounds' dates are not stated on the page.
duration: Preliminary and final rounds (the page does not say where)
pay_detail: No pay. First and second prize winners in each division receive cash awards.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in North Carolina, chosen by American Legion posts. The About page describes the program as for young men in North Carolina. No age or residency rule beyond that is listed.
how_to_apply: Applications open Nov 1, 2026. Local American Legion posts pick delegates. Find a post near you. The FAQ page links a post finder. Or email info@tarheelboysstate.org.
notes: Delegates must attend the full week. The FAQ page says graduates get an automatic $20,000 scholarship to Chowan University, spread over 4 years. The girls' program is a separate American Legion Auxiliary program (Tar Heel Girls State) and is not covered here.
duration: One week (the 87th session is June 20 to 26, 2027)
pay_detail: $500 per delegate for lodging, meals and two uniform shirts. A local American Legion post, business or community group often pays it. Families with money worries are told to contact the program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, per the national Civil Air Patrol page. Cadets join a local cadet or composite squadron, and you may join any one in the wing.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the NC Wing page. Then contact a squadron and visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the membership application and pay dues.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. NC Wing office: 3520 Alamance Road, Burlington, NC 27215, 336-290-7473, info@ncwgcap.org. The NC Wing site lists a 2027 summer encampment page.
duration: Weekly squadron meetings all year
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $60 for North Carolina in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Start as early as age 16. You must be enrolled in high school or be a high school graduate, interested in a high-demand career field, and ready to do both on-the-job learning and classroom instruction.
how_to_apply: Find a Registered Apprenticeship opportunity on the ApprenticeshipNC site and contact the program sponsor or employer to apply. Questions: apprenticeshipnc@nccommunitycolleges.edu or 919-807-6988. The page also mentions youth apprenticeship consortia that serve high school students.
notes: The NC Department of Labor says youth under 18 who work in North Carolina must have a Youth Employment Certificate, started by the employer once you have a job offer. Some jobs are off limits to people under 18 unless a supervised practice agreement is approved. Specific openings and employers change, so use the Find Apprenticeship Opportunities tool.
duration: Varies by apprenticeship
pay_detail: Apprentices are paid employees from day one, with raises as you gain skills. The wage depends on the employer and is not stated.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in good standing at a public, private, charter or home school in North Carolina. You do not need a legislator to sponsor you.
how_to_apply: The page says to complete the student application, but it shows no link. Contact the program coordinator, Erica Gallion, at (919) 301-1372. Ask for the application.
notes: The page does not say where the application is, what it costs or when it is due. Check the page again or call the coordinator before you plan.
duration: A conference of about three days (the 2025-26 session was March 13 to 15, 2026)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Open to rising sixth graders through recent high school graduates. For the Junior Wildlife Assistant role you must be in 10th or 11th grade when you apply, live within 90 miles of the zoo, and be able to lift 50 lbs and stand for 30 minutes. Other roles have their own rules on their pages.
how_to_apply: When recruitment opens, choose a teen role on the zoo's Teen Volunteers page. Send in that role's application. Junior Wildlife Assistants also do a 20 minute phone interview. They go to at least two Zoo Pathways events.
notes: Roles listed: Play Pals (middle school), Junior Wildlife Assistant (high school), Camp Crew (middle and high school), Zoo Futures (middle school). Zoo address: 4401 Zoo Parkway, Asheboro, NC 27205, 336-879-7001.
duration: Summer only, May through August. Junior Wildlife Assistant: 6 weeks, 13 to 15 hours a week (last season June 17 to July 31)
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time $20 onboarding fee for new volunteers, which can be waived for families with financial hardship.

who_can_apply: Age or grade requirements are not stated on the page. Ask the program manager.
how_to_apply: The page does not say when the next council opens. Questions: Erin Hanehan, manager of teen and college programming (erin.hanehan@dncr.nc.gov).
notes: The museum also runs teen workshops for ages 13 to 18 (separate, listed on the same page).
duration: Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 pm, Sept 17, 2026 to June 3, 2027
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: North Carolina residents. The page does not list grade levels. It wants students with strong school skills from many walks of life.
how_to_apply: Online application through the INSPIRE page. Contact inspire@ncssm.edu or 919-416-2784.
notes: Held at NCSSM-Morganton in western NC, not in the Triangle. Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week residential (June 21-26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free (room and meals included)

who_can_apply: Current North Carolina 8th graders. You must live in the counties listed for each campus. The Durham campus counties include Wake, Durham, Orange and many more.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. There is a workshop on how to apply on Dec 3, 2026. There is an info session in Durham on Jan 14, 2027.
notes: Only for students who are in 8th grade when they apply. Cohort 1 is for current 8th graders; Cohort 2 is for the returning rising 10th graders.
duration: 1 week residential each summer, two summers, plus school year workshops
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Rising 7th through 12th graders from anywhere. You apply for a course whose requirements you meet. A parent fills out part of the application.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian with custody fills out part 1 of the application. The student writes the short answers. Admission is rolling. Students can ask for money help after they are accepted.
notes: There is also a free sponsored option for 60 students in 18 western NC counties (Dogwood Health Trust). Dates and fees are from the last cycle's pages.
duration: Varies by course
pay_detail: $495 to $1,495 for rising 7th to 9th graders; $695 to $1,925 for rising 10th to 12th graders. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: The page links to an interest form and to a program website. It does not list application steps.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential

who_can_apply: High school students with disabilities in grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th to 12th graders). You can be in regular classes. You can also be on the Occupational Course of Study (a high school diploma track). Students in public, charter, private and home school can apply.
how_to_apply: Student and at least one parent must attend an open house first, then apply. Contact program director Joann Blumenfeld, (919) 633-3120.
notes: The first open house date (Jan 14, 2027) is the one that starts the process. Pay amount for internships is not stated.
duration: June to June (summer week plus Saturdays in the school year)
pay_detail: The program is free. Paid STEM internships are also offered. The pay amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who can show they know English. The page says students 12 and younger are not allowed. Students who have already graduated are not allowed either.
how_to_apply: Sign up online. Use the Register Now button on the Global Training Initiative page (event ID OGE-F26-GC). When you sign up, you get access to the Knowledge Database.
notes: Deadline is very close. Run by NC State, but open to students anywhere.
duration: One weekend, online (Saturday 8am to Sunday 8pm Eastern)
pay_detail: $299. $30 off before Sept 27. $50 off for past GTI participants.

who_can_apply: Must be a high school student. The page does not say whether out-of-state students can apply.
how_to_apply: Visit the program website to learn more and apply (growforit.ces.ncsu.edu/growforit-programs/hssi). The page does not list application steps.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: $650. Some financial help may be available.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors who like farming and farm careers (NC Farm Bureau page).
how_to_apply: Download the application from the NC Farm Bureau IFAL page. Or get one at your county Farm Bureau office.
notes: Dates are last year's. The NC Farm Bureau page does not state a cost, so the no cost entry is not confirmed. In 2026 the program ran at three campuses (NC State, NC A&T and University of Mount Olive). The site you attend may differ.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: No cost

who_can_apply: Any current high school student.
how_to_apply: Apply on the program website. The address is cals.ncsu.edu/animal-science/extension/livestock-science-camp.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 through 12. NC State chapter works with schools in northeastern and central North Carolina.
how_to_apply: Apply through the MSEN office. See the program website (fi.ncsu.edu/teams/msen).
notes: Dates are last year's pattern. Contact the MSEN office about scholarships.
duration: Yearlong, September to July
pay_detail: $110. Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Must be a high school student. The page does not list grade rules or a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Visit the program website to learn more and sign up (growforit.ces.ncsu.edu/growforit-programs/nc-youth-institute). The page does not tell how to sign up.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: One-day conference at NC State (the 2026 listing gives April 16 and 17, 2026)
pay_detail: No cost

who_can_apply: You must be in high school now, in grade 10 or higher. International students need English test scores.
how_to_apply: Apply on the GTI website.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 4 weeks, online
pay_detail: $1,295. Early registration discounts and partial scholarships (short essay).

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors with an interest in poultry.
how_to_apply: Apply at go.ncsu.edu/applypssi
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders from North Carolina.
how_to_apply: Apply through your local NC Soil and Water Conservation District. Deadlines differ by district. They are usually in late March. Contact the co-coordinators listed on the page (Liz Driscoll, liz_driscoll@ncsu.edu, 919.886.3424).
notes: Dates are last year's. Awards and scholarships are given to students at the workshop.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: No cost

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade (2026 page). Homeschooled, out-of-state and international students are encouraged to apply. Admission is based on academics (typically A's and B's in math and science) and interest.
how_to_apply: Online application: GPA, school and counselor info, and two short written answers (camp goals and a problem you would like to solve). Each applicant is placed in one workshop.
notes: All dates and the fee on the page are for 2026; 2027 terms were not posted. The Engineering Place also runs day camps for younger students.
duration: 1 week (2026 weeks: June 14-19, June 21-26, July 5-10, July 12-17)
pay_detail: $1,550 camp fee in 2026, no refunds. A limited amount of financial aid is available for demonstrated need.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Contact the program (Kent Lupino, named on the page) to ask about joining a team.
notes: The page does not give a season or the fee. Tournaments can go to the state, regional and national level if a team qualifies.
duration: Team practice Mondays and Thursdays 6 to 9 pm, plus Saturdays as needed
pay_detail: Team registration fee (amount not stated). Donations also help fund teams.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th to 12th graders (program precollege page). Scholarships based on need are offered. The Shelton page says 1 in 3 participants gets one.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More and Apply link on the Shelton Challenge site for the Red Hat Shelton Challenge at NC State. Other partner sites run the same program in other places.
notes: Dates are last year's. Check sheltonleadership.ncsu.edu/shelton-challenge-programs for 2027 dates.
duration: 6 days, residential

who_can_apply: High school students. Preference goes to rising juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Visit the TexTEC program website to learn more (textiles.ncsu.edu/academics/k-12/textec-camp). The page does not list the steps to apply.
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 2 days, day camp

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors. Up to 40 students per week are chosen. The choice is based on grades, activities and interest in the Wilson College of Textiles.
how_to_apply: Apply on the STEP website (step.textiles.ncsu.edu).
notes: Dates are last year's.
duration: 1 week, residential
pay_detail: $450. Partial and full scholarships for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: U.S. or U.S. territory residents who are rising high school sophomores, juniors or seniors (rising college freshmen also accepted) and are 15 by June 7, 2027. Past in-person campers cannot apply for in-person VetCAMP again.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline. Pay the $30 application fee for each week you apply for. Virtual VetCAMP is offered to all who are not picked for the in-person camp.
notes: Applicants must upload an unofficial high school transcript. Maximum of about 5 wait-listed per week.
duration: 5 days. 2027 weeks: June 28 to July 2 and July 5 to July 9. A virtual VetCAMP is also offered.
pay_detail: $800 for the week as a day camper, or $1,050 as an overnight camper ($800 plus $250 for dorm and meals). $30 application fee. Pricing may change.

who_can_apply: Students ages 9 to 19. The eligibility section of the page says 9 to 19, but its header says ages 9 to 14. Check the page to be sure.
how_to_apply: Apply on the workshop website. The address is english.chass.ncsu.edu/youngwriters.
notes: Dates are last year's. Several sessions, check which one fits your age. Page is inconsistent on age range (header says 9 to 14, body says 9 to 19).
duration: 2 weeks, afternoons (day program)

who_can_apply: You must be 16 years old and a 10th or 11th grader in the year you apply. You must live in Nebraska. You must be a US citizen or have proof of work authorization. Commuter only, no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply during the early spring window on the program page. You need teacher recommendations. Spots are very limited.
notes: Research areas include biology and physics. They include chemistry too. The featured project has a lab. It is at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
duration: Up to 8 weeks, early June to early August
pay_detail: $15 per hour for 20 to 40 hours a week, up to 8 weeks. Pay and schedule are set by the faculty mentor.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 (high school students) in Nevada 4-H.
how_to_apply: Email nevada4h@unr.edu with questions. The page does not say how to sign up for Capital Days.
notes: Activities also include a visit to the state museum and the Governor's Mansion. Ask Nevada 4-H for dates and cost.
duration: Trip dates not posted
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Members are ages 9 to 19 as of January 1 of the current year. Younger Cloverbuds are ages 5 to 8.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Extension office to enroll and find a club.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Fee amounts are set by each county and club. Ask your county Extension office.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Costs vary: project books, project supplies, a county activity fee, club dues and event fees.

who_can_apply: High school or homeschool students in good behavior and academic standing with a GPA of 2.5 or higher. Your high school must approve. Talk to your counselor before you sign up.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WNC application if you are new to WNC. Check your email for your NSHE ID and your WNC login. Send the high school authorization form with a student and parent signature. Then sign up for classes in myWNC. Questions: 775-445-3277.
notes: The page mentions a Fallon campus and Fernley offerings. After you pass a class, you must ask WNC to send your transcript to your high school. Allow up to five business days for WNC to process your school's approval.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the dual credit page. WNC lists fees on a separate page.

who_can_apply: Nevada students in 8th, 9th or 10th grade, so you can finish the two year term in high school. You apply for the Senate district where you live or go to school.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the application, which has short essays. Add one letter of recommendation. Send it by email, fax or mail. Questions: info@youthleg.state.nv.us or (775) 684-6740.
notes: Each of the 21 state senators appoints one Youth Legislator. Meetings are often on weekday afternoons and may mean missing class. The brochure is the 2024 edition, so confirm the grade rule and dates with the program.
duration: Two year term, June 1 to May 31. Eleven required meetings and trainings.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The program pays for the one day and two day trainings, including travel, meals and lodging.

who_can_apply: East Brunswick resident teens who want to work with children and be a camp counselor. The page does not give an age range. Needs an application and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application on the page, then interview.
notes: The township lists separate paid seasonal jobs on its Recreation and Parks jobs page. They include Camp Daisy, Crystal Springs and parks staff. The ages for those were not read.
duration: All 6 weeks of camp (June 29 to August 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: Not a paid position: CITs are campers learning to be counselors. 2026 registration fee was $600, with no payment plan.

who_can_apply: You must reach these ages by May 1 of the season. Lifeguards must be at least 15. Lazy river attendants must be at least 14. Guest relations, maintenance and slide tower dispatch must be at least 16. You do not need a lifeguard card to apply. Crystal Springs gives the training.
how_to_apply: Use the apply links on the Crystal Springs summer employment page. Questions: crystalsprings@eastbrunswick.org or 732-390-6797.
notes: Lazy river attendant and guest relations spots were listed as limited or waitlist only. Applying does not guarantee a job.
duration: Summer season (exact dates not stated)
pay_detail: Pay rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: East Brunswick residents in or entering 8th grade and up. Use the teen application, not the adult one.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online teen volunteer application in June or December, wait for the welcome email, join the Remind app, then sign up for shifts. Questions: teens@ebpl.org.
notes: Online application only, no paper forms. The page does not say whether Teen Action Group meetings count as service hours.
duration: Monthly shifts; shifts fill fast
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours count as community service.

who_can_apply: East Brunswick residents in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the Volunteer Matrix site. The page links to it. Email ebyouthcouncil@eastbrunswick.org.
notes: Run with the Township Division of Recreation and Community Services. The page also links to a membership guide for 2025-2026.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Membership dues are $40 per school year.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 18 must come with a guardian, and you must secure an individual volunteer slot for both the adult and child.
how_to_apply: Register for a shift on the volunteer site linked from the page; a minor and the supervising adult each need their own slot. Questions: volunteer@elijahspromise.org or 732-545-9002 ext. 122.
notes: Wear closed-toed shoes and long pants; expect to stand for the whole shift. Only five people fit in the kitchen at once. Large groups are booked through January 2027.
duration: One shift at a time, Monday to Saturday between 8:00 am and 12:30 pm
pay_detail: Unpaid. Court-ordered service hours are not accepted.

who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 17 who live in Franklin Township (Somerset County). You need a Franklin Township library card that is active. Reading Buddies are teens going into grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Action Group form on the teen volunteering page. Register online for each Kindness Club meeting. Questions: use the Reference Desk form or call 732-873-8700, option 3.
notes: Only for Franklin Township residents with an active Franklin Township library card. The page does not give the Kindness Club meeting date or place. Search the teen event calendar.
duration: School year 2026-27 for the Teen Action Group; Kindness Club meetings; summer Reading Buddies
pay_detail: Unpaid. Kindness Club gives 1 volunteer hour per meeting.

who_can_apply: The library says a volunteer is someone 16 or older who helps on a regular basis. If you are under 18, use the teen form. Call the library to ask if younger teens can apply.
how_to_apply: Download and print the teen volunteer application from the volunteering page, fill it out, and bring it to the library at 60 Livingston Ave. There is no online submission. Phone: (732) 745-5108.
notes: The teen form file name says 2018, so ask the library if it is still current. The page does not mention work permits; ask the library.
duration: Regular, ongoing help; hours not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: The Teen Advisory Board is open to Metuchen residents in grades 6 to 12. Summer volunteering is open to all teens in grades 9 to 12. In the school year, volunteering is only for grades 9 to 12. You must have volunteered in a summer or be active on the board.
how_to_apply: Use the volunteer application on the teens page. Then contact the Teen Services Librarian. Her name is on the application.
notes: Board meetings in fall 2026 are listed for Oct 20 and Nov 17 on the page.
duration: Summer volunteering runs July to August. The board meets once a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Teen Advisory Board has a 15 hour service minimum for the year.

who_can_apply: High school age youth in Middlesex County who finished 8th grade for 9th grade entry. Students are picked by grades, a career-tech test, an interview and a counselor's note. Space is limited. County applicants are admitted first.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the district enrollment link. A parent or guardian must say yes. You can also get applications at the schools in all county towns.
notes: This is a school program, not a job. Students from outside the county are admitted only if there is space.
duration: High school years
pay_detail: No tuition for Middlesex County residents. Non-residents pay tuition set by the board.

who_can_apply: Any Middlesex County student who finished 7th grade and is going into 8th grade. You should like the idea of career and tech classes.
how_to_apply: In 2026 the page offered a waiting list form. Watch the Magnet Schools site for the 2027 sign up.
notes: For younger teens only: students must have just finished 7th grade.
duration: 12 days: July 6 to 23 in 2026, Monday to Thursday
pay_detail: Free. Students provide their own transportation.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12 (the library cannot accept volunteers after they turn 18). Math Tutors are grades 9 to 12; Chess Tutors are grades 8 to 12. Teen Advisory Board needs an application.
how_to_apply: Stop by the Youth Services desk to get an application. If you want to try for an Organization Club spot, write to teenvolunteers@oldbridgelibrary.org. There are not many spots.
notes: You can request a letter that confirms your volunteer hours by email.
duration: Varies by role (Math Tutors are Saturdays 11 am to 1 pm during the school year; Tech Helpers work Mondays and Saturdays, year-round)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer credit hours.

who_can_apply: Shelvers must be going into 9th grade or older. Teen Advisory Board needs an application.
how_to_apply: Apply with the Teen Advisory Board form on the page. For volunteering, email the Teen Volunteer Coordinator and join the volunteer mailing list. Shelvers interview and train first.
notes: Selection is not first come first served.
duration: Shelvers get one 1 hour shift a week. The Teen Advisory Board meets about twice a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours can be confirmed.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be ages 14 and older. Teens who are younger than that cannot join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Registration Form linked on the page.
notes: The township public safety page lists separate police volunteer options. The ages for those were not read.
duration: As needed; events are in early May, October and December
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: College-bound youth from urban communities in Atlantic, Camden, Essex, Hudson, Mercer, Middlesex, Passaic and Union counties, with a B or better GPA, top 25% of the class, and interest in volunteering to help 4-H with STEM programs.
how_to_apply: Online application on the program site (opens early in the year). About 60 students are accepted each year. Contact on the Rutgers 4-H STEM site: Chad Ripberger, ripberger@njaes.rutgers.edu.
notes: Only students in the listed counties qualify. Selected students start with an orientation in May and two short online modules.
duration: Year-round, multi-year; 2026 summer program at Rutgers-New Brunswick was July 6 to 10
pay_detail: Free: direct summer program expenses are paid by a scholarship valued at $1,000. No wage or stipend is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade in the fall. Only 45 students were accepted in 2026. Applicants write a five paragraph personal response.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and write the five paragraph answer. Questions: BOLD@cinj.rutgers.edu.
notes: Two groups run it. They are the LIFE Center at Rutgers Cancer Institute and the Center for School and Community-Based Research and Education. A reunion camp is open to past campers.
duration: 1 week, 9:30 am to 4:00 pm (July 20 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: No application fee. Accepted students paid a non-refundable $500 enrollment fee in 2026 (due June 1, 2026).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Sessions are by grade level in spring 2026: 9th graders July 20 to 24, 10th graders July 27 to 31, 11th graders July 13 to 17 (2026 dates). Open to all students of any gender.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps in the text read. Check the TARGET page and the School of Engineering contact page.
notes: Program director is named on the page. Programs for grades 6 to 8 run in June and July too.
duration: 1 week, 9 am to 5 pm
pay_detail: $500 for the one-week program. Need-based sponsorship is available after acceptance. Families provide transportation.

who_can_apply: High school students finishing sophomore or junior year, ages 16 to 18. The page states this age rule for Summer 2026, so check the 2027 rules. U.S. and international students.
how_to_apply: Online application on the Pre-College Summer site. Join the email list for 2027 updates.
notes: Costs money. Check the Costs page for the current year before planning. The page did not list financial aid; ask the program. Per the Costs page for 2026: credit academies are Physical Therapy $3,784 in-state and $4,804 out-of-state, and Building Leadership Strategies $3,887.50 in-state and $5,068 out-of-state. The $500 deposit is non-refundable. No 2027 cost is posted.
duration: One week, residential
pay_detail: 2026 cost was $2,899 for most academies ($3,887.50 to $5,068 for the two credit academies), with a $500 non-refundable deposit. Includes dorm for the week.

who_can_apply: Strong high school students, from 8th graders going into 9th through 12th graders about to graduate. You need a transcript. You also need letters from your math, science or engineering teachers.
how_to_apply: Apply online with your transcript and letters from your teachers. Applications that are not complete are not reviewed.
notes: Selective program. Email the coordinator listed on the page if you need help getting a laptop.
duration: 2 weeks, 9 am to 4:30 pm (July 6 to 17 in 2026). Non-residential.
pay_detail: $875 for the two-week session.

who_can_apply: Current high school students ages 16 to 18 (must be 16 by the course start date) with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Graduating seniors are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus unweighted transcript, a Parent/Guardian Permission Form and a letter of recommendation (teacher or anyone who knows your work). Reviewed first come, first served; decisions in 5 to 7 business days.
notes: Some courses need extra technology or prerequisite courses. Withdrawing after the add/drop period puts a W on a Rutgers transcript. Questions: summerscholars@rutgers.edu.
duration: Summer Session I (started May 26, 2026) or Session II (started July 6, 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 rates per credit: in-state $482 (Arts and Sciences) to $551 (SEBS), out-of-state $1,148 to $1,338, plus a one-time $162 student fee. Courses are typically 3 credits; up to two courses.

who_can_apply: Motivated high school students entering grades 10 to 12 who have completed at least one high school biology course.
how_to_apply: Online application only: about 250-word essay on your interest, high school transcripts or report cards, and your preferred session. Acceptance emails go out in the first week of April; pay within 2 weeks to hold the spot.
notes: Held at EOHSI, 170 Frelinghuysen Road, Piscataway. Questions: THED@eohsi.rutgers.edu. Expect the 2027 cycle to follow the same winter pattern, but confirm on the page.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31)
pay_detail: $975 non-refundable camp fee covers tuition, manuals, materials, safety equipment, lab supplies and lunch. Need-based financial aid may be available. No housing or transportation provided; no stipend.

who_can_apply: Students who finished 8th grade and are in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. You must live in and go to school in New Brunswick, Perth Amboy or Plainfield. You must be first in your family to go to college, or low income. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You need at least a C average and need academic support. You must send an application and a personal statement, and do an interview.
how_to_apply: Email upwardbound@echo.rutgers.edu or call (848) 445-3090 to ask how to apply. The page says you fill out an application and a personal statement, and you have an interview. It shows no link to apply. Virtual open houses are held in fall in English and Spanish.
notes: Students must be willing to get to campus every day of the summer (parent ride or bus program). A separate Pre-College Outreach program is described on the same page. Checked 2026-10-10: the page names the 2027 application but shows no link to it, so apply_url stays empty.
duration: Year-round, with a six-week Summer Institute
pay_detail: Free program. The program page does not say if students get paid.

who_can_apply: Mathematically talented high school students. No specific grade or age is listed. You must submit solutions to the Problems to Explore.
how_to_apply: Four parts: Student Information and Consent Google Form (with a parent), your solutions to the Problems to Explore, a teacher recommendation emailed directly, and a transcript emailed by your counselor.
notes: Residential; students go home on weekends. The page was the Summer 2026 listing.
duration: Four weeks (2026: July 6 to 31), residential, home on weekends
pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who have completed ninth grade. Weekday shifts are 4 to 6 p.m. for ages 15 and up, or 6 to 8 p.m. for ages 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Director (Jacob.Persily@rwjbh.org) with the teen's name, high school and current grade. Applications are not sent at a parent's request. Then comes orientation. Next is medical clearance. That is a health form from a doctor covering TB screening, immunizations and flu vaccine. Then a drug screen. Phone: 732-937-8507.
notes: Volunteers must be fully vaccinated and wear the provided uniform. The page says internships and shadowing are not offered. A newer and an older version of this page disagreed on hours (75 vs 100 a year); the page on 2026-10-09 says 100.
duration: Minimum 100 hours of service per year; the hospital hopes for 2 to 3 hours a week. Shifts mornings, afternoons and evenings, 7 days a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The required urine drug screen is free to the volunteer; no other costs are listed.

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed a high school level biology course. No age or grade range is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the WISE page; first come, first served. Pay the fee within 2 weeks of approval.
notes: In-person sessions are non-residential at the Waksman Institute on the Busch campus in Piscataway. The year-long Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP) is a separate, school-based program that starts with teachers.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday (2026 sessions: June 22 to July 2, July 27 to August 7; vWISE August 10 to 21)
pay_detail: $2,200 for the in-person WISE (non-refundable, due 2 weeks after approval). A virtual vWISE costs $600.

who_can_apply: Library patrons in grades 7 to 12. Book reviews are for grades 8 to 12 who live in Woodbridge. Details differ by branch.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch library. You can also write to the Teen Services team at teenservices@woodbridgelibrary.org. You can just drop in to a Community Service Club meeting.
notes: The Fords Branch Library will help you get volunteer hours for National Honor Society applications. It does this when other ways do not work.
