duration: Most roles are all year, about 1 hour a week. Summer Reading Club volunteering is June to August, up to 5 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours and signatures.

who_can_apply: 15 high school students. High school principals suggest them, one member and one backup per school. The Mayor then names them for one year starting in August. Members can apply again until they graduate.
how_to_apply: Ask your high school principal to recommend you. The Mayor then appoints members for a one-year term starting in August.
notes: Very small: about 15 seats. The page lives on a township website that uses the woodbridgelibrary.org address.
duration: One year term, August 1 to July 31
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a civic board.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades K to 13. The Rutgers 4-H homepage says it serves everyone in grades K through 13.
how_to_apply: Use the Join 4-H form on the New Jersey 4-H site, or find your county 4-H office on the Rutgers 4-H page.
notes: Not a job. It is a youth group. The Rutgers homepage has a Join 4-H form and a link to the New Jersey 4-H Camp. The pages did not give fees, so ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Ongoing clubs and programs; camp is a week in summer
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your county 4-H office.

who_can_apply: Juniors who live or go to school in New Jersey and are legal U.S. residents. You must be fluent in English and able to attend the whole session. You must be willing to take part in nondenominational prayer, patriotic ceremonies, the Pledge and the National Anthem. An Auxiliary unit must sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact a local American Legion Auxiliary unit or a county chairperson to ask for sponsorship. The site lists contacts. You cannot apply without a sponsor.
notes: Girls only. Start asking local Auxiliary units in the winter. The 2026 site says sponsorships were already filled. A matching program for boys (Jersey Boys State) is run by the American Legion.
duration: About 5 days (2026: Sunday June 21 to Thursday June 25)
pay_detail: No pay. Sponsors (units, posts or other groups) enroll and sponsor delegates; the site does not list a fee to the student.

who_can_apply: High school juniors with at least one semester left. Posts pick students with school help, or you can apply on your own as self-sponsored.
how_to_apply: If a post sponsors you, your school staff recommend you. The local American Legion post interviews you. If you sponsor yourself, make an account on the ALJBS CampSite portal. Fill out the questionnaire. Add a 300 to 500 word essay, or a video or a counselor reference. Pay the $50 fee.
notes: Boys only (Jersey Girls State is a separate program). Post-sponsored and self-sponsored costs are in pay_detail.
duration: One week; delegates arrive on Father's Day (the 80th session began June 21, 2026)
pay_detail: Post-sponsored: parents pay a $50 non-refundable fee and the post pays the rest. Self-sponsored: $50 non-refundable application fee plus $325 tuition if accepted (food, housing and supplies included). Scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 or older. You must give immunization records or get screened (MMR, chickenpox, TB blood test, hepatitis B, and a flu shot Dec 1 to Apr 30) and attend orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application only, then orientation and on-site training. Questions: Volunteer Services, 609-303-4023, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday.
notes: Does not offer internships or shadowing. Year-round track runs Sept 14, 2026 to June 30, 2027 when open. Check the page for when applications reopen.
duration: Summer: 7 weeks, at least 56 hours. Also 12 week seasonal and Sept to June year-round tracks.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: New Jersey residents who have finished their junior year at a public, private or home school. Applicants must be nominated by their high school (one nominee per 325 juniors). It is competitive. Fewer than 25% of nominees get offers.
how_to_apply: Get nominated by your high school, then submit the online application with essays (admission is based heavily on essays). Contact: njgset@soe.rutgers.edu or 848-445-4753.
notes: Residential at Rutgers School of Engineering, 98 Brett Road, Piscataway. The Application Instructions page on the program site still mentions the Summer 2023 application, so rely on the state page and director for 2027 dates.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors with at least a 3.2 GPA and 95 percent attendance. Students in the MCTS Academy or Shared-Time programs cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Create an account in the MCTS online application portal and apply. Your counselor then uploads transcripts and attendance. Email admissions@mcts.edu with questions.
notes: You become a regular college student with a MyMercer account. Most classes are on the West Windsor campus. Mercer County residency is not spelled out on the page, so ask admissions. The Aviation section says that by continuing this program, costs could range from $24,000 to $36,000. The page does not say what that covers.
duration: Senior year, follows the college calendar
pay_detail: Free. No tuition for the college classes.

who_can_apply: 10th graders. The page gives no acceptance criteria for shared-time programs and refers to a separate admissions procedures page. The page says no RSVP is required for the information sessions. Your home district provides transportation.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the online application portal and fill in the form. Your school counselor then sends your grades and attendance. Email admissions@mcts.edu with questions.
notes: Students in a shared-time program cannot also do Career Prep. Ask your counselor for the deadline. Programs are at the Assunpink Center (Trenton) and the Sypek Center (Pennington).
duration: 2 years (grades 11 and 12), half day
pay_detail: Part of your regular school day. No cost stated.

who_can_apply: Students applying for the 2027-28 school year. Some programs (biomedical, finance, HVACR, global business) are shared-time only.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the admissions page. An admissions test may be required (see the CTE Admissions Testing page). Call Pupil Services at 908-526-8900 ext. 7250 or 7243.
notes: The health sciences academy has its own admission page and phone, 908-526-8900 ext. 7148. Enrolled students can join a paid co-op job. Outside teens cannot.
duration: 2027-28 school year start
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students. Ages and grades are not listed on the page. Scholarships are first come, first served, with priority to Greater Trenton Area students who attend all four weeks.
how_to_apply: Register through CampDoc and pay a 50 percent deposit. For a scholarship, fill out the separate online Financial Aid form for each child.
notes: The scholarship wording on the page still says 2025, so confirm it. Bus rides from several Trenton stops are mentioned. Contact 609-737-3735.
duration: 1 to 4 weeks, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: $525 to $575 per week in 2026. Limited full scholarships based on financial need.

who_can_apply: Ages differ by role: 14 for Critter Care (and stream sampling with an adult), 15 for Sunday Stewardship on your own, 16 for the Welcome Desk and Butterfly House Crew.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application through the Apply Here link on the page. You get a link to log your hours after you apply. Questions: 609-737-3735.
notes: Some roles need your own ride. The page says one stream monitoring role is not a good fit for 12th graders.
duration: Varies: Sundays March to November, Tuesday mornings mid June to August, one year for animal care

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 25 who do not have a high school diploma.
how_to_apply: Send the online services request form on the NJ Department of Labor page for general questions. The state page does not list sign-up steps, so ask for the site that serves your county.
notes: For teens 16 and up who left school without a diploma. Not for students still working toward a diploma in a regular school. It includes help getting a high school equivalency diploma or an adult high school diploma. It includes counseling and help moving on to college or jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Full time, year-round program; length of each cohort is not stated on the state page
pay_detail: Corpsmembers get a stipend while enrolled. The amount is not stated on the state page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 12. The page does not list an age rule or a residency rule; it describes students from New Jersey.
how_to_apply: Research a global issue and write a paper with a teacher or mentor, following the guidelines PDF on the page. Register and submit the paper through the World Food Prize website.
notes: The Rutgers page was read through a summarizing fetch tool because the site blocks plain page requests, so check the page itself for the 2027 date. It is listed on the New Jersey 4-H page as a program for high school students.
duration: One day (2026 date: March 6, 2026)
pay_detail: Free to take part (no registration cost). For students invited to the Global Youth Institute in Des Moines, most expenses are covered by the World Food Prize, but travel is not included.

who_can_apply: Any New Mexico youth ages 5 to 18 can join. You do not need a farm or any skills. Cloverbuds are ages 5 to 8. Novice is 9 to 11. Junior is 12 to 13. Senior is 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office and talk with your 4-H agent. Then create a family account and enroll at 4h.zsuite.org. Returning members re-enroll each year, update projects and submit the required forms.
notes: State office phone on the page is 575-646-3026. Call it if you are not sure which county you are in.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: New Mexico 4-H generally has no statewide membership fee. Some counties, clubs or projects have costs for supplies, livestock, workshops or camps. Ask your County Extension Office.

who_can_apply: Students in New Mexico ag education programs. The association says it serves over 5,300 members in over 85 schools. No age or grade rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The site lists FFA chapter lists, a 2026-2027 plan for events, scholarships and Jr. High contests.
notes: Some pages on this site carry a 2022 copyright, so camp fees and dates may be out of date. Confirm with your ag teacher or the state office. The homepage does not show the $225 camp fee, so confirm it before relying on it.
duration: School year. Leadership Camp is a separate event.
pay_detail: Leadership Camp fee was $225 per camper on a page that looks older (copyright 2022). Camp scholarships were offered.

who_can_apply: Young people from forest-dependent communities in New Mexico. The summer program is for high school age youth. The Guild says its work covers ages 16 to 25.
how_to_apply: Watch the Guild's FSYC page for position descriptions and application forms. Crew member information is posted on the project page later in the year.
notes: The New Mexico Youth Conservation Corps Commission and the Cibola and Santa Fe National Forests pay for part of it. Past crew members who log 640 hours may get a federal hiring status. Pay and crew sites could not be read on the pages checked.
duration: Early June to early August (2026)
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly rate is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 30, per the 2027 job list. No earlier experience is needed for crew member jobs.
how_to_apply: Open the apply page and find the 2027 Conservation Crew Corpsmember job in Albuquerque or Taos. Then use its Apply Now link.
notes: The work is outdoors. The program page says ages 17 to 25, and the job list says 17 to 30. Ask RMYC if you are close to the top age. Some crews camp for 8 days in a row, then have 6 days off. Corpsmembers who complete a full AmeriCorps season become eligible for a scholarship award. The FAQ lists UNM College Credit as a member benefit.
duration: Seasonal, full time (40 or more hours a week). The end date is not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: $700 per week for the 2027 Corpsmember job. Paid by stipend.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 16 to 24. You live in Bernalillo, Sandoval, Valencia or Torrance County. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Call 505-818-1428 (WIOA Youth inquiries) or 505-977-3216, or use the contact form on the program page.
notes: Ask YDI if you qualify.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the program. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 14 to 24. You live in Cibola, Colfax, Los Alamos, McKinley, Mora, Rio Arriba, San Juan, San Miguel, Santa Fe or Taos County. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Contact YDI through the form on the program page or call 505-977-3216 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
notes: WIOA programs have federal rules on who qualifies. Ask YDI if you qualify.
duration: Year-round support. Paid work experience typically runs 250 to 350 hours.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: New Mexico youth ages 14 to 25. Local governments, tribes and nonprofits apply for state funding and then hire the corps members.
how_to_apply: Find a funded project near you on the YCC projects map. Then contact that sponsor about jobs. A sponsor can be a city, county, tribe or nonprofit.
notes: Teens do not apply to the state. The state funds sponsors, who do the hiring. Pay, dates and application steps vary by sponsor. The projects map on this page shows 2021 to 2023 projects, and older ones are on a separate Projects page.
duration: Set by each sponsor
pay_detail: Pay not stated on this page. Returning corps members can earn a $500 cash benefit or a $1,500 education voucher.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who go to a high school in the NRCC service region. You must meet college placement rules. You need a note of support from a high school official and a signed form from a parent. Strong freshmen and sophomores may be able to join. They need the OK of the high school principal and the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor and use the dual enrollment forms on the NRCC page. The parent signature form is required.
notes: The NRCC page still showed an old campus closure banner, so confirm the details with the college. Cost to students is not stated on the page.
duration: Semester by semester
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth from kindergarten up to age 19. A kindergartner must turn 5 by January 1 of the 4-H year. A teen cannot enroll or re-enroll if they will turn 19 before January 1 of the new club year (club year runs Oct 1 to Sept 30). Counties can set their own details.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Cornell Cooperative Extension office. Join a club. If you cannot join a club, you can enroll as an independent member. You work on projects at your own pace with an adult helping.
notes: Not a job. The rules are for New York State 4-H as described by two county Cornell Cooperative Extension pages (Jefferson and Erie). The listed URL is the Erie County page. Your own county office has the sign-up steps and costs.
duration: 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30; you can re-enroll each year
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the program pages. Ask your county office.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: Youth 14 to 17 can go to the weeks set aside for that age. Campers must be the minimum age by December 1 of the calendar year. The pages do not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Set up a family account in the DEC online registration system. Fill out the camper forms and waivers in the Document Center before registration opens. Then register for a week and pay online. If a week is full, join the waitlist.
notes: This is a camp for campers, not a job. The main camp page still mentions a March 2025 opening, so use the How to Register page for dates. Ask DEC about sponsorships early.
duration: One week, Sunday afternoon to Friday afternoon (2026 teen weeks ran July 12 to Aug 7, depending on the camp)
pay_detail: $350 per camper per week, with meals and trips included. Transportation to and from camp is not included. Many campers are sponsored by local conservation groups, clubs and community groups.

who_can_apply: Girls. Your local American Legion Auxiliary unit picks citizens and alternates, sometimes with interviews, essays or a nomination. The pages did not list a grade or residency rule, so ask your unit.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Auxiliary unit. Ask your guidance counselor or email egsregistrar@gmail.com with your hometown, county and school. Join the local selection. Then use the login the unit gives you. Register online and pay the fee.
notes: Girls only. The site says there is a virtual orientation on Zoom in May or June. The program says it is not a sports camp or a recreational camp.
duration: One week: Sunday June 27 to Friday July 2, 2027
pay_detail: A non-refundable application fee is required. The amount is not stated on the program pages. Optional extras (shirts, survival kit) have order forms.

who_can_apply: Strong swimmers who meet the age and certification rules. Outside Long Island, the minimum age is 15 for pool posts and 16 for other posts. On Long Island the minimum is 17 (16 for pool posts only). You also need a background check, a medical form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the lifeguard job application and email it to the address on the page. Then sign up for a qualifier. Long Island has its own preregistration. After you pass, regional staff tell you the next steps.
notes: The minimum age depends on region (see who_can_apply). Confirm your age with the regional office. The New York Department of Labor page returned an access error. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Seasonal; the page says the peak operating season is May through September
pay_detail: Paid job. Candidates are in pay status during the mandatory 40 hours of training. The hourly rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Newark-area high school students. The page does not list grade, residency or GPA rules.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain the steps. Email explorersprogram@newarkmuseumart.org or call 973-596-5143.
notes: This is a long commitment. Ask about the 2027 application dates.
duration: 3 to 4 years: 6 after-school hours a week, 60 service hours a year, 25 hours a week in summer
pay_detail: Students are paid. The amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. No other rules listed.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the program page. For aid, use the financial aid form or contact April Jeffries at ajeffries@njpac.org.
notes: The page lists month and day but not the year, so confirm the dates before registering. Tuition is $500 for the year, with a payment plan option and aid available. Not a paid job.
duration: Fall semester Oct 3 to Dec 12 and spring semester Jan 30 to May 15, 1 to 5 pm, at 31 Mulberry Street, Newark. The page does not show the year.
pay_detail: $500 for the full year. NJPAC says no student is turned away for financial need; use the financial aid form.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21. You must live in or go to school in Orange County and have finished 9th grade. You should want to learn about fire and emergency careers.
how_to_apply: Email the fire department using the contact link on the program page. Ask for the program application. Ride-along forms for minors are posted on the page.
notes: This program used to be Explorer Post 309. You learn what school you need for fire careers. You also get tips on how to get ready.
duration: Weekly program
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.
how_to_apply: Teens fill out the online application themselves on the library's volunteer portal (application form number 2) and lead communication with staff. You must attend volunteer training before starting.
notes: Volunteers age 15 and up must complete fingerprinting and a background check. Applying does not guarantee a spot. Questions go to the library's Teen Services team through the email link on the page.
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: You must be 16 years old on or before March 30, 2027. No lifeguard experience is needed. You must pass a 1000-meter ocean swim and a 1000-meter run-swim-run tryout.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the Lifeguard Trainee job. If you qualify, you are invited to a tryout. Top finishers get an interview. You must also pass the Basic Lifeguard Academy.
notes: Practice workout schedule is on the program page. Dates can change with weather. The tryout has no wetsuits or fins. The info night is at Lifeguard Headquarters, 70 Newport Pier, in person or on Zoom, and is not required. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work.
duration: Training academy, then seasonal work
pay_detail: Paid training is $16.90 an hour. Lifeguard I pay is $25.50 to $31.02 an hour.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.

who_can_apply: Newport News residents ages 16 to 17 and young adults ages 18 to 24. Under 18 needs a signed parent or guardian consent form.
how_to_apply: Use the Youth - Apply for the Youth Career Program link on the city page. Finish the application steps.
notes: Not open to 14 and 15 year olds. The city page does not state the wage.
duration: About 25 hours a week, June to August (from the employer page)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 by the program start date. You must be entering grades 9 to 12 (or home school at that level).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application. Go to an info session (online or in person). Chosen volunteers go to 3 days of training in person.
notes: The page does not state a set application window. Summer volunteers can also earn hours through trips and career activities. Contact: volunteer@aquarium.org.
duration: School-year program: 20 hours of training and 48 hours of volunteering in 4-hour shifts (68 total). Summer first-year program: 66 hours total.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fees. Perks include a free aquarium membership after 50 hours and guest passes.

who_can_apply: The Impact League is for ages 13 to 24. Younger kids (5 to 12) enter the Imagination League. Single entries and teams are both allowed.
how_to_apply: Go to innovation.nfte.com and submit your entry before the deadline. The announcement page does not give step-by-step rules, so read the full rules on that site.
notes: Online, so it works from any city. The Impact League age range runs past 18, so you compete with college-age entrants too (page does not say whether groups are judged separately). NFTE also holds a Youth Entrepreneurship Showcase in New York City on Nov 18 to 19, 2026; the page did not say who can attend.
duration: Entries due Dec 13, 2026. Winners announced in spring 2027.
pay_detail: Free to enter. Cash prizes of $300 to $1,500 for winning entries.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Join the email list on the page to hear when applications open.
notes: The first group of Fellows began in fall 2023.
duration: A yearly group (the 2026 to 2027 group is already chosen)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 who can attend all required group meetings.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the next application opens. Email Erin Shupe or call 801-581-3774 with questions. Subscribe to quarterly updates on the page.
notes: Meetings are Wednesdays 6 to 8 PM, plus some Saturdays. Later you work 2 gallery shifts of 2.5 hours a month.
duration: School year group: October 7, 2026 to April 14, 2027, about 90 hours. A summer group runs June to August.
pay_detail: Hourly wage starting at $13.00. You can choose to volunteer instead. Staff can ride UTA transit free during the internship.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or green card holders who will be 18 by September 30, 2027. You must be a senior now who will finish high school before it starts, or a college student. If you are 17 on June 1, 2027, you must live within 40 miles of an NIH campus.
how_to_apply: Apply in the NIH Application Center. Send your grades, a resume, a short essay about your goals, and two references. Then email NIH scientists whose work you like and point them to your application. Each scientist picks their own interns by April 1.
notes: Very competitive, and mostly for college students. Only seniors who meet the age rule can apply; juniors cannot. Free online application webinars on Oct 20 and Nov 17, 2026. Questions: SIP@nih.gov.
duration: Full time, between May 10 and August 31, 2027. Exact dates are set with your mentor. No vacations during the internship.
pay_detail: Stipend, set each year by education level. The page does not state the amount. Free parking. You need proof of health insurance, and NIH does not provide housing.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old. The page does not list a minimum age for the part-time and camp jobs, so check the posting.
how_to_apply: For jobs, apply on NISRA's ADP Workforce Now site from the Employment page. For volunteering, use the Volunteer Opportunities link on the same page. Call NISRA at 815-459-0737.
notes: The City of Elgin is a member of NISRA. The city says NISRA offers programs at Elgin sites. The 15 week internship is for therapeutic recreation college students. Jobs need a reliable ride. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit.
duration: Program seasons are 6 to 8 weeks. Volunteers are asked to commit for the full season.
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Part-time jobs (1 to 20 hours a week) are paid, but pay is not on the program page.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens who are a high school junior or senior at the time of application, with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must be able to do the full seven weeks and live within 50 miles of the host campus. Families must provide their own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Watch for the SHIP job announcement on USAJOBS and follow the application page linked from the SHIP page. The page says to read the application process page for the full steps.
notes: The page lists two NIST campuses (Boulder, CO and Gaithersburg, MD); this card is for Gaithersburg. The 2026 poster session was held in Gaithersburg on Aug 6, 2026. The exact application dates for 2027 were not final on the page, so check it again in late October.
duration: Seven weeks, mid-June to early August (2027 dates to be decided)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a competitive volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 13 to 17. This includes teens going into 9th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the Conservation Youth Team page. Info sessions were held in February and March. Teens who are picked have an interview.
notes: Dates are from the 2026 cycle. Applications open December 1, and the year is not stated. The page lists interest sessions in February and March.
duration: About 150 hours in summer plus fall or spring sessions for first-year members
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $100 registration fee for shirts, name tag and materials. A scholarship covers this fee for a few first-year applicants.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 22. The program page does not say if you must be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Get the form from Ambassador Resources on the NDSU 4-H leadership page. Send it to the ND 4-H Center for Youth Development.
notes: Selection is the Saturday before Thanksgiving at 4-H Camp in Washburn. Questions: ndsu.4hambassadors@ndsu.edu.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth who have finished seventh grade. You do not need to be in 4-H.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the NDSU event page.
notes: Ask North Dakota 4-H about financial help. The page does not mention scholarships.
duration: 4 days. The 2026 conference was June 22 to 25 at NDSU in Fargo.
pay_detail: Teens pay. Early-bird price was $365 per person (Thanksgiving through December), then the price rises $10 a month. Payment is due June 1.

who_can_apply: Grades 7 to 12. The program page does not say whether you must be in 4-H.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the NDSU event page.
notes: Cost is not listed yet. Call North Dakota 4-H or your county Extension office to ask.
duration: Weekend, Feb 14 to 15, 2027. If weather cancels it, make-up dates are April 4 to 5, 2027.
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders who live in North Dakota. You can attend a public or non-public school. You need a cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher. Selection uses a personal essay of 250 words or less. It also uses two recommendations (one teacher, one counselor or administrator) and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the NDSU Governor's School site (2026 cycle). You need a personal essay of 250 words or less. You also need one teacher recommendation. You need one counselor or administrator recommendation too. Questions? Email ndsu.otl@ndsu.edu.
notes: The NDSU page says the program runs every other summer. The next session's host, dates and portal are not posted on the program pages. Ask NDSU at ndsu.otl@ndsu.edu.
duration: Four weeks. 2026 dates were June 8 to July 2.
pay_detail: The NDSU pages do not list a cost. A UND article says a North Dakota Department of Public Instruction grant covered tuition and on-campus housing for the 2025 session. Check that this still holds.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 8 to 12. Volunteers who work with the public must pass a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Fill in the teen volunteer form on the library page when it opens.
notes: Questions: 604-998-3450. The Dec 17 date comes from the Teens' community hub page. Exact roles are not listed on the page.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13. First Aid is 15. National Lifeguard is 15. Swim Instructor is 15. Lifesaving Instructor is 16. To apply for a job, you must be a citizen, a permanent resident or have a valid work permit.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses online. After you are certified, apply on the NVRC job site. Email swim@nvrc.ca with questions.
notes: Courses need 100% attendance. Withdraw 8 or more days before the start for a full refund. The minimum age to be hired is not stated on the pages.
duration: Several courses
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the program pages. Job pay not stated.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Some roles need an older age or certificates (for example Aquatics needs age 15, Bronze Cross and Swim Instructor). Fitness volunteers must be 17 or over. Under 18 needs a parent signature.
how_to_apply: There are eight steps. Fill out the online form. Give two references. Sign the volunteer agreement. Get a police check at the RCMP where you live. Sign the photo release. Upload your forms. Go to orientation. Then email volunteer@nvrc.ca.
notes: Contact volunteer@nvrc.ca or 604-983-6345. The police check must be done where you live.
duration: Varies. Early years roles ask for 4 to 6 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Domestic students in North Vancouver School District, mainly grade 12. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school Career Program teacher. If you missed the deadline, email jkinakin@sd44.ca.
notes: The page lists 16 programs.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Tuition covered by the school board

who_can_apply: The page says its volunteers are over 16 years old. You need to be grown up, on time and good at talking with people.
how_to_apply: Fill in the North Shore form online. It takes 4 to 8 weeks. VCH runs a record check. Then you have an interview, reference checks and training.
notes: North Shore Volunteer Resources: (604) 984-5929, nsvolunteer@vch.ca. VCH's Vancouver program (VGH, UBC Hospital, G.F. Strong) does not state a minimum age on its pages, so ask vanvolunteer@vch.ca before applying there.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week for at least 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can get reference letters and recognition.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. CTD uses levels based on test scores. Or it uses a school record and teacher recommendation. Check the course page and the CTD eligibility page.
how_to_apply: Apply online through MyCTD. For admission, you use test scores or a portfolio. The portfolio is your report card and a teacher recommendation. If you have questions, email ctd-admissions@northwestern.edu.
notes: Costs a lot and is for advanced learners. CTD also has many other summer and weekend courses for grades 6 to 12 that are not listed here.
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 tuition: $5,530 residential camp or $3,125 day camp. Financial aid for qualified students is given on a rolling basis while funds last.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 years old. For Northwestern Memorial Hospital the age is 18, and it has no summer program. You must pass a health screening and an interview. You must also go to a virtual orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during the window. Then do an interview. Onboarding includes a health screening and an orientation. Ages 18 and up also get a background check.
notes: Volunteer offices: Delnor, 630-938-2180. Central DuPage, 630-933-6207. Lake Forest, 847-535-6851. Call the one near you.
duration: One day a week for 8 weeks between May and August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who will be seniors in fall 2027. The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form, write a 200 to 225 word essay, list your journalism activities and send up to three work samples. Pay the $55 fee. Your counselor emails your transcript, GPA and school profile to Prof. Roger Boye. Add the financial aid form and a parent tax return if you want aid.
notes: Questions: r-boye@northwestern.edu (email is best) or (847) 491-2069.
duration: 4 weeks (June 27 to July 23, 2027)
pay_detail: Tuition $5,000 including room and board. Up to $100,000 in financial aid and scholarships is available. $55 application fee.

who_can_apply: Students rising into grades 9 to 12 the summer they attend. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and experience or interest in policy debate.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials such as a debate record, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. You need a laptop with a webcam, a mic and Microsoft Word.
notes: The 2026 program was online only. Check whether 2027 is online or on campus. Financial aid and scholarship page exists on the NHSI site but was not read.
duration: 4 or 6 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: $3,500 for the 4 week institute, $5,000 for the 6 week institute. $60 application fee.

who_can_apply: Students in their sophomore or junior year who will be rising juniors or seniors. The page asks for a class rank in or near the top 30 percent. It also asks for proof of special skill or strong interest in media arts.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials. These may include two essays, a resume, a letter of recommendation, test scores and your transcript.
notes: Competitive and costly. Travel is not included. Aid is need-based only. Not a paid program.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th or 11th grade who will be rising juniors or seniors. Juniors get priority. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and some theatre experience or strong interest.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send a resume, two essays, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. Test scores are optional. The Musical Theatre track needs a third essay.
notes: Competitive and costs a lot, but the program says need-based aid is given and does not offer merit aid. Travel is not included. Not a paid program.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.

who_can_apply: Attendants must be at least 14, lifeguards at least 15, cooks at least 16.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Now' link under the position on the Waterpark Employment page (current listings: lifeguard at Atlantis and Pirate's Cove, water safety instructor at Great Waves and Ocean Dunes).
notes: Atlantis is at Bull Run and Pirate's Cove at Pohick Bay (Fairfax County); Great Waves is in Alexandria and Ocean Dunes is at Upton Hill in Arlington. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or in Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale. High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income. They also need one of these: justice involvement, being unhoused or a runaway, or foster care (in it now or aged out).
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. In-school applicants need income under the program limits plus a barrier; the page's out-of-school barrier list is broader.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week

who_can_apply: Any high school student in grades 9 to 12. No experience is needed. No grades, essays or recommendation letters are needed. A parent consent form is needed.
how_to_apply: Register on the ACE GNY website. Use the yellow button on the students page. Get a parent to sign a consent form. Pick a team from the map you get by email. Then wait for a confirmation email.
notes: Teams meet at host firms or universities. The page also links to a Summer Internship Program for alumni, which this card does not cover.
duration: Late October through May (about 2 hours after school per meeting). Some teams start in January.
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned. Scholarship and internship chances are listed as benefits.

who_can_apply: You must live and go to school in New York City and be in 10th or 11th grade. You must have passed your classes for the last three or more terms. You also must have taken an AMNH course, or go to one of the partner schools or groups on the list. You do not need to be a U.S. citizen.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and answer short questions. They ask why you like science, how you work on a team, and how you will make time. No report card or letters are needed. Some people get an interview.
notes: The FAQ says you do not need working papers. SRMP is meant to be your main after-school activity for the year. Join the program's email list on the Join SRMP page to hear when the application opens. Questions: srmp@amnh.org.
duration: One year, August to June: a 4-week Summer Institute in August, then about 4 hours a week after school (Tuesdays and Thursdays) plus 1 or 2 Fridays a month.
pay_detail: $2,500 stipend when you finish the research and program requirements. You can also earn 1 CUNY Lehman College credit at no cost.

who_can_apply: High school seniors (12th grade) who live in one of the five boroughs. You must send a current transcript or report card that shows 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the Apollo page. It includes an essay, a transcript or report card, and recommendations. All are due by the deadline. Late or incomplete applications are not read.
notes: The FAQ says accepted interns under 18 must give the Apollo a copy of their New York State working papers before orientation. Ask your school guidance counselor how to get working papers. The Apollo also runs a paid technical theater internship in the summer. The page text about length is not the same in two places. Confirm with the Apollo.
duration: The 2026 internship ran Apr 21 to May 21, 2026, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 3 to 6 PM. The page calls it six weeks in one place and eight or ten weeks in others.
pay_detail: $17.00 per hour

who_can_apply: Rising seniors going into 12th grade in September who live in the five boroughs of New York City. You like technical theater. You must come to the full program and a parent or guardian orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on Formstack before the deadline. The page says group interviews happen by appointment. Accepted teens and a parent or guardian go to an orientation on the first day.
notes: The Apollo Arts Administration internship page says interns under 18 must show New York State working papers. This technical internship page does not say so. Expect to need them for a paid job.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday, on site. The 2026 program ran July 13 to Aug 21, 2026.
pay_detail: $17 per hour

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who start in Tier 1 (9th grade), Tier 2 (10th grade or Tier 1 done) or Tier 3 (11th grade or Tier 2 done). No age or borough rule is stated. The page says: Regardless of your immigration status, you are encouraged to apply to GAP.
how_to_apply: Apply online (an account lets you save your progress). You write short answers and give references, then join a group interview. Apprentices must reapply every year. Two references use a separate online reference form.
notes: Tiers 1 to 3 are not employees. Tier 4 apprentices must be legally authorized to work and eligible under NYC Department of Labor rules, per the page. Partial participation is not allowed. Questions: gap@bbg.org (shown on the page) or 718-623-7252.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.

who_can_apply: High school students who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or in the U.S. for other than a temporary purpose, from a low-income household and/or first in the family to go to college. About 60 students are served each year.
how_to_apply: The Program Overview page says to click its apply link (a short link). Phone: 718-289-5855. Ask the program about this year's dates.
notes: The page says low-income means family taxable income at or below 150 percent of the poverty level. Two thirds of participants must be both low-income and first generation. One third must be one or the other. After-school tutoring runs 4:30 to 7 PM on weekdays when the host school does not offer it.
duration: Academic year: 21 Saturdays from September to April, 10 AM to 2 PM plus STEM labs 2:30 to 4:30 PM. Summer: six weeks, with three weeks as a commuter at BCC and three weeks at a residential site.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. The pages do not list a cost.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 19. Twelve students are chosen for each session. The page encourages you to apply again if you were not accepted before.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free online application on the Bronx Museum event page for the session. Educators read the applications and pick 12 students. If you have questions, write to education@bronxmuseum.org.
notes: The fall 2026 application form is closed, so no apply link is listed here. Check the Teen Programs page for the next one. The museum is under renovation but stays open Wednesday to Sunday, 11 AM to 6 PM, at 1040 Grand Concourse. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Teen Council: two four-month sessions a year (fall and spring), twice a week after school. Fall 2026 runs late October 2026 to mid-February 2027, Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM. Teen Summer: four weeks, three afternoons a week.
pay_detail: Teens are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated on the pages.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors at a high school in any of the five boroughs. You need an interest in the arts, a GPA of 2.0 or higher, and an unofficial transcript.
how_to_apply: Use the Enroll button on the BAM BIAC page, which links to an online form. The page lists the Education Program Manager for questions. Include an unofficial high school transcript.
notes: Only 13 spots. After the program, BAM Education alumni ages 18 to 24 can join a separate paid Creative Career Collective (virtual, Oct to Dec). Pay amount and work-permit rules are not on the page.
duration: One year in 3 sessions: one week in August (Mon to Fri, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.), October to December, and February to June (1 to 2 days a week, 4 to 6 p.m.). The 2026-27 cohort runs Aug 2026 to Jun 2027.
pay_detail: The page says the internship is paid. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade in New York City public schools.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says applications usually open at the end of the school year. Check the Youth Advisory Council page or ask the Borough President's office.
notes: The council is run with the Brooklyn North and Brooklyn South high school superintendents and Sadie Nash Leadership Project. The page does not say whether members are paid or where teens must live, so ask the office.
duration: Throughout the school year, 2 meetings a month.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High schoolers ages 14 to 18 who live in Brooklyn. BRIC picks students from groups with less access to media training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page. Attending every class is required to get the stipend.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Finishing the program makes you eligible for other paid BRIC work, per the page. The page says eight sessions but lists nine Tuesdays, and gives Dec 9 in one place and Dec 8 in another, so confirm the last date.
duration: 8 sessions, 16 hours. Fall 2026: Tuesdays Oct 13 to Dec 8, 4 to 6 p.m.
pay_detail: Free class with a $200 stipend if you attend every session.

who_can_apply: NYC high school age teens. You can apply to only one of the two fellowships. The current page does not list exact ages; the 2023-24 page said NYC sophomores, juniors or seniors, or ages 15 to 19.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You cannot edit it after you submit. Then you have a virtual interview. After that you get an offer and steps to start.
notes: Pay is called a stipend on the page. Working papers are not mentioned for the fellowships, but BRIC requires them for its bootcamps for under 18, so ask. BRIC also accepts youth under 21 for its film festival.
duration: 2026-27 school year. Curatorial meets Wednesdays 4 to 6 p.m. Media meets Thursdays 4 to 6 p.m. In person at BRIC.
pay_detail: $17 per hour for 2 hours a week, paid every two weeks, based on attendance.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Beginners are welcome. You must attend every session; if you miss the first day your spot goes to the waitlist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Class is at Clarendon Library in Brooklyn, not at BRIC House. The page text says Mondays but its class-times list shows Thursdays (Oct 8 to Nov 26), so confirm the weekday.
duration: 8 sessions, 16 hours. Fall 2026: Mondays Oct 5 to Nov 30, 4 to 6 p.m. (no class Oct 12). Exhibition Thu, Dec 10, 5 to 7 p.m.
pay_detail: Free class with a $200 stipend if you attend every session.

who_can_apply: Volunteers under 16 must be accompanied and supervised by a parent or guardian at all times. Event volunteer opportunities are typically open to volunteers ages 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Make a Volunteer Profile with the Volgistics link on the park's volunteer page. Then pick events.
notes: The page lists no deadline and no 2027 dates. Most volunteer events run April to October.
duration: Green Team: twice a month on Saturdays, 10 a.m. to noon, April to October. Coastal Cleanups: about 2 hours each, now and then from April to October. Sign up for as many as you like.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who live in Brooklyn or go to school in Brooklyn. A strong interest in Brooklyn's past.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says the 2026 application is closed. Questions: CBHEducation@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Confirm first: pay, exact dates and application steps are not on the page. The page showed the 2026 application as closed. Ask CBH Education whether it is paid.
duration: Summer. The 2026 program had a final reception; exact weeks and hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. Ask CBH Education whether there is a stipend.

who_can_apply: Youth from across New York City. Most classes are ages 14 to 19; the Advanced Portfolio class is ages 16 to 24. You do not need to be an artist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the Studio Programs page. Questions: Phoebe@groundswell.nyc or Brandon@groundswell.nyc (shown on the page), or call 718-254-9782.
notes: The page described the 2025-26 school year, so check the page for the 2026-27 session. Classes are at the Gowanus studio, in person.
duration: The 2025-26 session ran Oct 27 to Mar 12, with one class a week (afternoons, about 2 to 2.5 hours).
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned for the studio classes.

who_can_apply: Youth. Ages, grades and how to join are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact Groundswell: Office@groundswell.nyc or 718-254-9782 (shown on the site), or check the Youth section for application news.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list ages, pay amount or how to apply. It says murals are made throughout New York City, and one project title mentions Queensbridge House.
duration: July to August
pay_detail: The page says youth get stipends and calls it a summer jobs program. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students in 11th or 12th grade, and college students, who like health careers. You must also be processed as a hospital volunteer. That means a form, a medical packet, an in-person interview and a 3-hour orientation.
how_to_apply: Send the intern application and the under-18 release form. Add a short essay (500 words max) on why you want it. Add proof of vaccination (COVID and flu) and two short recommendation letters. Then you have a 15 to 20 minute virtual interview. Questions: Volunteer@maimo.org or 718-283-3980.
notes: Unpaid, so no work permit. Students under 18 may only volunteer 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday, per the page. Check the page for the year of each deadline.
duration: Three rotation blocks a year: Dec 11 to Mar 10, Mar 11 to May 31, and Jun 1 to Sep 2.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a certificate of completion from the hospital.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says volunteers range in age from 14 to 90 but does not state a minimum teen age. All volunteers need medical clearance, references, an interview, a background check and orientation.
how_to_apply: Download the High School Student Application Packet from the volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer@maimo.org. Or mail it to Department of Volunteer and Student Services, 5014 Fort Hamilton Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11219. Phone 718-283-3980. They send medical clearance forms after they get your application.
notes: Students under 18 may not volunteer outside 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. The page says volunteering does not lead to a paid job at Maimonides. Some programs (Feeders, Summer Youth) go through partner schools.
duration: At least two 4-hour shifts a week. In the school year, volunteers under 18 must give at least 6 hours per workweek.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a cafeteria meal voucher and discounted parking. A recommendation letter is offered after at least 150 hours.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their senior year. Strong essay needed. You must be free Monday to Friday for all four weeks with no vacation or summer classes.
how_to_apply: Email the form and an essay as one PDF to Volunteer@maimo.org. Put "Science Scholars" and the year in the subject line. Add a parent waiver form. If accepted, you also finish the hospital volunteer form, the medical packet and an in-person interview by May 20.
notes: Formerly named Women in Science. Led by the Chief of Colon and Rectal Surgery. Incomplete applications are not looked at. Accepted students also go through the hospital volunteer process. Ask whether it is paid.
duration: 4 weeks. The 2026 session ran Mon, July 6 to Fri, July 31, 2026.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: All New York City high school students.
how_to_apply: Online application through the link on the program page when it is open.
notes: You must commit to the full schedule, including summer. Questions: teen.programs@brooklynmuseum.org.
duration: November 2026 to August 2027: Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM during the school year, then Wednesday to Friday 10 AM to 4 PM in July and August.
pay_detail: $17 per hour. Second-year apprentices are leaders and earn $18 per hour. Up to 180 hours for the year. OMNY cards for weekend and summer work.

who_can_apply: New York City teens who are in 10th, 11th, or 12th grade when it starts.
how_to_apply: Online application through the link on the program page when it is open.
notes: The museum says this is best for teens who have no other clubs or jobs. Questions: teen.programs@brooklynmuseum.org.
duration: September 2026 to June 2027: some Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, plus a weekly three-hour weekend art class each semester.
pay_detail: $17 per hour, up to 120 hours for the year. MetroCards for weekend work.

who_can_apply: All New York City teens.
how_to_apply: Online application through the link on the program page when it is open.
notes: Open to queer and trans youth and allies. You must commit to the full schedule. Questions: teen.programs@brooklynmuseum.org.
duration: November 2026 to June 2027: Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, plus some Fridays and weekends.
pay_detail: $17 per hour. Second-year members are leaders and earn $18 per hour. Up to 75 hours for the year. OMNY cards for weekend and evening work.

who_can_apply: All New York City high school students.
how_to_apply: Online application through the link on the program page when it is open.
notes: You must commit to the full schedule. Questions: teen.programs@brooklynmuseum.org.
duration: November 2026 to May 2027: Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, plus some Fridays and weekends.
pay_detail: $17 per hour. Second-year members are leaders and earn $18 per hour. Up to 75 hours for the year. OMNY cards for weekend and evening work.

who_can_apply: High school students who will be between 15.5 and 18 years old. U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or international students with a valid F-1 visa. All experience levels are welcome.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Pratt PreCollege form. It opens in November. Students are billed in mid-April and payment is due right away. Scholarship forms are separate. Email: precollege@pratt.edu (listed on the page).
notes: Scholarships go to students with strong art work and big money need. The FAQ says winners usually come from homes with income of $60,000 or less. Pratt also has shorter options. They include an Explore program, an online summer program, Saturday classes and one-day workshops.
duration: 4 weeks, 4 college credits. 2027 dates: check-in Tue, July 6; classes July 8 to July 30; exhibition and move out Sat, July 31.
pay_detail: Costs money. The tuition amount was not on the program pages. Budget $300 to $500 more for art supplies, plus metro fare. Need-based scholarships cover tuition, program fees, housing and meal plan.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 for the Teen Service Series. The Park Pitch In weekends are open to teens 14 and up, adults and groups. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Register online for each event through the Alliance volunteer page. Registration is required. Questions: (718) 965-8951. The phone number is listed under Contact Us.
notes: Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit. Some events have age limits, so check the age on each event. The Junior Volunteer Corps is for youth groups with children ages 4 to 13.
duration: Single days. Teen Service Series runs select Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, June to October (times vary). Park Pitch In runs select weekends April to November.
pay_detail: Unpaid and free. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Girls and nonbinary students in grades 9 to 12 (rising seniors OK) who live in the New York tri-state area and can commute to campus. Current 8th graders should apply the next year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Bossgirls page. The page strongly discourages submissions generated by AI tools. Check the page for the 2027 opening.
notes: Hours in 2026: 10am to 3pm in weeks 1 and 5, 10am to 1pm in weeks 2 to 4. A search summary said the 2026 deadline was in late February; the page itself gives no date, so confirm.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Thursday (2026: June 29 to July 30)
pay_detail: Free (sponsored by Standard Chartered Bank). No pay; it is an enrichment program, not an internship.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page says ages 13 to 18 in one place and 13 to 17 in another, so ask which applies to you. A parent or guardian must sign a consent form.
how_to_apply: Register in advance when a sign-up link appears on the page. Space is limited. You get an email the Thursday before with details and a waiver. Use the contact link on the page for questions.
notes: No one can join without the waiver. Check the page often, because sessions fill up.
duration: Saturdays 1:00 to 2:00 pm, April to June and September to December
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 or freshman year of college. The commuter option is for students who live in or near NYC. Academic strength is what the admissions team looks for.
how_to_apply: Online application. Columbia says applications are reviewed on the dates-and-deadlines schedule; early registration is cheaper to plan around.
notes: Expensive; the page says financial aid details are elsewhere and they were not read. The commuter page still shows a $95 application fee under a Summer 2026 cost heading while the cost page for Summer 2027 says $80. Free Columbia programs for NYC teens (Double Discovery Center, Freedom and Citizenship) exist but their pages blocked access, so they are not listed.
duration: 1 week (Jun 21 to 25, 2027) or 3 weeks (Jun 28 to Jul 16, 2027; more sessions listed on the dates page).
pay_detail: 1-week session $2,883. 3-week session $6,381. Plus an $95 application fee and $50 or more for course materials. Deposit $1,000 (1-week) or $2,000 (3-week) is credited toward the cost. These are estimates pending trustee approval.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors based in the New York City area. You must come to every weekly meeting at the museum.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Smithsonian application system (SOLAA). The application has short answer questions, an essay and two references. The references are adults who are not related to you. A teacher or mentor works. You can save and finish later. A virtual info session was offered. See the page.
notes: Meets at 2 East 91st Street and some offsite places. The page says the demographic and citizenship questions are optional and not tied to your application. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. Cooper Hewitt also runs free monthly Teen Drop-In workshops and a Design Career Fair.
duration: Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, Jan 19 to Jun 1, 2027, with NYC school breaks off
pay_detail: $1,250 stipend after you finish the program.

who_can_apply: New York City public or charter high school students in grades 9 to 12. The page says students meet a mix of these: attend a school without a full visual arts program, qualify for free school meals, or come from a low or moderate income household. No art experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the Saturday Program page when it is open. No recommendation letter is needed. You get an email when you are accepted. Sign up for the mailing list on the page for the next opening. Office phone and email are on the FAQ page.
notes: Classes are at the Foundation Building, 7 E 7th Street, and 41 Cooper Square. The FAQ page still shows the 2024-2025 year in places, so trust the main page for current dates. There is a year-end show for families.
duration: Saturdays 10 AM to 5 PM through the school year, in a fall and a spring semester
pay_detail: Free to students. The FAQ says round-trip MetroCards are handed out each Saturday on request. This is a class, not a job.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You are a rising sophomore to rising senior or the same level.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form and pay tuition to enroll. The page also links a scholarship section for the Jeffery and Paul Gural Merit Scholarship for NYC Public School Students. Questions: the program email is on the page.
notes: This is a commuter program on campus. The page does not give housing or college credit. The page lists the 2026 year; check the mailing list for the 2027 price.
duration: Four weeks, Monday to Thursday 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM. The 2026 program ran July 13 to Aug 6, 2026. No housing, meals or college credit.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $4,350 to $4,500 depending on the course, including a $270 non-refundable registration fee, art materials and field trips. The Gural Merit Scholarship for NYC Public School Students covers full tuition.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 9th, 10th or 11th grade. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to students from anywhere, but New York City students get priority for financial aid. Some courses need strong math or chemistry grades.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open on Dec 11, 2026. See the FAQs on the Summer STEM page for the aid process. The program is selective.
notes: Classes are in person at 41 Cooper Square. The page lists 2026 prices: $3,150 for a 3-week course and $5,150 for a 6-week course. Check the 2027 numbers when applications open.
duration: 3 or 6 weeks, Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 3 PM. The 2026 program ran July 6 to Aug 13, 2026.
pay_detail: 2026 cost was $3,150 per course. Financial aid is available to those who qualify. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 19 who completed 10th grade by the program start, live in the NYC area (or arrange a supervising adult and housing), and are U.S. citizens or permanent residents at U.S. curriculum schools. No interview or minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript, two recommendation letters and short essays (250 to 300 words each). Contact: summer@tech.cornell.edu.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page, so confirm the price and any financial aid with the program before applying. Selective. International students are not admitted at this time.
duration: 3 weeks, commuter only (no housing). Exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page (students earn 2 Cornell credits). Ask summer@tech.cornell.edu before applying.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 24. This includes teens who are pregnant or have kids. You do not need an appointment or a referral.
how_to_apply: Go to 460 West 41 Street, New York, NY any time, or call 212-613-0300. Intake is open 24 hours a day.
notes: This is a support program for teens who are on their own, not a typical job. The details of CovWorks (length, pay, who qualifies) are not on the program pages, so ask staff. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: Free. The site says there is no cost to stay or use the services. Pay for CovWorks training is not stated.

who_can_apply: NYC residents ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. You need at least a 5th grade reading level. You must be authorized to work in the United States. The Advanced Training track needs a high school diploma or HSE.
how_to_apply: The page has no application form. Call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646 to find a provider near you.
notes: The page lists these training areas: Healthcare, Construction, Transportation and Culinary Arts. It also lists Digital Marketing. Direct Service Professionals is listed too. The page does not mention a work permit. It does say you must be allowed to work in the United States.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: The page says participants are paid at each program level. It does not state the pay rate.

who_can_apply: 2025 FAQ: rising high school seniors or college students ages 16 to 24 who can legally work in the U.S. and have some prior paid or volunteer work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the SYEP application online at application.nycsyep.com and choose a Ladders community partner. Selection uses a personal statement, transcript and resume, then workshops, mock interviews and employer interviews (2025 FAQ).
notes: Competitive. Eligibility, pay and process come from the 2025 FAQ because no newer FAQ was found, so check the DYCD page when applications reopen. Interns under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). Free to apply.
duration: 6 weeks, 25 to 40 hours a week (2025 FAQ)
pay_detail: At least $16.50 per hour in 2025 (2025 FAQ). 2026 pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: NYC high school juniors and seniors who live in New York City, are low income (or meet an exception such as public assistance, foster care or living in a high-poverty area) and meet at least one other listed need. The page lists age 16 to 21 in one place and 14 to 21 in another, so ask a provider.
how_to_apply: Contact a Learn & Earn provider from the DYCD list, or call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646. Providers check your eligibility.
notes: Income-based, with extra eligibility rules listed on the page. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Year-round program with a six-week paid summer internship
pay_detail: Paid six-week summer internship. Rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Drop-in centers are for youth up to age 24 and their families. Housing for independent living is for ages 16 to 24 who have no home. The page does not state ages for crisis shelter and outreach.
how_to_apply: Use the discoverDYCD site to find a drop-in center, shelter or housing site near you. The page does not give a phone number.
notes: This is a safety and housing service, not a job. If you are in danger right now, call 911. The Door and Covenant House (other cards) also take walk-ins.
pay_detail: The page does not list a cost.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who live in the five boroughs of NYC and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. Some options (school-based, NYCHA, foster care, homeless youth) have extra rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at application.nycsyep.com or on paper with an SYEP provider. One application only. Community-based placements are picked by random lottery. Have ID documents ready (proof of age, identity, address, Social Security).
notes: Pay and hours above are the 2026 numbers and may change. Free to apply. NYS Department of Labor says anyone 14-17 needs working papers (employment certificate) to hold a job in New York State; ask your SYEP provider what they need from you. Teens in school-based (CareerReady) options apply through their school. You pay your own transportation and meals. Henry Street Settlement is one SYEP group. Its lottery takes ages 16 to 24. Teens in NYCHA's Baruch or Wald Houses, in shelters, or in foster care can apply first come, first served.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Ages 16-24 (2026): $17.00 per hour, 25 hours a week. Ages 14-15 (2026): up to $700 for about 12.5 hours a week.

who_can_apply: NYC residents ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. The page also lists a high school diploma or equivalent. It also lists U.S. work authorization. Males must register with Selective Service.
how_to_apply: The page has no application form. Call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646 to find a provider near you.
notes: The page says the program is for ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. Target industries are Infrastructure, Healthcare, Technology, Media and Government. The page does not state the pay rate, the program length or whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: The page says the program includes paid internships. It does not state the pay rate.

who_can_apply: NYC residents legally allowed to work in the U.S. who took part in the 2026 Summer Youth Employment Program as CareerReady (ages 16 to 19 in a CareerReady partner high school) or in Special Initiatives (ages 16 to 20, in high school or a high school equivalency program), as of Oct 26, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the WLG online application (CareerReady or Special Initiatives link), or ask your SYEP provider for help. If selected, submit documents online or in person to your provider.
notes: Only for teens who were in 2026 SYEP through a partner school or Special Initiatives provider, so most teens cannot start here. Internet access is required. The application deadline has passed. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).
duration: 22-week program. The page does not state start or end dates.
pay_detail: New York State minimum wage, paid every two weeks (DYCD FAQ).

who_can_apply: Youth in foster care and youth who have left foster care in New York City, from 6th grade through age 26.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Sign-up for Coaching form on the ACS Fair Futures page, or call 212-676-8609. Your foster care agency may also help.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Support, not a paid job. Ask your coach about paid internships.
pay_detail: Not a job. A cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending a New York City high school. Not every accepted student is matched with a site.
how_to_apply: Online application with short-answer questions and a resume, then an interview with the Futures and Options team. Then they try to match you to a site. Use the interest form on the page to get a notice when it opens. Questions: programquestions@futuresandoptions.org.
notes: Pay rate, season and length are not on the page, so confirm first. Futures and Options is based in Manhattan but serves NYC students from every borough. It also runs Career Essentials workshops (the fall application closed Oct 7, 2026).
duration: Not stated. Internship hours plus two orientations and a series of workshops.
pay_detail: The page says the internships are paid. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: New York City students who are about to graduate from high school. You like business, finance, government or public policy.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page. You will be told when the application opens.
notes: The page says 930 students have been ULF interns since 1996 and alumni have received $1.7 million in scholarships. Rate and dates are not stated.
duration: 6 weeks in the summer
pay_detail: Paid summer internship. The hourly rate is not stated. At the end you get a book and technology stipend and can apply for college scholarships.

who_can_apply: Driven high school juniors who are on track to graduate and allowed to work in the U.S. You can have a lighter class load in senior year for the internship. Students at partner schools apply in the fall or winter of junior year.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Genesys Works site and pick New York. If accepted you get an email to interview for a spot in summer training. You provide your own transportation to training and to the internship.
notes: The page says Genesys Works works with set schools, so ask your counselor if your school is a partner. The direct New York link on the location page gave a not-found error. Use the main Apply Now button or email info.nyc@genesysworks.org. Many schools give credit for the training and internship.
duration: 8 weeks of summer training (160 hours) between junior and senior year, then a year-long internship of about 20 hours a week during the school year
pay_detail: Hourly rates vary by site. The page says interns can make about $10,000 to $12,000 over the internship year. Another spot on the site says $10,000 to $13,000.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Send the application form. Add one letter from a teacher, coach, counselor, boss or camp counselor. A committee reads them. Only some applicants get an interview. Call 212-423-3254 with questions.
notes: Because there is a stipend, ask the museum about working papers for under 18. The page does not say. Check the museum site for the next call.
duration: Spring training, then the 2026 to 27 school year
pay_detail: Interns get a stipend. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents who come from a low-income household and/or are first-generation college students (neither parent has a bachelor's degree). The program checks income with tax papers such as a 1040. Grade levels and school lists are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask the program for the forms by email. You need the application and the recommendation forms. The Eligibility and Selection page lists who to write to: the Program Director or the Curriculum Coordinator. The form asks about you and your money. It also asks for a personal statement.
notes: This is a federal TRIO program that gets funding from the U.S. Department of Education. The pages do not say how many students are accepted or which schools it serves. Ask the program before you plan around the summer dates.
