duration: School-year activities plus a four-week summer academic program with high school level classes at John Jay, living on a college campus
pay_detail: Free to the student. The page says all Upward Bound activities and services are free. A stipend is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. Not residential.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the Program Registration Form. Step 2: pay with the Program Payment Form. Both steps are needed to confirm a spot. The contact is listed on the page.
notes: The page says to register early because the program has hit its limit in past years. Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it. The prices on the page are the 2026 prices.
duration: 4 days, July 19 to 22, 2027, 9 AM to 3 PM each day
pay_detail: $500 if you register before June 1 and $550 before July 1 (the page shows 2026 prices). The fee includes a light breakfast each day and a T-shirt. Finishers get a certificate and a $75 application fee waiver for the chemical engineering degree.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. Not residential.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the Program Registration Form. Step 2: pay with the Program Payment Form. Both are needed to confirm participation. The contact is listed on the page.
notes: Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it. Page pricing is $500 before May 1 and $550 before June 1, which does not match pay_detail; pay_detail needs a human check. The page also lists a free Summer Engineering Awareness Program. It lasts six or ten days.
duration: 4 days, July 19 to 22, 2027
pay_detail: $400 before May 1 and $450 before June 1.

who_can_apply: Any high school student.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Institute Registration Form to pick your weeks, then pay for each week with the Program Payment Form. Both steps are required to hold a spot.
notes: Contact details are on the page. The registration and payment forms are separate, and both are needed. The form link uses the old Manhattan College name. The form page did not load as text, so confirm it is open before you plan around it.
duration: Six one-week sessions from July 5 to Aug 12, 2027, Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 2:30 PM. You can attend one or more weeks. Not residential.
pay_detail: $600 per week. Finishing at least one week earns a certificate and a no-cost application to the engineering program (a $75 value).

who_can_apply: Motivated high school students. The page lists students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the pre-college sign-up form linked on the O'Malley page when it reopens.
notes: Manhattan University is in Riverdale in the Bronx. Check the page for 2027 prices and dates.
duration: 2026 session: June 22 to July 31, 2026, with a one-week in-person intensive July 13-17, 2026 plus five weeks online
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $6,000 tuition. A residential option adds $1,000 per week for room and board ($7,000 total).

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade who are entering their junior or senior year. You must stay in the residence.
how_to_apply: The page lists the School of Engineering contact for details. The phone is 718-862-7281. The email is deanengr@manhattan.edu. No sign-up form is linked for this program.
notes: Parents can come to the closing ceremony and final project contest. Other short summer engineering programs on the same page cost less or are free.
duration: 7 days, Aug 1 to 7, 2027, living on campus
pay_detail: $2,500 total, which covers tuition, room and board, supplies and events.

who_can_apply: Students now enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. The page says selection is based in part on strong math and science skills and interest in engineering.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application form. It says to complete the registration form, and the page lists the program director, Dr. Walter P. Saukin, at 718-862-7171 (Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 4 PM). Call to ask how to apply.
notes: The school is now called Manhattan University, formerly Manhattan College. The page says the program has run for over 40 years. The page lists a free program. It comes with a certificate and no fee to apply at Manhattan University. The page lists an email for the director that does not match the director's name, so call instead. Confirm the steps with the director.
duration: Choose a 6-day or 10-day session. The page lists 2027 dates: June 25-26 and June 28 to July 1 (8 AM to 3 PM); July 7-9, 12-16 and 19-20 (10-day program, 8:30 AM to 3 PM); and July 22-23 and 26-29.
pay_detail: Free to participants. Corporate and individual sponsors pay for it. You get a certificate and an application fee waiver at Manhattan University.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11, or working on a GED, at a New York City high school or home school. You need working papers and a Social Security Number or ITIN. A parent or guardian must say yes. You can't have done a Met internship before.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and write short essays. Ask one adult who is not family for a letter. If they pick you, you go to a group interview in person.
notes: You must come to every date on the list. A parent or guardian must come to the January 16, 2027 party. If you missed the October 16 deadline, try the summer internship. It also takes students from New Jersey and Connecticut.
duration: 40 hours, about 2 to 4 hours a week from Feb 9 to May 28, 2027, plus a Jan 23 bootcamp, monthly Saturday check-ins and three Teen Fridays.
pay_detail: $1,100 stipend when you finish, which the page says matches New York State minimum wage law.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11, or working on a GED. You must live in and go to school (or home school) in New York, New Jersey, or Connecticut. You need working papers and a Social Security Number or ITIN. A parent or guardian must say yes. You can't have done a Met internship before.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and write short essays. Ask one adult who is not family for a letter. If they pick you, you go to a group interview in person.
notes: You must come to every date on the list. A parent or guardian must come to the party in June. The Met also has a spring internship for New York City students. Connecticut is not a place on this site yet, but students there can apply.
duration: 40 hours, about 10 to 20 hours a week. In 2026: bootcamp July 1, placement July 7 to Aug 7, plus a June 27 family reception.
pay_detail: $1,100 stipend when you finish, which the page says matches New York State minimum wage law.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students in grade 10, 11, or 12 in the 2026 to 2027 school year who have a deep interest in art or museums.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. The link is on the program page when it is open.
notes: Attendance is required. Missing meetings again and again gets you removed. The 2026 to 2027 application form now says it has expired. Questions: momateens@moma.org.
duration: October 2026 to June 2027, every Tuesday 4:30 to 6:30 PM, plus some other days and weekends.
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend when you finish. MoMA pays for all materials, snacks and other costs.

who_can_apply: Students 16 and older. Some roles, such as Maternal Child Health, require 18. Montefiore also partners with SYEP. Its SYEP provider is Children's Arts and Sciences Workshop.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Summer Volunteer - High School posting on Montefiore's career site (linked from the volunteer page), then attend an orientation and interview. Interviews are first come, first served.
notes: Confirm first: the dates are from the 2025 posting. Contact: volunteerservices@montefiore.org (shown on the page).
duration: Summer session runs June to September; minimum 100 hours; each session at least 3 to 4 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. JuMP is for ages 15 to 17 and requires full availability for all six weeks. Unit Support is open to high school students. The emergency department and some other roles are 18+.
how_to_apply: Online application, one letter of recommendation from a non-relative, and a resume.
notes: Read through the fetch tool because direct downloads were blocked. The page says volunteers need a valid Social Security number (a hospital clearance rule on the official site) and pay for their own medical clearance. Other Mount Sinai campuses have their own pages and age rules that were not read.
duration: JuMP: 6 weeks, 100 hours. Unit Support: one 3-hour shift a week; the page lists a 100 hour minimum for high school students.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no JuMP cost or pay.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in health care who can attend the full month. The page wants motivated, mature students with volunteer experience. Ten students are accepted.
how_to_apply: Watch the Lenox Hill volunteer page for the next call for forms. If you have a question, write to the Manhattan campus volunteer team. The email is manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page is out of date, so check with the volunteer team to see if there is a 2027 program. The regular junior volunteer program has different rules and needs working papers.
duration: At least 100 hours in July, at least four days a week (Monday to Thursday) from 9 AM to 3 PM. No vacation during that time.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 at the Manhattan hospitals. Junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) hand in working papers and a parent consent form. All applicants are interviewed, then there is a six-month trial period.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Lenox Hill volunteer page. There is an interview. There is a required orientation. You also need a medical clearance. Questions? Write to manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page says junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) must submit working papers and a parental consent form. Orientation and medical clearance are required. Volunteers 18 and older must pass a background screening. The page asks for 100 hours a year. The page gives a minimum age of 16 and no maximum age.
duration: 100 hours per calendar year is required. Onboarding takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: Explainers are high school students. The page does not state a grade or age range. Interns work one weekend shift a week.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Complete applications get an invite to a group interview at the Children's Adventure Garden. Accepted teens attend orientation with a parent or guardian and 24 hours of training before starting.
notes: Questions: explainers@nybg.org. Intern tier is unpaid, so a work permit is not clearly needed there; the paid tiers are jobs and the page does not say what papers are required. The orientation date printed on the page shows the wrong year, so confirm it with NYBG. Late applications roll to the next session.
duration: Spring 2027 internship: one 4.5 hour Saturday or Sunday shift each week, Mar 20 to Jun 19, 2027 (the page lists both 105 and 125 service hours; confirm with NYBG), plus 4 required training days (Mar 6, 7, 13, 14, 2027).
pay_detail: Intern tier is unpaid volunteering (OMNY card help for transit can be provided). Later tiers (Advanced Explainer, Mentor, Senior) are paid part-time jobs; the page gives no hourly rate.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 (18 for some programs; check each campus). The Queens and Hudson Valley campuses do not offer Summer Only volunteering. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application and choose Summer Only plus your preferred program and campus. A volunteer services representative contacts you for an interview if a spot is open.
notes: Many NYP roles (emergency department, palliative care and others) are 18+. Brooklyn Methodist also runs a Junior Volunteer Program that was marked full when searched; its own page was not read for details. This entry covers the system-wide Summer Only option only.
duration: Minimum 120 service hours over the summer.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old at the start of the program. Under 18 cannot volunteer during the school year. The year-round program is 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Online application, a group information session, full summer availability, onboarding, health clearance (TB test, MMR and varicella proof, flu shot) and a background check.
notes: The Brooklyn campus requires age 18+. Long Island has its own teen program (not read in detail). The FAQ page still shows old 2022 dates, so only the Manhattan page was used for dates. Med-career internships and research are handled separately through HRNTV@NYULangone.org. The Manhattan page and the volunteer page do not mention working papers, so the work permit answer is unknown.
duration: 8 weeks, two 6-hour shifts a week (100 service hours total).
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says no pay or school credit is given.

who_can_apply: Students who have completed grade 9, 10 or 11 by the program start. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Online application, a 250 to 500 word essay about why you want the course, and an official high school transcript. Contact 212-998-7006 or sps.hsacademy@nyu.edu.
notes: Costs money and gives no college credit or certificate (students get an NYU transcript with a grade). Page does not say whether class is in person.
duration: One week per course (2026 had six weekly sessions, June 29 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: $2,579 tuition per course, $50 application fee, optional housing and dining $684 (summer 2026 prices). No financial aid or discounts offered.

who_can_apply: Full-time NYC residents who attend NYC schools, applying as 10th or 11th graders (rising juniors and seniors), with strong grades and interest in STEM. Students from groups underrepresented in STEM are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Online application (optional recommendation due after), a group interview and lab tours to pick your placement.
notes: Selective with limited spaces. Funded by the Pinkerton Foundation. Students present at an AMNH poster symposium at the end. The two NYU pages differ slightly on grade wording (10th or 11th grade now versus rising juniors and seniors), which is the same group. The program name on a second page reads Applied Research In Science and Engineering. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 10 weeks: about 4 weeks of remote after-school workshops in June, then 6 weeks of in-person lab work (about 150 hours of lab experience). Summer 2026 ran Jun 1 to Aug 14, 2026.
pay_detail: Free. A $2,000 stipend is paid for completing the program.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade at a New York City high school. You show strong effort in school. Most Fellows apply with a GPA of 87 or above. You come from an under-resourced community. Your household income (AGI) is under $125,000. You should not already have similar college and career help. You must commit to the whole program.
how_to_apply: Sign the interest form on the Apply page to get an email when the application opens. The online application takes a couple of hours. It needs your transcript, family facts and two recommendation forms. One is from a teacher. One is from a counselor or advisor. Chosen applicants are invited to group interviews. The page puts these in late March.
notes: Admitted Fellows must come to all days of the Summer Institute. A family member must come to an orientation. The application asks for household income. The program uses it to check the income limit. The pages do not say if a work permit is needed.
duration: Six years. Starts with the OppNet Summer Institute (length not stated on the page), then weekly after-school workshops in 11th and 12th grade.
pay_detail: Fellows do paid summer internships or enrichment programs (five summers over the six years). The page does not state the pay.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who attend PAL Teen Centers.
how_to_apply: Register through the link on PAL's Teen Programs page.
notes: CAP meets at PAL's Webster Center in the Bronx. It is built for teens who would be the first in their family to go to college. PAL Teen Centers, for teens 13 to 19, are free and open 3 to 5 evenings a week.
pay_detail: Free to join. The page does not say whether the internships are paid.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older by the first day of work. The test page said 16 by July 18, 2026. You must swim 50 yards and meet the vision rule.
how_to_apply: Register for a qualifying test on the Parks page when dates open (or join the notice list). Pass the swim and vision test, then do the training. A letter from an eye doctor can replace the on-site vision exam.
notes: The two Parks pages disagree on the swim time. The main page says 50 yards in 50 seconds or less. The test page says 50 yards in 40 seconds or less with proper form. Plan for the faster one. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Training course of 16 sessions, then the summer season. Beaches open Memorial Day weekend and outdoor pools open in late June. Both close the Sunday after Labor Day. You work five or six days a week.
pay_detail: $22 per hour for lifeguards who finish training and get a post. Lifeguards also get a $908 training payment after the summer season.

who_can_apply: Students entering high school in New York City. The program starts with career exploration in 9th grade, and college courses can begin as early as 10th grade. The page does not list entry rules for each school.
how_to_apply: The page says admission is unscreened (Educational Option method). Attend an information session, open house or high school fair, then rank a P-TECH school as a top choice on your high school application. Check each school's process on its website or at MySchools.nyc.
notes: This is a school choice made before 9th grade, so it fits 8th graders and their families. The page names five schools in Manhattan and the Bronx. Examples are Inwood Early College for Health and Information Technologies and Urban Assembly New York Harbor School. Check each listing to see how students get in.
duration: Six years or less (grades 9 to 14)
pay_detail: The degree is free: courses, materials and college textbooks cost nothing. Internships are listed as a possible part of work-based learning; pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who are seen as leaders at school, often through student government. Members are voted in at the borough meetings. Each year, two student reps are voted onto the Panel for Educational Policy.
how_to_apply: There is no open form on the page. Ask your school counselor or student government adviser how students are chosen for the borough council. Elections for the Chancellor's council happen at the borough meetings.
notes: There are six borough councils: one in each borough, with two in Brooklyn. The page does not list contacts or meeting dates. It is a leadership role, not a job.
duration: Borough councils meet monthly. The Chancellor's council meets monthly from October through June at the central office.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: Students at least 14 and now in high school. You can be outdoors for 2 hours. You have your own ride to the site. You pass an interview. You come to 5 of 6 classes.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the internship page, then do a virtual interview. Contact: Erica Chow (email on the page).
notes: This is a learning internship, not a job, and it costs $200 unless you get aid. You must find your own transportation. Supported by Con Edison and other funders per the page. The page says 5 of 6 classes in its eligibility section but 6 out of 7 dates for spring and fall, so ask which applies.
duration: 6 sessions of 3 hours per season (9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.). Spring 2027: Saturdays Mar 27 to May 8. Summer 2027: Tuesdays or Wednesdays, July 6 to Aug 11. Fall 2027: Saturdays Sept 18 to Oct 23.
pay_detail: $200 fee after you are accepted. Financial aid is available on request and needs no paperwork.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17. You must attend an interview and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer form on the volunteer page. Return it to the volunteer coordinator before the deadline. Then you have an interview and an orientation.
notes: The page lists deadline months, not the year. Popular program, so apply early.
duration: One of three semesters. Fall and spring: one day a week after school. Summer: up to 3 days a week for 6 weeks in July and August, plus a late June orientation.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you can earn school credit or work experience.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. Only the student should fill out the application, not a parent.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the form on the page. Applications only, no walk-ins.
notes: Popular program with an acceptance step and a waitlist. Mostly outdoors, weather permitting. The museum is the Queens County Farm Museum.
duration: 9 months of select Sundays, 1 to 3 p.m. 2026-27 dates: Oct 11 through June 6, 2027. Certification ceremony June 20.
pay_detail: Unpaid and free. No admission fee. You earn a certificate if you attend at least 13 of 16 sessions.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Junior volunteers cannot serve on weekends or late evenings.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 718-670-5952 to book an in-person interview. No walk-ins. Bring a valid ID (state, school or passport), a working permit and one professional letter of recommendation. Then you need medical clearance (doctor form, urine drug screen, flu shot). You also go to a 4-hour orientation.
notes: The hospital lists a "Working Permit" as a requirement for junior volunteers. This may mean New York working papers. Ask the Volunteer Services office which work permit paper they accept. The page says volunteering does not guarantee a job. Hospital address: 4500 Parsons Blvd, Flushing.
duration: Commit to 125 hours of service. Onboarding usually takes several weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens, with a focus on BIPOC and other under-served Queens youth. The page does not list exact ages, grades or home address rules, so ask the museum.
how_to_apply: Send in the QTI 2026-27 form through the Submittable link on the Queens Museum announcement. Phone 718-592-9700. Email info@queensmuseum.org.
notes: This is the fifth year of the program. Ages, grades and work-permit rules are not stated on the announcement, so ask the museum.
duration: 9 months of weekly hybrid sessions (in person and online). No more than 4 absences. Start and end dates are not stated.
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend for the 9-month commitment, plus extra money for travel. QTI teens can also be considered for other paid Queens Museum jobs like workshop assistant and camp counselor.

who_can_apply: New York City residents who are currently in high school or college in New York City. You do not need to love science. NYSCI wants curious students who will try new things and practice public speaking.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the page). You can also fill out an interest form to get a reminder and an invite to an info session. Questions: ebautista@nysci.org (listed on the page).
notes: NYSCI is at 47-01 111th St., Corona, Queens. The youth page lists "Young Adults, Age 14-24" in the site menu; the Explainer page itself does not state a minimum age, so confirm. The apply form link on the page showed as closed when read. Pay rate not stated. Work permit not stated on the page.
duration: One full year, including the summer. High school students work at least 5 hours a week (weekends). You must attend every day of orientation first.
pay_detail: The page calls it an education and youth employment program and says you "work" at NYSCI. The hourly rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors with a cumulative average of 92 (no test scores needed), or an average of 90 plus an SAT of 1210 or an ACT of 25. An interview may be required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with a parent consent form and an unofficial transcript. A counselor recommendation form and the official transcript come next. Contact: 718-990-7533. The number is on the page.
notes: Costs money and is for strong students. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates and price.
duration: About 5 weeks. In 2026, July 7 to August 10, classes Monday to Thursday for 2 hours.
pay_detail: $1,000 per course, due July 1 (2026 price). Students who later enroll at St. John's get a $2,000 High School Scholars Grant, renewable for up to four years.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors or seniors who are at least 16 when the program starts. Students from outside NYC and outside the Tri-State area may apply but get no help with housing or travel. No GPA minimum. Sophomores are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You also need a letter of recommendation and a transcript (to show you are in high school). Selected applicants get a Zoom interview.
notes: Very competitive (about 32 students a year). You must attend the entire program with no gaps. Minors cannot work with human patients. You may not use SSRP work in science competitions. Contact: program administrator listed on the page, 1230 York Ave.
duration: 7 weeks, Mon Jun 21 to Thu Aug 5, 2027, full time (about 35 hours a week, roughly 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
pay_detail: Free to apply and attend. An OMNY card covers NYC transit. Stipends are not guaranteed; need-based stipends may go to students with financial hardship who meet all attendance rules.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in 10th or 11th grade who live in New York City or Newark and can come in person once a week. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online from the Leadership Scholars page. Questions: charlie@sadienash.org.
notes: Office: 247 W 37th St, Suite 705, New York, NY. Next round not posted.
duration: Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., November to May, in person at the New York City or Newark office.
pay_detail: Up to $400 at the end of the semester, based on participation.

who_can_apply: High school seniors who are women or gender-expansive youth of color and live in New York City or Newark. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online from the Nash U page. Questions: charlie@sadienash.org.
notes: You must commit to the full internship. Next round not posted.
duration: Saturdays 10 a.m. to 12 noon, November 2026 to May 2027, plus some events.
pay_detail: Eligible for a $400 stipend at the end of the internship.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in grades 9 to 12 who live in New York City or Newark. You commit for the whole program. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online from the program page. Questions: cielito@sadienash.org.
notes: No more than 5 absences in person. Next round not posted.
duration: In person: once a week, Tuesdays or Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., November to May. Virtual: 10 weeks, offered each fall and spring.
pay_detail: In-person: up to $400 at the end. Virtual: up to $150 (you must attend 9 of 10 sessions). Referral bonus of $25 per friend.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth enrolled in high school who live in New York City or Newark and have not done Summer Institute before. No grade or skill rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Apply Now page when the cycle opens, then join a group interview. Sign up for the opportunities email list to hear when it opens. Questions: nashers@sadienash.org.
notes: For young women and gender-expansive youth. The Brooklyn, Queens and other borough sites are part of the same program.
duration: 6 weeks. In 2026: July 6 to Aug 13, Monday to Thursday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at sites in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Newark.
pay_detail: Eligible for a $450 stipend at the end of the summer, based on participation.

who_can_apply: High school students and recent grads ages 14 to 19 in the New York City, New Jersey and Connecticut area. Not everyone gets in.
how_to_apply: Watch the Current Opportunities list on the program page and apply through its Learn More and Apply links. You can also contact the Metro NY Region office.
notes: Contact: Pablo Galesi, (347) 200-4709, pgalesi@thesca.org. In New York, teens 14 to 17 need working papers to work.
duration: School year and summer programs. Length varies by crew.
pay_detail: Paid. The page does not state the rate for teen crews.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 18 in grades 9 to 12. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Apprenticeships page when it opens each March.
notes: Pay is not stated, so ask whether it is paid and whether working papers are needed. The site says the program has run for decades.
duration: July and August, up to 3 days a week, Wednesday to Sunday, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. The page calls it a service learning experience.

who_can_apply: Staten Island high school students in grades 11 and 12, per the program page.
how_to_apply: Download the application. It is a PDF on the program page. Email the finished form to the program email on the page: Medicalscienceprogram@rumcsi.org.
notes: Session dates, start month and cost are not stated, so call or email to confirm before you plan. The general volunteer page says its openings are filled right now. It states no age rule. The application email could not be read in this check, so confirm it.
duration: Six weeks, one day per week after school.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Send the application form, a one-page essay (500 words max) about your goals, and a parent or guardian signature. You can apply online, by mail or by email. Contact: lifelong-learning@wagner.edu, 718-390-3221.
notes: Ask the office whether spring 2027 spots are open and whether the internship is paid.
duration: The fall session runs Oct 2 to Dec 12 (year not stated), on Fridays 5:30 to 8 p.m. or Saturdays 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. (hours depend on class).
pay_detail: No pay or fee is mentioned. You get community service hours and a certificate of completion from Wagner College.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 years old and older who are in high school. Adults over 18 join the regular Docent program.
how_to_apply: Use the Docent application form linked on the zoo volunteer and job page. Candidates must pass the 10-week course. Volunteers go through a background check.
notes: The 2026 class deadline had passed as of 2026-10-09. Check the page around late summer for the next class. Teens learn public speaking and animal presentation skills.
duration: 10-week training course, then ongoing docent shifts.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 years old. You must be able to work on your own and on a team and be available on a regular basis. Some roles (like animal diet prep) are adults only.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer application form linked on the zoo volunteer page. All volunteers go through a background check. The zoo cannot give status updates. It only contacts qualified candidates.
notes: Limited spaces. Volunteers in animal care jobs must show a negative TB test and proof of COVID-19 vaccination, per the page.
duration: Minimum 3 months, can be extended. Regular availability needed.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school-aged youth. No photography experience needed. To get the stipend you must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or otherwise eligible to work in the U.S., and show valid working papers when accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link on the Expanding the Walls page) by Nov 6, 2026. Show valid working papers when you are accepted. Questions: use the contact email on the page.
notes: Meets at 144 W 125th Street. The FAQ on the page still shows the 2026 dates in one spot; the headline dates for 2027 are Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Public school holidays are observed. The page does not state an age range or whether you must live in NYC.
duration: Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Tuesdays 4:00 to 6:30 PM and Saturdays 11 AM to 3 PM, then Tuesday to Thursday 11 AM to 3 PM in the summer.
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend paid at the end of the program, a Canon DSLR camera, and transportation fare to and from the museum. The page says this is not a job or an internship.

who_can_apply: Anyone ages 12 to 24. No documents are needed. Some programs have their own age rules.
how_to_apply: Go to 555 Broome Street, Manhattan, Monday to Friday 2:00 to 5:30 pm (extra hours 10:00 am to 2:00 pm for urgent needs and for youth without stable housing). Or call 212-941-9090 or email membership@door.org.
notes: The Door also has a Bronx drop-in center for runaway and homeless youth. Ask staff for details, because ages for it are not stated. Some job training programs have their own age rules, so ask staff.
pay_detail: Joining is free. Pay is not stated on this page. A separate program, The CUT Culinary Training, lists a stipend (see its card).

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. All Door job programs need free Door membership first.
how_to_apply: Become a Door member (free), then contact Latasha Stephens at Lstephens@door.org or 917-696-3758.
notes: Other Door job programs have other age rules, such as 18 to 24 for several of them. Call first to ask about the next start date.
duration: 12 weeks
pay_detail: Stipend of up to $3,100 over 150 hours

who_can_apply: Open to all NYC youth, including current students and recent graduates. No experience needed. The page gives no age range.
how_to_apply: Email youth@transalt.org with questions or use the RSVP link on the Youth Activist Committee page. Meetings are hybrid, and in person is encouraged.
notes: The page describes youth activism and does not mention a work permit. The page lists meetings on the last Friday of each month from 4:30 to 6 PM, and says meetings are hybrid. Confirm before you go.
duration: Monthly meetings. The NYC Public Schools opportunities page lists the last Friday of the month, 4:30 to 6:00 PM (subject to change).
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer activism. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: New Yorkers ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Check the NYC Votes Youth Ambassadors page for the next call for applications.
notes: Run by the City of New York Campaign Finance Board. Past ambassadors registered voters at public events and with other city agencies. The pages do not say whether the work is paid or needs a work permit.
duration: Weekly meetings, with weekly summer trips. The full length of the program is not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. Ask the program.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, eligible to work in the United States. You must be free on weekends and for the full 13 months (June to June). The 2026 page said June 2026 to June 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen. Watch the ACES page for news. If you have questions, write to education@wavehill.org or youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Wave Hill House, where this program meets, is wheelchair accessible. Interns travel off site for some field trips.
duration: 13 months, about 4 to 8 hours each weekend (14 at most), plus two Saturday workshops a month and July weekday training
pay_detail: $17 per hour

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 16 years old by May 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for May 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the Forest Project page). Pay runs through SYEP, so you also need a separate SYEP application; for 2026 that was due before March 1. Wave Hill tells interviewed teens which SYEP provider to pick. Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Fieldwork is hard physical work outdoors with heavy tools on unpaved ground. The Ecology Building has 28 stairs and is not wheelchair accessible. You must be ready to join all of the program.
duration: One summer (exact weeks not stated on the page)
pay_detail: About $2,275 for the summer, paid through the NYC Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP). You also get credit for one college course.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for July 1, 2026. You must be free for all 14 months.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the WERM page). Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Courses are taught at Wave Hill and the University of Mount Saint Vincent. Fieldwork is outdoors on rough ground with heavy tools. The Ecology Building is not open to wheelchairs. The page names partners such as the American Museum of Natural History.
duration: 14 months: first summer (July to August), school year (September to June), second summer (July to August)
pay_detail: About $3,500 paid across the whole program, plus credit for three college courses.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.

who_can_apply: NYC high school students. YI Artists: grades 9 to 12. YI Arts Careers: entering grades 10 to 12. YI Introductions: entering grades 10 to 12 who are English Language Learners. YI Leaders: grades 11 to 12 who finished at least one semester of YI Artists or YI Arts Careers.
how_to_apply: Online form for each program (links on the Youth Insights page). YI Leaders is for teens who have already done another Youth Insights program.
notes: The page's closing note also lists YI Introductions graduates as eligible for Leaders. That conflicts with its Open to line. The page lists no program contact. Use whitney.org/contact. The Whitney also runs a separate Open Studio for Teens (free).
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. You must have done SYEP last summer and be in school now.
how_to_apply: Ask a group that runs SYEP if it runs WLG too. Two that do are PAL (email Myshanda Parks at MParks@palnyc.org) and Henry Street (email Iliana Balbuena at ibalbuena@henrystreet.org). If you can apply, you go into a lottery.
notes: Only for teens who did SYEP last summer. If you are new, start with the Summer Youth Employment Program. Selection is by lottery, so a spot is not guaranteed. New York State requires working papers for workers ages 14 to 17.
duration: Up to 25 weeks between October and April (PAL). Henry Street says its program runs November to March.
pay_detail: Paid employment. The pages do not state a rate.

who_can_apply: NYC public high school students at one of the 130+ schools with CTE programs. Students who finish a state-approved program can earn a CTE endorsement on their diploma.
how_to_apply: Browse programs on NYC MySchools. Talk to your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center about admissions and enrollment.
notes: This is a school choice, not a job. Ask your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center how enrollment works for your grade. The CTE endorsement needs 44 credits, 5 Regents exams, a technical assessment and work-based learning.
duration: Grades 9 to 12
pay_detail: Part of the school day at no cost. Some work-based learning (such as apprenticeships) can be paid, but pay is not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Any high school student interested in any major. Go to one session or all of them.
how_to_apply: Use the register link for each session on the Business Bootcamp page. Sessions run on Zoom.
notes: The page did not print the year next to the session dates, so check the dates when you sign up. A search summary named a separate High School Business Academy in Manhattan. Its page was not read and its cost is unknown.
duration: One hour per session, 7 to 8 pm
pay_detail: Free. You get a certificate of completion for each session you attend.

who_can_apply: Students in 11th or 12th grade who live or go to school in New York City.
how_to_apply: Online application on the program page when it is open. Selected teens are notified by email.
notes: The theme changes with each exhibition. The fall 2026 group studied the Declaration of Independence. Sign up for NYPL's teen newsletter to hear when the next application opens.
duration: About 9 weeks. In 2026 it ran Oct 20 to Dec 17, Tuesdays and Thursdays 4:30 to 6 PM, at the Schwarzman Building and the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library.
pay_detail: Stipend. The page does not state the amount.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12, per the page's 2026-2027 application form. The page does not list residency rules.
how_to_apply: Complete the application on the LETAB page. Questions: mhs@oppl.org.
notes: The page has an Apply now button and says questions go to mhs@oppl.org. It does not give dates.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It does not say if service hours are given.

who_can_apply: The page says boys and girls at least 14 years old are invited to learn new skills and gain work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and waiver on the volunteer page. Volunteers also go through a criminal background check.
notes: The page says the volunteer background check applies to volunteers. Ask whether it applies to under 18.
duration: Event and program based
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get rewards for their hours.

who_can_apply: Open to job seekers. The page does not list minimum ages. Check the age on each job posting.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online job form. You can upload a resume and cover letter. Hiring supervisors review it. The district cannot talk about forms with anyone but the person who applied.
notes: The page does not say when seasonal hiring opens. Check it in winter. Inclusion partner jobs are handled by WSSRA, a partner group. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.
duration: Seasonal, with set start and end dates
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay is listed on the job postings, not on the main jobs page.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents, at least 16 by the start date, with a 3.00 GPA or higher. You must be in good standing at a school or approved home school in Anderson, Blount, Campbell, Knox, Loudon, McMinn, Monroe, Morgan, Roane or Sevier County, Tennessee. Proof of health insurance is required.
how_to_apply: Apply on Zintellect by Oct 21, 2026. A full form needs recommendations from a STEM teacher and a principal. Home school students can use a curriculum coordinator. Forms that are missing a recommendation are not read.
notes: Closes very soon. You can miss up to five days without losing stipend. Appointments may be extended depending on funding. Only students from the ten listed Tennessee counties can apply.
duration: 16 to 17 weeks, Jan 26 to May 15 or May 22, 2027, part time each week
pay_detail: $125 per week for part-time participation

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 17 who will be in grade 10, 11 or 12 and are under 18. You must be able to attend the full camp.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps yet. Email the ORNL K-12 Education team (address on the SAGE page) or call 865-576-7658.
notes: The camp is at 1 Bethel Valley Road, Oak Ridge, TN 37830. Residency rules are not stated. Ask the K-12 team about cost and who can apply.
duration: About 1.5 weeks (July 12 to 22, 2027)
pay_detail: Pay and cost are not stated

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors interested in skilled trades and technical careers. No age range is given.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply yet. Contact the ORNL K-12 Education team (865-576-7658) or the contact listed on the Trades Camp page.
notes: The camp is at 1 Bethel Valley Road, Oak Ridge, TN 37830. Residency rules are not stated.
duration: 4 days
pay_detail: Pay and cost are not stated

who_can_apply: Must live in Oakland. No work experience needed. Free. Partner groups set their own ages (for example YEP 14 to 18, Youth UpRising 14 to 21, Lao Family 16 to 21).
how_to_apply: Pick a partner from the City list (YEP, Youth UpRising, Lao Family, Trybe, Rising Sun, Destiny Arts, Soccer Without Borders, YouthBeat, Alameda County Office of Education GCGI-GET) and apply on that group's site or by phone.
notes: City Council approved more than $3.1 million for 2026 and 2027 summer youth jobs, so a 2027 round is expected. Another City page lists ages 16 to 21, so check each partner's own age rule. Under-18 workers need a work permit (OUSD Linked Learning can help OUSD students).
duration: Up to 100 paid hours (varies by partner)
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage; exact rate set by each partner

who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per this City page.
how_to_apply: Contact Lao Family Community Development (510) 533-8850, Youth Employment Partnership (510) 533-3447, or Trybe (510) 985-9915. OWDB email: OWDB@oaklandca.gov.
notes: This City page is older than the MSYEP page (which lists partners with other ages, such as YEP 14 to 18 and Lao Family 16 to 21). Treat 16 to 21 as the safe range and confirm with the partner.
pay_detail: Not stated on this page; the City's MSYEP page says at least Oakland's minimum wage

who_can_apply: The City is hiring for its recreation jobs. The page does not state a minimum age. It strongly encourages people who speak Spanish, Cantonese and Mandarin to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply at governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca. Questions: parksandrec@oaklandca.gov or (510) 238-7275.
notes: The hiring process takes several months, so apply early. Check each posting for minimum age and pay. The governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca portal showed 0 openings on Oct 7, 2026. If you cannot find the posting, call (510) 238-7275.
duration: Varies by posting; mostly seasonal
pay_detail: Paid job. Not posted on the page; see each job posting

who_can_apply: Teens who join through the library teen volunteer application: ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. The TAB page itself states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and choose 'leadership', or ask your branch teen librarian.
notes: Meets monthly at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge. The same page also covers the Oakland Youth Poet Laureate program.
duration: One meeting a month

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. Also takes teens with court-ordered service hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application, or stop by a branch.
notes: The library cannot promise a spot at a specific branch. About two thirds of library volunteers are teens, per the page.
duration: Shifts when the library is open; the form asks for morning and afternoon or evening availability, any day of the week

who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade interested in animal care or environmental education.
how_to_apply: Online form with a cover letter (500 words max) and resume or transcript, then an interview.
notes: Up to 6 interns, so it is likely competitive. No stipend is listed; ask. Financial aid is available for the $50 fee.
duration: About 200 hours over 7 weeks (June 10 to July 28 or Aug 1 in 2026); shifts 9 am to 4:30 pm, Sunday to Wednesday or Wednesday to Saturday
pay_detail: $50 non-refundable fee when selected (aid available). No stipend is listed.

who_can_apply: Must be 13 or turning 13 in the application season.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, interview, then attend both mandatory training days.
notes: Unpaid, and teens pay a small fee (aid available). Must be 13 or turn 13 in the application season.
duration: School year: every other weekend. Summer: about once a week. Shifts 9:30 am to 4 pm.
pay_detail: $50 first year, then $25 a year; financial aid on request

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 for Teen Assistant (no experience needed). Paid Teacher and Administrative Intern roles are for grades 11 to 12 with previous camp experience and one letter of recommendation. All roles need at least 3 one-week sessions.
how_to_apply: Each role has its own online application (Volgistics link on the Oakland Zoo page). Interns also need one recommendation letter. A required training day is held in May.
notes: Great first step: be a Teen Assistant, then apply to be a paid intern. The 2026 info meetings were in March and the 2026 training was Sunday May 17; expect similar timing for 2027.
duration: 1-week sessions, Mon to Fri, June 1 to Aug 7 (2026); at least 3 sessions (Administrative Intern: 3 sessions in a row)
pay_detail: Teen Assistant unpaid (community service hours). Interns: $400 per week stipend, assuming full attendance.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. The page does not list a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: Email Alicia, the city staff contact named on the program page. Use the email link on that page. Ask how to join.
notes: Meetings are at the Oakley Recreation Center, 1250 O'Hara Avenue. The Teen page also mentions CORE Camp, a six-week summer camp that mixes camp games with community service. The Teen page does not give ages or dates for CORE Camp.
duration: Meets monthly, August to May
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. Income and home address rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Applications are not open yet. Check the Oak Futures page in spring 2027.
notes: The program page does not say where you must live. Ask before you apply.
duration: Nine weeks for the summer option; a year-round option also exists. Exact dates not stated.
pay_detail: Paid, part-time, 20 to 30 hours per week. Pay rate not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 to work at the annual OC Fair. Some jobs require 18 or older. Applicants 17 and under must provide a valid work permit, available through their school, unless they have already graduated from high school. You must show documents proving identity and work eligibility in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Read the Fair's jobs page, then contact Human Resources at (714) 708-1563 or humanresources@ocfair.com. The page lists no application link.
notes: The page does not describe an application link or a pay rate, so call or email HR to ask when summer 2027 hiring opens. Applicants 18 and older must pass a background screening.
duration: The OC Fair runs for a few weeks in summer. Fairgrounds also hosts 150+ events a year.
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Teens are typically 12 to 17, but each branch sets its own age range, so check with your local branch. Court-ordered community service is not offered.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch to confirm there is an opening. Once a spot is confirmed, fill out the OCCR Volunteer Registration Form, print it, and drop it off at the branch.
notes: The registration form is shared by several county agencies, so some questions may not apply to you. Ask your branch what it needs. Arrive on time and tell the branch as early as you can if you miss a shift. OC Public Libraries points teens who need court-ordered hours to the OneOC Court Referral Program.
duration: Flexible shifts, set by the branch
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: You must be 14 years old or entering 9th grade. You need basic sailing skills and should enjoy working with children.
how_to_apply: Check the class list and sign up online. For a scholarship, you must meet the eligibility requirements. Scholarship details are given at your interview. Call 949-645-9412 with questions.
notes: You can choose to take the written test for a Small Powerboat Certification. The program is at the OCC Waterfront Campus, 1801 West Coast Hwy, Newport Beach.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The fee is $525. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students, freshman through senior. You must apply before you can register.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CIT application on the program page. Then register for a session after you are accepted.
notes: This is a program you pay for. It is not a paid job. The same page lists a week-long Marine Science Careers and Internship Academy for ages 14 to 17.
duration: 3 weeks, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
pay_detail: $400, plus a 3% registration fee at checkout. Members at the Family level or above get 10% off.

who_can_apply: High school students and college students. You must be able to get to the Ocean Institute each week.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the summer 2027 opening. Then apply online. Last year, interviews ran from August 17 to September 4.
notes: Interns must go to all required workshops, the May poster session and the June showcase. They do not have to work on holiday weeks. Some projects need you to board the research vessel Sea Explorer on weekends.
duration: September to June, one 4-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Public Programs Docents must be 14 or older. Maritime Education Docents must be 16 or older. Other roles on the page are for ages 18 and up.
how_to_apply: When applications reopen, use the online form on the program page. Forms are reviewed three times a year. Then you have an interview and training.
notes: Public Programs Docents work at least two shifts a month on Saturday and Sunday, 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. or 12:00 to 3:00 p.m. Maritime Education Docents work shifts between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m., any day. If you get no confirmation email, submit the application again.
duration: At least 6 hours a month for at least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.

who_can_apply: Students age 15 or older and adults. You must volunteer for 6 months or more. No summer-only volunteering.
how_to_apply: Apply online, then email the volunteer reference form to OCHVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org. You will be contacted within two weeks for an interview. Then a 2-hour orientation, background check, health screening clearance and badging. Phone: 408-947-2830.
notes: Read on the official O'Connor Hospital page on 2026-10-16. Health screening asks for proof of a COVID-19 vaccine or booster, a yearly flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the past 3 months (then yearly). Start gathering shot records early. The page does not state weekly shift length or any fee. O'Connor is a sister hospital of Santa Clara Valley Medical Center. The email link on the page has a typo, so type OCHVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org by hand.
duration: 6 months or more

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. You must keep a 2.0 GPA or higher and be in good standing with school administrators. You cannot have arrests or convictions and cannot be on probation. You cannot have a severe mental or physical limit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Explorer Interest Form on the program page. Or call 714-566-2711 to learn more.
notes: The first police Explorer post in the US began in Santa Ana in 1959. The Sheriff also runs a Teen Academy for ages 16 to 18.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. Explorers are volunteers.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: To join the interest list, email TeenAcademy@ocsheriff.gov. In 2026, the flyer said to email your form to the same address.
notes: Space is limited. The service hours can count toward high school graduation rules. The flyer lists Community Engagement at 714-647-4141 for questions.
duration: 5 days, 8 a.m. to 12 p.m.
pay_detail: Free. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: In-school young adults ages 14 to 21 who are low income (free or reduced-price lunch counts) and have at least one barrier: basic skills deficient or English learner, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school (adult education is allowed) and have a barrier such as dropout, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the READY S.E.T. OC interest form (Interest and Eligibility Assessment) linked on the page. Services are delivered by a network of regional providers, which the page does not name.
notes: Federal WIOA program, so eligibility rules apply (income and barriers). Cost to the student is not stated on the page. Questions: County Directory Assistance 855-886-5400. Many teens will not qualify, so read the eligibility list first.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in Ogden City.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form at the bottom of the program page. Questions go to the Council Communications Director at 801-629-8103.
notes: This is a competitive process. Only the top rated applicants take part.
duration: The council meets 1 to 2 times each month.
pay_detail: No pay.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: First pay online and write down your confirmation number. Then fill out the application form linked on the program page. Print all documents before check in.
notes: The 2026 page listed 35 seats. Use the email on the program page for questions.
duration: 4 days (July 13 to 16 in 2026)
pay_detail: $350. This covers a t-shirt, lodging, meals and lab supplies.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. Graduating seniors can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Campers are picked in early May based on interest in business and a desire to learn. You can fill out the interest form to get an email when applications open.
notes: The page mentions dorm life for campers. The camp is hosted with the Utah Association of Certified Public Accountants.
duration: 4 days and 3 nights (June 8 to 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: No pay. The camp is free because of community sponsors.

who_can_apply: Eligibility is based on age and grade as of January 1 of the project year. Any youth age 9 or older can do a project, whatever the grade. Eligibility ends December 31 of the year you turn 19. You must join an authorized Ohio 4-H club or group.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office to be connected with a club. Go to a first meeting. Pick a project. Then enroll in 4-HOnline with your club volunteer or the county office. Do it before the county deadline.
notes: Club membership, not a paid job. The site menu has a Just for Teens section that was not read. The ohio4h.org home page was down (503) when tried, so only the join page was read.
duration: Project year
pay_detail: Membership fees are not stated on the page. Ask your county Extension office.

who_can_apply: Students who interview in their junior year for the next summer's program. That means incoming seniors from across Ohio. Local American Legion posts sponsor delegates. The pages do not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Ask a counselor, administrator or history teacher if a Legion post is interviewing at your school. If not, use the Apply or Become A Delegate form on the site. The program will match you with a post. Chosen delegates go to an orientation.
notes: Not a job. Office phone is 513-529-3860. The site describes the program as drawing over 1,200 young men a year.
duration: Eight days
pay_detail: No cost to the student or family when a local American Legion post sponsors you (stated on the Parent Information page).

who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a career-technical education program approved by the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's career-technical or business teacher about a DECA chapter. State questions go to the Ohio DECA advisor, Drew Goldfinger, at Drew.Goldfinger@education.ohio.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. Your school must have an approved career-technical program with a DECA chapter. The state website listed on the page is ohiodeca.org.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $16 per student member: $8 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Any Ohio student who is entering 9th grade through 12th grade, or freshman year of college, this fall.
how_to_apply: Pick the camp on the ExploreAg page and fill out its registration form. For questions, use the Contact Us page at ofbf.org/contact/.
notes: The Oct. 11 close date is figured from the "10 days prior" rule on the flyer, so check the Columbus registration page. Sign up on the page for email notices about future ExploreAg camps.
duration: One-day camps in fall (the weeklong camp is over for 2026)
pay_detail: Free to students. A deposit confirms your spot and is returned on the day of the program (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Students at schools with an Ohio FFA chapter. The membership page does not list grades or ages. Ask your chapter advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's FFA chapter advisor to add you. Chapters submit membership through FFA.org. Schools with no program can contact Ohio FFA about starting a chapter.
notes: Not a job. The homepage reports 30,880 members in 345 chapters. State office phone is (614) 387-7575. The September 30 and November 30 dates are chapter deadlines, so a student should ask the advisor early.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $17 per member covers State and National FFA dues. The school is invoiced by Ohio FFA. Local chapter dues are not stated.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders in any United States school can sign up for Science Adventurers or Horizons of Science. A third camp is for rising 5th to 8th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application and payment for each camp (separate forms on the page). Questions go to Tiffiny Rye-McCurdy at rye-mccurdy.1@osu.edu.
notes: This is at the Ohio State Marion campus, not in Columbus. The page mentions no housing or rides, so plan your own.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: $185 per camp, which includes lunch and lab costs (2026 price).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 20 who are now in a youth or career tech group. Examples are 4-H, FFA, DECA, Girl Scouts, Scouting America and Key Club. You need strong leadership and a record of being involved. Members serve one two-year term.
how_to_apply: Send the official Junior Fair Board application in the online portal on the Ohio State Fair page. Do it between January 1 and March 1. Interviews come next. Send questions to the co-coordinators listed on the page.
notes: The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for minors. Ask the coordinators.
duration: About 2 weeks (arrive the Monday before the Wednesday opening)
pay_detail: Flat-rate stipend, higher in the second year. The amount is not stated. Housing and meals are provided in dorms at the fair.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 through 17 who like animals and nature and enjoy talking with visitors. The page asks for at least 40 hours of volunteer service over the summer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button under Teen Volunteers on the volunteer page. It is an online form.
notes: The page says nothing about housing or rides.
duration: At least 40 hours through the summer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the unit locator. Visit with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ohio Wing office: 6031 E Main Street, PO Box 301, Columbus, OH 43213, phone 614-338-8198.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the page. Payment options are on the last page of the application.

who_can_apply: Middle school (6th to 8th) and high school (9th to 12th) students. You join through a local delegation run by a school or YMCA.
how_to_apply: Join or start a delegation at your school or YMCA in the fall. New delegations can email yg@ohioymcas.org or call (614) 407-4819. Students and advisors register on the State Assembly registration page.
notes: Not a job. The registration page still showed the 2026 assembly dates, so check it for the 2027 dates.
duration: Fall prep, then a 3-day State Assembly in spring
pay_detail: Registration fee amount is not stated on the program pages. A $25 late fee applied last year. Financial aid pages exist for middle and high school.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 19 during the program. You must be able to attend the whole season.
how_to_apply: Check the program page for the next application. Email dusty@goodgrub.org or call 360-753-5522.
notes: The farm is at 2016 Elliott Ave NW, Olympia. GRuB also runs other programs for teens and young adults, including GroundED for youth working on a GED.
duration: About 8 weeks, Tue and Thu 9 AM to 1 PM, Wed 11 AM to 5 PM (2026: July 7 to Aug 27)
pay_detail: Up to $1,000 educational stipend award, plus fresh farm food most weeks.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 pick the Teen Connection type on the application. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application form. Choose Teen Connection. For questions call Children's Nebraska. Use the phone number on the volunteer page.
notes: The application form asks for a Social Security number, a date of birth and an emergency contact. The same page also lists KIDS Nebraska. It is for young people ages 13 to 18 in Nebraska and western Iowa. No prior medical experience is needed.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. The application says services are donated and there is no payment.

who_can_apply: Current juniors at Omaha North, Omaha Central or Omaha South high school. You must be 16 or older by the start of the program. There are no exceptions. You need your own place to stay and a ride each day. You must go to every activity.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. A STEM teacher and a school counselor must also send in a review by the deadline.
notes: Only three Omaha high schools can apply. The poster session is typically held in early August. Start and end dates are Not stated on the program page.
duration: 8 weeks
pay_detail: Students can earn up to $4,800 for the hours they work.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18. Age is counted on January 1 of the 4-H year. You must be 8 by then for competitive events, large animal, shooting sports or food preservation projects.
how_to_apply: Join an existing club or start a new one. Then enroll online in 4HOnline. Call 402-444-7804 if you need help finding a club.
notes: A new club needs one trained 4-H volunteer and five youth from three different families. The page says enrollment in 4HOnline begins October 17. Clubs must meet at least six times per year.
duration: The 4-H year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30.
pay_detail: Enrollment fee is $10 per youth per year.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older, unless an adult comes with you. Some jobs need you to be 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form. Then you finish an application, an interview and training. This includes a background check.
notes: Quote from the page: Must be 16 years of age, unless accompanied by an adult. Check which roles are open to teens under 18.
duration: You must meet a minimum number of hours each year (the number is not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include a 25 percent museum shop discount and a 25 percent soda fountain discount on days you volunteer.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 and 8.
how_to_apply: Come back to the page on January 5, 2027 for application details.
notes: The 2026 Jr Crew program has concluded. Zoo Crew is for grades 9 to 12.
duration: Summer season. Exact length not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: High school students who love art and are committed to their education. Priority goes to students from schools not yet in the program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the program page. Staff interview applicants (mostly in March).
notes: Core program meets at Kent Bellows Studio, 3303 Leavenworth Street. Foundations meets at the Joslyn. The page also lists a Teen Pop-Up Market hosted by teens and an open call for youth ages 13 to 19.
duration: Twice a week: 4 to 6 pm in the school year, 3 to 6 pm in summer
pay_detail: Pay-as-you-are-able tuition of $1 to $600 per trimester. Supplies are provided.

who_can_apply: Incoming and current high school students in the Omaha metro area. You must commit to at least 1 year of service.
how_to_apply: Print the Volunteen form from the page and fill it out. Send it to the Volunteer Office.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the program page. The free meal on the page is listed under VIP perks. The page does not say it applies to Volunteens. Methodist Hospital and Methodist Women's Hospital may both have waiting lists.
duration: At least 1 year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free cafeteria meal on the day they volunteer.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who can commit to six months and 2 to 4 hours a week and finish orientation.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. Volunteer Services reviews it. They call you for a welcome meeting. You talk about what you like and when you can come. Then finish New Volunteer Orientation and onboarding.
notes: Quote from the page: Be at least 16 years old.
duration: Initial six-month commitment, 2 to 4 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 or older. Youth ages 11 to 18 need a parent or legal guardian to approve. The page does not list a city or school rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form. There is one form for Central Library and another for all other branches. Youth and summer reading volunteers need a parent or guardian signature before starting.
notes: The library says it may not be able to place each applicant. It has the right to reject any application without reason. It reserves the right to do a background check or check references. Quote from the volunteer policy: OPL accepts volunteers ages 11 and older. The Central Library has its own volunteer form. It is linked on the volunteer page.
duration: Short-term or ongoing, depending on the task
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library says it can provide volunteer hours for court-related community service.

who_can_apply: Omaha Public Schools sophomores, juniors and seniors who are on track to graduate. CNA students must be 16 by May of that year. EMT students must be seniors.
how_to_apply: Apply with your 6-digit student ID. The application is shared by QR code and email. Have your GPA, counselor name and email, top 2 pathways, and a list of activities and volunteer work ready.
notes: Only for OPS students. The page says the district provides bus transportation. The Career Center is at 3230 Burt Street, Omaha.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 21. The program page does not list city or school rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at StepUpOmaha.com. The news release says to apply there.
notes: This card uses the March 2026 news release on the organizer's site. Check StepUpOmaha.com for 2027 dates. The release says roughly 100 employers took part in 2025.
duration: 2026 program ran June 2 through July 31
pay_detail: Interns can earn $1,800 to $3,000 or more during the summer (2026 news release).

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors who are at least 16 at the start of the school year. Your school district must take part (districts around Omaha). You need grades of B or above in Algebra 1, Biology, a physical science and a third year of science. You also need parent permission and an interview.
how_to_apply: Check that you meet the criteria and that your school district takes part. Review the forms. Then apply online. Eligible students are scheduled for an interview. Then they are notified by email.
notes: The page says there are only 65 spots a year. Just one-third of applicants are accepted. Participating public school districts include Omaha, Millard, Bellevue, Elkhorn and Westside. They also include Council Bluffs Community Schools, Gretna, Bennington, Ralston and others. If you do not qualify, ask your teacher about uBEATS. It is an online alternative. Questions: 402-559-3027.
duration: Whole school year, August to May
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Students get three polo shirts and a jacket free and buy their own black pants, socks and closed-toe shoes.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 26 can help with Pediatric Programs. Students 16 and older can also help with Adult Programs.
how_to_apply: Email the volunteer coordinator. Their name is on the page. Then finish the required training.
notes: Training is on behavior and disability. It is on play and safety too. The institute also lists job shadowing for high school students.
duration: Opportunities are year-round. Camp Munroe runs in quarterly cycles: spring, summer, fall and winter.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors (when applying) with at least a 2.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must show you want to be a leader after you finish school.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Upload your unofficial high school transcript. Send one letter of recommendation. Write an essay of at least 300 words about two goals for the next five years.
notes: The same page also lists UNO Jumpstart. It is a 2 week program for graduating seniors who are already UNO students.
duration: The 2026 session ran May 26 to June 26, 2026.
pay_detail: Free. Tuition, fees, books and parking permits are covered for selected students.

who_can_apply: Tutors are ages 13 to 18, love working with young kids, have a B or higher in high school math, and bring a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up to volunteer on the OneInMath site. Use the register-volunteer page.
notes: The program pages do not list chapter locations. The tutor page's library news mentions North Texas libraries, so ask the group which library near you has a chapter. Re-check 2026-10-10: the tutor page does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week. Commit to at least one session, preferably a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked. Re-check 2026-10-10: the campus page does not say it is enrolling, and the Job Corps student page does not say applications are accepted on an ongoing basis, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling. The campus page footer shows 2023.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Students in high school, college, grad school or medical school who are interested in health care and innovation. You must be at least a high school freshman. You need to be on site 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CHOC website when the form opens. Interviews are rolling, so apply early. You are admitted by form and interview.
notes: The page links to a CHOC volunteer page but does not state its age rule here. Hospital and outpatient shadowing rotations are 18 and up. Business casual dress is expected.
duration: About 8 weeks, June 15 to Aug 7 (2026 dates). Monday to Thursday plus Friday field trips.
pay_detail: No cost to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page. Meals, housing and travel are on you; help for low-income students may be available.

who_can_apply: Girls in 9th to 12th grade. The four-week externship is for 11th grade girls.
how_to_apply: The page has a Contact Us link. Ask the Girls Inc. Programs Team how girls sign up.
notes: For girls only. Past host companies named on the page include PepsiCo, Edwards Lifesciences and Disneyland Resort. Confirm dates with Girls Inc. first. The 2026 host flyer says girls get a minimum of 50 hours of training; the page says up to 40, so ask Girls Inc. which is current.
duration: Four-month program with a four-week externship (the 2026 externship was in July)
pay_detail: Free to join. The page does not say the externship is paid.

who_can_apply: Current high school students. You need a parent consent form and one Dual Enrollment Release Form. Concurrent students also submit a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form from their high school every term. High school students cannot register for a college class without a valid release form on file.
how_to_apply: Apply to Golden West College (new students create an Open CCC account) and write down your CCCID number. Then turn in the consent forms and get your high school's approval.
