Dual enrollment classes are taught at your high school, so your counselor adds you to the roster. Concurrent students use a Concurrent Enrollment Release Form and register in MyGWC. Questions: dualenrollment@gwc.cccd.edu.
notes: The consent form also covers Coastline College and Orange Coast College in the same district. Only one parent consent form is needed for all high school years. The page says tuition is free, but students may still owe college fees and course costs. It offers a Foundation financial aid form and a possible fee waiver. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page says it is now accepting applications and consent forms for Fall 2026, with no closing date posted. Fetched by curl after a certificate error.
duration: By term: fall, winter/spring and summer
pay_detail: Tuition is free. Dual enrollment classes taught at a high school are free; concurrent students pay college fees and books unless their district covers them. A limited number of help grants are offered.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors from anywhere in Orange County. The 2025-26 group came from 9 school districts and was chosen from over 100 applicants.
how_to_apply: Application steps are not listed on the pages. Email langsonteens@uci.edu to ask.
notes: The museum is named UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art on the page. Confirm dates and any stipend with the museum first.
duration: One school year; the 2025-26 exhibition opens in June 2026
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14. You need a set schedule and must complete an application. Adults also complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out a volunteer application. Sign in with the Volunteer Coordinator for each shift. Training is given.
notes: The county document is titled 2024, so confirm shifts and openings with the library before you go. Main branch only: 137 W. Margaret Lane, Hillsborough. Re-check 2026-10-10: the county PDF matches the age, schedule, application and background check terms. It says nothing about ongoing intake or a 2026 date, so the status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: 1 or 2 hour shifts, Monday to Friday 10am to 5pm, as spaces are available
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 18, or 16 with parent permission. You must pass a background check and give at least 36 hours a year. The page does not give a separate age rule for OC Zoo roles.
how_to_apply: Complete the brief interest form linked from the OC Parks Volunteers page and tell them the work that interests you. Pass a background check and attend training. For short term opportunities, search the activity listing. Questions: volunteer@ocparks.com.
notes: Volunteers 16 with parent permission (the page does not mention 17). The page lists historic docent, backcountry patrol and OC Zoo roles. It lists others too. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page gives no sign-up deadline and does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: Long term; at least 36 hours a year. The page also lists short term volunteer opportunities.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who want to take their leadership to the next level. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Apply in spring. The page does not link a form, so email Nadia Khodadadi at OC Pathways (address on the page) to ask how to apply.
notes: Ask your school CTE teacher or counselor too. Confirm the spring dates with OC Pathways.
duration: One school year, built around a year-long Impact Project
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with a 2.0 GPA or higher, no arrests or convictions, and fire-safe grooming. Anyone over 18 also does a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the OCFA site to join the interest list. Later, people on the list are asked to finish a longer form.
notes: OCFA serves many Orange County cities. Ask which cadet post is nearest to you.
duration: 10 week Fire Cadet Trainee Academy (9 weeks at cadet posts, final exam in week 10)
pay_detail: Not stated; described as a community-based youth program

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 who live in Orange County. You must be in foster care, extended foster care or Kin-GAP. That means a current or past Orange County dependent. Young adults on probation may also qualify.
how_to_apply: Ask your social worker for an ILP referral. You can also call Orangewood at 714-619-0200 or visit the Orangewood Resource Center, 1575 E. 17th Street, Santa Ana.
notes: Orangewood's Lyon Workforce Academy is a separate program, so it is not listed here. The OC Social Services Agency pays for part of the program. Call to ask about cost.
duration: Nine months of case management
pay_detail: Not a job. Workshops may earn gift card incentives. The page does not say whether the program is free.

who_can_apply: High school students, called special admit students. Students in grades K to 8 need approval from a Santa Ana College dean.
how_to_apply: Use the New Students page on the Dual Enrollment site. Contact the Dual Enrollment Office at dualenrollment@sac.edu or (714) 564-6931.
notes: If you go over the unit limit you pay the enrollment fee for all units, not only the extra ones. The office is closed on Fridays in summer. Re-check 2026-10-10: the page says the program is active. It gives no term dates, no deadline, and no word that applications are taken on an ongoing basis. So the status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: The enrollment fee is waived for part-time special admit students (under 12 units, or 15 units or fewer from partner schools). Other costs are not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 19. The page says there are no exceptions to the age rule. A parent or guardian must consent if you are under 18.
how_to_apply: Check the County of Orange volunteer page in spring 2027 and apply there. Questions: SSATeenVolunteers@ssa.ocgov.com.
notes: You must dress in neat business clothes. There are several office sites. The addresses are on the application form. Volunteers sign a promise to keep client facts private.
duration: About 6 weeks, roughly June to August, up to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work experience.

who_can_apply: High school students (special admit students). Students in grades K to 8 need approval from an SCC division dean. High school students sign up through the SCC Dual Enrollment Portal.
how_to_apply: Apply to SCC. Make your dual enrollment profile in the portal with your SCC student email. Send a course request. Then confirm your enrollment. Phone (714) 628-4764 or earlycollege@sccollege.edu.
notes: SCC is phasing out the paper Special Admit Form for high school dual enrollment. It now goes through the portal.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: The page says free transferable college units. Fees for books or other costs are not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who were in 4-H in the 2025-26 year (member, camp, event or in-school program) and have not attended a national 4-H event before. Must be able to travel to DC in March 2027 and to Portland airport. Oregon youth join a chaperoned group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form and upload a 2 to 4 minute video at beav.es/ignite2027 answering the prompt on the page. Do not use the national 4-h.org site.
notes: Requests for disability help are due Oct 31, 2026. This is a 4-H event named Ignite. It is not the same as the Ignition youth conference.
pay_detail: Event page lists $300. A donor covers a large part of the conference cost and airfare.

who_can_apply: County Ambassadors: contact your local 4-H office for rules. State Ambassadors: 4-H youth in the Senior age division who have been in 4-H at least one year. The page does not give the Senior division ages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application (a fillable PDF) and upload it with the Qualtrics form. Ask your 4-H volunteer or office to review it first. Finalists interview at Summer Conference in Corvallis.
notes: The page says the 2026-2027 Ambassadors are announced on the last night of Summer Conference. The page does not give the Senior division ages. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: One 4-H year
pay_detail: Unpaid leadership role

who_can_apply: Oregon 7th to 12th graders. You do not have to be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens (about mid-May). Choose your workshops when you register. Watch for emails from your county 4-H program about financial help.
notes: 2026 dates were June 24 to 27 and registration opened May 15, 2026 at 3:00 pm. Buses leave from several Oregon towns for an added fee. 2027 dates not posted.
duration: 4 days (June 24 to 27 in 2026)
pay_detail: $275 registration fee plus a bus fee if you ride the bus. Financial assistance and transportation help are available through your local 4-H program.

who_can_apply: Oregon youth. Check with your local 4-H program coordinator to find a club and project that fit your area.
how_to_apply: Contact your local 4-H program coordinator. They will help you find a club. Then sign up online in 4-HOnline. Or return the paper forms to your county 4-H office.
notes: The page was written for the 2025-2026 4-H year. Not every project is offered in every county, since it depends on volunteers. To join in another county, you need an Out of County Participation Form.
duration: 4-H year starts October 1
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county 4-H office about enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17 who want a summer farm or ranch job. You must attend every session of your class.
how_to_apply: Pick a county class on the page and use its register link. Or contact Andrea Leao or your local Extension office.
notes: The page says Oregon requires farmers and ranchers who hire minors under 18 to be sure those minors passed tractor safety training. That is the page's own statement. Ask your boss. 2026 sites included Linn, Marion, Clackamas and Jefferson counties.
duration: 22 hours over 2 to 3 dates
pay_detail: $75 in most counties and $95 in Clackamas County (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Utah high school students in grades 9 to 11. The page says it is especially for first-generation college learners.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Share your interests, your goals and why you want to join. The application asks for short written responses, which carry strong weight. The team picks students by readiness, interest and fit. Applications can also go on the waitlist.
notes: You must go in person. Classes also have homework outside class time. Track choice is not guaranteed. Questions: text 801-928-7615. The page says you may be added to a contact list for future openings.
duration: 7 weeks. Tuesdays to Thursdays, 9:00 AM to 3:15 PM (June 24 to Aug 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: No pay. Tuition is free for admitted students. You pay for your own rides, lunches and personal costs.

who_can_apply: High school students and young creatives ages 14.5 to 19. No grade level is listed.
how_to_apply: Use Register Now on the Summer of Art page. Questions: soa@otis.edu or 310-665-6850. Scholarships have their own application.
notes: The page says ages 14.5 to 19; min_age is entered as 14 because the field takes whole years. Costs money. Prices shown are the 2026 numbers. In 2026 the early discount deadline was April 25. The April 16, 2027 date is the scholarship deadline, not the registration deadline.
duration: 4 weeks in July 2027. The main page says July 7 to 30; the dates page says orientation July 6, classes July 8 to July 30.
pay_detail: 2026 prices as posted: $4,390 full program (3 college credits) or $2,690 per individual class; $7,315 or $5,615 with housing. A $150 health center fee applies. 2027 prices are not posted.

who_can_apply: OUSD students (the page also says Alameda County high school students for the Peralta Summer Institute). Some internships are open to all; others go through your career pathway.
how_to_apply: Fill out the district Summer Internship Common Application. It is a Google Form linked on the OUSD page. For school-year internships, ask your pathway lead teacher or your school's work-based learning lead.
notes: The OUSD page still shows Summer 2024 forms, so look for a new form in January 2027. Not every internship is open to every student.
duration: Varies by employer
pay_detail: Summer internships are paid; amounts vary by employer (see the district list). The district's 2024 listing said Peralta Summer Institute students got a stipend; the current Peralta page only says classes are free.

who_can_apply: OUSD high school students.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Linked Learning or pathway coordinator, or call the district at (510) 879-8000. The office also processes work permits for students.
notes: The office handles work permits (needed for any paid job under 18). Check the pathways pages on the OUSD site to find work-based learning at your school.
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)

who_can_apply: Lifeguard I: at least 15 years old with an 8th grade education. You also need the city's Starguard lifeguard certification. Lifeguard II is 16 and up with one year of experience in Overland Park. Lifeguard III is 17 and up with two years.
how_to_apply: The job description does not say how to apply. It requires Starguard certification from the City of Overland Park. The course is the Starguard Lifeguard Course.
notes: Quote from the job description: a minimum of 15 years of age. The job description does not state pay. Current postings and pay were not on the program page.
duration: Seasonal. Exact season dates not stated on the job description.
pay_detail: Not stated on the job description

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17 for two roles. They are Junior Docent and Junior Outreach Assistant.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now for the Junior Docent or Junior Outreach Assistant role. The center reviews forms and then gets back to you.
notes: The page says most volunteer roles are for ages 18 and up. Use the Contact Us button on the page for questions.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who live in the Northeast San Fernando Valley. It is hard to get in. A parent or guardian must come to a required orientation.
how_to_apply: Not open now. If you have questions, write to aguau@pacoimabeautiful.org or call 818-899-2454.
notes: Pacoima Beautiful also lists Bee Wise, Agua Academy and YUTEP on its youth page. No details were posted for them.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM, 20 sessions (2026: June 15 to July 10)
pay_detail: The page does not mention pay. It says students earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in the Northeast San Fernando Valley with a 2.0 GPA or higher. Returning participants are not eligible. No age range is listed.
how_to_apply: Not open now. Selected students must provide a valid high school work permit. Questions: jfr@pacoimabeautiful.org or 818-899-2454.
notes: Classes run 8:00 AM to 2:30 PM and field days 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Dates may change each year.
duration: 6 weeks. 2026 ran with a June 5 orientation and a culmination on July 10, 2026.
pay_detail: Paid opportunity with up to 70 working hours. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in the grades listed for each role. You must finish the volunteer application and have it accepted before you can sign up for events.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Now on the volunteer page and finish the form. Then sign up for service projects on the events calendar.
notes: Service projects sign-up opens two weeks before each event.
duration: Member Services needs at least 20 hours. Teen Advisory Board meets monthly in the school year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn service hours (for example 2 hours for each accepted book review).

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. Morning or afternoon sessions.
how_to_apply: Register for a CIT or Lead CIT spot when Enjoy! summer camp registration opens on Feb 4, 2027. To get on the teen volunteer email list, email rebecca.passarello@paloalto.gov.
notes: Same page lists the Ceramics Apprentice Program (16 and older, 2 years of Art Center ceramics or instructor approval, 2 hours a week, one training session). Spots may fill fast once registration opens.
duration: At least 1 week

who_can_apply: Grades 8 to 12. Rising 8th graders can join in summer. You must live or go to school in Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Mountain View, Los Altos, Los Altos Hills, Portola Valley or East Palo Alto.
how_to_apply: Submit the TLAB volunteer application in Better Impact, finish the paperwork in Docusign, then go to an in-person Livescan fingerprint appointment. Contact libraryteens@paloalto.gov.
notes: Fingerprinting is required. Log your hours in Better Impact or the library cannot confirm them.
duration: Fall (Sept to Dec), Winter/Spring (Jan to May) and Summer (June to Aug) terms

who_can_apply: High school students. Needs an online application, a letter of recommendation (returning members are exempt), an intro video and an interview with a nominating committee. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, recommendation letter and intro video by the deadline, then interview with the nominating committee.
notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

who_can_apply: High school students. Needs an online application, a letter of recommendation (returning members are exempt), an intro video and an interview with a nominating committee. Residency rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Online application, recommendation letter, intro video, then an interview with the nominating committee, once applications open.
notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Dual enrollment is only at partner schools. These are in the Arcadia, El Monte Union (Rosemead High), La Canada, Pasadena, San Gabriel, San Marino, South Pasadena and Temple City districts. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Apply at OpenCCCApply. Pick courses with your counselor. Then send the Recommendation form. A counselor and a parent sign it. If you are under 18, send the Medical Consent form too. Send your latest unofficial transcript as well. Then turn on your LancerPoint account and register. Questions: outreach@pasadena.edu.
notes: Do not email documents to the outreach address; upload them as the page says. Check with your counselor which classes your school offers.
duration: By term. Fall 2026 runs 8/24/26 to 12/13/26.
pay_detail: Fees and fee waivers are not stated on the program pages. Ask outreach@pasadena.edu.

who_can_apply: Volunteer jobs are for ages 15 and over. Ambassador is open at 14 with a parent or guardian. Anyone under 15 must have a parent or guardian who also volunteers at all times.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a coming virtual orientation on the volunteer page. Then go to the training for each job you pick.
notes: The page does not say which roles are only for adults. Kids ages 6 to 14 have separate roles (Shelter Greeter, Boredom Busters). Those need a parent who volunteers too.
duration: At least 2 hours a month for at least 12 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 and up who live or go to school in Pasadena.
how_to_apply: Send your writing or art to the teen librarian (email on the page). To help with the magazine, fill out the library's Teen Volunteer Application. Limits: poetry up to 40 lines, short fiction up to 1,000 words, book reviews 250 to 500 words.
notes: The library page does not say the age rule for the Teen Volunteer Application, so ask the teen librarian. Teen librarian contact is on the page. The page does not say whether contributors are paid.
duration: Ongoing; the library publishes issues from time to time (Spring 2026 was Issue 1)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You are published, not paid.

who_can_apply: Students from Clifton or Paterson who will be in 10th, 11th or 12th grade in September 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form. Have a recommendation form sent for you. Go to a Teen Summer Program Info Session.
notes: The page gives grades, not ages. 2027 applications open in early spring 2027. You must go to a Teen Summer Program Info Session to apply.
duration: About June 30 to Aug 18, 3 to 4 days a week, 8:30 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $15.92 per hour (2026), daily lunch, weekly bag of produce, rides between sites

who_can_apply: Any child ages 5 to 18 who lives in Pennsylvania. Ages 8 to 18 (before January 1 of the current year) can join the program and take part in contests. Ages 5 to 7 are Cloverbuds. They do non-competitive activities.
how_to_apply: Look up your county 4-H program. Pick a club. Talk with your county educator. Then sign up in 4-H's ZSuite. If you cannot enroll online, ask the educator for help.
notes: A youth group, not a job. Ask your county educator what clubs and teen leader roles are near you.
duration: Ongoing club membership
pay_detail: Members pay a fee for educational materials. Extra fees vary by county and project area. Financial help is available. Amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. If your school has no chapter, you can join the Virtual Chapter. It is open if you are homeschooled or in a cyber charter, private or charter school. It is also open if your school has no FBLA chapter. The Virtual Chapter page says members must take a business class. Students at schools with an active FBLA chapter cannot join it.
how_to_apply: Ask your chapter adviser at school. If you do not know who that is, contact Bruce Boncal, PA FBLA Executive Director, bboncal@pafbla.us. Virtual Chapter members fill out an online application signed by a parent.
notes: Virtual Chapter members pay their own travel costs. State office: (570) 398-4652, stateoffice@pafbla.us.
duration: School year; the 2027 State Leadership Conference is April 12 to 14, 2027 at the Hershey Lodge and Giant Center
pay_detail: Yearly dues $18 for high school ($10 national and $8 state). Virtual Chapter dues are $16.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education at a school with an FFA chapter. All students in agricultural education are on the official roster. The page does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Sign up for agricultural education at a school that has an FFA chapter. Use the Chapter Locator on the Pennsylvania FFA site to find one near you.
notes: The state page says nearly 16,000 students are members, in four regions. Members compete at chapter, regional, state and national events. The National FFA Organization has its own listing in other cards. This one is the Pennsylvania state page.
duration: Ongoing while you are in agricultural education
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 in Pennsylvania: public, private, parochial or home schooled. You need an adult sponsor (a teacher, parent or scientist). You must do your own research and your own presentation.
how_to_apply: Pick a research category. Find a sponsor. Use the Find Your Region page for your region's deadlines, forms and location. Turn in any required SRC/IRB approval forms.
notes: A science fair, not a job. Your project may need extra approval forms depending on your research field, so ask your sponsor or Regional Director early. Regional pages list the exact deadlines.
duration: Regional meets January to March; State Meet in May (2026: May 17 to 19)
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Check your region page for fees.

who_can_apply: Boys who live in Pennsylvania, have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character and school service count.
how_to_apply: Register online on the Keystone Boys State site when registration opens. Posts also sponsor students; use the Legion post locator on the Pennsylvania Legion page.
notes: Boys only. A matching Girls State program is run by the American Legion Auxiliary, not this one. Check the Boys State site for the 2027 location and dates, because 2026 was at Messiah University.
duration: One week (2026 session ran Sunday June 14 to Saturday June 20)
pay_detail: No pay. American Legion posts and the Department pay the fees, so little or no cost to the family.

who_can_apply: Girls in Pennsylvania. The pages do not state grade, citizenship or cost rules, so check the application.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply tab on the Keystone Girls State site (the home page links an application for 2027). The old FAQ says to print and mail the form, then fill out a parent packet before camp. Check with a local Auxiliary unit for sponsorship.
notes: Girls only. The FAQ on the site is still from 2023, so confirm this year's dates, deadline and cost with the program before you plan. The national Auxiliary list shows June 21 to June 26, 2026 while the state site shows 20-25 June 2026.
duration: One week in June
pay_detail: No pay. The page says it is free in most cases; you may pay only for your own travel to Shippensburg University. Bring some cash for snacks and shirts sold during the week.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 at the start of the program. High school students. Crews are based in cities across Pennsylvania.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Student Conservation Association (SCA) website. The state page links to the current openings. It links to the application too. You can email paoutdoorcorps@thesca.org.
notes: Crew locations change by year; check the SCA page for this year's list. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (2026: June 29 to August 7)
pay_detail: $17.31 per hour (2026). Lunch, safety gear and daily transport from a central meeting spot in your city are provided.

who_can_apply: Pennsylvania residents who are in 11th grade when they apply.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a 15-minute Zoom interview. Contact PSEAS@psu.edu or 814-867-0383. The page also lists PGSAS@psu.edu, so confirm the address.
notes: No wage is paid. Page lists a contact email in two spellings, so confirm it.
duration: 2 weeks. Session 1: June 20 to July 2, 2027. Session 2: July 11 to 24, 2027.
pay_detail: No pay. Free for selected students: tuition, room, board, materials and activities are covered.

who_can_apply: High school students from Oakland, Berkeley and Alameda. You need counselor and parent or guardian signatures on the High School Special Enrollment Form.
how_to_apply: Meet your counselor. Apply to a Peralta college. Turn in the High School Special Enrollment Form, a transcript and photo ID. Meet a college counselor. Then register.
notes: Peralta also runs a free Summer Institute for Bay Area high schoolers, including incoming 9th graders. The 2026 dates were June 22 to July 31. No application deadline is posted. The old OUSD page mentions a stipend. The Peralta page does not.
duration: Per term (fall, spring, summer)
pay_detail: Tuition and fees excused. Unit caps: CCAP 15 units fall or spring; other dual enrollment 11 units fall or spring; 9 units in summer.

who_can_apply: Prince George's County youth and young adults ages 14 to 24 (your age as of the program start date picks which application you fill out). Placements are by random lottery.
how_to_apply: Apply online during March through the county's NEOGOV job site, choosing the application for your age group (14 and 15, 16 and 17, or 18 to 24). Eligible applicants go into a random lottery. Ages 18 to 24 are encouraged to attach a resume. Questions: syep@co.pg.md.us.
notes: Not everyone gets a job. To get ready, set up an email and voicemail, open a bank account, and have your Social Security Number and address ready. Teens who did SYEP can later try the county's Youth@Work Internship at 18. In Maryland, all teens under 18 need a work permit after they get a job offer.
duration: 6 weeks (Jul 6 to Aug 14 in 2026)
pay_detail: Paid. Some placements are hourly and some are stipends; the county page does not state a rate.

who_can_apply: Youth must reach the required age on or before May 31. It is 14 for Summer Playtime and 15 for Summer Day Camps. Youth cannot volunteer at a site where a younger sibling or child is a registered participant. Ages 15 and older need a criminal background history check.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Volunteer Opportunities page of pgparks.com. Each youth may volunteer at only one Summer Playtime or Summer Day Camp site. Transportation is not provided.
notes: Dates for the 2027 season are not posted on the page. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: 12 to 15 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Approved for Prince George's County Public Schools Student Service Learning hours.

who_can_apply: About 20 high school-age youth who live in Prince George's County. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Email your name, resume, school information and a list of extracurricular activities to Stephen.Makle@pgparks.com. The page names him as the contact.
notes: The same page lists other teen programs (Teen Arts Council, Teen Vocal Showcase for ages 10 to 18, Teen Nights for ages 10 to 17). Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: School year; meetings in person at community centers and online
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn student service learning credits or community service hours.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 14 (library system rule). VolunTEEN is for grades 6 to 12. The Kids Achieve Club welcomes teens over 15. Volunteers cannot staff the Circulation or Information desks.
how_to_apply: Get a volunteer application from your local branch. Ask for the volunteer coordinator. For VolunTEEN, sign up through the Beanstack app.
notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.
duration: Temporary (limited) or regular (at least 6 months) schedules
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student service learning hours are available.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 14. The page lists no teen-specific roles; ask which positions accept teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.
duration: Regular time from half a day to several days a week, for at least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. The page describes Teen Podcast as a program for Philly teens. The page does not list ages or a school-district rule for Teen Sketch.
how_to_apply: Each program has its own Apply now link (a Google form) on the teens page. Questions: teens@philamuseum.org.
notes: The page does not say whether the programs are paid or free, or when the forms close. Email the teen team before you plan around it. The museum also ran A Future of Artists, a June to August 2026 exhibition of work by Philadelphia-area high school students.
duration: Fall 2026 programs. Teen Sketch length is not stated.
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Awbury Adventures Summer Camp page. Ask for financial aid BEFORE you sign up, because aid spots are few.
notes: This is training, not a paid job. The page does not say whether graduates get counselor jobs. A 2021 posting on the same site said 2 to 6 trainees were chosen as stipend-paid counselors in training; that is old, so ask.
duration: 2 weeks (June 15 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 price was $675 ($641 for members) for the 2 week session. The camp page says scholarships (75% off) and sliding scale fees (30% to 60% off) are available to families in local zip codes.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors ages 14 to 18. You must live, go to school or have other ties in Southwest Philadelphia. Priority goes to 49th to 65th Streets between Chester Avenue and the river. You must have a work permit or be able to get one.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with short written answers. Then you have an in-person interview. If you are hired, you sign up for the city C2L-PHL program. It needs a Social Security card, an ID, proof of citizenship and Philadelphia home address, and a W-9.
notes: Competitive: about 50 students a year across all programs. The page still showed 2025-26 dates when read, so check it for the 2026-27 deadline. The Garden will never ask for birth dates or Social Security numbers by text message.
duration: October to spring in the 2025-26 cycle; some interns continue in summer.
pay_detail: $11 to $12.50 per hour in 2025-26; 8.5 hours a week in the school year. Some interns can continue in summer at 20 hours a week.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in Philadelphia. The page does not state an age range or residency proof.
how_to_apply: The page gives no intern application steps. Contact info@philaculture.org or 215-557-7811.
notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the page.
duration: Eight weeks, up to 35 hours a week (2026: June 19 to August 14); select interns may continue in a school-year program up to 10 hours a week
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support

who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. In-school youth get priority. You can apply to one program per cycle.
how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Summer program (plus school-year programming)
pay_detail: Stipend on a prepaid debit card, paid every other week; total $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program (hourly rate not listed).

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Contact the squadron: cc214@pawg.cap.gov (squadron commander) or 215-531-2278. The wing's Join CAP page has the cadet steps.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists five other squadrons in the Philadelphia area. They are Willow Grove, Liberty, Griffin, Gen Carl A Spaatz and Chester County. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets Fridays from 7:00 to 9:15 p.m. at the Naval Support Activity Center, 700 Robbins St, Philadelphia, PA 19111.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Drop in at 719 Catharine St, or email cy@fleisher.org.
notes: Not a job. Lead support from the William Penn Foundation and others is listed on the page.
duration: Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 4 to 6 pm, while Philadelphia schools are in session. Fall 2026 workshops start Sept 8.
pay_detail: Free. No attendance requirement. Snacks and bus passes provided.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8 who live in the Philadelphia area.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to the PACTS Program online form on the page.
notes: For younger teens (grades 6 to 8). Older teens can join the Franklin Ambassador program through STEM Scholars, which has its own card.
duration: School year, workshops meet twice a month on Saturday mornings
pay_detail: Free program.

who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12. The library says all volunteers must be at least 14 years old.
how_to_apply: Print the form and fill it out. Email it to volunteer@freelibrary.org or mail it to 1901 Vine Street. Then staff will set up a talk with you.
notes: The page asks for age 14 and up but also says grades 7 to 12, so younger 7th graders should call first. For a paid role, the library's LEAP after-school program hires Teen Leadership Assistants through Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L PHL). Questions: 215-686-5340.
duration: At least 1 to 3 hours a week for 2 to 3 months. Some seasonal and short-term roles are listed too.

who_can_apply: Philadelphia teens about to enter grades 10 to 12 who go to a high school in the city. You must be allowed to work in Philadelphia. If you are under 18, you must be able to get a work permit. You must be free for the whole program. It runs June through August, plus some Saturdays in September.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form linked from the page. Early applications get interviews first.
notes: Funded by The W.W. Smith Charitable Trust and The Hamilton Family Charitable Trust, both named on the page.
duration: June through August, plus select Saturdays in September
pay_detail: Described as a ten-week paid work and learning experience. The hourly rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone 16 or older who has the shots and health checks Jefferson asks for.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form on the volunteer page. If they pick you, the hospital checks your record. You fill out some papers and show your shots: chicken pox, MMR, Tdap, a new TB blood test, and a flu shot in flu season.
notes: Volunteering here does not lead to a job, but it is health care experience for your resume. Shadowing is possible only if you find a staff member to supervise you yourself. Jefferson's Center City hospitals (TJUH and Methodist) take volunteers 18 and up only. Questions: 215-481-2492.
duration: Most assignments need at least 2 to 4 hours a week. Some late afternoon, evening or weekend shifts.

who_can_apply: Students 16 or older who can keep a regular weekly shift. Needs two school references from teachers and proof of vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella and a TB test).
how_to_apply: Send the application, two letters of support from teachers and shot forms to the Volunteer Services Department. You can send by mail, scan, fax or email. Phone: 215-612-4170.
notes: Facts come from the 2024 application packet on the Jefferson site. The program web page shows only its title (checked 2026-10-09 with a normal fetch and with curl), so the age, time, pay and how-to-apply details are not confirmed on the page. Confirm the current dates, ages and form first. Spots are limited.
duration: 8 weeks, 4 hours a day, one day a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get their own transportation.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: the Philadelphia campus page lists transportation and no dorms. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists transportation to and from campus, breakfast and lunch, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Students now in high school or college from the greater Philadelphia area, including Camden, NJ. You must be able to prove you can work in the United States. No age or grade is stated. The committee gives strong preference to students from groups underrepresented in science.
how_to_apply: Use the MSAP Applications page on monell.org when it opens. Sign up for Monell's newsletter for updates. Questions: AcademicAffairs@monell.org or 267-519-4700. About 200 applications come in each year. 18 to 24 students are usually enrolled.
notes: Minors do not need working papers to apply. They must get them after they are admitted. They come from the School District of Philadelphia, per the Monell FAQ. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. Monell does not provide housing or meals. Students must commit to the full program with no vacations.
duration: The program page says eight weeks of paid full-time structured research. The 2026 program ran June 15 to July 31, 2026, which is shorter than eight weeks, so confirm the length. The page does not give the 2027 dates.
pay_detail: Described as paid. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 22 at the high school sites. Ages 10 to 13 are served at middle school sites. A parent or guardian must sign and provide extra information before a youth under 18 can be enrolled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Inquiry Form on the Mural Arts enroll page. It is not an application and does not confirm enrollment. An Art Education staff member follows up about classes near you. Contact: natalie.gearin@muralarts.org or (215) 685-0750.
notes: The pages say 3 high school sites and 6 middle school sites on the enroll page but 16 sites in total on the page, so ask which site is near you. Mural Arts also has paid summer work experience through Career Connected Learning (see the C2L PHL card). Ask whether classes are free. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Twice a week. The fall session begins in late September 2026. The page gives no end date.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program pages. The page says students can later apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. You must be able to go on weekdays for the whole program. You must live close enough to the museum to travel there each day.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Contact the museum education team through the museum website.
notes: This is a small program. The 2023 press release said eight took part. It is part of the museum's African American Interpretive Program. Check the museum site for the next call for applications.
duration: 6 weeks, weekdays (the 2023 session ran July 5 to August 11)
pay_detail: The page says it is a paid six-week program. The pay amount is not stated. Public transportation help is offered.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the Youth Council page, which goes to pafa-museum.coursestorm.com. Each session has its own Register link.
notes: PAFA is on North Broad Street. The status is shown as open because the page lists a Register link for both sessions; the page gives no closing date.
duration: Fall 2026: Wednesdays Oct 21 to Dec 9, 4 to 6 pm. Spring 2027: Wednesdays Jan 27 to Apr 14, 4 to 6 pm.
pay_detail: Free to join. No pay or stipend is stated.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24. Residency is not stated on this page (the parent C2L-PHL program requires Philadelphia residency).
how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Students who live in Philadelphia. You must go to a Philadelphia public, Catholic, private or charter high school. You need a minimum GPA of 3.0.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the program site when it opens in January 2027. You will need a high school transcript with fall 2026 grades. You need a 250 word essay about yourself and your interest in the program. You need an up to date vaccine record.
notes: The two pages word the grade rule differently (currently 9th or 10th on the apply page, entering 10th or 11th in fall 2027 on the main page); they describe the same group. Office: St. Leonard's Court, Suite 110, 3819 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104; contact form at https://vpse.upenn.edu/smp/contact-us/.
duration: Four weeks, on campus. Exact summer 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the program pages, so ask the program before you plan around either.

who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders (Pre-College: 10th to 11th).
how_to_apply: Online application from the student: essays (400 words each), transcript, recommendations. For the scholarship, say you attend a School District of Philadelphia school and fill in the scholarship section.
notes: There are no scholarships for the Pre-College programs. Contact hsprogs@sas.upenn.edu or 215-746-2309.
duration: 2 to 6 weeks depending on program (2026 Academies: July 11 to August 1)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: 2-week Academy $6,700; 3-week Academy $10,050; Pre-College Residential $15,192 to $23,604; Pre-College Online $8,692 or $14,300; Online Seminars $2,950. $1,500 deposit and $100 application fee (waived for School District of Philadelphia applicants).

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 17. The program targets high school students interested in health care, but all students are invited to apply.
how_to_apply: Starting February 1, 2027, create an account in the Penn Medicine volunteer portal and apply. More details will be posted closer to that date.
notes: It is only at the 800 Spruce Street site. Spots fill fast. Email PAHVolunteerServices@pennmedicine.upenn.edu or call 215-829-5187.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who want a law enforcement career. 14 year olds must be in high school. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent. Needs a passing behavior grade, good health for running and agility drills, and no arrests or convictions that would block a future police job.
how_to_apply: Use the online intake form on the program site. It is on the Apply and Forms page. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Most cadets are not paid, but the pages do not say. Cadets who want to be police officers are urged to join the police recruit testing later. Other Explorer camps include a Pennsylvania State Police week and a camp at Fort Indiantown Gap. The program site lists a $50 a year fee for insurance and registration, collected if you are accepted. It also lists about $350 for probation uniforms.
duration: Every Saturday 10 am to 5 pm at the Philadelphia Police Academy, plus optional summer camps and a Washington DC trip.
pay_detail: Pay, stipend or fees are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Middle school students in the School District of Philadelphia. They must go to one of the PYN school sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online forms in the PYN application portal. There are no paper applications. Send questions to afterschool@pyninc.org.
notes: For middle schoolers, so it suits younger teens. Pick a school site from the list on the page.
duration: School year (2026-27 sites are listed on the page)
pay_detail: Not stated; no cost is listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th or 12th graders enrolled at a PYN host high school, Martin Luther King High School or Simon Gratz High School. You must be able to come three days a week after school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Participant Interest Form on the PYN page. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: The page also lists a NextGen Career Club (Health Care).
duration: 3 days a week, 2 hours a session
pay_detail: Free career exposure program. The club itself is not described as paid.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18, primarily rising 9th to 12th graders. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks per cohort (page also says experiences last 6 to 12 weeks)
pay_detail: Up to $1,500 for a 6 to 8 week experience, depending on hours and milestones

who_can_apply: The page says young people ages 16 to 24. Families and supporters can come too.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free pre-registration form on the event page (deadline Oct 15). Bring several copies of your resume.
notes: The page gives the day and month only; the year is taken from Oct 23 falling on a Friday in 2026. Under 16 is not listed as eligible.
duration: Friday Oct 23, 3 to 7 pm
pay_detail: Free to attend. The page says employers there have jobs and internships, but it does not say if they are paid.

who_can_apply: District high school students starting in 10th grade. Middle schoolers choose a CTE program on their School Selection application; high schoolers can join if their school has the program and space allows.
how_to_apply: Middle school: pick schools that offer your CTE program on the School Selection application. High school: talk to your school counselor.
notes: The page notes that students ages 14 to 17 need working papers to work. Which schools offer which programs is in the CTE Programs List.
duration: Typically 3 years, 1,080 hours of instruction; some programs 1 or 2 years
pay_detail: School program; the page does not say whether internships are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Positions are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.
duration: Two full weeks required; may be asked to work up to three weeks; one Saturday training in May
pay_detail: Volunteer program with no fee listed; hours can count as school or organization service hours.

who_can_apply: Clinic Support volunteers must be 16 or older (Animal Care requires 18+). Must attend a training session, sign the volunteer agreement and finish online ethics and safety courses.
how_to_apply: Complete the Wildlife Clinic volunteer Google Form. It is linked on the page.
notes: The general volunteer page says regular volunteers who work with children need Pennsylvania child abuse and criminal history clearances (free for volunteers).
duration: Minimum one 4-hour shift a week (about 20 hours a month)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students about to enter grade 11 or 12. You need a transcript, a list of activities and a personal statement of 250 to 500 words. You also need a recommendation from a teacher or counselor.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add your transcript, a list of what you do outside class and a personal statement. Temple will email a form to your teacher or counselor. They use it to write about you.
notes: Finishing with a B or better can earn a Temple tuition grant of $1,000 a year for four years if you later enroll at Temple full time and keep a 3.0 GPA. Phone: (215) 204-7200.
duration: 4 weeks on campus
pay_detail: There is a program fee and optional housing. The cost page was blocked when read, so the amount is not confirmed here. Optional financial aid essay is on the application.

who_can_apply: Students in 9th or 10th grade at Philadelphia public district or charter high schools. They come from low-income families, or their parents do not have a bachelor degree, or both. They also plan to go to college. Five named schools get priority. They are Benjamin Franklin HS, Dobbins CTE, Gratz Mastery, Strawberry Mansion and The U School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send papers that show you are eligible, like a report card, test scores and proof of income. Then you have a virtual interview. Questions: 215-204-3636.
notes: Federally funded. You must have a goal of going to college. Income is not the only factor in who is accepted.
duration: Runs year-round, with a six-week summer program on campus.
pay_detail: Free to students. The program pages do not say if students get paid.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors, and incoming college freshmen. Needs a personal statement of 250 to 500 words.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Pre-College Summer Academy application online. Pick the Pre-College Summer Academy choice from the list. Add your personal statement to the form too.
notes: The page says that being accepted does not promise acceptance later at Villanova. It also does not give you an edge. A virtual info session is offered.
duration: 4 weeks in July
pay_detail: Residential $8,000 (room and meals). Non-residential $6,000. $2,000 deposit due at acceptance. $50 application fee.

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16 by the program start date and have finished at least one high school science course. The program gives priority to students in the School District of Philadelphia. It strongly encourages Philadelphia high school students to apply. No grade level or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has a personal statement of one page, single spaced. It has two letters of recommendation. One from a science teacher is preferred. It has an unofficial transcript or list of classes with grades. Finalists have a 15 minute virtual interview in April. Participants and a parent or guardian go to a mandatory orientation in June.
notes: Contacts: Jason Diaz, 215-898-3803, jdiaz@wistar.org, or Cailey Bice, 215-898-3749, cbice@wistar.org. Absences of more than two days in a row cannot be accommodated. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Four weeks (the 2026 session ran July 6 to July 30). An optional three week extension in August depends on funding.
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend for finishing the program, plus SEPTA passes for travel

who_can_apply: Any young person who is in a Philadelphia high school now will be considered. The program is for Philadelphia youth ages 12 to 24.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PYN youth interest form (Google form) and look at the opportunity list. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: PYN also runs a PYNtern program.
duration: 6 to 12 weeks per placement
pay_detail: $11 an hour starting wage, 120 paid hours split between classroom and job site.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who live in Philadelphia. Any young person in a Philadelphia high school is considered. There is a preference for 12 named zip codes (19104, 19134, 19124, 19140, 19132, 19121, 19131, 19133, 19120, 19143, 19139, 19142).
how_to_apply: If a program provider already knows you, they send a link and referral code. If not, pick a provider from the map on the PYN page and email their recruiter.
notes: Spots are limited. A job is never promised. PYN suggests you email your chosen provider yourself with a short hello.
duration: 6 to 12 weeks per placement
pay_detail: $11 an hour starting wage, 120 paid hours.

who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents who are ages 12 to 24. You do not need to be in school.
how_to_apply: Visit a PA CareerLink center and ask for a Youth Navigator, or call 1-833-750-JOBS (5627). Philadelphia Works main office: 215-963-2100.
notes: This is a guide to programs, not one job. Also links the PHL Career Portal, apprenticeship search and the School District Opportunity Network.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Free help finding programs. Pay depends on the program you are matched with.

who_can_apply: The 2021 city announcement said Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. The current page does not repeat the age rule, so confirm it.
how_to_apply: Current page links a standing committee interest form (Formstack). Phone for the office: (215) 685-8307.
notes: City-wide teen council. The committee form on the current page is an interest form, not confirmed to be the membership application. Ask the office how members are chosen now.
duration: Ongoing; not stated.
pay_detail: Not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Email the zoo through the contact link on the volunteer page. No application link is listed.
notes: Separate options: Special Events volunteers (13+ for family events) apply through an online form; school groups of grades 9 to 12 can join Boo at the Zoo takeover shifts (those 2026 dates have passed). Docents must be 21+.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older. It is picky, so not all applicants are accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form linked on the page. Do a phone interview. Then go to a volunteer orientation. Volunteer Manager: 602.716.2037.
notes: The Teens page also lists a Teen Advisory Board, but gives no ages or dates. Email teenadvisory@azscience.org to ask.
duration: At least 24 hours of service. Weekly shifts, event help, days, evenings or weekends.
pay_detail: Unpaid. May earn service-learning credit.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. Must be legally able to work in the U.S. A background check may be required. The page does not say whether Club membership is required; its application asks whether you are a BGCAZ member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form (10 to 15 minutes). Then go to a Zoom info session and interview with staff. Then do the AZYF Academy at hubs in Mesa and Glendale. Apply at azyouthforce.org/apply.
notes: You may face a background check and a pre-employment drug test. Pay, length and exact dates were not on the pages, so email Samantha.Hansen@bgcaz.org or Kevin.Chavez@bgcaz.org.
duration: 30-hour academy first, then the internship. Length not stated on the program pages.
pay_detail: Paid internship. Rate not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up link on the volunteer page. Fill out the online volunteer form.
notes: The page does not give a schedule or minimum hours. Ask the volunteer office.
duration: Short-term, seasonal or ongoing, depending on the role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page to be told when applications open. Questions: youthservices@gphxul.org.
notes: The page still talks about the 2026 application, so it may be out of date. Call or email to confirm the next cycle.
duration: 5 weeks, 110 paid hours
pay_detail: Paid for 110 hours of work and job readiness workshops. Hourly rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 during the school year, at least 13 at the start of the school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in mid-May 2027. The page does not give steps. Contact studentvolunteers@honorhealth.com.
notes: Medical Explorers meet at Thompson Peak, Deer Valley and John C. Lincoln Medical Centers. The Nursing Explorers meet near Deer Valley Medical Center.
duration: Monthly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school and college students 16 and older. Parent or guardian consent is needed under 18.
how_to_apply: Send in the Student form on the page. Meet the volunteer team. Pass a background check and drug test. Then finish orientation and training. Call 480.245.6915 or email volunteer@MIM.org.
notes: Museum is at 4725 E. Mayo Blvd., Phoenix. The background check and drug test are required.
duration: Summer: one full month, at least 2 shifts a week. Year-round: at least 2 shifts a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student volunteers do not need a museum membership.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older for these roles. Lifeguards need a lifeguard certificate first (StarGuard Elite or the city class).
how_to_apply: Get lifeguard certified (class cost for a short time: $40) or use an active StarGuard Elite card. Then apply online. Search "Aquatics" in the City of Phoenix job portal. Questions: 602-534-6587 or aquatics.pks@phoenix.gov.
notes: Swim Lesson Instructors also need a Starfish Swim Instructor certificate. A certificate or an application does not promise a job. The page does not name a work permit rule.
duration: Season dates not listed on the page
pay_detail: Lifeguard $17.72/hr, Shallow Water Lifeguard $16.88, Swim Lesson Instructor $19.54, Pool Cashier and Buddy Bear $15.69.

who_can_apply: Age 14 and older, and you must have finished 8th grade. Stay in school until you graduate. Keep at least a C average. No serious police record.
how_to_apply: Complete the Cadet Application Packet and bring it to testing night. Use the APPLY NOW link on the page. For recruitment, call 602-534-2677.
notes: New cadets serve a three-month probation. During that time they must do 8 hours of community service each month. At 18, cadets can apply for non-sworn positions, such as Police Assistants.
duration: Weekly meetings every Tuesday at 5:00 PM
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cadets are volunteers, not police employees.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Follow the steps on phoenixpubliclibrary.org/teens/summer-teen-volunteers. Then staff contact you for an interview. Turn in a signed Volunteer PHX Permission Form and waiver by your first day.
notes: Based on the 2026 cycle. Expect applications again in spring 2027. Four online orientations were offered in May.
duration: At least 4 weeks over the summer, plus one online orientation and branch training
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when you apply. You live in the City of Phoenix. You have papers that show you can legally work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps or give an apply link. Watch the City of Phoenix internships page for the next session. Selection was first come, first served.
notes: Only Phoenix residents. You must be able to work the whole program. Teens must be 16 or older. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: 4 weeks, 20 hours per week, 80 hours total (June to July 2026 session)
pay_detail: $15.15 per hour (2026 session)

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Apply with the online form the museum shares. Go to orientation and teen front desk training. Shadow a front desk volunteer for at least 4 shifts before working on your own.
notes: Teen Leaders help train new teen volunteers and help develop new program materials. Ask the museum for the current application form.
duration: Saturday mornings or afternoons, October to April. Minimum 3 to 4 hours a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free museum entry and a store discount. The page says it counts for volunteer and internship graduation hours.

who_can_apply: Age 12 and older with an adult. Age 16 and older can volunteer without an adult.
how_to_apply: Go to the volunteer portal on the food bank site. Make a login and pick a shift by site and activity.
notes: Teens 12 to 15 must come with an adult. Court-ordered volunteers should call 602-343-3135.
duration: Usually 2 to 3 hours at the Phoenix and Surprise sites. Food box packing shifts are 2 hours. Mobile distribution shifts run 3 to 5 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12. You do not need volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. If chosen, you get an interview. Then you get a yes or no. Join the interest list on the page. Questions: zooteens@phoenixzoo.org.
notes: Orientation and training are a must in August and September. Trailblazers Youth Advisory Council is a leadership choice. You can apply to both. You can join only 1.
duration: August to May, one 5-hour weekend shift per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get a Teen Volunteer membership after two of eight monthly shifts.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17 (must be 16 by June 1). A recent graduate can still apply if they are still 17 on June 1. Recent graduates who are 18 go to the college or adult programs. You need a 3.0 GPA or higher and interest in a health career.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Two or more recommendation forms (teacher, counselor, coach or boss, not family). Show you are immune to measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox, and have a TB test. Send a headshot and parent signatures.
notes: You must go to the required orientation, or you can apply next summer.
duration: June 8 to July 30, 2027: at least one shift a week for at least six of the eight weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $25 program fee. Uniform shirts are provided.

who_can_apply: Applications are open to people 13 and older. If you are 13 to 17 you need a parent or guardian permission.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the library volunteer system. If you do not want to apply online, email Karen Goates at kgoates@ppld.org.
notes: The age range 13 to 17 comes from the rule that people 13 and older apply and teens under 18 need permission. Call (719) 531-6333, ext. 6146 with questions.
duration: Summer Adventure season (2026). Other teen roles vary.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Piscataway residents only. Grades 6 to 12 and at least 12 years old; high school volunteers must be in grades 9 to 12 and at least 14. Must sign a Teen Volunteer Code of Conduct at training.
how_to_apply: High school: attend a library orientation session with a mandatory training video, then enroll if you meet requirements. Adopt-a-Shelf (grades 6 to 8): apply on the volunteering page when the session opens. Questions: teens@piscatawaylibrary.org (subject line Volunteer).
notes: Latecomers are not admitted to training sessions. Open only to Piscataway residents.
duration: Regularly scheduled volunteer hours after training
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 20 when you are appointed. You must live in Pittsburg city limits. The commission needs at least 3 middle school students, 4 high school students and 2 college students, unless nobody applies.
how_to_apply: Fill out the city application. Then the City Council interviews you and picks the members. Ask Pittsburg City Hall for the form and the dates.
notes: The facts come from the city code, Chapter 2.80, adopted in 2020. Check pittsburgca.gov or City Hall for the current application and meeting dates. The commission meets at least 10 times a year. Members can serve no more than two terms in a row.
duration: Two-year term, August 1 to May 31
pay_detail: Members get no pay. The city may repay approved costs.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17 at two sites: Canonsburg Hospital and the Wexford Health + Wellness Pavilion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the AHN volunteer application (Apply Now on the volunteer opportunities page).
notes: Only these two AHN sites list a junior program for 16 and 17 year olds. Most other AHN volunteer roles are for adults. Check with the site for current openings.
duration: Wexford: Saturdays and in the summer. Canonsburg: not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You need a current lifeguard certification, or you can take the county course. A background check is required before a final offer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lifeguard Employment Application Packet and email it to lifeguards@alleghenycounty.us. Then sign up for a county course to get certified. If you already have a card, sign up for an aquatics test. Call 412-350-2455 with questions.
notes: The county lifeguard course is 2 days with the American Red Cross. It is for ages 15 and up. It costs $250 for residents and $312 for non-residents. You need a physical first. If you get certified through the county and work at least 225 hours at a county pool that season, the $250 fee can be paid back in full. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district.
duration: The full pool season. Exact start and end dates are not stated.
pay_detail: $16.00 to $18.00 an hour (listed for the summer of 2026)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who are entering 7th grade or higher in the fall.
how_to_apply: Register for the training on the nature camps page. Questions to Scott at sdetwiler@aswp.org.
notes: The 2026 training was held at Beechwood Farms Nature Reserve in Fox Chapel. The page does not mention 2027 dates. The page does not say whether ANTS are paid for service hours.
duration: One 4-hour training plus 30 hours of service during June and July day camps
pay_detail: Free to join. Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens at Club locations that offer Workforce Pathways: Carnegie, Estelle S. Campbell (Lawrenceville), Shadyside, Downtown and McKeesport. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Use the Returning Teen or New Teen registration link on the Workforce Pathways page. Or use Register Now at bgcwpa.org/registration. Financial assistance is available. See the Financial Assistance page. Phone: (412) 782-5710. Email: contact@bgcwpa.org.
notes: Confirm first: ages, cost, schedule and whether any work is paid are not on the pages. The Clubs also run two Club Teen Centers (Downtown and McKeesport).
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program pages, and the page does not mention paid work. Financial assistance is available for Club membership.

who_can_apply: Natural History camps: teens 14 and older. Powdermill Nature Reserve camps: ages 14 to 19. Art museum camps: 16 and older. Each museum has its own application form.
how_to_apply: Use the museum's own teen camp volunteer application form. It is linked from the Carnegie Museums volunteer page. There is one form each for Natural History, Powdermill and Art. Questions: volunteers@carnegiemuseums.org or 412-353-4680.
notes: The apply link above is the Natural History form. The Art museum form is https://form.jotform.com/230685138792162 and the Powdermill form is https://form.jotform.com/230595011446148. The Natural History page also lists a Teen Advisory Board with an interest form (https://form.jotform.com/243505851081150); its ages are not stated. The Kamin Science Center teen volunteers are a separate card.
duration: Summer camp season. Hours and camp dates are not stated on the volunteer pages.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: At least 15 by June 6, 2026 (the 2026 posting). You must live in the City of Pittsburgh and hold current lifeguard, first aid, AED and CPR certificates. You must pass the Citiparks lifeguard performance exam and a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the City of Pittsburgh job application online. It is on governmentjobs.com. Then call the Citiparks Aquatics Office at (412) 323-7928. Ask them about test dates, classes and cards.
notes: The posting says applicants 18 and under with no high school diploma or GED must show a valid work permit before they are hired. It also needs Pennsylvania Act 153 clearance, fingerprints and a medical exam. The job number in 2026 was 26-LG1A-01.
duration: Part-time seasonal. Training starts in April; the end date is not stated.
pay_detail: $18.00 to $20.76 an hour (2026 posting)

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page links a Google Form for people interested in joining and the wing's Become a Cadet page. It lists no squadron email or phone. The Pennsylvania Wing headquarters can be reached at 717-220-3517 or hq@pawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists other squadrons in the Pittsburgh area. They are Golden Triangle, Jimmy Stewart, Washington, Beaver Falls and Butler. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets Tuesdays from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at Baldwin High School, 4653 Clairton Blvd, Pittsburgh, PA 15236.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 by the program start, in 10th grade when applying, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a green card. Meant for students who lack access or resources in computer science.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; full participation required.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the pages (the apply portal could not be read). Limited spots. The admission page lists two different dates for this application (February 1 and March 1, 2027); the page and the deadlines table both say February 1, 2027, so apply by then. Completers may be invited back to AI Scholars.
duration: 4 weeks, June 26 to July 24, 2027, residential
pay_detail: Fully funded: tuition, housing and meals are free; limited travel help for families with transportation barriers

who_can_apply: High school students at least 16 years old by June 26, 2027 who are in 10th or 11th grade when they apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal. The scholarship option is only considered under the February 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the pages (the apply portal could not be read). Expensive; shown so families know the cost and the scholarship route. The three fully funded programs (AI Scholars, CS Scholars, SAMS) cost nothing. Check the cost page again in November 2026 for 2027 prices.
duration: 3 to 6 weeks depending on the program (summer 2027 starts June 26)
pay_detail: 2026 prices ran from about $5,999 (3-week music, commuter) to $14,688 (summer session, residential, 2 courses), plus a $75 application fee and an $800 enrollment deposit. 2027 prices are posted in November 2026. Full scholarships for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old by the program start who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and in 11th grade when they apply. The program focuses on students underrepresented in STEM.
