how_to_apply: The application opening date is not posted; apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; scholars must attend the full program.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines above are confirmed on the pages (the apply portal itself could not be read, it needs JavaScript). Competitive and limited spots. The page gives no application opening date. Scholars cannot take other summer programs that overlap. Questions: cmu-sams@andrew.cmu.edu.
duration: 6 weeks in person, June 26 to August 7, 2027, plus a short virtual jumpstart June 21 and 22, 2027
pay_detail: No cost to scholars beyond travel to and from Pittsburgh

who_can_apply: High school students (and college students thinking about transferring). No grade or age minimum is listed.
how_to_apply: Pick a date under 2027 Pharmacy Exploration Day on the page and use that date's registration link. Questions: Jason Stack, (412) 396-5182.
notes: Sign in 7:45 to 8:00 a.m. Drop-off and pickup are on Bluff Street behind Mellon Hall.
duration: One day, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
pay_detail: No fee is stated on the page. Lunch, an ice cream social and parking are free.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. No art or glass experience is needed. Scholarships are offered to all students.
how_to_apply: Click Register Now or the scholarship link on the Youth Programs page.
notes: Not a job. Included as an art skills program. Check the registration page for cost and dates.
duration: 10 weeks (beginner) or 12 weeks (advanced), once a week after school
pay_detail: Class fee not stated on the page. Scholarships offered to all students.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 from surrounding neighborhoods. You must apply through Learn & Earn (Partner4Work).
how_to_apply: Apply to Learn & Earn at partner4work.org/learn-earn. Choose Homewood Children's Village as your group. Tell them you want to work at Grow Pittsburgh.
notes: Work sites: Shiloh Farm (7209 Thomas Blvd., 15206) and the Grow Pittsburgh office (6587 Hamilton Ave. #2W). The year includes a Garden Youth Summit (2026: July 30). The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district issuing officer.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to Aug 7), Tuesday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $12 an hour, 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Must be at least 14 by the application deadline. Late applications are not considered.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (or download one to email or mail) during the window. Selected teens are interviewed and must complete an orientation.
notes: Teens accepted twice a year (summer and school year). The next summer window should open in January; confirm on the page.
duration: Summer Teen Program and School Year Teen Program (hours per week not stated)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: All youth ages 11 to 17. Pre-registration is required.
how_to_apply: Register online with the ticket link for each tour or call 412-237-3400. Call to join a waitlist if full. Cancel at least one week ahead.
notes: Tours are NOT at the science center. They are on-site at partner workplaces or on a virtual platform, and each listing gives its own address. Some tours need long pants, closed shoes and tied-back hair.
duration: One 2 to 3 hour tour (10 a.m. to noon for most)
pay_detail: Most tours are $15 per student. The page also says $13 in one place, so confirm at sign up. Need-based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19 per the meeting schedule section (the program overview says 10 to 19). A separate Tween L.E.A.D. is for ages 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up link on the Teen L.E.A.D. page. Contact Tonja Grate, tgrate@kingsleyassociation.org.
notes: The page does not state a current start date. Its examples are from 2024 and 2026, so confirm the program is running this year and where it meets.
duration: Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, 4 to 6 p.m.
pay_detail: No cost to join. No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 23 in Allegheny County and the City of Pittsburgh. Income and residency requirements apply (details on the application).
how_to_apply: Apply online through Partner4Work during the spring application window (new participants and returning participants use different links). A complete eligible application does not guarantee a placement, so apply early.
notes: Questions: summer@partner4work.org or (412) 932-2950. A separate Year-Round Learn & Earn (fall, winter, spring work sessions) serves ages 16 to 23 in the City of Pittsburgh but only for people who already finished a summer. The page does not mention a work permit; the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18, so ask your school or the program how to get one.
duration: Tier 1 and 2: June 22nd, 2026 - August 7th, 2026. Hours per week are not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Paid wages (hourly rate not stated on the program page)

who_can_apply: In-person group: high school students in the Greater Pittsburgh area. Virtual group: high school students beyond the Greater Pittsburgh Area. The page lists no ages or grades beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the in-person or the virtual application form on the page. Questions: Taylor Goodman, development coordinator, tgoodman@greaterpawv.wish.org.
notes: In-person meetings are at the Make-A-Wish office, Koppers Building, 436 7th Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15219.
duration: In-person: usually the first Tuesday of each month, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Virtual: about every other month, usually a third Tuesday.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone enrolled in high school (grades 9 to 12) in the greater Pittsburgh region. Teens fill out their own application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It is linked from the museum page that asks for applicants. Applicants heard back in a few days. Send questions to Laurie Barnes, Education Director, at lbarnes@mattress.org.
notes: This is a high-commitment program: you are expected to come most Thursdays. The 2026-27 call was not found on the pages.The museum is at 509 Jacksonia St, Pittsburgh, PA 15212.
duration: Thursdays 4 to 6 pm, October to May, with a winter break (2025 to 2026 schedule)
pay_detail: Free to join. No pay or stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 interested in animal-related careers (age counted as of June 1, 2026 for the 2026 session). Must commit to at least 8 of the 10 days in the chosen session.
how_to_apply: Submit the volunteer application when it reopens, attend an in-person group interview, and attend orientation with a parent or guardian.
notes: Questions go to the volunteer contact on the National Aviary volunteer page.
duration: 10-day sessions; orientation with a parent or guardian in late May
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students who have finished 9th grade up to graduating seniors. No age limit is listed. You must be available for all program dates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form (Apply Now link on the page). It has short essays. Interviews include the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: 2027 dates are not posted yet. The page also lists an overnight retreat in the Laurel Highlands. Phone: South Side Office 412-682-7275 (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.). The page does not list a contact name or email.
duration: 5 weeks, Tuesday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: $1,200 stipend over the five weeks (2026). Also a raincoat, t-shirts, water bottle, work boots, bus passes and tuition.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19 who have finished at least one year of high school. You pick one of two weekly groups (Wednesday or Thursday) and must attend all of the dates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form on the Phipps page when the next group opens. Use the sign-up form on that page to be notified. Questions go to the high school programs coordinator at amule@phipps.conservatory.org or 412-622-6915 ext. 3804.
notes: The page lists two different dates for the final Youth Garden Summit, so confirm with Phipps. The stipend is not described as a job on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Seven-week course, one afternoon a week (12:30 to 4:30 p.m.) at Phipps, plus a Youth Garden Summit at the end
pay_detail: Free to join. Participants receive a stipend (amount not stated on the page).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who enjoy working with children. You must be able to get Pennsylvania Act 33/34 clearances. Phipps pays back the fees.
how_to_apply: The page says the first step for volunteers is to fill out an application. Accepted applicants then go to an interview, orientation and placement meetings. The page does not give a form just for teens. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the Phipps volunteer page to ask. That is Deb Knorr, dknorr@phipps.conservatory.org.
notes: Confirm first. The volunteer page gives no teen deadline or teen form. Ask Phipps for the current age rule and dates before you plan around this.
duration: Summer camps held June to August. Hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Clearance fees are reimbursed.

who_can_apply: Students from high schools in the Pittsburgh region who have completed one year of high school biology. The page does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: The page says a link to the application will be posted when applications open. To get updates, join the email list by contacting Jess Robertson at jah99@pitt.edu. Questions: Dr. Becky Gonda, 412-383-5739, reg11@pitt.edu.
notes: No research experience is needed. Free PRT bus passes are available. The honorarium is not called a wage on the page. The page's dates (June 28 to July 16) are shorter than 'four weeks', so confirm the length. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Described as a four week summer program. Summer 2027 is tentatively June 28 to July 16, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: $1,000 honorarium, paid at the end of the program

who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders at a high school in the Greater Pittsburgh area or Western PA. You need a strong interest in science and a GPA of 3.0 or above. You must finish a biology class by the end of the school year. You must commit to the full four weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two essays of up to 200 words each. A high school teacher must complete the recommendation form. It is uploaded at the end of the application or emailed to phsa@pitt.edu by the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered. Applicants are told by email in mid to late March. They confirm by April 1.
notes: The main page says public high schools in one place and all high schools in another, so ask which applies to you. The award is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Four weeks. The 2026 session ran June 22 to July 17, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Students who finish receive a $1,000 award at the end. Public transportation support to and from campus is provided, and transportation for field trips.

who_can_apply: Qualified high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. Students who are often left out are encouraged to apply. You must be at least 14 to live on campus. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Send the application on the page with at least two letters of support from counselors or teachers. If you are accepted, sign up and pay the $25 fee. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Run with the National Association of Black Accountants (NABA). Residents must be in their rooms by 10 pm. The page showed the 2025 schedule.
duration: 1 week, residential only (2026: July 26 to 31)
pay_detail: Tuition is free for accepted students. A $25 non-refundable registration fee holds your spot. You pay your own travel to Pittsburgh.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12, or recent graduates. No experience needed. Residents must be at least 14 on the first day. Only the first 15 students who register and pay the deposit get in.
how_to_apply: Register online through CampDoc using the Register Here link on the camp page. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Discounts: 30 percent off tuition for Point Park employees, alumni and immediate family, and $50 off for signing up more than one person or program. The schedule includes a firearm safety session. The schedule can change.
duration: 1 week. 2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31 (day or residential)
pay_detail: Tuition $700 plus $100 non-refundable registration fee ($800 commuter). Room and board adds $750 ($1,550 resident). Payment plans are available.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall, and/or recent high school graduates. No age range is listed.
how_to_apply: Register at app.campdoc.com/register/pointpark and pay the $25 fee. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Space is limited. In 2026 the page said housing for summer programs was full, so commuters were dropped off at Academic Hall, 201 Wood St. The page showed the 2025 schedule.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 29 to July 1), day or residential
pay_detail: Tuition is free (paid by the Rowland School of Business and sponsors). A $25 non-refundable registration fee holds your spot.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall, and/or recent high school graduates. No age requirement is listed.
how_to_apply: Register at app.campdoc.com/register/pointpark and pay the $25 fee. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Bring some cash for snacks and off-campus activities. The page showed the 2025 schedule. Instructor: Robert Derda, M.S.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 29 to July 1), day or residential
pay_detail: Tuition is free (paid by the Rowland School of Business and Brentwood Bank). A $25 non-refundable registration fee holds your spot.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Crews are for teens ages 14 to 18 who want to join the summer program.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. It says to check back for openings and links to an SCA job board. Call Darren Gruetze, Pittsburgh Program Manager, at (412) 325-1854.
notes: Crews have two adult leaders age 21 or older. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district issuing officer; ask SCA or your school how to get one. Check the SCA page often because it shows no openings right now.
duration: Starts the last week of June and runs through the first week of August each year
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 (having turned 15 by June 1, 2026 for the 2026 program). Two non-relatives must complete a reference form. Needs proof of a negative TB test and a Tdap shot before orientation.
how_to_apply: Check the teen page in early January for how to submit an inquiry. Questions: chpvolunteer@chp.edu or 412-692-5185.
notes: Interviews are limited and selected by criteria. The volunteer office does not handle shadowing, internships or research requests; contact departments directly for those. Adult volunteer program is 18 and older.
duration: At least 8 weeks over the summer. The program page says two or three days a week (6 to 8 hours). Assignments page: one 3 or 4 hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students in good school standing. You must be at least 15 at the program start for the computational sites (CompBio, COSBBI, Surgery). You must be at least 16 for the other sites. There is no residency rule, but out of region students must find their own housing.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has two short essays. It has one or two references, who get an email. It has a resume and a high school transcript. It has parent or guardian contact information with a digital signature. It also has your top research site choices. PDF files are preferred. In person students may need proof of vaccination.
notes: Very competitive. Another page describes it as an eight week program; the apply page says seven or eight weeks (June 14 to July 30, 2027). Questions: hillman.academy@pitt.edu or Steven Jones, 412-624-5904 (from the program's Oct 2025 profile). The stipend is not called a wage on the page. The apply page does not mention work permits, so check with the program before assuming one is needed.
duration: About seven weeks. Tentative 2027 dates: June 14 to July 30, 2027.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Stipends are offered to qualified students from a background underrepresented in biomedicine (details are on the stipend page linked from the application site).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who commit to at least 9 workshops. Space is limited. (The Tech25 page says 13 to 18; the Warhol page says 14 to 18, so ask if you are 13.)
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Watch the Warhol teens page and the Tech25 page for the next round. Questions: teens@warhol.org.
notes: The Warhol teens page says applications are closed. The Tech25 page says 'apply now!' but gives no dates. Ask Warhol before you assume it is open. The Warhol teens page also lists paid Student Assistant jobs at the museum. No ages or dates are stated. Email teens@warhol.org or see Carnegie Museums careers.
duration: 12 weeks, Mondays 4 to 6 pm (Print Lounge in The Pop District)
pay_detail: Free to join. Teens get a stipend for workshop sessions plus extra stipends for each performance. Amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: Pittsburgh area teens ages 15 to 18 (high school students).
how_to_apply: Send in the online application by the deadline. Work samples are optional. Email teens@warhol.org with questions. Bus tickets are available for transportation.
notes: The 2026-27 deadline was 2026-10-09, so email teens@warhol.org to ask whether late applications are accepted. The Warhol also hires paid Student Assistants and runs a free Teen DJ Academy (ages 14 to 18, stipend) and School of Drag (ages 14 to 18); see the Teens page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Weekly Thursdays 3:30 to 6 p.m., Oct 15, 2026 to May 2027
pay_detail: Participants receive stipends (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 who are interested in animals and conservation (having turned 14 by June 1, 2026). Must commit to one day a week for at least 5 of the 7 weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. All applicants are interviewed in person before acceptance. Not all applicants are accepted.
notes: Volunteer role, so no pay. Contact the Volunteer Services Manager through the zoo volunteer page. The page's age requirement reads 'having turned 14 by June 1, 2026' even though it describes the 2027 program, so ask the zoo to confirm the age cutoff date. Confirm dates when applications open.
duration: 7 weeks, one day a week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (June 15 to July 31, 2027)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The event page does not describe the application steps. Contact the zoo education or volunteer office, or watch the page for the next season.
notes: The Jan 23, 2027 session is on Zoom. Some sessions run 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. to fit field trips. The page lists no application steps or program-specific contact; the zoo's general phone is 412-665-3640.
duration: 13 sessions from Sept 26, 2026 to May 1, 2027, mostly 10 am to 12 pm, plus a May 1 all-day field trip
pay_detail: $25 program fee

who_can_apply: Teens in high school. Eligibility by town and grade is not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the crews page (rootsrising.org/apply). Questions: info@rootsrising.org, 413-344-0816.
notes: Market Crew is for Farm Crew graduates. Farm: 923 Barker Rd, Pittsfield.
duration: Summer 5 weeks (July to early Aug, Mon to Fri 9 to 4:30). Fall (Sept to Nov) and Spring (Mar to May) 8 to 9 weeks after school.
pay_detail: Summer Farm Crew pays up to $2,000 for 5 weeks. Fall and Spring Farm Crews pay up to $800. Market Crew pays $15 per hour.

who_can_apply: No age or grade rule is stated. The program focuses on youth facing challenges such as hunger or homelessness and aims to keep them in school.
how_to_apply: Email your resume to jobs@plantingjustice.org. Or call the East Oakland Nursery at 510-756-6965.
notes: Ages, season and hours are not stated, so call and ask. Pay is from the page and may change.
pay_detail: $17.50 per hour (page says 40+ paid internships)

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. No other rule is stated for teens on the employment page.
how_to_apply: Download the job application on the employment page. Fill it out. Email it to Ainsley Pearce, the Human Resources Admin. Her email link is on that page.
notes: The same page lists sports referee jobs for age 18 or older. Listings change, so check the page for the current jobs. A job description link is on the page.
duration: Part time, nights and weekends
pay_detail: $18.00 to $19.85 per hour, depending on experience

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12. The page does not list a residency or school rule.
how_to_apply: Stop by the Pleasant Hill Teen Center. Or email the Youth Services Manager, Katrina Hunn. Her email link is on the program page.
notes: Meetings are on the 1st and 3rd Mondays of the month, 7:00 to 8:00 PM, at the Pleasant Hill Teen Center. The council does not meet on holidays.
duration: Meets September to June
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Volunteers of all ages are welcome. The page says junior and senior high school students are encouraged to take part.
how_to_apply: Call Pleasant Home at (708) 383-2654. The Park District also asks volunteers to use the general Acorns to Oaks volunteer form and waiver.
notes: The same volunteer page lists the Oak Park Conservatory (call 708-725-2451). It also lists Cheney Mansion garden volunteers (call 708-383-2612). It does not give ages for those.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. You go to an orientation and get your fingerprints taken. Junior Lifeguards must also take a Red Cross class first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application online. Sign up for an orientation and a fingerprint visit. Junior Lifeguards also sign up for the training class on the city recreation site. Then pick your shifts online.
notes: Junior Lifeguards do not make rescues and do not get a lifeguard card. The 2026 class ran April 6 to 10 and June 15 to 19, 9am to 3pm. Swim Instructor sessions ran Monday to Thursday. Saturday shifts are daily sign-ups with no commitment. Both jobs prepare volunteers to become lifeguards or water safety instructors at age 15. For the fingerprint form, bring an approved photo ID and know your Social Security number. Contact: Katelyn DiGiosaffatte, Recreation Coordinator, kdigiosaffatte@cityofpleasantonca.gov.
duration: Junior Swim Instructor: 8 day sessions. Junior Lifeguard: shifts June 9 to August 2 in 2026.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Junior Lifeguard training class costs $145 for Pleasanton residents and $181 for non-residents. Every volunteer pays $25 on site for fingerprints.

who_can_apply: Must reside within Pleasanton city limits. Seats are set aside by grade: middle school, 9th grade, and 11th grade (fall 2026 ad: 3 seats each).
how_to_apply: Apply online through the City of Pleasanton boards and commissions page (link at the bottom of the page, per the recruitment ad). Questions: Office of the City Clerk, 925-931-5027.
notes: The next recruitment date is not posted in the ad; deadline_confidence is last-year-pattern because the most recent cycle was fall 2026. The recruitment ad describes city commissions in general; the Youth Commission's own duties and term length were not on any official page for it, so what_you_do is based on the ad's general description.
pay_detail: Volunteer appointed seat. No pay is stated in the recruitment ad.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 at appointment, enrolled in high school or college with a C average or better. Needs a valid government ID (CA ID, driver license or US passport), parent consent if under 18, and a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the completed application to joinsmpd@cityofsanmateo.org or call the Recruiting Unit at 650-522-7629.
notes: Training classes are on the 1st and 3rd Thursday, 5 to 7 p.m. Hours count toward school service requirements. You need a flexible schedule for weekdays and weekends. FAQ is at cityofsanmateo.org/4720.
duration: 9 week academy plus monthly service

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19 (not yet 19 and a half), full-time student, 2.5 GPA, must pass a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, or contact the coordinator at 510-293-5060 or Explorers@hayward-ca.gov.
notes: The page gives no closing dates, so check at the start of each window. Meetings are Wednesday nights 5 to 7pm plus training and some weekend events.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, currently enrolled in school with a C average or better. No felony or certain misdemeanor convictions, no pending criminal cases, and you must agree to fingerprinting for a background check.
how_to_apply: Email the Explorer application PDF to MHPD_Explorers@morganhill.ca.gov, then complete an oral board interview.
notes: Free to join, but you may need to buy a uniform and gear. Financial help is available. Expected to attend all meetings, trainings and events. Meeting times are not on the page.
pay_detail: Free; you may buy your own uniform (help available)

who_can_apply: High school students at least 14.5 years old, 2.0 GPA, average or better attendance and discipline, no felony or serious misdemeanor.
how_to_apply: Email Explorer Coordinator Officer Charles Stone at cstone@oaklandca.gov, or Oakland PAL (Officer Jumaal Hill) at 510-615-5758 or oaklandpal@oaklandpal.org.
notes: The page gives a minimum age of 14.5 and no upper limit. The page does not give meeting times or dates, so ask the coordinator. Oakland PD also runs the Police Activities League.

who_can_apply: Current 9th graders who live or attend high school in Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino or Ventura County. First-generation, low-income, or Geometry/Integrated Math II students are considered but not required. About 30 students are admitted each year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online New Student Application. Add two essays of up to 500 words each, this year's transcript and two recommendations. One must come from a core subject teacher. Some applicants get an interview. Contact PAYS@pomona.edu or (909) 607-1810.
notes: Checked 2026-10-13 on the apply page: it lists the 2026-2027 dates and the June 20 to July 16, 2027 residential dates. Its list of application materials still says 2025-2026. The program admits about 30 students each year. Contact the program if the form is not up by Nov 9.
duration: 4-week residential summer (2027: June 20 to July 16), then 3 years of involvement
pay_detail: Free. Pomona College covers housing, food, activities and field-trip transportation. No stipend mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students currently in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. The page does not list an age rule.
how_to_apply: The page has a link to its application site for high school volunteers. Use that link only to check whether high school applications are open. The page lists no phone number or email to ask about it.
notes: CONFIRM FIRST: the page offers a high school application link but also says only adult applications are being accepted right now. Scheduled Monday to Friday shifts.
duration: At least 1 year; one 3-hour shift a week (up to 3 shifts)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. There is a scholarship for volunteers who meet its rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Go to an orientation and interview. Finish the paperwork and a background check. Then do a health check with a TB test.
notes: The page gives a minimum age of 16 and no upper age limit. The page says to wait for the application to re-open for other Legacy medical centers. Usually the ask is one four-hour shift a week for one year.
duration: Usually one 4-hour shift a week for one year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students going into grades 9 to 12. Writing and Studio Art are for rising grades 10 to 12. The page lists grades, not ages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Precollege Program Interest Form on the program page. For questions, email summercamps@lclark.edu.
notes: Summer 2027 costs are still being set. These programs do not give college credit. Students who finish a program and are later admitted get a guaranteed minimum of $20,000 a year in renewable scholarship funding.
duration: Varies by program. Writing and Studio Art run June 20 to July 3, 2027.
pay_detail: Costs listed for 2026: $1,800 for Circular Innovation, Data in Action and Future Health Leaders. $3,600 for Theatre. $3,800 for the Writing Workshop. $3,650 for Studio Art. A $500 deposit is not refundable. Some partial scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. (A separate Tween Council is for ages 9 to 12.) Minimum age beyond "middle school" is not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your neighborhood library, or contact Volunteer Services at 503-988-5731 or libvols@multcolib.org.
notes: Which branches have a council is not listed on the page, so confirm with your branch. The library's volunteer page lists Volunteer Services contact details.
duration: Meets twice a month; length of membership not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 10 and older can volunteer on their own. Younger volunteers must have a parent or caregiver with them.
how_to_apply: Apply online or on paper at any library. Share your name, contact details and area of interest. You do not need a Social Security number. The library contacts you to schedule an interview. Orientation and training come after you are accepted.
notes: This is the general library volunteer page. Current jobs are listed on an outside volunteer site. A link is on the page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 21 who live, work, go to school or go to an after school program in Multnomah County or the City of Portland. Picks are based on drive and point of view, not grades or past leadership.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Apply to the Multnomah Youth Commission form on the county page. Ask for a reference. Meetings are 2 Sundays a month (4:30 to 7:30 pm) in Portland and Gresham. There is also a weekly after school meeting.
notes: The page was last reviewed February 2025, so confirm the current cycle. Reference letter due the same day as the application.
duration: Voting members give 12 hours a month; at-large members give 7 hours a month
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer (non-paid) positions.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You live in a northwest community where the program runs. The page names Portland area sites.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Northwest Youth Corps site (Apply link on the program page). Ask info@nwyouthcorps.org about help with tuition and school credit.
notes: You may be able to earn high school credit. Your school decides, and requests are handled only after you finish. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday (2026: June 15 to July 17 or July 21 to Aug 21)
pay_detail: Stipend of $480 a week plus up to $40 a week in bonuses (up to $520). Tuition fee $200, with need-based assistance available.

who_can_apply: Oregon high school students entering grades 10, 11 or 12 who like health care careers.
how_to_apply: Use the apply link on the OHSU Experience page when it opens.
notes: Not a job and not paid. The page describes 2025 as a pilot year. The 2026 camp had three one-day sessions with the same activities each day.
duration: One day (2026 dates: Aug 18, 20 and 25, 9 am to 4 pm; each day is the same)
pay_detail: Free. Scholarships from the Oregon Health Authority cover the cost.

who_can_apply: High school or college students who are only free in summer. Guides and Healing Through Music volunteers must be 14 or older. Art Cart volunteers must be 16 or older and have experience with children.
how_to_apply: Apply when the 2027 Summer Program opens. The page says that is January 2027. Healing Through Music volunteers must audition. They must bring their own instrument, except piano.
notes: The page asks volunteers to pick up extra shifts beyond their weekly schedule. The page does not give summer 2026 shift dates or hours beyond the weekly minimum.
duration: At least 26 shifts, with 2 regular shifts a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Oregon high school students. OHSU especially wants students from underserved and rural communities. Students at any Oregon high school may apply. Ages and grades are not stated. Students must meet health care worker shot rules.
how_to_apply: Send in a form. Also send a recommendation from a teacher, counselor, principal, adviser, coach or other teacher. If you have a question, you can send an email to knightscholars@ohsu.edu.
notes: Applications were closed when the page was read. Confirm whether a 2027 group is running before you plan around it. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Introduction 1 week; Immersion 10 weeks; Intensive 10 weeks (each level requires finishing the one before)
pay_detail: Scholars are paid a stipend (amount not stated). OHSU also pays for hotel or residence hall housing during time in Portland.

who_can_apply: Counselors must be 16 or older by June 1. Limited housing is for counselors over 18 who live outside Portland.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the OMSI Outdoors hiring page when the 2027 counselor job posts.
notes: Summer camp is overnight, and counselors stay with campers. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
pay_detail: Paid. Counselor wage not stated (the page lists $135 to $180 a day only for full-season staff). Housing and meals are provided during programming.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 and older apply with the Teen Volunteer Application. Some roles list other age rules. For example, the planetarium usher must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application on the OMSI volunteer page. If you are over 18, you must also take a class for mandatory reporters.
notes: The page sorts roles into Ages 14+, 16+ and 18+ sections, so check each role's minimum age.
duration: Most roles need at least 4 hours a month for 3 months (some roles ask for more)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Any teen age 13 to 18. Museum admission is not required to use The Mezz.
how_to_apply: Just visit during open hours. Teens who want to help run it can apply as Mezz volunteers (see the OMSI teen volunteer card).
notes: The page says some exceptions apply to the listed hours. Ticketed programs are not offered. To visit the rest of the museum you need to pay admission.
duration: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 11 am to 5 pm, Sept 8, 2026 to June 13, 2027
pay_detail: Free for teens. Not a job.

who_can_apply: The volunteer FAQ sets a minimum age of 8. Each shift lists its own minimum age. First-time volunteers under 18 need a youth release form.

notes: Check the minimum age on each shift. For small group or family volunteering, email volunteer@oregonfoodbank.org. Shoes must have closed toes and heels. Shirts must have sleeves.
duration: Single shifts, most days of the week

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 at the Portland campus. People who qualify go into a random lottery for limited spots.
how_to_apply: Send in the youth form during an application window. A lottery picks the spots.
notes: Confirm the window dates on the page, since the year is not printed. The page says applications for the Portland campus are closed now.
duration: One 2-hour shift every other week for at least 6 months (Wed to Sun 4 to 6 pm, plus weekend 10 am to noon)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens from the Portland metro area who are 13 to 15 on April 12 of the program year. Selected by application and interview (about 30 teens).
how_to_apply: Apply online in January. Then interview. Chosen leaders go to an orientation and trainings in spring (the page lists March 29, April 12 and May 17).
notes: Ages 13 to 15 only. No direct animal contact in the first year. The page says the program does not guarantee future employment.
duration: 10 weeks; at least one 6-hour shift a week for 8 of the 10 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. No fees.

who_can_apply: Advancing high school juniors and seniors. The page does not state a minimum or maximum age.
how_to_apply: Sign up online. Use the Register link on the Pacific University Synapse page when it opens.
notes: Sessions are in Hillsboro (June 22 to 25) and Forest Grove (June 26) in 2026. The page does not list a cost.
duration: 2026: June 22 to 25, 9 am to 4 pm in Hillsboro; June 26, 9 am to 1 pm in Forest Grove
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page. Check the registration page.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 by the first day of class (no exceptions). Lifeguard candidates must pass a swim test. It has a 50 yard freestyle or breaststroke swim, a 50 yard rescue tube swim, a 10 pound brick pickup and 1 minute of treading water. Lifeguard and swim teacher classes are only for people who plan to apply to work for PP&R Aquatics.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a class on the aquatics page. Then apply for a pool job through the City of Portland job site (GovernmentJobs.com). You must be 16 to apply.
notes: Go to every session. If you miss a day you must take a new class. Your certificate must stay current while you work. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Classes year-round; the city runs about 700 summer pool staff and up to 400 at indoor pools in other seasons
pay_detail: Paid city pool jobs. Hourly rate and class fee not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: The page says the bureau employs people aged 14 to 24. The minimum age depends on the job (pool jobs are 16 and older).
how_to_apply: Make an account on GovernmentJobs.com. Apply to the open Portland Parks & Recreation jobs.
notes: Check each job posting for its own minimum age. The page lists career fairs on March 24 and March 28, 2026. Oregon BOLI says minors age 14 to 17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon (employers need a certificate to employ minors).
duration: Summer season; exact dates vary by job
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 24. The page lists no other rules. Use the interest form to confirm you qualify.
how_to_apply: Complete the PDX Youth@Work Interest Form on the Worksystems page.
notes: It starts at age 16, so 14 and 15 year olds can not join. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Short-term SummerWorks jobs and year-round PDX Youth@Work experiences; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 who have finished at least one year of high school.
how_to_apply: Apply online on a rolling basis until programs are full. Applications open fall 2026, per the page.
notes: The page does not list dollar amounts for tuition or scholarships.

pay_detail: Tuition (includes materials) for Summer 2027 will be announced when applications open this fall. Need-based scholarships and payment plans are available; early registration saves 10%.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 years old.

notes: Volunteer Services phone: 503-215-5002. The page does not list teen-only roles, so ask which spots take 16 and 17 year olds.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 years old.

notes: Volunteer Services phone: 503-216-2159. The page does not list teen-only roles, so ask which spots take 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: At least 6 months in a row, usually 2 to 4 hours a week

who_can_apply: Crew members ages 14 to 18. The page does not list grade requirements. Crew leaders must be at least 18 and have a driver's license.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Portland job site when the crew member job posts.
notes: Crews: Trail (the hardest work on the body), Tree, Community Gardens, City Nature East, and West Side Nature (No Ivy League). Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 2026 crew members worked June 23 to August 7, 8:30 am to 2:30 pm. Summer hires can keep working Saturdays in the school year.
pay_detail: $18 an hour (2026 crew member rate)

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24. Volunteers age 15 to 17 must bring a parent or guardian to orientation. Sites are in Portland Metro, Warm Springs, Central Oregon and Maui, Hawaii.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a monthly orientation on the program page. You can also text YLVol to 85511 or email YLVolunteering@linesforlife.org. Next, you have an interview and training.
notes: The program page asks volunteers to commit to at least one year. Shifts are about 3.5 hours a week.
duration: About 3.5 hours a week for at least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page mentions Work Study positions for young people who face money or other barriers.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 12 or older. The TeensTeach and TeensTable teen programs are for ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: create an account and submit the individual application, read the handbook, finish the online orientation and quiz, then sign up for training. Teen programs: submit an idea through the page. Staff pick programs that fit the museum's mission and email chosen applicants.
notes: Address: 29 Hubble, Irvine, CA 92618. Volunteer questions: volunteer@pretendcity.org or 949-428-3900. The page also links a Youth Leadership Board but does not describe it.
duration: At least 3 hours a month and 15 hours a year before you sign up for training (volunteers). TeensTeach and TeensTable length is set by you.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.

who_can_apply: Students age 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student volunteer application in person at the branch you choose, or contact the branch. Volunteer Office: 703-792-6100.
notes: Adult volunteer roles on the same page need age 18. Branch list is at pwcva.gov/department/library/branch-locations-hours/.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12. Must live in Princeton or attend a Princeton high school, with an active library card in their own name.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a signed reference form. The papers were due Sept 4 at 5 pm in the 2026-27 year.
notes: Ask the library's teen staff if you have questions.
duration: October to June, first and third Tuesdays at 7 pm, one hour
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens going into grades 8 to 12 who have a Princeton Public Library card in their own name.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Give your library card number and a signed reference form. Spots for Maker Assistant and Program Intern are limited.
notes: The June 5 close date is from the page's 2026 cycle wording; confirm for 2027.
duration: At least 10 hours. Program Intern camps run in July and August. In the 2026 cycle, applicants heard back June 15.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid. Verified service hours.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9-12 who live in the five boroughs, with parental consent and NYS working papers, and who register as library volunteers.
how_to_apply: Complete the Idea Submission questionnaire on the library volunteer site during a submission window. The Civic Engagement Team will contact you to get your idea library ready. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: A limited number of projects are accepted and a branch must agree to host. Other QPL pages list ages as 14-18 for this program, so check the age limit if you are 18.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service credit for time presenting.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with a signed parent consent form. The page says some projects do not require NYS working papers, so check each project's description. Students at schools outside the country or the state may use a waiver.
how_to_apply: Get the parent consent form and NYS working papers (from your high school office), create a volunteer account, search projects and click Express Interest/Sign Up, then interview and get an offer letter. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: Library says some projects do not need working papers, so check each listing. Working papers take 1-3 weeks from your school, so start early. They are issued regardless of immigration status. Under-14s can only volunteer with a parent or guardian.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours count as community service credit.

who_can_apply: Rising 7th graders and older who are at least 12 years old by the first in-person training. The page lists no residency rule.
how_to_apply: Go to an info session with a parent or guardian. Then send the form, two letters from adults who are not family, and a short video. In the video, tell them your favorite way to play. Keep it under 2 minutes.
notes: Not everyone is accepted. If selected, you take a virtual Volunteer 101 and in-person Mission 101 and Play 101 trainings. Teens 16 and up can also volunteer on their own without Teen Play Corps. Questions: teenplaycorps@marbleskidsmuseum.org.
duration: One year. Minimum 30 service hours a year to stay active.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18 in 10th, 11th or 12th grade. You must be done with 9th grade before it starts.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form online. Two adults who know you, 21 or older and not family, email a reference form. This can be a teacher, a school counselor, or a boss. If they call you, go to an interview.
notes: There is also an Academic Year Program (one day a week, 3 to 5 PM, September to May), but it is closed for 2026 to 2027. If accepted, you need a health screening (TB, whooping cough, chicken pox, MMR). Questions: volsvcs1@unchealth.unc.edu or 919-784-3165.
duration: 8 weeks, June 21 to August 13, 2027. One 4-hour morning or afternoon shift a week, Monday to Friday. Only one absence allowed.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12 who are ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 before your first shift.
how_to_apply: Check the page in spring for the application link. Email volunteer@redbutte.utah.edu.
notes: Garden work can mean kneeling, weeding and standing on uneven ground.
duration: Dates not announced
pay_detail: Volunteer and intern roles. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Red Cross says the in-person Babysitter's Training is for ages 11 to 16, and its online Babysitting Basics course is designed for youth 11 and older.
how_to_apply: Pick a class on the Red Cross Babysitting and Child Care page, or buy the online course there.
notes: The old take-a-class/babysitting-training link no longer works, so the page address was updated. Red Cross says these courses do not qualify you for state-licensed child care. Casual babysitting in a private home does not need a work permit per the California child labor guide (2013 edition).
duration: Online course: about 4 hours; in-person length varies
pay_detail: Babysitting Basics Online costs $45 (4 hours, self-paced, certificate valid 2 years). In-person class prices vary by location.

who_can_apply: Lifeguarding: at least 15 years old by the last day of class, plus a swim test (swim, tread water, timed event). Water Safety Instructor and Basic Swim Instructor: at least 15 by the end of the course.
how_to_apply: Use Find a Class on the Red Cross lifeguarding page to pick a pool or YMCA class near you, and check the fee.
notes: Final test is a 50-question exam with an 80% pass mark. Certificate lasts 2 years. Before the update this file said Water Safety Instructor needs age 16; the Red Cross page says 15. For lifeguard jobs, check each employer's page for pay and work permit rules.
duration: Lifeguarding: about 27 hours in person, or about 6 hours online plus about 21.5 hours in person
pay_detail: Course fees are set by each provider and are not listed on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12, described on the page as 14 to 17 years old. Up to 25 teens are picked.
how_to_apply: Register online. Then do an interview. Bring a letter of recommendation. Or bring references from someone outside your family. Call 701.277.9240 to ask about the next trimester.
notes: Up to six teens work each shift.
duration: Trimesters during the school year. Saturdays and Sundays, 9 am to 2 pm. At least two 4.5 hour shifts a month, up to four.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay $125 per trimester for zoo members or $175 per trimester for non-members.

who_can_apply: In-person teen volunteers must be at least 16. You send a City of Redlands volunteer application and a liability waiver. If you are 18 or older you also need a LiveScan.
how_to_apply: Email yrr@akspl.org to ask what is open. They send details after you write. Youth Services phone: (909) 798-7674.
notes: The Youth Services volunteer rules say volunteers must commit at least one month and follow the City dress code. The Teens page also lists a Teen Makers and Helpers Lab for ages 13 to 18 with a sign-up form, but gives no details.
duration: Fall, winter/spring and summer sessions; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours available.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 with a reference from a teacher or school counselor. You must commit for one year.
how_to_apply: The page lists these steps for all volunteers: a volunteer application, an in-person interview, health requirements, a background screening, General Orientation and training. It shows no junior application link or contact, so ask the hospital volunteer office.
notes: Confirm first: no contact or junior application link on the page. The page says the commitment is one year and that junior recruitment opens periodically.
duration: One-year commitment, 2-hour shift at least once a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15; you must be 13 by the first training day. Written application, then an interview if selected. At most 20 L.I.T.s per session. Redwood City camps.
how_to_apply: Download the L.I.T. application and email it to tbrent@redwoodcity.org by the deadline. If chosen you interview, then get camp placement and payment instructions. Phone 650-780-5929.
notes: Teens pay a fee to take part (2026: $88, $98, $98 or $49 depending on session). The fee is due after a successful interview. Placement depends on camp needs. A mandatory Saturday training is required. 2027 dates are not posted, so expect a similar April to May window and watch the page.
duration: 1 to 2 weeks per session
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $88 for session 1, $98 for sessions 2 and 3, $49 for session 4

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 or equivalent. You cannot enter ISEF directly; you must win at a Society-affiliated fair. Use the Find-a-Fair tool for California fairs.
how_to_apply: Use Find-a-Fair on the Society for Science site, then register with your school or regional fair.
notes: Projects can include no more than 12 months of continuous research. The 2027 ISEF is in California, which can lower travel costs for California finalists. The ISEF site says students from nearly every state in the U.S. and more than 60 countries, regions, and territories compete at affiliated fairs.
duration: May 2027
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the program pages; more than $7 million in awards and prizes

who_can_apply: Students in their last year of high school who live and attend school in the US or its territories, any citizenship. You need your own original research with real data, plus essays, a paper of up to 20 pages, recommendations and a transcript.
how_to_apply: Apply online at the Society for Science application portal (sciencetalentsearch.smapply.org).
notes: Seniors only, so juniors should plan for next fall. Test scores are optional. Homeschooled students may apply.
duration: Application June 1 to November 5, 2026
pay_detail: No entry fee stated on the program pages; $3.1 million in annual awards, $250,000 first place

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17. You must give at least one 3 to 4 hour shift each week, for at least 144 hours and 12 months in a row. No summer-only or school-break-only volunteering. Spanish and Vietnamese skills are a plus.
how_to_apply: Apply online between Jan 1 and Jan 7, 2027. Send the reference form to RMCVolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org. If you are a good fit, you get a phone interview. Then you do an online orientation, a health check, a background check and training at the hospital.
notes: Read on the official Regional Medical Center page on 2026-10-16. You must be fully vaccinated and upload immunization records and a TB test for the health clearance. After 6 months and 100 hours you may qualify for shadowing. Have your reference form ready before Jan 1 since the window is only one week. Benefits include free parking and a free flu shot after one year.
duration: At least 12 consecutive months and 144 hours

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 14 by the first session date. You must pass a swim test: 25 yards of front crawl, a step into deep water with a 10 foot underwater swim, and 1 minute of treading water.
how_to_apply: Pick a session on the program page. Each session links to a registration page, and the site has an Online Registration link. For questions, call Parks Administration at 775-334-2262.
notes: This is a good step toward the City of Reno lifeguard class, which starts at age 15. You must attend every day of a session to be certified.
duration: 4 days, 8:30am to 1:30pm each day
pay_detail: The class fee is $100.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 by the final scheduled session. You must also pass a swim test. Swim 150 yards, then tread water for 2 minutes using only your legs. Swim 50 yards. Then finish a timed event in 1 minute 40 seconds: a 20 yard swim, a dive to 10 feet for a 10 pound object, a swim back, and an exit without a ladder.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Online button for a class, or join the interest list by email. To get the free certificate, apply online for a city job. Be onboarded by the class start date.
notes: You must attend every day of the class to be certified. A shorter $124 renewal class is for people with a valid lifeguard certificate, or one that ended in the last 30 days. The program page does not say if a work permit is needed.
duration: In-person class days run 9am to 3:30pm. The class is blended, with online lecture and in-class training.
pay_detail: The class costs $140. The page says the city will certify you for free if you are hired and onboarded by the class start date.

who_can_apply: Under 16 can do drop-in single-day tasks with a parent-signed release form. 16 and older can do continuous volunteering after a background check. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Drop in: a parent signs the Volunteer Release of Liability Form and you sign a time sheet. Ongoing: send in a Volunteer Application, a Consent and Disclosure form and a Reno PD background form. Get a photo ID card. Call the Volunteer Coordinator at 775-334-2046.
notes: The listed roles on the page are mostly for seniors programs and fund raising. Ask the coordinator what fits a teen.
duration: Drop-in single days, or recurring scheduled tasks
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Open to grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Teen Assistant Application button on the page (online form). Then a 15-minute Zoom interview and an in-person training. Contact Kristen Kellogg, 775-398-5920, kkellogg@nvdm.org.
notes: You must be free during Washoe County School District breaks.
duration: Camp breaks: fall, winter, spring and summer (Washoe County School District breaks)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Earns over 80 community service hours.

who_can_apply: Bilingual English and Spanish high school juniors in Northern Nevada. Up to 30 are chosen for the summer program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CBESS Interest Form at nevada.formstack.com/forms/cbess. Questions: cbess@unr.edu or (775) 784-1110.
notes: Chosen students also do an outreach internship. Up to 64 more juniors get a certificate. They must first finish some questionnaires.
duration: One week on campus plus two or more weeks virtual, then monthly mentoring in senior year
pay_detail: Free to attend. A stipend is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Sign up online when it opens on February 1. For a scholarship, add an essay on your interests and a teacher recommendation letter to the form. Questions: paigefroese@unr.edu.
notes: Camp prices and dates were not posted when this was checked. Check back before February.
duration: Camp dates not listed on the page
pay_detail: Fee not listed on the page. A $50 non-refundable deposit can hold a spot; full payment is due within a month of registering. Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Nevada high school students who meet each course's prerequisites. A counselor or vice principal must back you. That lets the classes count toward graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the UNR non-degree student application and the dual enrollment interest form. Send your shot records through the online portal (2 MMR doses and 1 Tdap). Upload your high school transcripts with the Transcript Upload form. Your counselor or vice principal fills out the school district contract form. They email it to DualEnrollment@unr.edu.
notes: Earlier college work can place you into classes. So can SAT or ACT scores, AP or IB scores, or placement tests.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: $154 per credit for tuition plus an $18 per credit tech fee, plus any class fees.

who_can_apply: Nevada high school juniors and seniors. The program is aimed most at girls and young women who have faced barriers to STEM learning and research.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Join Women in STEM page. A paper form can be picked up at the Dean's Office, 4th floor of the Davidson Mathematics and Science Center on campus.
notes: The program page still shows the 2024 to 2025 year. Check with the program before you plan on it. It asks for four events in each of three event series, two advisor meetings and three mentor meetings during the year.
duration: One school year
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Teen and a parent or guardian both sign the application.
how_to_apply: Online: make a Beanstack account and join the Volunteen Challenge. A coordinator emails the forms. Paper: fill out the online form or ask the volunteer coordinator at your branch.
notes: Paperwork and orientation come first. Both a teen and a parent or guardian must sign.
duration: Self-paced, up to 20 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a certificate at 20 hours.

who_can_apply: Lake County high school students who like health care, science and research.
how_to_apply: Email campmed@rfums.org to ask how to apply.
notes: In person only. Ask when applications open.
duration: 5 days, the last week of July
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Lake County students. High school students who live near the Rosalind Franklin University campus come first.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for INSPIRE link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026.
notes: Check whether it pays. Students can come back every summer until they finish a bachelor's degree. To reach the program, write to Rachael Lange at rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu or call 224-570-7325.
duration: 8 weeks in summer
pay_detail: Pay or stipend is not stated on the program page. Ask the program.

who_can_apply: Juniors in good standing with a GPA of 2.0 out of 4.0 or higher and an interest in nursing. Applications are for juniors at Cristo Rey St. Martin College Prep, Highland Park, North Chicago, Round Lake and Waukegan High Schools.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn More link on the Nursing INSPIRE page to find the form. To reach someone, write to Dr. Mosilda Asanji at mosilda.asanji@rosalindfranklin.edu.
notes: Only students at the five schools named can apply. The page looks about two cycles old (it shows 2024-25 dates), so ask the program for current dates. Parents join a session on financial planning for college.
duration: 8 weeks, four days a week, June to August
pay_detail: Described as a paid educational opportunity. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Local high school students. The page does not list a school list or grade rule beyond high school.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Science Saturdays link on the pathway programs page. It is a Google form. It opens in December 2026. Contact: Rachael Lange, rachael.lange@rosalindfranklin.edu, 224-570-7325.
notes: Only about 25 students are chosen each year.
duration: 9 Saturdays, 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., June to August
pay_detail: Free. Lunch and transportation are provided.

who_can_apply: Local high school and college students who like health care or science.
how_to_apply: Use the Register for the Virtual Mentor Program link on the pathway programs page. It opens a Google form (forms.gle). You must attend an orientation before being matched.
notes: Online, so you do not need to travel to North Chicago.
duration: Monthly meetings, October to May
pay_detail: No cost or pay is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: People who live in Richmond or North Richmond and are 15 or older. If you are 15 to 17, a parent or guardian must approve. Some seats are set aside for youth who are 15 to 24 years old. You must be able to go to at least 6 meetings a year and give at least 50 hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Oversight Board Application, a PDF on the city page. A parent or guardian signs it if you are under 18. Email it to the City Clerk or mail it to the City Clerk's office at the address on the form.
notes: The board meets every first Monday at 6:00 PM in the Richmond City Council Chamber, 440 Civic Center Plaza. City Council members and the Mayor pick the members. The application says you can learn more at richmondyouth.org or by calling 510-620-6523. Having work or school experience is not required.
duration: One-year term if you are under 24
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The application says members get training, childcare, meals and translation help at meetings.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Add a one-page cover letter. Add one letter from a teacher, boss or volunteer leader. Email volunteer@maymont.org or call 804-525-9000.
notes: Ask the volunteer lead for the 2027 dates.
duration: One 4-hour training and at least 10 morning shifts (8:45 am to 12:15 pm) in the summer camp season (2026: June 1 to Aug 14)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: City of Richmond residents who are in school. Counselors in Training: ages 14 to 16 (14 by July 1). Summer Work Experience: ages 16 to 19 (16 by July 1, not 19 before the program ends).
how_to_apply: Apply online starting March 1 with your latest report card and one proof of residency. Work experience also needs a signed Social Security card and a photo ID. Questions: 804-646-7000 or 3-1-1.
notes: Page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Work experience about 6 weeks, early July to mid-August; mandatory training in May
pay_detail: Paid by the employer or by the Academy. The youth pay rate is not stated on the FAQ page.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page (ages and residency are not listed).
how_to_apply: Download the YCC application (Word document) and email it to the park contact, or mail it to 3215 E. Broad Street, Richmond, VA 23223. Questions: 804-795-5019 ext. 1.
notes: Only five spots. The page was last updated April 2024, so confirm the year, pay and ages with the park.
duration: 8 weeks in July and August, Monday to Friday, 8 hours a day. Five youth are hired.
pay_detail: $7.25 per hour (as posted; page last updated April 2024)

who_can_apply: Teens in grade 8 to 12. Members join the library volunteer team.
how_to_apply: Email teenblog@yourlibrary.ca to learn more. You can also look at the library volunteer page for other jobs.
notes: Full when read, so confirm first. Email teenblog@yourlibrary.ca.
duration: Meets the first Tuesday of each month
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Students now in grades 10 to 12. You must do an interview and a fitness test.
how_to_apply: Download the application when posted, or ask at your school career programs board or RCMP liaison officer. Then interview and fitness test.
notes: Exact August dates are listed as to be decided. Email careerprograms@sd38.bc.ca.
duration: One week, Monday to Saturday, in August 2027 (exact dates to be decided)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, or at least a rising sophomore. Must attend the initial training and commit to 8 shifts over 16 weeks.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the museum's volunteer page. It is hard to get in. They look at writing, drive, growth and teamwork.
notes: The page labels these as 2027 spring applications, but its weekday and date pairs (Sunday, Nov 8 and Saturday, Jan 10) match 2026. Confirm the dates with the museum.
duration: 8 shifts over 16 weeks, every other weekend (Saturday or Sunday)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Richmond SD38 students. Must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Grade 11 students apply to start in semester 2 of Grade 12.
how_to_apply: Get the form on the district page once it is posted. You can also get it at the school Career Programs board.
notes: Earns 16 high school credits and 12 KPU credits. Opening date not posted.
duration: Feb to June 2028, 4 courses
pay_detail: District pays tuition

who_can_apply: Students registered in a Richmond SD38 school. English 12 and Math 11 at 67% or higher, strong attendance.
how_to_apply: Get the application form from the district page or the school Career Programs board.
notes: The page lists no contact name or email. Get the application form from the district page or the school Career Programs board. The page says applications for 2027-28 are open and due the year before the program; no due date is printed.
duration: February to June, 4 courses
pay_detail: District pays tuition. Books, supplies and travel are the student's cost.

who_can_apply: Students at Richmond SD38 schools. Sixteen trades are offered. Some are welding, wood building, electrical work, cooking, car repair, plumbing and hair styling.
how_to_apply: Get the form from the district page. You can also ask your counsellor or career advisor. Or check your school Career Programs board.
notes: Email careerprograms@sd38.bc.ca for questions. The page gives no grade eligibility. The page's school-year wording conflicts: the headline says 2025-2026, the linked PDF says 2026-2027, and the body says 2027-2028. Confirm the year with the district before applying.
duration: One full program, taken in the 2027-28 school year for this intake
pay_detail: Unpaid. The school district pays tuition for the first level (the page says this often saves $2,500 to $5,000).

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 19 who have a job in a known trade. A skilled worker called a journeyperson must agree to sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact the district coordinator by the email or phone on the page.
notes: Contact Peter Thackwray, pthackwray@sd38.bc.ca, 604-668-6000 ext 1463. Courses are taken off the timetable. You need a trades employer first. Written for Richmond students.
duration: 120 paid work hours plus 3 short online assignments per course, up to 4 courses (16 credits)
pay_detail: Paid by the employer. Rate not stated. Finishing may earn a $1,000 scholarship from the Ministry of Education and Child Care.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who are interested in pharmacy. About 30 are selected. No GPA rule listed.
how_to_apply: Register through the link on the VCU School of Pharmacy summer programs page. Questions: pharmacy@vcu.edu.
notes: Students are responsible for their own housing and transportation. The page is for 2026, so confirm the 2027 dates.
duration: 1 week, 9:30 am to 3:30 pm (2026: July 20 to 24). Not residential.
pay_detail: $50. Fee waivers can be requested when accepted.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 20. 20 spots, first come first served.
how_to_apply: Sign up through City of Richmond program sign up. The course ID for 2026 is 00530586.
notes: Held at Minoru Centre for Active Living and Richmond City Hall. Next summer dates not posted when read.
duration: 3 days, 10am to 4:30pm
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 24. Anyone, including you, can refer you. You can drop in without a referral to check it out.
how_to_apply: Fill in the referral form and talk with a Youth Outreach Worker, or just drop in. Email medialab@richmond.ca or call 604-247-8303.
notes: It is at the Richmond Cultural Centre Annex, 7660 Minoru Gate. It works with Richmond Addiction Services Society. You get in by referral. It is not a job.
duration: Weekly drop-ins and seasonal programs
pay_detail: Free to join

who_can_apply: Richmond youth ages 16 to 21. Must attend required workshops and training to be guaranteed an internship.
how_to_apply: Submit the online Work Experience Program application (2026-2027 form linked on the city page). The team contacts you for an intake. Phone (510) 412-2044.
notes: The page refers to Richmond youth but does not spell out a residency rule. Ask about the hourly wage and your start date at intake.
duration: Up to 100 hours
pay_detail: Paid internship; the hourly rate is not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24 living in Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Merced, Madera, Napa, San Francisco, San Joaquin, Santa Clara, Sonoma or Tulare county. Must commit to four days a week.
how_to_apply: Apply through the links on the job posts at risingsunopp.org/jobs/. Phone (510) 665-1501.
notes: As of Oct 10, 2026 the jobs page lists three staff postings: two Central Valley coordinator roles and a Bay Area Senior Program Manager. No Bay Area summer Energy Specialist posting is listed. Pay shown is the 2026 rate. The City of Oakland summer jobs list also includes Rising Sun.
duration: Summer; four days a week
pay_detail: 2026: up to $20.50 per hour for Energy Specialists (up to $22.50 during externship); drivers up to $21.50

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who live in River Forest. You must attend an orientation, and a parent or guardian must sign the release and waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen/Tween Volunteer form or the Book Buddies form online. Or print it. Email the form to volunteer@riverforestlibrary.org or drop it off at the library.
notes: River Forest residents only. The page says both that Summer 2026 applications are closed and that they are open, so it is out of date. Ask the library when the next call opens.
duration: Teen volunteers: one 1 hour shift a week in summer. Book Buddies: one weekly time slot for all of July (Tuesdays 3 to 5 p.m. or Wednesdays 5 to 7 p.m.).
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page mentions it can help with school community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens at branches that have a board. The page states no age range, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch. The page describes no teen application; its online application is for adult volunteers.
notes: Not every branch has a board. The page gives no ages, hours or sign-up steps for teens, so call the branch first. Separate from the City of Riverside Public Library.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 in Riverside County. You must be low income and have at least one of six barriers to work. The program mostly serves youth who are not in school.
how_to_apply: Call or visit the nearest Youth Opportunity Center. They are in Indio, Hemet, Lake Elsinore, Moreno Valley, Perris and Rubidoux. Staff check if you qualify.
notes: This is a federal WIOA program, so you have to qualify. Centers are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Phone numbers: Indio (760) 802-6059, Hemet (951) 765-0917, Moreno Valley (951) 653-1311, Perris (951) 657-7105, Rubidoux (951) 683-9622. Do not email your Social Security number. Paid work under 18 in California needs a work permit.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Some work experience is paid and some is unpaid. The page does not list a wage.

who_can_apply: High school students enrolled in a Riverside County high school. You must be able to go to meetings every other week and to service events.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Join Us page. Or contact the youth council coordinator for your supervisor district. Contacts for all five districts are on the home page.
notes: There are five councils, one per supervisor district. Students elect officers, and each council's Commissioner joins the county Youth Commission. Commission meetings are public, in the Board Chambers in Riverside. The paid Legislative Intern jobs that run the councils are for college students only.
duration: School year. Council meetings every other week. Youth Commission meetings every two months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The city recruits through local school districts, colleges and universities.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Ask your school counselor or the City of Riverside.
notes: Confirm first. This comes from a city news release about the first group, which had 15 students. Employment is not guaranteed.
duration: 20 weeks, 120 hours of training
pay_detail: The first group was paid. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: The center serves ages 14 to 22. Teens in Action serves ages 13 to 18. The youngest age at this site is 13, for Teens in Action.
how_to_apply: No sign-up steps are posted. Call the center at (951) 826-2272 (Teens in Action: 951-826-2000).
notes: Center at 2060 University Ave, Riverside. Hours: Mon to Thu noon to 7, Fri noon to 6. The page says the center aims to give youth an opportunity to gain employment, but it lists no specific job training or paid programs.
duration: Teens in Action runs Mon to Fri, 3 to 6 PM
pay_detail: Teens in Action is free. Costs of other programs are not stated. No pay.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 18. An 18-year-old can join if still in high school, but must be fingerprinted before turning 18. You must be free at least 8 and at most 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Call (951) 826-2272 to ask about joining. No online form is listed.
notes: Office: 6927 Magnolia Ave, Riverside, open Mon to Fri 9 to 5. The 8 to 40 hours a week is a lot, so ask if a school-year schedule is possible.
duration: 8 to 40 hours per week; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Possible chance to be hired later; no pay rate stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old who can pass a Department of Justice background check. The library cannot accept court-ordered volunteers.
how_to_apply: Create an account at riversideca.cervistech.com, find a Library opportunity, click 'Apply to participate', then wait for an email or call. If approved you book a processing appointment with Human Resources at City Hall and get cleared by background check.
notes: This is the City of Riverside library, not the Riverside County Library System. The page does not describe teen-specific roles; it applies to all volunteers ages 14 and up.
duration: At least 30 total hours at one library before switching
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older (some roles need 18). Must sign a liability waiver and complete a background check.
how_to_apply: Call 540-342-5718 or email hsell@smwv.org. The contact is Hunter Sell, Director of Operations.
notes: The page is not teen specific. Ask how the background check works for minors.
duration: No required hours stated
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid. Membership perks after 10, 50 and 100 hours.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, or 16 for clinical units.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the program page. It opens the volunteer application site.
notes: The page does not show whether applications are open now, so check before applying.
duration: At least one 3 to 4 hour shift per week
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
