You must be able to present proof of citizenship or legal right to work in the United States. Most positions require some related experience and/or an educational background in a related field. Students with no prior work experience: 'We will consider your application for our entry level positions.'
how_to_apply: Apply online for a specific opening on the Zoo's Employment Listings page. Send one application per job.
notes: The Careers page links to the Employment Listings on sbzoo.careerplug.com. It posted no specific openings when read, so check whether any are open now. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Seasonal, mostly spring and summer
pay_detail: Not stated on the page; see each job listing.

who_can_apply: Current junior high or high school students. Junior Camp Counselors give at least 3 weeks of summer Zoo Camp (about 100 hours). Leaders in Training give 4 summer weeks (about 130 hours). Special-event volunteers can be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply links under Teens on the Zoo volunteer page. They are for the junior camp counselor application plus a reference letter. Call or email the Zoo to confirm before you plan.
notes: Confirm first. The Zoo says no internships are available at this time. The Zoo held a Job and Volunteer Fair on February 22 (year not on the page).
duration: Junior Camp Counselor: 7 hours a day, Mon-Fri, 3 summer weeks plus 1 fall week and 2 winter weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who live in Santa Clara County.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the Teen CERT website or email scctcert@gmail.com to be told when the next academy opens. Paperwork drop-off happened before the last academy.
notes: The March 2026 flyer said ages 13 to 17 and the website says 13 to 18, so check your age with them. Cost is not stated; the last academy was at Los Altos Hills Town Hall. Santa Clara County residents only.
duration: 3 day academy (Friday evening to Sunday)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Santa Clara residents ages 12 to 19. You cannot be employed by the City of Santa Clara.
how_to_apply: Apply during the yearly recruitment. Call the Youth and Teen Center at 408-615-3760 or email youthcommission@santaclaraca.gov to ask when it opens.
notes: Meets the second Tuesday of the month at 6 p.m. at the Youth and Teen Center, 2446 Cabrillo Ave. The page was last updated 2026-09-30.
duration: September to May, up to six years

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12. No age range is stated. New members are always welcome.
how_to_apply: Use the Volunteer/TAB Sign Up link. It is at santaclaritavolunteers.com. Or contact a volunteer coordinator. They work at the Old Town Newhall library. They also work at the Canyon Country Jo Ann Darcy library and the Valencia library.
notes: Meeting dates are on the TAB Schedule calendar linked from the page. Branch coordinator emails are on the page.
duration: Meetings September through May
pay_detail: Unpaid. Participation can earn service hours (the number is not stated).

who_can_apply: High school students. The page gives no residency or other rules.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact SITE SANTA FE at info@sitesantafe.org or 505-989-1199.
notes: Ask about the start date and how to join.
duration: Ends with an exhibition (2026 show ran Feb 27 to Apr 4, 2026)
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. The program serves young people from Northern New Mexico.
how_to_apply: Open the Youth Jobs Application link on the YouthWorks site. You can also email info@santafeyouthworks.org with your resume and letter of interest, or call 505-989-1855. The office is at 1505 Llano St., Santa Fe.
notes: The page also lists GED prep, First Aid and CPR training, and trades certificates.
duration: A 6 month spring and summer season, per the page. The season listed is for 2025.
pay_detail: Wages and stipends. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students from schools across Santa Barbara County. Past members came from Lompoc, Orcutt, Santa Barbara, Santa Maria, Santa Ynez Valley and Carpinteria high schools.
how_to_apply: Use the Google form linked on the Student Advisory Council page.
notes: Confirm first: no ages, selection steps or deadline on the page. Past and current members are listed by district and school.
duration: One-year term that matches the school year
pay_detail: No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18 who go to a public high school in Santa Barbara County.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now student form on the page or book a call through the Calendly link there. Phone: (805) 964-4711.
notes: Internship needs a current work permit, a photo ID and a Social Security card. You can take the training without those but get no stipend. This year 10 internship spots are for students interested in energy. Office: 3970 La Colina Rd, Suite 9.
duration: Training is about 1 hour a week for 7 or 8 weeks (page says both). Internship is at least 10 hours a week, 80 hours total.
pay_detail: Internships pay minimum wage. A stipend is possible for the training (amount not stated; needs a W-9 and a Social Security card or TIN).

who_can_apply: Local high school students. 10 high school and 10 college students are chosen, in screenwriter and director pairs. No age or grade rule or county rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps. A pair can submit one script and one film sample. Questions: claire@sbiff.org.
notes: Competitive: only 20 local students are chosen. Past high school participants came from Santa Barbara High, San Marcos and Dos Pueblos. Composers (college students) are also added.
duration: About 5 months, ending with the festival (Feb 3 to 13, 2027)
pay_detail: Free to students. No pay. Winning student directors get a prize camera package.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18 who get CalWORKs benefits, or current and former foster youth ages 16 to 24. Open to year-round employment services.
how_to_apply: Call 408-758-3797 to begin your application, or use the Register/Refer form on the page.
notes: Only for teens who get CalWORKs benefits or who are/were in foster care, so most teens do not qualify. Under 18 needs a work permit. Positions are across the county.
duration: 8 weeks per cohort
pay_detail: $19.75 per hour, up to 30 hours per week

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer page at sccld.org/volunteer. Or ask a local library.
notes: Serves the library district branches, not every city in the county (San Jose has its own library). Hours, training and schedule are on the volunteer page. See the separate homework-help tutor card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteer Tutor) for a similar after-school tutoring role.

who_can_apply: High school student (regular, alternative vocational, or working toward equivalency), enrolled or graduated within 6 months, legal right to work in the US, overall GPA of at least 2.5. Application plus transcript and proof of enrollment. Under 18 needs a work permit (from your counselor or EDD). May need Live Scan and a physical.
how_to_apply: Subscribe to alerts for the Student Intern Level I posting on the county jobs site and apply with your transcript when it opens. You can also email departments, or the coordinator at studentinterns@esa.sccgov.org.
notes: Interns can be hired any time of year depending on department needs, so keep the alert on. Some departments (District Attorney, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Parks) run their own internships; contact them directly.
pay_detail: Paid on a five-step county salary scale; the rate is not stated on the page (see the county salary plan).

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. You must be free one afternoon, Monday to Thursday, from 3:30 to 6pm for a whole semester. You also need about 7 hours of training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application PDF from the library's volunteer page. Then upload it using the online form on that page.
notes: The page lists these libraries: Campbell, Cupertino, Gilroy, Los Altos, Milpitas, Morgan Hill and Saratoga. Check that your branch is on the list. Training is online (about 7 hours). The broader card (Santa Clara County Library District Teen Volunteers) also includes after-school tutoring of a kindergarten to grade 6 student.
duration: One semester

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live within the Schaumburg Township District Library service area. Grade level is not stated.
how_to_apply: The page invites eligible teens to apply but does not describe the method. Watch the library's Student Trustees page or ask the Teen Department.
notes: Board meetings are the third Monday of each month at 6:00 p.m., plus monthly meetings with the Teen Department. The next-cycle timing is a guess from this year's August 9 deadline.
duration: One year: October 2026 to September 2027
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: The page says the Volunteer Squad is open to students entering grades 8 to 12 in fall 2026. No age or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Check the volunteer page in spring or ask the library.
notes: The contact email on the page was a blank placeholder. Call or visit the library.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Unpaid. Students can earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Minimum ages are not stated on the pages. Check each job posting.
how_to_apply: Go to a job fair. Or apply on the district's online job board (BambooHR). Questions: Alex Khodan, Supervisor of Aquatics, alkhodan@parkfun.com.
notes: Pay figures for lifeguards are from the 2025 post, so check the current rate. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.
duration: Seasonal, May through September, per the district's aquatics job fair post.
pay_detail: In the aquatics job fair post (dated Feb 18, 2025): lifeguards $18 an hour, swim instructors $18, concession staff $15. The district job board (read Oct 2026) lists swim instructor at $18 and concessions at $15.

who_can_apply: Junior Camp Counselors are 14 to 18. General volunteers must be at least 14, pass a background check, sign a waiver and finish onboarding.
how_to_apply: Apply through the volunteer portal. Questions go to volunteer@sciowa.org.
notes: The exact opening day in February 2027 is not posted. Questions? Email volunteer@sciowa.org.
duration: Two weeks required, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Onboarding with staff comes before any volunteer role.
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 40 hours of service the position description says you get a free one-year membership.

who_can_apply: Not stated on the page. Which classes you can take depends on your school district. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask your school counselor and look at the SCOE CTE course catalog. Contacts listed: Michelle McIntosh (Director), mmcintosh@scoe.net; Raelynn Sharp (Project Specialist), rsharp@scoe.net.
notes: The pages describe CTE (career technical education, 15 industry sectors) and list staff contacts. They do not list eligibility, enrollment steps, dates or work-based learning details. Treat this as a starting point and call SCOE. Age and grade are not stated, so ask your counselor.
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens must be at least 14 and not yet 18. A parent or guardian must give permission.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the program page. A teen volunteer coordinator will contact you. New summer volunteers must go to a required orientation.
notes: Space is limited, and applying does not guarantee a spot. The program page says the Mustang and Arabian school year programs are full. New summer volunteers must attend a general orientation.
duration: School year program runs September to May. Summer program runs June to July.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn documented volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who live in the Scottsdale area.
how_to_apply: Call 480-312-0060 or email VistaCareerCenter@ScottsdaleAZ.gov to make an appointment. You can meet online or in person.
notes: The career center is at 7700 E. Roosevelt St., Scottsdale. It has a self-serve computer lab for job searches. The center is open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. Specialists are available 8 am to 4 pm.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. This program helps you find a job. It is not a job itself.

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 15 years old. Teens apply through the same process as adults; there is no separate teen program on the page.
how_to_apply: Submit one online application and choose one site. If chosen, you complete an interview, show proof of required immunizations and attend orientation. Onboarding takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
notes: Drop-in or on-call volunteering is not available. You pick a regular weekly shift. South region sites (Mercy San Diego, Chula Vista) take applications all the time. North region sites (Memorial La Jolla, Encinitas, Green) take them twice a year. Those times start on the first business day of April and October. Other applications are not reviewed. Only send one application.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 service hours; 2 to 4 hours a week depending on age and position
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must give one 4-hour shift a week for at least six months in a row and at least 100 hours. They cannot take summer-only or school-break-only volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a volunteer reference form, then interview, attend a 2-hour orientation, pass a background check and health screening.
notes: The health screening asks for proof of vaccines, a flu shot, immunity to measles, mumps, rubella and varicella, a Tdap shot, and a TB test within the last 3 months. Ask your parent to start gathering records early. Questions: vmcvolunteer@hhs.sccgov.org.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours

who_can_apply: High school students. The page gives no narrower age or grade range. Space is limited to 12 teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application on the Teens page. Only completed forms are considered. Questions: outreach@sdmart.org.
notes: Closed right now. Check the page around late summer 2027 for the next application.
duration: October 2026 to end of June 2027; monthly meetings on Zoom with several in-person events
pay_detail: No stipend or fee stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 with an IEP, a 504 plan or other proof of a disability. Tacoma Public Schools students and other students can join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the ANEW form linked on the Tacoma Public Schools summer credential page. Contact Stacy Kidd, who is listed on the page.
notes: The Tacoma Public Schools page says this is not an official Jobs 253 program. ANEW location is Lincoln High School per the page. The page lists Cohort 2 as July 13 to 16 but also says M to F, so confirm dates with ANEW. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 40 hours of training. 2026 cohorts: July 6 to 10 and July 13 to 16, 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., at Lincoln High School
pay_detail: Paid training. $500 completion stipend.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grades 9 to 12 in a high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool program when they apply. Tides is the easiest level (any high school-aged person); Currents is the hands-on volunteer level.
how_to_apply: Attend a required online info session, then complete the application, then interview. Accepted teens do training before starting shifts. Questions: YOA@seattleaquarium.org.
notes: The page says its timeline is rough and may change. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
duration: One school year or one summer; at least 8 activities of about 3 to 5 hours each; can stay until the summer after senior year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not mention a cost.

who_can_apply: High school-aged youth who care about leadership, community and art. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the TAG page when the application opens in spring. The process includes a virtual interview.
notes: The page gives only a typical month (May), so watch the page in spring. Questions: teenprograms@seattleartmuseum.org. SAM's other internships are for college students and early-career adults, not high schoolers. If you take the stipend, ask whether you need Washington parent and school papers for a minor.
duration: Thursday evenings, October to May
pay_detail: Members receive community-service learning credits or a stipend for taking part. The page does not give the stipend amount.

who_can_apply: Ages are not stated on the YouthForce page. Contact the program to ask.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button for the TeamWork Internship or the Contact Us buttons on the YouthForce page. Call (206) 436-1843 if urgent.
notes: The page does not give ages, pay amounts, or an application window. Ask about age and school rules before applying. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid internships. Pay amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Priority goes to teens with limited access to STEM role models or science resources.
how_to_apply: Apply online when a new session opens (see the Burke-ology page). Join the e-newsletter for dates.
notes: Not paid. The page lists no meeting dates for the session; the e-newsletter is the way to get them.
duration: Sessions run by topic (a spring 2026 session studied paleobotany); dates are posted on the Burke e-newsletter
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: People 16 and over for some positions and 18 and over for others. You must meet the minimum age when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online during an open period (you have one hour to finish), complete online training and forms within 2 weeks, do a 1-hour virtual group interview, then accept a placement. Onboarding includes a Washington State background check, an in-person health screening and a 90-minute orientation. Email VolunteerServices@seattlechildrens.org or call 206-987-4655.
notes: The youth service projects page (for ages under 16, such as donation drives or junior guilds) still carries a COVID-era notice, so it may be out of date. Nearly all shifts are weekdays starting between 9am and 2pm. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
duration: Most shifts are 3 hours on the same day and time every week; at least 6 months in a row (check each role)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a badge and free on-site parking.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 who live close enough to travel to downtown Seattle. You need no research experience. You must have a Social Security Number or ITIN to take part.
how_to_apply: Apply online and send a letter of support. You must go to an orientation in person. In 2026 it was May 21, 4 to 5:30 p.m.
notes: Competitive: the 2026 lab has capacity for 24 students. The 2026 stipend is $2,000 to cover transportation and meals, and the IRS treats it as reportable income. Not a medical program and no patient contact. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 4 weeks, weekdays 8:30 am to 3 pm (2026: July 13 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Free. A stipend is paid to cover transportation and meals (amount not read).

who_can_apply: Students now in grades 10 to 12. Grades 10 and 11 go first. You must have taken at least one science course. You must live close enough to travel to downtown Seattle. You need a device with internet.
how_to_apply: Online application when the next cycle opens. Check the page.
notes: Hybrid (virtual and in person). Each research consultation also has a stipend, amount not stated. Breakfast and lunch are provided at the in-person training; students arrange their own transportation. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Four 1.5-hour training sessions (the 2025 training day was a Saturday, Nov. 1, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.), then monthly 1-hour hybrid sessions and consultations through the year
pay_detail: $200 training stipend

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 by the start date, live in the Seattle metro area (map on the page), and have valid ID and proof of US work eligibility. New-to-environment teens are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Online application at King County. No resume or cover letter. Answer the supplemental questions in detail. About 30 applicants get a 30 minute online interview.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). Only 12 interns in 2026. Interns meet in downtown Seattle and are encouraged to ride transit, which is free for youth.
duration: About 5 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 27 hours a week (2026: July 7 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: $22 an hour in 2026

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 22. You must complete the Cadet Program Physical Ability Test, meet attendance expectations and want to be a Seattle firefighter.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Fire Cadet application and email it with the required documents to SFD_Cadets@seattle.gov. See the selection process guidelines on the page.
notes: This is training, not a paid job. The city page also describes the department as encouraging women, people of color, immigrants and refugees to apply.
duration: Saturdays 8 a.m. to noon
pay_detail: Initial cost $95 plus $10 a month dues. Extra fees for special trips. Financial help is available. You buy your own uniform and safety shoes.

who_can_apply: High school students entering senior year who are 16 or older by the program start. You need strong science interest. You must live in Greater Seattle or nearby. Out-of-state and international students are not accepted. You must be free for all eight weeks and able to do a Zoom interview.
how_to_apply: Online application with short essays, email addresses for two references (they get a recommendation link after you submit), a PDF transcript and a PDF resume. Applicants must be able to attend a Zoom interview with the selection committee.
notes: Highly competitive and designed for students without much research experience. Fred Hutch does not provide or arrange housing, and interns arrange their own transportation. In Washington there is no permit the teen carries: the employer must hold a minor work permit endorsement, and a parent/guardian (and the school during the school year) signs a parent authorization form (Parent Authorization for Summer Work if hired during summer break only) before the minor starts.
duration: 8 weeks full time (2026: June 22 to Aug 14)
pay_detail: Paid internship; the amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Up to 18 high school students in the WANIC Skill Center service area. Chosen by lottery plus a meeting with a program leader. First-time participants get priority.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the WANIC summer course site during the application window. Then meet with a program leader and your family.
notes: Meet daily at the Riverview Learning Center in Carnation. Transport to field sites is provided. You must attend all 5 weeks. Questions: education@mtsgreenway.org. The page states a $1,800 stipend for full attendance and 1.0 CTE credit toward graduation.
duration: 5 weeks, Mon to Fri, 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM (2026: June 29 to Aug 4)
pay_detail: Stipend plus credit toward graduation. The amount is not stated on this page. A gear kit is provided.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to help at the front desk. You must be 18 or older for patient units and clinics. If you are under 18, a parent must sign. You can only work Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it reopens and pick an in-person orientation date. Send proof of MMR, chickenpox and Tdap shots (and a flu shot October to March). Finish about three hours of online training, then pass a Washington State background check.
notes: Applications with missing shot records are denied, with no exemptions. It can take a few months to hear back. The volunteer office does not set up doctor shadowing. Questions: hmcvol@uw.edu.
duration: Four hours a week for six months in a row. No summer-only spots in the main program.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: High school students in the Seattle area who care about modern art.
how_to_apply: The only call for applications found is from 2023-24, so check the Henry teen page or ask the museum if a new call is open. Submit the Call for Applications form when it is open.
notes: The teen page lists ages 14 to 18 but the application page found is old (2023). The page does not state cost; confirm cost and the current cycle before relying on it.
duration: Weekly meetings through the school year
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12 in the school year after the summer. Only six spots. You do not need to be a history fan.
how_to_apply: The page says the 2026 deadline has passed. Check back in spring 2027 for information about next year's session (details on the History Lab page).
notes: Very small group (6 teens). Based at MOHAI with some field trips. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday 10 am to 4 pm (2026: July 27 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the work

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18. You may serve for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Watch the YAB page for the next application. Questions go to YAB@MOPOP.org.
notes: The page does not say when the next call opens or whether members are paid. Email YAB@MOPOP.org to ask.
duration: Meets every other week during the school year; up to three years
pay_detail: The page does not say if members are paid or if there is a cost.

who_can_apply: Teens and camp grads ages 13 to 17. All-Time Belayer: ages 13 to 17. Junior Counselor: ages 15 to 17. You do not need camp or climbing experience; training is given.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CIT page when applications open in March 2027. Questions: summercamp@mountaineers.org.
notes: A nonprofit summer camp, not Seattle Parks. Pick the weeks that fit your schedule. Unpaid volunteer role; Washington L&I says its minor work rules apply to employees, not volunteers.
duration: All-Time Belayer: 9 am to noon, at least 6 days. Junior Counselor: 9 am to 4 pm, at least 2 weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Junior Counselors can join a Camp Alumni Adventure trip at a highly discounted rate.

who_can_apply: The page says anyone age 16 and above can volunteer. Youth use the Youth Volunteer Application. One reference is required (the Youth Reference Form). Not all roles are open to youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth (16-17) Volunteer form. Attach the Youth Reference Form. The Volunteer Office reviews it and may set up an interview. New volunteers go to an orientation.
notes: Exact museum address is not on the page. The page does not state an upper age limit of 17; max_age is kept at 17 only because the card needs an integer, so confirm with the Volunteer Office (volunteers@museumofflight.org). Not a paid job.
duration: The museum asks for 8 hours a month; hours vary by role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Mentorship is for ages 13 to 21. The paid internship is for ages 15.5 to 21 and requires finishing the mentorship first. An E-13 form is required under 18.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the mentor program. Links are on the page. Go to all four Saturdays. Then apply and interview for the summer internship. You must apply again each year.
notes: Food and supplies are provided. Mentorship location rotates around Seattle (North, Central, Southeast, Southwest). Interns can return for up to 3 years. Work permit rule not stated on the page.
duration: Mentorship: 4 Saturdays (28 hours), offered 5 times a year. Internship: 8 summer weeks, 20 hours a week.
pay_detail: Mentorship: $300 stipend if you attend all 4 Saturdays. Internship: Seattle minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour in 2026.

who_can_apply: Seattle Parks summer jobs are open to ages 16 and up (18 and up for some positions). Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross Lifeguarding, First Aid and CPR/AED certification. The Red Cross course requires you to be at least 15 on or before the last class. You must also pass a swim test.
how_to_apply: Get Red Cross certified. Then apply on GovernmentJobs.com when a listing is active, or email an Aquatic Application (or resume and cover letter) to parksaquatics@seattle.gov, or give it to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle indoor pool. Hired lifeguards pass a background check, a physical and the NW Lifeguard Test. Call 206-684-4078.
notes: Red Cross certifications last 2 years. The cost of the Red Cross course is not stated on the Parks pages. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply).
duration: Summer-only at beaches and outdoor pools, or year-round at indoor pools
pay_detail: Listed on the Parks summer jobs page as 'starts at $26.92' (the unit is not stated on the page).

who_can_apply: Jobs are open to ages 16 and up. Some jobs need you to be 18 (for example the disability programs). Some need a WA driver license or certifications. Read each job posting.
how_to_apply: Apply to each job on the City of Seattle jobs site through the Open Temp Jobs link. Many recreation programs hire through the nonprofit Associated Recreation Council instead.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). See the separate Seattle Parks lifeguard and aquatics training card for guard training.
duration: Wading pools run mid June to Labor Day. Boat ramp jobs run May to September.
pay_detail: Starting pay in the 2026 postings: $26.92 an hour (wading pool attendant, lifeguard), $33.47 (aquatics customer service), $34.08 (boat ramp ranger)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 and in grades 6 to 12. You must first finish at least one cohort of the Youth Leadership Program (40 hours in a quarter).
how_to_apply: Finish the Youth Leadership Program first. Then apply when the window opens. You need a Participant E-13 form for internships. Contact the Late Night and Youth Leadership Coordinator listed on the page.
notes: Paid City of Seattle intermittent employee job. Sites include Bitter Lake, Garfield, Meadowbrook, Rainier Beach, Southwest and Van Asselt. Spaces are limited. The page does not mention a work permit.
duration: Two 6-month cohorts a year: January to June and June to December
pay_detail: City of Seattle minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour in 2026.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 9 to 18, aimed at youth of color. Auditions are held each spring.
how_to_apply: Audition in the spring. Contact the director listed on the page for sign-up details.
notes: Breakfast and lunch are provided. The page says costs are paid by ages 9 to 15 and stipends are paid at the end. Stipend for ages 9 to 12 is $300 per the page. 2026 auditions were April 17 and 18. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 2026: rehearsals June 29 to Aug 27, shows Aug 28 to 30
pay_detail: Cost $350 for ages 13 to 15 ($400 for ages 9 to 12) but participants get a stipend: $599 for ages 13 to 15. Ages 16 to 18 are paid minimum wage ($21.30 per hour in 2026) every 2 weeks.

who_can_apply: Pre-Employment Training is for ages 13 to 18, and you can take it once every 2 years. It is the prerequisite for Parks paid internships (Teen Late Night, Summer, Community Learning Centers), which are for ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: Email PKS_Teen_Employment@seattle.gov (phone 206-684-4575) for details and to apply. The page also lists career readiness workshops (resumes, mock interviews, food handler permit help) at Teen Life Centers and community centers.
notes: Youth may do one paid internship at a time. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply). The page also mentions free college tours for Seattle Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12.
duration: 7 weeks, 14 hours total, offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter
pay_detail: After finishing the training you may earn a $300 stipend or Service Learning credit toward high school graduation. Internship pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, full-time students with a 2.5 GPA or higher, no felony or serious misdemeanor, and able to pass a background check and oral interview. Under 18 needs a parent signature.
how_to_apply: Email Officer Tre Smith (tre.smith@seattle.gov) to attend a meeting. Attend 2 to 4 monthly meetings in a row, then get the application, then a background check and an oral board with current Explorers.
notes: Program is taught in English. Contact name is as listed on the page and may change.
duration: At least 2 meetings and 1 community event a month
pay_detail: Free to join. Hours count as service learning for high school.

who_can_apply: BIPOC girls and gender expansive youth ages 16 to 19 who live or go to school in or near Seattle and King County.
how_to_apply: Applications closed. Questions: aaron@powerfulvoices.org.
notes: Powerful Voices also lists other paid teen internships on its For Young People page (Activistas for ages 14 to 19, Artivism, DYVAS). Those pages do not post pay or dates, so they are not listed separately.
duration: About 3 months (2026: June 23 to Sept 22), about 5 to 7 hours a week, hybrid
pay_detail: $1,712 stipend, paid monthly

who_can_apply: BIPOC girls and gender expansive youth ages 13 to 19 (BIPOC adults 20 and up can also be fellows). Hybrid, Seattle area and online.
how_to_apply: Applications closed. Questions: healingjustice@powerfulvoices.org.
notes: Ask Powerful Voices whether the stipend counts as a job under Washington youth work rules.
duration: May to December 2026, 2 to 3 hours a week (more around events)
pay_detail: $20 an hour, up to $2,000 total

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Grade rules are not listed. You need two recommendations, an interview, a health screening and orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application (Volgistics link on the page), two recommendations on the provided forms or in your own letters, then an interview with Volunteer Services.
notes: Volunteers who turn 18 and keep going must complete a national background check. Ask Volunteer Services about openings and the health screening.
duration: 48 hours, usually over about 3 months

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors from 22 partner high schools in Highline, Federal Way, Tukwila and Tahoma. Students from other districts need an Inter-District Agreement from their home district. You need to be on track to graduate. No minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Apply in the online portal during the open window, then a lottery is used if there are more applicants than seats. Talk to your school counselor. Admissions: 206-631-7322.
notes: Consortium districts provide buses. Others provide their own ride. The Aeronautical Science program meets after school at The Museum of Flight.
duration: 1 or 2 years, half of each school day
pay_detail: Tuition-free. Earns 3.0 high school credits for a full year, with college credit options.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Grades: entering 9th grade (fall 2026) through high school seniors. Selected teens must give a copy of a Social Security card and complete a W-9.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form linked on the SafeFutures internship page. If you are picked, you have 2 business days to say yes.
notes: Very competitive: the page accepts 20 applicants. The page URL says 2023 but the content is the 2026 program. The 2026 page states no stipend amount. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, July 2 to Aug 14 in 2026, Monday to Thursday, 12 pm to 6 pm
pay_detail: Stipend paid after successful completion. 2026 page does not state the amount (older SafeFutures pages said $1,000).

who_can_apply: Crew members ages 14 to 18, currently in high school or recent high school graduates. Crew Leaders must be 21 or older.
how_to_apply: The page links to SCA's job listings. Call the SCA Seattle Office at (206) 693-3147.
notes: The page says "Check back next spring for our 2026 summer positions!", so the text may be out of date. Call (206) 693-3147 to ask when the next season is posted.
duration: July to August, about 35 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live or study in Seattle. No transportation experience needed. Only 15 spots.
how_to_apply: Online application, about 15 to 30 minutes. Selected teens under 18 need a parental consent form and a photo release form.
notes: Held at the Seattle Municipal Tower, 700 5th Ave. Youth 18 and under ride transit free. The page lists the 2026 application window as opening May 26 and closing June 16.
duration: About 4 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays 10 AM to 3 PM (2026: Aug 4 to 27)
pay_detail: $600 stipend at the end (you fill out a tax form)

who_can_apply: Teens who are 15 or older by May 19, 2027, not older than 19 during the program, enrolled in high school, with a Washington address and proof of US work eligibility.
how_to_apply: Create an account on Submittable, answer short questions, and get two letters of recommendation. Top applicants get a virtual interview.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). Competitive and interviews are not guaranteed. TIPS pays you, not the nonprofit. Free ORCA transit cards for youth up to 18 are mentioned on the page.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks, about 20 to 30 hours a week, plus 3 required training events
pay_detail: Seattle's minimum wage (projected $21.81 an hour in 2027), up to 160 hours, so up to about $3,490 before taxes

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Check the TeenTix Program Applications page to see the current round. The page is teentix.org/programs/apply.
notes: The page says there is no cost to participate and all New Guardians receive monthly stipends (amount not stated). The program page's only year reference is 2025-26, and the TeenTix applications page says 2026/27 applications are closed, with the next round opening in Spring 2027. Confirm with TeenTix that New Guard runs in the next cycle. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: School-year cohort (dates not stated)
pay_detail: Free to join. Monthly stipend, amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19, from grade 8 through early college. About 30 to 40 teens join each year. You must review at least one event during the school year.
how_to_apply: Check the TeenTix Program Applications page to see the current round. The page is teentix.org/programs/apply.
notes: The Newsroom runs from September to June on the school year schedule. It is good for building a writing portfolio. Ask TeenTix how much writers are paid.
duration: September to June
pay_detail: The page says writers are paid for their writing. The amount is not stated. You also get free press tickets to the events you review.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. Crew members must be able to do heavy lifting and work in rain or shine.
how_to_apply: The page does not list the steps to apply. Contact Suez Gebretsadik at (206) 633-0451 ext. 900 or suezgebretsadik@tilthalliance.org.
notes: Pay, dates and how to apply were not stated on the page. Confirm with the contact before you plan around it. These are temporary seasonal positions.
duration: Spring, summer and fall positions
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Washington state residents enrolled in a Washington high school in 10th or 11th grade. No coding experience needed. The program aims to include economically disadvantaged and future first-generation college students; the home page says it is open to all rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline (every application submitted on time is reviewed equally). Questions: cic@cs.washington.edu.
notes: Students must be able to get to the UW campus on their own. Absences are limited: after four absences students are dismissed. The stipend is described as a stipend, not a wage. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday, about 9am to 3pm (2026: July 6 to 30)
pay_detail: Free. Every mentee gets a $1,200 stipend; lunch and materials are provided. No housing, and bus passes are not provided.

who_can_apply: Any Washington state high school sophomore or junior in the 2025-2026 school year can apply. You need no engineering experience. You get yourself to and from the UW Seattle campus.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in March 2027.
notes: Free of cost to participants. The page is an introductory program for students curious about engineering. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 1 week, Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm (2026: July 20 to 24)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students (page lists rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders and graduating seniors; no age range stated). No business experience required.
how_to_apply: Apply through partner Summer Springboard's online portal (Apply now link on the page). Program questions go to the program contact listed on the page.
notes: Expensive paid pre-college program from a real university. The page says students can attend both experiences during a single extended stay, but it does not name a one-week Business Startup Bootcamp.
duration: 2 weeks (2026 session: July 5 to 17)
pay_detail: Commuter tuition $4,498 (lunch, a course, excursions, 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday). Residential adds $3,000. Commuters can join weekend excursions for $125 per day. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Washington state high school sophomores and juniors interested in nursing. You must be 16 before the first day of camp. The page says there are no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the 2027 application opens. For a waitlist spot or questions, use the inquiry form or email uwnursecamp@uw.edu.
notes: The camp provides breakfast, lunch and snacks each day. The 2027 camp dates are not posted yet. Join the email list on the page for updates.
duration: 1 week, day camp (2026: July 20 to 24)
pay_detail: Free to attend. You cover your own transportation, meals and any overnight housing.

who_can_apply: U.S. high school students who have finished eighth grade or equivalent by June 30 of the summer. If under 18 on the first day, you and a parent must sign an Under 18 form.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Summer Sessions form. Pay the $80 fee. Send the Under 18 form signed by you and a parent. Then sign up for courses once sign up opens.
notes: Costs real money and registration is first come, first served. Not a job or internship.
duration: Summer quarter (2026 started June 22)
pay_detail: $80 nonrefundable application fee plus UW Summer Sessions tuition (amount not read; see the UW tuition page).

who_can_apply: Community high school students. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Check the UW Medicine volunteering page in March 2027 for the application. For the waitlist, email uwmcvol@uw.edu.
notes: All UW Medicine volunteers must show required shots and pass a background check. The program does not offer job shadowing or internships. The adult program needs age 18 and a high school diploma, so the summer program is the teen route.
duration: Summer only (the page does not give the number of weeks)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Students in a public high school in Bellevue, Issaquah, Lake Washington, Mercer Island, Northshore, Riverview or Snoqualmie Valley. Private and homeschool students register with their local public high school. Outside students may join on a space-available basis with permission from their home district.
how_to_apply: Apply online through a WANIC parent account. Some in-district skill center classes use your school counselor instead. Questions: wanic@lwsd.org or 425-739-8400.
notes: Applications before March 31 get priority and are not first come, first served. Summer semester has no out-of-consortium students.
duration: Full school year (also a summer semester)
pay_detail: Tuition-free. You provide your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Anyone ages 13 to 19. All art levels welcome. Capacity is 15 students, first come, first served.
how_to_apply: Registration is first come, first served. Email youthcan@wingluke.org to ask about info sessions.
notes: Only 15 spots.
duration: After school, Wednesdays 4 to 6 p.m. The page gives no date for the group show.
pay_detail: Free. Students get a museum membership.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No prior experience required. The teen page does not state a minimum age; 15 teen volunteers were taken in 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Email teenambassadors@zoo.org for help. Sign up for recruitment updates at zoo.org/volunteer.
notes: The zoo's general volunteer program has its own rules (at least 16, one-year commitment, applications opening January 2027); those do not appear on the teen page. Applicants who identify with autism or ADHD can get application and interview support from Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: June to September: orientation day, at least 7 of 10 Wednesday meetings (3:30 to 6:30 pm), 20 volunteer hours between June 29 and Sept 6 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Active teen volunteers receive a $300 summer stipend to help with transportation, lunches and shoes. No participation fee is listed.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Clubs are school based. A map on the page shows partner schools, or you can ask to start a new club.
how_to_apply: Check the school map and join your school club, or email yesc@seattleymca.org to start one or join events. Teens can also volunteer as event support.
notes: The page says almost 1,500 young leaders took part in 2023-24. It does not give event dates for this year.
duration: School year clubs; meetings last 30 minutes to 2 hours
pay_detail: No cost stated.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 years old and have First Aid and CPR certification (training is available). Overnight camp and BOLD & GOLD jobs need you to be 18.
how_to_apply: Apply for a Summer Day Camp job on the YMCA of Greater Seattle careers page. Questions: recruiting@seattleymca.org.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). The page also lists lifeguard and swim instructor jobs, which need to be at least 16 at branches or 18 for overnight camp. Y childcare discount is mentioned.
duration: Season runs June 20 to Aug 26 (start dates vary by location). Shifts are 8 hours, Monday to Friday, between 6:45 am and 6:15 pm.
pay_detail: Starts at $21.30 an hour

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Other eligibility rules are not listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Today button on the page, which links to a YMCA job posting. You can also contact Ann Beasley at abeasley@seattleymca.org.
notes: Only 17 and 18 year olds are teens here. Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). Confirm the pay and start date before planning around it.
duration: 10 weeks
pay_detail: $20.97 an hour for up to 135 hours over 9 weeks. The first week is unpaid.

who_can_apply: Any student in grades 8 to 12. No experience needed. Delegations meet at YMCA branches in Bellevue, Seattle, Northshore, Sammamish, Snoqualmie Valley and nearby.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page and the Y connects you to the closest delegation. Email ygseattleyag@seattleymca.org with questions.
notes: The page also describes Mock Trial for grades 6 to 12, but no branch-based Mock Trial teams are offered in 2026-27.
duration: School year, with a statewide conference May 5 to 8, 2027
pay_detail: 2026-27: delegation fee $175 for Y members or $225 for others, plus conference fee $500. Financial help and payment plans are available.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19 who live in Seattle or go to school in Seattle. Two-year term. Parent or guardian consent is needed if under 18.
how_to_apply: Email SeattleYouthCommission@seattle.gov to hear when applications reopen. Then apply. If you are under 18, add the parent consent form.
notes: Not a paid job. Good for civic and government interest. The page does not list a deadline.
duration: Two-year term; monthly hybrid meetings on the 4th Saturday of each month, 9 to 11 am, at City Hall
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fees. Can count toward Seattle Public Schools service hours.

who_can_apply: Age 16 to 24 at the start of the program (you can apply at 15 if you will be 16 by the start date). You must live in Seattle or attend Seattle Public Schools or Seattle Colleges, and household income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (for example $81,700 for 1 person, $116,650 for 4).
how_to_apply: Create an account and complete the online application at youthconnect.powerappsportals.us (the page links a help guide). The 250 internship spots are chosen by lottery. Pathways requires finishing SYEP Foundations or passing the Assessment of Skill.
notes: Proof of authorization to work in the U.S. is required for the internship, and an SSN or ITIN is needed to receive stipends and take part. The SYEP page does not mention work permits. Placements include City departments, which Washington L&I says are exempt from state child labor rules ('Public entities, including state and municipal governments, are not subject to Washington's child labor rules'; federal rules still apply), and private businesses and nonprofits, which are not exempt, so ask your placement about the parent/school authorization form. Questions: SYEP@seattle.gov or 206-386-1375.
duration: Internship about 6 weeks (July 6 to Aug 18, 2026). Foundations: October 2026 to March 2027 (tentative), 2-hour weekly sessions.
pay_detail: Internship: at least Seattle's minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour. Learn & Earn Foundations: $325 stipend at the end of each module. Pathways: monthly stipend, amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 who identify as Black, Indigenous or a person of color, are in grades 10 to 12, and can attend every Tuesday and Thursday 4:30 to 7 PM for 17 weeks. Priority goes to teens without arts classes at school.
how_to_apply: Apply on the page. About 25 applicants are chosen to interview for 10 spots.
notes: Only 10 spots. Graduates can later be hired for Youth in Focus photo jobs. Exact dates are not set on the page.
duration: 17 weeks, about 5 hours a week in person plus 1 to 2 hours of homework
pay_detail: $1,400 stipend

who_can_apply: Teens who take part in Youth in Focus programs (ages 13 to 19) and have finished at least one of its free after-school photography classes.
how_to_apply: Finish at least one free after-school class (register on the Class Registration page). Staff pick a student for each event and send the details.
notes: Classes are free or pay what you can, and equipment, snacks and bus passes are provided. The page does not say whether the stipend is treated as a job for work-permit purposes, so ask.
duration: Event by event; students rotate
pay_detail: Stipend check mailed after each event. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students ages 6 to 18. Many students join through partner schools; some workshops allow direct sign-up.
how_to_apply: Check the calendar on the 826 Valencia site or contact a Writing Center.
notes: All 826 Valencia programs are free, and most students join through partner schools. The stipended Youth Leadership Advisory Board (grades 8 to 12) and Black Literary Achievement Club are listed on the SFPL page; the stipend amount is not posted.
duration: Varies
pay_detail: Free programs; some leadership roles are stipended (amounts not posted)

who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Preference goes to students in Breakthrough now. It also goes to people who are or were Breakthrough volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill in the notify form on the BLP page to hear when the summer 2027 application opens.
notes: Breakthrough's separate Teaching Fellow job is a paid summer teaching residency with housing for people from outside SF and does not say it is for high schoolers, so it is not listed here. Located at 350 Masonic Ave.
duration: Summer 2026 ran orientation June 15 to 18, then June 22 to July 31, 2026, about 6 weeks
pay_detail: Rate not posted. Paid through San Francisco's Opportunities for All program. Some hours also count toward school volunteer requirements.

who_can_apply: Current 9th or 10th graders at an SFUSD school, with a 2.5 GPA and a C or higher in science and math, authorized to work in the US, able to commit 2 to 3 years through high school, and able to get to the Academy after school and on Saturdays.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in February 2027. Contact CiS@calacademy.org.
notes: SFUSD students only. Sign up for the Academy's Youth Programs mailing list to hear when applications open. Questions: CiS@calacademy.org.
duration: 2 to 3 years through graduation
pay_detail: Paid above minimum wage (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: SFUSD high school students, through a partnership with City College. Talk to your high school counselor about which classes are offered. Non-SFUSD students, or SFUSD students who want a class their school does not offer, use the Concurrent Enrollment page.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: dualenrollment@ccsf.edu. Non-SFUSD students use the CCSF Concurrent Enrollment page.
notes: Classes can be at your high school or at a CCSF location. A permission consent form for high school students is linked on the page. Grade and credit rules are not stated on the page, so ask your counselor.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. Register with the Google Form on the DCYF listing.
how_to_apply: Register using the form linked from the sf.gov youth opportunities page. Bring a resume if you have one.
notes: The page does not list which employers will attend. It is a free event, not a job offer.
duration: Wed Oct 14, 2026, 12 to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Employers share job openings, but the page does not say if those jobs are paid.

who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students. No prior experience needed.
how_to_apply: Watch the Department of Elections high school programs page for the next application. Questions: hsp@sfgov.org or 415-558-6100.
notes: Same page: if you will be 16 by the next Election Day you can apply to be a high school poll worker, with a stipend up to $245. A poll worker application for the November 2026 election was due to be posted there in mid-August.
duration: About 2 weeks: Sept 14 to 27 in fall 2026, plus a 90 minute in-person training
pay_detail: Unpaid. Ambassadors get a participation certificate signed by the Mayor and community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school age students, 15 to 18 for first-time Explainers (up to 20 for returning ones). Must be able to get a work permit, attend all training dates and work the whole school year or summer session. No science background needed.
how_to_apply: When open, apply on the Exploratorium Current Openings page under the job title High School Explainer. Questions: hsesupervisors@exploratorium.edu.
notes: About 130 paid positions a year across two cohorts. The Current Openings list did not show on my read, so check it for a live posting. A separate PACE program serves ages 17 to 21.
duration: A summer session or a school-year session, with over 60 hours of training (20 before working with visitors)
pay_detail: Paid job; the wage is not on the program page

who_can_apply: Cadets must attend high school in San Francisco (or equivalent) or live in the City and County of San Francisco. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the academy's website.
notes: The site does not list an age range or application dates, so ask the academy. It is a project of the SF Black Firefighters Association. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Saturdays 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., following the SFUSD calendar. A 2025 news article said 15 weeks each fall.
pay_detail: Free to join. Cadets get breakfast, lunch and a bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 and in high school. The page says teens on Heart&Sole teams must identify as female, and males are welcome on Girls on the Run teams. Needs a completed reference, a signed waiver (parent signs if under 18) and the Junior Coach application. Background check at 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Coach application on the Girls on the Run Bay Area site. Email admin@gotrbayarea.org or call (415) 863-8942 to ask about late spots or the next season.
notes: The Oct 12, 2026 date on the sf.gov listing is for adult coaches (18 and up), not Junior Coaches. Teams meet at least once a week.
duration: 8 to 10 weeks, 1.5 to 3 hours per week; season starts early September, 5K on Nov 14, 2026
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 (high school). Priority goes to youth underrepresented in tech, students at high schools with few or no computer science classes, and girls and LGBTQIA+ youth. Online classes are for San Francisco students only.
how_to_apply: Pick a class. Then register on the Mission Bit Classes page when registration opens.
notes: Mission Bit's Tech Start career prep is ages 18 to 26, not for most high schoolers. College Connections (Nov 7, 2026, 10:30 a.m. to noon at Chase Center, grades 9 to 12) closes registration Oct 27, 2026 per sf.gov.
duration: Semester long. Fall 2026 classes ran Sep 8 to Dec 4, 2026.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: San Francisco youth ages 14 to 17 (the DCYF newsletter lists grades 9 and 10 for this round). Apply through the JCYC Workhub.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the JCYC Workhub (jcycworkhub.org). Ask the YMCA contact on the page about your neighborhood site.
notes: Pay rate is not stated on the pages, so ask your site. Contact the Buchanan YMCA ((415) 931-9622) about eligibility.
duration: School year: Oct to April, with an 8 hour per week internship Jan to April. Summer: June to August, 20 hours per week.
pay_detail: Paid work experience (hourly rate not posted on the program pages)

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Aimed at 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or not working.
how_to_apply: Apply on the New Door intake portal linked from their site. The application link is on the official page.
notes: Mainly for 17 year olds and older who are not in a regular school path; not the usual fit for a student who is in school. Pay is not stated on the pages.
duration: 6 months
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 24 who live and/or go to school in San Francisco, per the JCYC Workhub OFA page.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the JCYC Workhub, complete the application and submit before the spring deadline.
notes: JCYC runs the applications. B2SF and the OFA fellowships share an application with other youth programs. Your interests decide where you are placed.
duration: B2SF is 6 weeks; OFA length not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Paid; the hourly rate and hours are not posted on the program pages

who_can_apply: California residents ages 16 and 17 who are US citizens and not in prison for a felony or ruled mentally unable to vote by a court.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form at registertovote.ca.gov (linked from the Secretary of State page).
notes: Not a job or internship, but a real civic step. Your registration becomes active when you turn 18. Citizenship is required.
duration: A few minutes
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students (there are separate college tracks). The application page says details are coming soon.
how_to_apply: Use the High School Internship application page. Questions: sfprojectpull1996@gmail.com.
notes: The pages do not list age, pay or a deadline yet. Check the application page in early 2027.
duration: About 8 weeks (per the SFPUC page)
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted on the program page)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 in San Francisco.
how_to_apply: Email yep@sfgov.org or call Yuri Ugarte at 415-452-3863. The page's email link shows rec-yep@sfgov.org, so confirm which address works.
notes: This page replaced the older Workreation name on the department site. An older listing says applicants need work-permit papers and no citizenship is required.
duration: Up to 25 hours per week in summer; 10 hours per week in the school year
pay_detail: Pay not posted on the program page

who_can_apply: No minimum age is listed for youth volunteers. If a branch is not on the application form, it cannot take volunteers right now.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form at https://on.sfpl.org/yva
notes: FOG Readers tutoring takes some volunteers age 15 and up. It needs a 6 month commitment and fingerprinting. The same page lists paid teen jobs. YELL is a summer job, and applications open each March. The Youth Advisory Board closed applications for this year on Sept 14.
duration: Ongoing; some roles start late October or early November
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students from San Francisco's southeast neighborhoods; internships start after junior year.
how_to_apply: The SFPUC page does not list an application. It says SFUSD students are referred through SFUSD's Career and Technical Education office, so ask them or the SFPUC workforce team.
notes: Narrow neighborhood focus (southeast San Francisco). The same SFPUC page also lists YouthWorks and Project Pull.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)

who_can_apply: Nature Trail: ages 12 to 14. Junior Zoologists: ages 15 to 17. Leadership Fellows: entering grades 10 to 12 in fall 2026 (ages 15 to 17 per the zoo's volunteer page).
how_to_apply: Each track has its own page. Nature Trail and Junior Zoologists include an online interview. Questions: naturetrail@sfzoo.org (Nature Trail), izvolunteer@sfzoo.org (Junior Zoologists), luked@sfzoo.org (Leadership Fellows), or (415) 753-7080.
notes: Located in San Francisco (a long trip from Sacramento). Applications were closed when checked. The Leadership Fellows page gave 2026 dates, so check for 2027 dates.
duration: Nature Trail: Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day, at least 7 days a month. Junior Zoologists: 2 days a month for 6 months. Leadership Fellows: Mon to Fri, 8:15 am to 4 pm, mid June to early Aug (2026: June 15 to Aug 7).
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: Nature Trail and Junior Zoologists require buying a $40 uniform.

who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students who may have limited opportunities to engage with biomedical research, per the page. Grade range and other rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Email the program first, through the Contact Us link on the ImmunoX site, because the page is out of date. The page links a Google Form for 2026 camper applications.
notes: Re-read the ImmunoX page on 2026-10-09. It is still titled ImmunoExplore - Summer Camp 2025. It says 2026 Camper Applications are now open and links the Google Form. It posts no grade range, camp dates or deadlines, so none are listed here. Confirm dates and grades with ImmunoX before applying.
duration: Not stated (summer camp; dates not posted)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Current juniors at an SFUSD high school or an SF public charter school, no exceptions. Grades and science background are not used to pick students; low-income and first-generation college students are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Fill in the interest form to hear when the application opens, then submit the online application. About 50 students are interviewed for 25 spots; results come by email in April.
notes: The SEP high school programs page says 2025-26 is the final year of a program and that there will be no summer internship for 2026; it is not clear which program that means, while the intern page invites 2027 interest. Confirm with SEP at 415-364-8077.
duration: 8 weeks
pay_detail: $4,500 paid after completing the program (35 hours a week for 8 weeks)

who_can_apply: Mainly public high school students in San Francisco. Programs are free.
how_to_apply: Call (415) 574-8137. Or send an email to info@youthartexchange.org.
notes: Also runs summer camps for grades 3 to 5 and classes for adults. The page does not mention paid internships or exact ages.
duration: After school
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: 11th or 12th graders (rising juniors, rising seniors and graduating seniors) who live in or go to school in San Francisco and can get a work permit. Youth Leadership Team members must have finished a full YouthWorks session.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the JCYC Workhub portal. Expect a short application and an interview step.
notes: Interns work in City departments such as the SFPUC, the Library and SFO. Former interns can return as paid Youth Leadership Team members. Ask JCYC about work permit help.
duration: School-year and summer internships
pay_detail: $19.61 per hour for school-year interns; $20.36 per hour for Youth Leadership Team members

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 11, at least 14 years old, who have finished 8th grade and have a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Seniors are pointed to the college or adult program after graduation.
how_to_apply: Use the 'High school volunteers (junior volunteers)' online application during the window. A follow-up email asks for your transcript and parental consent, then teacher referrals, an interview and orientation.
notes: The hospital calls this program highly sought after and competitive, and says onboarding can take up to three months. Health requirements after acceptance include MMR, varicella, Tdap, COVID, flu and TB testing. Contact scv.volunteers@sharp.com or 619-502-3606. The two official pages differ by one day on the close date; use Nov 12 to be safe.
duration: Minimum 1 year, 2 to 4 hour shift once a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 who finished the Highwater Farm Summer Youth Program. You must commit to all 11 weeks.
how_to_apply: Start with the Summer Youth Program. Check the fall program page for details. Questions: savanna@highwaterfarm.org.
notes: Only for teens who completed the summer program.
duration: 11 weeks, Friday and Saturday (late August to early November)
pay_detail: Bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated), plus fresh produce on set days.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. You must be able to commit to the whole 7 weeks.
how_to_apply: The application will be on the program page in January 2027. Look for it then. Questions: savanna@highwaterfarm.org.
notes: Farm address: 7001 County Road 346, Silt, CO 81652. The 2027 pay rate is not posted. Page does not say which towns qualify.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 8 AM to 3 PM (2026: June 15 to July 30)
pay_detail: $15.16 per hour (2026), plus job training and fresh produce on set days.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 15 years of age to work for SFPR Aquatics. For the course, you must be 15 on the last day of class.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the lifeguard class on the city page. Call (605) 367-POOL with questions.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the certification page, and you must be 15 on the last day of the class. The city says finishing the course does not guarantee a job.
duration: Course runs Friday to Sunday. Job length not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Paid job. Pay rate not stated on the program page. The course costs $185 per person, or it is free if you commit to work for SFPR.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be age 14 or older and have finished 7th grade, with a parent's consent if under 18. Teen Advisory Board members must have finished 7th grade and be in public, private or home school.
how_to_apply: Print the volunteer form, get a parent to sign if you are under 18, and take it to any branch. Join the Teen Advisory Board when the next form opens.
notes: The library says it may not be able to place every volunteer. Court-ordered community service is not accepted on the form. Advisory Board meetings are at the Caille Branch, 4100 S. Carnegie Cir., first Monday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. Next Teen Advisory Board dates are not posted; the 2026-27 cycle is closed.
duration: Advisory Board meets once a month for one hour, Oct 5, 2026 to May 3, 2027. General volunteer time is set with the branch.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Teen Advisory Board page says meetings 'qualify for volunteer hours'.

who_can_apply: High school students can register for summer classes through Open University without being admitted to SJSU.
how_to_apply: Register as an Open University student using the first-time or returning student steps on the SJSU Summer registration page. Questions: professionaled@sjsu.edu or 408-924-2670.
notes: You pay college tuition. The page does not state age, grade or approval rules for high schoolers or the cost, so ask Summer Session. For fall and spring the page points to the Dual Enrollment Program (dualenrollment@sjsu.edu).
duration: 5 or 10 week sessions (2026: June 1 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Price not on the page; ask Summer Session (see SJSU Fees, Payment and Refund)

who_can_apply: Middle school, high school and college students in career and technical education, in a school chapter. Virtual chapters exist for students without a classroom chapter.
how_to_apply: Ask your CTE teacher, or use the 12 Steps to Start a Chapter or Virtual Chapter on skillsusa.org. Phone 844-875-4557, email customercare@skillsusa.org.
notes: Most useful if your school has a trades or tech CTE pathway.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the program pages; ask your CTE teacher.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 10 to 12. The page describes it as an opportunity for Los Angeles teens.
how_to_apply: Closed now. Email youthprograms@skirball.org or use the inquiry form on the Skirball youth programs page.
notes: The same page offers TeenTix LA. It is a free pass for teens to visit museums and culture events across Los Angeles (la.teentix.org).
duration: October 2026 to May 2027, meeting online and in person
pay_detail: Paid stipend plus community service credit. The amount is not listed.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who are 18 or younger and either live in Skokie or attend a Skokie school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Service contact form to join the email list. Or email teenteam@skokielibrary.info. You can also come to an upcoming teen volunteer event.
notes: Some opportunities are only on school breaks or days off. If you need hours for a ticket or a court order, the page says to email the teen team with your name and school.
duration: Teen Library Council meets Thursday afternoons
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school student teams registered by a coach or teacher. Team size and cost are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: A teacher or coach pre-registers the team on the National Science Bowl coach site (apps.orau.gov/nsb-coach). You do not need all team details for step one.
notes: Needs a school team and coach. Volunteer sign-up info is due to be shared by December 2026 (no experience needed). Event is at SLAC, 2575 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park.
duration: One day, Feb 27, 2027

who_can_apply: High school students from all backgrounds. The page lists no age, grade or residency limits. Apply on the Kaleidoscope platform.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Kaleidoscope platform when the next cycle opens. It is linked from the SAGE site.
notes: The SAGE page says the camp is free and residential (overnight). The only dates posted are June 21 to 27, 2026. 2026 applications ran Feb 24 to Mar 17, so check the SAGE site in February.
duration: 1 week (2026: June 21 to 27)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 with a 3.0 GPA and strong math scores. You must be at a public or scholarship-funded private high school. You need a strong interest in computer science. Bay Area schools within the radius are preferred.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list on smash.org/programs and watch for the application. Contact devo@smash.org.
notes: Based in Oakland (2148 Broadway). SMASH Virtual is a separate online option for a national audience; its cost is not stated. SMASH Morehouse is for males and SMASH Spelman for females.
duration: One year with a residential summer
pay_detail: Free; tuition-free

who_can_apply: Students at partner high schools: Jefferson Union HSD, San Mateo Union HSD, South San Francisco USD, Sequoia Union HSD and Gateway charter school. Need a C or better to get college credit.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school (talk to your counselor), submit the Skyline application on CCCApply, then attend an enrollment workshop to register and get parent approval.
notes: Grades become part of a permanent college record and can affect financial aid and college admission. Contacts on the page: hendrieg@smccd.edu or fuentesa@smccd.edu. Canada College and College of San Mateo run their own dual enrollment pages, not checked here.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: 16 or older (by June 2 in the 2026 cycle), current junior or senior, 2.5 GPA or higher, attends an eligible school in the service area, no relatives who work for the internship host, own transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Sacramento Works site before the deadline. Steps: application review, document check, computer random drawing (55 candidates), work readiness workshops and video interview, manager review, in-person interview. Up to 25 interns are chosen.
notes: Questions: SacramentoWorksFor.Youth@seta.net. Random drawing means even qualified students may not be picked. Check the school list on the Sacramento Works SMUD page. Age rule and school-area details come from the 2026 posting; confirm for 2027.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 31)
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour (2026), about 36 hours per week.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 6 to 12. Grades 11 and 12 attend their own session.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form on the program page. Returning campers who did not get an early form should contact the team right away. If the camp is full, join the waiting list on the page.
notes: Campers stay in dorms with staff watching around the clock. The 2026 camp had 120 spots.
duration: One week. Grades 6 to 10: July 12 to 17, 2026. Grades 11 and 12: July 19 to 24, 2026.
pay_detail: No pay. The camp is free. Spots are first come, first served.

who_can_apply: Students entering sophomore, junior or senior year of high school. You need at least a 2.75 GPA and must have finished Algebra 1.
how_to_apply: The program page says application links are at the bottom of the page. The link itself is not stated on the program page.
notes: The page says you can earn college credit. The number of credits is not stated on the program page.
duration: One week per session
pay_detail: $675 per session. This covers food, housing and classes.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24, in or out of school. Residency and income rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Here form. Or contact a job coordinator in your area. Or call the Inglewood office at 310.680.3700.
notes: Teen Centers for ages 13 to 17 (Inglewood Mon to Thu 3 to 6 PM, Hawthorne Mon to Fri 3 to 6 PM) are listed too but are not job programs. Bridge to Work is for foster youth only. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: STEP says you can earn money but gives no amount. Other pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 who live in Cumberland, Dauphin, Perry, Adams or York County, PA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, which is a Google Form. Then do an interview. Questions: hiring@leafprojectpa.org.
notes: 2026 season: June 22 to Aug 7, Monday to Thursday. Pay is $10 an hour, paid every other week. Applications for the 2026 season closed April 7.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: $10 per hour (2026 season), paid every other week

who_can_apply: Registered 4-H member in good standing, age 14 to 18 based on the 4-H year. The page lists no grade rule.
how_to_apply: Send the application form, a personal narrative and two letters of recommendation. Then interview at the State Fair. You can do it in person or online.
notes: Ambassadors must already be registered 4-H members. Costs for the orientation, retreat and events are not stated on the program page. Questions: call 605-688-4792.
duration: A full year of duties. The page does not give a term length.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 and allowed to work in the US. Live in South Dakota or a nearby county. In-school youth ages 14 to 21 must be low-income and have a barrier such as basic skills deficient, English learner, homeless, in foster care, pregnant or parenting, or have a disability. Out-of-school youth must be 16 to 24.
how_to_apply: Call 605-773-3101 (TTY 711) to ask where to start. Under 18, a parent or guardian must sign the application forms.
notes: Narrow: not every teen qualifies. The state may limit how many in-school youth it enrolls because at least 75 percent of funds go to out-of-school youth. Rules are from the state WIOA manual, section 4.1, revised October 2026. The state says all Title I youth also sign up for Wagner-Peyser job services. The manual also lists Selective Service registration rules (policy 4.6) that this card does not cover.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. The manual says the program is not an entitlement and depends on funding.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18. You live in the Four Corners region. That is Archuleta, Dolores, La Plata, Montezuma and San Juan counties and northern New Mexico counties. Or you live in the Los Valles region. That is Park, Chaffee, Saguache, Mineral and Rio Grande, Alamosa, Costilla and Conejos counties.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link for your region on the page. Find your region on the county map.
notes: The Colorado Youth Corps Association page lists other youth corps by county. They are Boulder County, Larimer County, Mile High Youth Corps and Rocky Mountain Youth Corps. The last has a youth program for ages 14 to 18 in Steamboat Springs. They also list Weld County and Western Colorado. Ask each one for the ages and dates.
duration: Two sessions: late May to June, or mid July to mid August. Each is 4 to 5 weeks.
pay_detail: $14.42 per hour, 32 to 40 hours per week

who_can_apply: Female high school students who are ready to start exploring college. Parent or guardian permission is required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form now for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
