notes: Costs money. Applying is not an application to Spelman and does not promise admission. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the CPI page itself says only that late submissions are not accepted.
duration: 2 weeks, residential. Session 1: June 5 to 18, 2027. Session 2: July 2 to 17, 2027.
pay_detail: $3,150 per session (the page says cost is subject to change)

who_can_apply: Female high school students in 11th grade with a 3.0 GPA and at least a 3.0 in English and science. Parent permission is required. One page also says juniors and seniors, so confirm your grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
notes: Costs money. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the ECP page itself does not give a due date.
duration: 4 weeks, residential, June 19 to July 16, 2027
pay_detail: Biology $4,500, English $4,500, Dance $4,400 (subject to change)

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. St. Charles Public Library cardholders and returning volunteers come first. Under 18 needs parent or guardian permission.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. It takes about 10 minutes. Answer every question. Applying does not mean you get a spot, because openings are limited.
notes: For summer, enter the grade you are going into. List dates you cannot volunteer. Contact details are behind a hidden email on the page.
duration: Not stated. There is a summer session.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: The Volunteer Center takes volunteers ages 6 and up. F.A.R.M. distribution events need volunteers who are 16 or older. Food on the Move events need volunteers who are 18 or older. Volunteers under 16 need one adult for every five of them.
how_to_apply: Pick a shift on the volunteer sign-up page and register. Do not wear open-heel or open-toe shoes. Minors use the minor waiver form.
notes: The Foodbank requires one adult volunteer for every five volunteers under 16, in groups or not. Plan 3 to 4 months ahead for groups. Court-ordered service is not accepted.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens from the St. Louis area. Age range not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Learn more and apply link on the museum's teen assistants page. A contact email is listed there.
notes: The page did not list ages. Ask the museum before you apply. The page title reads Museum Assistants.
duration: Up to 24 hours a week in summer. At least 5 hours a month in the school year.
pay_detail: $15 per hour

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 16. Teens volunteer through their high school and get community service credit hours.
how_to_apply: Call 314-362-5324 and ask for the student application packet. Send in all of the information at one time. If the spots are full, you can go on a waiting list.
notes: Students should not use the adult application. No more than three absences are allowed in Summer Teens. School-year community service hours are possible when there is room. Call the Volunteer Office to ask.
duration: At least 7 weeks and 60 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get community service credit hours.

who_can_apply: High school students in the St. Louis metro area. CAM aims for a mix of new and returning teens and a mix of art backgrounds.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply. Applications for 2026 are closed. Learning and Engagement staff review applications.
notes: You must attend all sessions to get the stipend.
duration: 2026: May 27 to July 16 (Wed, Thu, Fri 2 to 4 p.m.) plus three sessions Aug to Nov
pay_detail: $500 stipend if you finish the whole program. Public transit costs can be reimbursed.

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18 who live in the St. Louis County Library District.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in March. In 2026 the page had an Apply Now button for the teen internship application.
notes: The 2026 internship ran June 1 to August 7. The intern must be flexible with the schedule and with branches. The intern also writes a final reflection about the summer.
duration: 10 weeks, 12 hours per week
pay_detail: $15.00 per hour, about 12 hours per week

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Send the form on the program page. A participating branch will contact you.
notes: Only participating branches run TAG. Meeting times are not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 12 years old and in the 6th grade. Teens fill out the teen volunteer application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen volunteer application on the program page. You can also call 314-994-3300 or email volunteer@slcl.org.
notes: Each community service request is looked at on its own.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library says volunteering can count toward a community service requirement.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors at a public or private high school in the St. Louis area, in good academic standing. Children of St. Louis Fed employees cannot apply. Only one student per school is picked.
how_to_apply: A teacher nominates you. You send the application form. Your teacher then sends a Teacher Recommendation form.
notes: After the program, members may apply for a limited number of summer internships at the St. Louis Fed. Questions: STLSSBoD@stls.frb.org.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth starting at age 13. The museum wants people who are outgoing, flexible and patient, and who like working with children.
how_to_apply: Send an application on the program page. If chosen, you have a personal interview and then an orientation.
notes: Volunteer sites are the Magic House in Kirkwood and MADE for Kids at 5127 Delmar Blvd. in St. Louis. The page does not give an upper age limit.
duration: You are asked to serve at least 30 hours within a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says volunteering can help with community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students. Most programs are for rising juniors and seniors. The Health Professions Summer Institute also takes rising sophomores. The design and art program takes students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in spring. Each program has its own registration. Fees vary by program.
notes: Pick the program that fits your grade. Fees are from 2026 and may change.
duration: 1 day to 1 week
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $65 portfolio workshop, $75 Cybersecurity, $85 Biz Camp, $100 Saints Science Academy, $150 Health Professions, $700 Rawlings Sport Business (lodging and meals included).

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18 who like a career in medicine. Students fill out the application, not a parent.
how_to_apply: Send in the TLC form, a questionnaire, a letter of recommendation from a teacher or school mentor and a minor consent form. Accepted students do a background check and a health screen (shot history, TB test, urine drug screen). Questions: 314-251-6180.
notes: The Tuesday and Thursday program has room for 40 students. Mercy has a Monday, Wednesday and Friday program too.
duration: 2026: June 9 to July 30, Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. (three required orientation days)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Junior volunteers must be at least 16. You fill out an application and have an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the program page. Placement depends on an interview and on what the hospital needs.
notes: The hospital is in west St. Louis County. The page does not say how many hours a week you must give.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: You are a rising junior or senior. You go to a partner high school. The 2026-27 partners were Metro Classical and Academic and University City High. The rest were Rosati-Kain Academy, Crossroads College Prep and Nerinx Hall.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the form opens. You apply from a partner high school.
notes: Your school must be a partner school. Coordinator: 314-577-9466, eco-act@mobot.org. Transportation help is offered for activities outside school.
duration: One week of summer training, then the school year
pay_detail: Free. Taken as a for-credit class. Meals and gear for outings are provided.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 who like bugs, nature and working with kids and families. Must attend in-person orientation and training. Interviews are required.
how_to_apply: Apply online in spring, then go to a group interview. Questions: butterflyhouse@mobot.org.
notes: Spots are limited. Lead MANTIS needs 2 or more years of MANTIS experience.
duration: June to August, at least 30 hours (Lead MANTIS 40 hours)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Training is provided. Lead MANTIS volunteers get a Friends and Family membership.

who_can_apply: St. Louis region youth ages 16 to 20.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist form on the program page for future seasons.
notes: The page says it is mainly an education program and stipend details come at orientation. It serves St. Louis regional youth.
duration: Three programs a year (spring break, summer, fall)
pay_detail: Paid $15.00 per hour as a stipend. Bus passes, snacks and lunch provided.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 14 to 18. You must send a letter of recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online in the spring window. Upload a letter of recommendation. Spots are few. If you have a question, send an email to SageServiceProgram@mobot.org.
notes: Shifts run seven days a week, 10 a.m. to noon and 12:30 to 2:30 p.m. Not everyone who applies gets a spot.
duration: June to October. First year: at least 50 hours including training.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in the 16 county St. Louis area and like plant science, gardening, botany or nature studies. You must come to monthly meetings.
how_to_apply: See the program page for the application.
notes: The page lists acceptance notices by September 16, 2024, so its dates are old. Confirm details before you apply.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Stipend paid at the end of the program. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12 who live or go to school in St. Louis City.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the council page.
notes: Accepted teens serve at least one year. Meetings are virtual.
duration: At least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: High school and college students who are at least 16 when they submit the application. A student who turns 16 during the summer must wait for the next summer.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page early next year. The link was open for only 48 hours in 2026. You must attend the mandatory orientation and finish the screening.
notes: In 2026 the program ran June 8 to August 14, Monday through Friday. Screening has a urine drug screen, a background check (Social Security number needed), and blood tests for TB, measles, mumps and rubella. You also need proof of a flu shot or agree to get one. Call 314-542-4768 with questions.
duration: 10 weeks, one 4-hour shift per week (34 hours or more)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Current 9th and 10th graders from the St. Louis region (they join as rising 10th and 11th graders). A cohort of 20. Needs two teacher recommendations.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form from December to February. Send 2 teacher recommendations. Give clear answers to every question.
notes: The week of training has an overnight stay at the Dana Brown Overnight Center. Only full applications are looked at.
duration: 11 months (training week in early June, then field programs through April)
pay_detail: Stipend based on the number of hours you work at SIFT events. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Live in the City of St. Louis, age 16 to 24, and household income under $69,090 and/or live in a Qualified Census Tract. Under 17 needs a parent or guardian signature on the Eligibility Form.
how_to_apply: The program is closed because it reached capacity. Watch the SLATE program page and its Facebook page for updates. When it opens, you need proof of age, St. Louis residency and household income.
notes: SLATE is seeking more funding. Missouri work permit rules not checked.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Paid. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering grade 11 or 12 with a 3.0 GPA, parent and high school permission, the course prerequisites and an open seat. Up to 11 credit hours a semester.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Visiting Young Scholar application online. Questions: vys@slu.edu or 314-977-3534.
notes: Your high school decides if the credit counts toward graduation. SLU is a Catholic Jesuit college.
duration: Fall, spring or summer semesters
pay_detail: $350 per credit hour. Lab fees extra. No scholarships or tuition help.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 17 when they apply and in the spring of their junior year. Students must go to a one-hour information meeting and a 3-hour orientation.
how_to_apply: Check the program page this fall for the new timeline. You need an application, an interview, health requirements, a background check and two references.
notes: Spots are limited. The hospital takes one student per school and at most four students at a time during the school day.
duration: One year, at least one weekday evening shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Anyone who is at least 12 years old can volunteer with the library district.
how_to_apply: Call 636-441-2300, extension 1579, to ask how to start. The program page links only an adult application. Teen Leadership Committee meetings are on the library events calendar.
notes: You can volunteer at your local branch. You can also volunteer with the Library Foundation or the Friends of the Library.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens who attend committee meetings can get an hour of volunteer credit.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 and 15 who live in St. Louis City or North St. Louis County.
how_to_apply: Apply online at stlyouthjobs.org/apply. A Job Coach then contacts you.
notes: Not a job placement.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Stipend paid after you finish the program. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at a St. Louis area school with a 2.5 or higher GPA. You must be in or past Algebra. You need a transcript, a behavior report and a teacher or counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the UMSL Bridge page when it opens. Send a transcript, behavior report and recommendation form.
notes: Check the UMSL Bridge page for the next application date.
duration: First two Saturdays of each month, October to February, 7:45 a.m. to 12 p.m.
pay_detail: UMSL's landing page calls its Bridge services free. No pay.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 10 at a St. Louis area school with a 2.5 or higher GPA. You must be in or past Algebra. You need a transcript, a behavior report and a teacher or counselor recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the UMSL Bridge page when it is taking students. Send a transcript, behavior report and recommendation form.
notes: The landing page says grades 6 to 10 across middle and high school sessions; the high school page says grades 9 to 10.
duration: Mid-June to mid-July, Monday to Friday 7:45 a.m. to 12 p.m. (2026 high school session began June 22)
pay_detail: UMSL's landing page calls its Bridge services free. No pay.

who_can_apply: You must be in high school now. You can be a freshman, sophomore or junior.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the program page. Questions: precollege@wustl.edu.
notes: Costs and dates were not on the program page. Check the Fees and Scholarships and Dates and Deadlines pages.
duration: Summer program (length not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $985 commuter or $1,485 residential, plus a $50 nonrefundable application fee. Need-based scholarships offered.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the program page. Questions: precollege@wustl.edu.
notes: Costs and dates were not on the program page. Check the Fees and Scholarships and Dates and Deadlines pages.
duration: 5 weeks
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $4,075 for 3 credits online or commuter, $7,825 for 6 credits commuter, $8,385 to $12,135 residential, plus a $50 application fee. Need-based scholarships offered.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors (finished 11th grade) from any high school in Missouri or Illinois in the Greater St. Louis area. You do not need research experience. Missouri and Illinois residents only.
how_to_apply: Online application with five short answers and two essays. Two recommendation letters, one from a math or science teacher.
notes: Takes only 10 to 12 students a year. Students from St. Louis Public Schools and under-resourced schools are strongly encouraged to apply. Work is in person in the lab.
duration: 8 weeks (May 31 to July 23, 2027)
pay_detail: $4,800 stipend (before taxes) for the summer

who_can_apply: High school age students who are 15 by May 1 of the application year. Limited spots.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Ask a teacher or youth leader to send a recommendation form. Go to 1 group interview. If accepted, do a background check and online training.
notes: Next cycle dates follow last year's pattern. Email zooalive@stlzoo.org with questions.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18. Must be 15 by the volunteer orientation date (May 9 in 2026). Orientation and training are required.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page in February 2027 for the form and interviews.
notes: 2026 orientation was May 9 and training May 16.
duration: Late May to early August, at least 30 hours, shifts of 2 to 4 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts as service hours.

who_can_apply: Students age 16 or older and adults. No summer-only volunteering.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form online. Questions? Call the volunteer office at 408-852-2521.
notes: Read on the official St. Louise Regional Hospital page on 2026-10-16. It is South County's community hospital in Gilroy. The page does not state hours, commitment length, health screening, TB test or fees; ask the volunteer office. The page shows an email address whose link points to a different address, so call the phone number instead.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 before the program starts in January. The page does not state a maximum age. Minimum 3.0 GPA. Boise campus only. The program cannot take new volunteers past their junior year of high school.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application when it opens in November. Call (208) 381-2265 with questions. You must also finish orientation and service training. You must attend quarterly meetings. You also need proof of immunizations (MMR, varicella, Tdap, T-spot and a current flu shot).
notes: The opening date of Nov 2 is worked out from the page rule. The rule says the first Monday in November. The date is not printed on the page.
duration: 8 hours a month during the school year and 12 hours a month in June, July and August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: High school and college students who are 16 or older. You need a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add one letter from a counselor, teacher, principal or coach. Add your latest school transcript. Write an essay of at least 500 words about you and why volunteering matters.
notes: The page header says Temporarily Suspended, but the SHINE section still lists the steps. Call 510-264-4139 to ask when volunteering restarts. Leave your name, phone number and question. The program page does not give hours per week.
pay_detail: Volunteer. The program page does not list pay or service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students, per the page. The page does not state age, grade range, residency or citizenship rules.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application opens on Nov 10, 2026 (the page does not describe the form). Attend the free info session on Nov 10, 2026, or RSVP through the page. Questions: aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu.
notes: Re-read the AIMI page on 2026-10-07. The dates are for the Summer 2027 program. The page does not state pay or cost, length, detailed eligibility or whether the program is in person, so the pay and work-permit answers are not confirmed. Confirm those with aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu before applying. The Summer Health AI Bootcamp is a separate program on the same site and is not covered here.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the page. Ask aimi-hs-programs@stanford.edu.

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors who are at least 14 and can commute daily to the Palo Alto campus. You need a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up for application announcements on the CARE page; email carehighschoolprogram@stanford.edu.
notes: Pay-to-play. Day program, about 9am to 3pm on weekdays. No housing or transportation provided; lunch and snacks included. No application fee waivers in 2026.
duration: 2 weeks (2026 sessions: June 15 to 26 and July 6 to 17)
pay_detail: 2026 fee was $5,500; 2027 fee not announced. Limited need-based aid in 2026.

who_can_apply: Teens. Start with an online orientation, then a scheduled interview; eligible teens get the application link after the interview. Age and schedule rules are given in the orientation.
how_to_apply: Start with the online orientation on volunteer.stanfordchildrens.org, then interview. Questions: volunteerservices@stanfordchildrens.org.
notes: Minimum age is not stated on the page. Ask the volunteer office.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Live in Alameda, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara or Santa Cruz County; 16 or older by the start date; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; some biology, chemistry or programming background.
how_to_apply: 2026 process: email essays, transcripts, resume, science course list and one recommendation letter to grips-program@stanford.edu by the deadline.
notes: Decisions in 2026 came mid-March to mid-April. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year; check the page in December.
duration: 8 weeks, 4 hours a day, 5 days a week (2026: June 15 to Aug 6)
pay_detail: Application fee (amount not stated; waived for financial need). The page does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Inpatient unit roles need 18. Needs 6 to 8 hours of online training, a background check, a health screening (including a TB test), and orientation within 30 days of selection.
how_to_apply: Apply on volunteer.stanfordhealthcare.org. Questions: VolunteerResources@stanfordhealthcare.org or 650-723-7424.
notes: Stanford says this does not count for school clinical-hour needs and has no shadowing.
duration: At least 1 shift per week for 6 months (inpatient roles: 1 year)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors, and undergraduate pre-medical students. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores (if available), essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the MEDCSI SlideRoom portal when the new cycle opens. Needs transcripts, resume, test scores (if available), essay and a STEM teacher recommendation.
notes: Pay-to-play and expensive. Fees shown are 2026 prices. No stipend or work experience. The program also admits undergraduate pre-med students.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 13 to 24 on campus; July 27 to Aug 7 virtual)
pay_detail: 2026 fees: $6,580 on campus, $4,580 virtual, $2,480 for the 10-week fall virtual option. Application fee $95 for summer ($75 fall). Fee waivers for U.S. citizens or green card holders under $80,000 household income or in low-income support programs, limited and first come first served.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors, 16 or older, unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher, living in and attending high school in San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Marin, Alameda, Contra Costa or Santa Cruz County. You must live with a family member or legal guardian; housing and transportation are not provided.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the PIPS portal when the next cycle opens. Check the PIPS page for the next cycle.
notes: About 35 to 40 students are admitted. The page says in person, with some remote work possible. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.
duration: 7 weeks, 30 hours a week (2026: June 8 to July 24)
pay_detail: No fee. $3,000 stipend for students who show financial need.

who_can_apply: Currently in grades 8 to 11 and older than 13 and younger than 19 during the program dates. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with unofficial transcripts and the application fee; rank up to three courses. Financial aid is a separate form due about a week after the deadline.
notes: Pay-to-play. Prices and dates are from 2026. The page says to join the mailing list for future dates. Admissions page (checked 2026-10-10) says 'older than 13 and younger than 19 during the program dates'. The tuition page gives the $60 fee for financial aid applications; the admissions page gives $65.
duration: Two weeks, live online (2026: June 15 to 26 or July 6 to 17)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,200. Application fee $65 (the aid page says $60); waivers on request. Limited need-based aid. Some courses need materials costing up to $100.

who_can_apply: Juniors or seniors now (classes of 2027 and 2028), 16 or older by June 2027, living in and attending high school in the U.S., and a U.S. citizen or green card holder. Local Bay Area students are strongly favored. You must live with a family member or guardian.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts and recommendations. In 2026 the decision date was Apr 10.
notes: Very competitive. Housing and transportation not provided. Fee and decision date shown are from the 2026 cycle.
duration: 8 weeks, about 40 hours a week, tentatively June 7 to July 29, 2027
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: the 2026 application fee was $50 (waivable for family income under $80,000). No program cost. Most students get no stipend; a very limited number of need-based stipends exist.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who are low-income and first-generation college students living in Northern California. About 24 students are admitted.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the SlideRoom link on the SMYSP page when it opens. Contact: smysp-team@stanford.edu.
notes: The page (checked 2026-10-10) gives 2027 session dates of June 21 to July 23, 2027. It says the 2027 application is expected in December 2026. It does not say if housing or a stipend is given.
duration: About 5 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 26)
pay_detail: Tuition free. Housing and stipend not stated.

who_can_apply: The page says it is designed for grades 4 to 12, college learners and adults. It mentions guides for after-school and homeschool groups. It does not say whether a student can sign up with no teacher or group.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Register Now button. The registration wizard shows the program rules and key dates. Ask a teacher, club leader or parent whether your school or group already signs up.
notes: The page does not say whether a student can register alone; it talks about teams and group guides. Price was not stated beyond 'no cost or low cost'. Confirm first.
duration: Several weeks to a full school year, your choice
pay_detail: No pay. The page says it is available at no cost or low cost.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 for 2026-27 who attend a high school inside the City of Stonecrest. A parent or guardian must register you and send one proof of school enrollment. You must commit to regular attendance.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian fills out the Stonecrest NextGen Program Application Form on the page and sends proof of enrollment. Spots are first-come, first-served.
notes: Only 30 spots. City Hall: 3120 Stonecrest Boulevard, Suite 190, Stonecrest, GA 30038, 770-224-0200. Write to Nicholas Ivey at nivey@stonecrestga.gov. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: 6 Saturday sessions, 10 am to 1 pm, Oct 2026 to Mar 2027
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Durham County students who attend Durham Public Schools. Priority goes to students who would be the first in their family to graduate college (parents have not earned a Bachelor's degree) and/or qualify for free or reduced lunch. Students should be at or slightly below grade level and have strong family support. Rising 6th through 11th graders can apply. A lottery picks 60 to 65 students.
how_to_apply: Print the form for your grade, add the latest report card, End of Grade scores, a teacher recommendation and family questions, and drop it at the W.G. Pearson Center, 1200 Spaulding Street, Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 6 PM. Chosen by lottery.
notes: Only 60 to 65 students are picked. A lottery picks them. The page does not state the cost to families. You can contact Karla Fernandez, Director of Operations. Her email is karla.fernandez@studentudurham.org.
duration: Multi-year
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: The library accepts volunteers age 13 and older. VolunTEENs is for ages 13 to 18. The district serves Sugar Grove and parts of Montgomery and Aurora.
how_to_apply: Fill out the library volunteer form from the circulation desk. For short projects, use the Service Hour Project form. Contact Nichole at 630-409-1589. Or contact Christine Edison, Adult and Teen Services Manager, at 630-409-3131.
notes: The apply link is the Service Hour Project form for ages 13 to 18.
duration: Summer reading volunteers help 2 to 6 hours a week for the 8 week program. Shelving volunteers commit to a weekly 2 hour shift for at least 6 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens can earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 and a half to 18 (must turn 16 before the end of the residential phase and not turn 19 before the start). U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. At risk of dropping out or behind in credits. Never convicted of a felony or under indictment. Must be willing to be drug free, able to do the program (sports physical), and must volunteer; it cannot be court ordered.
how_to_apply: Register for and go to an in person orientation. This is the first step. You get the application there. Then you send in documents. You do a one on one interview of up to an hour. You go to an invited roll call. Phone 562-936-1759, call or text (916) 639-2260, or email admissions@SunburstYouthAcademy.com.
notes: The eligibility page lists documents to submit including a California ID, birth certificate and Social Security card, so go with a parent or guardian. The pages did not say which counties are served. The eligibility page still shows the earlier class dates (January to June 2026).
duration: 22 week residential program (per the site's video text), then support for 12 months. Class 39 begins January 2027.
pay_detail: Free to attend (page wording).

who_can_apply: Age 13 and up. Most roles ask volunteers who are 18 or older to be fingerprinted and cleared first.
how_to_apply: Fill one application: general, library, or recreation and senior center. Volunteer Resources: 408-730-7533.
notes: The official page was checked. Fill out only one application.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. You must have the right to volunteer in Canada.
how_to_apply: Fill in a form on MyImpactPage. Go to an interview. Send 2 references. Get a Police Information Check. It can take up to 6 weeks.
notes: Contact volunteer@surrey.ca or 604-598-5863. The page says interview slots are available to sign up for, but shows no dates. Intake status is unclear, so confirm first.
duration: At least 30 volunteer hours across the year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who live in Surrey.
how_to_apply: Wait for spring 2027 applications on the City of Surrey page. Email the youth team with questions.
notes: Meets Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:00pm at City Hall on the groups page. The council page says every other week. Spring 2027 date is the city's statement, exact day not posted.
duration: A school-year term, meetings every other week
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. New volunteers send 2 references and go to a training session.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City of Surrey My Impact page (an account is needed). Send 2 references. Attend training before the program starts.
notes: You must attend all 6 sessions. Branches: City Centre, Clayton, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, Ocean Park, Semiahmoo, Strawberry Hill. Spring dates not posted when read.
duration: 6 weekly sessions, 60 minutes each, twice a year (spring and fall)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts toward volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. New volunteers need two references. If you have not volunteered with the City of Surrey, the Teen Library Council or Reading Buddies in the past 12 months, you need a Police Information Check. Hand it in by July 31.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City of Surrey My Impact page (an account is needed). Send 2 references. Go to an orientation before the first meeting.
notes: Meets once a month from September to June at six branches: City Centre, Clayton-Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton-Strawberry Hill and Semiahmoo-Ocean Park. If you miss three meetings in a row, you may lose your spot. British Columbia work paper rules were not checked. This is unpaid.
duration: Monthly meetings, September to June
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older depending on the program. Parent or guardian consent is needed under 18. ICU, NICU and Palliative Care need age 20+.
how_to_apply: Apply online. If you qualify, you get an interview. Then you need a police record check and two references. You also do online orientation and training.
notes: Page last updated Aug 2, 2024. The STIR research program on the same page is for undergraduates, not high school.
duration: One shift a week on the same day for at least 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 who live, learn, work or volunteer in Surrey. You lead or take part in the project.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YEP Project Application Form.
notes: Funding requests are reviewed one by one.
duration: Depends on the project
pay_detail: Not a job. Eligible projects may get funding, not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Wait for the spring 2027 form on the City of Surrey page. Or email the youth team to ask about other ways to join in.
notes: Exact spring 2027 opening day not posted.
duration: A term, meets Thursdays 4:30 to 5:30pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Drop in. Sign up as a Squad member to hear about more dates and track hours. Groups over 5 email ahead.
notes: Events may be called off in extreme weather. Parks: Serpentine Heights Park (Sep 25, Oct 23) and Godwin Farm Biodiversity Preserve Park (Nov 14).
duration: Drop-in events (length not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sign up to track volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 and older.
how_to_apply: Send in the volunteer application, online or at a branch. Add a note from your doctor and a form from a parent. Then go to the Teen Volunteer Orientation at your home branch.
notes: Dates for the orientation are on the events page of the library site.
duration: Summer reading season
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Volunteers 16 years and older. No school or residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Call the hospital's volunteer office at 510-727-3080. Ask how to apply.
notes: Read on the Sutter Health page on 2026-10-16. The page also names a family support role in the ER. But Sutter's own listing for that role says 18 and up. So teens should expect the front desk or the gift shop. The page does not list hours, how long you must stay, a health check, a TB test or fees. Ask the volunteer office.

who_can_apply: High school students 16 and 17 years old. You need a consent form signed by a parent or guardian and one signed by a teacher.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form during the two week window. Add the parent form and the teacher form. Both are on the page. Then you do an interview, online training and health tests. Questions? Email MPHSvolunteerservices@sutterhealth.org or call 650-696-2465 and press 2.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing on 2026-10-16. The page gives the windows as May 1 to 15 and November 1 to 15 every year, without a year; the next one falls on Nov 1 to 15, 2026. Applications outside the windows are not described. Get the parent and teacher forms signed before Nov 1 so you can apply on day one. Health testing is required but the listing does not list which shots or tests.
duration: At least one 3 to 4 hour visit a week, with a one-year minimum commitment

who_can_apply: Age 16 and older. You are asked to make a six-month commitment.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on either page. Questions? Email PAMFSOUTHBAYADMIN@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listings on 2026-10-16. These are outpatient medical centers, not hospitals. Shifts are Monday to Friday only, so this fits summer or students with free weekday time. The Sunnyvale and Mountain View listings use the same text and the same contact. They do not state health screening, TB test or fees.
duration: Six months, weekday 4-hour shifts (8 am to 12 pm or 12 pm to 4 pm)

who_can_apply: Age 16 and older. No school or residency rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the page. Questions? Email pamfpeninsulaadmin@sutterhealth.org.
notes: Read on the official Sutter Health listing on 2026-10-16. This is an outpatient medical center, not a hospital. Shifts are Monday to Friday only, 8 am to 12 pm or 12 pm to 4 pm, with no weekend hours, so it fits summer or students with free weekday time. The listing does not state a minimum commitment, health screening, TB test or fees.
duration: Weekday 4-hour shifts (8 am to 12 pm or 12 pm to 4 pm)

who_can_apply: The pages do not list rules on who can join. Shadow Days require your home school counselor's approval. Ask your counselor or call SVCTE about enrollment.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor about enrolling in SVCTE courses. To visit, apply for a Shadow Day through the SVCTE site (your counselor must approve it). Phone (408) 723-6403, Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. The site lists Milthon Marquez as Post-Secondary Planning Coach.
notes: Re-read the SVCTE home page and the Shadow Days, Dual Enrollment, Internships and Post-Secondary Options pages on 2026-10-07. The homepage lists 22 career technical courses (the old file said more than 24 pathways). Dual enrollment courses are taught by college professors at the high school campus. Shadow Days: after talking to your home school counselor, submit interest on the site; the counselor must approve it, and you get a confirmation 7 days before the visit. Eligibility, costs, deadlines and enrollment dates are not stated on the pages.
pay_detail: Not stated. Dual enrollment courses earn college credit. The site links a Schedule of Fees page that was not read, so ask about costs.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19. No application. Just come to a meeting at a participating branch or join the Virtual Teen Council.
how_to_apply: Come to a meeting at a Pierce County Library branch that takes part. The page lists the places. You can also join the online council.
notes: Meeting places can change during the year (the page lists 2026-2027 locations and says they are subject to change). Meeting dates are on the library calendar.
duration: October to April, flexible drop-in meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens (the page does not state an age range). Slots are limited and filled through an application.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the form is posted. Look on the Pierce County Library page about teen volunteering.
notes: The page says teens attend weekly sessions for up to 20 service hours. The page does not state an age range or year. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, weekly sessions, up to 20 service hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Up to 20 hours of volunteer service.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 and in grades 9 to 12. You should be excited to talk with visitors about nature and animals.
how_to_apply: Apply on the youth volunteer page in December 2026. Large and small group interviews are held in late February; not everyone is interviewed. Join the waitlist form to get an email when applications open.
notes: Most zoo volunteer roles ask for at least one year. Explore the Shore (ages 16 and up) and Spot the Swallows (14 and up with a parent if under 18) are other teen options on the volunteer page. Questions: volunteer@pdza.org or 253-404-3687.
duration: 9 required trainings March to June, then one 6-hour shift a week for 10 weeks in summer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Tacoma Public Schools high school students, using their school account. Most experiences start at age 14; some have extra age or schedule rules. Limit of 3 experiences per student.
how_to_apply: Sign in to SchooLinks with your TPS student account. Apply to an experience. Interview with the employer. Then hand in the paperwork and a certificate from a money skills course.
notes: Only for Tacoma Public Schools students. Students new to Jobs 253 get priority. The page caps stipend funds at $1,500 per student and says students must complete a W-9 before starting. Payments typically arrive 4 to 6 weeks after the experience ends. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Five sessions a year; each internship starts and ends in one session
pay_detail: Up to $500 completion stipend (funded by the City of Tacoma) plus 0.5 elective credit.

who_can_apply: Tacoma Public Schools high school students and students of partner Maritime|253 districts. For the drone course you must be 16 or older to earn the FAA Part 107 certificate. The ANEW program is for ages 16 to 18 with a disability. See its own card.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Tacoma Public Schools Jobs 253 pages when courses are posted. Contact the course lead listed on the page.
notes: Open to TPS and partner district students only. Each course has its own dates, spots and lead; the auto course ran June 22 to July 9 in 2026. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Varies by course (the auto course ran June 22 to July 9, Monday to Thursday, 8 am to 3 pm)
pay_detail: Free training. $500 stipend at completion.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. The job is in Taos, NM.
how_to_apply: Open the apply page and find the Youth Coalition Member job under Prevention Program. Use the link for that job.
notes: The job runs from Oct 9, 2026 to Apr 30, 2027, per the listing. Hours per week and the last day to apply are not stated on the program page. The Prevention Program listing says its positions are for people pursuing a career in public health addressing substance misuse.
pay_detail: $17 per hour

who_can_apply: Students at a participating Georgia high school or approved home study program. 11th and 12th graders and returning 10th graders can take any approved course. New 10th graders take career courses, or core courses with the required SAT or ACT score. 9th graders can join but get no state funding.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school and parent or guardian, apply to the college, and apply for dual enrollment funding at GAfutures.org. Atlanta Tech asks for PSAT, SAT, ACT or Accuplacer scores (a 2.6 HOPE GPA can be used for 11th and 12th graders).
notes: Atlanta Tech funding rules on its page: 15 funded hours per semester, a 30 hour total, and funding ends after two course withdrawals. Atlanta Tech high school contact: hsadmissions@atlantatech.edu or 404-225-4511. This is a course program, not a job, so no work permit applies. The TCSG page sends students to GAfutures.org. The GAfutures Dual Enrollment Application Procedure page says students must apply to the college first, then complete the online Dual Enrollment Funding application; its Apply Now button opens secure.gafutures.org, which shows a GAfutures sign-in page first.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
pay_detail: No tuition, fees or books for the first 30 hours for eligible students. Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 or older by Nov 21, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the official page (vhub.at/TeenVolunteer). Questions: volunteer@thetech.org or 408-294-8324.
notes: The Oct 7 card said applications open Oct 9 to Oct 23, 2026. On Oct 9 the official page no longer shows that window, and the apply hub page shows no dates in its HTML (its content loads with JavaScript), so the status is unconfirmed. Re-check the official page for a new window. The page lists three mandatory 3.5-hour orientation and tour sessions on Saturdays Nov 14, Nov 21 and Dec 5, 2026, 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM. Applications are reviewed after the deadline by availability and answers. The page gives no year for Jan 3. The page's email addresses are encoded and could not be re-read on Oct 9; the email is kept from the Oct 7 read.
duration: Six shifts in the peak windows: Nov 21 to 29 and Dec 19 to Jan 3

who_can_apply: Must be at least 14 and live in or near Los Angeles. You can start from fall of 9th grade through fall of 11th grade. Seniors and second-semester juniors are not accepted. Training and shifts are in person in West LA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to every training, interview and orientation session. After you are accepted, show a negative TB blood test from the last 12 months. To hear about the next round, join the Prospective Teen Line Volunteer interest list on the page.
notes: Serious role that handles hard topics. Hotline runs every evening from West LA, no remote option. Training is 65+ hours per the volunteer page (the main Teen Line page says over 100). The page lists no pay and the role earns community service hours.
duration: Training of 65+ hours (the main Teen Line page says over 100), then at least two evening shifts a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns community service hours.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Pick up an application at the library reference desk (30600 Pauba Rd). No online form is listed. Phone 951-693-8900.
notes: The page does not say how many hours you can earn. Ask the library if late applications are taken.
duration: 2026-27 school year; meeting schedule not listed
pay_detail: Unpaid. Community service hours.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at a Phoenix-area high school who can attend in person at the Tempe campus. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian sign-off.
how_to_apply: Application steps are not posted yet. Use the Contact CTF form on the page for updates.
notes: The page says it will be updated when the revamped program opens. Do not plan around it until dates are posted.
duration: About 8 weeks, mostly June and July, 15 to 20 hours per week
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: High school 4-H members who are project finalists, state winners or All Stars. You sign up through a county Extension office.
how_to_apply: Register through your county Extension office. Students and a parent or guardian must sign Form 600A before attending.
notes: Level I is 9th and 10th grade. Level II is 11th and 12th grade. Council officer candidates must already be in the Tennessee 4-H Honor Club.
duration: About 4 days
pay_detail: $75 for state finalists. $325 for All Stars attending as non-finalists. State Council members and volunteer leaders attend on scholarship.

who_can_apply: Any Tennessee youth. The state site does not list ages or grades for joining. Ask your county Extension office. Some camps and events are set by grade.
how_to_apply: Call or visit your county Extension office. State office phone: 865-974-2128.
notes: The state site names these ways to lead: State 4-H Council, Honor Club, All Stars and the Southern Region Teen Leadership Conference. Camps for older teens are set by grade, so ask the county office.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the state site. Camps and events list their own fees or say to ask the county office.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12, and college students, who are in a farm and food class at their school.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or your ag teacher. Sign up for a farm and food class.
notes: If your school has no agricultural education program, the state office says to contact them. Camp Clements is the state FFA leadership camp. Association phone: 615-762-4930.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Dues not stated on the state site.

who_can_apply: High school students tied to FFA who are nominated by their teachers. Up to 4 students per FFA chapter. You can attend only one year.
how_to_apply: Your ag teacher gathers the 2-page application and the fee check. The teacher mails them to the camp director. Her name is Caley Peyton. The address is Tennessee Forestry Association, 2605 Elm Hill Pike, Suite G, Nashville, TN 37214.
notes: Camp has run since 1950 at Piney Creek Camp. Contact cpeyton@tnforestry.com or 615-281-0714.
duration: 6 days (May 31 to June 5 in 2026)
pay_detail: $95 for early registration, $120 after May 8 (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Student leaders in Tennessee. The 2027 page does not list grades. Ask your county Farm Bureau office about sponsorship and grade rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the Tennessee Farm Bureau summit page for the application. Call 931-388-7872 with questions.
notes: Check with your county Farm Bureau, since the application is still marked coming soon.
duration: 5 days (May 31 to June 4, 2027)
pay_detail: $200. Covers class materials, meals Monday through the Friday banquet, dorm housing, transport to activities and trained counselors.

who_can_apply: Youth who face barriers to work or school. In-school youth are ages 14 to 21, attending school and low-income. Out-of-school youth are ages 16 to 24, not in school, and must meet at least one barrier such as being homeless, in foster care, or having a disability.
how_to_apply: Contact the Workforce Essentials office in your county. Davidson is 615-253-8920. Rutherford is 615-898-8081. Williamson is 615-370-6004.
notes: Other Tennessee regions have different provider offices, listed on the same page. Teens must qualify under the rules above. Call first to ask if you are eligible.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: High school and middle school students. Exact grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: The page says to contact Senior Program Director Stella London at slondon@ymcamidtn.org to start a team at your school. It does not say how single students sign up.
notes: Over 80 students serve as elected officers. Ask the YMCA about cost and if a student without a school team can join.
duration: High school: 3-day conferences. Middle school: 1-day conferences.
pay_detail: Cost is not listed on the page

who_can_apply: High school and middle school students. Delegations are started at a school. Exact grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: The page says to contact Senior Program Director Stella London to start or join a team at your school. Her email is slondon@ymcamidtn.org.
notes: The YMCA also runs Model United Nations through the same center. Ask about cost and sign-up before you plan.
duration: High school conferences are 4 days. Middle school conferences are 1 day.
pay_detail: Cost is not listed on the page

who_can_apply: Youth in 3rd through 12th grade, ages 8 to 18. Each county sets up its own program.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office. Find a club. It needs at least five youth from three families. Choose at least one project. Then enroll online in 4HOnline.
notes: The October 31 date is the price cutoff, not a closing date. Counties customize their programs, so call your county Extension office first. This is a club and leadership program, not a paid job.
duration: One 4-H year. Every membership resets to inactive on August 15, so you re-enroll each year.
pay_detail: Youth fee is $25 if you enroll by October 31 and $30 from November 1 through the end of the 4-H year.

who_can_apply: Texas 4-H members in high school. STEM Ambassadors must be 15 or older. Photo Ambassadors must first finish training as a Junior Master Photographer.
how_to_apply: Pick a team on the Texas 4-H Ambassadors page, then use that team application or contact. Some teams post their details on their own sites.
notes: You need to be an enrolled 4-H member. The Water Ambassadors dates on the page looked out of date, so check that team's own site.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Older Texas 4-H members. Peers vote for district delegates. Six At-Large Delegates are voted in across the state.
how_to_apply: Send in the 2026-2027 At-Large Delegate application and the 2026-2027 Council Membership Contract. Or run in your district. Ask your District 4-H Specialist for the district due date.
notes: All delegates must sign the council contract for 2026-2027. Both kinds of delegate sign it.
duration: Not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Male high school students who finished their junior year. You need at least one semester left. You must never have been to Boys State. School officials must recommend you. You need a parent or guardian's permission. The sponsoring American Legion Post must certify you. You must sign the Texas Boys State Pledge.
how_to_apply: A school official nominates you. That can be a principal, teacher, coach or counselor. A local American Legion Post certifies and sponsors you. Ask your counselor or contact your local Post. The program's site is texasboysstate.com.
notes: Boys State is for boys. Girls State is a separate program. The site says the program asks for one or more boys nominated from each accredited public or private high school. Top delegates may be picked for Boys Nation. Confirm the 2027 dates and fee with your local Post.
duration: One week. The 2026 session ran Sunday June 7 to Friday June 12, 2026.
pay_detail: American Legion Posts or other community groups often pay the fee, so the cost to the boy is often little to nothing. The fee amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Female students now in their junior year at any Texas public or private high school. An ALA Unit may sponsor a home school student who meets the rules. You can attend only once. A student whose religion does not allow her to pledge allegiance to the U.S. flag is not eligible. You must be able to take part in all activities.
how_to_apply: You do not apply on your own. A school nominates you through faculty and a school official, and a local ALA Unit, the school or a community group reserves the spot. Ask your counselor or a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit early in the spring. Questions: GirlsState@alatexas.org or 214-733-7945.
notes: Girls State is for girls. Texas Boys State is a separate program run by the American Legion. Students chosen must attend the whole session to earn the certificate and pin.
duration: One week. The 2026 session was Sunday June 14 to Saturday June 20, 2026.
pay_detail: The 2026 fee was $550 per delegate, not including travel to Seguin. Rules say a unit, school or community group pays it, never the student or her family.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, from incoming 8th graders to incoming seniors. Apply as a Cadet. Past camp graduates can later apply as Assistant Leaders.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application with two essay questions and a list of achievements. Rank your top three camp choices.
notes: Camp phone 210-556-1391. Assistant Leaders can earn college scholarships. Camps listed for 2026 include Bobwhite, Buckskin, Ranch, Bass, Waterfowl and Coastal Brigades.
duration: 5 days
pay_detail: Camp price not stated on the program pages. The site says tuition help is available. Email camps@texasbrigades.org.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 and a half to 18 who are U.S. citizens and Texas residents and are physically and mentally able to take part fully. The program is for youth who are currently disengaged from school.
how_to_apply: Go to an information briefing with a recruiter. Send the application packet and documents. Do a virtual interview with a case manager. Have a mentor fill out a mentor packet. Then a review board decides. Main line: 877-822-0050.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 600 HWY 3013 West, Eagle Lake, TX 77434.
duration: The page lists a tuition-free 22-week residential program. It also lists a 20-week Residential Phase and a 5 and a half month on-campus phase, then a 12-month Post-Residential Phase. The page says the program requires a 17 and a half month commitment. Confirm with a recruiter.
pay_detail: Free. The page says the program is tuition free to the families it serves.

who_can_apply: High school students who are at least 15 by June 1 of the program year and enrolled in high school for the next school year. The flyer describes the program as ages 15 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, upload two recommendation letters from two different references, and upload your most recent report card. Accepted volunteers must show vaccine records (MMR, varicella, Tdap) and a negative TB test, and attend mandatory orientation on the first two days.
notes: The flyer calls the program prestigious and highly sought-after, so expect competition. Up to two absences are allowed. There are no weekend or make-up shifts. Questions: ATXNCVolunteerServices@texaschildrens.org or 737-229-3388. Check the Texas Children's volunteer pages for the 2027 flyer.
duration: About 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (June 1 to June 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Students at a Texas high school with a DECA chapter. Texas DECA members must take part in a career and technical education (CTE) program. Chapters must offer business or marketing courses. The official pages list no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Josh Shankle, shankle@texasdeca.org. State office phone: 817-900-8037.
notes: DECA's page lists 352 Texas high school chapters. The state website does not explain joining step by step, so start with your school's advisor.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student membership is $16 total: $8 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local costs.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12, or the home school match. You join a team of five from the same school or group. The team has an adult advisor.
how_to_apply: Contact the Texas Envirothon office at 281-283-3045 or reistle@uhcl.edu. Then send in the sign-up packet and the fee. You must show proof of health insurance.
notes: Teams need an adult advisor plus chaperones of each gender. The school or group pays for travel, meals and lodging. Teams with fewer than five can play but may lose points on the oral part.
duration: 3 day state event
pay_detail: A non-refundable team registration fee is required each year. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Students who sign up for an agricultural science class at a school with an FFA chapter. The FAQ says the grade depends on the district and that home-schooled students are not covered by the program. Junior FFA needs age 8 and 3rd grade.
how_to_apply: Your first contact is your local agricultural science teacher. Sign up for an agricultural science class.
notes: Junior FFA is a state-only membership at $9 a year, says the membership page.
duration: School year, tied to your agricultural science class
pay_detail: National dues $7 plus Texas dues $9 is $16 a year, not counting area, district or local dues. Junior FFA is $9 a year (state only).

who_can_apply: Secondary students in a state-approved Health Science program, or who plan a career in the health professions. Middle school students in grades 6 to 8 who like a health career path can also join. Membership goes through affiliated school chapters.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's health science teacher or chapter advisor about joining the chapter. State office: texashosa@texashosa.org or 1-877-728-0150.
notes: State office: 201 W. Hillside Road Suite 26, Laredo, TX 78041. Ask your advisor for the fee amount and conference dates.
duration: School year
pay_detail: There are membership fees, but the amounts are not on the program pages. The site links to a 2026 to 2027 fee schedule.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 16 must come with a parent or guardian. Everyone under 18 needs a parent or guardian's signed permission, and a parent signs the liability waiver. Each opening can add its own requirements. Minors cannot do some kinds of work.
how_to_apply: Search openings in the TPWD volunteer portal and apply online. Or contact a park's volunteer coordinator. TPWD checks your application and matches you to an opening. Questions: Volunteer@TPWD.Texas.gov or 512-389-8674.
notes: Park host jobs are long RV-based stays and are not a fit for most teens. The page lists Buffalo Soldiers, State Park Ambassadors and Texas Outdoor Family as special programs, but this card does not cover their age rules. Volunteers 18 and older in ongoing roles must pass a yearly background check.
duration: Varies by opening
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ mentions no volunteer fees or costs.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished at least one high school chemistry course before the summer. The pages give no grade, age or residency rule. You need a recommendation from a high school chemistry teacher. Selection is merit based and space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, which includes a short chemistry research statement. The form sends a request to your chemistry teacher for the recommendation. Questions: tamu_react@tamu.edu.
notes: The program ran for the first time in 2025 (July 14 to 25). The fee and rules above come from the 2026 pages, so check them again when the 2027 application opens. The program site is a Google Sites page run by the department.
duration: The 2026 header lists July 13 to 24, 2026 and also calls it a 6-day in-person program. The 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Applying is free. The registration fee is $250, due after you are accepted (2026 page). Lunch is provided.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 22 (and under 22 as of September 1 of the previous year) who get special education services under IDEA or have a disability under Section 504, and who are in an educational program. That includes secondary school, home school and other recognized programs.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions Vocational Rehabilitation Services office. Counselors refer current VR participants. Students who have not applied for VR but meet the disability rule may also be candidates. Statewide contact: 512-936-6400 or vr.office.locator@twc.texas.gov.
notes: Only for students with disabilities. Texas child labor hour limits for 14 and 15 year olds still apply. The pages do not give a posted 2027 timeline.
duration: At least five weeks of paid work, with at least four hours in a week to count as a week. No more than 40 hours a week.
pay_detail: Wages for hours worked. Each local board sets one hourly wage for its program. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18. You must be in school or a graduate with a satisfactory record. You must be unmarried (except marriage under 18) and not on active duty. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive). You must be of good moral character. Cadets who join before age 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Pick a local squadron from the Texas Wing unit listing. Go to three squadron meetings as a trial. The squadron and higher headquarters must accept you. Call Wing headquarters at 936-205-9013 with questions.
notes: Meeting times differ by squadron. This is a youth program, not a paid job.
duration: Year-round program with squadron meetings, plus encampments and other events
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 from across Texas.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked from the workshop website. Questions: tssrmyrw@gmail.com.
notes: Check the site for the 2027 application. Sponsor contacts: Dorian Damerau 830-387-8429 or Jr. Tompkins 979-541-3411.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: Program fee not stated on the page. Organizers say they can help applicants find sponsors.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page.
notes: The volunteer page lists the program for events, summer camps and more.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer. Teens earn incentives. The page does not name them.

who_can_apply: High school girls. The page does not list grades. The program is accredited through Alpine School District for the fall and spring semesters only.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page. Questions: Stacie Wilding, swilding@thanksgivingpoint.org, 801-768-7426.
notes: The page says the credit is for fall and spring semesters only.
duration: 40 hours per semester for the district credit; some roles need more
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. Interns in some roles get a Thanksgiving Point Team Member Membership.

who_can_apply: Students or recent high school graduates who want to learn about skilled trades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student intake form on the Student page. Parents can email info@thetradecollective.org.
notes: The page does not list specific internships or pay. It says the group is forming partnerships with high schools, colleges and universities. Address on the site: 1910 Greenwood Street, Evanston.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Not stated. The student page, checked on 2026-10-10, says nothing about pay. Ask the group.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 13 years old or accompanied by an adult while on duty.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the library website. You may be interviewed. Volunteers are chosen by their qualifications. The library's needs at the time also count. Call or email the volunteer contact listed on the page with questions.
notes: Quote from the volunteer policy: Volunteers must be at least 13 years old or accompanied by an adult while on duty. The page links to a separate Teen Volunteer path. This card does not cover it in detail.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12. Please RSVP before attending.
how_to_apply: RSVP, then pay online from the zoo page. A scholarship form is there too.
notes: This is a club, not a job. Meets at the Gary K. Clarke Education Center at the zoo, entering through the front admission gate.
duration: 1st and 3rd Tuesday of the month, 5:15 to 6:45 pm, during the school year
pay_detail: $125 per student for the whole school year (includes a t-shirt). A scholarship fund application is linked on the page.

who_can_apply: Individual volunteers must be at least 15. Younger teens can volunteer with an adult. They fill out the Family Volunteer form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Individual Volunteer form on the page.
notes: Group service projects for 5 to 25 people are also offered. Court ordered service is for 18 and older only.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a free annual family membership after 20 volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 18 (14 by April 1) and in middle or high school, and must live and/or attend school in Travis County. Teens with disabilities can apply up to age 22. Other factors such as household income may also be considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (Jotform) and upload a Social Security card and a school ID or recent report card. Eligible applicants are invited to a mandatory job readiness training, then matched to a host site if space allows. Applying does not guarantee a placement.
notes: Phone 512-854-4590. Pay rate, hours and program length are not stated on the page. The page does not mention a work permit. Texas rules for 14 and 15 year olds limit hours (see Texas Workforce Commission child labor page).
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience; hourly rate not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: No age limit. Minors need a signed parental consent form. Volunteers 15 and under (the FAQ says under 15) need an adult chaperone age 21 or older, one adult per 10 young volunteers.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the TreePeople events calendar. The confirmation email has the waiver and parent consent forms. Groups can email volunteer@treepeople.org to ask if there is room.
notes: TreePeople's jobs page lists only an 18+ fellowship, so this is the way in for teens. The page gives two versions of the chaperone age rule (15 and under vs under 15), so confirm by email.
duration: Single events; calendar posted at least a month ahead
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens who are in high school or about to start, and at least 14 as of May 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link is posted. You must finish every step. These are a required Challenge Day, a required volunteer tree planting and an interview.
notes: Competitive. Not everyone who applies gets a job. Returning members can apply for outside study spots with partner groups. 2026 dates are shown. Watch the page for the 2027 schedule. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit (employment certificate) is required for minors under 16, so 14 and 15 year olds need one. A school issuing officer or the county school superintendent gives it.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 12:30 pm
pay_detail: Starting at $12 per hour

who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 in the Tri-Valley area.
how_to_apply: The program page does not say whether you must register. It says to bring several copies of your resume and to dress professionally.
notes: Location: 9300 Alcosta Blvd, San Ramon. The program page does not list which employers will come. Questions: Dublin City Hall, 100 Civic Plaza, 925-833-6650.
duration: One afternoon, 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: Free to attend. This is a fair, not a job.

who_can_apply: Current rules are not posted. The 2022 posting said youth 16 and over with valid photo ID and a valid SSN or ITIN were paid; younger youth got a stipend. Confirm with the program.
how_to_apply: Call (510) 985-9915 or email info@oaklandtrybe.org. Trybe also has a Jobs/Internships page on its site.
notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.
duration: About 100 hours
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).

who_can_apply: Current or rising high school students who are interested in a medical career and can attend in person from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. every day.
how_to_apply: The program page does not describe an application. It says students hear about the camp when staff visit high schools in the El Paso region. Call René André at 915-215-4408.
notes: The program page has a link named Summer Med Camp Mentor. The page gives no details about that role.
duration: Two weeks per session
pay_detail: Snacks and learning materials are free. Camp cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors who live in the City of Tucker.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the city's Youth Council page. Members may reapply at the end of their term.
notes: The page lists no direct phone or email; it links to the city's Contacting the City page. The page does not post the next application date. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: One-year term. Meetings on the third Wednesday, September to April.
pay_detail: Unpaid civic role

who_can_apply: Teens 15 and older. A guardian enters their name to consent for a minor.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the volunteer page. You give contact info, free times, hours wanted, consent from a guardian and photo permission. Call (520) 792-9985 with questions.
notes: The museum hours listed on the page disagree, so confirm shift times.
duration: You choose hours on the application (daily, weekly, monthly or one time).
pay_detail: Unpaid. Can count for school service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Teens and parents must attend an orientation. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Call Class Registration at 520-791-4877 or use the Register for Classes link on the page. Orientation details are emailed after you sign up. A Discount Program is there for people who need low income help.
notes: Aims at recreation careers. Contact 520-791-4873 for the schedule.
duration: Up to 30 hours per week. Program dates not listed.
pay_detail: Registration fee $25 for City residents, $30 for non-residents. The page does not say participants are paid. A discount program exists for low-income families.

who_can_apply: Must be 15 when you apply. Must pass the swim test. Must be free to work all of June and July.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a swim test at tucsonparks.info/lifeguardfallswimtest. The page gives no other form. If you have questions, send an email to cotlifeguard@tucsonaz.gov or call 520-837-8119.
notes: The page shows 2026 in its footer, so the dates are likely fall 2026, but confirm. Swim test: 300 yard front crawl, 50 yard approach stroke with rescue tube, treading water, 50 yard side stroke with a dummy, 10 lb brick retrieval.
duration: Starguard class days listed on the page, then June and July work
pay_detail: Starts at $16.75 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form (PDF on the page) and give it to the library branch where you want to volunteer. The library contacts you if there is an opening.
notes: The application PDF on the page is labeled 2024. Openings depend on each branch, so ask staff.
duration: Not stated. Teens track hours with a log.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at summeryouth.pima.gov. Or pick up a paper form at high schools and community centers in Pima County.
notes: Expect applications to open again in early 2027 (last year it was February). Check the page in January.
duration: Two 2026 sessions: June 1 to June 26, or July 6 to July 31
pay_detail: Minimum $16.54 per hour (2026)

who_can_apply: Teens entering 9th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the zoo volunteer application when it reopens in January 2027, with the teen's own email and phone number. The page gives no direct Zoo Crew link. Call (520) 791-3204 with questions.
notes: Applications are closed now. Teens should be their own main contact with the zoo.
duration: About 4 hours a month for a year, plus a required 4-day training. After one year you must be invited back.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Currently in high school, 16 or older by June 7, 2027, a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and lived in Arizona at least one year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. It has 4 essay questions. Add a signed student and parent agreement. Add 2 recommenders. One must be a science teacher. Their letters are due Jan 7. Add an unofficial transcript.
notes: Both recommendations must be in by Jan 7. If not, your form will not be looked at.
duration: 7 weeks, June 7 to July 23, 2027
pay_detail: No cost to participate. A stipend is not mentioned. Earns 3 units of MCB credit.

who_can_apply: High school students, especially juniors. They come from backgrounds that are hard in money, school or social ways. You need a 3.0 GPA, 2 recommendation letters, a science fair or research example, U.S. citizenship or a permanent visa, and a Social Security number.
how_to_apply: Send in the form with a 1 to 2 page essay. The essay topic is "Why I love science and what the summer medical research apprenticeship will mean to me". The page points to ignorance.medicine.arizona.edu for more but does not give the steps.
notes: Applicants must have a Social Security number. Dates and deadline are not posted. Contact the College of Medicine to confirm.
duration: Length not stated
pay_detail: Federal minimum hourly wage, 40 hours a week for the length of the program

who_can_apply: Arizona teens ages 12 to 18 (grades 7 to 12). You must be 12 by Sept 30, 2026. You must come to monthly meetings and do at least 10 extra volunteer hours each semester.
how_to_apply: Sign up in ZSuites and fill out the Google form. A parent or caregiver and the teen both go to the info meeting. It is required. Questions: Alex Kolnacki, akolnacki@arizona.edu.
notes: Meetings are at the Big Farm, 2201 E. Roger Rd. The page says the program started in 2012.
duration: School year. Meetings are the first Thursday of the month, 5:30 to 7:00 PM, dinner provided.
pay_detail: $20 state and county 4-H fee at registration. Programming is mostly free or low cost.

who_can_apply: Camps are for youth ages 5 to 18. The page does not give an age rule for teen counselors. Ask the camp coordinator.
how_to_apply: Counselor applications open March 1, 2027 at noon on the camps page. Email the Camp Coordinator Moonie with questions.
notes: Applications for camper scholarships and sign-up open the same day. The page does not say if counselor jobs are paid.
duration: Summer camps (over 35 camps a year)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12, or ages 14 to 17. You should enjoy working with people and follow rules.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply online. Turn in your packet to the Parks and Recreation Department. The packet has the form, one reference and a personal statement. Questions: 714-573-3009 or tprd@tustinca.org.
notes: CITs at Camp Tustin volunteer 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. CITs at Little Folks volunteer 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. A training day is required.
duration: 2 to 3 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. The application calls it a non-paid position.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. If you are 14, you must have finished 8th grade. You must keep a 2.0 GPA, pass an oral interview and a background check, and show good judgment.
