how_to_apply: Go to three meetings in a row. Take part in an oral interview at the third meeting. Call 714-573-3197 or email Explorers@tustinca.org with questions.
notes: You must finish an explorer academy in your first year. The page lists two phone numbers, 714-573-3197 and 714-573-3297. Confirm the number before you call.
duration: Meetings every Wednesday at 6 p.m.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12, ages 14 to 17. You need a recommendation letter. You also write 5 to 7 sentences about yourself.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form. Add a recommendation letter. It can be academic, professional or athletic. Add a personal statement of 5 to 7 sentences. Mail it, email TPRD@tustinca.org, or drop it at City Hall, 300 Centennial Way. Then go to the orientation and interview.
notes: You apply once for each school year. The application form asks if you can attend meetings on Wednesday nights. City Hall Parks and Recreation phone: 714-573-3326.
duration: Monthly evening meetings. You volunteer at least 20 hours during the program year (June to May).
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students. Beginners and advanced options are listed.
how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the camp page. Aid questions: mnudlcamps@augsburg.edu.
notes: Students on free or reduced lunch with a qualifying GPA may get full tuition for the July 6 to 10 week. The $425 price is for the 4-day HS Debate & Argumentation commuter camp (June 29 to July 2, 2026). The 1-week policy commuter camp is $600.
duration: From 4 days (HS Debate commuter, June 29 to July 2, 2026) up to 3 weeks (June 21 to July 10, 2026)
pay_detail: From $425 (1 week debate and argumentation, commuter) up to $2,500 (3 weeks with partial residential). Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Any student in grades 9 to 12, from public, private, charter and home schools.
how_to_apply: Use the application flyer and FAQ linked on the page, or contact BestPrep.
notes: The page does not state where it is, what it costs or if there are scholarships. BestPrep also lists an Educational Forum on Feb 17, 2027. It is at the Minneapolis Convention Center.
duration: A week (dates not posted)
pay_detail: Cost not posted. The page says it is kept low with sponsor help. Call 763-233-6325.

who_can_apply: Listed on the theatre's Teens page. No age or other rules are stated.
how_to_apply: Email Associate Production Manager Todd Kalina at tkalina@childrenstheatre.org. Say which area you want to shadow. Say what you hope to learn. Say when you are free.
notes: The page also lists youth tryouts for student actors ages 8 to 18. Those roles are unpaid.
duration: Not stated; you give your availability
pay_detail: Not stated; described as job shadowing only.

who_can_apply: Students going into 8th grade through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Not listed. The page links to a position description and key dates document. Call 651-487-8201 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: The page says the program needs a big time commitment over the summer. It gives no hours. Other roles on Como's volunteer page are for ages 17 and older.
duration: Mid-June through mid-August, with training days in May and June
pay_detail: Described as a volunteer program; pay is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 at the start of the summer program. You must be eligible to work in the United States. The page states no school or residency rule beyond the Twin Cities base. If you join through Step Up or Right Track, those programs have their own rules.
how_to_apply: Look for open positions on the Corps Join page (filter for youth programs) or call the youth program staff at 651-209-9900. Step Up and Right Track applicants apply through those programs.
notes: 2026 home bases were Tamarack Nature Center (White Bear Lake), Harriet Alexander Nature Center (Roseville), Mississippi Gateway Regional Park (Brooklyn Park) and Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge (Bloomington). Do not mix this up with the Summer Youth Corps, the live-in camping crew. That program is not active in 2026 and the Corps is rethinking its youth programs.
duration: June to August, 13 to 17 hours a week, usually 9:00 am to 4:00 pm on Monday and Wednesday or Tuesday and Thursday. Staff provide rides between sites.
pay_detail: Most Youth Interns are paid starting at $13.50 an hour. Some positions are unpaid. Pay may be higher depending on your age and whether Step Up, Right Track or the Corps employs you.

who_can_apply: The page says teens and youth. No minimum age or GPA is stated. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for your contact info, school and GPA, and transcript. If you are under 18, a parent must sign. For questions about your status, email onesmartcookie@cookiecart.org. Do not call.
notes: 1119 W Broadway Avenue, Minneapolis. The page does not say whether the 90 day internship is paid.
duration: 90 day internship, then bakery program; new intern training starts in fall, spring and summer sessions
pay_detail: Pay rates are not listed. The bakery program is paid job training.

who_can_apply: Students who will be in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email Lisa Loudon to sign up. Her address is lloudon@dunwoody.edu.
notes: Camp is listed as an example of past offerings; 2027 camps are not posted yet.
duration: 4 days (Aug 3 to 6 in 2026), 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $350 ($300 early bird), includes lunch, supplies and a field trip

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors and seniors interested in a technical career with a 2.5 GPA. Seniors must file the FAFSA and show high financial need.
how_to_apply: Send the online application, a one page essay, transcripts and the FAFSA (Dunwoody code 004641). You also have an interview with staff. Email p2c@dunwoody.edu.
notes: Must attend a fall orientation and at least 85 percent of monthly workshops. Selection is not guaranteed.
duration: Monthly meetings in the school year plus 3 weeks in summer (2026 dates are not on the page)
pay_detail: Hourly stipend for the 3 week summer experience (amount not stated). Scholarship of up to $10,000 a year for two years for those who enroll at Dunwoody.

who_can_apply: Students in high school at schools that partner with Genesys Works, on track to graduate, who can work in the U.S. and can fit a lighter senior-year schedule.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Genesys Works application page. Then you interview for Summer Skills Training. Then you confirm your spot. Twin Cities contact: 651-789-0088 or tcadmin@genesysworks.org.
notes: Internships are earned. They are not promised. Students must get themselves to work. The application page named a rising senior as the target. The FAQ said junior year. The site did not agree with itself, so ask which grade to apply in. The families page gives $10,000-$12,000 for the internship year. Its summary gives $10,000-$13,000. Ask which is right.
duration: 8 weeks of summer training (160 hours), then 20 hours a week during senior year
pay_detail: Paid for hours worked; the site says interns can earn about $10,000 to $13,000 over the internship year. Rates vary by site.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and 17. You need a reliable ride to the hospital. You must be able to keep patient info private.
how_to_apply: Email three things to volunteer@gillettechildrens.com. They are the application, a Student Reference Form from a teacher or advisor, and a Parent Release Form. If a piece is missing, they will not review it. Some applicants are interviewed in person with a parent.
notes: Before starting you must pass a background check and fingerprinting and show proof of vaccination and a QuantiFERON-TB Gold blood test. These may cost money.
duration: One 3 hour weekday shift per week, June through August
pay_detail: Volunteer. There may be a cost to the applicant for the required health screenings.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 12 who like STEM, from across the Twin Cities. The University of Minnesota summer camps page says students entering grades 8 and 9 are eligible to apply. The page describes a pro-girl program. It does not say whether boys can join.
how_to_apply: Use the Eureka! online application or the PDF application on the page. Do this when registration opens. The PDF comes in English, Spanish or Somali. Contact: girlsinc@ywcampls.org or 612-215-4369.
notes: Described as a pro-girl program (Girls Inc.), so ask whether it is for girls only. Interns are treated as volunteers by the worksite because the stipend comes from Girls Inc., not the worksite. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.
duration: Summer camp about 4 weeks (2026: June 29 to July 24), Mon to Thu 8:45 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Fri to 2 p.m.
pay_detail: Eureka! interns get a stipend from Girls Inc. after completing a 4 week internship (20 hours a week). The amount is not stated. The cost of the summer program is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering or in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply or Request Info links on the camp page. For a scholarship, show proof of SNAP, TANF or FDPIR benefits (or tax forms) and proof of at least a C average in science.
notes: Oct 26, 2026 is a Monday, which matches the weekday on the page.
duration: 1 week, July 12 to 16, 2027, 9 am to 5 pm
pay_detail: $598 before April 30; $698 after. Need-based scholarships can cover full tuition.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. High school students bring a reference form, a parent consent form and a health screening form to the interview. Some roles have higher age limits.
how_to_apply: Send the volunteer application and do an interview. Finish an online orientation. Pass a Minnesota background check. Then train on site. For questions, call 651-254-5709. You can also write to volunteerservices@healthpartners.com.
notes: The page does not name which hospitals take teens, so ask when you call.
duration: Year-round program is at least 6 months and 100 hours. Summer program is 10 to 12 weeks.
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 28 who live in Hennepin, Ramsey or Dakota County. You must meet low income (WIOA) rules. You must also have at least one more barrier. Examples are being a parent, not having stable housing, being 1 to 2 grade levels behind, or being at risk of dropping out. You can still ask if you are not sure.
how_to_apply: Submit the youth and young adult referral form or the Inquire Now form on the Hired page. You must enroll to get services. Offices: Minneapolis 612-808-9500, Saint Paul 651-328-2777, Bloomington 952-303-8303.
notes: Funding sets what is offered. Help with school costs and living costs depends on what money is on hand.
duration: About 6 months of programming, with up to 2 years of support
pay_detail: The page does not state pay. It mentions subsidized internships, job shadows and work experience.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21 who have finished one VALT drawing session. Jobs go first to North Minneapolis residents, but teens from around the Twin Cities can join programs.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Program Registration Form. Then take a VALT session. Then you interview. Call 612-588-1148 or email ContactUs@juxtaposition.org.
notes: VALT is the free drawing class that comes first.
duration: Year-round, about 9 hours a week
pay_detail: Starting wage $16 an hour, about 9 hours a week on average during the school year

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 21.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Program Registration Form. Send questions to VALT@juxtaposition.org.
notes: Held at 1108 West Broadway, Minneapolis.
duration: About 10 weeks per session. Fall 2026: Sept 16 to Nov 20. Winter: Jan 6 to Mar 12, 2027.
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15. Volunteers under 18 need a signed permission slip from a parent. These hospitals take teens. Ridges is in Burnsville. St. John's is in Maplewood. Southdale is in Edina. The U of M Medical Center has an East and a West Bank site. Woodwinds is in Woodbury. Lake Medical Center is in Wyoming. Northland is in Princeton.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then you have an interview and online learning. You also need a background check, fingerprints, a TB test and proof of shots. Last is an online orientation. Call 1-855-324-7843.
notes: A flu shot each year is required. The 100 hour minimum is listed for volunteers in general.
duration: About 100 hours over 6 to 9 months
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the Youth Employment and Training Initiatives page and the Park Board temporary jobs page (minneapolisparks.org/jobs/temporary_jobs/) for the next application.
notes: Pay, season and hours are not stated on the page, so ask the Park Board before you plan. The same page lists Minneapolis Park Corps for ages 18 to 24 as paid training (not for teens). The Park Board teen page also lists Youthline, a mentorship program for ages 12 to 17. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.
duration: Not stated (the page only mentions a '2026 season')
pay_detail: The page lists this under Youth Employment and Training Initiatives but does not say whether Teen Teamworks is paid or give a pay rate. Ask the Park Board.

who_can_apply: Youth leaders ages 14 to 17. Members serve a two year term.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Contact Adrian Waters at Awaters@minneapolisparks.org or 612-849-9048 to ask when the next group is chosen.
notes: The teen programs page calls it a select group. Confirm how to apply and whether it is paid before you plan around it.
duration: Two year term, 5 to 12 hours a month
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. The page says members get support with professionalism, financial literacy and customer service.

who_can_apply: High school students or recent graduates ages 14 to 18 who are U.S. citizens.
how_to_apply: Online application. Choose YES on the form to request financial aid; aid does not affect admission.
notes: The page does not name the exact camp site. Scholarship details are at mnacecamp.org/scholarships (not read).
duration: 1 week (June 14 to 19 and June 21 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Tuition $1,750, due May 1 on acceptance. Travel is not included. $25,000 in financial aid was set aside for 2026.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall. The page also says "current 8th to 11th grade", so confirm before applying.
how_to_apply: Apply online. There is no fee to apply. A deposit is due with the application. It cannot be refunded.
notes: A class that fills moves to a waitlist.
duration: Two weeks per session. Summer 2027: June 14 to 25 and July 12 to 23, 9 am to 4 pm
pay_detail: Tuition is listed as TBA per session for 2027. Discounts: $100 for both sessions and $50 per extra sibling. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up can volunteer in the kitchen and farms without an adult. Ages 12 to 15 need an adult who has done volunteer training. Deliveries need an adult driver (18 to drive alone).
how_to_apply: Register for an orientation on the volunteer page. Under 18 needs a parent signed waiver. Call 612-872-1152.
notes: Some equipment use depends on age.
duration: Shift times not listed
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Volunteers under 18 use the teen form. A parent or guardian must sign it. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online teen volunteer application. Pick the roles, the times you are free and the branch you like.
notes: Some positions need a background check. The form asks for a personal reference and emergency contact. It also asks about required service hours if you need them for school.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 who attend a public school in Minneapolis or Saint Paul. The page says no exceptions at this time.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Call 612-624-4745.
notes: Grant funded. Students must commit to the whole program.
duration: 4 weeks (June 15 to July 10 in 2026), Monday to Friday 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $18 an hour

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You must pass a swim test in the first class (150 yard swim, tread water, a 20 yard timed swim and a 12 foot dive to get a 10 pound object) and show a birth certificate with photo ID.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through the city system. Or call Como Park Pool at 651-489-0378, Highland Aquatic Center at 651-695-3773, or Great River Water Park at 651-642-0390. After you pass, call Great River Water Park to apply for a job.
notes: You need 80 percent on the written exam and must pass all skills. Work permit rule for Minnesota minors not checked.
duration: Course dates not listed
pay_detail: Course cost and lifeguard pay are not listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21.
how_to_apply: Apply for the YJ2 internship through Right Track. Contact Furo Ejero, Furo.Ejero@ci.stpaul.mn.us or 651-266-8989.
notes: School year meetings may mean being excused from class. Right Track has its own program and application; see its own card.
duration: 8 weeks (June 20 to Aug 10 on the page, no year), then 6 to 10 hours a month for two years
pay_detail: Academy is a paid YJ2 internship at $15 an hour, 20 hours a week, Monday to Thursday. Board members also get up to $125 in stipends for meetings and learning tasks.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The page lists ages 15 to 18 for the high school stage. The page says the youth pathway starts in middle school.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe how to apply. Contact the museum at info@smm.org or 651-221-9444 and ask about the Kitty Andersen Youth Science Center.
notes: The season, hours and how to apply are not stated. Check before you plan. There are four STEM areas. They are biological sciences and public health, media and technology, environmental sciences and sustainability, and engineering and design. The work permit rule was not checked.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid as museum employees; the hourly rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Spark-Y serves youth from 14 to 24 and up. No other requirements are listed for the internship.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist through the form on the Spark-Y Engage page.
notes: The page lists several roles. The Pathways Summer Internship is the one for newer workers. Apprenticeships fill fast.
duration: Short term, annual; hours not listed
pay_detail: Described as paid; the rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Contact Mary Morris, the staff contact named on the page.
notes: Site: Baker Outdoor Learning Center. The date pattern comes from the general text on the page.
duration: Training plus at least one week of camp, June to August
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact Vicky Wachtler, the staff contact named on the page.
notes: Site: Eastman Nature Center. The date pattern comes from the general text on the page.
duration: Camps run June to August
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Meant for young people, most of all those who face barriers to work. The minimum age depends on the role. It is 15 for Explorers Camp and Community Engagement. It is 16 for the Camp Internship, Farm Garden, Outdoor Recreation and IT/GIS roles. It is 18 for several others, and some roles do not state a minimum.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Contact Char Myers (Char.Myers@threeriversparks.org) or Terrell Lhotka (Terrell.Lhotka@threeriversparks.org).
notes: The Three Rivers Park District Foundation gives rides money if getting to work is a barrier. The work permit rule was not checked.
duration: June through August, about 20 hours a week (some roles 40)
pay_detail: At least $15 an hour

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Contact Seth Eberle, the staff contact named on the page. No online form is described.
notes: Site: Silverwood Park. The date pattern comes from the general description. It is not a date posted for 2027.
duration: June to March, 30 hours of service
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Twin Cities high school students, new or skilled. Spots are limited. It is hard to get in.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on the Summer Programs page. Questions: denise.huang@stthomas.edu.
notes: Stipend amount is not stated. Radio Camp cost is not listed.
duration: MPR Radio Camp 1 week; Multimedia Storytelling Institute 3 weeks; College Essay Workshop 4 days
pay_detail: Free in 2026 (the Multimedia Storytelling Institute is normally $3,000 and the College Essay Workshop $1,000). Students get a stipend for finishing, plus free lunch and transit passes.

who_can_apply: Students entering their senior year. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: Not described. Phone the department at 612-624-4507.
notes: At the end, interns get a letter of support. It comes from the engineering faculty.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: A stipend and bus transportation are provided; the amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grade 11 or 12. Priority goes to students who have not been in Discover STEM before. Admission is competitive, and the program especially encourages applicants from underrepresented communities.
how_to_apply: Apply online, or by mail on request. Send an unofficial high school transcript and personal statement answers. Do not send the application in pieces. Those are not reviewed.
notes: The camps page for the college also lists other high school options, such as the Run the World AI Explorers Camp (grades 11 and 12) and a Summer Computer Academy for girls in grades 6 to 12. Not a job.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily (day program)
pay_detail: The page says there is no cost to apply and attend, thanks to 3M. It also mentions an enrollment fee or scholarship request after admission, so confirm that nothing is charged.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who have met barriers to science and medicine chances. The program focuses on high schoolers in the Twin Cities area.
how_to_apply: Fill in the enrollment survey on the program site. Send back the signed form by the deadline. You need a letter of reference from a science teacher, an organization leader, or a church pastor.
notes: The site says both ten and twelve students are chosen, so it is a small cohort.
duration: One week (July 20 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: Free for selected students; meals and travel are covered and students get a $400 stipend.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older, a current junior or senior at the time of application, and a U.S. citizen.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add a resume that lists your test scores, a transcript and two letters from faculty. Also add a statement of interest and a statement of goals.
notes: No housing or meals are provided. Applicants under 18 need an adult chaperone for University housing, or can stay off campus with family or friends. Number of spots is not stated.
duration: 8 weeks, May 31 to July 23, 2027 (tentative), 40 hours a week
pay_detail: Scholars earn an hourly wage; the amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Enrolled high school students who completed a full year of single variable calculus by the end of 2025-26. Graduating seniors still count.
how_to_apply: The student fills out the online form. A math teacher emails a short note of support. UMTYMP students do not need the note.
notes: This is a commuter camp only. You do not stay overnight.
duration: 1 week (June 22 to 26 in 2026), about 9 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not listed. No housing or meals are provided.

who_can_apply: Current 10th graders from groups that are not well represented in STEM. You should plan to go to a four year college. You must commit to one Saturday a month through December of 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It needs a note from a STEM teacher or counselor, personal essays, your GPA and a list of your courses.
notes: You must get yourself to the program. Money for rides is available if you ask. Only 10th graders are accepted from 2025 on.
duration: January of 10th grade to December of 12th grade
pay_detail: Free; lunch and a gift included. No stipend. Students who attend through fall of 12th grade and are admitted to the College of Science and Engineering can get a $40,000 scholarship ($10,000 a year for 4 years, from 3M).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students in grades 6 to 12. High school sessions are for grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register through the online form linked on the VetCamp page, or join the mailing list for new dates.
notes: It is held at the Ben Pomeroy Student-Alumni Learning Center. That is on the St. Paul campus. The Minnesota Veterinary Medical Foundation is the sponsor.
duration: One afternoon. Self-hosted camps are about 3 hours; the Aug 12, 2026 high school camp ran 12 to 5 pm. 2026 high school dates: June 10, July 15, Aug 12.
pay_detail: $15 registration fee for self-hosted camps; families with financial need can ask for a waiver.

who_can_apply: Teens from across the Twin Cities. The page does not state an age or grade range.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Applications for 2027-28 open in spring 2027. Follow @walkerteens on Instagram for programming info and updates.
notes: The Walker also offers free Teen Maker Break art sessions, monthly on the third Saturday from 2 to 5 p.m. (materials and snacks provided). Ask the Walker whether WACTAC members are paid and what ages can join.
duration: Weekly meetings during the school year
pay_detail: Pay or stipend is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 by the program start (June 15 in 2026). Two references (one must be from a school teacher, counselor, coach or similar), signed parent consent form, English fluency, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap shots, and TB testing. The page names no upper age limit.
how_to_apply: Register in the UC Davis Health VolunTEEN portal, finish all health clearance items, and submit references. Questions: 916-734-2401 or volunteer.services@health.ucdavis.edu.
notes: Located at the Sacramento medical campus (Davis II Building, 2420 Stockton Blvd). Health clearances (MMR, varicella, Tdap, TB test) take time, so start early. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.
duration: 8-week program, 6-week minimum (2026: June 15 to Aug 7)

who_can_apply: Students in career programs at Davis Senior High, MLK Jr. High, Da Vinci Charter Academy and Esparto High (2025 cohort). Through DJUSD, students are matched to internships by the Internship Specialist.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's CTE teacher or the DJUSD Internship Specialist (Alexha Contreras, 530-757-5400 ext 170). The DJUSD list shows an internship in the spring. It is at the UC Davis Center for Valley Fever.
notes: Based on a July 2025 UC Davis Health news story and the DJUSD CTE internship list. There is no UC Davis application page. Confirm that it runs in spring 2027.
duration: 10 weeks (2025 cohort: Mar 18 to May 22)
pay_detail: The DJUSD CTE page says its internships are unpaid. The UC Davis article does not mention pay.

who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students. No minimum GPA. Admission is first come, first served once your application is complete. No academic credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, two short-answer questions, and pay the application fee. Transcript and personal statement are optional but helpful.
notes: Expensive. The program moved to a new website (discoveryprograms.ucdavis.edu), and the fee page still shows 2025 numbers, so confirm the 2027 price and deadline. Age rule differs between UC Davis pages: other UC Davis pages say ages 16 to 18. A $1,500 deposit is due at enrollment. The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.
duration: about 2 weeks per session (2025: July 7 to 18 and July 21 to Aug 1)
pay_detail: 2025 tuition was $6,985 plus a $100 application fee (includes dorm and meals). 2027 price not posted yet.

who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.
how_to_apply: Get an application from the Upward Bound advisor at your school (Shasta County students ask the GO Center). Send student info and a short essay, a parent-signed eligibility form and two recommendation letters back to the advisor. Questions: eduadvising@ucdavis.edu or 530-752-5887.
notes: Only available at partner schools. Federally funded TRIO program for low-income or first-generation students. No fee or stipend is listed on the pages, so ask.
duration: school year plus summer
pay_detail: No fee listed on the page. Confirm with the program.

who_can_apply: Rising junior or senior. Must be 16 by the first day and not turn 18 before the last day. Must be a permanent US resident living and attending school in the US. Two teacher references needed (one must be a science teacher).
how_to_apply: Apply in the YSP portal between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Submit grades, activities, essays and two teacher references. Ask for a fee waiver before the deadline if you need one. Fee reduction requests are checked after you are accepted.
notes: Very competitive (about 40 students). Residential, so you live on campus. Late and incomplete applications are not accepted. Application fee waivers are given on request. Contact ysp@ucdavis.edu.
duration: 6 weeks (2026 dates: June 21 to Aug 1)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $7,750 (housing, meals and 5 units of credit included). Application fee $45 in 2026. Fee reduction and application fee waiver available.

who_can_apply: High school students looking to get ahead or recover credit. The site mentions free options for California public schools and scholarship applications for eligible students.
how_to_apply: Enroll from the courses page, ask your school counselor about school-paid seats, or call (408) 450-4962.
notes: This is coursework, not a job. Included because many teens use it to free up schedule time for jobs and internships.
duration: Self-paced
pay_detail: Fees vary by course and prices are not on the home page. The site lists free options for California public schools and scholarships. The page does not say anyone is paid.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in El Paso or Pueblo counties. You must be first in your family to go to college, low income, or tied to the military.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link opens at the end of January 2027.
notes: Students entering grades 11 and 12 can take a dual enrollment course for 3.0 college credits at no cost, Monday to Friday afternoons 1 to 3:30 PM during June. The program has run since 1987.
duration: Multi-year program. Summer Academic Institute runs during June.
pay_detail: Free to students. No pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up at the University of Colorado Hospital. It is in Aurora. The same goes for Highlands Ranch. It also goes for Broomfield and Steadman Hawkins Clinic Denver. Other places have other minimum ages.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the hospital you want. The Aurora hospital link is on the program page. Requirements differ by hospital, so check with the hospital first.
notes: Job shadowing at UCHealth is for ages 18 and older. The volunteer page does not list a summer teen program. Ask the hospital about other teen options.
duration: Most locations ask for 65 hours or a steady six months.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: California high school students in grades 8 to 12, per the COSMOS application site. A GPA of 3.5 or above is typical.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement, teacher recommendation(s), transcripts and a parent or guardian e-signature, plus the application fee. You choose one campus and cluster.
notes: Competitive. UCI's own pages still show 2026 details, so the statewide site is the source for the 2027 dates. Students must live on campus for the full program. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses. This card is the UC Irvine campus.
duration: 4 weeks, residential (2027 session dates TBA)
pay_detail: Fee-based residential program. The 2027 cost is not stated on UCI's page, so check the COSMOS site for the current fee.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and over. Selection looks at your application, your ability to keep the weekly schedule, past community service, and your education and career interests.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps. Email ucimcvolunteer@uci.edu or call 714-456-5541 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: Requires a physician-signed medical clearance with immunity proof (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella), Tdap, hepatitis B series, COVID-19 vaccine with booster, flu shot in season, and a negative TB blood test within 90 days of your start date. Also a three-hour orientation. The page says the uniform costs $40, paid by card at orientation.
duration: One 3-hour shift a week, Monday to Friday 4 to 7 p.m., minimum 75 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page lists no age or grade rule. No research experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Email Dr. Victoria Deguzman at Vvdeguzm@uci.edu. Attach a letter of interest, a resume and a transcript. An unofficial transcript is fine.
notes: Exact start and end dates are not posted on the program page.
duration: 8 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid summer internship. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students, including this year's graduates, ages 15 to 19. You must be 15 by the first day of your session. You need one reference from a teacher, coach, administrator or counselor.
how_to_apply: Use the apply link on the program page. Have these ready: an unofficial transcript, your reference's name and email, and answers to three essay questions. Each essay has a 1,500-character limit.
notes: Sessions may change. Notices go out in mid-April. Your reference must email the letter by the same March 1 deadline. Scholarships are available to students with financial hardship.
duration: 5 days. Listed 2027 sessions: June 21 to 25, June 28 to July 2 and July 12 to 16.
pay_detail: Tuition is $2,000. It is due two weeks before the session and cannot be refunded. Partial and full scholarships are available for financial hardship.

who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in high school. The page lists no age or GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the program page. The page recommends preparing your answers ahead to avoid session timeouts. Questions go to Leanna Fong at leannaf@uci.edu.
notes: The program is hybrid. The page says to prepare your answers ahead to avoid session timeouts.
duration: 6 weeks. In 2026 it ran June 15 to July 22. Weeks 2 to 5 take up to 15 hours a week.
pay_detail: The registration fee is $750. The page does not mention scholarships.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or older. A parent must also sign the permission form. You must find a UC Irvine faculty sponsor on your own. The program will not match you with one.
how_to_apply: Find a lab and a UC Irvine faculty sponsor. Give your sponsor and their department the packet. It has an application, a medical form, a safety form and a parent form.
notes: Without a faculty sponsor, your application is not considered. Email Alondra Garcia at alondg19@hs.uci.edu with questions. The page also lists 949-824-5388 for general Education and Admissions.
duration: 1 month to 12 months. It runs in fall, winter, spring and summer.
pay_detail: Unpaid. It is a volunteer, non-credit program. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 with a 3.3 unweighted GPA or higher. You should be interested in healthcare research.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Email your transcript to highschoolresearch@hs.uci.edu. An unofficial copy is fine. You then get a signed confirmation by email.
notes: For a scholarship you write an essay and give family tax information. Tax forms are due before acceptance. The page still mentions the 2025 program in its scholarship text, so ask the program to confirm the details.
duration: 3 weeks. In 2026 the sessions were June 22 to July 10 and July 13 to July 31.
pay_detail: $2,350 for each 3-week session. Limited scholarships are for low-income families at underserved Southern California high schools.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page. Incomplete applications are not read. For a scholarship, check the scholarship box, send a transcript and answer the scholarship question.
notes: This is not an overnight program. Past students may reapply, but the page says preference goes to students who will benefit most. You get a certificate. Questions: Rachel Do, rkdo@hs.uci.edu.
duration: 5 days. In 2026 it ran July 27 to 31, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Breakfast and lunch are included.
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,550. Ten full scholarships are based on financial need and merit.

who_can_apply: Must be 16 by June 1. Grade and residency are not stated. A government photo ID and immunization proof are required.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a required Zoom info session. You get the form by email. Send it back with proof of shots (varicella, MMR, TB test). Then go to one required in-person orientation. Email studentvol@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Info sessions fill fast. Every slot showed FULL or CLOSED when read. The page also points to the Mattel Youth Ambassador program as another option. Santa Monica and West Valley campuses have their own student pages.
duration: At least 50 hours, finished by August 31
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not free for student volunteers.

who_can_apply: High school students. The Summer Precollege Focus Series requires being at least 15 by the first day of Summer Sessions, and some programs set older ages. Regular summer courses must come from a pre-approved high school list.
how_to_apply: Apply or enroll through each page on summer.ucla.edu. California students in grades 9 to 11 can apply for Summer Scholars Support (need and merit scholarships), and 10th and 11th graders from under-resourced California communities can apply for BASE, a free 6-week online course with a UCLA mentor.
notes: Out-of-state and international students cannot receive UCLA Summer Sessions financial aid. Exact program prices were not found; use UCLA's fee calculator before applying.
duration: Focus Series: 3 weeks; other formats vary (2026 sessions ran June 22 to July 31)
pay_detail: Fee-based. Ask UCLA Summer Sessions for current fees. Scholarship programs described on the page include BASE and Summer Scholars Support.

who_can_apply: High school students. No specific grades or ages are listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Today form at engr.ucr.edu/form/ai-enabled-robotics-summer-camp. Email roboticssummercamp@ucr.edu.
notes: Held at Winston Chung Hall on the UCR campus. Dates and price are from the 2026 camp.
duration: 5 days, 9 AM to 4 PM (July 6 to 10 in 2026)

who_can_apply: Current high school students in the Inland Empire. No grades or ages are listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Register Now form on the camp page. Email stemsummercamp@ucr.edu or call the XCITE Center at (951) 827-2612.
notes: The 2026 theme was The Science of Fighting Wildfires. Location in 2026: Tomas Rivera Library, 900 University Ave, Riverside. Confirm first: no cost is stated, and the page does not say whether the theme changes each year.
duration: 5 days, 9 AM to 4 PM (June 22 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the camp page.

who_can_apply: High school students in the Inland Empire (Riverside and San Bernardino counties) who are older than 16 by the program start date. Southern California permanent residents in Inland Empire school districts are encouraged, especially with a referral from a STEM teacher or a UCR outreach program.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the STRIDE page. Email stride@engr.ucr.edu or call (951) 827-5190.
notes: Confirm first: one Apply Now button on the page points to an older 2023 form. The page says applicants must be older than 16 by the program start date and states no maximum age. No stipend or cost is stated. Funded through a CIRM grant.
duration: 5 weeks (June 22 to July 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to get an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application. Give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu. You can also call the TRIO office at (951) 827-4865.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.
duration: Year-round support; UB summer program is 6 weeks (5 weeks bused to campus, final week in residence halls)
pay_detail: Free to join. Only Upward Bound summer participants receive a stipend (amount not stated).

who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 5 to July 31)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $5,518 (housing, meals, field trips) plus a $46 application fee. Financial assistance form available for California residents. Amounts for 2027 not posted.

who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page. Add the course to your cart. No application or essay is needed. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2026: July 6 to July 24)
pay_detail: $3,500 for the July 2026 session (commuter only; no housing or transportation). A hybrid fall session cost $2,000.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months

who_can_apply: Students who finished 9th or 10th grade. You should be truly curious about farming, food, nature science, math and tech.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add your unofficial transcript and two short essays. Add a recommendation form from one or two teachers or counselors.
notes: Questions: agriquest@uga.edu. Cancel 6 or more weeks ahead for a refund minus $50.
duration: 7 days
pay_detail: $300 covers housing, meals, instruction, field trip transport and activities. Full scholarships for accepted students with financial need.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished sophomore year and are 16 by the program start date. You must have taken one high school lab science course and one semester of algebra. You should be interested in ag, food and environmental science. First time participants only.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with short essays. Pick a campus (Athens, Griffin or Tifton). Add two recommendation letters from science or math teachers. Upload an official transcript.
notes: Not residential. You must arrange your own housing and transport, and travel to the campus daily. Contacts on the page: Athens 706-542-2713, Griffin 770-228-7264, Tifton 229-326-4663. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This program requires age 16.
duration: Five weeks (June 1 to July 7 on the page, plus a three day conference July 8 to 10). The page does not show the year.
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship, 30 hours a week. The pay amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students from across Georgia who are going into their senior year. No other rules are listed on the pages. In 2026 exactly 50 students were chosen from 664 applications.
how_to_apply: Apply through the UGA Admissions application portal when it opens. Ask the Office of Academic and Community Engagement (oace@uga.edu) about future cycles. Admissions phone on the application page: 762-400-8800.
notes: Very competitive: a UGA news story dated Sep 3, 2026 says the program got a record 664 applications for 50 spots. Exact 2026 dates and application requirements were not on the pages the reader could open. The ACE page says there is no cost to attend and describes residence hall living and dining, but does not explicitly say housing and meals are covered.
duration: One week, residential
pay_detail: Free to attend. The pages say there is no cost and that housing and meals are included.

who_can_apply: High school students. No grade or age rule is listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Email sdd@uidaho.edu or call 208-885-1186.
notes: Full refunds were offered only through June 11 in 2026. Check the page next spring for new dates and prices.
duration: 4 days (June 24 to 27 in 2026)
pay_detail: $450, or $425 for returning campers. It covers workshops, supplies, room and board. Local students who go home at night can email sdd@uidaho.edu for a different price.

who_can_apply: Montana high school students. The page says sophomores and juniors during the 2025-2026 school year. That wording may be old, so ask the program contact about your grade.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply here form on the program page when it opens. Questions: Annie Zavitz at Annie.Zavitz@mso.umt.edu.
notes: Students live in residence halls and share meals. No closing date is posted, so apply as soon as the form opens.
duration: 2 weeks (July 5 to 16, 2027)
pay_detail: Free. A US Department of Education grant pays the cost.

who_can_apply: Rising 12th graders with at least a 3.2 GPA and no C's in math or science, who finished Trigonometry, Chemistry and Pre-Calculus with a B or better, want to study engineering at UMD, and can attend full time for all 4 weeks.
how_to_apply: Online application with an essay and resume, two teacher recommendations (one math, one science), and a virtual interview with the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: The page says taking part does not guarantee admission to UMD. No housing is offered. A free program, not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 4 weeks (Jul 7 to Jul 31 in 2026), commuters only
pay_detail: No cost to students selected (stated on the page). No stipend is stated.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th grade through graduating 12th grade. The page does not state a minimum age or a GPA rule.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and choose a campus or online. Then apply online. You need a transcript, a health insurance card and a card to pay the application fee and deposit. There are no essays or recommendations.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 prices; 2027 prices are not posted. Commuter program: no campus housing except the business course BMGT262. The grade posts to a UMD college transcript. Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 3 weeks (Jul 13 to Jul 31 in 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 package fee: $1,791 campus option or $1,420 online option (3 credits, tuition and fees). Also a $75 application fee and a $275 program deposit that is credited to the bill. Partial scholarships, none above 30% of the package fee.

who_can_apply: The page title says ages 12 to 15 (the University youth programs list says 12 to 16). Applicants attend a February info session, interview, and a mandatory one-day orientation in June.
how_to_apply: Attend the free virtual info meeting in February, get the application, sign up for an interview, pay the fee if accepted, then attend orientation. Call 612-301-1210 for questions.
notes: Good first leadership experience for younger teens. Volunteer hours can be logged.
duration: Flexible half or full days over the summer
pay_detail: One-time $100 registration fee (orientation, training, t-shirt, certificate, supplies); financial aid available for students who qualify for free or reduced school lunch. CIT service is volunteer time.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 with an interest in automotive tech, manufacturing, engineering, planning or robotics. Space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Application steps for 2027 are posted early in 2027 on the camp page.
notes: Competitive: 20 spots. Day camp; the page does not mention transportation.
duration: One week, day camp
pay_detail: Free to attend; lunch is provided

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 9 with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, who have completed or can enroll in pre-algebra and are interested in engineering, science, transportation or technology.
how_to_apply: Application information for 2027 is posted early in 2027. Selection process details are on the camp's admission decisions page.
notes: For younger teens. The University's youth programs list shows ages 13 to 16 for this camp.
duration: Two weeks, day camp
pay_detail: Free two-week day camp

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2027, at a high school or homeschooled. Not open to 8th grade or below or to graduates.
how_to_apply: Pre-register online (interest form on the Explore@UNC pages). Pre-registering improves placement chances. Payment details come after placement.
notes: Families must have a local trusted contact. A temporary drop-off pass is $25 for the week and all-day parking is the family's cost. UNC also lists dual enrollment as a visiting student for rising seniors (see summer.unc.edu/dual-enrollment/); its cost was not read. Questions: explore@unc.edu.
duration: 1 week. 2027 weeks: June 14-18, June 21-25, June 28-July 2, July 12-16. Commuter only, no residential option.
pay_detail: $625 per student per week (includes a $50 non-refundable registration and placement fee); some tracks may add a $25 activity fee; lunch and snacks included. Need-based aid for permanent NC residents who are rising seniors.

who_can_apply: Honor roll students who have finished their junior year. International high school students cannot be considered. If you are under 17, you must say you will live with a parent or legal guardian during Summer School.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the Summer Visitor application. Send a transcript. Send a personal statement that names the course. Also send a letter of support from a teacher, principal or counselor.
notes: You can only take courses in Summer Session 2. High school seniors cannot audit courses. The 2027 application is not open yet, so no dates exist to confirm.
duration: Summer Session 2
pay_detail: Summer School tuition applies. Amount is not on this page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.
duration: August to May

who_can_apply: The page says 'Be 14-18 years of age or older' and 'Currently enrolled in high school'.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then do a placement interview and orientation. Other steps are a handbook review, state and national background checks, a health screening, an annual flu shot and a TB test. Email DM_Volunteers@unitypoint.org or call (515) 263-5227.
notes: This card is for Iowa Lutheran Hospital only. Other UnityPoint hospitals in Des Moines have their own volunteer pages; teen rules for them were not read. The health screening, flu shot and TB test take time, so start early.
duration: Set number of hours not stated for teens.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers can earn silver cord hours for graduation.

who_can_apply: In 2026: high school students entering their senior year and 2026 high school graduates. The page says the 2027 details will be updated later.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You fill out a separate scholarship application too. Got a question? Call 406-243-2537. Or send a note to bethany.applegate@umontana.edu.
notes: Students earn two college credits. The page says to check back in early 2027 for updated information and the application.
duration: About 10 days (2026 dates: June 10 to 19)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $2,800 for tuition, course fees, housing, all meals and program costs. Scholarships are worth about 10 to 50 percent of the cost and need a separate application.

who_can_apply: Current 8th graders who will start high school in the fall and are first-generation college students (no parent finished college in the U.S.). No minimum GPA. Plan to join for all 4 years.
how_to_apply: Apply online with essay answers. A committee picks students.
notes: The page text looks old (it lists a May 30, 2022 deadline). Email or call before you plan around it. For 8th graders only, so it is for students about to start 9th grade.
duration: 4 years. Two weeks of summer camp each year.
pay_detail: Free. Lunch and rides are provided. A one-time $15 registration fee is due if you are accepted (tell the team if that is a problem).

who_can_apply: Current 10th graders at a public or private high school in Wyoming or homeschooled, who live in Wyoming and plan to return to a Wyoming school. Must stay all three weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online student application. It needs a personal statement. This is an essay of at least 300 words or a video of no more than 4 minutes. It also needs an awards and achievements list and a recommendation letter. Your counselor uploads your transcript.
notes: The how-to-apply page says HSI 2027 applications open October 1 and all pieces are due February 7, 2027. Wyoming students only.
duration: Three weeks in June (the exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program pages)
pay_detail: Room, board and supplies are paid by funds from the Wyoming Legislature. There is a $325 activity fee. Travel and personal spending are on the student.

who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or one who has completed the sophomore year (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent high school transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office. The page lists Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov as the contact for questions and does not say where to submit, so confirm the submission address with the office. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated

who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.
duration: Washington Week March 6 to 13, 2027
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.
duration: Four weeks, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each class day (2026 classes began June 22)
pay_detail: 2026 total for domestic students: $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential. That adds tuition $7,401, course materials $300, program fee $325 and health center $104; residential adds $3,440 room and board. Also a $85 nonrefundable application fee and a $1,000 deposit that counts toward the total.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 in 2026, rising grades 9 to 12. Active MESA, Mission Science and Engineering Transformer students come first. So do students at STEM Center schools. All students are considered.
how_to_apply: When it is open, send a student form and a teacher recommendation. You can use the online form or the PDF. Forms that are not complete are not considered. Contact k12summer@usc.edu.
notes: The page says in person at USC main campus. The USC Viterbi summer programs list calls it virtual. Confirm the format before you count on it.
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores or juniors who are 16 by July 5 of the program year, interested in STEM, and U.S. citizens. Past SEES interns cannot repeat.
how_to_apply: Apply online at spacegrant.net/apps/sees: essays (maximum 250 words per response), a short intro video (submit the link), an unofficial transcript or report card, and a recommendation form. Travel scholarships are available and do not affect your selection.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applications and 215 accepted in 2024 (FAQ). It is an educational internship, not a paid job.
duration: Online work in June and July plus a 2-week on-site session in Austin (July 5-18 in 2026)
pay_detail: No stipend. Free for scholarship recipients and for virtual participation; paid participants pay $2,000 tuition (meals, housing, tours and local travel included, travel to Austin not included). Travel scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Texas residents are prioritized. You must be 15 or older by June 1, 2027 and available all five weeks. In person only. You arrange your own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in mid January 2027. First round notices go out at the end of April and second round in early May, with a deposit due one week after you accept. Email hsra@utexas.edu.
notes: This costs a lot and is hard to get into. The page says a few need-based scholarships may be available. They give a stipend plus free tuition. There are no merit scholarships now. Your lab spot is based on your interests, your free time and space. Full tuition is due in mid May.
duration: 5 weeks, June 7 to July 14, 2027 (off June 18 and July 5)
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $4,500. Payment is due only after you accept a lab placement. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Participation does not guarantee admission to UT Austin.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button on the UT page. Summer Discovery, not UT, handles applications and sign-up. You can email summerdiscovery@utexas.edu. Or call 516-447-4907.
notes: Expensive. Students get a certificate of completion and a campus grade letter. The Summer Discovery page shows an early enrollment discount ending Oct 31 but does not say the year.
duration: 2 week or 3 week sessions (2026: June 14 to 26 and June 28 to July 17)
pay_detail: Costs $3,799 to $7,999 depending on the options chosen (the Summer Discovery page gives one range). Some courses add fees. Financial aid is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students entering 8th or 9th grade. A panel reviews applications (not first come, first served), and students who attend schools without engineering or STEM offerings are encouraged to apply. Houston and San Antonio sessions are by invitation only.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp page; you are notified by email by mid-May. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: For younger teens (about 13 to 15). Both 2026 Austin sessions are listed as full.
duration: 4 days (Austin sessions June 8-11 and July 6-9 in 2026; both were full)
pay_detail: $75 commitment fee for Austin participants, collected only after acceptance (day camp, no lodging)

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 50 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $200 is a barrier.
duration: 5 days (June 21-25 and July 12-16 in 2026)
pay_detail: $200, paid only after acceptance (students stay in a campus residence hall)

who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.
duration: June 20 to 25, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.

who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.
duration: June 6 to 11, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.

who_can_apply: Texas high school juniors only. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April. More info: https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/undergraduate/subiendo/
duration: June 13 to 17, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Travel is covered by the program.

who_can_apply: 4-H youth in 9th to 12th grade. Adults also attend.
how_to_apply: Register on Zsuite (4h.zsuite.org). Questions: contact the Utah 4-H State Office at 435-797-4444 or your county 4-H office.
notes: Held with Rep. Joel Briscoe and the Office of Legislative Research.
duration: 1 day (2026: April 22, 9 AM to 3 PM)
pay_detail: $25 per person (includes t-shirt and lunch).

who_can_apply: All teens in grades 9 to 12 (those who have finished 8th grade).
how_to_apply: Sign-up for the 2027 Teen Summit will open in summer 2027. Contact Vernon Parent at vernon.parent@usu.edu or 385-468-4832.
notes: A youth waiver is needed. Check the page for the cost when registration opens.
duration: 3 days (July 12 to 14, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not posted yet.

who_can_apply: Utah teens in grades 9 to 12. A waiver must be uploaded in Zsuite when you register.
how_to_apply: Sign up through Zsuite and upload the signed waiver. Teens in grades 10 to 12 can also apply to the Teen Winter Retreat Design Team, which has 8 spots. Apply by Oct 24 with a 4-H portfolio, which is a resume and cover letter, and short answers.
notes: Design Team applications are open Sept 1 to Oct 24 and let teens plan activities and teach workshops. Questions: Utah 4-H State Office, 435-797-4444.
duration: Friday 4 PM to Saturday 3 PM (Jan 22 to 23, 2027)
pay_detail: $135 per person. Includes lodging, meals and activities.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18 in any Utah county. Find your county office to sign up.
how_to_apply: Use the Find your County Office link on the Utah 4-H site, then ask that office how to join. Registration for state events is through Zsuite.
notes: State events include Teen Summit, Teen Winter Retreat and Mock Legislature. Fees and dates differ by county and event. Ask your county office.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county office about fees.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The apply page says the help is for youth who are out of school and struggling to connect to work or school, or who struggle at school or work. A counselor decides if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Apply online or at a local Employment Center. A counselor contacts you within three business days. You then send the papers they ask for within 45 days. Together you make a job plan.
notes: This is a state program with eligibility checks, so not every teen qualifies. You need a Utah ID account to apply online. The program page does not say which employers or pay rates are used.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The page says paid internships. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 when you finish the application. Some jobs have other age rules. You need a valid email address.
how_to_apply: Fill out one online application. List other jobs you would take as backups. Read the employee rules before you apply. You can call Employee Services at 801-451-8058 for help.
notes: Lagoon is in Farmington, Utah. Perks include free entry to Lagoon Family Days and park store discounts. The park uses E-Verify to check work eligibility. A separate job page covers the fall Frightmares season.
duration: Seasonal. Dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Pay is called competitive. The rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 through 21 (or age 22 while in special education services). You must be in a high school or after high school program. You must be eligible for IDEA services. Or you have a disability under section 504. You do not have to be a client of Vocational Rehabilitation.
how_to_apply: Contact your school Vocational Rehabilitation liaison or a local VR office. You can send an email to vrtransition@utah.gov. You can also call 801-887-9500.
notes: Every public high school and charter school has a VR counselor. Contractors check that a student fits before services start.
duration: Varies by student
pay_detail: Instruction by community partners is free.

who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders enrolled in an approved agriculture class for the next school year, with an approved SAE plan. High school graduates are not eligible. Your school must run a Summer Ag Program.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school agriculture teacher. You need an approved SAE plan in the Agricultural Experience Tracker (AET). Use your boundary school's Summer Ag Program. If that is not available, you can work with a school in the same district with parent consent and approval.
notes: The guide is written for teachers and districts. Each program needs at least 35 students and a licensed ag teacher, so not every school has one. Ask your ag teacher.
duration: Starts the day after the school contract ends and runs to the day before the next one starts
pay_detail: The program itself is school based. Projects can be paid or unpaid, and your employer may pay you for SAE work. School credit may be offered.

who_can_apply: High school students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade. You should like STEM jobs and mining engineering.
how_to_apply: The program page has a Get Notified for Future Camps option. Email miningengineering@utep.edu. Or call 915-747-7057.
notes: No 2027 dates are posted on the program page.
duration: 3 days per session
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: High school students at schools in the program. Low-income students who could be the first in their family to go to college must qualify. Schools: Bel Air, Del Valle, Parkland, Riverside and Ysleta (YISD). Also Eastlake, El Dorado, Fabens, Pebble Hills, Socorro and Tornillo (SFT ISDs).
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Email upwardbound@utep.edu or call (915) 747-5062.
notes: Federally funded. Students must qualify to be selected. This is a college prep program, not a job.
duration: Through high school graduation and the first summer semester at UTEP
pay_detail: Free to students.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in good standing with a minimum 3.5 GPA in a college prep curriculum, age 15 or older on the first day and 18 or younger on the last day.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts, one teacher or administrator recommendation uploaded by the recommender, and a 350 to 500 word essay. Financial aid materials are due by March 1.
notes: Residents live in an air-conditioned residence hall with a 10 pm curfew. Travel, books, laundry and spending money are not included. Questions: UVaAdvance@virginia.edu, 434-243-2241. The Cost and Payment page was not read.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 11 to August 7), residential
pay_detail: The FAQ says the maximum aid package covers full tuition and fees for Virginia residents, which is $7,097 for 2026. The cost for other students and the full breakdown were not read. Small number of need-based aid packages.

who_can_apply: High school youth ages 14 to 18. Students must attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian and an all-day orientation on the first day of the program.
how_to_apply: Submit the online interest form, attend a mandatory virtual information session with a parent or guardian, then interview if selected. Two references must complete the online reference form before the interview.
notes: The page mentions a lottery. Cost and immunization rules for juniors were not stated on that page; UVA Health's general volunteer page lists a health assessment, vaccination requirements, background check and training for volunteers. Questions: 434-924-5251.
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 8 to July 31); at least 50 hours, or one full weekday, with at least 6 weeks of service

who_can_apply: 4-H participants are youth ages 5 to 19. Community 4-H clubs are for ages 9 through 18. You join by contacting your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Virginia Cooperative Extension office and ask about the 4-H program.
notes: The page also lists a 4-H State Congress, camps, maker education, shooting education and youth leadership opportunities. Details such as dates and fees for those were not on the page.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Ask your local Extension office.

who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You and your parents must live in Virginia. Home-schooled boys can apply if they meet the home school rules on the site. You cannot attend Boys State twice.
how_to_apply: Your high school counselor suggests candidates. Local American Legion post members interview them. Find your district chairperson on the Apply page. Ask about how your district does it.
notes: Delegates stay in university dorms. A delegate who turns 18 before the last day must pass a background check. It costs about $16, and the program refunds it. Two delegates go to Boys Nation in Washington, DC. The site lists a 2027 page, but no 2027 dates were found on the pages. The apply page lists the fee as a $600.00 application fee per delegate. It says individual or parental sponsorships are not permitted. Registrar: registrar@vaboysstate.org.
duration: One week (the 2026 session ran June 21 to 27, 2026)
pay_detail: Free to the delegate. The $600 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as an American Legion post, business or school group. Parents and students may not pay it.

who_can_apply: Students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Coordinator at elpcdce@va.gov. Ask about the summer youth program.
notes: The program page says applications open in May but gives no 2027 dates.
duration: June through August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. Public, private and home school students can apply. Must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident of the United States (proof is needed).
how_to_apply: Delegates are selected by local American Legion Auxiliary units by interview, whenever possible. If your school has not been contacted, find your district on the map and email your district registrar for help. Online registration opens in spring 2027 for chosen delegates.
notes: The 2027 director listed is Cheryl Shine, director@vagirlsstate.org. Delegates must stay until 3:00 PM Friday to get program credit. The pages do not say the cost, so ask your district registrar.
duration: One week: Sunday June 20 to Friday June 25, 2027
pay_detail: There is a delegate fee, but the amount is not stated on the program page. Fees are paid to the district registrar (the site lists April 15, 2027 for fees to reach registrars). Ask your district registrar about the cost and who may sponsor you.

who_can_apply: Virginia youth who will be 13 or 14 years old on January 13, 2027. You must be in good school standing. Your school must agree to the long absence.
how_to_apply: Apply on the portal linked from the Page Programs page. Finish every part. Talk to your school first, since you will miss weeks of class. Questions: HousePageInfo@house.virginia.gov or (804) 698-1502.
notes: Pages live together and have a study hall each night. Not the Senate Page Program. 2028 dates not posted.
duration: The 2027 session. The page says 7 weeks in odd-numbered years
pay_detail: Paid, about 40 hours a week: a weekly expense payment plus a wage every two weeks. Amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 (18-year-olds must be enrolled in high school). Based on the 2024 flyer; check the current year's rules.
how_to_apply: 2024 flyer: application with parent signature, a 1-page essay, an availability schedule, and a virtual orientation. Contact the VA Center for Development and Civic Engagement, vhalomyouthprogram@va.gov.
notes: Closed now. The age, hours and application steps come from the 2024 flyer because the current page only says 2026 applications are closed. The 2024 flyer also required COVID vaccination or an exemption; check the current policy.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2024: June 17 to July 26)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free to join; volunteers over 100 hours can be considered for scholarships through community partners (2024 flyer).

who_can_apply: Virginia residents who are 13 or 14 on the first day of session (the second Wednesday in January), with no exceptions. You live with a parent or guardian. You go to an accredited school or a qualifying home school. You should have an A or B average.
how_to_apply: Use the Application for Admission page of the Prospective Senate Page Portal during the open window. Questions: pageinfo@senate.virginia.gov or (804) 698-7410.
notes: Pages stay at a designated hotel Sunday night to Friday noon each week, and the hotel room is billed to the Senate Clerk's Office. Admission counts as an excused school absence. Cell phones are turned in during work hours. Rates are listed as subject to change. The overview page lists a $50 activity fee in recent years and does not list uniform or binder costs.
duration: The whole legislative session: 46 calendar days in odd-numbered years and 60 calendar days (nine total weeks) in even-numbered years
pay_detail: $340 a week before taxes plus a $225 a week non-taxed expense deposit (per diem). Rates can change. Families pay about $50 for an activity fee, uniform clothes and a binder, and get the student to Richmond.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 through 17. You must be at least 14 by June 1, 2027, must not turn 18 before the session ends, and must still be in high school the fall after the program. You need your own email, bank account and photo ID.
