how_to_apply: Fill out the online Crew Member application on the page. Two professional or academic references must turn in their forms by the deadline. Chosen applicants join a group interview. They also go through a background check.
notes: Competitive. The page says it gets many more applications than spots. About ten crew members live at each host park with three to four adult crew leaders. Crews are split into male and female groups. Cell phones, laptops and other devices are not allowed during the program. Contact: vspycc@dcr.virginia.gov. Virginia's labor department says 14 and 15 year old workers need an Employment Certificate before working. Its page does not mention this program. Ask the program if one is needed.
duration: Two weeks. 2027 sessions: June 20 to July 3, or July 11 to 24
pay_detail: $750 stipend after you finish the two-week program. You may also get community service hours.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens).
how_to_apply: Use the unit locator to find a cadet or composite squadron. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Or apply online if your squadron says you can.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Virginia Wing HQ: 7401 Airfield Drive, Richmond, VA 23237, 804-454-7356. The wing site lists squadrons in Blacksburg, Charlottesville, Herndon, Springfield, Richmond and other towns.
duration: Weekly squadron meetings all year
pay_detail: Not a job. Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. Some jobs need you to be 18. These are AniMeals, customer service and events. Parent and child volunteering is not offered.
how_to_apply: Look at the open shifts and apply for one you can work. A volunteer coordinator then contacts you to set up an orientation. You also take role workshops and shadow shifts.
notes: Students can earn community service hours with the same six month, weekly shift promise. Court ordered hours are not accepted. Volunteers must be fully vaccinated, according to the FAQ. Sunday dog care is the greatest need.
duration: Most roles ask for one shift a week for six months to one year
pay_detail: Unpaid. New volunteers buy a $30 Volunteer Starter Kit with a shirt, name badge and manuals.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18, attending high school in Santa Clara County and living in the county. Able to give up to 5 hours a month for 2 years, and attend quarterly Wednesday evening meetings in person.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Commission interest form. To apply you need to know your Valley Water board district (find your home address on the map on the page).
notes: Meetings are at Valley Water headquarters, 5700 Almaden Expressway, San Jose.
duration: 2-year term, up to 5 hours a month

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the program page. The page does not list the steps.
notes: You also get help with your resume and may be placed in a job at the Y. The page does not list locations, so ask your nearest Y.
duration: 8 weeks, flexible
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Cost is not listed either.

who_can_apply: Teens aged 13 to 15. Applicants send a portfolio of 10 images in all. It has 5 to 7 finished works and 3 to 5 sketchbook images. They also send a letter of intent of 500 to 1,000 words.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY NOW link on the page to submit the portfolio and letter of intent. Questions: submissions@artsumbrella.com or 604-681-5268.
notes: Scholarship-funded learning program, not a paid job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: October 2026 to June 2027
pay_detail: Free to students (full scholarship). Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students aged 15 to 18, or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Emily Carr University Continuing Studies site (use the Apply Now link on the page). Questions: teens@ecuad.ca.
notes: Paid-for arts program, not a job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: Thursdays 4 to 7 PM, October 15, 2026 to February 11, 2027
pay_detail: Registration fee $555.90 (the page does not state the currency; likely Canadian dollars). Four full-tuition scholarships are available for Indigenous students or students facing financial barriers.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older before you apply or go to an information session. Patient contact roles need age 18 or older. Child patient support roles need work or volunteer experience with children.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Staff will call you for an interview. If you get in, you do a record check, a reference check and training.
notes: The biggest need is Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm; evening and weekend spots usually go to current volunteers. Intake can take several months. If you are not placed within 6 months, the application is closed and you may apply again. Contact: volunteer@cw.bc.ca.
duration: One year for every volunteer role
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Grade 12 students in BC and the Yukon. From Fall 2026, Grade 11 students are not eligible even if they take Grade 12 level courses. Students in grades 8 to 11 can use the Self-Directed program instead, which offers recorded sessions.
how_to_apply: Register online. You give your contact details and a sponsor teacher's name and email. You give a signed Participant Agreement Form. You give three answers of 150 words or less. After the deadline, students are picked by random draw. Priority goes to First Nations, Inuit and Metis students and to students from different schools.
notes: Registration for the 2026 round is closed. Watch the page for the next round. In person sessions are at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them.
duration: 4 Thursday evenings, 6:30 to 8:00 p.m.
pay_detail: No cost is listed on the page. Attending all sessions makes you eligible to apply for a scholarship with $1,000 CAD toward post-secondary tuition.

who_can_apply: Grade 11 and 12 students in BC and the Yukon. No research experience needed. Limited to the first 1,000 students who apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for your name, contact details, grade and school. It asks for a parent or guardian's contact. It asks for one answer of 150 words or less. Say why you want to attend.
notes: Online talks only, not a job or hands-on lab work. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The institute says it does not offer any formal placements for students who want to volunteer, job shadow or gain work experience. The application form link is on the page.
duration: 10 monthly online sessions, Sept 2026 to June 2027, about 1 hour each
pay_detail: Free. You get a certificate of participation if you apply and attend 7 of the 10 sessions.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 30 who need to find work. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Click an event under Upcoming Events on the page to apply. Central office: 604-879-6554 or info@bgcbc.ca. Seats are limited.
notes: Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet. The page did not say where the workshops are held.
duration: 8 weeks per session
pay_detail: Participants are paid to take part, with a completion bonus for finishing all 8 weeks. Amounts are not stated on the page. Free to join.

who_can_apply: High school students in BC, grades 10 to 12 on the research institute page. A teacher must first register the school with the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame. The organizers encourage schools to consider students who are Indigenous, Black, a person of colour, or from rural or lower income backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to register your school on the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame website (cdnmedhall.ca/discoverydays). The teacher then gets the student sign-up steps. If you cannot find a teacher, email cmhf@cdnmedhall.ca. Give your city, high school and the event.
notes: One day event, not a job. The Medical Hall of Fame page does not name the city, but the research institute page says the event is at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Grades come from the institute page only.
pay_detail: No registration fee. You or your school pay for transportation and any parking.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older for long-term care sites; 18 or older for acute care (hospitals). You must complete a free criminal record check and get a free yearly flu shot or wear a mask.
how_to_apply: Pick a site on the volunteer page (for example Holy Family Hospital, Mount Saint Joseph long-term care or a St. Vincent's site) and fill out its online form. List references like teachers or coaches. If chosen, you will be called for an interview.
notes: At 16 or 17 you can only volunteer at the long-term care sites. There is no shadowing or direct patient care. Most shifts are weekdays during work or school hours. The FAQ also says Public Health requires two COVID-19 shots for volunteers.
duration: 1 to 3 hours a week for at least 4 or 6 months in a row, depending on the program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can ask for a reference after 30 hours at long-term care sites.

who_can_apply: Core volunteer program: at least 16 years old, 100 hours minimum. High School Work Experience: Lower Mainland students in Grades 11 and 12; teachers sign students up.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page for the next intake. For the work experience placement, ask your teacher to sign you up.
notes: The Science World Teen Advisory Group (ages 16 to 18) is on hiatus and not taking applications (page checked 2026-10-09). Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: 100 hours minimum, one 2 to 3 hour shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Indigenous (First Nations, Metis or Inuit) high school students in grades 9 to 12. You live in Metro Vancouver or Kelowna.
how_to_apply: Watch the seed2STEM page for the application. Email seed2STEM@icord.org or call 604-675-8830.
notes: Exact opening day not posted.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Minimum wage for 25 hours a week. Transit passes, loaner laptops, some meals and youth support workers are provided.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 years of age by June 29, 2026. If accepted, you submit a criminal record check and complete training.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application, attend one in-person interview, then complete in-person or online training. Returning volunteers can apply as Lead Volunteers by email.
notes: SFU Camps says it is not a registered non-profit; check with your teacher that your school accepts these hours for service or work experience credit. Top volunteers are encouraged to apply as paid instructors later (2026 instructor wage $27.05 to $28.50 per hour, CAD); the minimum age for instructors is not stated on the page. Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: Minimum 2 weeks (at least 80 hours), consecutive or separate
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get volunteer hours, evaluations, confirmation letters and a reference request option.

who_can_apply: Teens age 16 and older, and adults. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the "Volunteer with us" form linked on the Space Centre careers page. Questions can go to careers@spacecentre.ca.
notes: Age 16 and up, so 13 to 15 year olds cannot apply. The pages do not give shift length, hours or a start date, so ask before you plan. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Rechecked 2026-10-10: the volunteer page loads and confirms age 16 and up, the summer Augmented Reality role and the "Volunteer with us" form. It gives no year, dates or deadline.
duration: Not stated. The summer Augmented Reality role is weekly support.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page lists education and skills training and mentions telescope viewing on some evening shifts as a volunteer benefit.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17 can join EcoStewards, DIRT, Nature House Hosts, EcoRangers and EcoCamp Assistants. Ages 12 to 15 can join only EcoStewards, and only with adult supervision. A parent or guardian must sign the youth consent form.
how_to_apply: Register and sign up through Better Impact. If a role is closed, fill in the Volunteer Interest Form. Email vols@stanleyparkecology.ca with questions.
notes: Volunteer role in Canada. British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet, so work permit is marked unknown. Most other roles on the site are for volunteers 16 and older.
duration: Varies by role; many are seasonal
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can request a reference letter after 25 hours.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed grade 10 or equivalent. UBC recommends about a 78% average, 3.5 GPA, B average or IB 5. Students still learning English should have IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 80 or higher. Open to students from other countries.
how_to_apply: No application, transcripts or proof of English are needed. Check that you are eligible. Add a course or mini school to your cart. Have a parent or guardian create a Family Account. Pay the deposit at checkout. Then finish the information package within 48 hours.
notes: Costs money, and it is a camp-style university course, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The fee table is labeled 2026 and still shows a 'due May 1, 2026' date next to the 2027 sessions, so check the 2027 fees before you plan. An online version also exists (3 week courses); this card covers the on-campus version. Rechecked 2026-10-10: the on-campus page confirms the 2027 session dates and the residence and commuter deadlines on this card. It does not say when 2027 registration opens. It still labels the fee table 2026.
duration: 2 weeks per session
pay_detail: 2026 fees listed in CAD: course $1,940 for Canadian students (including permanent residents) or $2,620 international; mini school $2,110 Canadian or $2,855 international. Optional residence add-on $2,650. A $500 deposit is due when you register. Fees can change. The President Bursary is for B.C. grade 11 students with financial need.

who_can_apply: First Nations, Inuit or Metis students going into grades 9 to 12. Week 1 is for students going into grades 11 or 12. Week 2 is for students going into grades 9 or 10. The pages do not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Science application online (UBC form). Or send it by email to summer.science@ubc.ca, or by mail. A reference letter of about 200 words is recommended. It can come from a teacher, coach, mentor or community leader.
notes: Only for Indigenous students (First Nations, Inuit, Metis). It is a camp, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The page still shows 2025 dates, so check the newest page before you plan. The application page lists the 2026 deadline of June 15, 2026.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: $200 program fee covers housing and meals. Workshops and Vancouver Aquarium admission are covered. Bursaries for students with financial need and travel bursaries are available. Travel to Vancouver is not included.

who_can_apply: Teens going into Grade 10, 11 or 12 who live or go to school in Vancouver. You must want to finish school and not miss a lot of it. You cannot have serious arrests, a record of trouble with police, or gang ties.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Apply Now button on the VPD Cadet page when it reopens in spring 2027. Questions: cadets@vpd.ca.
notes: About 90 cadets a year. It is a leadership program, not police recruiting. The VPD Indigenous Cadet Program is a different summer job for ages 19 to 29. Unpaid, so BC child employment rules for paid work do not apply here.
duration: 28 weeks, September to May
pay_detail: Free. The Vancouver Police Foundation pays for all program materials and fees.

who_can_apply: Vancouver School Board students. Apply in grade 11 for grade 12, semester 2, at John Oliver Secondary. Grade 12 students can apply if a space is left.
how_to_apply: Use the application on the page or ask your counsellor. Email careerprograms@vsb.bc.ca.
notes: Page says students should apply in grade 11, and that grade 12 students can apply if a space remains. Confirm with the school. Contact Mark Reid, Career Programs Teacher, mreid@vsb.bc.ca.
duration: Semester 2 of grade 12
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 at Vancouver School Board schools. You need an employer in a known trade. The employer, you, a parent and the district sign an agreement.
how_to_apply: Email careerprograms@vsb.bc.ca. For building trades, ask to join the SiteReady safety course.
notes: Contact Mark Reid at the program. Students who need only one or two classes can work four days a week and take self-paced classes at South Hill Education Centre.
duration: Credits earned over the school year or semester
pay_detail: Paid by the employer. Rate not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 as of Dec 31, in the Vancouver region. This includes Vancouver, North Vancouver, West Vancouver, Burnaby and Richmond. A youth group, like a school or community group, must name you. Five members of that group must sign.
how_to_apply: Download the form. Find a sponsor group and five people to name you. Add a personal note if you did not take part last year. Fill out the online form and upload your files.
notes: Contact vyp@bcyp.org for session questions and registrar@bcyp.org for applying. The 40th session dates were not posted when read.
duration: One weekend session plus events during the year
pay_detail: $60 registration fee; financial help may be asked for by email

who_can_apply: High school students in partner school districts, including Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond and Langley. Process starts in grade 11 for courses in grade 12.
how_to_apply: Talk to the career staff at your school district. You need two references, a letter from a counselor or school leader, a letter from a parent, and the form.
notes: Recommended B or higher in English 11 and Math 11. Tuition amounts are from the VCC page and can change. Ask your district whether it pays.
duration: Varies by program (about 6 months to 40 weeks)
pay_detail: VCC lists program tuition (for example $2,513 for Baking Foundation High School). Application and student fees are waived if accepted. School district may pay tuition for select courses.

who_can_apply: High school students. Applicants must apply by the posted deadline, attend a short interview and orientation, and commit to at least 25 service hours.
how_to_apply: Apply by the posted deadline, then interview and attend orientation. Contact Anna Deater-Deckard, anna@vadm.org, 434-977-1025 x104.
notes: The museum is a small children's museum for infants to age 8, so the work is with young kids. Weekday and Saturday shifts are available.
duration: June to August; at least 25 service hours. Gallery shifts of 2-4 hours, 1-3 times a week; camp assistants commit to a full camp week (Mon-Fri, 8:45 a.m. to 1:45 p.m.)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Interns get high school service credit, a letter of recommendation, training, free parking and museum passes to share.

who_can_apply: Virginia residents ages 13 to 16 on the first day of camp. You like nature, have good grades and have not been before. An adult who is not family must nominate you.
how_to_apply: Student fills in the first three sections of the application and nomination form. The nominating adult (teacher, forester, youth leader) fills in the fourth. Submit both together by mail, email or fax.
notes: Camp has run for more than 70 years. It was formerly called Holiday Lake Forestry Camp. Scholarships come from forest industry and conservation sponsors.
duration: 5 days (June 15 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: Selected students get a $300 scholarship and pay a $95 registration fee.

who_can_apply: High school students on a team of five with one adult coach or chaperone. The page says high school students but gives no grade range.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Soil and Water Conservation District. If you do not know it, email byron.minson@vaswcd.org.
notes: Exact 2027 dates were not posted on the program page. Check the Current Competition page on the same site.
duration: Spring contests
pay_detail: No fee is mentioned on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors from Virginia public, private and home schools. Selection is by your school or county, not by Virginia Tech.
how_to_apply: Start with your school counselor. Or ask the gifted and talented lead. The Virginia Department of Education handles applications. They go through your school or county.
notes: Contact Dr. Brett Milliken, agschool@vt.edu, 540-231-6836 for cost and deadlines. Classes run 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with evening and weekend activities.
duration: 3 weeks (June 20 to July 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: Cost not listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders) enrolled in Virginia high schools who are interested in health careers. 20 students took part in 2026.
how_to_apply: The application starts at the local school district level. Forms are on the Virginia Department of Education Summer Residential Governor's School page. You can also email MHSgovschool@radford.edu.
notes: Held in Roanoke, not in Blacksburg. Email MHSgovschool@radford.edu. The Virginia Department of Education page blocked our reader, so check it for current dates.
duration: About 3 weeks, late June to early July in 2026
pay_detail: $300 activity fee for outings and enrichment. Hardship waiver available. Tuition not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors (current 10th or 11th graders) enrolled in Virginia high schools. Starts at your local school district.
how_to_apply: The application starts at the local school district level. Application forms and guides are on the Virginia Department of Education Summer Residential Governor's School page. Admitted students register on SchoolDoc.
notes: Email rugovschool@radford.edu. The Virginia Department of Education page blocked our reader, so check it for current dates and forms.
duration: Summer residential session (dates not stated on the program pages)
pay_detail: $300 activity fee for outings and enrichment. Hardship waiver available. Tuition not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 18 who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. You must be able to commute to and from the work site daily. Transportation to the site is not available.
how_to_apply: Download the YCC application form (DI-4014) from the park page and send it in. Questions go to nathaniel_phelps@nps.gov.
notes: The park is a drive from Charlottesville. Teens must arrange their own ride every day. Work permit rules for Virginia were not checked.
duration: About 8 weeks (2026 season June 15 to August 6)
pay_detail: $15.00 per hour

who_can_apply: Open to rising high school juniors and seniors. The pages do not state a Virginia residency rule for this program (WEE VT has one).
how_to_apply: Send the joint application with WEE VT and UPWARDS. Rank your choices. Write short essays of 120 words each. Add a grade transcript and a parent financial statement for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 2 weeks, residential (Jun 28 to Jul 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks, covering all expenses except travel and personal items. Full and partial need-based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Rising high school students in the grade band for each camp. No GPA or residency rule appears on the pages.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp application link on the College of Science camps page; apply for a scholarship inside the form. Cancellation refund minus a $30 fee until 4 weeks before camp.
notes: Explore Science rising 9-10 camp was listed as full in 2026. Questions: explorescicamp@vt.edu. Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 5 days (Sunday to Thursday)
pay_detail: 2026 price $1,150 per residential camp ($700 for the day camp for rising 7th-8th). Camp fees cover instruction, supplies, room and board; need-based scholarships are available in the application.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at the listed high schools. They are Floyd, Franklin County, Giles, Narrows, Bassett, Magna Vista, E.C. Glass, Heritage, Martinsville, Pulaski, Salem, William Fleming and Patrick Henry. When first picked, you must be 13 to 19. You must have low income, be first in your family to go to college, or be at risk in school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form that matches your school (Roanoke City, Salem, or Southwest Virginia list). A Spanish PDF application is also posted.
notes: Only for the listed schools, so Blacksburg and Christiansburg students are not on the list. Ask the TRIO office if your school can be added. Federal income and first-generation rules apply.
duration: School year (weekly tutoring, monthly events) plus up to six weeks in summer
pay_detail: Free. The page says students get paid for participating but does not give an amount.

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors who are Virginia residents.
how_to_apply: Joint application with the C-Tech2 and UPWARDS summer programs: rank your choices, add short essays (120 words each) and a grade transcript, and a parent completes a financial statement used for scholarships. You get an offer to only one camp.
notes: The program page as fetched on 2026-10-10 does not state the $2,500 cost or any amount; confirm the cost on the apply page before quoting it. Not a job, so no work permit.
duration: 2 weeks, residential (Jul 12 to Jul 25 in 2026)
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks, covering all expenses except travel and personal items. Full and partial need-based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Virginia high school juniors and seniors who are at least 16, Virginia residents, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents. A 2.7 GPA is required. You also need a teacher recommendation and a school counselor letter. NASA security rules usually allow only citizens and permanent residents at the summer academy.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then ask a teacher and a school counselor to send their letters through the online system. They get an email from notices@spacegrant.net. Letters sent any other way are not accepted. Contact: Regina Delzer, rdelzer@odu.edu.
notes: Closing soon. Statewide for Virginia, so it may also appear on another Virginia list. The page says 180 top scholars who finish the course attend the summer academy. The application link is on the page.
duration: Six online modules from late November, then a 6 day summer academy for selected scholars
pay_detail: Free. Scholars picked for the summer academy get transportation, housing and meals.

who_can_apply: Virginia students now in grades 9 to 12. Your local district sends the application on. The state group makes the final picks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the camper application and give it to your local Soil and Water Conservation District. Ask them about scholarships.
notes: Questions: byron.minson@vaswcd.org. If you are 13 to 16, see Camp Woods and Wildlife from the Virginia Department of Forestry.
duration: 1 week (July 12 to 18 in 2026)
pay_detail: Camp fee not listed on the state page. Local districts may give scholarships, so ask yours.

who_can_apply: Students at partner schools. Schools join by filling out an interest form and talking with a VEI Regional Director.
how_to_apply: Ask your school or counselor about the program. Contact info@veinternational.org or 855-740-6555.
notes: Not an individual sign-up; your school must be a partner. Cost to schools is not posted.
duration: School year
pay_detail: School/district pays (cost not public)

who_can_apply: A high school break internship. The page does not give grade levels, ages or where you must live. Call or email the farm to ask.
how_to_apply: Watch the High School Opportunities page in February. Call 808-696-5569 with questions. You can also email info@maoorganicfarms.org.
notes: Pay, exact dates and ages are not stated on the page. MA'O also runs college internships, which are not for high schoolers.
duration: 1 week (Fall Break in October, Spring Break in March)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors with a 2.8 or higher unweighted GPA, or test scores showing college readiness. The career path also accepts a principal recommendation in place of the GPA. You must keep a 2.0 college GPA after two courses.
how_to_apply: Use the New CCP Students page and the Advising and Registration page on the Wake Tech CCP site. Or email CCP staff with questions.
notes: Only one application per student. Use a personal email address. Wake County Public School students name their principal or a stand-in on the application.
duration: Semester by semester
pay_detail: Tuition-free

who_can_apply: Wake County high school juniors or seniors who are allowed to work in the U.S. You must have applied for Career and College Promise at Wake Tech. The path is Electrical Systems Technology.
how_to_apply: Talk with the career coordinator at your school. Or talk with Career and Technical Education staff. You can also email Todd Campbell. He runs the Wake Tech Electrification Training Project.
notes: You need your own transportation to Wake Tech and to the employer, though help may be available. Attend at least 90% of sessions. The 2026 page listed juniors and seniors expected to graduate in 2026 or 2027.
duration: 6 weeks, 8am to 5pm Monday to Wednesday, employer days Thursday and Friday
pay_detail: $2,000 stipend and 6 hours of college credit. Tools and materials provided.

who_can_apply: Juniors in Wake County Public School System high schools. Talk to your career development coordinator or CTE teacher.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Wake Tech page. Your school's career coordinator can help.
notes: Paths: building trades, car and truck tech, and advanced making. Career and College Promise helps with tuition. Next round not posted.
duration: Starts Spring 2027; about two years including paid apprenticeship
pay_detail: First year: monthly stipend, plus help with books, supplies and transportation. Second year: paid apprentice. Career and College Promise helps cover tuition.

who_can_apply: High school students age 16 or older (the page covers ages 16 through the summer after graduation). Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN and Occupational Health clearance. Apply to only one location: Raleigh Campus or Cary Hospital.
how_to_apply: Apply online for one campus while it is open. If picked, you interview, give two references, get health checks and go to orientation.
notes: Not first come, first served. It takes 3 to 5 weeks. You need flu, MMR, Varicella, Tdap and TB clearance. Not for court-ordered service. Check dates may change.
duration: Minimum 6 months, one day a week on a regular set day and time

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. You must attend at least two weeks of camp. You can join more weeks if you want.
how_to_apply: Summer 2026 applications are closed. Check the Lindsay camp counselor page for the next round. Interviews were in April for 2026.
notes: The page does not say if the role is paid, a volunteer role, or has a fee. Ask Lindsay before you apply. Lindsay is at 1931 First Avenue, Walnut Creek.
duration: At least two weeks of camp
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The page says Lindsay offers chances for community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who have not graduated from high school. You must give at least 100 hours in the program year and come to a 2.5 hour shift each week. You must be willing to give public talks, lift 15 pounds, and walk safely around animal pens.
how_to_apply: The 2026-2027 application is closed. Email the youth programs team to ask when the next one opens. The email is on the program page.
notes: Youth programs email: youthprograms@lindsaywildlife.org. Lindsay is at 1931 First Avenue, Walnut Creek. The same page describes Keepers in Training (KIT), a second step for teens who complete at least one year in the OWL program. KIT teens work closely with Lindsay's Animal Encounters department and commit to a 4 hour weekly shift. Lindsay lists its wildlife hospital and exhibit volunteer jobs as ages 18 and up. The OWL program is designed for teens ages 13 to 18.
duration: One program year, at least 100 service hours
pay_detail: Annual program fee of $700. Limited scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: Open to volunteers under 18 with rules. You need a waiver signed by a parent or guardian. You must come with your parent, guardian or chaperone. Or you can come with a school or youth group and its leader. Workdays are not drop-off programs.
how_to_apply: Pick a workday on the sign-up calendar linked on the volunteer page. You can also email the stewardship team. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian signs a waiver.
notes: The office is at 201 N. Civic Drive, Walnut Creek. Groups can fill out a group workday interest form. Group workdays are three hours long, from Wednesday through Saturday, at sites in Clayton, Concord and Pittsburg. All tools, equipment and instruction are provided. The volunteer page also lists other jobs, such as hike leader and office help. It does not give an age for them.
duration: Workdays on a calendar; group workdays are 3 hours
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Middle school students, high school students and adults can apply. Students under 17 need a parent to say yes. The library cannot give drop-in volunteer work. It also cannot give court-ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student volunteer application (a PDF from the volunteer page) or pick one up at the Welcome or Information Desk. Contact Laura Stone, Volunteer Coordinator, (847) 244-5150 ext. 3059, lstone@wnpl.info. For TAG, complete the registration form on the TAG page.
notes: Adults who apply must agree to a background check for crimes. The page says TAG is a good way to earn volunteer hours for National Honor Society and other service rules.
duration: Weekly assignments or one-time tasks. TAG meets monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library tries to help students who need school service hours, with advance notice.

who_can_apply: Youth starting at age 5 up to those who have not yet reached their 19th birthday on October 1 of the current 4-H year. Clubs run through your county WSU Extension office.
how_to_apply: Choose your project or projects. Find a club through your county WSU Extension 4-H office. Or start one if none exists. Talk with local staff, then enroll through 4-H Online. Then go to meetings and events.
notes: Fees, clubs and projects differ by county. This is a youth club and leadership program, not a paid job.
duration: One 4-H year. Enrollment opens each Oct. 1.
pay_detail: The statewide Join page does not list fees. Fees may be set by county, so ask your local Extension office.

who_can_apply: Washington state residents who are high school juniors (per the 2025 WAS FAQ: 'Scholars must be a Washington state resident and be a current junior in high school'). No math or science prerequisites are listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WAS 2026-27 Program Application linked on the page. Questions: WAS@museumofflight.org or 206-768-7214. Phase 2 invitations use a lottery. It is among students who meet the Phase 1 requirements.
notes: Deadline is very close. Graduates can apply for Museum scholarships. Participation in Phase 2 is not required for Phase 1. Students who are not juniors yet can fill out the Program Interest Form on the page to be contacted when they are eligible.
duration: Phase 1: November through March (15-20 hours per two-week lesson). Phase 2: six-day residency in July or August.
pay_detail: Phase 1 online course is free (optional 5 UW credits cost $255; financial assistance up to 100% available). Optional Phase 2 six-day residency costs $1,850 including room and board; tuition assistance up to 100% available.

who_can_apply: Students in a business or marketing class taught by a CTE certified teacher at a school with a DECA chapter. The official page lists no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Lori Hairston, lori@wadeca.org.
notes: DECA's page lists 187 chapters in Washington. The state site is wadeca.org.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student membership is $20 total: $12 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local costs.

who_can_apply: Any high school junior, typically a 16 or 17 year old finishing 11th grade. No political experience is needed. The program is for both boys and girls.
how_to_apply: Apply yourself with the online application at ebgs-wa.org/apply. Or ask a teacher, counselor or local American Legion Post to nominate you. They use the program's nomination form. After screening, the program helps find a sponsor if you need one.
notes: The site describes a 7-day, 6-night leadership experience. Confirm the 2027 dates on the main page of ebgs-wa.org.
duration: One week. 2027 session: Sunday June 20 to Saturday June 26, 2027.
pay_detail: The program is valued at $700 with meals and housing. A local American Legion Post can sponsor a student for $350 on request, and help for the full $700 is available on request. The site says cost is not a barrier.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education at a school with an FFA chapter. The page does not give age or grade limits.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's ag teacher if your school has an FFA chapter and how to join.
notes: The page says the association has over 14,500 members in 194 chapters. Dues are $7 a year nationally and $10 a year for Washington. Local chapters may charge more.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher about dues.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Seniors are told not to apply because onboarding is long (a college program exists).
how_to_apply: Email volunteer_services@washingtonhealth.com with your name, grade, school, phone and email. They contact you only when an info session is scheduled. Phone 510-818-7465.
notes: No GPA rule or fee appears on the current page (older versions listed a GPA rule and $20 fee). Openings are limited. Office: 2500 Mowry Ave, Fremont. The page says the list is closed as of May 22, 2026, but also says you are welcome to join the list now; call to confirm.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state an age or grade rule. Teen volunteering is available at the Bainbridge Island, Bremerton (Sylvan Way), Port Orchard, Poulsbo and Silverdale branches.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application online. It shows which branches have openings.
notes: The application form did not load for this guide, so the questions and age rule were not checked. Call your branch to confirm the minimum age.
duration: Not stated

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old and not yet 17. You need a parent or guardian's permission and a teacher's recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open on the Page Program page. Pick the weeks you can do with care. Senate contact: SenatePageProgram@leg.wa.gov, 360-786-7498. House contact: 360-786-7889.
notes: The page lists no closing date, so apply soon after Nov 1. Check the Page Program page for the current application link. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: One week during the session. The 2027 session runs January through April.
pay_detail: Stipend of $67 per day. You need a Social Security card to get it. Pages without one can still take part but get no daily stipend.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18. The page describes it as for urban teens. Crews go home each night for the first four weeks.
how_to_apply: Use the apply link for Tacoma or Olympia on the page. Ask about tuition help.
notes: Teens may be able to get school credit, but only your school can decide. Participants who leave early get a prorated stipend and lose bonuses.
duration: 5 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 weekly dependability bonus and $20 weekly safety bonus. $200 tuition, with tuition help based on need.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who can travel to the central meeting place each day. Housing is not provided.
how_to_apply: Use the Tacoma apply link on the page. Ask about tuition help.
notes: Crews may earn high school credit if your school agrees. The same program also runs in Eugene, OR and Boise, ID.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday (2026: June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 weekly dependability bonus and $20 weekly safety bonus. $200 tuition, with tuition help based on need.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Washington. The SBCTC page does not list other requirements; contact the college's Running Start coordinator.
how_to_apply: Contact the Running Start coordinator at the college you want to attend (the SBCTC page links a coordinator list) and your high school counselor.
notes: Work hours tie-in from Washington L&I: 16 and 17 year olds enrolled in a bona fide college program, such as Running Start, may work non-school week hours during the regular school year (employers should ask for proof such as a college transcript).
duration: Per quarter or semester
pay_detail: No tuition. Students and families pay mandatory fees, books and transportation.

who_can_apply: Volunteers of all ages. Volunteers 13 and under must be supervised by a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator at your local library for a list of openings, or use the Volunteer Portal on the page.
notes: Library jobs at Sno-Isle require you to be 16 or older (from the same page). The page says to check with your local library for current openings.
duration: A regular portion of your time each week

who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18 (national Civil Air Patrol page). The Washington Wing pages do not list other rules. Ask a squadron about citizenship and school rules.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron on the Washington Wing Locations list or the national unit finder. Visit a meeting. Ask the squadron for the application. Wing office: 253-982-7774 or wa@wawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Washington Wing join page links to separate Youth, Adults and Educators pages, so the age and cost figures come from the national page. This is a youth program, not a paid job.
duration: The national page describes about a 2-hour squadron meeting each week, a monthly Saturday event and a week-long summer encampment. School-based squadrons may differ.
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 18. Under 14 must have a parent, guardian or teacher with them.
how_to_apply: Search the WTA work party list, pick one and sign up online. Youth groups can contact WTA to set up a private work party.
notes: The overview page does not say whether youth work parties are unpaid; it describes them as volunteer service hours. Multi-day shared-identity trail trips are also offered. Details on gear, rides and sign-up are on the work party page, not read here. Youth group bookings: volunteer@wta.org.
duration: Work parties run Tuesday to Sunday; one day or multi-day
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Washington residents who are U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents, ages 15 and a half to 18 at entry (the main page says 15 to 18). You must be behind in school, have dropped out, or be at risk of not graduating. No felony charges or pending court cases. You must choose to attend, stay drug free and be able to take part.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send the doctor and dentist forms and other documents (WYA.Applications@mil.wa.gov or fax 360-473-2623). Then do an interview and final review. Phone: 877-228-8947.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 1207 Carver Street, Bremerton, WA 98312.
duration: 22 weeks on campus (a 147-day class cycle), then a two-year follow-up phase
pay_detail: Free. The page calls it a free life intervention and credit retrieval program.

who_can_apply: Students at East Aurora High School or West Aurora High School only. The pages do not list income or first-generation rules, so ask the staff.
how_to_apply: Fill out the new student application (from your counselor, Room 201 at East or A104A at West, or the website). Staff then set up a family interview, and new students do a 10 to 60 day trial period. Email upwardbound@waubonsee.edu.
notes: The form asks for copies of your transcript and birth certificate. It also asks for your Social Security card and a parent tax return. Give these only to program staff at the school or the Sugar Grove office.
duration: Through high school graduation
pay_detail: Free. Federally funded TRIO program. No stipend is mentioned on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Individuals and groups. People under 18 need a parent or legal guardian to sign the forms. No minimum age is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Agreement Form. A parent signs it if you are under 18. Email it to efallon@waukeganparks.org. Phone: Elizabeth Fallon, (847) 782-3626.
notes: Park projects: contact Bryant Brown. Bryant is the Park Services Supervisor. The phone is 847-360-4756. Read the Volunteer Requirements and Expectations document before you start.
duration: Year-round, event and project based
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Right now the library does not take volunteers who must do court ordered community service.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer form. Or visit the Youth and Teen Department during normal hours.
notes: The library's Maker Space (3D printer, laser engraver, sewing machines) is open to teens ages 16 and up, which is a good way to build skills. Hours and training are not on the pages.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. If you are under 15, you can volunteer with an adult who is 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Volunteer Application. You get a confirmation email, then a call or email after approval. Contact Lisa Snow, 630-681-0962 ext. 548, lisasn@wdsra.com.
notes: WDSRA also hires part-time program staff (the volunteer page does not give a minimum age for them). The jobs page lists openings and how to apply.
duration: Flexible. You choose how often. New volunteer orientation takes about 1 hour.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18 who are interested in a health care career. Spots are limited and competitive.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Send shot records (MMR, DPT, Varicella). Have your school counselor fill out and sign the School Records Release. You can email, fax or mail documents to Volunteer Services. If you are picked, there is a short 15-minute interview.
notes: Volunteer Services: 3950 Austell Rd, Austell, GA 30106, (470) 732-3767. Picks use a finished application and the required documents. They also look at time commitment, past volunteering, GPA and leadership. They look at speaking skills and interest in health care too. Unpaid, so no work permit.
duration: June 4 to July 29 in 2026, one 4-hour shift a week plus a 2-hour orientation
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role (16 service hours validated)

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Picks are based on the full application. They also look at whether you can keep the time commitment. They look at past volunteering, GPA, leadership, speaking skills and interest in health careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the window. Email your shot record as a PDF. It needs 2 MMR, 2 Varicella or proof of the illness, and 1 Tdap. Your school counselor fills out and signs the recommendation form and emails it. The interview is in March and the orientation is in April. After you are accepted, you get TB test steps.
notes: Accepted students may keep volunteering in the school year if Volunteer Services says yes. It is competitive. This is an unpaid volunteer role, so no work permit.
duration: 8-week summer session in June and July, one 2-hour shift a week for 6 of the 8 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page mentions no fees.

who_can_apply: High school students aged 16 to 18. You need shot records, a school counselor form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online VolunTeen application. Email your shot record (2 MMR, 2 chickenpox or proof you had it, 1 Tdap) as a PDF. Have your school counselor sign the recommendation form and email it. Then you are called for an interview.
notes: Spots are limited. Not everyone is accepted. Picks look at past service, GPA, leadership and interest in health careers. Students accepted for summer may keep volunteering in the school year with approval.
duration: Summer session in June and July: one two-hour shift per week for six of the eight weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: At least 15 when you start. Before you start, you need cards for Lifeguard Training, CPR for the Professional Rescuer, First Aid and Title 22. A Water Safety Instructor card is a big plus. Past lifeguard work helps, but you do not need it.
how_to_apply: Fill out the whole city job form online on NEOGOV. Add a resume. The city reads every form. The best fits go on a hiring list. The top people move to the next step.
notes: The posting does not list hours or season dates, so ask Parks and Recreation at (916) 617-4567. Get your lifeguard certificates before you apply, since they are required before you start. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit. Teens 14 to 16 who are too young for this job can look at the city's unpaid Teen Heroes summer camp program.
pay_detail: $17.25 to $18.75 per hour (2026 posting). Temporary, extra help.

who_can_apply: At least 17 at the time of employment, with one year of experience working with youth or the public. Some assignments need CPR and First Aid certificates before you start. You must pass a fingerprint check and drug screen before you start.
how_to_apply: Fill out the whole city job form online on NEOGOV. Add a resume and answer the extra questions. The city reads every form. The top people are sent to the department.
notes: The city also has a Recreation Aide job for ages 15 and up. It paid $17.00 an hour in the 2022 job sheet. But the last Recreation Aide post on the city jobs page ran Aug 29 to Sep 19, 2018. Lead, senior and KidZone leader jobs need a high school diploma or age 18. A 17 year old still needs a California work permit for paid work.
pay_detail: $17.00 to $18.50 per hour (2026 postings). Part-time extra help.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 16, eligible West Sacramento residents. Needs proof of the hepatitis B vaccine series, fingerprinting and a background check.
how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. Call the Club West Teen Center at (916) 373-5877 or ask City of West Sacramento Parks and Recreation.
notes: Page has no year or dates, so ask when applications open. Vaccine proof may take weeks to collect. Runs in summer.
pay_detail: Free to join, unpaid. The page does not list a stipend.

who_can_apply: Concurrent enrollment: grades 9 to 12. Middle College: juniors and seniors from LGSUHSD and CUHSD. Dual enrollment on high school campuses: CUHSD (Campbell Union High School District) students only.
how_to_apply: Start at the college's high school students page and apply through the admissions portal; the page also covers assessment, orientation and registration.
notes: Ask the college about unit limits and your counselor about credit.
pay_detail: Free (per the college page)

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 on a team of four to six with a teacher advisor.
how_to_apply: A teacher advisor and the team register on the Wharton Global Youth site. The page does not give a date for the next cycle's registration; check the site.
notes: Sign-up steps are on the Rules and Roles and Register pages, which were not read. Travel costs to the finale were not stated.
duration: Trading starts Sept 28, 2026, then virtual semifinals (date not posted) and a finale Apr 29 to 30, 2027 (2026-27 cycle)
pay_detail: Free to enter. No pay.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12 can earn service hours. There are separate Teen Library Council groups for middle school and high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Interest Form. Or fill out the Teen Library Council form. Questions: teenread@wheatonlibrary.org.
notes: You can also earn hours by making cards. Four cards earn 1 volunteer hour. You can also write book reviews. Each review earns 30 minutes of service hours.
duration: School year volunteering begins the week of Monday, September 14 (no year printed; the weekday matches 2026)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: The event page does not say if you need to sign up. Call the museum at 316-268-4921 to ask.
notes: It is at the Wichita Art Museum, 1400 West Museum Boulevard. The event page does not say whether sign-up is required.
duration: One evening, 6 to 8 p.m.
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 14 years old unless an event says something different. Volunteers 16 and older must pass a background check.
how_to_apply: All volunteers must go through an application process. Then sign up for a shift on the volunteer calendar. To apply to be a gallery docent, use the application link on the program page. Call the volunteer coordinator at 316-660-0603.
notes: Special events can have their own age rules. The page says volunteers 16 and older must complete a background check.
duration: Pick shifts from the volunteer calendar. The page does not state a minimum time.
pay_detail: Volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Use the printable flyer on the page. The museum's general number is 316-265-9314.
notes: The page says the program is in its third year. Last Teen Night dates listed were April 5, 2025 and April 11, 2026. The school flyer needs principal approval before it is handed out.
duration: Meets once a month from October. The Teen Night event is in April.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a good way to earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: The Teen Advisory Board is open to teens in grades 6 to 12. The program page does not give a grade rule for the Summer Reading volunteers.
how_to_apply: For the Teen Advisory Board, email the teen librarian named on the page. Watch the same page for the next Summer Reading Volunteer application.
notes: The Summer Reading volunteer program has run since 1990, says the page. The library's main Volunteer page lists other volunteer options.
duration: Teen Advisory Board: one meeting a month at the Advanced Learning Library. Summer Reading volunteers: during the summer program.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours. Summer Reading teens can earn more than 30 hours.

who_can_apply: Sedgwick County residents between ages 7 and 19. You can enroll if you turn 7 before January 1 of the 4-H year. If you turn 19 before January 1, you cannot enroll.
how_to_apply: Call 316-660-0115 to find clubs near you. Then enroll online in Kansas 4-H.
notes: The same page also says 4-H is for ages 5 to 18, and it names a county fair deadline for a different county. To show in the county fair 4-H division, join by May 1. Call the Sedgwick office to confirm.
duration: The 4-H year runs Oct 1 to Sep 30.
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older for special events. For some events, volunteers under 18 must come with an adult. Husbandry aide volunteers must be 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Get Started link on the volunteer page to contact the zoo, complete a volunteer application, and go to a volunteer orientation (2nd Saturday 8 to 10 a.m. or 4th Thursday 4 to 6 p.m. at the Cargill Learning Center).
notes: Quote from the page: Must be 14 years of age to volunteer for Special Events. Groups can do service days in the zoo departments from age 16, scheduled two weeks ahead, April through October. Adults 18 and over must pass a background check.
duration: Event by event, spread through the year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Applicants must be 16 or older. Wesley does not take volunteers for court-ordered hours, and it does not offer one-time or group volunteering.
how_to_apply: Download the volunteer application and fill it out. Then mail it to Wesley Volunteer Services, 550 N. Hillside St., Wichita, KS 67214, or scan and email it. Next come a personal interview and a criminal background check. Then you submit personal health records and go to orientation.
notes: Quote from the page: Applicants must be 16 years of age or older. Volunteers must keep up a regular schedule. A mandatory flu shot policy applies in flu season.
duration: At least 4 shifts a month and 60 total hours, which the page says takes about six months
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 4 to 12. The page lists the grades for each camp. Two 2026 camps were for grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the program page. Use the scholarship form on the same page to ask for help with cost.
notes: In 2026 the Biomedical Engineering camp ran June 22 to 26. Ethical Hacking ran July 13 to 17.
duration: Most camps last 1 week in June and July
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Scholarships are available through a form on the page.

who_can_apply: Kansas high school students, or eighth graders who are about to start high school. You must be first in your family to go to college (neither parent in the home has a bachelor's degree). Or your family income must be within federal rules. You should like math, science, engineering or health jobs.
how_to_apply: Tell your school counselor you are interested, or call Upward Bound Math Science at 316-978-3316.
notes: Application deadlines, cost and pay are Not stated on the program page.
duration: 6 weeks in June and July
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17. Classes are at several YMCA branches and Wichita high schools. Newton picks 15 students based on birthdate and location.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online enrollment form. Or use a printable form from the page and turn it in at your YMCA branch front desk. You can also email the Job Prep contact on the page.
notes: Spots are limited. The page names past summer job sites. They include the Sedgwick County Zoo, the Wichita Art Museum and Exploration Place. They also include Wesley Medical Center and Wichita Habitat for Humanity. The page says over 350 summer jobs were offered. The Workforce Alliance YEP page also points teens to this program.
duration: Class once a week for 2 hours, February to May
pay_detail: The course is free. The summer job is the reward; the program page does not state the pay.

who_can_apply: Workshops are open to anyone age 14 and older. Work experience placements need you to be at least 16 by June 1 of that year. The workforce centers are in Wichita, El Dorado, Wellington and Arkansas City. Some employers only place ages 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Make a KANSASWORKS account. Then fill out the YEP registration form. Once it is on file, you are sent information to sign up for workshops and job fairs. Age 14 to 17: bring a non-expired picture ID and birth certificate, plus a signed Social Security card, for a work placement.
notes: Camp HYPE is listed for age 15. The FAQ also points to the City of Wichita Way to Work program and the YMCA Job Prep program. A different Workforce Alliance program, WIOA Youth, is for out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers and an income limit.
duration: Workshops March to June. Most jobs run June to August.
pay_detail: Placements pay at least $7.25 per hour. Workshops do not pay. Most placements are 20 hours a week or less and last 8 weeks or less.

who_can_apply: Open to almost anyone, even without logging in. The page links to guidance for younger editors but states no minimum age.
how_to_apply: Start editing, or make a free account (not required). Try The Wikipedia Adventure tutorial.
notes: Protect your personal info; do not share your school or address.
duration: Whenever you want
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 can join the teen program. Kids ages 11 to 13 can apply to be library helpers for certain youth programs, with parent or guardian approval.
how_to_apply: Summer 2026 applications are closed for the season. School year applications are open. Go to the volunteering page. Fill out the volunteer form there. If you have a question, write to teenvolunteers@wilmettelibrary.info.
notes: Summer jobs run June to August. Krista Hutley is the teen librarian. Eti Berland is the school engagement librarian. They are the teen volunteer coordinators. The Studio program has its own info sheet.
duration: School year positions, plus summer positions that run June to August
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: 15 or older. You need a lifeguard card (with deep water) and CPR and AED for the Professional Rescuer. You can get them within 30 days after you are hired. First Aid for Public Safety (Title 22) is a plus. You must pass a fingerprint check and a TB skin test. You must be able to work early, late, on holidays and on weekends.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the city's NEOGOV jobs page. Answer the extra questions. One asks if you can pass the swim test. You swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes with only your legs and swim 50 yards. Then you bring up a 10 pound object in a timed test. Training is required.
notes: A good choice if you are not certified yet, because the city pays for the certification class. The posting window was short in 2026 (about one month), so check in January. Lifeguards are mandated reporters and must finish that training in the first two weeks. Paid work under 18 needs a California work permit.
duration: Summer pool season. Exact dates are not on the posting.
pay_detail: $18.00 to $20.00 per hour (2026 posting), starting at $18. Seasonal, no benefits. The city registers you for and pays for the certification class.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin youth in grades 9 to 12 at the time of application.
how_to_apply: Apply through 4-H Online. The team checks references in December.
notes: Key 2027 dates: State Leader Teams Weekend Apr 9 to 11, Fall Forum Nov 5 to 7.
duration: One program year (events April to November 2027)
pay_detail: $500 (shirts, lodging and meals at four events). Scholarships up to 70% on request.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin youth in grades 8 to 11. Each track has its own grade range.
how_to_apply: Register in 4-H Online (make a profile if you are new). A paper form is also on the 4-H site. Apply for a scholarship during registration.
notes: The page says track details are labeled 2026 and may change for 2027.
duration: 5 days (June 13 to 17, 2027)
pay_detail: $150 per youth, covers lodging, meals, bus and activities. State scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Students entering their senior year of high school next fall. You must be from a Wisconsin high school or home-schooled in Wisconsin.
how_to_apply: School staff such as counselors or the social studies department often help choose students. You can also email info@badgerboysstate.org to say you want to attend. Include your name, high school, phone number and email.
notes: Not a job. The 2027 session is the 83rd. Office: 2930 American Legion Drive, Portage, WI 53901, phone 608-745-1090.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
pay_detail: The program says it is 100% funded by donations. A student fee is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Young women in their junior year of high school in Wisconsin. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: The page says to speak to your high school counselor if you want to become a delegate.
notes: Not a job. A tuition sponsor is needed, usually found through the school or the local American Legion Auxiliary. Dates for the next session come from the program site.
duration: One week, June 20 to 25, 2027
pay_detail: The American Legion Auxiliary and Legion family sponsor and pay the tuition for a delegate. Clubs, businesses and school groups can also pay. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin DECA strongly encourages members to also be enrolled in a marketing or business course. Chapters need an advisor with a marketing or business educator license. Detailed rules are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. For eligibility and deadlines, contact the Wisconsin DECA advisor, Tim Fandek, at Timothy.Fandek@dpi.wi.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is wideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Wisconsin.
duration: School year
pay_detail: $18 per student member: $10 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.

who_can_apply: Wisconsin students interested in the outdoors. It is best suited to high school students and younger students may apply. Some DNR volunteer tasks are only for ages 16 and up. You can take part through the summer after senior year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YCC application and parent consent form from the DNR YCC page. Or contact the YCC Coordinator, Kyle Zenz, at kyle.zenz@wisconsin.gov or 715-299-0925.
notes: Volunteer program, not a job. A parent or guardian must sign the consent form. It can count toward school service-learning or independent study credit if your school agrees. The packet's example activities are from 2025, so check this year's schedule.
duration: Year-round. Two district meetings plus Spring Hearings and a May convention, with extra field days.
pay_detail: No pay. Free to join, apart from your own travel costs.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. The applicant page lists no GPA, age or residency rule. You also need an employer to hire you.
how_to_apply: Pick a career area. Talk with your counselor and parents. Contact your local YA Regional Coordinator and apply. Then interview with employers. After you are hired you go to orientation and safety training.
notes: Wisconsin's youth apprenticeship page says work permits are no longer required for 16 and 17 year olds. The Wisconsin work permit page says 14 and 15 year olds still need a permit ($10 fee, repaid by the employer by the first paycheck). A 15 year old junior is possible, so ask your coordinator. Student learner status does not override minor employment laws. DWD phone (608) 266-3131.
duration: Not stated on the program pages. Work and classes run during high school.
pay_detail: You earn a paycheck from day one. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in a school agricultural education program that has an active FFA chapter. The Affiliation page says grades 5th to 12th. No age limit is listed.
how_to_apply: Contact your school's ag education teacher. If your school has no program, contact the state ag education staff. Ask about starting one.
notes: Not a job. The site has a Local Chapter Locator that links to Find a Program. Your school must have an ag program and an FFA chapter. The Affiliation fee is based on enrollment. The page does not say who pays it, so the claim in pay_detail that the school pays is not confirmed by this page.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Traditional membership is $15 total ($8 state, $7 national). Local chapters may charge more. Affiliation program fees depend on enrollment and are paid by the school.

who_can_apply: The Wisconsin Wing site labels the cadet program as ages 12 to 19. The national CAP cadet page says between 12 and 18. This guide uses the national ages, 12 to 18, so ask the squadron if you are 19. The interest form lists grades 6 through 12 and high school graduates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the Wisconsin Wing site. The wing aims to pass your info to a local unit within 48 hours, and the unit should contact you within 48 hours after that. If you hear nothing in four days, email Major Todd Mandel at todd.mandel@wicap.us.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ages differ between the Wisconsin page (12 to 19) and the national page (12 to 18), so confirm with the squadron. Wing address: 2400 Wright Street, Madison, WI 53704.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the program pages. Ask the squadron.

who_can_apply: Students who join a delegation near them. The page does not list grades. Media spots are by application and may be limited.
how_to_apply: Find a delegation near you on the Wisconsin YG site. Then register at wiyg.org/register before the closing date for your role. Use the Contact Us page if you need help starting a delegation.
notes: Not a job. Legislative and Media materials are due in January and Judicial materials in February.
duration: Fall to March: prep, a Pre-Gov session, then the Model Government conference
pay_detail: Dues and conference fees are not listed on the program page. Ask your delegation.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 8th grade. Partner high school classes are arranged through your counselor. Tuition is free for 11 units or fewer.
how_to_apply: Explore with your counselor, apply on CCCApply, set up your student account, submit the CCAP or High School Non-CCAP form, then register.
notes: Students may pay for books and materials. Check your counselor for term deadlines. Davis High was not on the CCAP list I saw, so a Davis student would use the non-CCAP route. Charter and homeschool students may need grade verification.
duration: Per term
pay_detail: Free up to 11 units ($46 per unit fee waived); books may cost

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Register online through the Woodland Community Services registration portal (linked from the Teen Programs page) or call (530) 661-2000. Email: WoodlandCSD@cityofwoodland.gov.
notes: The page gives no hours, dates or fees. Call Community Services to ask how it works and when to start.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 7 to 12. Teens should limit in-person volunteering to no more than two events a month.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a teen volunteer event on the library page. Or send a book review of at least 5 sentences through the form. Questions: askus@woodridgelibrary.org.
notes: If you register and cannot come, cancel so someone else can take the spot. Some events have waitlists.
duration: Event based. Hours depend on the event length.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Library staff give letters with the service hours earned.

who_can_apply: Worcester teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. REC runs an annual spring hiring process. Call REC at 508-799-9139 or check its Employment page.
notes: The pay rate and teen application steps are not stated on the page, so confirm with REC. Address: 108 Beacon Street, Worcester. The program employs up to 40 teens year-round.
duration: Year-round, with a 6-week summer intensive
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly wage is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Santa Clara County residents ages 16 to 24 who are low-income and have at least one barrier to employment or education.
how_to_apply: Call the San Jose Job Center at 408-794-1101 or the Gilroy center at 408-758-3477 and ask about the young adult program.
notes: San Jose Works, a partner program, is also on the page. The page gives ages 14 to 18 for its Paid Work Experience Program and ages 16 to 29 for other city services. Income and barrier rules apply. The page does not say whether job centers are by appointment only. It does not say whether the other services are free.
pay_detail: Paid work experience; the page says you can earn up to $25 an hour.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24.
how_to_apply: Call 303-271-4755 or schedule an appointment with a Career Coach on the page.
notes: The page says the Governor's Summer Job Hunt is a free program for ages 14 to 24. Job Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also listed: 303-623-0420. Office: 3500 Illinois St, Suite 1600, Golden, CO.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Services are free. The page says it connects people to paid and unpaid work experience.

who_can_apply: Eligible young adults ages 17 to 24. The page does not list other rules or say which counties qualify.
how_to_apply: Click Apply Now or Get Started at worknetdupage.org/job-seekers/get-started/, or call 630-955-2030. Career Center: 2525 Cabot Drive, Suite 302, Lisle.
notes: Starts at 17, so it fits only older high schoolers. Spanish-speaking services are available. The Get Started page was not read, so check eligibility there.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid work experience is offered; pay rates and length are not stated. Training or school help is up to $10,000.

who_can_apply: City of Atlanta residents ages 16 to 24 who are WIOA eligible. In-school youth are generally 16 to 21, must meet income and other criteria, and may have a barrier such as disability, English learner, foster care, homeless, justice-involved or parenting. A WorkSource Atlanta Eligibility Specialist makes the final decision.
how_to_apply: 1) Finish the online youth orientation. 2) Create a profile in the WorkSource Georgia portal and save your SID number. 3) Upload your documents. 4) Book an eligibility appointment, or email WSAYouth@AtlantaGa.Gov with subject Ready to RISE. 5) Take the My Next Move career assessment. 6) Eligibility review.
notes: Eligibility is income and barrier based, so not every teen qualifies. The document list includes a Social Security card and proof of address; this is the official city workforce board, but upload documents only through the portal named on the page. Under 18 using parent documents: proof of relationship and shared address is needed. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.
duration: Year-round, no set end date
pay_detail: Paid work experience and internships are one service. Wage not posted on the page. Services are no cost.

who_can_apply: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 24 who face barriers to work. The page does not define barriers.
how_to_apply: Apply online at ATLworks.org. Send everything it asks for. An eligibility specialist reviews it and replies within 7 business days. Then you meet the specialist and make a career plan.
notes: The page does not mention work permits. Contact 404-371-2000 (Mon to Fri, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm) or 311CCC@dekalbcountyga.gov.
duration: Paid work experience up to 14 weeks
pay_detail: $13 per hour for paid work experience, up to 14 weeks. Up to $250 more in milestone rewards. Free to join.

who_can_apply: Fulton County residents ages 16 to 24 who are interested in employment or training and meet low-income guidelines and/or have significant barriers to education or employment.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe an application. Visit the youth center at 4405 Mall Blvd., Suite 400, Union City, GA 30291, or call a career center: South Fulton 404-613-6800 (5710 Stonewall Tell Rd., Suite 160, College Park) or North Fulton 404-613-4480 (7741 Roswell Rd., Suite 205, Sandy Springs).
notes: A March 2026 county news release says WorkSource Fulton also offers the Career Compass Academy, a five-week paid virtual work readiness program for ages 14 to 24 that is income based. Teens signed up at the county's Summer Teen Hiring Fair on April 11, 2026; next year's dates are not posted. If you live inside the City of Atlanta, also look at Youth R.I.S.E. and ask which office serves your address. The county's older Summer Youth Job Training and Summer Youth Internship pages return errors now.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Paid work experience is one service. Wage not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Washington Unified School District high school students who are 16 by the first day. River City HS students need a Career Technical Education course; Yolo HS and Washington Middle College students need a teacher or counselor recommendation. Everyone attends one online info session.
how_to_apply: Go to the Internships page, attend the info session, send the recommendation form if needed, then apply and interview with employers.
notes: Employers have included Center for Land Based Learning, Elica Health Centers, City of West Sacramento and others. The 2026 calendar on the page is an image, so ask for 2027 dates: wshomerun@cityofwestsacramento.org or (916) 617-4500.
duration: summer, up to 40 hours per week
pay_detail: Paid by the City of West Sacramento, up to 40 hours per week. Hourly rate not posted on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 15 at the start of camp. Separate Girls Camp and Boys Camp weeks. Residency rules are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the camps page when it opens. Questions: Parker Everhart, parker.everhart@wyo.gov, 307-823-2368.
notes: Ages 12 to 15 only, so older teens should look at other cards.
duration: About one week (2026: Boys Camp June 14 to 20, Girls Camp July 5 to 11)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. The camps are funded in partnership with the Wyldlife Fund.

who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21, or out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24. Must live in Wyoming and meet low-income rules or have another qualifying barrier to work.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Workforce Center to see if you qualify.
notes: Out-of-school youth can join up to age 24. Eligibility rules vary, so ask your local Workforce Center.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The page lists "paid or unpaid" work experience and training. Pay rates are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Register online for the day camp or residential option; a separate summer program scholarship application is available. Questions: summerprograms@xavier.edu.
notes: Xavier's Summer Programs page also lists other high school options: Summer in Cincy (one-week residential pre-college), D'Artagnan Summer Business Academy (rising juniors and seniors), CSI Forensics Camp (grades 10 to 12) and STRONG eXplorer Career Camp. Check each page for 2027 prices. High school students who attend may get a $500 to $1,000 award if they later enroll.
